Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā

The Old Sub-commentary on the Dispelling of Doubts.

Ganthārambhakathā

Introduction to the Text

Buddhaṃ [M 0.0001][V 0.0001] dhammañca saṅghanti-ādinā yā pakāsitā;

Bhadantabuddhaghosena, mātikāṭṭhakathā subhā;

Tassā hi līnapadaṃ vi-kāsanakoyamārambho.

The Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha—thus, beginning with these words, was the beautiful commentary on the Mātikā expounded by the Venerable Buddhaghosa. This is the beginning of an attempt to clarify its obscure passages.

Ganthārambhakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Introduction

Vippasannenāti [V 0.0002] vividhappasannena. Kathaṃ? “Itipi so…pe… buddho bhagavā, svākkhāto…pe… viññūhi, suppaṭipanno…pe… lokassā”ti (a. ni. 5.10) evamādinā. “Cetasā”ti vuttattā tīsu vandanāsu cetovandanā adhippetā. Tanninnatādivasena kāyādīhi paṇāmakaraṇaṃ vandanā, guṇavasena manasāpi tathāva karaṇaṃ mānaṃ, paccayappaṭipattiyādīhi pūjākaraṇaṃ pūjā, paccayādīnaṃ abhisaṅkharaṇaṃ sakkacca karaṇaṃ sakkāro, tesaṃ. Bhājananti ādhāro, adhikaraṇaṃ vā.

"With a clear mind" means with a mind clear in various ways. How? "Such indeed is the Blessed One... the Buddha; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed... by the wise; the Sangha has practiced well... of the world" (Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.10), and so on. Because "with the mind" is stated, mental homage is intended among the three types of homage. Homage is the act of bowing with the body, etc., out of devotion; reverence is doing likewise with the mind, out of respect for qualities; veneration is performing worship through requisites and practice, etc.; respect is carefully preparing requisites, etc. "Vessel" means a support or a basis.

Therā mahākassapādayo, tesaṃ vaṃsoti theravaṃso, āgamādhigamasampadāya tassa vaṃsassa padīpabhūtāti theravaṃsappadīpā, tesaṃ theravaṃsappadīpānaṃ. Asaṃhīrattā thirānaṃ. Vinayakkameti vinayapiṭake, ārambhānurūpavacanametaṃ. Suttābhidhammesupi te thirā eva. “Buddhaṃ dhammañca saṅghañca pubbācariyasīhānañcā”ti avatvā kasmā visuṃ vuttanti ce? Payojanavisesadassanatthaṃ. Vatthuttayassa hi paṇāmakaraṇassa antarāyanivāraṇaṃ payojanaṃ [M 0.0002] attano nissayabhūtānaṃ ācariyānaṃ paṇāmakaraṇassa upakāraññutādassanaṃ. Tena buddhañca dhammañca saṅghañca vanditvā, ca-saddena pubbācariyasīhānañca namo katvāti yojanā. Atha vā “vanditvā”ti cetovandanaṃ dassetvā tato “namo katvā”ti vācāvandanā, “katañjalī”ti kāyavandanāpi dassitāti yojetabbaṃ.

The Elders, beginning with Mahākassapa—their lineage is the lineage of elders. Being the torchbearers of that lineage through the accomplishment of learning and realization, they are the torchbearers of the elders' lineage. Of those torchbearers of the elders' lineage. They are firm due to being unshaken. "In the Vinaya"—this refers to the Vinaya Piṭaka; this statement is appropriate to the beginning. They are also firm in the Suttas and Abhidhamma. If asked why it is not said, "The Buddha, the Dhamma, the Sangha, and the former teachers, the lions," but stated separately, it is to show a special purpose. For paying homage to the Triple Gem has the purpose of removing obstacles, while paying homage to one's own teachers, who are one's support, shows gratitude. Therefore, the connection is: having paid homage to the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, and, with the word "and," having paid homage to the former teachers, the lions. Alternatively, "having paid homage" shows mental homage, then "having bowed" shows verbal homage, and "with hands joined in reverence" shows bodily homage—this should be understood.

Idāni abhidhānappayojanaṃ dassetuṃ “pāmokkha”ntiādimāha. Tattha pāmokkhanti padhānaṃ. Sīlañhi sabbesaṃ kusaladhammānaṃ padhānaṃ ādibhāvato. Yathā ca sattānaṃ khajjabhojjaleyyapeyyavasena catubbidhopi āhāro mukhena pavisitvā aṅgamaṅgāni pharati, evaṃ yoginopi cātubhūmakaṃ kusalaṃ sīlamukhena pavisitvā atthasiddhiṃ sampādeti. Tena vuttaṃ “mukha”ntiādi. Atha vā mukhanti upāyo, tena mokkhappavesāya nibbānasacchikiriyāya mukhaṃ upāyoti attho. Mahesinā yaṃ pātimokkhaṃ pakāsitanti sambandho. Mahante sīlādikkhandhe esi gavesīti mahesi.

Now, to explain the purpose of the term, he says "foremost" and so on. Here, "foremost" means principal. For virtue is the principal of all wholesome qualities, being the first. Just as the four kinds of food—solid, soft, lickable, and drinkable—enter through the mouth and pervade the limbs, so too, for the yogi, wholesome action pertaining to the four planes, entering through the mouth of virtue, accomplishes the attainment of the goal. Hence, "mouth" and so on is said. Alternatively, "mouth" means the means; thus, the mouth is the means for entering liberation, for realizing Nibbāna—this is the meaning. The connection is: "the Pātimokkha proclaimed by the great seer." "Great seer" means one who seeks the great aggregates of virtue, etc.

Sūratena nivātenāti “tattha katamaṃ soraccaṃ? Yo kāyiko avītikkamo”tiādinā (dha. sa. 1349) sūratena, nīcavuttinā mānuddhaccavasena attānaṃ anukkhipanabhāvena nivātena. Vinayācārayuttena cārittavārittehi yuttena. “Soṇattherena yācito”ti avatvā “sūratenā”tiādi [V 0.0003] kasmā vuttaṃ, kiṃ dussīlena vā duṭṭhena vā alajjinā vā yācitena vaṇṇanā kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti ce? Na na vaṭṭati. Therassa vacanaṃ paṭikkhipituṃ na sakkā, evarūpaguṇo therova, yācanavasena kattabbo ādarenāti dassetuṃ vuttaṃ.

"By docility and humility" means: "What is docility there? It is bodily non-transgression," etc. (Dhammasaṅgaṇī 1349), by docility; by lowly conduct, by the absence of self-exaltation due to pride and arrogance, by humility. "Endowed with the practice of discipline" means possessing both proper conduct and restraint. If asked why it was said, "By docility," etc., without stating, "Requested by the Elder Soṇa," is it because it is not proper to make a commentary based on the request of one who is immoral, wicked, or shameless? No, it is not improper. The Elder’s words cannot be rejected; rather, it was said to show that the Elder is of such qualities that what he requested should be undertaken with respect.

Nāmenāti attano guṇanāmena. Saddalakkhaṇasubhato, vinicchayasubhato, viññeyyasubhato ca subhaṃ.

By name means by the name of one's own quality. It is beautiful in the characteristic of sound, beautiful in discernment, and beautiful in what is to be understood.

Ganthārambhakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the introduction to the text is finished.

Nidānavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Nidāna.

“Āvikatā hissa phāsu hoti, tatthāyasmante pucchāmi…pe… tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti vatvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidāna”ntiādinā nayena vuttaṃ. Ettheva yāvatatiyānusāvanakathāvasāne atha [M 0.0003] kho uddesakāle “āvikatā hissa phāsu hotī”ti vatvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidānaṃ. Tatthāyasmante pucchāmī”tiādinā nayena āgataṃ. Uposathakkhandhakepi evameva āgataṃ. Tattha pubbe vuttaṃ pacchā āgatasuttena virujjhati. Tasmā yathā na virujjhati, tathā upaparikkhitvā gahetabbaṃ. Evaṃ na virujjhatīti eke. Kathaṃ? “Āvikatā hissa phāsu hotī”ti vatvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidānaṃ. Tatthāyasmante pucchāmī”tiādinā suuddiṭṭhaṃ hotīti etaṃ uddesalakkhaṇaṃ idhāpi khandhakepi vuttattā. Tasmā “phāsu hotī”ti vatvā “tatthāyasmante pucchāmī”ti vuttaṭṭhāne avuttampi ānetvā gahetabbaṃ. Kasmā? Idha nidānaṃ na dassitaṃ, uddeso uddesakāle uddisitabbalakkhaṇassa tattha vuttattā. Apica “nidānuddeso”ti padaṃ uddharitvā nidānuddesaṃ dassetukāmopi “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… āvikatā hissa phāsu hotī”ti pāṭhavasena āgataṃ nidānaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā upari aṭṭhakathāvasena yojetabbaṃ pāḷiṃ idha yojetvā “tatthāyasmante pucchāmi…pe… dhārayāmī”ti nidānapāḷiṃ paripuṇṇaṃ katvā puna “tattha nidānuddeso”ti uddhaṭapadavasena saṅkhepato nidānuddesalakkhaṇaṃ dassetuṃ “evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti vatvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ, tasmā evaṃ upari ca khandhake ca, atha kho uddesakāle “āvikatā hissa [V 0.0004] phāsu hotī”ti vatvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidānaṃ. Tatthāyasmante pucchāmī”tiādi nidānuddesova dassito, na nidānaṃ.

"It is agreeable to him when it is declared; therefore, venerable ones, I ask… (and so on)… Silence; thus I hold it." Having said this, "The Nidāna has been recited, venerable ones," and so on, was stated in that manner. Here, up to the end of the third proclamation, then at the time of recitation, having said "It is agreeable to him when it is declared," "The Nidāna has been recited, venerable ones; therefore, venerable ones, I ask… (and so on)," it comes in this manner. In the Uposatha Khandhaka as well, it comes in the same way. There, what was said earlier contradicts what comes later in the sutta. Therefore, it should be examined and understood in a way that does not contradict. Thus, some say it does not contradict. How? Having said "It is agreeable to him when it is declared," "The Nidāna has been recited, venerable ones; therefore, venerable ones, I ask… (and so on)" means it is well-recited—this is the characteristic of recitation, as it is stated both here and in the Khandhaka. Therefore, having said "It is agreeable," at the place where "Therefore, venerable ones, I ask" is stated, even if it is not explicitly said, it should be brought in and understood. Why? Here, the Nidāna itself is not shown, because the characteristic of what is to be recited at the time of recitation is stated there. Moreover, even if one wishes to show the Nidāna recitation by extracting the term "Nidāna recitation," having completed the Nidāna that comes in the text, such as "May the Sangha listen to me, venerable sirs… (and so on)… it is agreeable to him when it is declared," and having connected the Pali here according to the commentary, completing the Nidāna Pali with "therefore, venerable ones, I ask… (and so on)… thus I hold it," then again, to briefly show the characteristic of the Nidāna recitation by means of the extracted term "Nidāna recitation," having said "thus I hold it," "The Nidāna has been recited, venerable ones," and so on, is stated. Therefore, both above and in the Khandhaka, then at the time of recitation, having said "It is agreeable to him when it is declared," "The Nidāna has been recited, venerable ones; therefore, venerable ones, I ask… (and so on)" only the Nidāna recitation is shown, not the Nidāna itself.

Savanāṇattivacananti ettha saṅghanavakatarena vattuṃ ayuttanti ce? Yuttameva. “Pātimokkhuddesakena evaṃ vattabba”nti bhagavatā vuttattā bhagavatova āṇatti, na uddesakassa. Idha navakataravasena vuttaṃ. Theropi pana uddisituṃ labhatīti dassanatthaṃ “therādhikaṃ pātimokkha”nti vuttaṃ. Iminā suttena navakataro na labhatīti ce? Taṃ dassetuṃ “yo tattha bhikkhū”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Regarding the statement, "announcement of listening"—if it is asked whether it is inappropriate for a junior monk to speak here, it is indeed appropriate. Because the Blessed One said, "The one who recites the Pātimokkha should speak thus," it is the Blessed One’s instruction, not the reciter’s. Here, it is stated in terms of the junior monk. But, to show that an elder also has the right to recite, it is said, "The elder has precedence in the Pātimokkha." If it is asked whether this rule implies that a junior monk does not have the right, to address this, "Whatever bhikkhu there…" etc., is said.

Yathā catuvaggena ṭhapetvā upasampadāpavāraṇāabbhānāni sabbaṃ saṅghakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, evaṃ “atirekavīsativaggena imaṃ nāma kammaṃ kātabba”nti avatvā atirekavacanattā aññaṃ atthaṃ sūceti, kiṃ tanti “catuvaggādinā”tiādi. Tañhi tehi eva siddhaṃ. Kathaṃ? Catuvaggena upasampadāpavāraṇā…pe… vīsativaggena [M 0.0004] na kiñci saṅghakammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti. Ettha “dasavaggena abbhānakammamattaṃ ṭhapetvā”ti vadantena catupañcavaggena karaṇīyānipi dasavaggena kātuṃ anuññātāni. Tasmā atirekena vaṭṭatīti dīpitaṃ, “ṭhapetvā”ti vacanena ūnatarena na vaṭṭatīti dīpitameva. Tasmā na vattabbaṃ atirekavīsativaggoti ce? Vattabbameva. Catupañcavaggena kattabbaṃ chasattaaṭṭhanavavaggena kātabbanti ca, dasavaggena kātabbaṃ ekādasadvādasa…pe… ekūnavīsativaggena kātabbanti ca dīpitaṃ. Ūnatarena na vaṭṭatīti dīpitaṃ pākaṭato. Sabbappakārena pana atirekavīsatianatirekavīsativagge vuttepi dīpitaṃ hotīti vajirabuddhittherena likhitaṃ. Ito paṭṭhāya “likhita”nti vutte vajirabuddhittherenāti gahetabbaṃ.

Just as all Saṅgha acts can be performed with a group of four, except for higher ordination, the invitation ceremony, and rehabilitation, so too, without stating, 'This act should be done with a group of more than twenty,' the mention of 'more' implies another meaning. What is that? It is explained by the phrase 'with a group of four, etc.' For that is already established by those examples. How? With a group of four, higher ordination, the invitation ceremony... and so on... with a group of twenty, any Saṅgha act is permissible. Here, when one says, 'except for the act of rehabilitation by a group of ten,' it is implied that acts requiring groups of four or five are also permitted to be done by a group of ten. Therefore, it is clarified that it is permissible with more, while the phrase 'except' clarifies that it is not permissible with less. So, should one not say 'with a group of more than twenty'? It should indeed be said. It is clarified that acts to be done by groups of four or five may also be done by groups of six, seven, eight, or nine, and that acts to be done by a group of ten may be done by groups of eleven, twelve... up to nineteen. That it is not permissible with less is clearly explained. In every way, however, it is clarified even when speaking of a group of more than twenty or not more than twenty, as written by the Elder Vajirabuddhi. From here onward, when 'written' is mentioned, it should be understood as by the Elder Vajirabuddhi.

Sace anuposathepi vaṭṭeyya, “uposathaṃ kareyyā”ti na vadeyya, yasmā anuposathe kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, tasmā “ajjuposatho”ti vatvā puna “uposathaṃ kareyyā”ti vuttaṃ. “Pacchimakattikapuṇṇamā evā”ti avadhāraṇaṃ tato paraṃ pavāraṇādivasassa natthitāya kataṃ. Uddhaṃ pakatiuposathe vuttena pakaticārittena saddhiṃ idampi.

If it were permissible even on a non-Uposatha day, one would not say, 'Let us perform the Uposatha,' because it is not permissible to perform it on a non-Uposatha day. Therefore, having said, 'Today is the Uposatha,' it is then said, 'Let us perform the Uposatha.' The emphasis, 'only on the last full moon of Kattika,' is made because after that there is no day for the invitation ceremony and so on. This is also in accordance with the normal custom mentioned above concerning the regular Uposatha.

“Nimittena nimittaṃ sambandhitvā”ti na vattabbaṃ “tividhasampattiyuttā”ti vuttattāti ce? Vattabbameva. Kasmā? Tividhasampatti nāma nimittasampatti, parisāsampatti, kammavācāsampattītiādiṃ vatvā “nimittasampatti nāma pabbatanimittaṃ, pāsāṇanimitta”ntiādi [V 0.0005] vuttaṃ, na nimittena nimittasambandhanaṃ vuttaṃ. Apica “tividhasampattiyuttā”ti sampayogaṅgesu dassetvā puna tameva pahānaṅgesu dassetuṃ “nimittena nimittaṃ sambandhitvā”ti vuttaṃ. Nadisamuddajātassaresu sammatasīmāto kammāni na vipajjanti udakukkhepasīmattāti “vipattisīmāyo nāmā”ti kasmā vuttāti ce? Sesalakkhaṇāni sampādetvā nadiyaṃ sīmāya baddhāya udakapariyantaṃ katvā sīmāgatattā puna taṃ nadiṃ anto katvā taḷāke kate sace tassā sīmāya kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭeyya, sīmāto kammāni na vipajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā pana evaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, tasmā “udakukkhepasīmattā”ti vuttaṃ akāraṇaṃ.

If it is asked, 'Should it not be said, "having connected a sign by means of a sign," because it has been stated, "endowed with threefold suitability"?' It should indeed be said. Why? Because having stated, 'Threefold suitability means suitability of the sign, suitability of the assembly, and suitability of the formal act,' and so on, it is then said, 'Suitability of the sign means a mountain sign, a rock sign,' and so forth, but the connecting of a sign by means of a sign is not mentioned. Furthermore, having shown 'endowed with threefold suitability' among the factors of conjunction, it is again stated, 'having connected a sign by means of a sign,' in order to show the same among the factors of disjunction. If it is asked, 'In rivers, oceans, and natural lakes, acts are not invalidated from an agreed boundary on account of it being a water-throw boundary, so why is it said, "these are called boundaries of failure"?' Having fulfilled the remaining characteristics, if a boundary were fixed in a river by marking the water's edge, and because it has become a boundary, that river were then enclosed to create a pond, and if it were permissible to perform an act within that boundary, the acts would not be invalidated by the boundary. But since it is not permissible to do so, therefore the reason given, 'because of the water-throw boundary,' is baseless.

Vīsativaggakaraṇīyattā saṅghakammassa kammārahena saddhiṃ ekavīsati bhikkhū nisīdituṃ na sakkontī”ti vuttaṃ, sukhanisajjāvasena nisīditunti adhippāyo. “Parimaṇḍalākārena nisīditu”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tiyojanaṃ atikkamitvāti majjhe ṭhatvā diyaḍḍhaṃ katvā tiyojanaṃ. Koṇato [M 0.0005] hi koṇaṃ tiyojanaṃ atikkāmeti, āpattiñca āpajjati, sīmā ca asīmā hoti. Kittetvāti nimittāni sampannānipi aññamaññanāmavipariyāyena, animittānaṃ nāmehi ca kittetvāti attho.

It is said that because a Saṅgha act is to be done by a group of twenty, twenty-one bhikkhus, together with the one qualified for the act, are not able to sit down, the intention being that they sit comfortably. In the commentary, it is said, 'They should sit in a circular formation.' 'Having exceeded three yojanas' means that standing in the middle and measuring one and a half yojanas on each side makes three yojanas. For if from corner to corner it exceeds three yojanas, an offense is incurred, and the boundary becomes a non-boundary. The meaning of 'having announced' is that even when the signs are established, one announces them by an interchange of their names, and by the names of non-signs.

Rāsikataṃ paṃsupi rukkhesu jātesu suddhapaṃsupabbato hoti. Guḷapiṇḍaparimāṇo thūlatāya, na tulagaṇanāya. Bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhito”ti iminā kuṭasarāvādīsu ropitaṃ paṭikkhipati, tato apanetvā pana taṅkhaṇampi bhūmiyaṃ ropito vaṭṭati. Navamūlasākhāniggamanaṃ pana akāraṇaṃ. Khandhaṃ chinditvā ropite pana etaṃ yujjati. Sūcidaṇḍakappamāṇo kaniṭṭhaṅguliparimāṇamatto. “Aṭṭhaṅgulubbedho”ti iminā ubbedho paricchinno hoti, “govisāṇamatto”ti iminā pariṇāho. “Evaṃ santepi govisāṇapariṇāhe paricchedo natthi, tasmā khuddakopi mahantopi vaṭṭati evāti vadanti.

Even a piled-up heap of dust, when trees grow on it, becomes a pure dust-hill. The size of a lump of molasses is in terms of thickness, not by weighing or counting. 'Established on the ground'—by this is rejected what is planted in pots or bowls, but if removed from there and planted on the ground at that very moment, it is acceptable. The emergence of new roots and branches, however, is not a requirement. But if the trunk is cut and planted, this is suitable. The size of a needle’s shaft is about the size of the little finger. 'Eight finger-breadths in height'—by this the height is defined; 'the size of a cow’s horn'—by this the circumference. 'Even so, for the circumference of a cow's horn there is no fixed limit; therefore, they say, whether small or large, it is acceptable.'

Jātassare paripuṇṇameva udakaṃ nimittūpagaṃ disvā aparipuṇṇaṃ antarā ṭhitibhūtaṃ “jātassare sammatā”ti vuttaṃ vipattiṃ na āpajjatīti “nadiyā sammatā, samudde sammatā, jātassare sammatā”ti etthāpi loṇī na gahitā. Baddhasīmaṃ vā nadisamuddajātassare vā anokkamitvāti etthāpi “nadiyā vā, bhikkhave, samudde vā jātassare vā”ti (mahāva. 147) etthāpi na gahitā. Tasmā loṇī na abaddhasīmāti ce? Abaddhasīmāva. “Yopi nadiṃ vā samuddaṃ vā bhinditvā nikkhantaudakena kato sobbho etaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayampi [V 0.0006] jātassaroyevā”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) vuttattā jātassaraggahaṇena gahitāti tattha tattha avuttā. “Yāvatikā tasmiṃ gāmakhette”ti vuttattā aññampi gāmaṃ anto katvā samānasaṃvāsakasīmāsammannanakāle tasmiṃ gāme bhikkhū āgacchantu vā mā vā, vaṭṭati. Avippavāsasīmāsammannanakāle āgantabbameva.

In a natural lake, whether the water is seen as full and serving as a sign, or as incomplete, or as being in an intermediate state, what is called 'accepted in a natural lake' does not lead to failure. Thus, in the statement 'accepted in a river, accepted in the sea, accepted in a natural lake,' a salt-pan is not included. And in the phrase 'without encroaching on a fixed boundary, or a river, sea, or natural lake,' and also in 'whether in a river, monks, or in the sea, or in a natural lake' (Mahāvagga 147), it is still not included. Therefore, if it is asked whether a salt-pan is not an unfixed boundary, it is indeed an unfixed boundary. Because it is stated, "Even a pool created by water that breaks through a river or the sea and flows out—if it attains this characteristic, this too is a natural lake" (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Nidānavannana), it is included by the term 'natural lake,' though not explicitly mentioned in each context. Since it is stated, "As far as that village territory extends," even if another village is included within it, at the time of determining a common-communion boundary, whether bhikkhus come to that village or not, it is valid. At the time of determining a non-separation boundary, they must indeed come.

Agamanapathesūti ettha ekadivasena gantvā paccāgantuṃ asakkuṇeyyaṭṭhāneti vadanti, baddhasīmābhāvaṃ paṭikkhipitvāti attho.

Regarding 'on impassable paths,' here they say it refers to a place where one is unable to go and return in a single day; the meaning is that this asserts the existence of a fixed boundary.

“Samantā udakukkhepā”ti vuttattā sabbadisāsu gahetabbamevāti ce? Yato labbhati, tato gahetabbo “yasmiṃ padese pakativīciyo ottharitvā [M 0.0006] saṇṭhahanti, tato paṭṭhāya kappiyabhūmi, tattha ṭhatvā uposathādikammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttattā. Anubandho aḍḍhamāso anvaḍḍhamāso, aḍḍhamāsassa vā anu. Yo pana kenaci antamaso tiracchānenapi khaṇitvā akatoti adhippāyo.

If it is asked, 'Since it is said, "a water-throw all around," must it be taken in all directions?' It should be taken from wherever it is obtained, because it is said, 'Starting from the place where the natural waves spread and settle, that is the suitable ground. Standing there, it is permissible to perform the Uposatha and other acts.' The sequence is a fortnight, every fortnight, or following the fortnight. The intention, however, is that it is not something made by being dug by anyone, not even by an animal.

“Aññaṃ tattakaṃyeva paricchedaṃ anatikkamitvā ṭhitopi kammaṃ kopetī”ti vuttattā atikkamitvā ṭhito na kopetīti dīpitameva hotīti upatissatthero, taṃ pana “dvinnaṃ udakukkhepānaṃ antare añño eko udakukkhepo upacāratthāya ṭhapetabbo”ti vacanena virujjhati. Samantapāsādikāyañhi “aññaṃ tattakaṃyevā”ti padaṃ natthi. Tasmā tassādhippāyo pariyesitabbo. Antoudakukkhepasīmāya upacāratthāya ṭhapitaṃ udakukkhepaparicchedaṃ anatikkamitvāti attho gahetabbo. Therena aññathā papañcitvā likhitaṃ.

The Elder Upatissa stated: 'Because it was said, "Even one standing without exceeding another boundary of just that same size invalidates the act," it is thereby clarified that one standing beyond it does not invalidate it.' But that conflicts with the statement, 'Between two water-throws, another single water-throw should be established for the purpose of proximity.' For in the Samantapāsādikā, the phrase 'another of just that same size' does not exist. Therefore, its intended meaning should be investigated. The meaning should be understood as: 'without exceeding the limit of the water-throw that was established for the purpose of proximity to the inner water-throw boundary.' The Elder wrote, elaborating on it differently.

“Sabhāgavatthunā lahukāpatti”nti vuttattā sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ ārocetuṃ vaṭṭatīti ce? Na vaṭṭati desanāgāminiṃ sandhāya idha vuttattā. Tasmā eva samuccayakkhandhake “sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ āpannassa pana santike āvikātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace āvikaroti, āpatti āvikatā hoti, dukkaṭā pana na muccatī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) vuttaṃ. Yathā saṅghena “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… paṭikarissatī”ti vatvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ labhati, evaṃ tīhi dvīhipi aññaṃ suddhaṃ passitvā “paṭikarissāmā”ti vatvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Ekenāpi “parisuddhaṃ labhitvā paṭikarissāmī”ti ābhogaṃ katvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti. Aṭṭhakathāyampi “sāmanto bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyoti ettha sabhāgo eva vattabbo. Visabhāgassa hi vuccamāne bhaṇḍanakalahasaṅghabhedādīnipi honti, tasmā tassa avatvā ito vuṭṭhahitvā [V 0.0007] paṭikarissāmī”ti ābhogaṃ katvā uposatho kātabboti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vutta”nti vatvā tassa appaṭikkhittattā vaṭṭatīti dīpitameva. “Yadā aññaṃ suddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpattikaṃ passissati, tadā tassa santike”ti vuttattā lahukasseva anuññātattā samuccayakkhandhake vuttattā sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ pana ñattiyā ārocetvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati.

If it is asked, 'Since it is said, "a light offense in a similar case," is it permissible to announce a Saṅghādisesa offense to one of a similar class?' It is not permissible, because here it is said with reference to an offense that is cleared by confession. Therefore, in the Samuccayakkhandhaka, it is stated: 'For one who has committed a Saṅghādisesa offense, it is not permissible to reveal it in the presence of one of a similar class. If one does reveal it, the offense is revealed, but one is not freed from the dukkaṭa' (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 102). Just as the Saṅgha is permitted to perform the Uposatha after saying, 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me… will make amends,' so too, for three or two, upon seeing another pure monk, it is permissible to perform the Uposatha after saying, 'We will make amends.' Even for a single monk, it is permissible to perform the Uposatha after having resolved, 'Having found a pure one, I will make amends.' In the commentary also, it is explained: 'Regarding "A neighboring monk should be addressed thus," here, only one of a similar class should be spoken to. For if one speaks to one of a different class, quarrels, disputes, and schisms in the Saṅgha may arise. Therefore, without speaking to him, the Uposatha should be performed after having resolved, "Having risen from here, I will make amends." This is stated in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā.' And since this is not rejected, it is indeed shown to be permissible. Because it is said, 'When one sees another pure monk who is without offense, then in his presence,' and because only a light offense is permitted, as stated in the Samuccayakkhandhaka, it is not permissible to perform the Uposatha after announcing a Saṅghādisesa offense to one of a similar class by means of a motion.

Devabrahmā [M 0.0007] pana “tiracchānagato”ti padaṃ ṭhapetvā yena kenaci padena asaṅgahitāpi iminā saṅgahitāti dassanatthaṃ “yassa upasampadā paṭikkhittā”ti vuttaṃ.

But Devabrahma, in order to show that even those not included by any other term are included by this, and leaving aside the term 'animal,' said, 'one for whom higher ordination is forbidden.'

“Cātumāsiniyaṃ pana pavāritānaṃ santike anupagatena vā chinnavassena vā vuṭṭhavassena vā”ti avatvā “anupagatena vā chinnavassena vā”ti ettakameva vuttaṃ. Vuṭṭhavasso pana tasmiṃ kāle anupagatattā “anupagato”ti saṅkhyaṃ gatoti. Sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya sabbe vuṭṭhahitvā gate sannipātetuṃ na sakkā, ekacce sannipātetvā pārisuddhiṃ ārocetuṃ vaṭṭatīti vadanti. Kasmā? Ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā kattabbasaṅghakammābhāvā vaggaṃ na hotīti. Pavāraṇāyapi eseva nayo. Ayañhettha viseso – sace purimikāya upagatehi pacchimikāya upagatā thokatarā ceva honti samasamā ca, saṅghapavāraṇāya ca gaṇaṃ pūrenti, saṅghapavāraṇāvasena ñatti ṭhapetabbāti. “Ekova bhikkhu hoti…pe… aññesaṃ anāgatabhāvaṃ ñatvā”ti vuttattā adhiṭṭhānuposathaṃ sīmaṃ pavisitvā kātuṃ na sakkāti vadanti.

But regarding the four-month Pavāraṇā, instead of saying, 'in the presence of those who have performed Pavāraṇā, by one who has not arrived, or by one whose rains-residence is broken, or by one whose rains-residence is completed,' only 'by one who has not arrived or by one whose rains-residence is broken' was said. But one who has completed the rains-residence, since at that time he has not arrived, is counted as 'one who has not arrived.' When the entire assembly has risen and departed, it is not possible to gather them all. Some say it is permissible to gather a few and announce purity. Why? Because, apart from establishing a motion, there is no Saṅgha act to be done, it does not constitute an incomplete group. This same principle applies also to the Pavāraṇā. Herein lies the distinction: if those who have come for the later Pavāraṇā are fewer than or equal to those who have come for the earlier one, and they complete the quorum for the Saṅgha Pavāraṇā, then a motion should be established for the purpose of a Saṅgha Pavāraṇā. Because it is said, 'There is only one monk… having known the non-arrival of others…,' some say it is not possible to perform the Adhiṭṭhāna Uposatha after entering the boundary.

“Kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakicca”nti idaṃ na ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā vattabbaṃ. Tañhi ñattito puretarameva karīyati. Tasmā “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakiccaṃ, yadi saṅghassa pattakalla”nti vattabbaṃ siyāti. Tathāpi na vattabbaṃ. Na hi taṃ ñattiyā anto karīyatīti. Evaṃ sante netaṃ vattabbanti āpajjati payojanābhāvāti ce? Na, yathāgataṭṭhāne eva vattabbato, parapadāpekkhatāyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Idaṃ pubbakiccaṃ akatvā uposathakammaṃ karonto saṅgho, puggalo vā ṭhapanakkhettātikkame āpajjati. Tasmiñhi khette atikkante sammajjanādikaraṇe āpattimokkho na hoti uposathakammato pubbe kattabbakammākaraṇapaccayattā tassā āpattiyā. Na sā kammapariyosānāpekkhā etthāgatasampajānamusāvādāpatti viya, tasmā pātimokkhuddesako bhikkhu “pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocethā”ti vattukāmo paṭhamameva pārisuddhāpārisuddhipaccayaṃ pubbakiccaṃ sarāpeti. Tañhi kataṃ pārisuddhipaccayo hoti, akataṃ apārisuddhipaccayo. Teneva ubhayāpekkhādhippāyena kataṃ, na katanti avatvā “kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakicca”miccevāha. Tattha akatapakkhe tāva pārisuddhiārocanakkamanidassanatthaṃ parato [M 0.0008] “yassa [V 0.0008] siyā āpatti, so āvikareyyā”ti ca, katapakkhe “asantiyā āpattiyā tuṇhī bhavitabba”nti ca vakkhati.

The question, ‘What is the preliminary duty of the Saṅgha?’ is not to be said after establishing the motion. For that is done even before the motion. Therefore, one might think it should be said: ‘Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. What is the preliminary duty of the Saṅgha? If the Saṅgha is ready.’ Even so, it should not be said thus, for it is not included within the motion. If that is so, does it follow that this should not be said, as it has no purpose? No, because it must be said in its proper place; it is said to be dependent on the words that follow. A Saṅgha or an individual who performs the Uposatha ceremony without doing this preliminary duty incurs an offense by transgressing the established domain. For when that domain is transgressed, there is no release from the offense related to sweeping and so forth, because that offense is due to the non-performance of the duties that should be done before the Uposatha ceremony. That offense is not dependent on the completion of the act, unlike the offense of intentional false speech mentioned here. Therefore, the monk reciting the Pātimokkha, wishing to say, 'Venerable Sirs, declare your purity,' first reminds them of the preliminary duty, which is the condition for purity or impurity. For when it is done, it is a condition for purity; when not done, it is a condition for impurity. For this reason, with the intention of covering both possibilities, without saying ‘it is done’ or ‘it is not done,’ he simply says, ‘What is the preliminary duty of the Saṅgha?’ Then, in the case where it has not been done, to show the procedure for announcing purity, it will be said later, ‘Whoever has an offense, let him reveal it.’ And in the case where it has been done, it will be said, ‘If there is no offense, one should remain silent.’

“Sabbantimena paricchedena catūhi bhikkhūhi sannipatitvā”ti ca, “uposathakaraṇatthaṃ sannipatite saṅghe bahi…pe… adentena chando dātabbo”ti ca vadanti. Asannipatitepi pana vaṭṭati. Idañhi chandadānasamayadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Uposathakaraṇatthaṃ sannipatite saṅghe bahi uposathaṃ katvā āgatassa kattabbākāradassanatthañca vuttaṃ. Padhānagharavāsino padhānagharaṃ pavisitukāmā attano sabhāgabhikkhūnaṃ chandaṃ datvā sace saṅgho sannipatati, “mayhaṃ chando ārocetabbo”ti vatvā padhānagharaṃ pavisanti. Ayaṃ sīhaḷadīpe payogo. Ārocentena pana sannipatite ārocetabbaṃ. Pañcasu bhikkhūsu ekasmiṃ vihāre vasantesu ekassa chandapārisuddhiṃ āharitvā catunnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ anuññātattā sannipatite chando gahetabbo ārocetabboti vacanaṃ niratthakaṃ viya. “Theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānātīti (mahāva. 165) vacanato sāmaṇerena āhaṭāpi vaṭṭati. Kammaṃ na kopetī”ti ca, “sace pubbe chandaṃ datvā bahisīmāgato puna pavisati, pacchā chandaggahaṇakiccaṃ natthi, tassa payogo sīmāsammutivasena veditabbo”ti ca “chandadāne tikkhattuṃ vacane idaṃ payojanaṃ – paṭhamaṃ samaggabhāvaṃ, dutiyaṃ pacchā vidhātabbabhāvaṃ, tatiyaṃ chandahārakassa dukkaṭamocanaṃ dīpetī”ti (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 164) ca likhitaṃ. Biḷālasaṅkhalikābaddhāva hoti antogehe eva sampayojanattā, yathā sā na katthaci gacchati, tathā sāpi na katthaci gacchatīti adhippāyo. Itarathā visesanaṃ niratthakaṃ hotīti ācariyena gahitaṃ.

‘At the very least, four bhikkhus having assembled,’ and ‘When the Saṅgha has assembled for the purpose of performing the Uposatha, consent should be given by one who is outside…,’ they say. However, it is also valid even if they have not assembled. This was stated to show the time for giving consent. It was also stated to show the proper procedure for one who, having performed the Uposatha outside, returns when the Saṅgha has assembled to perform the Uposatha. Those dwelling in the principal dwelling, wishing to enter it, give their consent to their fellow bhikkhus. If the Saṅgha assembles, they say, 'My consent should be announced,' and then enter the principal dwelling. This is the practice on the island of Sri Lanka. However, the one announcing it should do so when the Saṅgha has assembled. Since it is permitted for the Pātimokkha to be recited to four bhikkhus after bringing the consent and purity of one, when five bhikkhus are dwelling in one monastery, the statement that consent should be taken and announced when they have assembled seems somewhat meaningless. Based on the passage, 'one who dwells by theft acknowledges...' (Mahāva. 165), it is also valid if brought by a novice. It is also written: 'The act is not vitiated,' and 'If one gave consent beforehand and then went outside the boundary, but later re-enters, there is no need to take consent again; his case should be understood in accordance with the agreement on the boundary,' and 'Regarding the threefold utterance in giving consent, this is the purpose: the first indicates unity, the second indicates what is to be arranged afterwards, and the third indicates the release of the consent-bearer from a dukkaṭa offense' (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 164). It is like a cat bound by a chain, because it serves its purpose only inside the house; just as it does not go anywhere, so too this one does not go anywhere—this is the meaning. Otherwise, the qualification would be meaningless—this was understood by the teacher.

“Na hi taṃ akatvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti pubbe dassitattā “idampi hi ubhaya”nti kasmā vuttanti ce? Sesāni therena āṇattena kātabbāni dassitāni, ime pana dve therena vā pātimokkhuddesakena vā ñattiṭṭhapanakena vā yena vā tena vā kātabbānīti ca, sammajjanādīni tattha tattha tādisāni payojanāni nipphādenti, ime pana dve tattha tattha na kiñci kammaṃ sādhenti, tasmā “kiṃ iminā”ti avatvā kātabbamevāti dassetuñca “idampi hi ubhaya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. “Āyasmantānaṃ pāde vandatī”ti [M 0.0009] gaṇavasena vatvā puggalavasena na vuttaṃ tena ārocetabbassa aññassa abhāvā.

If it is asked, 'Since it was previously shown that “It is not proper to perform the Uposatha without doing that,” why then is it said, “This too is indeed both”?' The remaining tasks were shown as to be done by the elder’s command; but these two must be done either by the elder, by the reciter of the Pātimokkha, by the one who places the motion, or by anyone at all. And sweeping and the like fulfill such purposes in their respective places, but these two accomplish no task in those places. Therefore, to show that it must simply be done without saying, ‘What is the use of this?’, it was said, ‘This too is indeed both,’ and so on. ‘He pays homage to the feet of the venerable ones’ is said with reference to the group, not with reference to an individual, because there is no other to be informed.

Saṅghassa uddiṭṭhaṃ hotīti saṅghena uddiṭṭhaṃ hotīti attho. Samaggassa hi saṅghassāti ettha samaggabhāvassa kāyasāmaggikāraṇattā natthi dosoti ce? Taṃ na, uddesepi savanepi samaggabhāvassa [V 0.0009] icchitabbattā. “Suṇātu me, bhante”ti hi iminā cittasāmaggiṃ dīpeti savane sabbehi ekībhūtabhāvato.

‘It has been recited to the Sangha’ means it has been recited by the Sangha. If it is said, 'Regarding the phrase “of the harmonious Sangha,” is it that there is no fault because the state of harmony is the cause of bodily harmony?' That is not so, because a state of harmony is desired in the recitation and in the listening as well. For by ‘Venerable sirs, let the Sangha listen to me,’ it indicates mental harmony in the listening, from the state of all having become one.

Sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjatīti ettha anādariyavasena āpajjanto eva alajjī hoti, na itaroti. Āpattiṃ parigūhatīti ettha lajjāya parigūhanto alajjī na hoti, ‘kiṃ iminā’ti anādariyavasena parigūhanto hotī”ti ca likhitaṃ.

Regarding ‘intentionally commits an offense’—here, one who commits an offense out of disrespect is indeed shameless, not the other. Regarding ‘conceals an offense’—here, one who conceals out of shame is not shameless; but one who conceals out of disrespect, thinking, ‘What is the use of this?’, is shameless. This is written.

“Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhāna”nti na vattabbaṃ, “channa”nti vattabbanti ce? Sattannamevāti vattabbaṃ. Pārājikāpattiṃ āpanno hi sace attano sāpattikabhāvaṃ pakāseti, saṅghassa ca uposatho sampajjati, tassa ca gihibhāvena vā sāmaṇerabhāvena vā suddhi hotīti.

If it is said, 'It should not be said “of the seven classes of offenses”; rather, it should be said “of six”?' It must be said ‘of seven.’ For if one who has committed a pārājika offense reveals their state of having offended, the Sangha’s Uposatha is accomplished, and for that person, purification occurs by way of becoming a layperson or a novice.

Ekacce ācariyā nāma dhammabhāriko kira ācariyo. Kasmā evaṃ vuttanti ce? Yāvatatiyānusāvanā nāma tikkhattuṃ vacanaṃ. Tathā pāṭhe anāgatattā kevalaṃ “yāvatatiyaṃ anusāvita”nti padameva disvā “yassa siyā āpatti, so āvikareyyā”ti idaṃ “sace āpattiṃ āpannā, āvikarothā”ti imamatthaṃ dīpeti. “Asantiyā āpattiyā tuṇhī bhavitabba”nti idampi tamevatthaṃ dīpeti. “Tuṇhībhāvena kho panāyasmante parisuddhāti vedissāmī”ti idampi tamevāti evamatthaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ kira.

Some teachers, it is said, are teachers known as 'bearers of the Dhamma.' If it is asked why this is said: ‘The announcement up to the third time’ means speaking three times. Since this does not appear in the text in that way, seeing only the phrase ‘announced up to the third time,’ they explain that ‘Let him who has an offense reveal it’ conveys this meaning: ‘If you have committed an offense, reveal it.’ ‘If there is no offense, one should remain silent’—this also conveys the same meaning. ‘By your silence, venerable ones, I shall know you to be pure’—this too conveys the same. It is said that it was spoken having understood the meaning in this way.

Apareti atthadassitthero kira. Etaṃ sandhāyāti ettha “sakimpi anusāvita”nti padassa vacanena tikkhattuṃ anusāvanā kātabbāti ettakameva dīpitaṃ viya dissati.

‘Others’—this means the Elder Atthadassī, it is said. Referring to this, it seems that by the phrase ‘announced even once,’ only this much is indicated: that the announcement should be made three times.

Imamatthaṃ sandhāya vuttanti kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Ayamettha ācariyaparamparābhato vinicchayo”ti vuttaṃ.

If it is asked, 'How is it known that this was said with reference to this meaning?' It is because it is said, ‘This here is the decision handed down through the lineage of teachers.’

“Saramānenā”ti [M 0.0010] iminā sampajānamusāvādassa sacittakattaṃ dasseti. Saṅghamajjhe vātiādi lakkhaṇavacanaṃ kira. Saṅghuposathakaraṇatthaṃ saṅghamajjhe ce nisinno, tasmiṃ saṅghamajjhe āvikātabbā. Gaṇuposathakaraṇatthañce gaṇamajjhe nisinno, tasmiṃ gaṇamajjhe. Ekasseva santike ce pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kattukāmo, tasmiṃ ekapuggale āvikātabbāti, etena na kevalaṃ saṅghamajjhe evāyaṃ musāvādo sambhavati, atha kho ettha vuttalakkhaṇena asatipi “pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocethā”tiādividhāne gaṇuposathepi sāpattiko hutvā uposathaṃ [V 0.0010] kattukāmo anārocetvā tuṇhībhūtova ce karoti, ayaṃ sampajānamusāvādāpattiṃ āpajjatīti imassatthassa āvikaraṇato lakkhaṇavacanaṃ kiretanti vuttanti takkikā. Aññathā “gaṇamajjhe vā”ti na vattabbanti tesaṃ adhippāyo. Ārocanādhippāyavasena vuttanti ācariyassa takko. Ārocento hi “saṅghassa ārocemī”ti adhippāyena āvikaronto saṅghamajjhe āvikaroti nāma, ubhatopasse nisinnānaṃ ārocento gaṇamajjhe āvikaroti nāma, “ekasseva ārocessāmī”ti adhippāyena āvikaronto ekapuggale āvikaroti nāma. Sacepi vematiko hoti…pe… paṭikarissāmīti evaṃ kate yāva vematiko hoti, tāva sabhāgāpattiṃ paṭiggahetuṃ labhati, aññesañca kammānaṃ parisuddho nāma hoti. Puna nibbematiko hutvā desetabbaṃ vā na vāti neva pāḷiyaṃ, na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ atthi, desite pana doso natthi. Tathā ito vuṭṭhahitvā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmīti ettha ca sakalasaṅghe sabhāgāpattiṃ āpanne, vematike cāti likhitaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 169-170).

By ‘remembering,’ it shows the intentional nature of knowingly speaking falsely. The phrase ‘in the midst of the Sangha,’ and so on, is said to be a defining statement. If one is seated in the midst of the Sangha for the purpose of performing the Sangha's Uposatha, it should be disclosed in the midst of that Sangha. If one is seated in the midst of a group for the purpose of performing a group Uposatha, then in the midst of that group. If one wishes to perform the Uposatha of purity in the presence of a single individual, it should be disclosed to that single person. By this it is shown that this false speech does not occur only in the midst of the Sangha. Rather, even in a group Uposatha where the procedure described here, such as ‘Venerable sirs, declare your purity,’ is not present, if one who has an offense and wishes to perform the Uposatha does so while remaining silent without declaring it, this person commits the offense of knowingly speaking falsely. Because it reveals this meaning, it is said to be a defining statement—so say the dialecticians. Otherwise, they intend, ‘in the midst of a group’ would not be said. The teacher’s reasoning is that it is stated according to the intention of declaring. For one who declares with the intention, ‘I declare to the Sangha,’ is said to disclose in the midst of the Sangha. One who declares to those seated on both sides is said to disclose in the midst of a group. One who declares with the intention, ‘I will declare to just one,’ is said to disclose to a single person. Even if one is doubtful… when one resolves, ‘I will make amends,’ then for as long as one is doubtful, one is able to undertake the procedure for a common offense and is considered pure with respect to other formal acts. Then, having become free from doubt, whether it must be confessed or not—this is found neither in the Pāli nor in the commentary, but there is no fault in confessing it. Likewise, regarding ‘having arisen from this, I will make amends for that offense,’ it is written that this applies when the entire Sangha has committed a common offense and is doubtful (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 169-170).

Nidānavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Introduction is concluded.

Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

The Pārājika Section

1. Paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the First Pārājika

Idha [M 0.0011][V 0.0011] pana ṭhatvā sikkhāpadānaṃ kamabhedo pakāsetabbo. Kathaṃ – sabbasikkhāpadānaṃ yathāsambhavaṃ desanākkamo, pahānakkamo, paṭipattikkamo, uppattikkamoti catubbidho kamo labbhati. Tattha bhagavatā rājagahe bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujānantena pātimokkhuddesassa yo desanākkamo anuññāto, taṃ desanākkamaṃ anukkamantova mahākassapo paṭhamaṃ pārājikuddesaṃ pucchi, tadanantaraṃ saṅghādisesuddesaṃ, tadanantaraṃ aniyatuddesaṃ, tadanantaraṃ vitthāruddesaṃ. Tadanantaraṃ bhikkhunivibhaṅgañca teneva anukkamena pucchi. Tato paraṃ tayo āpattikkhandhe saṅgahetuṃ vinā gaṇanaparicchedena sekhiyadhamme pucchi. Āpattikkhandhe sabhāgato paṭṭhāya pucchanto vīsatikhandhake pucchi. Nidānuddesantogadhānaṃ vā sarūpena anuddiṭṭhānaṃ pucchanatthaṃ khandhake pucchi. Etena khandhake paññattā thullaccayāpi saṅgahitā honti. Pucchitānukkameneva āyasmā upālitthero byākāsi. Ayamettha desanākkamo. Ubhatovibhaṅgakhandhakato pana uccinitvā tadā parivāro visuṃ pāḷi kato, imameva vacanaṃ sandhāya aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ “eteneva upāyena khandhakaṃ parivārepi āropayiṃsū”tiādi (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.paṭhamamahāsaṅgaītikathā). Apica pāḷiyaṃ “eteneva upāyena ubhatovibhaṅge pucchi. Puṭṭho puṭṭho āyasmā upāli vissajjesī”ti (cūḷava. 439) ettakameva vuttaṃ. Tasmā thero ubhatovibhaṅge eva pucchi. Vissajjanto pana āyasmā upāli niravasesaṃ dassento khandhakaparivāre anto katvā desesi. Gaṇasajjhāyakāle pana tadā khandhakaparivārā visuṃ pāḷi katāti ayamettha desanākkamo.

Now here, the division of the order of the training rules should be explained. How? The order of all the training rules, as is applicable, is found to be fourfold: the order of teaching, the order of abandoning, the order of practice, and the order of arising. In this regard, when the Blessed One at Rājagaha permitted the recitation of the Pātimokkha for the monks, he approved an order of teaching for the Pātimokkha recitation. Following that order of teaching, Mahākassapa first asked about the recitation of the Pārājikas, next the Saṅghādisesas, next the Aniyatas, and next the detailed recitation. After that, he asked about the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga in the same sequence. Then, in order to include the three classes of offenses without enumerating them, he asked about the Sekhiya rules. Asking about the classes of offenses, starting from those of a common nature, he asked about the twenty Khandhakas. He asked about the Khandhakas in order to question matters included within the recitation of the introduction or those not recited in their own form. By this, the Thullaccaya offenses laid down in the Khandhakas are also included. The Venerable Upāli explained in the very same order as he was asked. This is the order of teaching here. However, having selected from the two Vibhaṅgas and the Khandhakas, the Parivāra was then made into a separate Pāli text. With reference to this very statement, it is said in the commentary: ‘By this method, they also placed the Khandhaka in the Parivāra,’ and so on (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1, First Great Council). Moreover, in the Pāli it is said only this much: ‘By this method, he asked about the two Vibhaṅgas. Being asked and asked, the Venerable Upāli answered’ (Cūḷava. 439). Therefore, the elder asked only about the two Vibhaṅgas. But when answering, the Venerable Upāli, showing everything without omission, taught including the Khandhaka and Parivāra within it. At the time of the communal chanting, however, the Khandhaka and Parivāra were then made into separate Pāli texts. This is the order of teaching here.

Yadi evaṃ nidānuddeso paṭhamadesanāti ce? Na, uposathakkhandhake (mahāva. 133) “yāni mayā bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadāni paññattāni, tāni nesaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujāneyya”nti [V 0.0012] vacanato, “yassa siyā āpattī”ti (mahāva. 134) vacanato ca. Akusalābyākatānaṃ āpattīnaṃ diṭṭhadhammasamparāyikāsavaṭṭhāniyattā yathābhūtaṃ sīlasaṃvarakena parivajjanena pahātabbattā pahānakkamopettha sambhavati “tāvadeva cattāri akaraṇīyāni ācikkhitabbānī”ti [M 0.0012] vacanato. Tathā “samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesū”ti (ma. ni. 3.75; vibha. 508) vacanato yathābhūtaṃ ācikkhanasikkhanena paṭipattikkamopi sambhavati. Yathuddesakkamaṃ pariyāpuṇitabbapariyattiatthenāpi paṭipattikkamo, evamimehi tīhi kamehi desetabbānametesaṃ sikkhāpadānaṃ yathāsambhavaṃ uppattikkamo sambhavati. Tathā hi yaṃ yaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ, taṃ taṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha uppanne eva vatthusmiṃ “yā pana bhikkhunī chandaso methunaṃ dhamma”ntiādinā nayena bhikkhunīnampi paññattaṃ. Yato bhikkhunīnaṃ taṃ anuppannapaññatti na siyā, tato anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthīti (pari. 201-202) parivāravacanaṃ na virujjhati. Ettāvatā purimena kamattayena yaṃ paṭhamaṃ desetabbaṃ, taṃ pārājikuddese paṭhamuppannattā methunadhammapārājikaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ desetukāmo āyasmā upālitthero “tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharatī”ti (pārā. 23) vesāliyameva pāpetvā ṭhapesi.

If so, is the recitation of the introduction the first teaching? No, because in the Uposathakkhandhaka it is stated: 'Those training rules that I have laid down for the monks, let them authorize the recitation of them as the Pātimokkha,' and also because of the statement: 'For whom there may be an offense.' Since unwholesome and indeterminate offenses are a basis for the taints pertaining to this life and the next, and must be abandoned through virtuous restraint and avoidance in accordance with reality, the sequence of abandonment is applicable here, as stated: 'At that very time, the four things not to be done should be declared.' Similarly, because of the statement: 'Having undertaken them, one trains in the training rules,' the sequence of practice also arises through teaching and training in accordance with reality. The sequence of practice also arises in the sense of the scriptural learning to be mastered according to the order of recitation. Thus, for these training rules to be taught by these three sequences, the sequence of origination is applicable as appropriate. For example, whatever is common, having arisen concerning a monk, in that very matter the rule is also laid down for nuns in the manner of: 'Whatever nun should willingly engage in sexual intercourse,' and so on. Since for the nuns that would not be a rule promulgated before an occasion for it had arisen, the statement in the Parivāra that 'there is no un-arisen promulgation in that case' is not contradicted. To this extent, the Venerable Upāli Thera, wishing to teach first of all the pārājika offense of sexual intercourse—which is to be taught first according to the preceding three sequences and was the first to arise in the Pārājika recitation—placed it at the very beginning by stating: 'At that time, the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī,' thus situating it in Vesālī itself.

Idāni sabbesaṃ sikkhāpadānaṃ paññāpanavidhānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Kathaṃ? “Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ uddiseyyāthā”ti (pārā. 39, 43) evaṃ sauddesaanuddesabhedato duvidhaṃ. Tattha pātimokkhe sarūpato āgatā pañca āpattikkhandhā sauddesapaññatti nāma. Sāpi dvidhā sapuggalāpuggalaniddesabhedato. Tattha yassā paññattiyā anto āpattiyā saha, vinā vā puggalo dassito, sā sapuggalaniddesā. Itarā apuggalaniddesā.

Now, the method of promulgating all the training rules should be understood. How? 'And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule'—thus, it is twofold, divided into promulgation with recitation and without recitation. Therein, the five groups of offenses that appear in the Pātimokkha in their own form are called promulgation with recitation. That too is twofold, divided into designation with a person and without a person. Therein, a promulgation in which a person is indicated, either together with or without the offense, is designation with a person. The other is designation without a person.

Tattha sapuggalaniddesā dvidhā adassitadassitāpattibhedato. Tattha adassitāpattikā nāma aṭṭha pārājikā dhammā veditabbā. “Pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso”ti (pārā. 39, 44, 89, 91, 167, 171, 195, 197) hi puggalova tattha dassito, nāpatti. Dassitāpattikā nāma bhikkhunipātimokkhe āgatā sattarasa saṅghādisesā dhammā. “Ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṃ dhammaṃ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti (pāci. 683, 687) hi tattha āpatti dassitā saddhiṃ puggalena.

Here, the designation with reference to a person is twofold, divided into those where the offense is not shown and those where it is shown. Herein, the eight pārājika rules are to be understood as those where the offense is not shown. For in the phrase, 'He is defeated, no longer in communion,' it is the individual who is shown there, not the offense. The seventeen saṅghādisesa rules found in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha are those where the offense is shown. For in the phrase, 'This bhikkhunī, having committed this first offense, is subject to expulsion, a saṅghādisesa,' the offense is shown there along with the individual.

Tathā apuggalaniddesāpi adassitadassitāpattibhedato dvidhā. Tattha adassitāpattikā nāma sekhiyā dhammā. Vuttāvasesā dassitāpattikāti veditabbā.

Similarly, the designation without reference to a person is also twofold, divided into those where the offense is not shown and those where it is shown. Herein, the sekhiya rules are those where the offense is not shown. The remaining are to be understood as those where the offense is shown.

Sāpi [M 0.0013][V 0.0013] dvidhā aniddiṭṭhakārakaniddiṭṭhakārakabhedato. Tattha aniddiṭṭhakārakā nāma sukkavisaṭṭhimusāvādomasavādapesuññabhūtagāmaaññavādakaujjhāpanakagaṇabhojanaparamparabhojanasurāmerayaaṅgulipatodakahasadhammaanādariyatalaghātakajatumaṭṭhakasikkhāpadānaṃ vasena pañcadasavidhā honti. Tattha niddiṭṭhakārake missāmissabhedo veditabbo – tattha upayogabhummavibhattiyo ekaṃsena missā. Avasesā missā ca amissā ca. Seyyathidaṃ – paccattaṃ tāva dvīsu aniyatesu upayogena missaṃ, dvādasasu pāṭidesanīyesu karaṇena missaṃ, ūnapañcabandhanapattasikkhāpadesu sāmikaraṇehi, ūnavīsativasse bhummena, mohanake upayogasāmibhummehi. Yasmā “vivaṇṇaka”nti bhāvo adhippeto, na kattā, tasmā vivaṇṇakasikkhāpadaṃ yadā na sambhavati, evaṃ paccattaṃ pañcavidhaṃ missaṃ hoti. Sesesu paṭhamāniyataṃ ṭhapetvā ādimhi “yo pana bhikkhū”ti evamāgataṃ paccattaṃ vā, dutiyāniyataṃ ṭhapetvā paṇītabhojanasamaṇuddesatatiyacatutthapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadesu majjhe “yo pana bhikkhū”ti evamāgataṃ paccattaṃ vā, dubbacakuladūsakasaṃsaṭṭhasikkhāpadesu ādimhi kevalaṃ “bhikkhū”ti āgataṃ paccattaṃ vā, bhedānuvattakasikkhāpade majjhe āgataṃ paccattaṃ vā aññāya vibhattiyā amissameva hoti. Tattha bhedānuvattakatuvaṭṭanadvayasaṃsaṭṭhadutiyapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadesu bahuvacanaṃ, itarattha sabbattha ekavacanamevāti veditabbaṃ.

That too is twofold, divided into those with an unspecified agent and those with a specified agent. Therein, those with an unspecified agent are of fifteen kinds, by way of the training rules on: emission of semen, false speech, abusive speech, slander, plants, prevarication, complaining, eating in a group, eating successively, fermented and distilled intoxicants, tickling, playing in water, disrespect, striking with the hand, and a lacquered bowl. Therein, regarding those with a specified agent, the distinction between mixed and unmixed should be understood. There, the accusative and locative cases are entirely mixed. The remaining are both mixed and unmixed. For example: the nominative, for its part, is mixed with the accusative in the two aniyata rules; it is mixed with the instrumental in the twelve pāṭidesanīya rules; with the genitive and instrumental in the training rule on a bowl with less than five fastenings; with the locative in the case of one less than twenty years old; and with the accusative, genitive, and locative in the case of concealment. Since in the training rule on speaking in dispraise, the state of being is intended, not the agent, when this is not possible, the nominative is thus mixed in five ways. In the remaining cases—except for the first aniyata, where 'whatever bhikkhu' appears at the beginning; or except for the second aniyata and the training rules on choice food, on a novice, and the third and fourth pāṭidesanīya, where 'whatever bhikkhu' appears in the middle; or in the training rules on being difficult to correct, on corrupting families, and on association, where only 'bhikkhu' appears at the beginning; or in the training rule on following a schismatic, where it appears in the middle—the nominative is entirely unmixed with any other case. Therein, it should be understood that the plural is used in the training rules on following a schismatic, the two on turning away, on association, and the second pāṭidesanīya; in all other places, only the singular is used.

Tathā upayogo dvīsu vikappanasikkhāpadesu, tantavāyasikkhāpade ca paccattena misso, abhihaṭasikkhāpade karaṇena, rājasikkhāpade karaṇasāmipaccattehīti upayogo tidhā misso hoti. Karaṇañca kuṭikāramahallakadutiyakathinadvebhāganisīdanasanthatadubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadesu chasu paccattena missaṃ, paṭhamatatiyakathinaaṭṭhaṅgulapādakanisīdanakaṇḍuppaṭicchādikavassikasāṭikaudakasāṭikadvedhammapaccāsīsanasikkhāpadesu aṭṭhasu sāminā missanti karaṇaṃ dvidhā missaṃ hoti. Avasesesu chabbassavassikasāṭikadvatticchadanāvasathapiṇḍamahānāmagarulahupāvuraṇasikkhāpadesu sattasu karaṇavibhatti aññavibhattiyā amissā, accekaeḷakalomasikkhāpadesu sāmivibhatti karaṇavibhattiyā missā. Atirekapattabhesajjasikkhāpadesu aggahitaggahaṇena sāmivibhatti amissāva hotīti veditabbā. Evaṃ tāva niddiṭṭhakārakesu sikkhāpadesu –

Likewise, the accusative is mixed in three ways: in the two training rules on assigning and in the training rule on a weaver, it is mixed with the nominative; in the training rule on what is brought, with the instrumental; and in the training rule concerning a king, with the instrumental, genitive, and nominative. The instrumental is mixed in two ways: it is mixed with the nominative in six training rules—on making a hut, on a large dwelling, the second on the Kathina, on a two-part sitting-cloth, on a felt rug, and on making something a bad color; it is mixed with the genitive in eight training rules—the first and third on the Kathina, on an eight-finger-span foot-rest, on a sitting-cloth, on an itch-covering cloth, on a rains-retreat cloth, on a bathing cloth, and on hoping for two things. In the remaining seven training rules—on a six-year rains-retreat cloth, on a double-layered robe, on a lodging, on almsfood, on Mahānāma, and on a heavy or light outer robe—the instrumental case is unmixed with any other case. In the training rule on urgent sheep's wool, the genitive case is mixed with the instrumental case. In the training rules on an extra bowl and on medicine, it should be understood that the genitive case is unmixed because of the taking of what has not been given. Thus far, regarding the training rules where the agent is specified—

Pañcadhā [M 0.0014] ca tidhā ceva, dvidhā cepi tathekadhā;

Bhinnā vibhattiyo pañca, sabbekādasadhā siyuṃ.

Fivefold and threefold, twofold and also onefold; The five cases are thus divided; in all, they become elevenfold.

Evaṃ [V 0.0014] tāva yathāvuttesu sauddesapaññattisaṅkhātesu sikkhāpadesu aggahitaggahaṇena paññāsuttaresu tisatesu navutianiddiṭṭhakārake vajjetvā niddiṭṭhakārakāni atirekasaṭṭhidvisatāni honti. Tesu paccattakaraṇāni tiṃsuttarāni dvisatāni honti. Tesu amissapaccattakaraṇāni dvādasuttarāni dvisatāni, missapaccattakaraṇāni aṭṭhārasa honti. Avasesesu tiṃsatiyā sikkhāpadesu missopayogakaraṇāni pañca honti, missakaraṇāni cuddasa, amissāni satta, missāmissakaraṇāni dve, amissāni dveti sabbesupi niddiṭṭhakārakesu bhedānuvattakadubbacakuladūsakapaṭhamadutiyatatiyakathinaabhihaṭakuṭikāramahallakavikappanadvayadvebhāgachabbassanisīdanasanthataeḷakalomātirekapattabhesajjavassikasāṭikatantavāyaaccekachārattadva pañcattiṃsesu “yo pana bhikkhū”ti natthi. Dutiyāniyatapaṇītabhojanasamaṇuddesatatiyacatutthapāṭidesanīyesu majjhe atthi.

Thus, by a general reckoning, in the aforementioned training rules designated as those with full descriptions, there are three hundred and fifty. Excluding the ninety with an unspecified agent, there are more than two hundred and sixty with a specified agent. Among these, there are two hundred and thirty with personal and instrumental cases. Of these, two hundred and twelve are unmixed personal and instrumental cases, while eighteen are mixed personal and instrumental cases. In the remaining thirty training rules, five are mixed use and instrumental cases, fourteen are mixed instrumental cases, seven are unmixed, two are mixed and unmixed instrumental cases, and two are unmixed. Thus, in all the rules with a specified agent, the phrase 'whatever bhikkhu' is not found in the thirty-five rules concerning: following a schismatic, being difficult to correct and corrupting families, the first, second, and third Kathina, what is brought on invitation, hut-making, a large dwelling, the two on disposal, the two-part robe, the six-year sitting cloth, a felt rug, sheep's wool, an extra bowl, medicines, the rainy-season robe, a weaver, an urgent robe, and the two on six nights. In the second Aniyata, the rule on superior food, the rule on novices, and the third and fourth Pāṭidesanīya rules, it is found in the middle.

Ettāvatā sauddesānuddesadukaṃ, sapuggalāpuggalaniddesadukaṃ, paccekadassitāpattidukadvayaṃ, aniddiṭṭhakārakadukaṃ, tattha niddiṭṭhakārakesu paccattabhummadukaṃ, sayopanāyopanadukaṃ, ayopanamajjheyopanadukaṃ, ekānekavacanadukanti nava dukāni dassitāni honti. Visesakāraṇaṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sikkhāpade sampatte āvibhavissati. Evaṃ tāva sauddesapaññattiṃ ñatvā sesavinayapiṭake yā kāci paññatti anuddesapaññattīti veditabbā. Sā padabhājanantarāpattivinītavatthupaṭikkhepapaññattiavuttasiddhisikkhāpadavasena chabbidhā hoti.

Thus far, the pair of direct and indirect legislation (sauddesānuddesaduka), the pair of explanations with and without individuals (sapuggalāpuggalaniddesaduka), the two pairs of offenses shown individually (paccekadassitāpattidukadvaya), the pair of unspecified agents (aniddiṭṭhakārakaduka); and among the specified agents, the pair of personal and locative cases (paccattabhummaduka), the pair of rules with and without 'yo pana' at the beginning (sayopanāyopanaduka), the pair of rules without 'yo pana' at the beginning and with it in the middle (ayopanamajjheyopanaduka), and the pair of singular and plural terms (ekānekavacanaduka)—these nine pairs have been shown. The specific reason will become evident when each training rule is encountered. Thus, having understood direct legislation (sauddesapaññatti), whatever legislation remains in the Vinaya Piṭaka should be known as indirect legislation (anuddesapaññatti). It is sixfold, by way of the training rule of word-division (padabhājana), of intermediate offense (antarāpatti), of a disciplinary instance (vinītavatthu), of prohibition (paṭikkhepa), of enactment (paññatti), and of unstated establishment (avuttasiddhi).

Tattha “yebhuyyena khayite āpatti thullaccayassa (pari. 157-158), vaṭṭakate mukhe acchupantassa āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pārā. 73) evamādikā padabhājane sandissamānāpatti padabhājanasikkhāpadaṃ nāma. “Na ca, bhikkhave, sabbamattikāmayā kuṭi kātabbā, yo [M 0.0015] kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”tiādi (pārā. 85) antarāpattisikkhāpadaṃ nāma. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, divāpaṭisallīyantena dvāraṃ saṃvaritvā paṭisallīyitu”nti (pārā. 77) evamādi vinītavatthusikkhāpadaṃ nāma. “Saṅghabhedako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo”ti (mahāva. 115) evamādi paṭikkhepasikkhāpadaṃ nāma.

Herein, 'When it is mostly eaten, there is an offense of grave offense (thullaccaya)'; 'For one touching the mouth made round, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa)'—such offenses and so forth found in the word-division are called the training rule of word-division. 'Monks, a hut should not be made entirely of clay; whoever should do so, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa)'—this and so forth is called the training rule of an intermediate offense. 'I allow, monks, for one withdrawing during the day, to close the door and then withdraw'—this and so forth is called the training rule of a disciplinary instance. 'Monks, a schismatic who is not yet ordained should not be given the higher ordination'—this and so forth is called the training rule of prohibition.

Yasmā pana tena tena paṭikkhepena “yo pana bhikkhu samaggaṃ saṅghaṃ adhammasaññī bhindeyya, pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso. Yo pana bhikkhu duṭṭhacitto bhagavato jīvamānakasarīre lohitaṃ [V 0.0015] uppādeyya, pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso”ti sikkhāpadāni paññattāni honti. Yāni sandhāya “ekassa chejjakā hoti, catunnaṃ thullaccayaṃ, catunnañceva anāpatti, sabbesaṃ ekavatthukā”ti vuttaṃ. “Atthāpatti tiṭṭhante bhagavati āpajjati, no parinibbute”ti (pari. 323) ca vuttaṃ. Tena na kevalaṃ “na, bhikkhave, jānaṃ saṅghabhedako anupasampanno upasampādetabbo…pe… āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti idameva sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hoti sādhakaṃ hoti. “Paṇḍako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabbo”ti (mahāva. 109) evamādīsu pana upajjhāyādīnaṃ dukkaṭameva paññattaṃ, na paṇḍakādīnaṃ pārājikāpatti. Na hi tesaṃ bhikkhubhāvo atthi. Yato siyā pārājikāpatti. Tathā “na acchinne theve pakkamitabba”nti (mahāva. 66, 67, 78, 79) evamādikañca paṭikkhepasikkhāpadameva nāma.

Because by those various prohibitions, these training rules were laid down: 'Should any bhikkhu, perceiving a united Sangha as contrary to the Dhamma, cause it to split, he is defeated (pārājika), no longer in communion (asaṃvāsa). Should any bhikkhu, with a corrupt mind, cause blood to flow from the body of the Blessed One while he is still alive, he is defeated (pārājika), no longer in communion (asaṃvāsa).' Regarding which it was said: 'For one, it entails severance; for four, a grave offense (thullaccaya); for four, no offense; for all, the same basis.' And it was said: 'An offense is incurred while the Blessed One is living, not after his final Nibbāna' (Pari. 323). Therefore, not only was this training rule laid down as effective: 'Monks, a schismatic who is not yet ordained, knowing that he is such, should not be given the higher ordination... an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) is incurred.' But also in cases like: 'A eunuch (paṇḍaka), monks, who is not yet ordained should not be given the higher ordination; if ordained, he should be expelled' (Mahāva. 109), and so on—only an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) is laid down for the preceptor and others, not a defeat offense (pārājikāpatti) for the eunuch and the like. For they have no status as a bhikkhu, from which a defeat offense could arise. Similarly, 'One should not depart leaving the robe unfinished' (Mahāva. 66, 67, 78, 79), and so on—these are also merely called training rules of prohibition.

Khandhakesu paññattadukkaṭathullaccayāni paññattisikkhāpadaṃ nāma. “Tena hi, sāriputta, bhedānuvattake thullaccayaṃ desāpehī”ti (cūḷava. 345) vuttaṃ, thullaccayampi tattheva samodhānaṃ gacchati. Idaṃ tesaṃ vibhattikammakkhaṇe apaññattattā avijjamānampi bhagavato vacanena visuddhakkhaṇepi vijjamānaṃ jātanti eke. “Bhedānuvattake desāpehī”ti vacanato sesabhedānuvattakānaṃ “yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ saṅghabhedakānaṃ anuvatteyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ. Tathā sabbāni khandhakavattāni, vinayakammāni ca tattheva samodhānaṃ gacchanti. Yathāha “paññatte taṃ upāli mayā āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukavattaṃ…pe… evaṃ supaññatte kho mayā upāli sikkhāpade”tiādi. “Yā pana bhikkhunī naccaṃ vā gītaṃ vā vāditaṃ vā dassanāya gaccheyya[M 0.0016], pācittiya”nti (pāci. 834) iminā suttena bhikkhunī nacceyya vā gāyeyya vā vādeyya vā, pācittiyanti evamādikaṃ yaṃ kiñci aṭṭhakathāya dissamānaṃ āpattijātaṃ vinayakammaṃ vā avuttasiddhisikkhāpadaṃ nāma. Chabbidhampetaṃ chahi ākārehi uddesārahaṃ na hotīti anuddesasikkhāpadaṃ nāmāti veditabbaṃ. Seyyathidaṃ – pañcahi uddesehi yathāsambhavaṃ visabhāgattā thullaccayadubbhāsitānaṃ sabhāgavatthukampi dukkaṭathullaccayadvayaṃ asabhāgāpattikattā antarāpattipaññattisikkhāpadānaṃ, nānāvatthukāpattikattā paṭikkhepasikkhāpadānaṃ, kesañci vinītavatthupaññattisikkhāpadānañca adassitāpattikattā, adassitavatthukattā bhedānuvattakathullaccayassa, adassitāpattivatthukattā avuttasiddhisikkhāpadānanti. Ettāvatā “duvidhaṃ sikkhāpadapaññāpanaṃ sauddesānuddesabhedato”ti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ samāsato pakāsitaṃ hoti.

The dukkaṭa and thullaccaya offenses laid down in the Khandhakas are called the training rule of enactment. It is said, 'Therefore, Sāriputta, have the followers of schismatics confess a thullaccaya' (Cv. 345); the thullaccaya is also included in that same context. Some say that this, though not existing at the time of the formal act of classification because it was not laid down, came into existence at the moment of purification by the word of the Blessed One. From the statement, 'Have the followers of schismatics confess,' it should be understood that for the other followers of schismatics the training rule, 'Should any bhikkhu knowingly follow schismatics, he incurs a thullaccaya,' was laid down. Similarly, all Khandhaka duties and Vinaya formal acts are included in that same context. As it is said: 'Upāli, I have laid down for incoming bhikkhus the incoming duty... and thus, Upāli, I have well laid down the training rules.' By the rule, 'Should any bhikkhunī go to see dancing, singing, or instrumental music, she incurs a pācittiya' (Pāc. 834), any offense or Vinaya formal act appearing in the commentaries—such as that if a bhikkhunī should dance, sing, or play music, it is a pācittiya—which is not explicitly stated but implicitly established, is called the training rule of unstated establishment. This sixfold division is not suitable for recitation for six reasons; hence it should be known as the training rule of non-recitation. Namely: because of the dissimilar nature of thullaccaya and dubbhāsita in the five recitations, as is appropriate; because, even with a common basis, the two offenses of dukkaṭa and thullaccaya are dissimilar offenses in the case of the training rules of intermediate offense and enactment; because of having offenses with various bases in the case of the training rules of prohibition; because the offense is not shown for some training rules of disciplinary instances and of enactment; because the basis is not shown for the thullaccaya for following schismatics; and because the offense and basis are not shown for the training rules of unstated establishment. Thus, what was stated as 'The laying down of training rules is twofold, by way of recitation and non-recitation,' has been briefly elucidated.

Paññattiyaṃ [V 0.0016] tāva –

Regarding the enactment, to begin with—

“Kārako idha niddiṭṭho, apekkhāya abhāvato;

Pubbe vattabbavidhānā-bhāvato ca ādito yopanena sahā”ti. –

Here the agent is specified, / due to the absence of dependence; / and due to the absence of a prior stipulation, / from the outset, along with 'yo pana'.

Ayaṃ nayo veditabbo. Tassattho – ye te aniddiṭṭhakārakā pubbe vuttappabhedā sukkavisaṭṭhiādayo sikkhāpadavisesā, tesu adhippāyakammavatthupuggalapayoge apekkhāya bhāvato kārako na niddiṭṭho tesaṃ sāpekkhabhāvadassanatthaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sikkhāpade āvibhavissati, idha pana pārājikapaññattiyaṃ apekkhāya abhāvato kārako niddiṭṭho. Yo pana kārako “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā ubbhatasmi”ntiādīsu (pārā. 462, 472, 475) viya pubbe vattabbavidhānābhāvato karaṇādivasena aniddisitvā paccattavasena niddiṭṭho apekkhāya abhāvato. Tattha niddisiyamāno sesadutiyāniyatapaṇītabhojanaṃ samaṇuddesatatiyacatautthapāṭidesanīyesu viya majjhe aniddisitvā “na heva kho pana…pe… obhāsitu”ntiādi (pārā. 453) viya pubbe vattabbavidhānābhāvato eva ādimhi niddiṭṭho. Ādimhi niddisiyamānopi pubbe vuttappabhedesu bhedānuvattakādīsu pañcattiṃsesu sikkhāpadesu viya aniddisitvā pubbe vattabbavidhānābhāvato eva “yo pana bhikkhū”tiāditova yopana-saddena saha [M 0.0017] niddiṭṭho. Evaṃ niddisiyamānopi so yasmā “yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭeyyu”ntiādi (pāci. 933) āpatti viya parappabhavaṃ āpattiṃ na āpajjati, tasmā “yo pana bhikkhū”ti ekavacanena niddiṭṭho. Methunadhammāpattipi parappabhavā “dvayaṃdvayasamāpattī”ti (pārā. 39) vacanatoti ce? Taṃ na, adhippāyajānanato. Anekissā eva bhikkhuniyā āpatti, na ekissāti niyamo tattha atthi, na evaṃ idha niyamoti aniyamitādhippāyo. Lambīmudupiṭṭhīnaṃ kuto “dvayaṃdvayasamāpattī”ti (pārā. 55) vacanato tesaṃ methunadhammāpatti. Ayamattho catasso methunadhammapaccayāti aṭṭhavatthukaṃ sandhāya “chejjaṃ siyā methunadhammapaccayā”ti (pari. 481) ca parivāre vuttavacanena sādhetabbo.

This method should be understood. Its meaning is as follows: in those specific training rules, such as those concerning the emission of semen and so forth, where the agent is not specified, this is to show their dependence on intention, action, basis, person, and application. All that will become clear in each respective training rule. Here, however, in the laying down of the pārājika rule, since there is no such dependence, the agent is specified. As for the agent, in cases like 'when the Kaṭhina has been removed by the bhikkhu upon the completion of the robe-making' (Pārā. 462, 472, 475), because there was no prior stipulation to be stated, it is specified in the nominative case without specifying by way of instrumentality and so forth, due to the absence of dependence. There, when being specified, it is not specified in the middle, as in the rules concerning leftover food, the second indeterminate rule, choice food, and the third and fourth pāṭidesanīya rules, but is specified at the beginning, as in 'yet if... he should illuminate' (Pārā. 453), due to the absence of a prior stipulation to be stated. Even when specified at the beginning, it is not specified as in the thirty-five training rules of the previously stated types, such as those concerning following schismatics, but is specified from the very beginning with the word 'yo pana' along with 'bhikkhu,' due to the absence of a prior stipulation to be stated. Even when specified in this way, since he does not incur an offense originating from another, as in the case of 'if two bhikkhunīs were to lie down on one bed' (Pāc. 933), therefore, it is specified in the singular as 'yo pana bhikkhu.' If it is said that the offense of sexual intercourse also originates from another because of the statement 'a two-by-two union' (Pārā. 39), that is not so, because the intention is understood. There, the rule is that many bhikkhunīs incur the offense, not just one; but here there is no such rule, so the intention is unrestricted. For those with long and soft buttocks, whence is their offense of sexual intercourse? From the statement 'a two-by-two union' (Pārā. 55). This meaning—that there are four conditions for the sexual act—should be established by reference to the eightfold basis and the statement in the Parivāra, 'there may be severance on account of the sexual act' (Pari. 481).

Bhedānuvattakasikkhāpade tiṇṇaṃ uddhaṃ na samanubhāsitabbā, na saṅghena saṅghaṃ ekato kātabbanti. Nayadassanatthaṃ āditova “bhikkhū hontī”ti bahuvacananiddesaṃ katvā puna “eko vā dve vā tayo vā”ti (pārā. 418) vuttaṃ, aññathā na tato uddhaṃ “anuvattakā hontī”ti āpajjati. Tato nidānavirodho. Pañcasatamattā hi tadanuvattakā ahesuṃ. Yaṃ pana sattasatikakkhandhake “saṅgho cattāro pācīnake bhikkhū, cattāro pāveyyake bhikkhū sammanneyya [V 0.0017] …pe… sammatā”tiādi (cūḷava. 456) ñattidutiyakammaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ “ubbāhikāya imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametu”nti vuttattā tehi kattabbavidhānaṃ. Sammutikaraṇameva vā tatiyaṃ katvā kappati. Na hi te tena kammena kammārahā kammakatā honti. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, so kammārahoti lakkhaṇaṃ. Na ca tadā saṅgho tesaṃ aṭṭhannampi bhikkhūnaṃ kammaṃ akāsi. Bhajāpiyamānā te kammapattabhāvaṃ bhajanti. Adhikaraṇavūpasamakammassa pattā yuttā saṅghena katāti katvā kammapattā eva hi te honti. “Te bhikkhū bhikkhūhi yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāyā”ti (pārā. 418) vacanato tehi kattabbavidhānaṃ. Sammutikaraṇameva kammaṃ hotīti ce? Taṃ na, adhippāyajānanato, tassa paṭinissaggāya eva te bhikkhū kammārahā kātabbā, na dosāgativasenāti ayamettha adhippāyo. Na hi pācīnakādīnaṃ sammutiyā adhikaraṇavūpasamasiddhi viya tesaṃ samanubhāsanakammena tassa paṭinissaggasiddhi hoti, sammuti nāmesā [M 0.0018] paṭhamaṃ anumatiṃ gahetvā yācitvāva karīyati, na tathā kammanti. Kammakaraṇe pana tadatthasiddhi hotiyeva. Parasammutiyā bahutarāva sammannitabbāti veditabbaṃ.

In the training rule concerning those who follow schismatics, it is said that those beyond three should not be admonished, and that one Sangha should not be made into a unified Sangha with another. For the purpose of showing the method, initially, the plural designation 'they are bhikkhus' was made, and then it was said, 'one or two or three' (Pārā. 418); otherwise, it would not follow that those beyond that number are 'followers.' This would create a contradiction with the origin story, for indeed, about five hundred were their followers. As for what was said in the Khandhaka of the Seven Hundred—'the Sangha should appoint four eastern bhikkhus and four Pāveyyaka bhikkhus... they were appointed' (Cv. 456), etc.—that ñattidutiyakamma was stated because it was said, 'Let them settle this legal issue by means of a committee.' Alternatively, it is permissible to make the appointment itself the third admonition. For by that formal act, they do not become deserving of a formal act, nor are they those for whom a formal act has been done. The characteristic of one deserving a formal act is that the Sangha performs the formal act for him. But at that time, the Sangha did not perform a formal act for those eight bhikkhus. While being appointed, they attain the state of being subject to the formal act. Because it was done by the Sangha, which is fit and proper for the act of settling a legal issue, they are indeed those who are subject to the formal act. From the statement, 'Those bhikkhus should be admonished by the bhikkhus up to the third time for the sake of relinquishing it' (Pārā. 418), the procedure to be carried out by them is prescribed. If it is asked whether the appointment itself is the formal act, that is not so, from understanding the intention. The intention here is that those bhikkhus should be made deserving of the formal act for the sake of relinquishing that view, not by way of falling into fault. For the accomplishment of its relinquishment through the formal act of admonishing them is not like the accomplishment of settling the legal issue through the appointment of the easterners and others. An appointment, namely, is done only after first gaining consent and being requested; not so with a formal act. But in the performance of a formal act, the accomplishment of that purpose indeed occurs. It should be understood that a greater number should be appointed by the agreement of others.

“Methunadhamma”nti evaṃ bāhullanayena laddhanāmakaṃ sakapayogena vā parapayogena vā attano nimittassa sakamagge vā paramagge vā paranimittassa vā sakamagge eva pavesanapaviṭṭhaṭṭhitauddharaṇesu yaṃ kiñci ekaṃ paṭisādiyanavasena seveyya, pārājiko hoti asaṃvāsoti. Keci pana “pavesanādīni cattāri vā tīṇi vā dve vā ekaṃ vā paṭiseveyya, pārājiko hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘so ce pavesanaṃ sādiyati, paviṭṭhaṃ sādiyati, ṭhitaṃ sādiyati, uddharaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti pārājikassā’tiādī”ti (pārā. 58) vadanti. Tesaṃ matena catūsupi catasso pārājikāpattiyo āpajjati. Teyeva evaṃ vadanti – āpajjatu methunadhammapārājikāpatti, methunadhammapārājikāpattiyā taṃbhāgiyāti attano vītikkame pārājikāpattiyo, saṅghādisesāpattiñca āpajjitvā sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya gahaṭṭhakāle methunādikaṃ pārājikaṃ āpajjitvā puna pabbajitvā upasampajjitvā ekaṃ saṅghādisesāpattiṃ ekamanekaṃ vā paṭikaritvāva so puggalo yasmā nirāpattiko hoti, tasmā so gahaṭṭhakāle sāpattikovāti.
