Idaṃ [V 0.0049] pana sikkhāpadaṃ catutthapārājikaṃ viya nidānāpekkhaṃ. Na hi vaggumudātīriyā bhikkhū sayameva attano asantaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ musāvādalakkhaṇaṃ pāpetvā bhāsiṃsu. Aññamaññañhi te uttarimanussadhammavaṇṇaṃ bhāsiṃsu. Na ca tāvatā pārājikavatthu hoti, tattakena pana lesena bhagavā taṃ vatthuṃ nidānaṃ katvā pārājikaṃ paññapesi, tathā idhāpi. Na hi nidāne “adesitavatthukāyo sārambhāyo aparikkamanāyo”ti vuttaṃ. “Appamāṇikāyo”ti pana vuttattā pamāṇamatikkamantassa saṅghādisesova nidānāpekkho. Tattha sārambhe aparikkamane saṅghādisesappasaṅgaṃ viya dissamānaṃ “vibhaṅgo taṃniyamako”ti vuttattā vibhaṅge na nivāreti. Tathā mahallake.

This training rule, like the fourth pārājika, is dependent on the origin story. For the monks on the bank of the Vaggumudā River did not themselves make a false claim about a non-existent superhuman state, thus committing a falsehood. Instead, they spoke in praise of one another's superhuman states. That by itself does not constitute a pārājika offense, but with that slight pretext, the Blessed One made that incident the origin story and laid down the pārājika rule. It is similar here. For in the origin story, it is not stated, 'without a designated site, with hostile intent, and without circumspection.' However, since it is said to be 'of immeasurable size,' for one who exceeds the measure, it is a saṅghādisesa, dependent on the origin story. Therein, what appears to be an occasion for a saṅghādisesa in a case of hostile intent and no circumspection is not precluded by the Vibhaṅga, since it is said, 'The Vibhaṅga is its regulator.' The same applies to a large hut.

Etthāha – kimatthaṃ mātikāyaṃ dukkaṭavatthu vuttaṃ, nanu vibhaṅge eva vattabbaṃ siyāti? Evametaṃ. Kiṃ nu bhikkhū abhinetabbā vatthudesanāya, tehi bhikkhūhi vatthu desetabbaṃ, kīdisaṃ? Anārambhaṃ saparikkamananti. Itarañhi “sārambhe ce bhikkhu vatthusmiṃ aparikkamane”ti evaṃ anuppasaṅgavasena āgatattā vuttaṃ. Yasmā vatthu nāma atthi sārambhaṃ aparikkamanaṃ, atthi anārambhaṃ saparikkamanaṃ, atthi sārambhaṃ saparikkamanaṃ, atthi anārambhaṃ aparikkamananti bahuvidhaṃ, tasmā bahuvidhattā vatthu desetabbaṃ anārambhaṃ saparikkamanaṃ, netaranti vuttaṃ hoti. Kimatthikā panettha vatthudesanāti ce? Garukāpattipaññāpanahetuparivajjanupāyattā. Vatthuadesanā hi garukāpattipaññāpanahetubhūtā. Garukāpattipaññāpanaṃ akataviññattigihipīḷājananaṃ, attadukkhaparadukkhahetubhūto ca sārambhabhāvoti ete vatthudesanāpadesena upāyena parivajjitā honti. Na hi bhikkhū akappiyakuṭikaraṇatthaṃ gihīnaṃ vā pīḷānimittaṃ, sārambhavatthukuṭikaraṇatthaṃ vā vatthuṃ desentīti. Honti cettha –

Here it is said: For what purpose is the basis for a dukkaṭa offense mentioned in the summary? Should it not be stated in the analysis itself? It is so. But then, are monks to be led to declare the site? And what kind of site should be declared by those monks? One that is without hostility and involves circumspection. For the other case—'if a monk, regarding a site with hostility and without circumspection'—is stated because it arises by way of secondary implication. Since a site can be of many kinds—with hostility and without circumspection, without hostility and with circumspection, with hostility and with circumspection, or without hostility and without circumspection—therefore, because of its many varieties, it is said that the site to be declared is one without hostility and with circumspection, not the other kinds. But what is the purpose here of declaring the site? It is a means of avoiding the cause for laying down a grave offense. For not declaring the site is a cause for laying down a grave offense. Laying down a grave offense causes distress to laypeople who have not been informed, and the state of being hostile becomes a cause of suffering for oneself and others. Thus, these are avoided by the skillful means of declaring the site. Monks do not declare a site for the purpose of making an unallowable hut, or as a cause of distress to laypeople, or for the purpose of constructing a hut on a site involving hostility. In this case, there are these verses—

“Dukkaṭassa [M 0.0054] hi vatthūnaṃ, mātikāya pakāsanā;

Garukāpattihetūnaṃ, tesaṃ evaṃ pakāsitā.

Indeed, the exposition in the summary of the bases for a dukkaṭa offense is thus the exposition of those very causes of a grave offense.

“Vatthussa desanupāyena, garukāpattihetuyo;

Vajjitā honti yaṃ tasmā, sārambhādi jahāpita”nti.

Because the causes of a grave offense are avoided by the means of declaring the site, therefore hostility and the like are caused to be abandoned.

Kuṭikārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on making a hut is concluded.

7. Vihārakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Training Rule on Making a Monastery

Kiriyāmattato [V 0.0050] samuṭṭhānabhāvato akiriyamevetaṃ. Taṃ desanāakaraṇavasena. Bhikkhū vā anabhineyyāti ettha vā-saddo avadhāraṇatthoti veditabbo. “Āyasmā channo cetiyarukkhaṃ chedāpesī”ti (pārā. 365) āgatattā idampi nidānāpekkhanti veditabbaṃ.

Due to its nature of arising from mere action, this is itself a non-action. That is by way of not making a declaration. Here, in the phrase 'or the monks are not to be led,' the word 'or' should be understood as being for emphasis. Since it is stated, 'The venerable Channa had a cetiya-tree cut down' (Pārā. 365), this too should be understood as being dependent on the origin story.

Vihārakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on making a monastery is concluded.

8. Duṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule on a Malicious Offense

“Kasmā mama vandanādīni…pe… ‘ghaṭiteyeva sīsaṃ etī’ti vuttattā antimavatthuajjhāpannakaṃ vandituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Parivārāvasāne upālipañcake “kati nu kho, bhante, avandiyā”tiādinā (pari. 467) vuttapāḷiyaṃ avuttattā, “pacchā upasampannena pure upasampanno vandiyo”ti (pari. 468) vuttattā ca, tasmā eva imissaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ “upasampannoti saṅkhyupagamana”nti vuttaṃ. Suttādhippāyo pana evaṃ gahetabbo – avandanto sāmīcippaṭikkhepasaṅkhātāya codanāya codeti nāmāti dassanatthaṃ vuttanti. Tasmā eva “ettāvatā ca codanā nāma hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Idha adhippetaṃ āpattiāpajjanākāraṃ dassetuṃ “‘kasmā mama vandanādīni na karosī’tiādi vutta”nti likhitaṃ.

Some say, 'Because it is said, "his head would split," it is not proper to pay respects to one who has committed a final offense,' beginning with 'Why do you not pay respects, etc., to me?' That should not be accepted. This is because it is not stated in the Pāli text at the end of the Parivāra, in the Upālipañcaka, beginning with, 'How many, venerable sir, are unworthy of veneration?' (Pari. 467), and because it is stated, 'One ordained earlier is to be venerated by one ordained later' (Pari. 468). Therefore, in this Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, it is said, '“Ordained” means inclusion in the reckoning.' However, the intention of the Sutta should be understood thus: it is stated to show that one who does not pay homage is indeed accusing with an accusation known as the rejection of proper conduct. Therefore, it is said, 'To this extent, it is called an accusation.' Here, to show the manner of incurring an offense, it is written, 'It is said, "Why do you not pay respects, etc., to me?"'

Katūpasampadanti yassa upasampadā ruhati, taṃ, paṇḍakādayo. Ṭhapanakkhettanti ettha sabbasaṅgāhikaṃ, puggalikañcāti duvidhaṃ pavāraṇāṭhapanaṃ. Tattha [M 0.0055] sabbasaṅgāhike “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… tevācikaṃ pavāre”ti su-kārato yāva re-kāro. Puggalikaṭhapane pana “saṅghaṃ, bhante, pavāremi…pe… passanto paṭī”ti saṃ-kārato yāva ayaṃ sabbapacchimo ṭi-kāro, etthantare ekapadepi ṭhapentena ṭhapitā hoti. Uposathe pana iminānusārena viseso veditabbo “kareyyā”ti re-kāre anatikkamante.

'One who has received ordination' means one whose ordination is valid, such as eunuchs and the like. 'The scope of suspension' here refers to two types of Pavāraṇā suspension: collective and individual. In the collective suspension, it is from the syllable 'su' up to the syllable 're' in 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me... I invite for the third time.' In the individual suspension, it is from the syllable 'saṃ' up to this very last syllable 'ṭi' in 'Venerable sirs, I invite the Sangha... seeing it, I will make amends.' If one suspends it at even a single word within this interval, it is considered suspended. However, regarding the Uposatha, the distinction should be understood according to this method, without going beyond the syllable 're' in 'kareyyā'.

Duṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a malicious offense is concluded.

9. Aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Training Rule on a Matter of Another Category

Aññabhāgo [V 0.0051] vā assa atthīti yathā suvaṇṇassedaṃ sovaṇṇamityatra suvaṇṇavā anena suvaṇṇo ityuccate. Taṃ paṭimāya sarīraṃ, silāputtakassa sarīranti ca nidassanaṃ. Chagalakassa “dabbo”ti dinnaṃ nāmaṃ “deso”ti vuccati. Kasmā? Theraṃ anuddhaṃsetuṃ therassāpi apadisitabbattā. Aññampi vatthuṃ na theraṃyeva. Lissati silissati vohāramattenevana atthato. Īsakaṃ allīyatīti lesoti adhippāyo. Lisaselachakolaallībhāve. Tena vuttaṃ “īsakaṃ allīyatīti leso”ti. Yasmā desalesā atthato ninnānākaraṇaṃ, tasmā “kiñcidesaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāyā”ti padaṃ uddharitvā “dasa lesā jātileso”tiādi (pārā. 394) padabhājane vuttaṃ.

'Or it has another part' is like when, regarding gold, one says 'this is golden,' or 'he is endowed with gold by this gold.' An example is the body of an image or the body of a stone doll. The name 'Dabbo' given to the goat is called a 'pretext' (desa). Why? Because it should also be attributed to the elder, so as not to disparage him. And the object is not only the elder. 'Lissati' and 'silissati' are only by way of convention, not in reality. The intention is that 'lesa' means 'it adheres slightly.' This refers to the state of adhering, sticking, or clinging. Therefore, it is said, 'lesa means it adheres slightly.' Since 'desa' and 'lesa' are not different in meaning, therefore, having extracted the phrase 'taking some pretext, a mere trace,' it is stated in the word-analysis, 'ten traces, the trace of birth,' and so on (Pārā. 394).

Aṭṭhuppattivaseneva āvibhūtanti ettha kiñca bhiyyo aniyamattā. Na hi mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ viya aññesaṃ sabbesampi “chagalakamevettha aññabhāgiyaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hoti, aññaṃ gomahiṃsādikampi hoti, na ca mettiyabhūmajakā viya sabbepi nāmalesamattameva upādiyanti, aññampi jātilesādiṃ upādiyanti, tasmā aniyamattā na vibhattaṃ. Kiñca bhiyyo tathāvutte chagalakasseva aññabhāgiyatā sambhavati, na aññassa, yena sova dassito. Leso ca nāma lesova, na jātiādi, yena sova dassitoti evaṃ micchāgāhappasaṅgatoti veditabbaṃ. Idha ca…pe… saññinopīti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade ca amūlakasikkhāpade cāti attho.

Here, 'manifested by way of the origin of the case' means that it is not analyzed in detail, and what is more, this is due to its indefiniteness. For it is not that for all others, like the Mettiyā and Bhūmajakā monks, the issue here is only about a goat; it can also be about cows, buffaloes, and the like. Nor do all, like the Mettiyā and Bhūmajakā monks, take up only a mere trace of a name; they also take up traces of birth and so on. Therefore, because of this indefiniteness, it is not analyzed in detail. Moreover, if it were stated in that way, it would be possible for only the goat to be 'of another category,' not anything else, which is why it was shown in that way. And a 'trace' would be just a name-trace, not birth and so on, which is why it was shown in that way. Thus, it should be understood that this would lead to the error of wrong grasping. Here, '...even of one who is percipient' means in this training rule and in the training rule on a baseless accusation.

Aññabhāgiyasikkhaṃ [M 0.0056] yo, neva sikkhati yuttito;

Gacche vinayaviññūhi, aññabhāgiyataṃva so. (vajira. ṭī. pārājika 408);

He who does not train rightly in the training rule on a matter of another category, is considered by those skilled in the Vinaya as belonging to another category himself.

Aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a matter of another category is concluded.

11. Bhedānuvattakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. Explanation of the Training Rule on Following a Schismatic

Tiṇṇaṃ uddhaṃ kammārahā…pe… karotīti ettha “ime cattāro”ti vā “imañca imañcā”ti vā vatvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti likhitaṃ.

Three or more are fit for a formal act... and so on... Here, in 'he does,' it is written that it is not proper to perform the act by saying 'these four' or 'this one and this one.'

Bhedānuvattakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on following a schismatic is concluded.

12. Dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

12. Explanation of the Training Rule on Being Difficult to Admonish

Dukkhena [V 0.0052] vattabbo dubbaco. Vuccamāno na sahati.

He is contentious in speech, difficult to admonish. When spoken to, he does not endure.

Dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on being difficult to admonish is concluded.

Nigamanavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Conclusion

“Nāmamattavasenā”ti pāṭho. “Nāmagottavasenā”ti likhitaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kiriyā bhikkhūnaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti jānitvā sace chādeti, channāva hotīti attho. Sabhāgamattamevāti averisabhāgamattamevāti adhippāyo.

The reading is 'by name only' (nāmamattavasenā). It is written as 'by name and clan' (nāmagottavasenā). This is what is meant: if, knowing that 'this action is not permissible for monks,' he conceals it, it is indeed concealed—that is the meaning. 'Only to the extent of sharing' means only to the extent of sharing without animosity—that is the intention.

Vatthu ceva gottañcāti ettha vatthūti vītikkamanaṃ asucimuccanaṃ. Gottanti gaṃ tāyatīti gottaṃ, sajātito aññattha gantuṃ adatvā gaṃ buddhiṃ, vacanañca tāyatīti attho. Vatthu ca sajātimeva gacchati. Sajāti nāmettha aññehi visiṭṭhāvisiṭṭhabhūtā kiriyā, na kāyasaṃsaggādi. Nāmañceva āpatti cāti ettha āpattīti vītikkamenāpannāpattiyā nāmaṃ.

Regarding 'the object and the lineage'—here, 'object' means the transgression, the emission of impurity. 'Lineage' (gotta) means 'it protects the gaṃ' (gaṃ tāyati), hence gotta; the meaning is that it protects the gaṃ—that is, the intellect and speech—by not allowing it to go elsewhere than to its own kind. The object also goes only to its own kind. Here, 'own kind' means an action that is distinguished or undistinguished by others, not bodily contact and so on. Regarding 'name and offense'—here, 'offense' means the name of the offense incurred through transgression.

Puna [M 0.0057] āgatāgatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocentenāti ettha dvinnaṃ ārocentena “āyasmantā dhārentu”tiṇṇaṃ vā atirekānaṃ vā ārocentena “āyasmanto dhārentū”ti evaṃ ārocanavidhānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Vattabhedañca ratticchedañca akatvāti ettha ṭhapetvā navakataraṃ pārivāsikaṃ avasesānaṃ antamaso mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādīnampi abhivādanādisādiyane, paṭipāṭiyā nisīdane, ovadane, kammikānaṃ garahaṇe cātiādīsu vattabhedo hoti. Dassanasavanavisayesu anārocane ca bhikkhūhi ekacchanne vasane ca ajānantasseva vihāre bhikkhūnaṃ āgantvā gamane cātiādīsu ratticchedo hoti. Nānāsaṃvāsakehi vinayakammābhāvato tesaṃ anārocane ratticchedo na hoti. “Dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā”ti vacanato anto na vaṭṭati. Nikkhittavatteneva hutvā vicarantena yassa santike pubbe samādiyitvā ārocitaṃ, tassāpi santike pacchā nikkhipanakāle ārocetvāva nikkhipitabbaṃ. Tasmā puna samādānakālepi so ce tato gacchati, taṃ divasaṃ agantvā divā ārocetvāpi yadi evaṃ atītadivasaṃ hoti, “aruṇe uṭṭhite tassa santike ārocetvā vattaṃ nikkhipitvā vihāraṃ gantabbanti tassa santike ārocetvā vattaṃ nikkhipitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Apica “vihāraṃ gantvā yaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ [V 0.0053] bhikkhuṃ passati, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Sace ratticchedo hoti, vihārasīmāpariyāpannānaṃ sabbesaṃ ārocetabbaṃ siyā. “Tassa ārocetvā”ti idaṃ pana pubbe anārocitaṃ sandhāya vattabhedarakkhaṇatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā eva samantapāsādikāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) evaṃ vuttaṃ “aññaṃ vihārato nikkhantaṃ vā āgantukaṃ vā”ti.

Regarding 'by one who informs the incoming monks': here, the method of informing should be understood thus: when informing two, one should say, 'Venerable sirs, please bear this in mind' (āyasmantā dhārentu); when informing three or more, 'Venerable sirs, please bear this in mind' (āyasmanto dhārentu). Regarding 'without breaking the observance and without a break in the nights': here, excepting a very new probationer, for the remaining ones—even down to those deserving to be sent back to the beginning—a break in the observance occurs in matters such as accepting salutations, sitting according to seniority, giving admonition, and rebuking the officials. A break in the nights occurs in cases such as not informing about matters within the range of sight and hearing, dwelling under the same roof with monks without informing them, and monks arriving at and departing from the monastery without one's knowledge. Since there are no Vinaya acts with those of a different communion, not informing them does not constitute a break in the nights. Because of the text, 'having gone beyond two clod-throws,' it is not permitted within that range. Having relinquished the observance, one may wander. When relinquishing it later in the presence of the one to whom one announced it when undertaking it previously, one must announce it again before relinquishing it. Therefore, at the time of undertaking it again, if that monk leaves and does not return that day, even if one informed him during the day and a day has thus passed, it is said: 'When dawn breaks, one should inform him, relinquish the observance, and go to the monastery.' Thus, the observance should be relinquished after informing him. Moreover, it is said: 'Having gone to the monastery, one should relinquish it after informing the very first monk one sees.' If there is a break in the nights, all who are included within the monastery boundary would have to be informed. This phrase, 'having informed him,' however, is said with reference to a prior failure to inform, for the sake of protecting the observance. Therefore, it is said thus in the Samantapāsādikā (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 97): 'another who has left the monastery or a newcomer.'

Suddhantaparivāse pana sace “māsamattaṃ asuddhomhī”ti aggahesi, parivasanto puna ūnaṃ vā adhikaṃ vā sanniṭṭhānaṃ karoti, tattakampi parivasitabbameva, parivāsadānakiccaṃ natthi. Ayañhi suddhantaparivāso nāma uddhampi ārohati, heṭṭhāpi orohati. Idamassa lakkhaṇaṃ.

But in the case of probation until purity, if he undertook it thinking, 'I was impure for about a month,' and then while undergoing probation he makes a new determination for a shorter or longer period, he must undergo probation for that very amount of time. There is no need for the act of granting probation to be done again. For this probation until purity is such that it ascends upwards and also descends downwards. This is its characteristic.

Samodahitvāti mūlāpattiṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā, pakkhipitvāti attho. Appaṭicchannā ce antarāpatti, mūlāya paṭikassanaṃ akatvā pubbe gahitaparivāseneva parivasitabbaṃ. Yo pana āpattiṃ āpajjitvā vibbhamitvā puna upasampanno [M 0.0058] hutvāpi paṭicchādeti, yo ca pubbe paṭicchādetvā pacchā na paṭicchādeti, yo ca ubhayattha paṭicchādeti, sabbesaṃ paṭicchannadivasavasena parivāso dātabbo. “Purimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe vā”ti ca “pacchimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe vā”ti (cūḷava. 166 ādayo) ca pāḷiyaṃ vuttattā dve bhikkhū visuddhikaṃ āpannā honti, te suddhikadiṭṭhino honti. Eko chādeti, eko na chādeti. Yo chādeti, so dukkaṭaṃ desāpetabbo. “Ubhopi yathādhammaṃ kārāpetabbā”ti (cūḷava. 181) vacanato yaṃ kañci āpattiṃ chādetvā dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatīti veditabbo.

'Having included' means having placed, having inserted it in the position of the root offense. If there is an unconcealed intervening offense, one should undergo probation with the previously undertaken probation period, without being sent back to the beginning. But as for one who, having committed an offense, disrobes, and then, having been ordained again, conceals it; or one who conceals it before but does not conceal it after; or one who conceals it in both instances—for all of them, probation should be given according to the number of days of concealment. Because it is said in the Pāli, 'in the former aggregate of offenses' and 'in the latter aggregate of offenses' (Cūḷavagga 166 ff.), if two monks are undertaking a purification process, they hold the view that they are pure. One conceals, one does not conceal. The one who conceals should be made to confess an offense of wrong-doing. From the statement, 'Both should be dealt with according to the Dhamma' (Cūḷavagga 181), it should be understood that one incurs an offense of wrong-doing by concealing any offense whatsoever.

Tesu gatesu vā agatesu vā purimanayeneva paṭipajjitabbanti ettha ūne gaṇe caraṇaṃ, anuṭṭhahanaṃ ekarattampi gaṇena vippavāsaṃ, sace rattiyā ekakkhaṇena saṅgho vasati, sace so pure aruṇameva kenaci karaṇīyena gatoti etthapi mānattepi evaṃ jāte. “Ayañca yasmā gaṇassa ārocetvā, bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāva vasi, tenassa ūne gaṇe caraṇadoso vā vippavāso vā na hotī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā tena ārocite muhuttampi nisīditvā gatepi vippavāso natthi. Pārivāsikassa, ukkhittakassa ca pakatattena tasmiṃ vasanaṃ udakapātena vāritaṃ, tasmā nānūpacārepi ekacchanne na vaṭṭati.

Regarding 'whether they have gone or not gone, one should proceed in the same way as before': here, wandering in an incomplete group, not undertaking the observance, being separated from the group for even one night—if the Saṅgha dwells for a single moment of the night, or if he has gone on some business just before dawn—when such a thing has occurred even during the mānatta period, it is the same. It is said in the Samantapāsādikā (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 97): 'And because this one dwelt only after informing the group and taking note of the presence of the monks, for him there is no fault of wandering in an incomplete group or of separation.' Therefore, when he has informed them, even if he leaves after sitting for just a moment, there is no separation. For a probationer and for one who is suspended, dwelling in that place is barred due to their special status, as if by a line drawn with water. Therefore, it is not permissible to be under the same roof even in a separate area.

Idāni pāṭhavicāraṇā veditabbā – “nava paṭhamāpattikā cattāro yāvatatiyakā”ti idaṃ sabhāvaniyamavacanaṃ. Tena vuṭṭhānaṃ aniyamanti dasseti. Ekaccāpattivuṭṭhānañhi kammatopi [V 0.0054] hoti akammatopi, na evaṃ āpajjananti vuttaṃ hoti. Aññataraṃ vā aññataraṃ vāti tesaṃ dvidhā bhinnānampi vuṭṭhānakkamabhedābhāvadīpakavacanaṃ. Yāvatīhaṃ, tāvatīhanti ettha ahaparicchedo aruṇavasena. “Jāna”nti iminā jānanappaṭicchannassa akāmā parivatthabbanti dasseti. Tena bhikkhunā akāmā parivatthabbanti tena bhikkhunā vasatā akāmā parivatthabbaṃ, na parivattitaliṅgenāti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Parivutthaparivāsenāti ādimhi parivutthaparivāseneva parivāsato uttari itivārena ādito bhikkhunāva chārattaṃ, parivattitaliṅgena uddhampi bhikkhumānattāya paṭipajjitabbaṃ, na parivāse viya tappaccayā aciṇṇamānatto. Ciṇṇamānattova abbhetabbo, na itaro, na parivāse viya mānattārahe, pakkhamānattañca [M 0.0059] carantiyā bhikkhuniyā liṅgaṃ parivattātikkame sati ciṇṇamānatto bhikkhu hoti, puna bhikkhumānattaṃ gahetvā ciṇṇamānattova bhikkhu abbhetabboti dasseti.

Now the examination of the reading should be understood. 'Nine are first offenses, four are up-to-the-third offenses'—this is a statement of a natural rule. By this it shows that the rehabilitation is not fixed. For rehabilitation from some offenses occurs both by a formal act and without a formal act; it means that the incurring of them is not like this. 'Either one or the other' is a statement indicating that although they are divided in two, there is no difference in the sequence of rehabilitation. In 'for as many days... for so many days,' the determination of days is by means of the dawn. By 'knowing,' it shows that one who knowingly conceals must undergo probation unwillingly. 'By that monk, probation must be undergone unwillingly' is said to show that probation must be undergone by that monk while dwelling as such, not by one whose gender has changed. 'By one who has completed probation': at the outset, by one who has completed probation; further than probation, in this way, from the beginning the six-night period is for the monk. One whose gender has changed must undertake the monk's mānatta even for the period beyond; he is not one who has not practiced mānatta on account of that, as in the case of probation. Only one who has completed mānatta is to be rehabilitated, not another; not one who is merely eligible for mānatta, as in the case of probation. And when a nun practicing the half-month mānatta transgresses by changing her gender, she becomes a monk who has completed mānatta. It shows that, having undertaken the monk's mānatta again, only as a monk who has completed mānatta is he to be rehabilitated.

Yattha siyāti yassaṃ samānasaṃvāsakasīmāyampi vīsatigaṇo bhikkhusaṅgho atthi. Ekenapi ce ūno vīsatigaṇoti na yujjati, ūno ce. Na hi vīsatigaṇo, saṅgho ce ūno. Tasmā “ekenapi ce ūno saṅgho”ti ettakameva vattabbanti ce? Na, catuvaggapañcavaggadasavaggappasaṅganivāraṇappayojanato. Tasmā vīsativaggo bhikkhusaṅgho ce bhikkhunā ekenapi ūno, naṭṭho daṭṭhabbo. Keci pana vinaye appakataññuno “yathā atirekacatuvaggopi saṅgho catuvaggakaraṇīye kamme ‘catuvaggo’ti vuccati, tathā pañcavaggadasavaggakaraṇīye kamme atirekapañcavaggadasavaggopi ‘pañcavaggadasavaggo’ti vuccati. Tasmā ūnopi catuvaggapañcavaggadasavaggavīsativaggovā”ti maññeyyuṃ, tesaṃ maññanānivāraṇatthaṃ “ekenapi ce ūno”tiādi vuttaṃ. Atha vā vīsati bhikkhusaṅgho ce, ṭhapetvā ekenapi ce ūno appakatatto, taṃ ṭhapetvā ekenapi ceti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Ayaṃ tattha sāmīcīti vacanaṃ yaṃ vuttaṃ sabbattha “tassa āpattiyā parivāsaṃ deti, mūlāya paṭikassati, mānattaṃ deti, abbhetī”ti, tassa āvibhāvakaraṇatthaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tena tesu ayaṃ yathāvuttā sāmīci niyatā icchitabbā, na rājasikkhāpadādīsu viya aniyatā. Tattha hi kenaci antarāyena taṃ sāmīcimakarontepi anāpattīti dīpitaṃ hoti.

Where there may be: in any boundary of common residence where there is a community of twenty bhikkhus. Even if it is short by one, it is not considered a group of twenty; if it is short, it is not a group of twenty, for the community is incomplete. Therefore, should only this much be said: 'even if the community is short by one'? No, for the purpose of preventing the application to groups of four, five, or ten. Therefore, if a community of twenty bhikkhus is short by even one bhikkhu, it is to be regarded as invalid. However, some who are unskilled in the Vinaya might think, "Just as a community exceeding four is called 'a group of four' in a formal act requiring four, so too in a formal act requiring five or ten, a community exceeding five or ten is called 'a group of five or ten.' Therefore, even if it is short, it may still be considered a group of four, five, ten, or twenty." To prevent such misconceptions, it is said, "Even if short by one," and so on. Alternatively, if there is a community of twenty bhikkhus, and one is incompetent, he is to be excluded; even with his exclusion, it is short by one. This is how the meaning should be understood here. The statement "This is the proper procedure" refers to what is said everywhere: "He gives probation for that offense, sends him back to the origin, gives the mānatta, and rehabilitates him." It should be understood that this is stated to make it manifest. Therefore, in these cases, this proper procedure as stated should be considered fixed, not unfixed as in the royal training rules, and so on. For in that case, it is shown that even if one does not perform the proper procedure due to some obstacle, there is no offense.

Saṅghādisesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Saṅghādisesa is concluded.

Aniyatakaṇḍaṃ

The Section on the Undetermined Matters

1. Paṭhamāniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the First Undetermined Training Rule

Aniyate [M 0.0060][V 0.0055] āditova idaṃ pakiṇṇakaṃ. Seyyathidaṃ – idaṃ aniyatakaṇḍaṃ nippayojanaṃ tattha apubbābhāvatoti ce? Na, garukalahukabhedabhinnāpattiropanāropanakkamalakkhaṇadīpanappayojanato. Ettha hi “sā ce evaṃ vadeyya ‘ayyo mayā…pe… so ca taṃ paṭijānāti, āpattiyā kāretabbo’”tiādinā (pārā. 446) āpattiyā garukāya, lahukāya ca āropanakkamalakkhaṇaṃ, “na kāretabbo”ti iminā anāropanakkamalakkhaṇañca dassitaṃ. Lakkhaṇadīpanato ādimhi, ante vā uddisitabbanti ce? Na, asambhavato. Kathaṃ na tāva ādimhi sambhavati, yesamidaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ, tesaṃ sikkhāpadānaṃ adassitattā. Na ante garukamissakattā. Tasmā garukalahukānaṃ majjhe eva uddisitabbataṃ arahati ubhayamissakattā. Yā tattha pācittiyasaṅkhātā lahukāpatti dassitā, sāpi garukāti kathitā. Tenevāha “methunadhammasannissitakilesasaṅkhātena rahassādenā”tiādi. Tasmā garukānaṃ eva anantaraṃ uddiṭṭhantipi eke. Evaṃ sati paṭhamāniyatamevālaṃ tāvatā lakkhaṇadīpanasiddhito, kiṃ dutiyenāti ce? Na, okāsaniyamapaccayamicchāgāhanivāraṇappayojanato. “Paṭicchanne āsane alaṃkammaniye”ti okāsaniyamato hi tabbiparīte okāse idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ na vikappitanti micchāgāho hoti. Taṃnivāraṇato dutiyāniyatampi sātthakamevāti adhippāyo. Kasmā? Okāsabhedato, rahobhedadīpanato, rahonisajjassādabhedadīpanato. Okāsaniyamabhāve ca rahonisajjassādabhedo jāto. Dvinnaṃ rahonisajjasikkhāpadānaṃ nānāttajānanañca siyā tathā kāyasaṃsaggabhedadīpanato. Nālaṃ kammaniyepi hi okāse appaṭicchanne, paṭicchannepi vā nisinnāya vātapānakavāṭacchiddādīhi nikkhantakesādiggahaṇena kāyasaṃsaggo labbhatīti evamādayopi nayā vitthārato veditabbā.

This section on the Undetermined Matters is, from the outset, a miscellaneous one. Namely: is this section on the Undetermined Matters without purpose, there being no precedent for it? No, because it serves the purpose of clarifying the characteristics of imposing and not imposing an offense, which are distinguished by being heavy and light. Here, indeed, by the statement, "If she were to say thus, 'Venerable, by me…' and he admits it, he is to be dealt with for the offense," and so on (Pārā. 446), the characteristic of imposing a heavy offense and a light offense is shown, while by the statement, "he is not to be dealt with," the characteristic of not imposing is also indicated. Should it be recited at the beginning or at the end for the purpose of clarifying the characteristics? No, because it is impossible. How so? It is not possible at the beginning because the training rules whose characteristics these are have not yet been shown. It is not possible at the end because it would be mixed with heavy offenses. Therefore, it is fitting that it should be recited in the middle, between heavy and light offenses, because it is a mixture of both. The light offense designated as a pācittiya that is shown there is also spoken of as heavy. Hence it is said, "by the enjoyment of seclusion, which is reckoned as a defilement connected with sexual intercourse," and so on. Therefore, some say it should be recited immediately after the heavy offenses. Thus, if the clarification of the characteristics is accomplished by the first Undetermined Rule alone, what need is there for the second? No, because it serves the purpose of preventing wrong assumptions regarding the condition of a stipulated place. For by the stipulation, "on a concealed place suitable for the act," if the place is otherwise, the wrong assumption arises that this characteristic is not applicable. By preventing that, the second Undetermined Rule is also meaningful—this is the intention. Why? Due to the distinction in the place, the clarification of the distinction in seclusion, and the clarification of the distinction in the pleasure of sitting in seclusion. When there is a stipulation of the place, the distinction in the pleasure of sitting in seclusion arises. There could also be knowledge of the difference between the two rules on sitting in seclusion, as well as the clarification of the distinction in bodily contact. For even in a place not suitable for the act, whether unconcealed or concealed, bodily contact can be obtained by grasping hair and so on, protruding through windows, door-gaps, and the like—such methods should be understood in detail.

Tatridaṃ [V 0.0056] mukhamattanidassanaṃ – okāsabhedatoti alaṃkammaniyanālaṃkammaniyabhedato. Paṭicchannampi hi ekaccaṃ nālaṃkammaniyaṃ vātapānādinā antaritattā[M 0.0061], ubhayappaṭicchannampi ekaccaṃ nālaṃkammaniyaṃ vijānataṃ ajjhokāsattā. Rahobhedadīpanatoti ettha rahabhāvasāmaññepi raho dvidhā paṭicchannāpaṭicchannabhedatoti adhippāyo. Rahonisajjassādabhedadīpanatoti methunassādavasena nisajjā, duṭṭhullassādavasena nisajjāti tādisassa bhedassa dīpanatoti attho. “Idha āgatanayattā bhikkhunipātimokkhe idaṃ kaṇḍaṃ parihīnanti veditabba”nti vadanti. “Aṭṭhuppattiyā tattha anuppannattā”ti eke, taṃ anekantabhāvadīpanato ayuttaṃ. Sabbabuddhakāle hi bhikkhūnaṃ pañca, bhikkhunīnaṃ cattāro ca uddesā santi. Pātimokkhuddesapaññattiyā asādhāraṇattā tattha niddiṭṭhasaṅghādisesapācittiyānanti eke. Tāsañhi bhikkhunīnaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalika (pāci. 658) -aṭṭhavatthuka (pāci. 675) -vasena kāyasaṃsaggaviseso pārājikavatthu, “hatthaggahaṇaṃ vā sādiyeyya, kāyaṃ vā tadatthāya upasaṃhareyyā”ti (pāci. 675) vacanato sādiyanampi, “santiṭṭheyya vā”ti (pāci. 675) vacanato ṭhānampi, “saṅketaṃ vā gaccheyyā”ti (pāci. 675) vacanato gamanampi, “channaṃ vā anupaviseyyā”ti (pāci. 675) vacanato paṭicchannaṭṭhānappavesopi hoti, tathā “rattandhakāre appadīpe, paṭicchanne okāse ajjhokāse ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā”ti (pāci. 839) vacanato duṭṭhullavācāpi pācittiyavatthukanti katvā tāsaṃ aññathā aniyatakaṇḍassa avattabbatāpattito na vuttanti tesaṃ adhippāyo. Pakiṇṇakaṃ.

Here is a mere indication of the main points: due to the distinction in the place, that is, the distinction between what is suitable for the act and what is not. For some places, though concealed, are not suitable for the act because they are obstructed by windows or the like. And some places, though fully concealed, are not suitable for the act because they are in an open space for those who know. The 'clarification of the distinction in seclusion' means that even though seclusion is a common factor, seclusion is of two kinds: concealed and unconcealed. The 'clarification of the distinction in the pleasure of sitting in seclusion' means that the sitting is according to the pleasure of sexual intercourse or the sitting is according to the pleasure of offensive speech—this is the meaning of the clarification of such a distinction. Some say, "It should be understood that this section is omitted from the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha because of the method presented here." Others say, "Because it did not originate there in the Aṭṭhuppatti (origin story)," but that is incorrect because of the explanation of its non-exclusivity. In all eras of the Buddhas, there are five recitations for bhikkhus and four for bhikkhunīs. Some say that because the laying down of the Pātimokkha recitation is not common to both Orders, the Saṅghādisesa and Pācittiya rules mentioned there are not included. For those bhikkhunīs, specific kinds of bodily contact, such as the case of raised knees (Pāc. 658) and the eight-based case (Pāc. 675), constitute a Pārājika offense; due to the statement, "If she approves of the taking of her hand, or offers her body for that purpose" (Pāc. 675), even approval is included; due to the statement, "or stays there" (Pāc. 675), even staying is included; due to the statement, "or goes to a pre-arranged place" (Pāc. 675), even going is included; due to the statement, "or enters a covered place" (Pāc. 675), even entering a covered place is included. Similarly, due to the statement, "if she stands alone or talks alone with one man in the darkness without a lamp, in a covered place or in an open space" (Pāc. 839), even offensive speech constitutes a Pācittiya offense. Therefore, their intention is that these are not mentioned because, for them, these offenses would otherwise have to be stated in the Aniyata section. Miscellaneous.

“Desanāvuṭṭhānagāminīnaṃ āpattīnaṃ vasena alajjiādayo lajjīnaṃ codessantī”ti āgatattā lajjipaggahatthāya patirūpāyapi upāsikāya vacanena akatvā bhikkhusseva paṭiññāya kātabbanti āpattiyo pana lakkhaṇadassanatthaṃ paññattaṃ vitthāranayameva gahetvā vattuṃ yuttaṃ “ime kho panāyasmanto dve aniyatā dhammā”ti (pārā. 443) uddesadassanattāti likhitaṃ. Sotassa rahoti ettha rahoti vacanasāmaññato vuttaṃ. Duṭṭhullasāmaññato duṭṭhullārocanappaṭicchādanasikkhāpadesu pārājikavacanaṃ viya. Tasmā “cakkhusseva pana raho ‘raho’ti idha adhippeto”ti vuttaṃ. Kathaṃ paññāyatīti ce? “Mātugāmo nāma…pe… antamaso tadahujātāpi dārikā”ti (pārā. 445) vuttattā duṭṭhullobhāsanaṃ idha nādhippetanti dīpitamevāti. Antodvādasahatthepīti [M 0.0062] pi-saddena apihitakavāṭassa gabbhassa dvāre nisinnopīti attho. Acelakavagge rahopaṭicchannāsanasikkhāpade (pāci. 288) “yo koci viññū puriso dutiyo hotī”ti imassa anurūpato “itthīnaṃ pana satampi anāpattiṃ na karotiyevā”ti vuttaṃ. “Alaṃkammaniyeti sakkā hoti methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitu”nti (pārā. 445) vibhaṅge [V 0.0057] vacanato rahonisajjassādo cettha methunadhammasannissitakileso, na dutiye viya duṭṭhullavācassādakileso. Tasmā ca paññāyati sotassa raho nādhippetoti.

Because it is stated, 'The shameless will accuse the conscientious regarding offenses that are resolved by confession,' it is for the sake of upholding the conscientious that this should be done only by the monk's acknowledgement and not by the word of even a suitable female lay follower. Furthermore, it is fitting to speak of the offenses, which are laid down for the purpose of showing their characteristics, by taking up the detailed method, as it is written, 'Venerable sirs, these are the two Undetermined Rules' (Pārā. 443), for the purpose of recitation and illustration. Here, in 'private for the ear,' 'private' is spoken of in the general sense of speech. This is like the term 'pārājika' in the training rules on declaring and concealing lewdness, in the general sense of lewdness. Therefore, it is said, 'Here, 'private' is intended only for the eye.' If it is asked how this is known, it is because it is stated, 'A woman… even a girl born that very day' (Pārā. 445), which clarifies that lewd speech is not intended here. In 'even within twelve cubits,' the particle 'pi' implies 'even if one is sitting at the door of a chamber with an unclosed door.' In the Acelaka section, in the training rule on sitting in a private, concealed place (Pāc. 288), in accordance with 'whatever discerning man is the second person,' it is said, 'but even a hundred women do not make it a non-offense.' In the analysis, it is stated, '“Suitable for the act” means it is possible to engage in sexual intercourse' (Pārā. 445). Here, the pleasure of sitting in seclusion is a defilement connected with sexual intercourse, not a defilement connected with the pleasure of lewd speech, as in the second case. Therefore, it is known that 'private for the ear' is not intended here.

Tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ aññatarena vadeyyāti rahonisajjasikkhāpadavasena nisinnassa tassānusārena pācittiyameva avatvā pārājikasaṅghādisesāyapi āpattiyā bhedadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Puna āpattippaṭijānanaṃ avatvā kasmā “nisajjaṃ bhikkhu paṭijānamāno”ti vatthuppaṭijānanaṃ vuttanti? Vuccate – āpattiyā codite vinayadharena “kismiṃ vatthusmi”nti pucchite cuditakena “imasmiṃ vatthusmi”nti vutte vinayadharena “īdisaṃ nāma akāsī”ti pucchite so vatthuṃ paṭijānamānova kāretabboti dassanatthaṃ “nisajjaṃ bhikkhu paṭijānamāno”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ nisajjaṃ paṭijānamānopi āpattiyāva kāretabboti? Anurūpameva. Evaṃ pana gahetabbaṃ – tiṇṇampi āpattīnaṃ vatthūni aggahetvā idha sikkhāpadavasena nisajjameva vuttaṃ. Tasmiṃ gahitepi hi āpatti gahitāva hotīti. Yena vā sāti ettha vā-saddo “tena so bhikkhu kāretabbo vā”ti yojetabbo. So ca vikappattho. Tasmā “kāretabbo vā paṭijānamāno, na vā kāretabbo appaṭijānamāno”ti attho. Tena vuttaṃ “paṭijānamāno vā”tiādi. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadavasena nisajjapaccayā āpattiyā vuttattā sesesupi sesasikkhāpadavasena āpatti gahetabbā. “Samuṭṭhānādīni paṭhamapārājikasadisānevā”ti vuttattā idha duṭṭhullobhāsanassa anadhippetabhāvo veditabbo.

When it says, 'he should speak of any one of the three matters,' this is stated in accordance with the training rule on sitting in seclusion. It is stated not merely as a Pācittiya offense for the one who was sitting, but to show the distinction of offenses, which could also be Pārājika or Saṅghādisesa. Again, without mentioning the acknowledgement of the offense, why is the acknowledgement of the matter mentioned as 'a monk acknowledging the sitting'? It is explained thus: When charged with an offense and asked by a Vinaya expert, 'Regarding what matter?' and the accused says, 'Regarding this matter,' and the Vinaya expert asks, 'Did you do such and such?'—it is said, 'a monk acknowledging the sitting,' to show that he should be dealt with only if he acknowledges the matter. If so, should even one who acknowledges the sitting be dealt with for the offense? It is indeed appropriate. However, it should be understood thus: without taking up the matters of all three offenses, here only the sitting is mentioned in terms of the training rule. For when that is taken up, the offense is also taken up. In 'or by which,' the particle 'or' should be construed as 'or that monk should be dealt with.' And that is in the sense of an alternative. Therefore, the meaning is: 'He should be dealt with if he acknowledges, or he should not be dealt with if he does not acknowledge.' Thus it is said, 'acknowledging or,' and so on. Since the offense is stated as being conditioned by sitting in accordance with the training rule on sitting in seclusion, in the other cases too, the offense should be understood in accordance with the respective training rules. Because it is said, 'The origin and so forth are just like the first Pārājika,' it should be understood that lewd speech is not intended here.

Paṭhamāniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first Undetermined Training Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyāniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Undetermined Training Rule

Saṅghādisesena [M 0.0063] vāti kāyasaṃsaggaduṭṭhullobhāsanena. Tasmā evaṃ kāyasaṃsaggavāro pāḷiyampi vutto. Anandho abadhiroti anandho kāyasaṃsaggaṃ passati, abadhiro duṭṭhullaṃ suṇāti, tasmā eva adinnādānasadisānevāti vutta”nti likhitaṃ. Ettha ca kāyavācācittato samuṭṭhānaṃ kathanti ce? Kāyasaṃsaggañhi samāpajjanto duṭṭhullampi bhaṇati, duṭṭhullaṃ bhaṇanto nisīdati cāti sambhavati, duṭṭhullameva vā sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tañhi adinnādānasamuṭṭhānanti.

'Or by a Saṅghādisesa offense' means by bodily contact or lewd speech. Therefore, the section on bodily contact is also stated thus in the Pāli. 'Not blind, not deaf' means one who is not blind sees the bodily contact, and one who is not deaf hears the lewd speech. Hence, it is written, 'it is just like taking what is not given.' And here, if it is asked how the origin is from body, speech, and mind: Indeed, while engaging in bodily contact, one also speaks lewdly; and while speaking lewdly, it is possible that one also sits down. Or it is said with reference to lewd speech alone, for that has an origin like taking what is not given.

Yo [V 0.0058] desanaṃ sabbavidūpamova;

Nānānayākāravicittabhedaṃ;

Ñātuṃ upāyāna mano satimā;

Taṃ lābhahetuṃ na karoti puññanti.

He who is like the All-Knower in his teaching—diverse in methods, varied in distinctions—that mindful one, with a mind to understand the means, does not perform meritorious deeds for the sake of gain.

Dutiyāniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Second Undetermined Training Rule is concluded.

Aniyatavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Undetermined is concluded.

Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Offenses Entailing Forfeiture

1. Cīvaravaggo

1. The Chapter on Robes

1. Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Kathina Training Rule

Nissaggiyakaṇḍe [M 0.0064][V 0.0059] tiṇṇaṃ kathinasikkhāpadānaṃ, vassikasāṭikaaccekacīvarasāsaṅkasikkhāpadānañca ekadesanāya tathākiṇṇāpattikkhandhāva veditabbā –

In the Chapter on Offenses Entailing Forfeiture, the three Kathina training rules, and the training rules concerning the rainy-season cloth, the emergency robe, and the doubtful robe, should be understood as a partial exposition and likewise as a collection of mixed offenses.

Kathinaṃ yassa cattāro, sahajā samayadvayaṃ;

Channaṃ sikkhāpadānañca, ekadesavinicchayo.

The Kathina has four aspects: its inherent qualities, its two periods; and for the six training rules, there is a partial determination.

Tattha kathinanti “saṅghassa anumodanāya, gaṇassa anumodanāya, puggalassa atthārā saṅghassa atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti (pari. 414) vacanato tesaṃyeva anumodanādidhammānaṃ saṅgaho kathinaṃ nāma. Yathāha “kathinaṃ jānitabbanti tesaññeva dhammānaṃ saṅgaho samavāyo nāmaṃ nāmakamma”ntiādi (pari. 412). Tasmā kathinanti idaṃ bahūsu dhammesu nāmamattaṃ, na paramatthato eko dhammo. Ko panassa atthāroti? Tadekadesova khīrassa dhārā viya. Yathā cāha “atthāro ekena dhammena saṅgahito vacībhedenā”ti. Sahajā nāma aṭṭha mātikā, dve palibodhā, pañcānisaṃsāti ime pannarasa dhammā. Samayadvayaṃ nāma kathinatthārasamayo, cīvarasamayo cāti. Tattha kathinatthārasamayo vassānassa pacchimo māso. Cīvarasamayo nāma anatthate kathine ayaṃ kattikamāso, atthate cattāro hemantikā cāti pañca māsā.

Herein, 'kathina' means the collection of those very qualities—approval and so on—in accordance with the statement (Pari. 414): 'By the Sangha's approval, by the group's approval, by the individual's spreading, the kathina is spread for the Sangha.' As it is said (Pari. 412): 'The kathina should be known as the gathering, the combination, the name, the designation of those very qualities,' and so on. Therefore, 'kathina' is merely a name for many qualities, not a single reality in the ultimate sense. What, then, is its spreading? It is just one part of it, like a stream of milk. As it is also said: 'The spreading is comprised under one quality, but with a variety of expressions.' The 'inherent qualities' are the eight matrices, the two obstructions, and the five benefits—these fifteen qualities. The 'two periods' are the kathina-spreading period and the robe period. Therein, the kathina-spreading period is the last month of the rains-residence. The robe period is this month of Kattika if the kathina is not spread, and if it is spread, the four winter months—thus, five months.

Tattha aṭṭha mātikā nāma pakkamanantikādayo. Tā sabbāpi atthārena ekato uppajjanti nāma. Tabbhāvabhāvitāya atthāre sati uddhāro sambhavati. Tattha kathinatthārena ekuppādā [V 0.0060] ekanirodhā antarubbhāro sahubbhāro, avasesā kathinubbhārā ekuppādā, nānānirodhā ca. Tattha ekanirodhāti atthārena saha nirodhā, antarubbhārasahubbhārānaṃ uddhārābhāvo ekakkhaṇe hotīti attho. Sesā nānā nirujjhanti nāma. Tesu hi uddhārabhāvaṃ pattesupi atthāro tiṭṭhati evāti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ atthavibhāvanā. Sace atthate kathine bhikkhusmiṃ sāpekkhe [M 0.0065] tamhā āvāsā pakkamante saṅgho antarubbhāraṃ karoti, tassa bhikkhuno paṭhamameva mūlāvāse niṭṭhitacīvarapalibodhābhāvepi sati antarubbhāre palibodho chijjati satipi sāpekkhatāya saussāhattā. Iminā pariyāyena pakkamanantiko kathinuddhāro atthārena ekuppādo nānānirodho hoti. Tathā antarubbhāre sati suṇantassāpi yāva cīvaraniṭṭhānaṃ na gacchati, tāva parihārasambhavato niṭṭhānantiko. Yāva sanniṭṭhānaṃ na gacchati, tāva parihārasambhavato sanniṭṭhānantiko. Yāva na nassati, tāva parihārasambhavato nāsanantiko. Yāva na suṇāti, tāva parihārasambhavato savanantiko. Yāva cīvarāsā na chijjati, tāva parihārasambhavato āsāvacchediko. Yāva sīmaṃ nātikkamati, tāva parihārasambhavato sīmātikkantiko. Atthārena ekuppādo nānānirodho hotīti veditabbo.

Herein, the eight matrices are those beginning with 'pakkamanantika'. All of them arise together with the spreading. When the spreading has been established, its withdrawal becomes possible. Among them, the interim withdrawal and the simultaneous withdrawal are of single arising and single cessation with the kathina spreading; the remaining kathina withdrawals are of single arising but of various cessations. Herein, 'of single cessation' means ceasing together with the spreading; the meaning is that the withdrawal for the interim and simultaneous withdrawals occurs in a single moment. The others are said to cease at various times. For even when they have reached the state of withdrawal, the spreading still persists—this is the explanation of the meaning in the commentary. If, while the kathina is spread, a monk with an expectation departs from that residence, the Sangha performs an interim withdrawal. For that monk, even if there was no initial impediment of an unfinished robe at the original residence, the impediment is cut off by the interim withdrawal, due to his expectation and enthusiasm. In this way, the 'pakkamanantika' kathina withdrawal is of single arising with the spreading but of various cessations. Similarly, when there is an interim withdrawal, for one who hears of it, as long as the robe is not completed, the privilege remains possible—hence, the 'niṭṭhānantika.' As long as the decision is not made, the privilege remains possible—hence, the 'sanniṭṭhānantika.' As long as it is not destroyed, the privilege remains possible—hence, the 'nāsanantika.' As long as it is not heard, the privilege remains possible—hence, the 'savanantika.' As long as the hope for the robe is not cut off, the privilege remains possible—hence, the 'āsāvacchedika.' As long as the boundary is not crossed, the privilege remains possible—hence, the 'sīmātikkantika.' It should be understood that these are of single arising with the spreading but of various cessations.

Tattha antarubbhārasahubbhārā dve antosīmāyaṃ eva sambhavanti, na bahisīmāyaṃ. Pakkamanasavanasīmātikkantikā bahisīmāyameva sambhavanti, na antosīmāyaṃ. Niṭṭhānasaaāṭṭhānāsāvacchedikā antosīmāyañceva bahisīmāyañca. Antarubbhāro saṅghāyatto, pakkamananiṭṭhānasanniṭṭhānasīmātikkantikā puggalādhīnā, sesā tadubhayaviparītā.

Herein, the two, interim withdrawal and simultaneous withdrawal, are possible only within the boundary, not outside the boundary. Those ending with departure, hearing, and crossing the boundary are possible only outside the boundary, not within the boundary. Those ending with completion, decision, destruction, and cutting off of hope are possible both within and outside the boundary. Interim withdrawal is dependent on the Sangha; those ending with departure, completion, decision, and crossing the boundary are dependent on individuals; the rest are the opposite of both.

Tattha “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”nti iminā cīvarapalibodhābhāvameva dīpeti. Na āvāsapalibodhābhāvaṃ. “Ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti iminā ubhayapalibodhābhāvaṃ dīpeti, tasmā ubhayapalibodhābhāvadīpanatthaṃ tadeva vattabbanti ce? Na, visesattā. Kathaṃ? Kāmañcetaṃ tasmā “ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti kesañci kathinuddhārānaṃ nānānirodhattā, saṅghapuggalādhīnānadhīnattā ca antobahiubhayasīmāsu niyamāniyamato ca ubbhatasmiṃ kathine saṅghassa, na puggalassa ubbhataṃ hoti, tathāpi “ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti idaṃ sāmaññavacanaṃ. Tasmā “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”nti iminā niyameti.

Herein, by 'when the robe is completed,' it indicates only the absence of the robe impediment, not the absence of the dwelling impediment. By 'when the kathina is withdrawn,' it indicates the absence of both impediments. Therefore, should it be said that only that should be stated to show the absence of both impediments? No, because of the distinction. How so? Although it is true that—because some kathina withdrawals are of various cessations, and are dependent or not dependent on the Sangha or individuals, and are restricted or unrestricted within, outside, or in both boundaries—when the kathina is withdrawn, it is withdrawn for the Sangha, not for an individual; nevertheless, 'when the kathina is withdrawn' is a general expression. Therefore, by 'when the robe is completed,' it specifies a restriction.

Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti – saṅghassa antarubbhārena ubbhatasmiṃ kathine acchinnacīvarapalibodho bahisīmāgato pacchā gantvā attano sīmāgato aniṭṭhitacīvaro ānisaṃsaṃ labhati evāti katvā “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”nti vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tattha āvāsapalibodho nāma vasati vā tasmiṃ [V 0.0061] āvāse, sāpekkho vā pakkamati. Cīvarapalibodho nāma cīvaraṃ akataṃ [M 0.0066] vippakataṃ, cīvarāsānupacchinnā, tabbiparītena apalibodho veditabbo. Tattha anatthatakathinānaṃ cīvarakālasamaye niyamato cattāro ānisaṃsā labbhanti, asamādānacāro aniyamato. Tena sāsaṅkasikkhāpadaṃ vuttaṃ. Kathaṃ cattāro niyatāti ce? “Cīvarakālasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo māso”ti (pārā. 649) vacanato anatthatakathinānaṃ tasmiṃ māse yāvadatthacīvaraṃ siddhaṃ, tathā tatiyakathinasikkhāpade (pārā. 497 ādayo) akālacīvaraṃ nāma piṭṭhisamayato paṭṭhāya taṃ paṭiggahetvā saṅghato labhitabbaṃ ce, yāva cīvarakālasamayaṃ nikkhipitvā bhājetvā gahetabbaṃ. Puggalikaṃ ce, vassānassa chaṭṭhapakkhassa pañcamito paṭṭhāya yāva cīvarakālasamayaṃ anadhiṭṭhitaṃ avikappitaṃ vaṭṭati accekacīvarasikkhāpadena anuññātattā, na tato paraṃ. Tadā uppannacīvarassa paṭisiddhattā paṭhamakathinena. Tattha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayo saṅghikaṃ sandhāya, tathā porāṇagaṇṭhipade cāti veditabbaṃ.

What is meant is this: It should be understood that 'when the robe is completed' is said because, when the kathina has been withdrawn by the Sangha's interim withdrawal, a monk whose robe impediment is not cut off, who has gone outside the boundary and later returned to his own boundary, still obtains the benefit even if his robe is not completed. Herein, a dwelling impediment means either dwelling in that residence or departing with an attachment. A robe impediment means the robe is unmade or incomplete, or the hope for a robe has not been cut off; the absence of an impediment should be understood as the opposite of this. For those for whom the kathina has not been spread, four benefits are obtained by rule during the robe-making time, while wandering without taking leave is unregulated. Therefore, the training rule concerning doubt is stated. If it is asked how the four are regulated: From the statement, 'The robe-making time for one for whom the kathina has not been spread is the last month of the rains season' (Pārā. 649), it follows that for those for whom the kathina has not been spread, as much robe-cloth as is needed is available in that month. Likewise, in the third Kathina training rule (Pārā. 497 ff.), what is called untimely robe-cloth, if it is to be received from the Sangha, may be accepted starting from the 'piṭṭhisamaya' and kept until the robe-making time, then distributed and taken. If it is personal, from the fifth day of the sixth fortnight of the rains season up to the robe-making time, it is allowable to keep it undetermined and unallocated, as permitted by the training rule on urgent robes, but not beyond that. At that time, newly arisen robe-cloth is prohibited by the first Kathina rule. Herein, it should be understood that the method stated in the commentary is with reference to what belongs to the Sangha, and likewise in the ancient gaṇṭhipada.

Paṭhamakathine (pārā. 459 ādayo) paṭhamapaññattiyā, avisesena vā ekādasame divase āpatti. Vassānassa hi antonivāraṇatthaṃ aṭṭhakathāya “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti (pārā. 462 ādayo) vuttaṃ. Eseva nayo dutiye, tatiye ca. Tena cīvarakālato pure vā anto vā uppannaṃ cīvarakālato uddhaṃ ekadivasampi parihāraṃ na labhati. Yadi labheyya, accekacīvarasikkhāpadavirodho. “Yāva cīvarakālasamayaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, tato ce uttari nikkhipeyya, nissaggiya”nti (pārā. 648) hi tattha vuttaṃ. Vassāvāsikabhāvena saṅghato laddhaṃ vuṭṭhavassattā attano santakabhūtaṃ accekacīvaraṃ cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmayato eva āpatti, na accekacīvarakālaṃ atikkāmayato āpattīti. “Anatthate kathine ekādasamāse uppanna”nti (pārā. 500) vacanato yo ca tattha cīvaruppādo, so ca nesaṃ bhavissatīti siddhaṃ, anāmantacāragaṇabhojanasikkhāpade “aññatra samayā”ti (pāci. 222 ādayo) vuttattā sesadvayaṃ siddhameva. Tasmā “kālepi ādissa dinnaṃ, etaṃ akālacīvara”nti (pārā. 500) vacanato ādissa dinnacīvaraṃ parihāraṃ na labhati.

In the first Kathina rule (Pārā. 459 ff.), according to the first enactment, an offense occurs on the eleventh day without distinction. For the purpose of preventing the end of the rains season, the commentary states, 'when the robe has been completed and the Kathina has been withdrawn by a bhikkhu' (Pārā. 462 ff.). This same principle applies to the second and third rules. Therefore, a robe that has arisen before or during the robe season does not obtain an exemption for even a single day beyond the robe season. If it were to obtain one, it would contradict the training rule concerning urgent robes. For it is said there, 'It should be kept until the time of the robe season. If one keeps it beyond that, it is to be forfeited' (Pārā. 648). An urgent robe obtained from the Sangha by virtue of having kept the rains residence, which becomes one's own possession upon having completed the rains, incurs an offense only when one lets the robe season pass, not when one lets the time for urgent robes pass. From the statement, 'When the Kathina is not spread, what has arisen in the eleventh month...' (Pārā. 500), it is established that any arising of a robe there will belong to them. And due to the statement 'except on appropriate occasions' (Pāci. 222 ff.) in the training rules concerning wandering without invitation and eating in a group, the remaining two privileges are indeed established. Therefore, from the statement, 'Even if given by designation at the proper time, this is an out-of-season robe' (Pārā. 500), a robe given by designation does not obtain an exemption.

Aparakattikāyameva vā ubbhatasmiṃ kathine labhati, evaṃ “ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti vuttattāti ce? Na vattabbaṃ. Cha ṭhānāni hi sāpekkhatāya vuttāni[M 0.0067]. Duṭṭhadosadvaye adhikaraṇacatutthaṃ, paṭhamāniyate sotassa raho, tatiyakathine ādissa dinnaṃ cīvaraṃ, accekacīvarasikkhāpade [V 0.0062] “saññāṇaṃ katvā nikkhipitabba”nti padaṃ, duṭṭhullārocanappaṭicchādanadvaye adhikaraṇaṃ, pārājikavacanañca, tīsu kathinasikkhāpadesu “aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānaṃ aññatarāyā”ti vacananti. Tattha ādissa dinnaṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghikaṃ bhājitabbacīvaraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na puggalikaṃ. Saññāṇaṃ katvā nikkhipitabbanti vassāvāsikacīvaraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Avuṭṭhavassena pacchā dātabbattā saññāṇaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ñātippavāritato laddhaṃ puggalikaṃ sandhāya. Tasmā duvidhaṃ accekacīvaraṃ saṅghe ninnaṃ, puggale ninnañcāti siddhaṃ. Tattha saṅghe pariṇataṃ accekacīvaraṃ vassūpanāyikadivasato paṭṭhāya, piṭṭhisamayato paṭṭhāya vā yāva pavāraṇā nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati eva saṅghikattā, puggalikampi “vassaṃvuṭṭhakāle gaṇhathā”ti dinnattā. Tādisañhi yāva vassaṃvuṭṭho na hoti, tāva tasseva dāyakassa santakaṃ hoti. Ettako visesahetu.

Or is it that one receives it only in the later Kattika period when the Kathina has been withdrawn, because it is stated, 'when the Kathina has been withdrawn'? This should not be said. For six instances are stated with reference to dependence: the fourth legal matter in the two cases of a malicious offense; what is private for the ear in the first undetermined rule; a robe given by designation in the third Kathina rule; the phrase 'it should be marked and set aside' in the training rule concerning urgent robes; the legal matter in the two cases of informing on and concealing a grave offense, and the statement in the Pārājika; and the statement 'one of the eight matrices' in the three Kathina training rules. Therein, the robe given by designation refers to a communal robe to be distributed, not a personal one. The phrase 'it should be marked and set aside' refers to the robe for the rains-residence. Since it must be given later by one who has not completed the rains-residence, it should be marked—this does not refer to a personal robe obtained from an invitation by relatives. Thus, it is established that there are two types of urgent robes: those assigned to the Sangha and those assigned to an individual. Among these, an urgent robe that has been assigned to the Sangha may be set aside from the day of entering the rains-residence or from the latter part of the rains until the Pavāraṇā, due to its communal nature. A personal one may also be, because it is given with the words, 'Take it at the time of having completed the rains-residence.' For such a robe remains the property of that very donor until one has completed the rains-residence. This is the specific reason.

“Anaccekacīvare anaccekacīvarasaññī cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmeti, anāpattī”ti vacanato accekacīvarakasseva so aparādho. Yena “virodho”ti vacanaṃ dasseyyāti na vinaye visesahetu pariyesitabbo. Buddhavisayattā pamāṇanti ce? Na, yadi evaṃ ettha attano santakabhūtampi accekacīvaraṃ saññāṇaṃ katvā nikkhipitabbameva, na adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ na vikappetabbaṃ na vissajjetabbaṃ. Tato “anāpatti, antosamaye adhiṭṭheti vikappeti vissajjetī”tiādivacanavirodho (pārā. 651) adhivāsetabbo siyā. Tathā “vassānassa pacchime māse kathinuddhāre kate tasmiṃ māse atthate kathine kathinuddhāradivasaṃ atikkāmeti, nissaggiyaṃ hotī”ti vacanato nissaggiyaṃ hotīti ayampi atthavirodho adhivāsetabbo siyā. Tasmiñca “anaccekacīvare anāpattī”ti vuttaṃ, tañca anadhiṭṭhitaṃ avikappitamevāti ettako visesahetu. Atirekacīvarañcetaṃ paṭhamasikkhāpadenāpatti, itaraṃ ce anāpattiyevāti imassa atthassa ayaṃ bhagavato visesahetu. Tathā atirekadasāhānāgatāyeva kattikapuṇṇamāya saṅghassa vassāvāsikatthaṃ accekacīvaraṃ viya dadamānaṃ na [M 0.0068] gahetabbaṃ, dasāhānāgatāya eva gahetabbanti ettako visesahetu. Tato aṭṭhakathānayavirodho ca adhivāsetabbo siyā. Tattha “adhiṭṭhitato paṭṭhāya uppannaṃ accekacīvaraṃ na hotī”ti vatvā aññathā nayo dassito. Porāṇagaṇṭhipade so ca nayo saṅghikaṃ upādāya vuttattā na virujjhatīti neva so ca paṭikkhitto. Yathā anaccekacīvaraṃ chaṭṭhito paṭṭhāya uppannaṃ atirekadasāhānāgatāyapi paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭiggahetvā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmayatopi anāpattīti ayampi nayo adhivāsetabbo siyā. Tato paṭhamakathinavirodho. Dasāhānāgatāya eva paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭiggahetvā [V 0.0063] cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmayato anāpattīti ce, taṃ dve dasāhe labhatīti ettako visesahetu.

According to the statement, 'Regarding a non-urgent robe, being aware that it is a non-urgent robe, one lets the robe-season pass; there is no offense,' that fault belongs only to one who has an urgent robe. Therefore, a specific reason should not be sought in the Vinaya to show a contradiction. If it is said that the Buddha's domain is the authority, this is not so. If it were so, then even an urgent robe that has become one's own property should be set aside after marking it; it should not be determined, assigned, or relinquished. Then the contradiction with statements such as, 'There is no offense if one determines, assigns, or relinquishes it within the proper time' (Pārā. 651), would have to be accepted. Similarly, according to the statement, 'If, after the Kathina has been withdrawn in the last month of the rains-residence, one lets the day of the Kathina withdrawal pass in that month when the Kathina has been spread, it becomes subject to forfeiture,' this contradiction in meaning would also have to be accepted. And in that case, it is said, 'Regarding a non-urgent robe, there is no offense,' and that refers only to what has not been determined or assigned—this is the specific reason. And this extra robe is an offense by the first training rule, whereas the other is indeed no offense—this is the Blessed One's specific reason for this meaning. Likewise, an urgent robe being given for the Sangha's rains-residence before the full moon of Kattika, when the extra ten days have not yet arrived, should not be accepted; it should be accepted only when the ten days have arrived—this is the specific reason. Then a contradiction with the method of the commentary would also have to be accepted. There, having said, 'An urgent robe that has arisen after being determined is not an urgent robe,' the method is shown otherwise. And in the ancient glossaries, that method is not contradicted because it is stated with reference to what is communal, nor is it rejected. For example, the method that a non-urgent robe that has arisen from the sixth day onward may be accepted even if the extra ten days have not arrived, and that there is no offense even for one who lets the robe-season pass after accepting it—this too would have to be accepted. This then contradicts the first Kathina rule. If it is said that it should be accepted only when the ten days have arrived, and there is no offense for one who lets the robe-season pass after accepting it, then one obtains two ten-day periods—this is the specific reason.

Antarā anāpattikkhettacīvarakālappaviṭṭhattā adhiṭṭhahitvā paccuddhaṭaṃ viya taṃ punapi dasāhe labhatīti ce? Na, kālappaveso adhiṭṭhānaṃ viya hotīti ce? Na, “vassikasāṭikaṃ vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ, tato paraṃ vikappetu”nti vacanavirodhaṃ katvā, tato paraṃ dasāhaṃ avikappentassāpi anāpatti siyā. Apica yaṃ vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “vassikasāṭikā antovasse laddhā ceva niṭṭhitā ca, antodasāhe adhiṭṭhātabbā, dasāhātikkame niṭṭhitā, tadaheva adhiṭṭhātabbā, dasāhe appahonte cīvarakālaṃ nātikkāmetabbā”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.630). Tena āpattito na mucceyya. Kālappaveso hi adhiṭṭhānapariyāyo na jātoti. Ettāvatā yathāvutto atthavikappo pāḷinayeneva patiṭṭhāpito hoti.

If it is said that because one has entered the robe-season, which is a domain of no offense, one may receive it again within ten days, as if it were determined and then withdrawn, this is not so. If it is said that entering the season is like a determination, this is not so. It would create a contradiction with the statement, 'The rains-season cloth is to be determined for the four months of the rains, and after that, it is to be assigned.' Then, there would be no offense even for one who does not assign it after those ten days. Moreover, regarding what is stated in the commentary: 'A rains-season cloth that is both obtained and finished within the rains-residence should be determined within ten days. If it is finished after the ten days have passed, it should be determined on that very day. If ten days are not sufficient, the robe-season should not be transgressed' (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.630). By this, one would not be freed from an offense. For entering the season is not in the category of a determination. Thus far, the analysis of meaning as stated is established by the method of the Pāli Canon itself.

Apicettha yaṃ vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “dasāhe appahonte cīvarakālaṃ nātikkāmetabbā”ti, tatthapi cīvarakāle uppannaṃ, dasāhe appahonte cassa karaṇaṃ natthi, taṃ accekacīvaraṃ akālacīvaramiva cīvarakālaṃ nātikkāmetabbanti siddhametaṃ. Pāḷito ca tañce antokāle uppajjati, dasāhe appahontepi uppajjati, evaṃ uppannaṃ accekacīvaraṃ accekacīvarameva na hoti. Na hi taṃ kālavisesavasena accekacīvarasaṅkhaṃ gacchati. Vuttañhetaṃ “accekacīvaraṃ nāma senāya vā gantukāmo hoti, pavāsaṃ vā gantukāmo hoti, gilāno vā hoti, gabbhinī vā hoti[M 0.0069], assaddhassa vā saddhā uppannā hoti…pe… ‘vassāvāsikaṃ dassāmī’ti evaṃ ārocitaṃ, etaṃ accekacīvaraṃ nāmā”ti (pārā. 649). Tasmā yathā taṃ cīvaraṃ nātikkāmetabbaṃ, tathā anaccekacīvarampīti siddhaṃ hoti. Tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “dasāhe appahonte cīvarakālaṃ nātikkāmetabbā”ti. Apica yadi evaṃ taṃ accekacīvarasikkhāpadameva accekacīvaraṃ cīvarakālaṃ nātikkāmetabbanti imassa pana atthavisesassa dassanatthaṃ bhagavatā paññattaṃ.

Furthermore, regarding what is stated in the commentary, 'If ten days are not sufficient, the robe-season should not be transgressed,' in that case also, for a robe that has arisen during the robe-season, when ten days are not sufficient and there is no making of it, it is established that such an urgent robe, like an out-of-season robe, should not transgress the robe-season. And according to the Pāli, if it arises within the proper time, it arises even when ten days are not sufficient. An urgent robe that has thus arisen is not an urgent robe in the full sense. For it does not receive the designation 'urgent robe' on account of a specific time. For it is said: 'An urgent robe, so-called, is when one is about to go with an army, or about to go on a journey, or is ill, or is pregnant, or when faith has arisen in one who was faithless... and so on... or when it is announced, “I will give a rains-residence robe.” This is called an urgent robe' (Pārā. 649). Therefore, it is established that that robe should not transgress the time, just as a non-urgent robe. For this reason it is stated in the commentary: 'If ten days are not sufficient, the robe-season should not be transgressed.' Moreover, if this is so, then the training rule concerning urgent robes itself was laid down by the Blessed One to show this specific distinction of meaning: that an urgent robe should not transgress the robe-season.

Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana taṃ evaṃ vuttaṃ – kāmañcedaṃ “dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabba”nti iminā siddhaṃ, aṭṭhuppattivasena pana apubbaṃ viya atthaṃ dassetvā sikkhāpadaṃ ṭhapitanti atthavisesadīpanapayojanato. Tasmā taṃ tassa atthavisesadassanatthaṃ vuttanti siddhameva. Tasmāpi veditabbameva yaṃ kiñci cīvaraṃ cīvarakālasamayaṃ nātikkāmetabbanti. Apica yaṃ vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “chaṭṭhito paṭṭhāya pana uppannaṃ anaccekacīvarampi paccuddhāretvā ṭhapitacīvarampi [V 0.0064] etaṃ parihāraṃ labhatī”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.646-649). Tena “anaccekacīvare anaccekacīvarasaññī cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmeti, anāpattī”ti (pārā. 650) imināpi anaccekacīvarassāpi accekacīvaraparihāralābhaṃ dīpetīti.

In the Great Commentary, however, it is stated thus: 'Although this is established by the rule, “An extra robe may be kept for a maximum of ten days,” the training rule was laid down by showing a seemingly unprecedented meaning on account of the origin of the matter, for the purpose of elucidating a special meaning.' Therefore, it was spoken to reveal that special meaning, and thus it is indeed established. Hence, it should also be understood that any robe whatsoever must not go beyond the robe-season. Furthermore, it is stated in the Commentary: 'From the sixth day onward, even a non-urgent robe that has arisen or a robe whose determination has been rescinded and which has been set aside obtains this allowance' (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.646-649). Thus, by this statement, 'If one, perceiving a non-urgent robe as a non-urgent robe, lets it go beyond the robe-season, there is no offense' (Pārā. 650), it is also shown that even a non-urgent robe obtains the allowance of an urgent robe.

Ettāvatā yathāvutto dutiyo atthavikappo pāḷinayena, aṭṭhakathānayena ca patiṭṭhāpito hoti. Evaṃ tāva pakiṇṇakāya adhikathā parato pāṭhato vitthāritā hotīti apakiṇṇakaṃ.

To this extent, the second division of meaning, as stated, has been established according to the method of the Pāli and the method of the Commentary. Thus, the discussion on miscellaneous matters is expanded upon from the text hereafter; this concludes the non-miscellaneous section.

Cīvarapalibodho, āvāsapalibodho cāti dve palibodhā. Tesu ekapalibodhepi sati anāmantacārādiānisaṃsaṃ labhati, taṃ idha natthīti dassetuṃ “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā ubbhatasmiṃ kathine”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā eva “atthatakathinassa hi bhikkhuno”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kathinatthārārahassāti ettha “aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ – pubbakaraṇaṃ jānāti, paccuddhāraṃ jānāti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, atthāraṃ jānāti, mātikaṃ jānāti, palibodhaṃ jānāti, uddhāraṃ jānāti, ānisaṃsaṃ jānātī”ti (pari. 409) vacanato imehi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgato puggalo kathinatthārāraho nāma. Pubbakaraṇaṃ nāma dhovanavicāraṇacchedanasibbanarajanakappakaraṇaṃ.

The robe-impediment and the residence-impediment are the two impediments. Even when one of these impediments is present, one obtains the benefits such as wandering without asking leave; to show that this is not the case here, it is stated: 'When the Kathina has been withdrawn by a monk whose robe-work is finished.' Therefore, it was stated, 'For a monk for whom the Kathina has been spread,' and so on. Regarding being worthy of spreading the Kathina, it is said: 'A person endowed with eight factors is able to spread the Kathina—he knows the preliminary work, he knows the rescinding, he knows the determination, he knows the spreading, he knows the matrix, he knows the impediments, he knows the withdrawal, he knows the benefits' (Pari. 409). Thus, a person endowed with these eight factors is called one worthy of spreading the Kathina. Preliminary work means washing, examining, cutting, sewing, dyeing, and applying the determination-mark.

“Cīvaraṃ [M 0.0070] nāma khoma”ntiādinā pāḷivasena jātiñca pamāṇañca dassetvā idāni atirekacīvaraṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ pana vuttaṃ adhiṭṭhitavikappitesū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ sallakkhetvā”ti vuttepi yasmiṃ ṭhāne yaṃ ṭhapitaṃ, tasmiṃ taṃ pacchā hotu vā, mā vā, adhiṭṭhānaṃ ruhateva. Pure pacchā ṭhapanaṭṭhānaṃ na pamāṇaṃ.

Having shown the type and measure according to the Pāli with the words, 'A robe means one of linen,' and so on, now, to explain an extra robe, it is said, 'But as to what was said regarding robes that have been determined or assigned to another,' and so on. Even when it is said, 'having taken note of the place where it was put,' whether that thing is later in that place or not, the determination is indeed effective. The place where it was put, before or after, is not the standard.

Antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannassa bhikkhubhāvapariccāgavasena setavatthanivāsanaṃ vā kāsāvacajanaṃ vā hīnāyāvattanaṃ.

For a monk who has committed the final offense, relinquishment of monkhood is effected by wearing white clothes, or renouncing the saffron robe, or returning to a lower state.

Ekādasame aruṇuggamaneti antimaṃ ṭhapetvā tato purimatarasminti attho veditabbo. Tattha antimaṃ nāma aparakattikāya paṭhamāruṇuggamanaṃ. Tañhi kālattā nissaggiyaṃ na karoti. Idha “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā”ti karaṇavacanaṃ nidānānapekkhaṃ nidāne karaṇābhāvato. Tasmā eva “dasāhaparama”nti ayamettha anupaññattīti vuttaṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetu”ntiādi (mahāva. 358) vacanato ca idha “vikappetī”ti avisesena vuttavacanaṃ viruddhaṃ viya dissati, na ca viruddhaṃ tathāgatā bhāsanti, [V 0.0065] tasmā evamassa attho veditabbo – ticīvaraṃ ticīvarasaṅkhepena parihārato adhiṭṭhātumeva anujānāmi, na vikappetuṃ. Vassikasāṭikaṃ pana catumāsato paraṃ vikappetumeva, na adhiṭṭhātunti. Evañca pana sati yo ticīvare ekena cīvarena vippavasitukāmo hoti, tassa ticīvarādhiṭṭhānaṃ paccuddharitvā vippavāsasukhatthaṃ vikappanāya okāso dinno hoti, dasāhātikkame ca anāpattīti. Etena upāyena sabbattha vikappanāya apaṭisiddhabhāvo veditabboti likhitaṃ.

Regarding 'at the rising of the dawn on the eleventh day,' the meaning should be understood as 'at a time earlier than that,' setting aside the final one. Here, 'the final one' is the first rising of the dawn in the following month of Kattika. That robe does not become subject to forfeiture at that time, because that is its time limit. Here, the instrumental phrase 'by a monk whose robe-work is finished' is independent of the occasion, because there is no instrumental action in the occasion. Therefore, it is said that 'for a maximum of ten days' is a supplementary regulation here. And according to the statement, 'I allow, O monks, the triple robe to be determined, not to be assigned to another' (Mahāvagga 358), the statement here, 'he assigns it to another,' spoken without distinction, seems to be a contradiction. But the Tathāgatas do not speak in contradiction; therefore, its meaning should be understood thus: I allow the triple robe to be determined only for the sake of using it under the designation of 'triple robe,' not to be assigned to another. The rains-residence robe, however, is only to be assigned to another after four months, not to be determined. This being the case, for a monk who wishes to be separated from one robe of his triple robe, having rescinded the determination of the triple robe, the opportunity is given for assigning it to another for the sake of comfort while separated, and there is no offense in exceeding ten days. By this method, it should be understood that assigning to another is not prohibited in all cases—so it is written.

Imassa pana sikkhāpadassa ayaṃ saṅkhepavinicchayo – anatthate kathine hemantānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya, atthate kathine gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya uppannacīvaraṃ sandhāya “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Etthāha – “rajakehi dhovāpetvā setakaṃ kārāpentassāpi adhiṭṭhānaṃ adhiṭṭhānamevā”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.465) vacanato arajitepi adhiṭṭhānaṃ ruhatīti. Tena sūcikammaṃ katvā rajitvā kappabinduṃ datvā adhiṭṭhātabbanti niyamo kātabbo, na kātabboti? Kattabbova. Patto viya adhiṭṭhito yathā puna setabhāvaṃ vā tambabhāvaṃ vā patto adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahati, na ca pana tādiso [M 0.0071] yaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ upagacchati, evametaṃ daṭṭhabbanti. “Sve kathinaṃ uddharissatī”ti laddhacīvaraṃ sace ajjeva na adhiṭṭhāti, aruṇuggamane eva nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Kasmā? “Niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”ntiādinā (pārā. 462-463;) sikkhāpadassa vuttattā. Kathinabbhantare dasāhato uttaripi parihāraṃ labhati, kathinato pana pacchā ekadivasampi na labhati. Yathā kiṃ – yathā atthatakathino saṅgho ticīvaraṃ atthatadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva ubbhārā ānisaṃsaṃ labhati, na tato paraṃ, evaṃ atthatadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva ubbhārā labhati, uddhate pana kathine ekadivasampi na labhati. Etthāha – ubbhatadivasato paṭṭhāya puna dasāhaṃ labhatīti? Na, kasmā? “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretu”nti vacanato. Kathinabbhantarepi ekādase aruṇuggamane nissaggiyanti āpannaṃ. Taṃ pana atippasaṅgaṃ nivāretuṃ “niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”ntiādi vuttaṃ, na kathinadivasāni adivasānīti dīpanatthaṃ. Ayamattho tattha tattha āvibhavissati. Atha vā vassikasāṭikā anatirittappamāṇā nāmaṃ gahetvā vuttanayeneva cattāro vassike māse adhiṭṭhātabbā, tato paraṃ paccuddharitvā vikappetabbāti vuttaṃ. Ettha “paccuddharitvā”ti vacane uposathadivase eva paccuddharitvā vikappetvā ṭhapitaṃ hoti, tato paraṃ hemantassa paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya paccuddharaṇābhāvā. Evaṃ kathinabbhantare uppannacīvarampi veditabbanti likhitaṃ.

Of this training rule, this is the concise determination: The words 'when the robe-work is finished,' etc., are stated with reference to a robe that has arisen, starting from the first day of the cold season when the Kathina is not spread, and starting from the first day of the hot season when the Kathina is spread. Here it is said: 'Even for one who has it washed by washermen and made white, the determination is still a determination' (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.465). Thus, even if it is not dyed, the determination is effective. Therefore, should a rule be made that it must be determined after doing the needlework, dyeing it, and applying the determination-mark, or should it not be made? It must indeed be made. Just as a determined bowl does not lose its determination if it again reaches a state of being white or copper-colored, and yet such a bowl is not one that undergoes determination, so should this be understood. If one who has received a robe thinking, 'Tomorrow they will withdraw the Kathina,' does not determine it today, it becomes subject to forfeiture at the rising of the dawn. Why? Because the training rule is stated with the words 'when the robe-work is finished,' etc. (Pārā. 462-463). Within the Kathina period, one obtains an allowance even beyond ten days, but after the Kathina, one does not obtain it even for a single day. Like what?
