'Two or three bowlfuls are to be received' means that cakes brought thus should be taken by one who has need of them, up to the measure of a standard bowl. If, when an excess is received, one informs others with the perception that it was prepared for the purpose of provisions for a journey, etc., and does not share it, one is not released from the offense, because this training rule is one not requiring intention. Then if one takes what has been set aside, one is not released at all. But in the case of not sharing, there is no offense because it is improper. Some say that its being an offense not requiring intention is only due to not knowing the rule, not due to not knowing the object. The ancient masters say that since 'knowing that it was prepared for the purpose of provisions for a journey, etc.' is not mentioned among the factors, if one does not speak intentionally, it is an offense of expiation. There, 'receiving an excess' is stated as the fifth factor. Therefore, because it was not received, there is no offense of expiation, but there is an offense of wrong-doing for not doing what should be done. Otherwise, this would become an offense of action and non-action. 'Not preventing' or 'not informing' should be stated as the sixth factor.

Kāṇamātāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning Kāṇamātā is finished.

5. Paṭhamapavāraṇāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the First Training Rule Concerning Invitation

Bhuttāvī pavāraṇaṃ nāma pañcaṅgikaṃ. Tesu “asanaṃ paññāyattī”ti eteneva “bhuttāvī”ti etassa siddhattā visuṃ atthasiddhi na dissati. Dissati ce, aṅgānaṃ chakkattadassananti [V 0.0085] (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 238-239) likhitaṃ. “Bhojanaṃ paññāyatī”ti abhihaṭaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

The invitation by one who has eaten has five factors. Among these, since the meaning of 'one who has eaten' is established by the words 'food is apparent,' a separate establishment of its meaning is not seen. If it is seen, it is written: 'the seeing of the factors as sixfold' (Vajirabuddhi Tīkā, Pācittiya 238-239). 'Food is apparent' is said in reference to what has been brought.

Koṭṭetvā [M 0.0091] katacuṇṇampīti pi-kārena kuṇḍakaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Samapākabhajjitānaṃ pana ātapasukkhānaṃ vā kuṇḍakaṃ vā ye keci taṇḍulā vāti ettakameva vuttattā samapākabhajjitānaṃ vīhīnaṃ, vīhipalāsānaṃ vā taṇḍulacuṇṇaṃ pavāreti. Tathā kharapākabhajjitānaṃ kuṇḍakampi pavāreti. Bhajjitasattuyo piṇḍetvā kato apakkasattumodakopi pavāretīti likhitaṃ. Sace avasiṭṭhaṃ natthi, na pavāreti. Kasmā? Asanasaṅkhātassa vippakatabhojanassa abhāvato.

In the phrase 'and powder made by pounding,' the word 'and' includes bran. But since it is only said this much: 'of lightly parched grains, or sun-dried grains, or bran, or any kind of rice grains,' one may be invited with rice powder from lightly parched paddy or from paddy husks. Similarly, one may be invited with the bran of hard-parched grains. It is written that one may also be invited with uncooked sweet-balls made by kneading roasted barley-meal. If there is no remainder, one is not invited. Why? Because of the absence of an unfinished meal that is counted as food.

Akappiyamaṃsaṃ pana kiñcāpi paṭikkhipitabbaṭṭhāne ṭhitaṃ, khādiyamānaṃ pana maṃsabhāvaṃ na jahāti, tasmā pavāreti. Bhojanasālāya bhuñjanto ce attano apāpuṇanakoṭṭhāsaṃ abhihaṭaṃ paṭikkhipati, na pavāreti. Kāmaṃ paṭikkhipati, patte pana ārāmikā ākiranti, taṃ bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭati. Idañhi buddhappaṭikuṭṭhāya anesanāya uppanneyeva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Yathā hi saṅghato laddhaṃ piṇḍaṃ dussīlo deti, tañce paṭikkhipati, na pavāreti, evaṃsampadamidanti ca, vibhāgo lajjī ce deti, taṃ so na ajjhoharitukāmatāya paṭikkhipati, pavāretīti ca, “samaṃsarasaṃ samaccharasa”nti āpajjanato “maṃsarasa”nti vutte pana paṭikkhipato hoti, “maṃsassa rasaṃ maṃsarasa”nti ayaṃ viggaho nādhippetoti ca vuttaṃ. Bhattamissakaṃ yāguṃ āharitvā “yāguṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, na pavāreti. “Bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vutte pavāreti. Kasmā? Yenāpucchito, tassa atthitāya. Ettha pana “yāgumissakaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, tatra ce yāgu bahutarā vā hoti, samasamā vā. Bhattaṃ mandaṃ, na pavāreti. Yāgu ce mandā, bhattaṃ bahutaraṃ, pavāreti. Idañca sabbaaṭṭhakathāsu vuttattā na sakkā paṭikkhipituṃ. Kāraṇaṃ panettha duddasaṃ. “Bhattamissakaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati. Tatra bhattaṃ bahutaraṃ vā samakaṃ vā appataraṃ vā hoti, pavāreti eva. Bhattaṃ vā yāguṃ vā anāmasitvā “missakaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati. Tatra ce bhattaṃ bahutaraṃ, samakaṃ vā hoti, pavāreti. Appataraṃ na pavāreti. Taṃ sabbaṃ vīmaṃsitabbanti.

But although unallowable meat is something to be rejected, when being eaten it does not abandon its nature as meat; therefore, one is invited. If one eating in the dining hall rejects what has been brought before it reaches one's own portion, one is not invited. Though one may reject it, if the monastery attendants scatter it into the bowl, it is not allowable to eat it. For this is reckoned as having arisen from improper seeking, which is censured by the Buddha. Just as when an immoral person gives almsfood obtained from the Sangha, if one rejects it, one is not invited—this is a similar case. And if a conscientious person gives a share, and one rejects it with the desire not to consume it, one is invited. And it is said that because one incurs an offense for a meal 'with meat-sauce' or 'with fish-sauce,' when 'meat-sauce' is said, one who rejects it is liable, for the analysis 'the sauce of meat is meat-sauce' is not the intended meaning. If someone brings gruel mixed with rice and says, 'Take the gruel,' one is not invited. If 'Take the rice' is said, one is invited. Why? Because of the existence of that by which one was asked. Here, if one says, 'Take the gruel-mixed,' and in it the gruel is more or equal, and the rice is little, one is not invited. If the gruel is little and the rice is more, one is invited. Since this is stated in all the commentaries, it cannot be rejected. The reason here, however, is difficult to see. If one says, 'Take the rice-mixed,' and in it the rice is more, equal, or less, one is invited. If, without specifying rice or gruel, one says, 'Take the mixed,' and in it the rice is more or equal, one is invited. If it is less, one is not invited. All this should be investigated.

Phalaṃ [M 0.0092] vā kandamūlādi vā pañcahi samaṇakappehi kappiyaṃ akatanti ettha kappiyaṃ akārāpitehi kadaliphalādīhi saddhiṃ atirittaṃ kārāpetvāpi taṃ kadaliphalādiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Amissakarasattā puna tāni kappiyaṃ kārāpetvā aññasmiṃ bhājane ṭhapetvā [V 0.0086] kāretvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Pubbe tesu vinayakammassa anāruḷhattāti vadanti.

Regarding 'fruit or tubers, roots, and so on, not made allowable by the five means proper for a recluse': Here, even if one has had something made left-over along with bananas and other fruits that had not been made allowable, it is allowable to eat the remainder after setting aside those bananas and so on. Because their tastes are not mixed, it is allowable to eat them after having them made allowable again, placing them in another vessel, and having them prepared. Why? They say it is because a disciplinary act had not previously been performed on them.

Patte rajaṃ patitaṃ appaṭiggahitameva hoti. Tasmā paṭiggahetvāva bhikkhā gaṇhitabbā. “Apaṭiggahetvā gaṇhato vinayadukkaṭa”nti (pāci. aṭṭha. 265) vuttattā etamaññesampi na vaṭṭatīti vadanti. “Taṃ pana puna paṭiggahetvā bhuñjantassa anāpattī”ti etthāpi evameva. Imasmiṃ pana “atirittaṃ kataṃ anatirittakataṃ hotī”ti etthāpi evameva. Imasmiṃ pana “atirittaṃ kataṃ, anatirittaṃ kataṃ hotī”tiādīhi upaparikkhitvā vinicchayo veditabboti dīpitaṃ. Alametaṃ sabbanti idampi te adhikaṃ, ito aññaṃ na lacchasīti attho.

Dust fallen into the bowl is indeed unreceived. Therefore, alms should be taken only after having been received. Since it is said, 'For one who takes without having received, there is an offense of wrong-doing against the discipline' (Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā 265), they say that this is not allowable for others either. Here too, it is just the same regarding 'But for one who eats it after receiving it again, there is no offense.' It is explained that in this case, the decision should be known after examining such statements as 'what was made left-over, becomes not made left-over.' The meaning of 'Enough of all this' is: 'This is extra for you; you will not get anything else from this.'

Āhāratthāyāti vikāle evāti eke. “Paṭhamakathinasadisāni. Idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho. Kāyakammaṃ ajjhoharaṇato. Vacīkammaṃ vācāya “atirittaṃ karotha, bhante”ti akārāpanatoti veditabbaṃ.

'For the sake of food': some say this means only at the wrong time. The reading is: 'Similar to the first kaṭhina acts. But this is a matter of action and non-action.' Bodily action is from consuming. Verbal action should be understood as being from not having it made left-over by the words, 'Venerable sirs, make it left-over.'

Paṭhamapavāraṇāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the Commentary on the First Training Rule Concerning Invitation.

6. Dutiyapavāraṇāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Second Pavāraṇā Training Rule

“Bhuttasmiṃ pācittiya”nti (pāci. 243) mātikāyaṃ vuttattā “bhojanapariyosāne pācittiya”nti vuttaṃ, na ajjhohāre ajjhohāre.

Because it is stated in the matrix (Pācittiya 243), “An offense of expiation when one has eaten,” it is said, “An offense of expiation at the conclusion of the meal,” not with each mouthful.

Dutiyapavāraṇāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Pavāraṇā Training Rule is finished.

7. Vikālabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Training Rule on Eating at the Wrong Time

Jambudīpassa [M 0.0093] kālena paricchedoti evaṃ kira.

The delimitation is by the time of Jambudīpa, so it is said.

Vikālabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Eating at the Wrong Time is finished.

8. Sannidhikārakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Training Rule on Storing Food

“Duddhoto [V 0.0087] hotī”tiādinā nayena idha vuttattā, “duddhotaṃ pattaṃ dhovitvā puna

Because it is stated here in the passage beginning “it is badly washed,” and because it is said, “having washed a badly washed bowl, again…”

Tattha acchodakaṃ vā āsiñcitvā, aṅguliyā vā ghaṃsitvā nisnehabhāvo jānitabbo”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 253) samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttattā ca mattikāpattassa kapālena pīto sneho sannidhiṃ karotīti siddhanti likhitaṃ. Sayaṃ paṭiggahetvā apariccattamevāti ettha apariccattaṃ nāma anupasampannānaṃ nirapekkhaapariccattaṃ avijahitaṃ. “Paṭiggahaṇanti ettha paṭiggahitabhāvamavijahitameva sannidhiṃ janetī”ti dhammasiritthero, taṃ “paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pāci. 255) pāḷiyā virujjhati. Tassa pana puna paṭiggaṇhanakiccābhāvato vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.

Because it is stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Pāc.a. 253): “There, the state of being free from grease should be ascertained by sprinkling clear water or by rubbing with a finger,” and because it is written that it is established that grease absorbed by a clay bowl constitutes storing. “When one has received it oneself, it is simply unabandoned.” Here, “unabandoned” means not having been relinquished without expectation to those not fully ordained. The Elder Dhammasiri says: “Here, ‘receiving’ means that the state of having received, not having been relinquished, generates storing.” That contradicts the Pāḷi text (Pāc. 255): “He receives it; there is an offense of wrong doing.” However, since there is no need for him to receive it again, this should be investigated.

Sannidhikārakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Storing Food is finished.

9. Paṇītabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Choice Foods

“Tesaṃ maṃsañca khīradadhīni ca idha adhippetānī”ti idaṃ pācittiyavatthuparicchedo, na pana kappiyakhīrādiparicchedo, tasmā yassa kassaci khīrādīni vaṭṭantīti ca, “mahānāmasikkhāpadena kāretabbo”ti saṅghavasena pavārite bhesajjatthāya sappiādibhesajjapañcakaṃ viññāpeti ce, tattha “na bhesajjakaraṇīyena bhesajjaṃ viññāpetī”ti ettha saṅgahaṃ gacchati, tasmā “tena pācittiya”nti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 261) ca likhitaṃ.

“For them, meat and milk-curds are here intended”—this is the delimitation of the basis for an offense of expiation, not the delimitation of what is allowable regarding milk, etc. Therefore, for whomever milk and so on are allowable, and “it should be done according to the Mahānāma training rule”—if, having been invited on behalf of the Saṅgha, one requests the five medicines beginning with ghee for a medicinal purpose, then it is included under “one should not request medicine when there is no medicinal need.” Therefore it is written (Vajiraṭīkā, Pācittiya 261): “For that, there is an offense of expiation.”

Paṇītabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Choice Foods is finished.

10. Dantaponasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Training Rule on Tooth-sticks

“Sarīrāvayavenā”ti [M 0.0094] vuttattā mukhena paṭiggahaṇaṃ anuññātaṃ. “Ciñcādipattesu bhūmiyaṃ atthatesu na vaṭṭati, kallakhette tattha vaṭṭatī”ti ca, “sāmaṃ gahetvā”ti iminā na kevalaṃ sappadaṭṭhaṃyeva, aññampi daṭṭhaṃ viseseti. Sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti ca likhitaṃ.

Because it is said “with a part of the body,” receiving with the mouth is permitted. And: “It is not allowable for things in tamarind-leaf containers and so on when they are strewn on the ground, but it is allowable there in a suitable place.” By this, “having taken it oneself,” it specifies not only what has been bitten by a snake but also what has been bitten by another. And it is written: “It is allowable to consume it after taking it oneself.”

Dantaponasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Tooth-sticks is finished.

Bhojanavaggo catuttho.

The Food Chapter, the Fourth.

5. Acelakavaggo

5. The Naked Ascetics Chapter

1. Acelakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Naked Ascetics

Acelakādayo [V 0.0088] yasmā, titthiyāva matā idha;

Tasmā titthiyanāmena, tikacchedo kato tato.

Since naked ascetics and others are regarded as sectarians here, therefore, by the name “sectarian,” a threefold division was made from that.

Atitthiyassa naggassa, tathā titthiyaliṅgino;

Gahaṭṭhassāpi bhikkhussa, kappatīti vinicchayo.

For a naked person who is not a sectarian, and for one with the marks of a sectarian, and even for a bhikkhu who is a householder, it is allowable—this is the decision.

Atitthiyassa cittena, titthiyassa ca liṅgino;

Sotāpannādino dātuṃ, kappatītīdha no mati.

To give to one with the mind of a non-sectarian, and to one with the marks of a sectarian, and to a stream-enterer and others—it is not our opinion here that this is allowable.

Acelakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Naked Ascetics is finished.

3. Sabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Training Rule on a Meal with a Family

Anupavisitvā nisīdanacittena sacittakatāti veditabbā.

It should be understood as intentional from the intention to enter and sit down.

Sabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on a Meal with a Family is finished.

4-5. Rahopaṭicchannarahonisajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4-5. Commentary on the Training Rules on Sitting in a Secluded Place and a Concealed Place

Catutthaṃ paṭhamāniyate, pañcamaṃ dutiyāniyate vuttanayameva. Idha pañcamaṃ upanandassa catutthaṃ hoti.

The fourth is in accordance with the method stated in the first Aniyata rule; the fifth is in accordance with the method stated in the second Aniyata rule. Here, the fifth becomes the fourth in the case of Upananda.

Rahopaṭicchannarahonisajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rules on Sitting in a Secluded Place and a Concealed Place is finished.

6. Cārittasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Training Rule on Proper Procedure

Sabhatto [M 0.0095][V 0.0089] samānoti nimantanabhattoti porāṇā. Santaṃ bhikkhuṃ, anāpucchā, purebhattaṃ pacchābhattaṃ, aññatra samayāti ayamettha catubbidhā anupaññatti. Tattha samayā dve samayā. Bhattiyagharanti nimantitassa gharaṃ vā salākābhattādidāyakānaṃ vā gharaṃ. “Samuṭṭhānādīni paṭhamakathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho, “idha nimantanā akappiyanimantanā”ti eke.

The ancients say: “‘Being on equal terms with the meal’ means an invitation meal.” “A bhikkhu who is present; without asking permission; before the meal; after the meal; ‘except at the proper time’—this is the fourfold supplementary ruling here. Therein, ‘the proper time’ refers to two occasions. ‘A house providing meals’ means the house of the one who invited or the house of the givers of ticket-food and so on. The text reads: ‘The origins and so on are similar to the first Kathina rule, but this is a matter of action and non-action.’ Some say: ‘Here the invitation is an improper invitation.’”

Purebhattañca piṇḍāya, caritvā yadi bhuñjati;

Siyā paramparāpatti, pacchābhattaṃ na sā siyā.

If, having gone for alms before the meal, one eats, there would be a consecutive offense; but eating after the meal, it would not be so.

Pacchābhattañca gamiko, pubbagehaṃ yadi gacche;

Eke āpattiyevāti, anāpattīti ekacce.

And after the meal, if a traveler should go to the previous house, some say it is an offense, others say it is not an offense.

Kulantarassokkamane, āpattimatayo hi te;

Samānabhattapaccāsā, iti āhu idhāpare.

In transgressing to another family, their intention is indeed an offense; others here say it is because of the hope for an equal meal.

Matā gaṇikabhattena, samenti naṃ nimantane;

Vissajjanaṃ samānanti, eke sammukhatāpare.

Some consider it a group meal, others are satisfied by the invitation; some by the dismissal, others by the face-to-face meeting.

Sanniṭṭhānatthikeheva, vicāretabbabhedato;

Viññū cārittamicceva, sikkhāpadamidaṃ vidū. (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 294);

Because of the different points to be investigated by those who desire a firm conclusion, the wise know this training rule as ‘Cāritta’ (Proper Procedure). (Vajiraṭīkā, Pācittiya 294)

Cārittasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Proper Procedure is finished.

7. Mahānāmasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Mahānāma Training Rule

Paṇītabhojanasikkhāpade “mahānāmasikkhāpadena kāretabbo”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paṇītabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) yaṃ vuttaṃ, tassattho saṅghavasena pavārite bhesajjatthāya sappiādibhesajjapañcakaṃ [V 0.0090] viññāpeti ce, “nabhesajjena karaṇīyena bhesajjaṃ viññāpetī”ti (pāci. 309) vacanena pācittiyanti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 310) likhitaṃ. “Tayā imināva pavāritamhā, amhākañca iminā ca iminā ca attho”ti yathābhūtaṃ ācikkhitvā viññāpetuṃ gilānova labhati, na itaroti ca, “aññassa atthāyā”ti [M 0.0096] assa ñātakappavārite, attano vā ñātakappavāriteti atthoti ca, “apariyantappavāraṇāya pavārite”ti saṅghavasena, puggalavasena ca pavāretvā dāyakā. Tasmā “saṅghappavāraṇatā”ti vatvā “puggalappavāraṇatā”ti na vuttanti ca, “pariyantātikkamo”ti vacanena gilāno gahito, tasmā “gilānāgilānatā”ti na vuttaṃ. Evaṃ santepi “saṅghappavāraṇāya pavāraṇatā”ti pāṭhoti ca likhitaṃ, vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.

In the training rule on fine foods, it is said: 'It should be dealt with according to the Mahānāma training rule.' The meaning of this is: if, having been invited by an invitation to the Sangha, one requests the five medicines beginning with ghee for a medicinal purpose, it is a pācittiya offense, according to the statement: 'One requests medicine when there is no medicinal need for it,' as it is written. Only a sick person is permitted to request, not another, after having declared the matter as it really is, saying: 'We have been invited by you with this, and we have need of this and that.' And the meaning of 'for the sake of another' is when one has been invited by one's relatives, or when one has been invited on account of one's relatives. 'When invited with an unlimited invitation' refers to donors who have invited either through the Sangha or through an individual. Therefore, having said 'the state of being an invitation to the Sangha,' 'the state of being an invitation to an individual' is not mentioned. And by the statement 'exceeding the limit,' a sick person is included; therefore 'the state of being sick or not sick' is not mentioned. Even so, it is also written that the reading is 'the state of an invitation by means of an invitation to the Sangha,' and this should be investigated.

Mahānāmasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Mahānāma Training Rule is finished.

8. Uyyuttasenāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a Marshaled Army

Hatthiādīsu ekamekanti antamaso ekapurisāruḷhahatthimpi, ekaṃ sarahatthaṃ purisampi. Samuṭṭhānādīni eḷakalomasadisāni, idaṃ pana lokavajjaṃ, akusalacittaṃ tivedana”nti pāṭho.

‘Each one among elephants and so on’ means at least a single elephant mounted by one person, or a single person with an arrow in hand. The origins and so on are similar to those of the Eḷakaloma training rule. But this is a worldly fault; the reading is: ‘the unwholesome consciousness is accompanied by three kinds of feeling.’”

Uyyuttasenāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a Marshaled Army is finished.

9. Senāvāsasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Staying with an Army

Kenaci palibuddhassāti verikena vā issarena vā kenaci ruddhassa. Senāparikkhepena vā parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena vā sañcaraṇaṭṭhānapariyantena vā paricchinditabbā.

‘Obstructed by someone’ means obstructed by some enemy or lord. It should be delimited either by the army's perimeter, or by a place suitable for an enclosure, or by the boundary of the area of movement.

Senāvāsasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Staying with an Army is finished.

Acelakavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter: On Naked Ascetics.

6. Surāpānavaggo

6. The Chapter on Drinking Intoxicants

1. Surāpānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Training Rule on Drinking Intoxicants

“Surā”ti [V 0.0091] vā “na vaṭṭatī”ti vā jānitvā pivane akusalamevāti likhitaṃ. Akusalacittanti yebhuyyena taṃ sandhāya kira vuttaṃ. Atha kasmā [M 0.0097] vinayaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “akusaleneva pātabbatāyā”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 329) vuttanti ce? Sacittakapakkhe akusaleneva pātabbatāyāti.

It is written: 'When one drinks knowing, “This is liquor,” or, “This is not allowed,” it is definitely unwholesome.' It is said, it seems, that 'unwholesome consciousness' is stated mostly with reference to that. If so, why then is it said in the Vinaya Commentary: 'because it is to be drunk only with an unwholesome state'? Because in the case of an intentional act, it is to be drunk only with an unwholesome state.

Surāpānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Drinking Intoxicants is finished.

2. Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Training Rule on Tickling with a Finger

Kāyasaṃsaggasaṅghādisesāpattibhāve samānepi bhikkhuniyāpi anupasampannepi dukkaṭaṃ, upasampanne eva pācittiyanti evaṃ puggalāpekkhaṃ dassetuṃ “aṅgulipatodake pācittiya”nti vuttaṃ. Sati karaṇīyeti ettha purisaṃ sati karaṇīye āmasatoti adhippāyo, na itthiṃ.

Even though the nature of the offense is similar to the Saṅghādisesa of bodily contact, it is a dukkaṭa offense with a bhikkhunī or an unordained person, and a pācittiya offense only with an ordained person. To show this distinction depending on the person, it is said: 'For tickling with a finger, there is a pācittiya.' Here, regarding 'when there is a reason,' the intention is that one touches a man when there is a reason, not a woman.

Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Tickling with a Finger is finished.

3. Hasadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Training Rule on Playing for Amusement

“Cikkhallaṃ vā”ti vacanato sakkharampi khipanakīḷāya kīḷato dukkaṭameva. Uparigopphake pācittiyaṃ, aññattha dukkaṭanti pācittiyavatthuatthavasena “udake hasadhamme pācittiya”nti vuttaṃ.

From the phrase 'or mud,' playing a throwing game even with gravel is a dukkaṭa offense. It is a pācittiya offense in water above the ankles, and a dukkaṭa offense elsewhere. Based on the substance of the pācittiya offense, it is said: 'For playing for amusement in water, there is a pācittiya.'

Idaṃ saññāvimokkhaṃ ce, tikapācittiyaṃ kathaṃ;

Kīḷitaṃva akīḷāti, micchāgāhena taṃ siyā.

If this is an offense not dependent on perception, how can it be a pācittiya with three permutations? Perceiving what is play as not play—this would be due to wrong apprehension.

Ettāvatā [V 0.0092] kathaṃ kīḷā, iti kīḷāyaṃ evāyaṃ;

Akīḷāsaññī hotettha, vinayatthaṃ samādaye.

To what extent is it play? Thus this is indeed in play; herein one becomes one who perceives it as not play; one should undertake this for the sake of the Vinaya.

Ekantākusalo yasmā, kīḷāyābhiratamano;

Tasmā akusalaṃ cittaṃ, ekamevettha labbhatīti. (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 336);

Because one whose mind delights in play is entirely unwholesome, therefore only a single unwholesome consciousness is found here.

Hasadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Playing for Amusement is finished.

4. Anādariyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Training Rule on Disrespect

Tassa [M 0.0098] vacananti “ayaṃ ukkhittako vā vambhito vā garahito vā imassa vacanaṃ akataṃ bhavissatī”ti anādariyaṃ karoti. Dhammanti kathāyaṃ dhammo nasseyya vā vinasseyya vā antaradhāyeyya vā, taṃ vā asikkhitukāmo anādariyaṃ karoti. “Lokavajjaṃ atikkamitvā ‘idaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyuggaho’ti vadantassa na vaṭṭatī”ti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 344) likhitaṃ.

‘His word’ means one shows disrespect thinking: ‘This one is suspended, or reviled, or censured; his word will be undone.’ ‘The Dhamma’ means one shows disrespect if the Dhamma in the talk might be lost, or perish, or disappear, or if one is unwilling to train in it. It is written: ‘It is not allowable for one who, having transgressed a worldly fault, says, “This is what we have learned from our teacher.”’

Anādariyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Disrespect is finished.

6. Jotisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Fire

“Visibbanāpekkho”ti vuttattā aññassa vaṭṭati, aññesañca.

Since it is said, ‘expecting to get warm,’ it is allowable for another, and for others too.

Jotinekamaneke vā, jālenti munayo saha;

Eko sopeti nāneko, adhippāyavisesato.

Whether one fire or many, sages kindle them together; one sleeps, not many, because of a difference of intention.

Jotisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Fire is finished.

8. Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Disfigurement

Morakkhimaṇḍalamaṅgulapiṭṭhīnanti [V 0.0093] na ekantato, adhikaṃ, orañcāti vadanti. Ekakoṇepi vaṭṭati, evaṃ yattha katthaci ekabindupi vaṭṭatīti.

Regarding ‘a circle like a peacock's eye and the back of the fingers,’ they say this is not exclusive, but can be more or less. It is allowable even in one corner; thus, it is allowable wherever there is even a single dot.

Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Disfigurement is finished.

9. Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Determination

“Samuṭṭhānādīni paṭhamakathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho. Ettha paribhogena kāyakammaṃ. Apaccuddharaṇena vacīkammaṃ.

The reading is: ‘The origins, etc., are similar to the first Kathina rule, but this concerns action and non-action.’ Here, the bodily action is through use; the verbal action is through non-revocation.

Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Determination is finished.

10. Apanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Concealment

Sasūcike [M 0.0099] sūcighare sūcigaṇanāya āpattiyoti porāṇā.

The ancients say that in the case of a needle-case with needles, there are offenses according to the number of needles.

Apanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Concealment is finished.

Surāpānavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Chapter on Drinking Liquor, the Sixth.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Chapter on Living Beings

1. Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Intentionally Depriving of Life

Vatthugaṇanāya kammabandhagaṇanācetanāmāraṇānaṃ, na kammabandhagaṇanāya cetanāmāraṇā. Ettha ekacetanāya bahupāṇakā marantīti ayaṃ vibhāgo veditabbo.

The kamma-binding for intentions to kill is counted by the number of objects, not that the intentions to kill are counted by the number of kamma-bindings. Here, this distinction should be understood: by one intention many living beings may die.

Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Intentionally Depriving of Life is finished.

2. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Water with Living Beings

Sappāṇakanti [V 0.0094] pāṇakānaṃ maraṇavasena pācittiyaṃ, na sappāṇakaudakaparibhogavasena pācittiyaṃ, tasmā eva “paṇṇattivajja”nti vuttaṃ. Asuddhacittattā pācittiyaṃ, suddhacitte anāpatti. Padīpujjalane viya paṇṇattivajjatā vuttāti likhitaṃ.

Regarding ‘with living beings’: a pācittiya offense is incurred on account of the death of the living beings, not on account of the mere use of water with living beings; therefore it is called ‘an offense by prescription.’ It is a pācittiya because of an impure mind; with a pure mind, there is no offense. It is written that its being an offense by prescription is stated to be like the kindling of a lamp.

Jale pakkhipanaṃ pubbaṃ, jalappavesanaṃ idaṃ;

Evaṃ ubhinnaṃ nānāttaṃ, ñeyyaṃ ñāṇavatā sadāti. (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 387)

Placing in water is the former, entering the water is the latter; thus the difference between the two should always be known by the wise.

Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Water with Living Beings is finished.

5. Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on One Under Twenty Years of Age

Aññaṃ upasampādetīti –

'He gives higher ordination to another'—

Upajjhāyo sace sāmaṃ, kammavācañca sāveti;

Kammaṃ ruhati icceke, neti vinayakovido.

If the preceptor himself announces the formal act, some say the act is valid, but the expert in the Vinaya says it is not.

Dukkaṭaṃ [M 0.0100] vihitaṃ yasmā, ācariyassa gaṇassa ca;

Tasmā bhinnāva ācariya-upajjhāyā visuṃ idhāti.

Because a dukkaṭa offense is prescribed for the teacher and the assembly, therefore the teacher and the preceptor are here separate and distinct.

Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on One Under Twenty Years of Age is finished.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Making an Arrangement

Idha ekatoupasampannā, sikkhamānā, sāmaṇerīti imā tissopi saṅgahaṃ gacchanti, imāsaṃ pana tissannaṃ samayo rakkhati, ayamimāsaṃ, mātugāmassa ca visesoti veditabbaṃ.

Here, a fully ordained nun, a probationer, and a female novice—these three are also included. But for these three, the period is observed. This should be understood as the distinction for them and for women in general.

Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Making an Arrangement is finished.

9. Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Communion with a Suspended Bhikkhu

“Taṃ [V 0.0095] diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhenāti laddhinānāsaṃvāsakaṃ sandhāyā”ti likhitaṃ. Ticittanti ettha vipākābyākatacittena sahaseyyaṃ kappeyyāti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Aññathā sacittakattā sikkhāpadassa kiriyābyākataṃ sandhāya na yujjati.

It is written: '“With one who has not abandoned that view” refers to one who is in non-communion because of his doctrine.' Regarding 'with three minds,' here the meaning should be understood thus: that one might lie down together with a resultant-indeterminate mind. Otherwise, since the training rule is intentional, it would not be tenable in reference to a functional-indeterminate mind.

Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Communion with a Suspended Bhikkhu is finished.

10. Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a 'Thorn'

“Ayaṃ samaṇuddeso pārājiko hoti. Sace taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjati, saṅghassa ārocetvā saṅghānumatiyā pabbājetabbo”ti porāṇagaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Daṇḍakammanāsanā hi idhādhippetā. Yadi so pārājiko hoti, liṅganāsanā nāma siyā. “Te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti ca diṭṭhi satthari asatthādidiṭṭhi na hoti. Sace sā yassa uppajjati, so pārājiko hoti, tasmimpi evameva [M 0.0101] paṭipajjitabbaṃ, saṃvare atiṭṭhanto liṅganāsanāya nāsetabboti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 428) ācariyassa takko.

'This novice is a pārājika offender. If he abandons that view, having informed the Sangha, he should be ordained with the Sangha's permission'—so it is said in an old glossary, but that is not correct. For here a punitive act of banishment is intended. If he were a pārājika offender, it would be called 'banishment by loss of the characteristic mark.' And the view 'For one who follows them, it is not sufficient for an obstacle' is not a view about the Teacher such as 'the Teacher is not the Teacher.' If such a view arises in someone, he is a pārājika offender, and one should proceed in just the same way in that case too. 'One who does not abide in restraint should be banished by banishment by loss of the characteristic mark'—this is the teacher's reasoning. (Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā, Pācittiya 428)

Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on a 'Thorn' is finished.

Sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on Living Beings, the Seventh.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Chapter on What is in Accordance with the Dhamma

4. Pahārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Striking

Aṅgesu na mokkhādhippāyatā viya amaraṇādhippāyatā vattabbāti ce? Na vattabbā. Kasmā? Yo bhikkhu sayaṃ pahāraṃ dātukāmo, so adhippāyena tassa maraṇe payogavirahovāti katvā [V 0.0096] amaraṇādhikārattā kevalaṃ amaraṇādhippāyo eva soti tā viya tā na vuttā. Mokkhādhippāyassa pana kopo natthi, tasmā anāpattīti vuttaṃ.

If it is asked: 'Should it be said that with respect to the limbs, there is an intention not to kill, just as there is an intention to release?' It should not be said. Why? Because a bhikkhu who wants to deliver a blow himself has merely an intention not to kill—since his intention is devoid of any effort towards the other's death and thus falls under the category of not-killing—it is not said to be like the intention to release. But for one with an intention to release, there is no anger; therefore it is said there is no offense.

Pahārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Striking is finished.

5. Talasattikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Threatening with an Uplifted Hand

Talameva talasattikaṃ. “Pothanasamatthaṭṭhena sattika”nti eke. Yasmā paharitukāmatāya paharato purimena pācittiyaṃ, kevalaṃ uccāretukāmatāya uggiraṇamatte kate iminā pācittiyaṃ. Iminā pana virajjhitvā pahāro dinno, tasmā napaharitukāmatāya dinnattā dukkaṭaṃ. Kimidaṃ dukkaṭaṃ pahārapaccayā, udāhu uggiraṇapaccayāti? Pahārapaccayā eva dukkaṭaṃ, purimaṃ uggiraṇapaccayā pācittiyanti sadukkaṭaṃ pācittiyaṃ yujjati. Purimañhi uggiraṇaṃ, pacchā pahāro. Na ca pacchimaṃ pahāraṃ nissāya purimaṃ uggiraṇaṃ anāpattivatthukaṃ bhavitumarahatīti no takkoti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 456) ācariyo.

The palm itself is the 'talasattika.' Some say it is a 'sattika' in the sense of being capable of striking. For one who strikes with the intention to strike, there is a pācittiya by the former rule; when there is merely the raising of the hand with the intention to threaten, there is a pācittiya by this rule. But if, having become disaffected with this, one gives a blow, then because it was given without the intention to strike, it is a dukkaṭa. Is this dukkaṭa on account of the blow, or on account of raising the hand? The dukkaṭa is on account of the blow, while the former raising of the hand is a pācittiya. Thus, a pācittiya together with a dukkaṭa is appropriate. For the raising of the hand is first, and the blow is later. And the later blow cannot be a reason for the former raising of the hand to become a ground for no offense; this is not logical, says the teacher (Vajirabuddhi).

Talasattikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Threatening with an Uplifted Hand is finished.

7. Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Deliberately Causing Vexation

Paro [M 0.0102] kukkuccaṃ uppādetu vā, mā vā, taṃ appamāṇaṃ. “Kukkuccupādana”nti tatiyamaṅgaṃ tassa adhippāyavasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

Whether vexation arises in the other person or not, that is not the measure. 'Causing vexation' is the third factor; it should be understood as stated in terms of one's intention.

Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Deliberately Causing Vexation is finished.

8. Upassutisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Eavesdropping

Upassutinti yathā upakujjhaṃ “samīpakujjha”nti vuccati, tathā upassuti “samīpassutī”ti veditabbā. Yattha ṭhito suṇāti, taṃ ṭhānanti attho. Sutīti panettha paresaṃ vacanasaddo ca. So hi suyyatīti suti nāma. Upasuyyati vā etthāti upassuti. Okāso hi suti nāma. Imesaṃ sutvāti ettha “vacana”nti pāṭhaseso.

Regarding 'upassuti': just as 'upakujjhaṃ' is called 'samīpakujjha' (a nearby pot), so 'upassuti' should be understood as 'samīpassuti' (hearing nearby). The meaning is the place where one stands and listens. Herein, 'suti' is the sound of others' speech. For since it is heard (suyyati), it is called 'suti.' Or, one listens nearby (upasuyyati) at it, thus it is 'upassuti.' For the occasion is called 'suti.' In the phrase 'having heard these,' the word 'speech' (vacana) is to be supplied.

Samuṭṭhānādīni [V 0.0097] atītadvayasadisānīti na gahetabbāni. Theyyasatthasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Siyā kiriyaṃ gantvā savane. Siyā akiriyaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ āgantvā vadantānaṃ ajānāpanavasena samuṭṭhānato. “Saññāvimokkhaṃ, sacittakaṃ, lokavajjaṃ, kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, akusalacittaṃ, dukkhavedana”nti likhitaṃ.

The origins, etc., are similar to the previous two and need not be treated separately. The origin is from (the categories of) theft and a weapon. It may arise from an action, by going to listen. It may arise from inaction, by not informing those who come and speak at the place where one is standing. It is written: 'There is no release through misperception; it is intentional, a worldly fault, an act of body, an act of speech, with an unwholesome mind, and with painful feeling.'

Upassutisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Eavesdropping is finished.

9. Kammappaṭibāhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Obstructing a Formal Act

Appamattakavissajjanakena pana cīvaraṃ karontassa senāsanakkhandhakavaṇṇanāyaṃ (cūḷava. 328) vuttappabhedāni sūciādīni anapaloketvāpi dātabbāni. Tato atirekaṃ dentena apalokanakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Evaṃ kataṃ pana apalokanaṃ kammalakkhaṇamevāti adhippāyo. Evaṃ sabbattha kammalakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Gāmasīmāvihāresu osāraṇādīni saṅghakammāniyeva na vaṭṭanti. Vissajjiyavebhaṅgiyāni pana vaṭṭanti. “Saṅghassa santaka”nti sāmaññato avatvā “imasmiṃ vihāre saṅghassa santaka”nti apaloketabbanti ca, “samuṭṭhānādīni adinnādānasadisāni, idaṃ pana dukkhavedana”nti pāṭhoti ca likhitaṃ.

But for one making a robe, needles and so on—the kinds mentioned in the explanation of the Senāsanakkhandhaka—may be given by the distributor of minor articles even without an announcement. One giving more than that must perform the act of announcement. The intention is that an announcement done thus is merely a feature of the formal act. Thus should the feature of the formal act be understood in all cases. In monasteries within a village boundary, formal acts of the Sangha such as rehabilitation are not allowable. But acts of distribution and apportionment are allowable. And one should make the announcement by saying, 'It is the property of the Sangha in this monastery,' not by saying generally, 'It is the property of the Sangha.' And it is written in the text: 'The origins and so on are similar to that for taking what is not given, but this one has painful feeling.'

Kammappaṭibāhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on obstructing a formal act is finished.

10. Chandaṃadatvāgamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Departing Without Giving Consent

Sannipātaṃ [M 0.0103] anāgantvā ce chandaṃ na deti, anāpattīti eke. Dukkaṭanti eke dhammakammantarāyakaraṇādhippāyattā.

Some say that if one does not come to the assembly and does not give one's consent, there is no offense. Others say it is a dukkaṭa offense because of the intention to cause an obstruction to a formal act in accordance with the Dhamma.

Chandaṃadatvāgamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on departing without giving consent is finished.

11. Dubbalasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Weakening

Akappiyena vāti suvaṇṇarajatamayamañcādinā. Kappiyamañco sampaṭicchitabboti “saṅghassa demā”ti dinnaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tehi pana “vihārassa demā”ti vutte suvaṇṇarajatamayādiakappiyamañcāpi [V 0.0098] sampaṭicchitabbāti ca, “arañjaro bahuudakagaṇhanako”ti ca, “saṅghikapaabhogena vāti sace ārāmikādayo paṭisāmetvā paṭidenti, paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti ca, “kaṃsalohādibhājanaṃ saṅghassa dinnampi pārihāriyaṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321) samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttattā attano hatthena gahetvā paṭisāmituṃ na labhatīti ca, “vedhako kāyabandhanassāti vadantī”ti ca, “hiṅgu hiṅguliharitālamanosilā añjanānī”ti pāṭhoti ca, “dārumayo vā…pe… apādakopi samuggo”ti pāṭhoti ca, “dārumayo tumboti dārumayo udakatumbo”ti ca, “thambhatulāsopānaphalakādīsū”ti ca likhitaṃ.

'By what is not allowable' means by a bed, etc., made of gold and silver. 'An allowable bed should be accepted': this is said with reference to what is given with the words, 'We give this to the Sangha.' But if they say, 'We give this to the monastery,' then even an unallowable bed made of gold, silver, etc., may be accepted. And: 'A water-strainer is one that holds much water.' And: 'By use of Sangha property': if monastery attendants, etc., repair it and return it, it is allowable to use. And: because it is said in the Samantapāsādikā, 'Even a vessel of bronze, copper, etc., given to the Sangha is not allowable for personal use,' one may not take it with one's own hand and appropriate it. And: 'They say a "vedhaka" is a waistband.' And: the reading is 'asafoetida, cinnabar, orpiment, realgar, and collyrium.' And: the reading is 'made of wood ... or a footless casket.' And: 'a wooden "tumba"' means a wooden water-gourd. And it is written: 'on pillars, beams, stairs, planks, etc.'

Dubbalasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on weakening is finished.

12. Pariṇāmanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

12. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Diverting

Eko bhikkhu ukkhittakassa dātukāmo hoti, tassa dānaṃ nivāretvā aññassa dāpeti, anāpatti. Tathā saddhādeyyavinipātanaṃ karontassa dāpeti, attano nissitakā itthannāmassa pattaṃ dātukāmā āpucchanti, “visabhāgo eso, sabhāgassa dehī”ti vadati. Anāpatti attano bhārabhūtattā. Tassa pana dātukāmaṃ aññassa dāpeti[M 0.0104], āpatti eva. Sabbattha āpucchitvā dātukāmaṃ yathāsukhaṃ vicāretuṃ labhati.

A bhikkhu wishes to give to a suspended one; if one prevents that gift and has it given to another, there is no offense. Similarly, if one has a gift intended for one who is causing the ruin of a faith-offering given to another, there is no offense. If his dependents, wishing to give a bowl to a certain named person, ask him, and he says, 'This one is of a different affiliation; give it to one of the same affiliation,' there is no offense, because it is his responsibility. But if he has a gift intended for that person given to another, there is an offense. In all cases, when asked, he is permitted to manage the intended gift as he wishes.

Pariṇāmanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Diverting is finished.

Sahadhammikavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Sahadhammika Chapter, the Eighth.

9. Ratanavaggo

9. The Jewel Chapter

1. Antepurasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Inner Quarters

Asayanighareti parikkhittassa bahibhūtesu rukkhamūlādīsu. “Sace khattiyova hoti, nābhisitto, abhisittova hoti, na khattiyo, rakkhatī”ti ācariyo “khattiyatā, abhisittatā”ti [V 0.0099] āpattiyā aṅgabhāvena vuttattā. Samuṭṭhānādīni paṭhamakathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho.

'Near the dwelling' means at places outside the enclosed area, such as at the foot of a tree and so on. The teacher says: 'If he is a khattiya but not anointed, or is anointed but not a khattiya, he is guarded,' because 'being a khattiya' and 'being anointed' are stated as factors of the offense. The origins and so on are similar to the first Kathina rule. But here the reading is: 'action and non-action.'

Antepurasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Inner Quarters is finished.

2. Ratanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Jewels

Sabbopi kathāmaggo bhaṇḍāgārikasīsena nikkhipanaṃ, gopanañca paṭikkhipitvā pavatto.

The entire course of the discussion proceeded by rejecting depositing and guarding, with the 'treasurer' as the main topic.

Ratanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Jewels is finished.

3. Vikālagāmappavesanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Entering a Village at an Unsuitable Time

“Santaṃ bhikkhu”nti ca “anāpucchā”ti ca “tathārūpā accāyikāti ca imāti ettha tisso”ti pāṭho. “Samuṭṭhānādīni kathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho.

The reading here is of three points: 'a resident bhikkhu,' 'without asking leave,' and 'such an urgent matter.' The origins and so on are similar to the Kathina rule. But here the reading is: 'action and non-action.'

Vikālagāmappavesanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Entering a Village at an Unsuitable Time is finished.

4. Sūcigharasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Needle Case

Taṃ [M 0.0105] assāti taṃ bhedanakaṃ assa pācittiyassa atthi paṭhamaṃ bhedanaṃ katvā pacchā desetabbattā. Esa nayo itaresupi. Vāsijaṭeti vāsidaṇḍake.

The phrase 'it would be' means that it would be subject to breaking for this pācittiya offense, because it must first be broken and then confessed. This is the method in the other cases too. 'Vāsijaṭe' means on an adze-handle.

Sūcigharasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Needle Case is finished.

5. Mañcapīṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Beds and Chairs

Aṭṭhaṅgulapādakanti bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ. Tulāsaṅghāte ṭhapanameva aṭṭakaraṇaṃ.

'Having feet eight fingerbreadths long' is a neuter abstract noun. Placing it on a 'balance-joint' is what constitutes making a platform.

Mañcapīṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Beds and Chairs is finished.

6. Tūlonaddhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Being Stuffed with Cotton

Kiñcāpi [V 0.0100] paṭilābheyeva pācittiyaṃ viya dissati, paribhoge eva pana āpatti daṭṭhabbā. “Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pāci. 529) vacanaṃ ettha sādhakaṃ.

Although it may appear to be a pācittiya offense at the very moment of acquisition, the offense should be seen as occurring only upon use. The statement (Pāc. 529), 'Having acquired what was made by another, he uses it: there is an offense of wrong-doing,' is the proof here.

Tūlonaddhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Being Stuffed with Cotton is finished.

7. Nisīdanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Sitting-cloth

Kiñcāpi nisīdanassa jāti na dissati ettha, tathāpi cīvarakkhandhake anuññātattā, “nava cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātabbānī”ti ettha ca pariyāpannattā cīvarajāti evassa jātīti veditabbaṃ. “Lābhe sadasaṃ, alābhe adasampi vaṭṭatī”ti eke, taṃ na yuttaṃ “nisīdanaṃ nāma sadasaṃ vuccatī”ti (pāci. 531-532) tassa saṇṭhānaniyamanato.

Although the type of sitting-cloth is not specified here, still, because it is allowed in the Robes Chapter and is included in the statement, 'Nine robes are to be determined,' it should be understood that its type is that of a robe. Some say, 'If one with a border is obtained, it is allowable; if one without a border is obtained, that too is allowable.' That is not correct, because its form is regulated by the statement (Pāc. 531-532), 'A sitting-cloth is said to be one with a border.'

Nisīdanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Sitting-cloth is finished.

Ratanavaggo navamo.

The Jewel Chapter, the Ninth.

Suddhapācittiyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Simple Pācittiyas is finished.

Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

The Section on Offenses to be Acknowledged

1. Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the First Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule

Yāmakālikādīsu [M 0.0106][V 0.0101] āhāratthāya eva dukkaṭaṃ. Tampi āmisena asambhinnarase, sambhinne pana ekarase pāṭidesanīyameva.

In the case of tonics for a watch of the night and so on, there is an offense of wrong-doing only when it is for the sake of food. And that too, when the flavor is not mixed with savory food; but if it is mixed, even if it has a single flavor, it is just a pāṭidesanīya offense.

Paṭhamapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the First Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule is finished.

2. Dutiyapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Second Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule

“Samuṭṭhānādīni kathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho.

The reading is: 'The origins and so on are similar to the Kathina rule, but this is a matter of action and non-action.'

Dutiyapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Second Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule is finished.

4. Catutthapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Fourth Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule

Ārāme vā ārāmūpacāre vā paṭiggahetvā ajjhoharantassāti ārāme vā ārāmūpacāre vā paṭiggahetvā ārāme vā ārāmūpacāre vā ajjhoharantassāti attho.

The phrase 'for one who receives and consumes in a monastery or in the precincts of a monastery' means: for one who receives in a monastery or in the precincts of a monastery and consumes it in a monastery or in the precincts of a monastery.

Bahārāme paṭiggahitaṃ ajjhārāme bhuñjantassa anāpatti. Aṅgesu ca “ajjhārāme vā ārāmūpacāre vā paṭiggahaṇa”nti gahetabbaṃ. Ajjhārāme hi dassite ārāmūpacāraṃ dassitamevāti. “Samuṭṭhānādīni kathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho.

There is no offense for one who eats inside a monastery what was received outside the monastery. And among the factors, it should be understood as 'receiving inside the monastery or in the precincts of the monastery.' For when 'inside the monastery' is stated, 'the precincts of the monastery' is also implied. The reading is: 'The origins and so on are similar to the Kathina rule, but this is a matter of action and non-action.'

Catutthapāṭidesanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Fourth Pāṭidesanīya Training Rule is finished.

Pāṭidesanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Pāṭidesanīya Rules is finished.

Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ

The Sekhiya Chapter

Sekhiyesu [M 0.0107][V 0.0102] satipi vītikkame anādariyāpekkhasseva āpattīti dassanatthaṃ kārako na vutto. Ayañhi vinayadhammatā, yadidaṃ sāpekkhe kārakaniddeso, so vuttaniyame vidhi, bhummakaraṇañca. Aṭṭhaṅgulādhikampi otāretvā nivāsetuṃ vaṭṭati. Tato paraṃ otārentassa dukkaṭanti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Ārāme vāti buddhupaṭṭhānādikāle. Pārupitabbanti uttarāsaṅgakiccavasena vuttaṃ.

In the Sekhiya rules, the agent is not mentioned to show that the offense occurs only when there is disregard. This is the nature of the Vinaya, namely, that the specification of the agent is conditional; that is the method in the stated regulation, and it concerns the basis and the action. It is allowable to wear the lower robe having lowered it even more than eight fingerbreadths. Beyond that, for one who lowers it, there is a dukkaṭa—as stated in the Great Commentary. 'In the monastery' means at times such as attending upon the Buddha. 'Should be covered' is said with reference to the function of the upper robe.

Ṭhatvāti ettha gacchantopi parissayābhāvaṃ oloketuṃ labhatiyevāti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 582) likhitaṃ. Yathā vāsūpagatassa antaraghare kāyaṃ vivaritvā nisīdituṃ vaṭṭati, tathā tassa santike gantukāmassapi kāyabandhanaṃ abandhitvā saṅghāṭiṃ apārupitvā gāmappavesanamanārocetvā yathākāmaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Tasmā addhānamaggagamanakāle eko bhikkhu gāmappavesanavattaṃ pūretvā gāmaṃ pavisitvā ekaṃ āvasathaṃ puratova ṭhitaṃ patvā parikkhāraṃ ṭhapetvā vāsūpagato ce hoti, itarehi tassa santikaṃ yathāsukhaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Ko pana vādo catūhapañcāhaṃ vāsamadhiṭṭhāya vasitabhikkhūnaṃ santikaṃ gantuñca vāsūpagatānaṃ santikaṃ gantuñca vaṭṭatīti. Buddhapūjampi yathāsukhaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Vuttampi cetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “anāpatti kāraṇaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ oloketī”ti. Tattha kāraṇaṃ nāma āmisapūjāti veditabbāti likhitaṃ.

Here, regarding 'having stood,' it is written that even while going, one may indeed look for the absence of danger. Just as one who has taken up residence is allowed to sit inside a house with the body exposed, so too for one intending to go to him, it is permissible to go as one pleases without fastening the waistband, without putting on the outer robe, and without announcing entry into the village. Therefore, while traveling on a long road, if a monk, having fulfilled the village-entry duties, enters the village and reaches a dwelling standing directly in front, places his belongings there, and has thus taken up residence, it is permissible for others to go to him as they please. What need be said about it being permissible to go to monks who have resided for four or five days after determining their lodging, and to go to those who have taken up residence? Even for the worship of the Buddha, it is permissible to go as one pleases. It is also stated in the commentary: 'There is no offense when one looks here and there on account of a reason.' Here, the reason should be understood as material offerings.

Chabbīsatisāruppavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the twenty-six kinds of suitable behavior is concluded.

Yasmā “samatittiko piṇḍapāto paṭiggahetabbo”ti (pāci. 602-603) vacanaṃ piṇḍapāto samapuṇṇo paṭiggahetabboti dīpeti, tasmā attano hatthagate patte piṇḍapāto diyyamāno thūpīkatopi ce hoti, vaṭṭatīti dīpito hoti. Sūpodanaviññattiyaṃ mukhe pakkhipitvā vippaṭisāre uppanne puna uggiritukāmassāpi sahasā ce pavisati, ettha asañcicca [V 0.0103] bhuñjati nāma. Viññattikatañca akatañca ekasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhitaṃ sahasā anupadhāretvā gahetvā bhuñjati, assatiyā bhuñjati nāma.

Because the statement 'almsfood should be accepted up to the level of the rim' (Pāc. 602-603) indicates that almsfood should be accepted fully level, therefore, even if the almsfood given into one's own hand-held bowl is heaped up, it is explained as being allowable. In the case of requesting soup and rice, if, having placed it in the mouth, regret arises, and it hastily goes down even when one intends to spit it out, here, it is called eating unintentionally. If, without considering, one hastily takes and eats food that was requested and food that was not, placed together in one spot, it is called eating unmindfully.

Sayaṃ [M 0.0108] yānagato hutvā, yathā yānagatassa ce;

Alaṃ vatthuṃ tathā nālaṃ, sachatto chattapāṇino.

If one is oneself in a vehicle, it is suitable to speak to one who is also in a vehicle; otherwise, it is not suitable. It is not suitable to teach one with an umbrella, unless one is also holding an umbrella.

“Sūpodanaviññattisikkhāpadaṃ theyyasatthasamuṭṭhānaṃ, kiriyaṃ, saññāvimokkhaṃ, sacittakaṃ, lokavajjaṃ, kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, akusalacittaṃ, dukkhavedana”nti pāṭho.

The reading is: 'The training rule concerning requesting soup and rice has its origin in the intention to steal, involves an action, is absolved by a change in perception, is intentional, is a worldly fault, is a bodily action, is a verbal action, arises from an unwholesome mind, and is accompanied by painful feeling.'

Sekhiyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sekhiya rules is concluded.

Bhikkhupātimokkhavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Bhikkhunīpātimokkhavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha

Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

The Pārājika Chapter

Abhilāpamattamevāti [M 0.0109][V 0.0104] ettha daharavasena “bhante”ti ca vuḍḍhavasena “āvuso”ti ca tattha duvidho abhilāpo, idha pana vuḍḍhadaharānaṃ “ayyā”ti ekameva.

Here, in the phrase 'merely a form of address,' there are two forms of address there: 'bhante,' used by a junior, and 'āvuso,' used by a senior. But here, for both senior and junior, there is only one form of address: 'ayyā.'

Kāyasaṃsagge vuttanayenāti ettha tabbahulanayena kiriyasamuṭṭhānatā vuttā. “Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjeyyā”ti avatvā pana “sādiyeyyā”ti vuttattā akiriyatopi samuṭṭhātīti veditabbaṃ. Yathā cettha, evaṃ heṭṭhā “manussitthiyā tayo magge methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpatti pārājikassā”tiādinā (pārā. 56) nayena kiriyasamuṭṭhānataṃ vatvā tadanantaraṃ “bhikkhupaccatthikā manussitthiṃ bhikkhussa santikaṃ ānetvā vaccamaggena aṅgajātaṃ abhinisīdenti, so ce pavesanaṃ sādiyatī”tiādinā (pārā. 58) nayena akiriyasamuṭṭhānassapi vuttattā paṭhamapārājikāyapi tabbahulanayeneva kiriyasamuṭṭhānatā veditabbā. Na hi pavesanasādiyanādimhi kiriyasamuṭṭhānatā dissati.

Regarding 'in the manner stated for bodily contact,' here the arising from action is stated according to the predominant method. However, because it is said, 'he should consent,' and not 'he should engage in bodily contact,' it should be understood that it also arises from non-action. Just as here, so too below, where after stating the arising from action in the manner of 'for one who engages in sexual intercourse with a human female through the three orifices, there is an offense of defeat' (Pārā. 56), immediately afterward, the arising from non-action is also stated in the manner of 'the monk's adversaries bring a human female to the monk and make her sit down with her sexual organ on his anus, and if he consents to the entry' (Pārā. 58). Therefore, even in the first offense of defeat, the arising from action should be understood as being according to the predominant method. For in consenting to entry and so on, arising from action is not seen.

Aṅgajātacalanañcettha [V 0.0105] na sārato daṭṭhabbaṃ “so ce pavesanaṃ na sādiyati, paviṭṭhaṃ na sādiyati, ṭhitaṃ na sādiyati, uddharaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti pārājikassā”ti (pārā. 58) ettha ṭhitanasādiyane pakatiyāpi paripuṇṇacalanattā. Sādiyanapaccayā paṭisevanacalanañcettha na dissatevāti tabbahulanayeneva kiriyasamuṭṭhānatā gahetabbā.

And here, the movement of the sexual organ should not be regarded as essential. In the passage, 'If he does not consent to the entry, does not consent to it having entered, does not consent to it remaining, but consents to the withdrawal, it is an offense of defeat' (Pārā. 58), in the case of not consenting to it remaining, there is naturally a complete movement. And here, the movement of intercourse conditioned by consent is not seen at all. Therefore, the arising from action should be understood as being according to the predominant method.

Apica bhikkhuniyāpi paṭhamapārājike tassa sādiyanassa sarūpena vuttattā tadanurūpavasena vibhaṅganayamanoloketvā “kiriyasamuṭṭhāna”micceva vuttaṃ. Yathā cetesu tabbahulanayena kiriyasamuṭṭhānatā vuttā, tathā surādīnaṃ akusaleneva pātabbatā. Itarathā “yaṃ akusaleneva [M 0.0110] āpajjati, ayaṃ lokavajjā, sesā paṇṇattivajjā”ti vutte lokavajjapaṇṇattivajjānaṃ niyamalakkhaṇasiddhi hoti, tathā taṃ avatvā “yassā sacittakapakkhe cittaṃ akusalameva hoti, ayaṃ lokavajjā, sesā paṇṇattivajjā”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanā) vutte lokavajjavacanaṃ niratthakaṃ siyā vatthuajānanapakkhepi akusaleneva pātabbattā. Yasmā tattha surāpānavītikkamassa akusalacittuppādo natthi, tasmā khandhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ “majjapāne pana bhikkhuno ajānitvāpi bījato paṭṭhāya majjaṃ pivantassa pācittiyaṃ. Sāmaṇero jānitvāva pivanto sīlabhedaṃ āpajjati, na ajānitvā”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 108) vuttaṃ, na vuttaṃ “vatthuajānanapakkhe pāṇātipātādīnaṃ siddhikaraakusalacittuppādasadise cittuppāde satipi sāmaṇero sīlabhedaṃ nāpajjatī”ti. Abhinivesavacanaṃ pāṇātipātādīhi samānagatikattā sāmaṇerānaṃ surāpānassa. “Surāmerayime”ti vatthuṃ jānitvā pātabbatādivasena vītikkamantassa akusalassa asambhavo natthi. Tena vuttaṃ “yassā sacittakapakkhe”tiādi.

Moreover, in the case of a bhikkhunī's first offense of defeat, because that consent is stated in its own nature, without considering the method of the Vibhaṅga in accordance with it, it is simply said to be 'arising from action.' Just as in these cases the arising from action is stated according to the predominant method, so too, the drinking of liquor and so on is to be incurred only through what is unwholesome. Otherwise, if it were said, 'That which one incurs only through what is unwholesome is an offense in the world; the rest are offenses by convention,' then the establishment of the defining characteristics of offenses in the world and offenses by convention would occur. But since it is not said thus, and instead it is said, 'That for which, in the case with intention, the mind is only unwholesome, this is an offense in the world; the rest are offenses by convention' (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. First Pārājika Commentary), the statement about an offense in the world would be meaningless, since even in the case of not knowing the object, it is to be incurred only through what is unwholesome. Because in that case, for the transgression of drinking liquor, there is no arising of an unwholesome mind, it is said in the Khandhakaṭṭhakathā: 'But in the case of drinking intoxicants, for a bhikkhu who drinks an intoxicant unknowingly, even from its seed stage, it is a pācittiya. A sāmaṇera, drinking it knowingly, incurs a breach of virtue, but not if unknowingly' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 108). It is not said: 'In the case of not knowing the object, even if there is an arising of mind similar to the arising of an unwholesome mind that brings about accomplishment in killing living beings, etc., a sāmaṇera does not incur a breach of virtue.' The statement about firm adherence applies to a sāmaṇera's drinking of liquor because of its having the same course as killing living beings, etc. For one who transgresses by way of drinkability, etc., knowing the object as 'liquor, fermented drink,' there is no non-existence of the unwholesome. Therefore, it is said, 'That for which, in the case with intention,' etc.

Kiñcettha – yuttivacanena arahantānaṃ appavisanato sacittakācittakapakkhesu akusalaniyamoti ce? Na, dhammatāvasena sekkhānampi appavisanato. Acittakapakkhe akusalaniyamābhāvadassanatthaṃ supantassa mukhe pakkhittajalabindumiva surābinduādayo udāharitabbā. Tabbahulanayena hi atthe gahite pubbenāparaṃ aṭṭhakathāya sameti saddhiṃ pāḷiyā cāti. Ācariyāpi surāpāne akusalaniyamābhāvameva vadanti. Ekacce pana kiriyasamuṭṭhānatā panassa tabbahulanayameva, na paṭhamapārājike. Kathaṃ? Kāyasaṃsaggasikkhāpadaṃ paṭhamapārājikasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Ettha bhikkhussa ca bhikkhuniyā ca kāyasaṃsaggabhāve sati bhikkhunī kāyaṅgaṃ acopayamānāpi citteneva adhivāseti, āpajjati, na evaṃ bhikkhu. Bhikkhu pana copayamānova āpajjati, evameva paṭhamapārājikepi copane sati eva āpajjati, nāsati. Pavesanaṃ [V 0.0106] sādiyatīti ettha pavesanasādiyanaṃ nāma sevanacittuppādanaṃ, maggena vā maggappaṭipannampi icchanti. Tassāpi kāyacalanaṃ ekantaṃ atthi eva. Evaṃ santepi vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbanti vadantīti likhitaṃ

And what of this? If it is said: 'By the word of reason, because Arahants do not engage in it, in both the intentional and unintentional cases, it is necessarily unwholesome?' No, because by nature even trainees do not engage in it. To show the absence of necessary unwholesomeness in the unintentional case, examples like a drop of liquor and so on, like a drop of water placed in the mouth of a sleeping person, should be cited. For when the meaning is grasped through the predominant method, the earlier with the later commentary agrees, and with the Pāḷi as well. The teachers also state that there is no necessary unwholesomeness in drinking liquor. Some, however, say that its arising from action is only by the predominant method, not so in the first offense of defeat. How so? The training rule on bodily contact is the origin of the first offense of defeat. Here, when there is bodily contact between a bhikkhu and a bhikkhunī, a bhikkhunī, even without moving a part of her body, if she consents with the mind alone, incurs an offense; it is not so for a bhikkhu. A bhikkhu, however, incurs an offense only when moving. Similarly, in the first offense of defeat, he incurs an offense only when there is movement, not when there is none. Here, 'consents to the entry' means the arising of a mind for indulgence, or they desire the path or what has entered the path. For that too, bodily movement is certainly present. Even so, they say it should be accepted after investigation—so it is written.

Pārājikavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Offenses of Defeat is concluded.

Saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Offenses of Formal Meeting.

1. Ussayavādikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Contentious Speech.

Bhikkhunīnaṃ [M 0.0111][V 0.0107] saṅghādisesaṃ patvā vuṭṭhānavidhayo sandassanatthaṃ “ayaṃ bhikkhunī…pe… āpannā”ti puggalaniyamaṃ katvā pārājikato adhippāyanti “nissāraṇīyaṃ saṅghādisesa”nti āpattināmaggahaṇañca kataṃ. “Samuṭṭhānādīni paṭhamakathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyamevā”ti pāṭho.

For the purpose of showing the procedure for rehabilitation for bhikkhunīs who have incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense, having made a designation of the person as, 'This bhikkhunī... has incurred an offense,' and intending to distinguish it from an offense of defeat, the name of the offense, 'Saṅghādisesa requiring expulsion,' was also adopted. The reading is: 'The origins, etc., are similar to the first kathina; this, however, is only an action.'

Ussayavādikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Contentious Speech is concluded.

2. Corivuṭṭhāpikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Reinstating a Female Thief.

Katthaci agantvā nisinnaṭṭhāne eva nisīditvā karontiyā vācācittato, khaṇḍasīmādigatāya kāyavācācittato.

For one who acts while sitting right in the place where she is seated, without having gone anywhere, it arises from speech and mind; for one who has gone to a broken boundary and so on, it arises from body, speech, and mind.

Corivuṭṭhāpikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Reinstating a Female Thief is concluded.

3. Ekagāmantaragamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Going to Another Village Alone.

“Ābhogaṃ vinā”ti vuttattā ābhoge sati anāpatti, imasmiṃ pana sikkhāpade samantapāsādikāyaṃ upacārātikkame āpatti vuttā, idha okkame. Dvīsupi vuttaṃ atthato ekameva gāmantaragamanasaṅghādisesaṃ upacārassa sandhāya vuttattā. Gaṇamhā ohīyanassa virodho. “Araññe”ti idaṃ atthavasena vuttaṃ, gāmantarepi hoti eva.

Because it is said, 'without intention,' when there is intention, there is no offense. In this training rule, however, an offense is stated in the Samantapāsādikā for transgressing the precinct, but here for entering. Although stated in two ways, in meaning it is one and the same Saṅghādisesa offense of going to another village, because it is stated with reference to the precinct. It is a contradiction to being left behind by the group. This 'in the wilderness' is stated in terms of meaning; it also occurs in another village.

Sikkhāpadā [V 0.0108] buddhavarena vaṇṇitāti gāthāya vasena, aṭṭhakathāyampi gāmantarapariyāpannaṃ nadipāranti vuttaṃ.

By way of the verse, 'The training rules were praised by the best of Buddhas...' In the commentary, it is also said that 'the other side of the river' is included in 'another village'.

Ekagāmantaragamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Going to Another Village Alone is concluded.

“Chādanapaccayā [M 0.0112] pana dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatī”ti idaṃ –

'However, due to the condition of concealing, one incurs a dukkaṭa offense.' This refers to:

“Āpajjati garukaṃ sāvasesaṃ;

Chādeti anādariyaṃ paṭicca;

Na bhikkhunī no ca phuseyya vajjaṃ;

Pañhāmesā kusalehi cintitā”ti. (pari. 481) –

'One incurs a serious offense that has a remainder; one conceals it on account of disrespect; it is not a bhikkhunī, nor would she touch the fault; this is a question considered by the skilled.' (Pari. 481)

Imāya virujjhati. Tasmā pamādalekhā viya dissatīti gavesitabbo ettha attho. Bhikkhūnaṃ mānattakathāyaṃ “parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nigamanavaṇṇanā) vuttaṃ, idha pana “gāmūpacārato ca bhikkhūnaṃ vihārūpacārato ca dve leḍḍupāte”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatra bhikkhūnaṃ vuttappakārappadesaṃ atikkamitvā gāmepi taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, bhikkhunīnaṃ pana gāme na vaṭṭati. Tasmā evaṃ vuttanti eke. Apare pana bhikkhūnampi gāme na vaṭṭati. Bhikkhuvihāro nāma pubbe eva gāmūpacāraṃ atikkamitvā ṭhito, tasmā gāmaṃ avatvā vihārūpacārameva heṭṭhā vuttaṃ. Bhikkhunīnaṃ vihāro gāme eva vaṭṭati, na bahi, tasmā gāmūpacārañca vihārūpacārañca ubhayamevettha dassitaṃ. Tasmā ubhayatthāpi atthato nānāttaṃ natthīti vadanti. Yaṃ yujjati, taṃ gahetabbaṃ.

This is contrary to that. Therefore, the meaning here should be investigated as though it were a scribal error. In the discussion of the mānatta for monks, it is said: "Beyond two stone-throws from the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, or from a place suitable for enclosure in an unenclosed monastery" (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Nigamanavaṇṇanā). Here, however, it is stated: "Beyond two stone-throws from the village's precinct and from the monks’ monastery's precinct," and so on. In that case, for monks, even having gone beyond the specified area, performing the act in the village is allowable; but for nuns, it is not allowable in the village. Therefore, some say it is stated thus. Others say that even for monks, it is not allowable in the village. A monks’ monastery is, from the outset, already situated beyond the village's precinct. Therefore, without mentioning the village, only the monastery's precinct is mentioned below. For nuns, a monastery is allowable within the village, not outside it. Thus, both the village's precinct and the monastery's precinct are shown here. Therefore, they say there is essentially no difference in meaning in either case. What is fitting should be accepted.

Saṅghādisesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Saṅghādisesas is concluded.

Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Offences Entailing Forfeiture.

Dutiye [M 0.0113][V 0.0109] idha bhājāpitāya laddhacīvaraṃ nissaggiyaṃ hoti, taṃ vinayakammaṃ katvāpi attanā na labbhati.

In the second rule, a robe obtained by distribution becomes subject to forfeiture, and even after performing the disciplinary procedure, one does not obtain it for oneself.

Tatiye “samuṭṭhānādīni adinnādānasadisāni, idaṃ pana dukkhavedana”nti pāṭho.

In the third rule, the reading is: "The arising, etc., are similar to taking what is not given, but this is painful feeling."

Catutthe paṭhamaṃ viññattaṃ alabhitvā aññaṃ tato ūnatarampi labheyya, nissaggiyameva aṅgasampattito.

In the fourth rule, if, having failed to obtain what was first requested, one obtains another that is inferior to it, it is still subject to forfeiture, owing to the completeness of the factors.

Nissaggiyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Nissaggiyas is concluded.

Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Offences Entailing Expiation.

1. Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the First Section.

Paṭhame [M 0.0114][V 0.0110] haritapattavaṇṇo haritako. Cāpalasuṇaṃ amiñjako. Aṅkuramattameva hi tassa hoti. Palaṇḍukādayo sabhāveneva vaṭṭanti. Sūpasampākādī vināpi antamaso yāgubhattepi pakkhipituṃ vaṭṭatīti likhitaṃ, “bhikkhuniyāpi gilānāya purebhattameva lasuṇaṃ kappati, na agilānāyā”ti abhayagirīnaṃ uggahoti.

In the first rule, garlic is green, having the color of green leaves. Cāpala garlic is not oily. It is only a sprout. Onions and the like are allowable by their very nature. It is written that even without curry and other cooked dishes, it is permissible to add it even to rice-gruel. "For a sick bhikkhunī, garlic is allowed only before the meal, but not for one who is not sick"—this is the tenet of the Abhayagirivāsins.

Dutiye ābādhapaccayā bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ āpucchitvā saṃharāpetuṃ vaṭṭati, bhikkhussa ettha ca lasuṇe ca dukkaṭaṃ.

In the second rule, on account of illness, it is permissible to ask permission from the community of bhikkhunīs and then have it collected; but for a bhikkhu, there is a dukkaṭa offence in this matter and regarding garlic.

Sattame “samuṭṭhānādīni addhānamaggasikkhāpadasadisānī”ti pāṭho.

In the seventh rule, the reading is: "The arising, etc., are similar to the training rule on a journey along a road."

Navame kuṭṭo nāma gharakuṭṭo. Pākāro nāma parikkhepapākāro.

In the ninth rule, "kuṭṭa" means a house wall. "Pākāra" means an enclosure wall.

Chaḍḍitakhetteti purāṇakhette. Saṅghasantake bhikkhussa chaḍḍetuṃ vaṭṭati saṅghapariyāpannattā. Bhikkhunīnampi saṅghasantake bhikkhusaṅghasantake vuttanayeneva vaṭṭati. Evaṃ santepi sāruppavasena kātabbanti likhitaṃ.

"Chaḍḍitakhetta" means an old field. It is permissible for a bhikkhu to dispose of something in property belonging to the Saṅgha because it is included in Saṅgha property. It is also permissible for bhikkhunīs in property belonging to the Saṅgha and in property belonging to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, following the method stated. Even so, it is written that it should be done in a suitable manner.

Dasame “sayaṃ tāni vatthūni karontiyā”tiādi idha sikkhāpade natthi. Kasmā? Eḷakalomasamuṭṭhānattā. Yadi evaṃ kasmā vuttanti ce? Suttānulomamahāpadesato. Yadi naccādīni passituṃ vā suṇituṃ vā na labhati, pageva attanā kātunti nayato labbhamānattā vuttaṃ. Itarathā mahāpadesā niratthakā siyuṃ. “Evaṃ aññatthapi nayo netabbo. Samuṭṭhānampi idha vuttameva [V 0.0111] aggahetvā chasamuṭṭhānavasena gahetabba”nti ācariyā. Idha vuttaṃ samuṭṭhānaṃ nāma mūlabhūtassa antarā vuttāpattiyā, tasmā eḷakalomasamuṭṭhānamevāti apare. Ārāme ṭhatvāti na kevalaṃ ṭhatvā, tato gantvā pana sabbiriyāpathehipi labhati. Ārāme ṭhitāti pana ārāmapariyāpannāti attho. Itarathā nisinnāpi na labheyyāti.

In the tenth rule, "if she herself makes those things," etc., is not found in this training rule. Why? Because it originates from sheep's wool. If so, why is it mentioned? Due to the Great Reference in accordance with the Suttas. If one is not allowed to see or hear dances, etc., how much less to do it oneself—it is said because it is obtained from this principle. Otherwise, the Great References would be meaningless. The teachers say: "This principle should be applied elsewhere as well. The origin here should also be understood in terms of the six origins, without taking only what is stated here." Others say: The origin mentioned here is for the offence stated in between, which is the root; therefore, it is solely from sheep's wool. "Standing in the monastery" does not mean only standing; having gone from there, one incurs it in all postures. "Standing in the monastery" means that it is included in the monastery. Otherwise, one would not incur it even while sitting.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Section is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Section.

Pañcame [M 0.0115] upacāro dvādasahattho. “Samuṭṭhānādīni kathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho.

In the fifth rule, the precinct is twelve cubits. The reading is: "The arising, etc., are similar to the Kathina, but this concerns action and non-action."

Sattame dhuvapaññatteti bhikkhunīnaṃ atthāya. Kulānīti kulagharāni.

In the seventh rule, "permanent regulation" is for the benefit of the bhikkhunīs. "Families" means family homes.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Section is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Third Section.

Catutthe saṅghāṭiādivasena adhiṭṭhitānaṃ saṅghāṭicāraṃ.

In the fourth rule, for robes determined as an outer robe, etc., it is the practice concerning the outer robe.

Pañcame “idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho.

In the fifth rule, the reading is: "But this is action and non-action."

Chaṭṭhe aññasmiṃ parikkhāre dukkaṭanti thālakādīnaṃ vā sappitelādīnaṃ vā aññatarasmiṃ.

In the sixth rule, regarding another requisite, it is a dukkaṭa offence—in any one of either bowls, etc., or ghee, oil, etc.

Tatiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Third Section is concluded.

4. Catutthavaggavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Fourth Section.

Chaṭṭhe saṃsaṭṭhavihārasikkhāpade “sesamettha paṭhamaariṭṭhasikkhāpade vuttavinicchayasadisamevā”ti pāṭho.

In the sixth training rule, on dwelling in association, the reading is: "The remainder here is just like the decision stated in the first training rule concerning Ariṭṭha."

Catutthavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Fourth Section is concluded.

5. Pañcamavaggavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Fifth Section.

“Cittāgāraṃ [V 0.0112] nāma yattha katthaci manussānaṃ kīḷituṃ ramituṃ kataṃ hotī”tiādinā (pāci. 979) pāḷiyaṃ vuttattā cittāgārādīni sabbesaṃ atthāya katāni, na rañño eva.

Because it is stated in the Pāli text (Pāc. 979), beginning with "A picture hall is a place made anywhere for people to play and enjoy themselves," etc., picture halls and so on are made for the benefit of all, not only for the king.

Sattame etena nissajjituṃ kappiyaṃ vuttaṃ. “Nissajjitvā paribhuñjatī”ti (pāci. 1007) pāḷi ca atthi. “Samuṭṭhānādīni kathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho. Aṭṭhamepi esova pāṭho.

In the seventh, it is stated that it is allowable to relinquish this. There is also the Pāli passage, “Having relinquished, one may use it” (Pāc. 1007). The reading is, “The arising, etc., are like the Kathina; however, this is action and non-action.” The same reading applies in the eighth.

Pañcamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the fifth section is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Sixth Section

Dasame [M 0.0116] “samuṭṭhānādīni kathinasadisāni, idaṃ pana kiriyākiriya”nti pāṭho.

In the tenth, the reading is, “The arising, etc., are similar to the Kathina, but this is action and non-action.”

Chaṭṭhavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the sixth section is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Eighth Section

Paṭhamadutiyatatiyesu “gihigatā”ti vā “kumāribhūtā”ti vā na vattabbā. Vadanti ce, kammaṃ kuppati.

In the first, second, and third, one should not say “gone to a householder” or “become a maiden.” If one says so, the formal act is invalidated.
