Adhicitte ca āyogoti vipassanāpādakaṃ [V 0.0145] aṭṭhasamāpatticittaṃ, tatopi maggaphalacittameva adhicittaṃ, tasmiṃ yathāvutte adhicitte āyogo ca anuyogo cāti attho. Etaṃ buddhāna sāsananti etaṃ parassa anupavadanaṃ, anupaghātanaṃ, pātimokkhe saṃvaro, paṭiggahaṇaparibhogesu mattaññutā, aṭṭhasamāpattivasibhāvāya vivittasenāsanasevanañca buddhānaṃ sāsanaṃ ovādo anusiṭṭhīti. Imā pana tisso gāthā sabbabuddhānaṃ pātimokkhuddesagāthāyo hontīti veditabbā. Taṃ buddhā eva uddisanti, na sāvakā.

In the third verse, 'not reviling' means not reproaching anyone by speech. 'Not harming' means not causing harm to anyone with the body. 'In the Pātimokkha' refers to that which is the Pātimokkha, the principal, the chief, the supreme virtue. It protects from wrong courses and liberates from the fears of bad destinations. Or, because it liberates one who protects it, it is called 'Pātimokkha.' 'And restraint' in that Pātimokkha is the restraint characterized by not transgressing the seven classes of offenses. 'Moderation' means knowing the proper measure in receiving and using. 'And a remote lodging' refers to a lodging that is remote from the clashing of people, uncrowded, secluded. And here, contentment with the four requisites should be understood as being indicated by means of only two requisites, because the other two are also illuminated by the method of inferring a characteristic from the general principle of contentment with requisites. 'And application to the higher mind' refers to the mind of the eight attainments that is a basis for insight; even more so, the path and fruit consciousness itself is the higher mind. The meaning is application and devotion to that higher mind as described. 'This is the teaching of the Buddhas' means that this—not reproaching others, not harming them, restraint in the Pātimokkha, moderation in receiving and using, and frequenting secluded lodgings for the sake of mastery over the eight attainments—is the teaching, the exhortation, the instruction of the Buddhas. These three verses, however, should be understood as the verses for the recitation of the Pātimokkha of all Buddhas. The Buddhas themselves recite them, not the disciples.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”tiādinā (mahāva. 134) nayena vuttaṃ āṇāpātimokkhaṃ nāma. Taṃ sāvakā eva uddisanti, na buddhā saṅghakammaṃ karonti, na ca tattha pariyāpannāti āha “taṃ sāvakā eva uddisanti, na buddhā”ti. Imasmiṃ attheti “pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyā”ti etasmiṃ atthe.

That which is spoken in the manner beginning, 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me' (Mahāvagga 134), is called the Pātimokkha of command. The disciples alone recite this, for the Buddhas do not perform a formal act of the Saṅgha, nor are they included therein. Thus it was said: 'The disciples alone recite it, not the Buddhas.' 'In this sense' means in the sense of 'one should recite the Pātimokkha.'

Anupagato nāma tattheva upasampanno, asatiyā purimikāya anupagato vā. Cātumāsiniyanti cātumāsiyaṃ. Sā hi catunnaṃ māsānaṃ pāripūribhūtāti cātumāsī, sā eva “cātumāsinī”ti vuccati, tassaṃ cātumāsiniyaṃ. Pacchimakattikapuṇṇamāsiniyanti attho. Kāyasāmagginti kāyena samaggabhāvaṃ, hatthapāsūpagamananti vuttaṃ hoti.

One who has not entered means one who was ordained right there, or one who has not entered because the earlier period was not undertaken. `Cātumāsiniyaṃ` means on the four-monthly day. For, because it is the completion of four months, it is called Cātumāsī; that same is called Cātumāsinī; on that four-monthly day. The meaning is: on the last full-moon day of Kattika. Bodily concord means the state of being together bodily; that is to say, coming within hand's reach.

Ayaṃ panettha vinicchayo – sace purimikāya pañca bhikkhū vassaṃ upagatā, pacchimikāyapi pañca, purimehi ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārite pacchimehi [M 0.0153] tesaṃ santike pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo, na ekasmiṃ uposathagge dve ñattiyo ṭhapetabbā. Sacepi pacchimikāya upagatā cattāro, tayo, dve, eko vā hoti, eseva nayo. Atha purimikāya cattāro, pacchimikāyapi cattāro, tayo, dve, eko vā, eseva nayo. Atha purimikāya tayo, pacchimikāya tayo, dve vā, eseva nayo. Idañhettha lakkhaṇaṃ – sace purimikāya upagatehi pacchimikāya upagatā thokatarā ceva honti samasamā ca, saṅghappavāraṇāya ca gaṇaṃ pūrenti, saṅghappavāraṇāvasena ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā purimehi pavāretabbā. Sace pana purimikāya tayo, pacchimikāya eko hoti, tena saddhiṃ te cattāro honti, catunnaṃ saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavāretuṃ na vaṭṭati. Gaṇañattiyā pana so gaṇapūrako hoti, tasmā gaṇavasena ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā purimehi pavāretabbaṃ, itarena tesaṃ santike pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Sace purimikāya dve, pacchimikāya dve vā eko vā, etthāpi eseva nayo. Sace purimikāya eko, pacchimikāyapi eko, ekena ekassa santike pavāretabbaṃ, ekena pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo[V 0.0146]. Sace purimavassūpagatehi pacchimavassūpagatā ekenapi adhikatarā honti, paṭhamaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitvā pacchā thokatarehi tesaṃ santike pavāretabbaṃ. Kattikacātumāsinipavāraṇāya pana sace paṭhamaṃ vassūpagatehi mahāpavāraṇāya pavāritehi pacchā upagatā adhikatarā vā samasamā vā honti, pavāraṇāñattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavāretabbaṃ. Tehi pavārite pacchā itarehi pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Atha mahāpavāraṇāya pavāritā bahū honti, pacchā vassūpagatā thokā vā eko vā, pātimokkhe uddiṭṭhe pacchā tesaṃ santike tena pavāretabbanti.

Here is the ruling on this matter: If five bhikkhus entered the rains in the earlier period and five in the later period, the earlier ones should invite after putting the motion, and the later ones should perform the Uposatha of purity in their presence. Two motions should not be put in a single Uposatha hall. The same procedure applies if those who entered in the later period are four, three, two, or one. And if those who entered in the earlier period are four, and those in the later period are four, three, two, or one, the same procedure applies. And if those who entered in the earlier period are three, and those in the later period are three or two, the same procedure applies. This is the guiding principle here: If those who entered in the later period are fewer than or equal in number to those who entered in the earlier period, and they complete the number for a Saṅgha invitation, the earlier ones should invite after putting the motion on the authority of a Saṅgha invitation. But if there are three from the earlier period and one from the later period, they are four in total, and it is not allowable for four to invite after putting a motion for the Saṅgha. However, that one completes the number for a group motion, so the earlier ones should invite after putting the motion on the authority of a group, and the other should perform the Uposatha of purity in their presence. If there are two from the earlier period and two or one from the later period, the same procedure applies. If there is one from the earlier period and one from the later period, the former should invite in the presence of the latter, and the latter should perform the Uposatha of purity. If those who entered the rains in the later period are more numerous, even by one, than those who entered in the earlier period, the Pātimokkha should be recited first, and afterwards the smaller group should invite in the presence of the larger group. As to the four-monthly invitation of Kattika, if, after those who entered the rains in the earlier period have invited with the great invitation, those who entered later are more numerous or equal in number, they should invite after putting the invitation motion. After they have invited, the others should perform the Uposatha of purity. But if those who invited with the great invitation are many, and those who entered the rains later are few or only one, then after the Pātimokkha has been recited, the latter should invite in their presence.

Ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvāti ekasmiṃ aṃse sādhukaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvāti attho. Añjaliṃ paggahetvāti dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalaṃ añjaliṃ ukkhipitvā. Sace pana tattha pārivāsikopi atthi, saṅghanavakaṭṭhāne nisīditvā tattheva nisinnena attano pāḷiyā pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Pātimokkhe uddisiyamāne pana pāḷiyā anisīditvā pāḷiṃ vihāya hatthapāsaṃ amuñcantena nisīditabbaṃ. Pavāraṇāyapi eseva nayo.

Having arranged the upper robe over one shoulder means having properly arranged the upper robe over one shoulder. Having raised the joined palms means having lifted up the joined palms, resplendent with the ten fingernails brought together. If a monk on probation is also present, he should sit in the place of the most junior monk of the Saṅgha and, while seated right there, perform the Uposatha of purity with his own recitation. But while the Pātimokkha is being recited, he should not sit in the line of monks; having left the line, he should sit without going beyond hand's reach. The same procedure applies for the Pavāraṇā.

Sabbaṃ [M 0.0154] pubbakaraṇīyanti sammajjanādiṃ navavidhaṃ pubbakiccaṃ. Yathā ca sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāpattiṃ āpajjitvā “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… paṭikarissatī”ti (mahāva. 171) ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ labhati, evametthāpi tīhi “suṇantu me āyasmantā ime bhikkhū sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpannā, yadā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ suddhaṃ anāpattikaṃ passissanti, tadā tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissantī”ti gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā, dvīhipi “aññaṃ suddhaṃ passitvā paṭikarissāmā”ti vatvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Ekenāpi “parisuddhaṃ labhitvā paṭikarissāmī”ti ābhogaṃ katvā kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Tadahūti tasmiṃ ahu, tasmiṃ divaseti attho. Nānāsaṃvāsakehīti laddhinānāsaṃvāsakehi. Anāvāso nāma navakammasālādiko yo koci padeso. Aññatra saṅghenāti saṅghappahonakehi bhikkhūhi vinā. Aññatra antarāyāti pubbe vuttaṃ dasavidhamantarāyaṃ vinā. Sabbantimena pana paricchedena attacatutthena antarāye vā sati gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Yathā ca āvāsādayo na gantabbā, evaṃ sace vihāre uposathaṃ karonti, uposathādhiṭṭhānatthaṃ sīmāpi nadīpi na gantabbā. Sace panettha koci bhikkhu hoti, tassa santikaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Vissaṭṭhauposathāpi āvāsā gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ gato adhiṭṭhātumpi labhati. Āraññakenāpi bhikkhunā uposathadivase gāme piṇḍāya caritvā attano vihārameva āgantabbaṃ. Sace aññaṃ vihāraṃ okkamati, tattha uposathaṃ katvāva āgantabbaṃ, akatvā āgantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Yaṃ jaññā “ajjeva tattha gantuṃ sakkomī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 181) [V 0.0147] evarūpo pana āvāso gantabbo. Tattha bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ uposathaṃ karontenāpi hi iminā neva uposathantarāyo kato bhavissatīti.

All preliminary duties refers to the ninefold preparatory tasks, such as sweeping. Just as the entire Saṅgha, having committed a shared offense, can perform the Uposatha by proposing the motion, “Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me… he will make amends,” so too here, it is permissible to perform the Uposatha if three monks propose a group motion with the words, “Venerable sirs, let the venerable ones listen to me. These monks have committed a shared offense. When they see another monk who is pure and without offense, they will make amends before him,” or if two monks declare, “We will make amends after seeing another pure monk.” It is also permissible for a single monk to perform it after making the resolution, “I will make amends after finding a pure one.” On that day means on that very day. Those of different communion means those of different communion on account of doctrine. Anāvāsa means any place such as a new workshop. Except for the Saṅgha means without a number of monks sufficient to form a Saṅgha. Except for an obstacle means without the ten previously mentioned obstacles. But as a final resort, when there is an obstacle, it is permissible to go with oneself as the fourth. And just as one should not go to residences and so on, so too, if they perform the Uposatha in a monastery, the boundary or a river should not be gone to for the purpose of determining the Uposatha. If a monk is present there, however, it is permissible to go to him. It is also permissible to go from a residence where the Uposatha has been dismissed. Having gone thus, one is also allowed to determine it. A forest-dwelling monk, after going for alms in the village on the Uposatha day, should return to his own monastery. If he enters another monastery, he must perform the Uposatha there before returning; it is not permissible to return without doing so. But one should go to the kind of residence about which one knows, “I can get there today itself.” For by performing the Uposatha with the monks there, no obstacle to the Uposatha will have been created by him.

Udakaṃ āsanena cāti āsanena saha pānīyaparibhojanīyaṃ udakañcāti attho. Saṅghasannipātato paṭhamaṃ kattabbaṃ pubbakaraṇaṃ. Pubbakaraṇato pacchā kattabbampi uposathakammato paṭhamaṃ kattabbattā pubbakiccaṃ. Ubhayampi cetaṃ uposathakammato paṭhamaṃ kattabbattā “pubbakicca”micceva ettha vuttanti āha “evaṃ dvīhi nāmehi navavidhaṃ pubbakiccaṃ dassita”nti. Kiṃ taṃ katanti pucchatīti āha “na hī”tiādi. Taṃ akatvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati “na, bhikkhave, therena āṇattena agilānena na [M 0.0155] sammajjitabbaṃ, yo na sammajjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”tiādi (mahāva. 159) vacanato. Tenevāha “tasmā therena āṇattenā”tiādi.

And water with a seat means water for drinking and for use, together with a seat. The preliminary duty is what should be done before the Saṅgha assembles. What should be done after the preliminary duty is also a preliminary task because it must be done before the Uposatha act. Because both of these must be done before the Uposatha act, they are here called simply 'preliminary tasks.' Thus he says: 'In this way the ninefold preliminary task has been shown with two names.' To answer the question, 'Why must this be done?', he says: 'For it is not...', etc. It is not permissible to perform the Uposatha without doing this, because it is said: 'Monks, a healthy monk who has been instructed by an elder should not fail to sweep; whoever should not sweep, commits an offense of wrong-doing,' etc. Therefore he says: 'Therefore, when instructed by an elder...', etc.

Sace pana āṇatto sammajjaniṃ tāvakālikampi na labhati, sākhābhaṅgaṃ kappiyaṃ kāretvā sammajjitabbaṃ. Tampi alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti. Pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbanti āgantukānaṃ atthāya pānīyaparibhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Āsanaṃ paññāpetabbanti pīṭhaphalakādiāsanaṃ paññāpetabbaṃ. Sace uposathāgāre āsanāni natthi, saṃghikāvāsatopi āharitvā paññāpetvā puna haritabbāni. Āsanesu asati kaṭasārakepi taṭṭikāyopi paññāpetuṃ vaṭṭati. Taṭṭikāsupi asati sākhābhaṅgāni kappiyaṃ kāretvā paññāpetabbāni. Kappiyakārakaṃ alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti. Padīpo kātabboti padīpetabbo, padīpujjalanaṃ kātabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Āṇāpentena pana “asukasmiṃ nāma okāse telaṃ vā vaṭṭi vā kapallikā vā atthi, taṃ gahetvā karohī”ti vattabbo. Sace telādīni natthi, pariyesitabbāni. Pariyesitvā alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti. Apica kapāle aggipi jāletabbo. Āṇāpentena ca kiñci kammaṃ karonto vā sadākālameva eko vā bhāranittharaṇako vā sarabhāṇakadhammakathikādīsu aññataro vā na āṇāpetabbo, avasesā pana vārena āṇāpetabbā. Tenāha “therenāpi patirūpaṃ ñatvā āṇāpetabba”nti.

If, however, the one instructed does not obtain even a temporary broom, he should have a broken branch made allowable and then sweep. If he does not obtain that either, it is allowable as obtained. Drinking water and water for use should be provided means that drinking water and water for use should be provided for the sake of incoming monks. Seats should be prepared means that seats such as stools and planks should be prepared. If there are no seats in the Uposatha hall, they should be brought from a Saṅgha residence, prepared, and then returned. If there are no seats, it is permissible to prepare mats of grass or woven leaves. If even mats are not available, broken branches should be made allowable and prepared. If one does not find a maker of allowable things, it is allowable as obtained. A lamp should be made means it should be lit; that is, the lighting of a lamp should be done. When giving the instruction, one should say: “In such and such a place there is oil, a wick, or a potsherd; take that and do it.” If oil and so on are not available, they should be sought. If they are not found after searching, it is allowable as obtained. Moreover, a fire may be lit in a potsherd. And when giving an instruction, one should not always instruct the same person who is already doing some work, or one who carries out burdens, or one among the chanters, Dhamma-talkers, and so on; but the rest should be instructed in turn. Therefore he says: “Even an elder should give the instruction after knowing what is suitable.”

Bahi uposathaṃ katvā āgatenāti nadiyā vā sīmāya vā yattha katthaci uposathaṃ katvā āgatena chando dātabbo, “kato mayā uposatho”ti acchituṃ na labhatīti adhippāyo. Kiccappasuto vāti gilānupaṭṭhākādikiccappasuto vā. Sace gilāno chandapārisuddhiṃ dātuṃ na sakkoti, mañcena vā pīṭhena vā saṅghamajjhaṃ ānetvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ [V 0.0148] bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti “sace kho mayaṃ imaṃ gilānaṃ ṭhānā cāvessāma, ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati, kālakiriyā vā bhavissatī”ti, na tveva so gilāno ṭhānā cāvetabbo, saṅghena tattha gantvā uposatho kātabbo, na tveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo. Kareyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Sace bahū tādisā gilānā honti, saṅghena paṭipāṭiyā ṭhatvā [M 0.0156] sabbe hatthapāse kātabbā. Sace dūre dūre honti, saṅgho nappahoti, taṃ divasaṃ uposatho na kātabbo, na tveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe pārisuddhiṃ dentena chandampi dātuṃ, santi saṅghassa karaṇīya”nti (mahāva. 165) vuttattā bhagavato āṇaṃ karontena “chandaṃ dammī”ti vuttaṃ. “Chandahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande tattheva pakkamati, aññassa dātabbo chando”tiādivacanato (mahāva. 165) puna attano chandadānaparissamavinodanatthaṃ “chandaṃ me harā”ti vuttaṃ. “Chandahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande saṅghappatto sañcicca na āroceti, āhaṭo hoti chando, chandahārakassa āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 165) vuttattā dukkaṭato taṃ mocetuṃ “chandaṃ me ārocehī”ti vuttaṃ.

By one who has performed the Uposatha outside and returned means that one who has performed the Uposatha anywhere—at a river or at a boundary—and returned should give his consent; the intention is that he is not allowed to remain silent, thinking, “I have performed the Uposatha.” Or one who is occupied with duties means one who is occupied with duties such as attending to the sick. If a sick monk is unable to give his consent and purity, the Uposatha should be performed after he has been brought into the midst of the Saṅgha on a bed or a chair. If the monks attending to the sick think, “If we move this sick monk from his place, his illness will worsen or he will die,” that sick monk should not be moved from his place. The Saṅgha should go there and perform the Uposatha; the Uposatha should not be performed by an incomplete Saṅgha. If one should do so, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If there are many such sick monks, the Saṅgha should stand in order and bring them all within hand’s reach. If they are far apart and the Saṅgha is not able to do this, the Uposatha should not be performed on that day; but the Uposatha should not be performed by an incomplete Saṅgha. Because it is said, “I allow, monks, that on the Uposatha day, one giving his purity may also give his consent, for the Saṅgha has business to attend to,” one who is carrying out the Blessed One’s instruction says, “I give my consent.” Because of the statement, “If, monks, the consent-bearer, after the consent has been given, departs right there, the consent should be given to another,” etc., one says, “Convey my consent,” in order to avoid the trouble of giving one’s consent again. Because it is said, “If, monks, the consent-bearer, after the consent has been given, having reached the Saṅgha, deliberately does not announce it, the consent is considered conveyed, but the consent-bearer commits an offense of wrong-doing,” one says, “Announce my consent,” in order to free him from that offense of wrong-doing.

Kāyena vā vācāya vā ubhayena vā viññāpetabboti manasā cintetvā kāyappayogaṃ karontena yena kenaci aṅgapaccaṅgena vā, vācaṃ pana nicchāretuṃ sakkontena tatheva vācāya vā, ubhayathāpi sakkontena kāyavācāhi vā viññāpetabbo, jānāpetabboti attho. “Ayaṃ attho”ti vacanato pana yāya kāyacipi bhāsāya viññāpetuṃ vaṭṭati, pārisuddhidānepi chandadāne vuttasadisova vinicchayo. Taṃ pana dentena paṭhamaṃ santī āpatti desetabbā. Na hi sāpattiko samāno “pārisuddhiṃ dammi, pārisuddhiṃ me hara, pārisuddhiṃ me ārocehī”ti (mahāva. 164) vattuṃ labhati. “Santi saṅghassa karaṇīyānī”ti vattabbe vacanavipallāsena “santi saṅghassa karaṇīya”nti vuttaṃ. Tesañca attano ca chandapārisuddhiṃ detīti ettha chando ca chandapārisuddhi ca chandapārisuddhi, taṃ detīti sarūpekasesanayena attho daṭṭhabbo. Itarāti aññesaṃ chandapārisuddhi. Biḷālasaṅkhalikā chandapārisuddhīti ettha biḷālasaṅkhalikā nāma biḷālabandhanaṃ. Tattha hi saṅkhalikāya paṭhamavalayaṃ dutiyavalayaṃyeva pāpuṇāti, na tatiyaṃ, evamayampi chandapārisuddhi dāyakena yassa dinnā, tato aññattha na gacchatīti (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.164; vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.164). Tasmā sā biḷālasaṅkhalikasadisattā “biḷālasaṅkhalikā”ti vuttā. Biḷālasaṅkhalikaggahaṇañcettha yāsaṃ kāsañci saṅkhalikānaṃ upalakkhaṇamattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

One should make it known by body, or by speech, or by both means that one who has conceived it in his mind should make it known by making a bodily gesture with some limb or member, or, if able to utter speech, by speech just so, or, if able to do both, by body and speech. The meaning is one should inform. However, because of the statement, “This is the meaning,” it is permissible to make it known by any gesture or language. In giving purity, the ruling is the same as that stated for giving consent. But when giving it, one must first confess any existing offense. For one who has an offense is not allowed to say: “I give my purity; convey my purity; announce my purity.” When one should say, “The Saṅgha has business (plural),” it was said, “The Saṅgha has business (singular),” by a slip of the tongue. In the phrase 'he gives their and his own consent-and-purity,' here 'consent' and 'consent-and-purity' become 'consent-and-purity.' The meaning, that he gives this, should be understood by way of the sarūpekasesa method. Others’ means the consent-and-purity of others. In cat’s chain consent-and-purity, cat’s chain means a cat’s tether. For in a chain, the first link reaches only the second, not the third; so too this consent-and-purity, having been given by the giver to someone, does not go elsewhere. Therefore, because it is similar to a cat’s chain, it is called “cat’s chain.” And the taking up of “cat’s chain” here should be understood as merely an illustration for any kind of chain.

Utukkhānanti [M 0.0157][V 0.0149] taṃ taṃ kiriyaṃ arati vattetīti utu, tassa akkhānaṃ utukkhānaṃ, utuācikkhananti attho. Yathā ca tassa ācikkhanaṃ, taṃ sarūpato dassetuṃ “hemantādīna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Gaṇanāti kalanā. Bhikkhunīnaṃ aṭṭhagarudhammehi ovadanaṃ bhikkhunovādo. Sve uposathoti āgantvāti “sve uposatho hotī”ti vutte ajjeva āgantvā pannarasike uposathe pakkhassa cātuddasiyaṃ, cātuddasike terasiyaṃ āgantvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “pakkhassa terasiyaṃyeva āgantvā ‘ayaṃ uposatho cātuddasiko vā pannarasiko vā’ti pucchitabba”nti (pāci. aṭṭha. 149) vuttaṃ. Evaṃ pucchitena ca bhikkhunā sace cātuddasiyaṃ uposathaṃ karonti, “cātuddasiko bhaginī”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace pannarasiyaṃ karonti, “pannarasiko bhaginī”ti vattabbaṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā bālaṃ, ṭhapetvā gilānaṃ, ṭhapetvā gamikaṃ avasesehi ovādaṃ gahetu”nti (cūḷava. 414) vuttattā “taṃ ṭhapetvā”tiādimāha. Tattha ārocanavidhānaṃ ajānanto bālo. Cātuddasikapannarasikesu uposathesu vā pāṭipade vā gantukāmo gamiyo, dutiyapakkhadivasato pana paṭṭhāya tato uddhaṃ gacchanto idha gamiyo nāma na hoti. Araññe nivāso assāti āraññiko. Sopi “ahaṃ araññavāsī, sve uposatho, vihāre na vasāmī”ti appaṭiggahituṃ na labhati. Yadi na gaṇheyya, dukkaṭaṃ āpajjeyya. Vuttañhetaṃ “na, bhikkhave, ovādo na gahetabbo, yo na gaṇheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 414). Tena pana paccāharaṇatthāya saṅketo kātabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āraññikena bhikkhunā ovādaṃ gahetuṃ, saṅketañca kātuṃ atra patiharissāmī”ti (cūḷava. 415). Tasmā āraññikena bhikkhunā sace bhikkhunīnaṃ vasanagāme bhikkhā labbhati, tattheva caritvā bhikkhuniyo disvā ārocetvā gantabbaṃ. No cassa tattha bhikkhā sulabhā hoti, sāmantagāme caritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ gāmaṃ āgamma tatheva kātabbaṃ. Sace dūraṃ gantabbaṃ hoti, saṅketo kātabbo “ahaṃ asukaṃ nāma tumhākaṃ gāmadvāre sabhaṃ vā maṇḍapaṃ vā rukkhamūlaṃ vā upasaṅkamissāmi, tatra āgaccheyyāthā”ti. Bhikkhunīhi tatra gantabbaṃ, agantuṃ na labbhati. Vuttañhetaṃ “na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā saṅketaṃ [M 0.0158] na gantabbaṃ, yā na gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 415). Uposathaggeti uposathakaraṇaṭṭhāne. Aṭṭhahi aṅgehīti –

The declaration of the season (utukkhānaṃ): a season (utu) is that which brings about this or that activity; its declaration (akkhānaṃ) is utukkhānaṃ, meaning, announcing the season. And to show its announcement in its own form, the words 'of winter, etc.' have been stated. Counting is calculation. The admonition of bhikkhunīs concerning the eight weighty rules is the admonition to bhikkhunīs (bhikkhunovādo). 'Tomorrow is the Uposatha' means arriving beforehand. When it is said, 'Tomorrow is the Uposatha,' it means that for a fifteenth-day Uposatha of the fortnight one should arrive today, on the fourteenth, and for a fourteenth-day Uposatha, on the thirteenth. But in the Mahāpaccarī it is said: 'One should arrive on the thirteenth day of the fortnight and ask, “Is this Uposatha a fourteenth-day or a fifteenth-day one?”' When asked thus, if the bhikkhunīs observe the fourteenth-day Uposatha, the bhikkhu should say, 'Sisters, it is the fourteenth.' If they observe the fifteenth-day Uposatha, he should say, 'Sisters, it is the fifteenth.' Since it is said, 'I allow, bhikkhus, that the admonition be received by the remaining ones, setting aside the foolish, setting aside the sick, and setting aside the traveler' (Cv.X.9.4), he says, 'setting that aside,' etc. Here, one who does not know the procedure of announcement is the foolish one. One who intends to go on the fourteenth- or fifteenth-day Uposatha days or on the first day of the new fortnight is a traveler. But one who goes from the second day of the fortnight onwards is not called a traveler here. One who has his dwelling in the forest is a forest-dweller (āraññiko). Even he cannot refuse to accept it, thinking, 'I am a forest-dweller; tomorrow is the Uposatha; I will not stay in the monastery.' If he did not accept it, he would incur an offense of wrong-doing. For it has been said: 'Bhikkhus, the admonition is not to be refused. Whoever should not accept it, there is an offense of wrong-doing' (Cv.X.9.4). But by him an appointment should be made for the purpose of reporting back. For it has been said: 'I allow, bhikkhus, a forest-dwelling bhikkhu to receive the admonition and to make an appointment: “I will report back at this place”' (Cv.X.9.5). Therefore, if a forest-dwelling bhikkhu can obtain alms in the village where the bhikkhunīs reside, he should go on almsround there, see the bhikkhunīs, inform them, and then depart. If alms are not easily obtained for him there, he should go on almsround in a neighboring village, go to the bhikkhunīs’ village, and do the same. If he must go far, an appointment should be made: 'I will approach a certain assembly hall or pavilion or the root of a tree at your village gate; you should come there.' The bhikkhunīs must go there; they are not allowed not to go. For it has been said: 'Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not fail to go to the appointed place. Whichever one should not go, there is an offense of wrong-doing' (Cv.X.9.5). 'In the Uposatha hall' means in the place for performing the Uposatha. 'By eight factors' means—

“Sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā [V 0.0150] honti, dhātā vacasā paricitā, manasā anupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso. Kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo. Yebhuyyena bhikkhunīnaṃ piyo hoti manāpo. Paṭibalo hoti bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ. Na kho panetaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa pabbajitāya kāsāyavatthavasanāya garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannapubbo hoti. Vīsativasso vā hoti atirekavīsativasso vā”ti (pāci. 147) –

“He is virtuous, dwelling restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint, endowed with good conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, he trains himself in the training rules, having undertaken them. He is erudite, a preserver of what he has heard, a treasurer of what he has heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the perfectly complete and pure holy life—such teachings have been often heard by him, borne in mind, practiced with the voice, reflected upon with the mind, and well penetrated by view. Both Pātimokkhas are well mastered by him in detail, well analyzed, well transmitted, well determined, rule by rule, clause by clause. He is a good speaker with a pleasing delivery. For the most part, he is dear and agreeable to the bhikkhunīs. He is capable of admonishing the bhikkhunīs. He has not previously transgressed a weighty rule with a bhikkhunī who has gone forth for the sake of the Blessed One and wears the ochre robe. He is twenty years of age or more than twenty years of age.” (cf. AN 8.51) –

Imehi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi. Pāsādikenāti pasādāvahena niddosena kāyavacīmanokammena. Sampādetūti tividhaṃ sikkhaṃ sampādetu. Yadā pana tāhi bhikkhunīhi pātimokkhuddesakaṃyeva disvā ovādo yācito, tadā uposathagge sannipatitehi bhikkhusaṅghehi pubbakiccavasena “atthi kāci bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ yācamānā”ti pucchite “evaṃ vadehī”ti attanā vattabbavacanaṃ aññena kathāpetvā “atthi koci bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammato”tiādiṃ sayaṃ vatvā puna sayameva gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Aññena vā bhikkhunā tasmiṃ divase pātimokkhaṃ uddisāpetabbaṃ. Idanti “tāhī”ti bahuvacanaṃ. Ekato saheva.

With these eight factors. 'Inspiring confidence' means by inspiring confidence, by faultless action of body, speech, and mind. 'Should fulfill' means one should fulfill the threefold training. But when those bhikkhunīs, having seen only the Pātimokkha reciter, request the admonition, then the Bhikkhu Saṅgha, assembled in the Uposatha hall, should ask as a preliminary duty: 'Are there any bhikkhunīs requesting the admonition?' Then, having had another say the words that should be said by oneself—'Speak thus'—one should oneself say, 'Is there any bhikkhu appointed as an admonisher of bhikkhunīs?' and so on, and then go oneself and announce it to the bhikkhunīs. Or on that day, another bhikkhu should be made to recite the Pātimokkha. 'This' refers to 'by those,' which is plural. 'Together' means at the same time.

Ñattiṭṭhapakena vāti yattha tiṇṇaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne pātimokkhuddeso natthi, tattha ñattiṭṭhapanakena vā. Itarena vāti yattha dve bhikkhū vasanti, eko vā, tattha itarena vā bhikkhunā sace sayameva sammato, “aha”nti vattabbaṃ[M 0.0159]. Tathevāti uposathagge vuttasadisameva. “Ārocetvāvā”ti iminā anārocanaṃ paṭikkhipati. “Na, bhikkhave, ovādo na ārocetabbo, yo na āroceyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 415) vacanato ovādaṃ gahetvā uposathagge anārocetuṃ na vaṭṭati.

'Or by one who places a motion': where there is no recitation of the Pātimokkha in a residence of three, there it is by one who places a motion. 'Or by another': where two bhikkhus reside, or one, there it is by another bhikkhu; if he himself is appointed, he should say, 'I am.' 'Just so' means just as was said in the Uposatha hall. By 'having announced,' it rejects not announcing. Because it is said, 'Bhikkhus, the admonition should not be unannounced. Whoever should not announce it, there is an offense of wrong-doing' (Cv.X.9.5), it is not proper, having received the admonition, not to announce it in the Uposatha hall.

Parisuddhabhāvanti āpattiyā parisuddhataṃ. Ārocethāti āvi karotha. Ettha siyāti “pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmī”ti etasmiṃ pade ayamanuyogo bhaveyya. Kiṃ taṃ, yaṃ siyāti āha “saṅgho uposathaṃ kareyyā”tiādi. Pubbenāparaṃ sandhiyatīti pubbavacanena aparaṃ vacanaṃ sandhānaṃ gacchati. Sāmaggiyāti kāyacittehi sahitatāya. Gaṇassāti uddesakaṃ ṭhapetvā catuvagge sesabhikkhūnaṃ. Saṅghassa uddiṭṭhaṃ hotīti saṅghena uddiṭṭhaṃ hoti. Karaṇatthe cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Etthāti pātimokkhuddese. Lakkhaṇanti sabhāvo.

'The state of being pure' means purity from an offense. 'You should declare' means you should make it manifest. 'Here there might be': in this phrase, 'I will recite the Pātimokkha,' this question might arise. What is it that might be? He says: 'The Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha,' etc. 'The latter is connected with the former' means the latter statement connects with the former statement. 'Harmony' means being together in body and mind. 'Of the group' means of the remaining bhikkhus in a group of four, setting aside the reciter. 'It is recited for the Saṅgha' means it is recited by the Saṅgha. And this is a genitive in the sense of the agent. 'Here' means in the recitation of the Pātimokkha. 'Characteristic' means intrinsic nature.

Therā [V 0.0151] ca navā ca majjhimā cāti ettha dasavassā, atirekadasavassā ca therā. Ūnapañcavassā navā. Pañcavassā, atirekapañcavassā ca majjhimā. Aṭṭhiṃ katvāti attānaṃ tena pātimokkhena atthikaṃ katvā, taṃ vā pātimokkhaṃ “idaṃ mayhaṃ pātimokkha”nti atthiṃ katvā. Manasi karitvāti citte ṭhapetvā. Sotadvāravasenāti sotadvārikajavanaviññāṇavasena. Sabbacetasā samannāharāmāti cittassa thokampi bahi gantuṃ adentā sabbena cittena āvajjema, sallakkhemāti attho. Manasi karomāti āvajjema, samannāharāmāti attho. So ca kho manasikāro na ettha ārammaṇappaṭipādanalakkhaṇo, atha kho vīthippaṭipādanajavanappaṭipādanamanasikārapubbakacitte ṭhapanalakkhaṇoti āha “ekaggacittā hutvā citte ṭhapeyyāmā”ti. Na sametīti na saṃgacchati. Kasmā na saṃgacchatīti āha “samaggassa hī”tiādi. Kiñca bhiyyoti āha “pātimokkhuddesako cā”tiādi. Saṅghapariyāpannoti saṅghe pariyāpanno antogadho.

'Elders, new bhikkhus, and those of middle standing': here, those of ten years' standing and more than ten years are elders. Those with less than five years are new bhikkhus. Those of five years' standing and more than five years are of middle standing. 'Making it a matter of concern' means making oneself concerned with that Pātimokkha, or making that Pātimokkha a matter of concern, thinking, 'This Pātimokkha is for me.' 'Attending' means placing it in the mind. 'By way of the ear-door' means by way of the ear-door javana-consciousness. 'Let us attend with our whole mind' means, not allowing the mind to go outside even a little, let us advert with the whole mind, let us mark it well—this is the meaning. 'We attend' means we advert; this is the meaning of 'we give heed.' And that attention is not here characterized by presenting an object, but rather it is characterized by placing in the mind preceded by the attention that leads to the cognitive process and leads to the javana process; thus he says: 'having become of unified mind, we should place it in the mind.' 'It does not come together' means it does not agree. Why does it not agree? He says: 'For of a united Saṅgha...,' etc. 'And what more?' He says: 'And the Pātimokkha reciter...,' etc. 'Included in the Saṅgha' means included, comprised within the Saṅgha.

Idāni taṃ dassetunti sambandho. Āyasmantoti sannipatitānaṃ piyavacanena ālapanaṃ.

'Now I will show that' is the connection. 'Venerable sirs' is an address with a term of endearment to those who have assembled.

Alajjitāti [M 0.0160] alajjitāya, alajjanabhāvenāti attho. Tatiyatthe hi idaṃ paccattavacanaṃ. “Aññāṇatā”tiādīsupi eseva nayo. Kukkuccappakatatāti kukkuccena abhibhūtatāya. Satisammosāti sativippavāsato. Vītikkamanti sikkhāpadavītikkamanaṃ.

'Through shamelessness' means by shamelessness; the meaning is through the state of being shameless. For this is a personal ending in the sense of the instrumental. This same method applies also to 'through ignorance,' etc. 'Through being beset by scruples' means through being overwhelmed by scruples. 'Through confusion of mindfulness' means from the absence of mindfulness. 'Transgression' means the transgression of a training rule.

Sañciccāti sañcetetvā, akappiyabhāvaṃ jānantoyeva vītikkamacittaṃ pesetvāti attho. Parigūhatīti nigūhati na deseti na vuṭṭhāti. Lajjāya parigūhanto alajjī na hoti, “kiṃ iminā”ti anādariyena parigūhanto alajjī hotīti dasseti. Agatigamanañca gacchatīti bhaṇḍabhājanīyaṭṭhānādīsu chandāgatiādibhedaṃ agatigamanañca gacchati. Alajjipuggaloti ajjhattikasamuṭṭhānalajjāvirahito puggalo. Ettha ca “sañciccā”ti iminā anādariyavaseneva āpattiṃ āpajjanto, āpannañca āpattiṃ parigūhanto, bhaṇḍabhājanīyaṭṭhānādīsu agatigamanaṃ gacchanto ca alajjī hoti, na itaroti dasseti.

'Sañcicca' means having deliberately intended, knowing it to be improper, and then sending forth a mind to transgress; that is the meaning. 'Parigūhati' means one conceals, does not declare, does not rise from it. One who conceals out of shame is not shameless; it is shown that one who conceals out of disregard, thinking, 'What of this?,' is shameless. 'And one goes on a wrong course' means one goes on a wrong course distinguished by biases such as desire to places for dealing in goods and utensils, etc. 'Alajjipuggalo' refers to a person devoid of the shame that arises internally. And here, by 'sañcicca,' it is shown that one who incurs an offense out of mere disregard, conceals the offense incurred, and goes on a wrong course to places such as those for dealing in goods and utensils, is shameless, and not others.

Mandoti mandapañño, apaññassevetaṃ nāmaṃ. Momūhoti atisaṃmūḷho. Virādhetīti na rādheti na sādheti. Kukkucceti vinayasaṃsaye. Kappiyaṃ ce kattabbaṃ siyāti vinayadharaṃ pucchitvā tena vatthuṃ oloketvā mātikaṃ, padabhājanaṃ, antarāpattiṃ, anāpattiñca oloketvā “kappati, āvuso, mā ettha kaṅkhī”ti vutte kattabbaṃ bhaveyya.

'Mando' means of dull wisdom; this is a name for one without wisdom. 'Momūho' means utterly deluded. 'Virādheti' means one fails, one does not accomplish. 'Kukkucceti' means one has scruples in a case of doubt about the Vinaya. 'Kappiyaṃ ce kattabbaṃ siyā' means: if something allowable is to be done, one should ask a Vinaya expert. After he has examined the case—having looked at the matrix, the word-by-word analysis, the intermediate offenses, and the non-offenses—and one is told, 'It is allowable, friend; have no doubt about this,' it should be done.

Sahaseyyacīvaravippavāsādīnīti [V 0.0152] ettha sahaseyyā nāma anupasampannena uttaridirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyāpatti, vippavāso nāma ekarattachārattavasena vippavāso. Ādisaddena sattāhātikkamādīsu āpattiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānanti pārājikasaṅghādisesathullaccayapācittiyapāṭidesanīyadukkaṭadubbhāsitasaṅkhātānaṃ sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ.

Regarding 'sahaseyyacīvaravippavāsādīni' (sleeping together, separation from robes, etc.): Here, 'sleeping together' (sahaseyyā) refers to the offense of sleeping in the same dwelling with an unordained person for more than two or three nights. 'Separation' (vippavāso) refers to separation from one's robes for one night or four nights. By the word 'etc.' (ādi), it includes offenses such as exceeding seven days. 'Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ' refers to the seven classes of offenses, namely: Pārājika, Saṅghādisesa, Thullaccaya, Pācittiya, Pāṭidesanīya, Dukkaṭa, and Dubbhāsita.

Desetu vā pakāsetu vāti saṅghamajjhe vā gaṇamajjhe vā ekapuggale vā desetu vā pakāsetu vā. Ettha ca pārājikāpattidesanā nāma bhikkhubhāvassa pariccāgo. Vuṭṭhānaṃ pana desanāvisesattā “desanā”ti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pakāsetu vāti ārocetu vā.

'Desetu vā pakāsetu vā' means one should declare or reveal it either in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, or to a single person. Here, the declaration of a Pārājika offense is the abandonment of the state of a bhikkhu. But rehabilitation (vuṭṭhāna), since it is a special kind of declaration, should be understood as a 'declaration' (desanā). 'Pakāsetu vā' means one should announce it.

Evaṃ anāpannā vāti evaṃ channaṃ ākārānaṃ aññatarena anāpannā vā. Vuṭṭhitā vāti parivāsādinā vuṭṭhitā vā. Ārocitā vāti āvikatā [M 0.0161] vā. Ārocento ca “tuyhaṃ santike ekaṃ āpattiṃ āvikaromī”ti vā “ācikkhāmī”ti vā “ārocemī”ti vā “mama ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpannabhāvaṃ jānāhī”ti vā vadatu, “ekaṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āvikaromī”ti vā ādinā nayena vadatu, sabbehipi ākārehi ārocitāva hoti. Sace pana garukāpattiṃ āvikaronto “lahukāpattiṃ āvikaromī”tiādinā nayena vadati, anāvikatā hoti āpatti. Vatthuṃ āroceti, āpattiṃ āroceti, ubhayaṃ āroceti, tividhenāpi ārocitāva hoti. Asantiyā āpattiyāti bhāvenabhāvalakkhaṇe bhummaṃ. Tuṇhībhāvenāpi hīti ettha na kevalaṃ “āma, mayaṃ parisuddhā”ti vutteyeva, atha kho tuṇhībhāvenāpīti apisaddassa attho veditabbo.

'Evaṃ anāpannā vā' means: or not having incurred it in any of these six ways. 'Vuṭṭhitā vā' means: or having risen from it through probation, etc. 'Ārocitā vā' means: or having been disclosed. When disclosing, whether one says: 'I disclose one offense in your presence,' or 'I inform,' or 'I announce,' or 'Know that I have incurred one offense,' or one says, by way of example, 'I disclose one grave offense,' it is disclosed in all these ways. But if, when disclosing a grave offense, one says, by way of example, 'I disclose a light offense,' the offense is not disclosed. One discloses the basis, one discloses the offense, one discloses both; in all three ways it is disclosed. The phrase 'asantiyā āpattiyā' (when an offense is non-existent) is a locative of condition. In the phrase 'tuṇhībhāvenāpi hi,' the meaning of the particle 'api' (even) should be understood thus: not only when it is said, 'Yes, we are pure,' but also through silence.

Kiṃ taṃ yāvatatiyānusāvitaṃ nāma, kathañcetaṃ yāvatatiyānusāvitaṃ hotīti vicāraṇāyaṃ ācariyānaṃ matibhedamukhena tamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “yāvatatiyaṃ anusāvitaṃ hotīti etthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yadetaṃ tikkhattuṃ anusāvitanti sambandho. Atthabyañjanabhedatoti arīyati ñāyatīti attho, abhidheyyaṃ, byañjīyati attho anenāti byañjanaṃ, akkharaṃ, attho ca byañjanañca atthabyañjanāni, tesaṃ bhedo atthabyañjanabhedo, tato, atthassa ca byañjanassa ca visadisattāti attho.

In the course of the investigation into the questions, 'What is this so-called “proclamation up to the third time”?' and 'How does this “proclamation up to the third time” come about?,' the passage beginning 'Here, “it is proclaimed up to the third time”' was stated in order to show the meaning by way of the different opinions of the teachers. In this context, the connection is that it is proclaimed three times. 'Atthabyañjanabhedato' means from the difference in meaning and phrasing. 'Attho' (meaning) is that which is reached or known; the denotation. 'Byañjanaṃ' (phrasing) is that by which the meaning is manifested; the letter. Meaning and phrasing are 'atthabyañjanāni.' Their difference is 'atthabyañjanabhedo.' From that, the meaning is: because of the dissimilarity of the meaning and the phrasing.

Idāni tamevatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “anusāvanañhi nāmā”tiādimāha. Hīti kāraṇatthe nipāto. Tassa pana “abhinna”nti iminā sambandho veditabbo. Tenāti bhinnattā. Assāti “yassa siyā”tiādivacanattayassa. Avassañcetamevaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ, aññathā atippasaṅgopi [V 0.0153] siyāti dassetuṃ “yadi ceta”ntiādimāha. Etanti “yassa siyā”tiādivacanattayaṃ. Apare “anusāvita”nti padaṃ na atītatthaṃ dīpeti, atha kho anāgatatthaṃ. Dhātvatthasambandho kālantaravihitopi paccayo kālantare sādhu hotīti vikappesuṃ. Tenāha “apare ‘anusāvita’nti padassā”tiādi. Upari uddesāvasāneti pārājikuddesāvasāne. Atthayuttīnaṃ abhāvatoti anāgatatthassa ca kāraṇassa ca abhāvato. Idāni tameva vibhāvetuṃ “idaṃ hī”tiādimāha. Kathametaṃ viññāyatīti āha “yadi cassā”tiādi. Ayanti [M 0.0162] anāgatakālo. Anusāvitaṃ hessatīti vadeyyāti anuppayogaṃ anāgatakālaṃ katvā “anusāvitaṃ hessatī”ti buddho vadeyya. Ayaṃ hetthādhippāyo – yadi cettha dhātvatthasambandho ta-paccayo siyā, tathā sati dhātvatthasambandho nāma visesanavisesyabhāvo, so ca anuppayogassa samānatthabhāve sati uppajjati, nāsatīti “hessatī”ti anuppayogaṃ vadeyya, na ca vuttaṃ. Tasmā anāgataṃ na dīpeti, atītakālameva dīpetīti. Anusāviyamāneti vacanatoti “anusāviyamāne”ti vattamānakālavacanato. Yadi evaṃ “yāvatatiyaṃ anusāvitaṃ hotī”ti kimidanti āha “yāvatatiya”ntiādi. Kiṃ tena lakkhīyati, yenetaṃ lakkhaṇavacanamattaṃ siyāti āha “tenā”tiādi. Tenāti lakkhaṇavacanamattena hetunā.

Now, to clarify this very meaning, he states the passage beginning: “For proclamation is the name….” The particle “hi” is in the sense of a reason. Its connection should be understood with the word “unbroken.” “Tenā” means because it is different. “Assā” refers to the three statements beginning “If there should be….” To show that this must be accepted in this way, for otherwise there would be an over-extension, he states the passage beginning: “And if this….” “Etaṃ” refers to the three statements beginning “If there should be….” Others speculated that the word “anusāvita” does not indicate a past meaning but a future one, thinking that a suffix related to a root-meaning, though prescribed for one tense, is valid in another. Therefore he says: “Others say of the word ‘anusāvitan’ti….” “Upari uddesāvasāne” means at the end of the Pārājika recitation. “Atthayuttīnaṃ abhāvatoti” means because of the absence of a future meaning and a reason for it. Now, to clarify this, he says: “For this….” How is this to be understood? He says: “And if for this….” “Ayaṃ” means this future time. “Anusāvitaṃ hessatīti vadeyyā” means that, making the application a future one, the Buddha would have said, “it will be proclaimed.” The intention here is this: if the ta-suffix here were connected to the root meaning, then, that being so, the connection to the root meaning is a qualifier-qualified relationship, and that arises when the application has the same meaning, not otherwise. Thus he would have used the application “hessati” (it will be), but he did not. Therefore, it does not indicate the future but only the past. “Anusāviyamāneti vacanatoti” means: from the word “anusāviyamāne,” which is in the present tense. If so, what is “yāvatatiyaṃ anusāvitaṃ hoti”? He says: “yāvatatiyan’ti….” What is indicated by that, such that this would be a mere descriptive statement? He says: “tenā’ti….” “Tenā” means: for that reason, which is that it is a mere descriptive statement.

Tadetanti pātimokkhaṃ. Taṃ panetanti “tatthāyasmante pucchāmī”tiādikaṃ yāvatatiyānusāvanaṃ. Na dissatīti nopalabbhati. Imameva ca atthanti imaṃ amhehi vuttamevatthaṃ. Yadi hi “yassa siyā āpattī”tiādivacanattayaṃ yāvatatiyānusāvanaṃ siyā, tadeva uposathakkhandhake (mahāva. 132 ādayo) vadeyya, na pana “sakimpi anusāvitaṃ hotī”tiādikanti adhippāyo. Nanu cāyaṃ vinicchayo aṭṭhakathāsu na āgato, atha kuto laddhoti āha “ayametthā”tiādi. Vinayaṭṭhānesu kataparicayānaṃ ācariyānaṃ taṃ taṃ atthaṃ ñāpentī paveṇi ācariyaparamparā, tāya ābhato ānīto ācariyaparamparābhato.

“Tadetan”ti: this is the Pātimokkha. “Taṃ panetan”ti: this is the proclamation up to the third time, beginning: “In this matter I ask the venerable ones….” “Na dissati” means it is not found. “Imameva ca atthan”ti: this very meaning stated by us. The intention is: for if the threefold statement beginning “If there is an offense for any…” were the proclamation up to the third time, he would have stated just that in the Uposathakkhandhaka, not the passage beginning “it is proclaimed even once….” One might object: “But this determination is not found in the commentaries, so from where was it obtained?” To this, he says: “ayametthā” etc. “Ācariyaparamparābhato” means brought, carried down by the tradition, the succession of teachers, which makes known each meaning to the teachers who are experienced in the sections of the Vinaya.

Nanu sampajānamusāvāde pācittiyena bhavitabbaṃ, atha kathaṃ dukkaṭāpatti hotīti āha “sā ca kho na musāvādalakkhaṇenā”tiādi. Sampajānamusāvāde kiṃ hotīti yvāyaṃ “sampajānamusāvādo assa hotī”ti vutto, so āpattito kiṃ hoti, katarā āpatti hotīti attho. Dukkaṭaṃ hotīti dukkaṭāpatti hoti. Vacīdvāre akiriyasamuṭṭhānāpatti hotīti assa hi bhikkhuno adhammikāya paṭiññāya tuṇhībhūtassa nisinnassa manodvāre āpatti nāma natthi. Yasmā pana āvikātabbaṃ nāvikāsi, tenassa vacīdvāre akiriyato ayaṃ [M 0.0163] āpatti samuṭṭhātīti [V 0.0154] veditabbā. Idāni vuttamevatthaṃ pāḷiyā sādhetuṃ “vuttampi ceta”ntiādimāha. Etaṃ upālittherena parivāre sedamocanagāthāsu (pari. 479) vuttampi cāti attho.

One might ask: “Should there not be a pācittiya offense for a deliberate lie? How, then, is it an offense of wrong-doing?” He says: “But that does not have the characteristic of a lie….” As to the question, “What happens in the case of a deliberate lie?,” regarding the statement, “there would be for him a deliberate lie,” the meaning is: what does this become in terms of an offense? What offense is it? It is an offense of wrong-doing; a dukkaṭa offense occurs. “An offense arises from inaction through the door of speech”: for this bhikkhu who sits in silence after an unlawful acknowledgment, there is no offense through the door of the mind. But because he did not reveal what should have been revealed, it should be understood that this offense arises for him from inaction through the door of speech. Now, to confirm this stated meaning with the Pāḷi, he says: “And this has been said….” The meaning is: and this was also said by the Elder Upāli in the Parivāra, in the “Sweat-Inducing Verses”.

Anālapanto manujena kenaci vācāti kenaci manujena vācāya anālapanto. Giraṃ no ca pare bhaṇeyyāti “iti ime sossantī”ti parapuggale sandhāya saddampi na nicchāreyya. Āpajjeyya vācasikanti vācato samuṭṭhitaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjeyya. Pañhāmesā kusalehi cintitāti ettha pañhāmesāti liṅgabyattayena vuttaṃ, eso pañho kusalehi cintitoti attho. Ayaṃ pañho imameva musāvādaṃ sandhāya vutto.

“Anālapanto manujena kenaci vācā” means not conversing by speech with any human being. “Giraṃ no ca pare bhaṇeyyā” means, with other persons in mind, thinking, “Thus they will hear,” one should not even emit a sound. “Āpajjeyya vācasikaṃ” means one would incur an offense arising from speech. “Pañhāmesā kusalehi cintitā”: here “pañhāmesā” (this question, fem.) is stated with a change of gender; the meaning is “eso pañho kusalehi cintito” (this question, masc., is considered by the skillful). This question was asked with reference to this very lie.

Taṃtaṃsampattiyā vibandhanavasena sattasantānassa antare vemajjhe eti āgacchatīti antarāyo, diṭṭhadhammikādianattho, atikkamanaṭṭhena tasmiṃ antarāye niyutto, antarāyaṃ vā phalaṃ arahati, antarāyassa vā karaṇasīloti antarāyiko. Tenāha “vippaṭisāravatthutāyā”tiādi. Tattha vippaṭisāravatthutāyāti vippaṭisāro nāma pacchānutāpavasena cittavippaṭisāro, tassa kāraṇatāyāti attho. Paṭhamajjhānādipaccayabhūtaaappaṭisāraviruddhassa vippaṭisārassa paccayattāti vuttaṃ hoti. Pāmojjādisambhavanti dubbalataruṇā pīti pāmojjaṃ, taṃ ādi yesaṃ te pāmojjādayo, tesaṃ sambhavo paṭilābho pāmojjādisambhavo, taṃ. Ādisaddena pītippassaddhādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Paṭhamajjhānādīnanti etthādisaddena pana “dutiyassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko, tatiyassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko, catutthassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko, jhānānaṃ, vimokkhānaṃ, samādhīnaṃ, samāpattīnaṃ, nekkhammānaṃ, nissaraṇānaṃ, pavivekānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhigamāya antarāyiko”ti (mahāva. 135) vuttadutiyajjhānādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. “Tasmā”ti vutte yaṃtaṃsaddānaṃ abyabhicāritasambandhatāya “yasmā”ti ayamattho upaṭṭhitoyeva hotīti āha “tasmāti yasmā”tiādi. Jānantenāti jānamānena. Imināssa sampajānamusāvādassa sacittakataṃ dasseti. Visuddhiṃ apekkhatīti visuddhāpekkho, tena [M 0.0164] visuddhāpekkhena. Sā ca visuddhi idha vuṭṭhānādīti āha “vuṭṭhātukāmena visujjhitukāmenā”ti. Vuṭṭhānagāminito saṅghādisesato vuṭṭhātukāmena, desanāgāminito visujjhitukāmenāti attho. Saṅghamajjhe vā gaṇamajjhe vā ekapuggale vāti uposathagge saṅghassa ārocanavasena saṅghamajjhe vā tattheva ubhato nisinnānaṃ ārocanavasena gaṇamajjhe vā anantarassa ārocanavasena ekapuggale vā pakāsetabbā. Ito vuṭṭhahitvāti ito uposathaggato vuṭṭhāya. Ettha pana sabhāgoyeva vattabbo. Visabhāgassa hi vuccamāne bhaṇḍanakalahasaṅghabhedādīnipi honti. Tasmā tassa avatvā “ito vuṭṭhahitvā [V 0.0155] paṭikarissāmī”ti ābhogaṃ katvā uposatho kātabboti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 170) vuttaṃ.

Because it obstructs the respective attainments, it comes or arrives in the middle of a being's continuity, it is an 'obstacle.' It is a disadvantage in this present life and so on. One who is engaged in that obstacle in the sense of transgression, or who deserves the fruit that is an obstacle, or who has the nature of causing an obstacle, is 'obstructive.' Hence it is said, 'because it is a basis for remorse,' etc. Herein, 'because it is a basis for remorse' means: remorse is mental affliction in the sense of subsequent regret; 'the state of being its cause' is the meaning. This means it is said because it is a condition for remorse, which is contrary to non-remorse, the latter being a condition for the first jhāna and so on. 'The arising of joy and so on': Weak and tender zest is joy. That which has this as its beginning are 'those beginning with joy.' Their arising or attainment is 'the arising of joy and so on.' By the word 'and so on,' zest, tranquility, etc., are included. 'Of the first jhāna and so on': Here, by the word 'and so on,' the inclusion of the second jhāna, etc., should be understood as stated: 'an obstacle to attaining the second jhāna, an obstacle to attaining the third jhāna, an obstacle to attaining the fourth jhāna, an obstacle to attaining jhānas, liberations, concentrations, attainments, renunciations, escapes, seclusions, and wholesome qualities.' 'Therefore': When this is said, because of the invariable connection of the pronouns 'that' and 'which,' the meaning 'because' is indeed established. Hence it is said, 'therefore means because,' etc. 'By one who knows' means by one who is aware. By this, it shows that this intentional false speech is done with conscious intent. 'One who seeks purification' is one who desires purity; by that seeker of purity. And that purity here is emergence, etc. Thus it is said: 'by one wishing to emerge, by one wishing to be purified.' The meaning is: wishing to emerge from a Saṅghādisesa offense, which leads to emergence; wishing to be purified from an offense that leads to confession. 'In the midst of the Saṅgha, or in the midst of a group, or to a single person': It should be disclosed in the midst of the Saṅgha by announcing it to the Saṅgha in the Uposatha hall; or in the midst of a group by announcing it to those sitting on both sides there; or to a single person by announcing it to the one next to him. 'Having arisen from this' means having arisen from this Uposatha hall. Here, however, it should be told only to one of a similar standing. For if it is told to one of a different standing, quarrels, disputes, schisms in the Saṅgha, and so on may arise. Therefore, without telling that person, having made the resolution, 'Having arisen from here, I will make amends,' the Uposatha should be performed—so it is said in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā.

Karaṇattheti tatiyāvibhattiatthe. Kattari hetaṃ paccattavacanaṃ hoti phāsusaddāpekkhāya. Paccattavacananti paṭhamāvacanaṃ. Paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ adhigamāya phāsu hotīti adhigamatthaṃ tassa bhikkhuno phāsu hoti sukhaṃ hoti saṃvarassa avippaṭisārahetuttā. Tenāha “avippaṭisāramūlakāna”ntiādi. Pāpapuññānaṃ katākatavasena cittavippaṭisārābhāvo avippaṭisāro, so mūlaṃ kāraṇaṃ yesaṃ te avippaṭisāramūlā, avippaṭisāramūlāyeva avippaṭisāramūlakā, tesaṃ avippaṭisāramūlakānaṃ. Sukhappaṭipadā sampajjatīti sukhā paṭipadā samijjhati, paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ sukhena adhigamo hotīti adhippāyo. Hoti cettha –

'In the instrumental sense' means in the sense of the instrumental case. For this is in the nominative case with reference to the agent, in dependence on the word 'ease.' 'Nominative case' means the first case. 'It is easy for the attainment of the first jhāna, etc.' means: for the sake of attainment, it is easy for that bhikkhu, it is pleasant, because restraint is a cause of non-remorse. Hence it is said, 'of those rooted in non-remorse,' etc. Non-remorse is the absence of mental remorse concerning evil and meritorious deeds done and not done. That is the root, the cause, of those things that have it as their root; those that have non-remorse as their root are 'rooted in non-remorse.' 'Of those rooted in non-remorse.' 'The pleasant practice is accomplished' means the pleasant path succeeds; the intention is that the attainment of the first jhāna and so on occurs with ease. And here there is this:

“Nidāne ñattiṭṭhapanaṃ, pubbakiccassa pucchanaṃ;

Nidānuddesasavane, visuddhārocane vidhi;

Anārocane cāpatti, ñeyyaṃ piṇḍatthapañcaka”nti.

In the introduction, the placing of the motion; the questioning about the preliminary duties; the recitation and hearing of the summary of the introduction; the procedure for announcing purity; and an offense in case of non-announcement—this fivefold summary of points should be known.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the commentary on the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the Elucidation of the Subtle Meaning,

Nidānavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the commentary on the Introduction is concluded.

Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

The Pārājika Section

Idāni [M 0.0165][V 0.0156] nidānuddesānantaraṃ vuttassa pārājikuddesassa atthaṃ saṃvaṇṇetuṃ “idānī”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Nidānānantaranti bhāvanapuṃsakaniddeso, nidānaṃ anantaraṃ katvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tatthāti pārājikakaṇḍe. Pātimokkheti bhikkhupātimokkhe. Cattāroti gaṇanaparicchedo ūnātirekabhāvanivattanato. Pārājikāti sajātināmaṃ. Āpattiyoti sabbasādhāraṇanāmaṃ. Uddisīyatīti uddeso. Bhāvappadhānoyaṃ niddeso. Tenāha “uddisitabbata”nti.

Now, to explain the meaning of the Pārājika section, which was stated after the recitation of the Introduction, the passage beginning 'Now...' is introduced. 'Immediately after the Introduction' is a reference to a neuter abstract noun; this means it is said as 'having placed the Introduction immediately before.' 'Therein' means in the Pārājika section. 'In the Pātimokkha' means in the Bhikkhus' Pātimokkha. 'Four' is a numerical determination to prevent there being more or less. 'Pārājikas' is a specific name. 'Offenses' is a general name. 'It is recited,' hence 'recitation.' This is a reference where the abstract sense is primary. Hence it is said, 'the state of being what is to be recited.'

1. Paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the First Pārājika

Yo panāti (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.45 bhikkhupadabhājanīyavaṇṇanā) ettha yasmā panāti nipātamattaṃ, yoti atthapadaṃ, tañca aniyamena puggalaṃ dīpeti. Tasmā tassa atthaṃ dassento “yo kocī”ti āha. Yasmā pana yo yokoci nāma, so avassaṃ liṅgayuttajātināmagottasīlavihāragocaravayesu ekenākārena paññāyati, tasmā taṃ tathā ñāpetuṃ “rassadīghādinā”tiādimāha. Ādisaddena navakammādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Liṅgādibhedenāti liṅgīyatiñāyati etenāti liṅgaṃ, taṃ ādi yesaṃ teti liṅgādayo, tesaṃ bhedo liṅgādibhedo, tena liṅgādibhedena. Etthādisaddena pana yuttādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – liṅgavasena yādiso vā tādiso vā hotu, dīgho vā rasso vā kāḷo vā odāto vā maṅguracchavi vā kiso vā thūlo vā. Yogavasena yena vā tena vā yutto hotu, navakammayutto vā uddesayutto vā vāsadhurayutto vā. Jātivasena yaṃjacco vā taṃjacco vā hotu, khattiyo vā brāhmaṇo vā vesso vā suddho vā. Nāmavasena yathānāmo vā tathānāmo vā hotu, buddharakkhito vā dhammarakkhito vā saṅgharakkhito vā. Gottavasena yathāgotto vā tathāgotto vā hotu, kaccāyano vā vāsiṭṭho vā kosiyo vā. Sīlesu yathāsīlo vā tathāsīlo vā hotu, navakammasīlo vā uddesasīlo vā vāsadhurasīlo vā. Vihāresupi yathāvihārī vā tathāvihārī vā [V 0.0157] hotu, navakammavihārī vā uddesavihārī vā vāsadhuravihārī vā[M 0.0166]. Gocaresupi yathāgocaro vā tathāgocaro vā hotu, navakammagocaro vā uddesagocaro vā vāsadhuragocaro vā. Vayesupi yo vā so vā hotu thero vā navo vā majjhimo vā, atha kho sabbova imasmiṃ atthe “yo”ti vuccatīti.

In the phrase “Yo panāti” (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1.45, Bhikkhupadabhājanīyavaṇṇanā), since “pana” is a mere particle, “yo” is the meaningful word, and it indicates a person indefinitely. Therefore, to show its meaning, he said “yo koci” (whoever). Moreover, since anyone called “yo koci” is necessarily known by one aspect among characteristic, endowment, caste, name, clan, virtue, dwelling, resort, or age, he said “rassadīghādinā” (by short, tall, etc.) to make that known. By the word “ādi” (etc.), new work and so on are included. “By the distinction of characteristic, etc.” (liṅgādibhedena): “characteristic” (liṅga) is that by which one is characterized or known. Those that begin with characteristic are “characteristics, etc.” (liṅgādayo). The distinction among them is the “distinction of characteristics, etc.” (liṅgādibhedo); by that distinction. Here, by the word “ādi,” endowment and so on are included. This is what is meant: by way of characteristic, whether one is tall or short, dark or fair, of golden hue, thin or stout. By way of endowment, whether one is endowed with this or that—endowed with new work, endowed with recitation, or endowed with the duty of residence. By way of caste, whether one is of this or that caste—a khattiya, a brahmin, a vessa, or a sudda. By way of name, whether one has this or that name—Buddharakkhita, Dhammarakkhita, or Saṅgharakkhita. By way of clan, whether one is of this or that clan—Kaccāyana, Vāsiṭṭha, or Kosiya. In terms of virtues, whether one has this or that virtue—the virtue of one engaged in new work, the virtue of one engaged in recitation, or the virtue of one undertaking the duty of residence. In terms of dwellings, too, whether one dwells in this or that way—dwelling while doing new work, dwelling while engaged in recitation, or dwelling while undertaking the duty of residence. In terms of resorts, too, whether one has this or that resort—the resort of new work, the resort of recitation, or the resort of the duty of residence. In terms of age, too, whether one is an elder, a new bhikkhu, or a middle-aged one—in every case, one is referred to as “yo” in this sense.

Idāni “bhikkhū”ti padaṃ saṃvaṇṇetuṃ “ehibhikkhūpasampadā”tiādimāha. Tattha “ehi bhikkhū”ti bhagavato vacanamattena bhikkhubhāvo ehibhikkhūpasampadā. “Buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”tiādinā (mahāva. 105) nayena tikkhattuṃ vācaṃ bhinditvā vuttehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi upasampadā saraṇagamanūpasampadā. Ovādappaṭiggahaṇūpasampadā (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.45) nāma –

Now, to explain the term “bhikkhu,” he begins with “ehibhikkhūpasampadā,” etc. Herein, the state of being a bhikkhu by the mere utterance of the Blessed One, “Come, bhikkhu,” is the ehibhikkhūpasampadā. The ordination by the three goings for refuge, by uttering three times, breaking the utterance, the phrase “I go to the Buddha for refuge,” etc., according to the method in the Mahāvagga (105), is the saraṇagamanūpasampadā. The ovādappaṭiggahaṇūpasampadā (ordination by acceptance of an exhortation) is as follows:

“Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ ‘tibbaṃ me hirottappaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ bhavissati theresu navesu majjhimesū’ti, evañhi te kassapa sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ ‘yaṃ kiñci dhammaṃ suṇissāmi kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi karitvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇissāmī’ti, evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ ‘sātasahagatā ca me kāyagatāsati na vijahissatī’ti, evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabba”nti (saṃ. ni. 2.154) –

“Therefore, Kassapa, you should train thus: ‘A keen sense of shame and fear of wrongdoing will be established in me toward the elders, the newly ordained, and those of middle standing.’ Thus, Kassapa, should you train. Therefore, Kassapa, you should train thus: ‘Whatever teaching I hear that is connected with the wholesome, I will take it to heart, pay attention to it, apply my whole mind to it, and listen to the Dhamma with an attentive ear.’ Thus, Kassapa, should you train. Therefore, Kassapa, you should train thus: ‘Mindfulness directed to the body accompanied by pleasure will not be abandoned by me.’ Thus, Kassapa, should you train.”

Iminā ovādappaṭiggahaṇena mahākassapattherassa anuññātaupasampadā.

By this acceptance of the exhortation, higher ordination was granted to the Elder Mahākassapa.

Pañhābyākaraṇūpasampadā nāma sopākassa anuññātaupasampadā. Bhagavā kira pubbārāme anucaṅkamantaṃ sopākasāmaṇeraṃ “‘uddhumātakasaññā’ti vā sopāka ‘rūpasaññā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā, udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.45) dasa asubhanissite pañhe pucchi. So te byākāsi. Bhagavā tassa sādhukāraṃ datvā “kativasso tvaṃ, sopākā”ti pucchi. Sattavassohaṃ bhagavāti. “Sopāka, tvaṃ mama sabbaññutaññāṇena saddhiṃ saṃsanditvā pañhe byākāsī”ti āraddhacitto upasampadaṃ anujāni, ayaṃ pañhābyākaraṇūpasampadā.

The ordination by answering questions is the ordination granted to Sopāka. It is said that the Blessed One, while walking to and fro in the Eastern Monastery, asked the novice Sopāka ten questions based on the foul perceptions: “‘The perception of a bloated corpse,’ Sopāka, or ‘the perception of form’—are these things different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning with only the phrasing being different?” Sopāka explained them. The Blessed One gave him his approval and asked, “How old are you, Sopāka?” “I am seven years old, Blessed One.” With a pleased mind, the Blessed One said, “Sopāka, you have explained the questions in conformity with my omniscient knowledge,” and he granted him higher ordination. This is the ordination by answering questions.

Aṭṭhagarudhammapaṭiggahaṇūpasampadā [V 0.0158] nāma mahāpajāpatiyā aṭṭhagarudhammappaṭiggahaṇena anuññātaupasampadā.

The ordination by acceptance of the eight weighty rules is the ordination granted to Mahāpajāpatī through her acceptance of the eight weighty rules.

Dūtenūpasampadā [M 0.0167] nāma aḍḍhakāsiyā gaṇikāya anuññātaupasampadā.

The ordination by messenger is the ordination granted to the courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī.

Aṭṭhavācikūpasampadā nāma bhikkhuniyā bhikkhunisaṅghato ñatticatutthena, bhikkhusaṅghato ñatticatutthenāti imehi dvīhi kammehi upasampadā.

The ordination by eight announcements is the ordination for a bhikkhunī, consisting of two formal acts: one from the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha with a motion and three announcements, and another from the Bhikkhu Saṅgha with a motion and three announcements.

Ñatticatutthakammūpasampadā nāma bhikkhūnaṃ etarahi upasampadā. Ñatticatutthenāti tīhi anussāvanāhi, ekāya ca ñattiyāti evaṃ ñatticatutthena. Kiñcāpi hi ñatti sabbapaṭhamaṃ vuccati, tissannaṃ pana anussāvanānaṃ atthabyañjanabhedābhāvato atthabyañjanabhinnaṃ ñattiṃ tāsaṃ catutthanti katvā “ñatticatuttha”nti vuccati. Akuppenāti akopetabbataṃ, appaṭikkositabbatañca upagatena. Ṭhānārahenāti kāraṇārahena satthu sāsanārahena. Upasampanno nāma uparibhāvaṃ samāpanno, pattoti attho. Bhikkhubhāvo hi uparibhāvo, tañcesa yathāvuttena kammena samāpannattā “upasampanno”ti vuccati. Kasmā panettha imināva upasampanno idha gahito, nāññehīti? Vuccate – ehibhikkhūpasampadā antimabhavikānameva, saraṇagamanūpasampadā parisuddhānaṃ, ovādappaṭiggahaṇapañhābyākaraṇūpasampadā mahākassapasopākānaṃ, na ca te bhabbā pārājikādilokavajjaṃ āpajjituṃ, aṭṭhagarudhammappaṭiggahaṇādayo ca bhikkhunīnaṃyeva anuññātā. Ayañca bhikkhu, tasmā ñatticatuttheneva upasampadākammena upasampanno idha gahito, nāññehīti veditabbo. Paṇṇattivajjesu pana sikkhāpadesu aññepi ehibhikkhūpasampadāya upasampannādayo saṅgayhanti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.45 bhikkhupadabhājanīyavaṇṇanā). Vakkhati hi “paṇṇattivajjesu pana aññepi saṅgahaṃ gacchantī”ti. Idāni “akuppena ṭhānārahena upasampanno”ti saṃkhittena vuttamatthaṃ vitthāretvā dassetuṃ “tassa panā”tiādimāha.

The ordination by a formal act with a motion as the fourth part is the present-day ordination for bhikkhus. “With a motion as the fourth part” means with three announcements and one motion. Although the motion is stated first, since the three announcements do not differ in meaning and phrasing, the motion, which does differ, is counted as their fourth part; hence it is called “a motion as the fourth part.” “Unshakeable” means having attained a state that cannot be overturned or rejected. “Worthy of the state” means worthy of the cause, worthy of the Teacher’s Dispensation. “Ordained” means having attained the higher state; “attained” is the meaning. For the state of a bhikkhu is the higher state, and since one has attained it by the aforesaid formal act, one is called “ordained.” But why is only one ordained in this way considered here, and not the others? It is said: The “Come, bhikkhu” ordination was only for those in their final existence; the ordination by going for refuge was for the purified ones; the ordination by accepting an exhortation and by answering questions was for Mahākassapa and Sopāka, and they were incapable of committing a Pārājika or other worldly offense. The acceptance of the eight weighty rules and so on were permitted only for bhikkhunīs. But this is a bhikkhu; therefore, it should be understood that only one ordained by the formal act with a motion as the fourth part is considered here, not the others. However, in the training rules concerning formulated offenses, others such as those ordained by the “Come, bhikkhu” ordination are also included (Sārattha. Ṭī. 2.45, Bhikkhupadabhājanīyavaṇṇanā). For it will be said: “But in the case of formulated offenses, others are also included.” Now, to explain in detail the meaning briefly stated as “ordained by an unshakeable act worthy of the state,” he begins with “tassa panā,” etc.

Tatthāti tesu pañcasu. Vasati etthāti vatthu, ādhāro patiṭṭhā. Tenāha “upasampadāpekkho puggalo”ti. Ūnāni aparipuṇṇāni vīsati vassāni assāti ūnavīsativasso. Ettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ upari sappāṇakavagge ūnavīsatisikkhāpade (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vaṇṇayissāma. Tesūti paṇḍakādīsu ekādasasu abhabbapuggalesu. Paṇḍako (mahāva. aṭṭha. 109) panettha pañcavidho hoti āsittapaṇḍako, usūyapaṇḍako[V 0.0159], opakkamikapaṇḍako, napuṃsakapaṇḍako, pakkhapaṇḍakoti. Tesu āsittapaṇḍakassa ca usūyapaṇḍakassa [M 0.0168] ca pabbajjā na vāritā, itaresaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vāritā. Tesupi pakkhapaṇḍakassa yasmiṃ pakkhe paṇḍako hoti, tasmiṃyevassa pakkhe pabbajjā vāritāti. Tayo cettha pabbajjūpasampadānaṃ abhabbatāya avatthū. Tenāha “āsittapaṇḍakañcā”tiādi. Tattha yassa paresaṃ aṅgajātaṃ mukhena gahetvā asucinā āsittassa pariḷāho vūpasammati, ayaṃ āsittapaṇḍako. Yassa paresaṃ ajjhācāraṃ passato usūyāya uppannāya pariḷāho vūpasammati, ayaṃ usūyapaṇḍako. Yassa upakkamena bījāni apanītāni, ayaṃ opakkamikapaṇḍako (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 135; vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.109). Yo pana paṭisandhiyaṃyeva abhāvako uppanno, ayaṃ napuṃsakapaṇḍako. Ekacco pana akusalavipākānubhāvena kāḷapakkhe paṇḍako hoti, juṇhapakkhe panassa pariḷāho vūpasammati, ayaṃ pakkhapaṇḍakoti veditabbo.

“Therein” means among those five. “Vatthu” (basis) is explained as “one dwells in this”; it is a support, a foundation. Therefore, he said the basis is “a person who is a candidate for higher ordination.” “One of less than twenty years” means one whose twenty years are incomplete. What needs to be said here will be explained below in the Sappāṇaka Vagga, in the commentary on the training rule concerning one of less than twenty years (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā). “Among them” refers to the eleven unsuitable individuals, beginning with the paṇḍaka. Here, the paṇḍaka (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 109) is of five kinds: the āsittapaṇḍaka, the usūyapaṇḍaka, the opakkamikapaṇḍaka, the napuṃsakapaṇḍaka, and the pakkhapaṇḍaka. Of these, the going forth is not forbidden for the āsittapaṇḍaka and the usūyapaṇḍaka, but it is forbidden for the other three. Furthermore, for the pakkhapaṇḍaka, the going forth is forbidden only during the fortnight when he is a paṇḍaka. Here, three are non-bases for the going forth and higher ordination due to their unsuitability. Hence it is said, “the āsittapaṇḍaka, and so on.” Here, the āsittapaṇḍaka is one whose burning subsides when, having taken another's sexual organ into his mouth, he is sprinkled with impurity. The usūyapaṇḍaka is one whose burning subsides from the arising of jealousy on seeing others’ transgression. The opakkamikapaṇḍaka is one whose testicles have been removed by a procedure (Vi. Saṅga. Aṭṭha. 135; Vi. Vi. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 2.109). The napuṃsakapaṇḍaka is one who is born impotent right from conception. Another, through the ripening of unwholesome kamma, is a paṇḍaka in the dark fortnight, but in the bright fortnight his burning subsides; this should be understood as the pakkhapaṇḍaka.

Theyyena saṃvāso etassāti theyyasaṃvāsako. So ca na saṃvāsamattasseva thenako idhādhippeto, atha kho liṅgassa, tadubhayassa ca thenakopīti āha “theyyasaṃvāsako pana tividho”tiādi. Na bhikkhuvassāni gaṇetīti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 110) “ahaṃ dasavasso vā vīsativasso vā”ti musā vatvā bhikkhuvassāni na gaṇeti. Na yathāvuḍḍhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vā sāmaṇerānaṃ vā vandanaṃ sādiyatīti attanā musāvādaṃ katvā dassitavassānurūpena yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vandanaṃ nādhivāseti. Na āsanena paṭibāhatīti “apehi, me etaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti āsanena nappaṭibāhati. Na uposathādīsu sandissatīti uposathappavāraṇādīsu na sandissati. Liṅgamattassevāti evasaddena saṃvāsaṃ nivatteti. Samānoti santo. Liṅgānurūpassa saṃvāsassāti sāmaṇeraliṅgānurūpassa sāmaṇerasaṃvāsassa. Sace pana kāsāye dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā naggo vā odātavatthanivattho vā methunasevanādīhi assamaṇo hutvā kāsāyāni nivāseti, liṅgatthenako hoti. Sace gihibhāvaṃ patthayamāno kāsāyaṃ ovaṭṭikaṃ katvā, aññena vā ākārena gihinivāsanena nivāseti “sobhati nu kho me gihiliṅgaṃ, na sobhatī”ti vīmaṃsanatthaṃ, rakkhati tāva, “sobhatī”ti sampaṭicchitvā puna liṅgaṃ sādiyati, liṅgatthenako hoti. Odātaṃ nivāsetvā vīmaṃsanasampaṭicchanesupi eseva nayo[M 0.0169]. Sacepi nivatthakāsāvassa upari odātaṃ nivāsetvā vīmaṃsati vā sampaṭicchati vā, rakkhati eva.

One whose communion is by theft is a `theyyasaṃvāsaka`. And here, what is meant is not a thief of communion only, but also a thief of the outward sign, or of both—thus it is said, “The `theyyasaṃvāsaka` is of three kinds,” and so on. “He does not count the years as a bhikkhu” (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 110) means that he falsely states his years as a bhikkhu, saying, “I am of ten years’ or ‘of twenty years’ standing.” “He does not accept veneration from bhikkhus or sāmaṇeras according to seniority” means that, having spoken falsely, he does not consent to the veneration appropriate to the seniority he has displayed. “He does not ward others off from a seat” means he does not push others away from a seat, saying, “Go away, this belongs to me.” “He does not appear at the Uposatha, etc.” means he does not show himself at the Uposatha, Pavāraṇā, and so on. “Of the sign only”—by this word, communion is excluded. `Samāno` means being (`santo`). “Of the communion appropriate to the sign” means of the communion of a sāmaṇera, which is appropriate to the sign of a sāmaṇera. But if someone, having laid down the burden of the saffron robe, having become a non-ascetic by going naked, wearing white clothes, engaging in sexual intercourse, etc., then wears the saffron robes, he is a thief of the sign. If, desiring the household life, having made his saffron robe into a roll, or wearing it in another way in the manner of a householder to see, “Does the household sign suit me or not?”, and while still keeping it, having decided “It suits me,” he again takes up the monastic sign, he becomes a thief of the sign. The same method applies in the cases of wearing white clothes for examination and acceptance. Even if he wears white clothes over his donned saffron robe while examining or accepting, he still keeps it.

Antimavatthuajjhāpannakepi eseva nayoti pārājikaṃ āpannake bhikkhumhipi eseva nayoti attho. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – sace koci bhikkhu kāsāye saussāhova odātaṃ nivāsetvā [V 0.0160] methunaṃ paṭisevitvā puna kāsāyāni nivāsetvā vassagaṇanādibhedaṃ sabbaṃ vidhiṃ āpajjati, ayaṃ bhikkhūhi dinnaliṅgassa apariccattattā na liṅgatthenako, liṅgānurūpassa saṃvāsassa sāditattā nāpi saṃvāsatthenakoti. Videsanti paradesaṃ. Idañca vañcetuṃ sakkuṇeyyaṭṭhānaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Yo pana sadesepi evaṃ karoti, sopi saṃvāsatthenakova. “Saṃvāsamattassevā”ti iminā liṅgaṃ paṭikkhipati. Sace koci vuḍḍhapabbajito (mahāva. aṭṭha. 110) bhikkhuvassāni gaṇetvā mahāpeḷādīsu diyyamānabhattaṃ gaṇhāti, sopi theyyasaṃvāsako hoti. Sayaṃ sāmaṇerova sāmaṇerappaṭipāṭiyā kūṭavassāni gaṇetvā gaṇhanto theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti. Bhikkhu pana bhikkhupaṭipāṭiyā kūṭavassāni gaṇetvā gaṇhanto bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbo.

The same principle applies also in the case of one who has committed a final offense; the meaning is that the same principle applies also to a bhikkhu who has committed a pārājika offense. This is what is said: If any bhikkhu, while still zealous for the saffron robe, puts on white clothes, engages in sexual intercourse, then again dons the saffron robes and follows all the procedures, such as counting the rains-residences, this one—because the sign given by the bhikkhus has not been relinquished—is not a thief of the sign; and because he partakes of the communion appropriate to the sign, he is also not a thief of communion. `Videsaṃ` means a foreign country. This is stated to show a place where one might be able to deceive. But one who does so even in his own country is also a thief of communion. By “of communion only,” the sign is excluded. If someone who has gone forth in old age (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 110), after falsely counting his years as a bhikkhu, accepts food given in large refectories and so on, he too is a `theyyasaṃvāsaka`. A sāmaṇera who himself, following the procedure for sāmaṇeras, accepts things after falsely counting his years is not a `theyyasaṃvāsaka`. But a bhikkhu who, following the procedure for bhikkhus, accepts things after falsely counting his years should be made to pay the value of the goods.

Nanu saṃvāso nāma ekakammaṃ ekuddeso samasikkhatāti āha “bhikkhuvassagaṇanādiko hī”tiādi. Iminā na kevalaṃ ekakammādikova kiriyabhedo saṃvāsoti idhādhippeto, atha kho tadañño bhikkhuvassagaṇanādikopīti dasseti. Imasmiṃ attheti theyyasaṃvāsakādhikāre. Sikkhaṃ paccakkhāyāti sikkhaṃ pariccajitvā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – sace koci bhikkhu sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya liṅgaṃ anapanetvā dussīlakammaṃ katvā vā akatvā vā “na maṃ koci jānātī”ti puna sabbaṃ pubbe vuttaṃ vassagaṇanādibhedaṃ vidhiṃ paṭipajjati, so theyyasaṃvāsako hotīti.

Is it not said that communion means having the same formal acts, the same recitation, and the same training? He says, 'such as the counting of a bhikkhu's years, etc.' By this, it is shown that not only is the distinction of actions, such as having the same formal acts, meant here as communion, but also other things, such as the counting of a bhikkhu's years, are included. This is in the matter of one who lives in communion by theft. 'Having renounced the training' means having abandoned the training. This is what is said: if any bhikkhu, having renounced the training and without removing the outward sign, whether having committed an immoral act or not, thinking, 'No one knows me,' again follows all the previously mentioned procedures, such as the counting of years, he is one who lives in communion by theft.
