'Having been requested' means having been requested three times thus: 'Having arranged the upper robe over one shoulder, having paid homage at the feet of the senior bhikkhus, having sat down in a squatting position, having raised the joined palms, he should speak thus: “Venerable sirs, I desire to build a hut by solicitation, without an owner, for my own use. I, venerable sirs, request the Saṅgha for the designation of a hut site.”' 'By an act with a motion as the second part' means—

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kattukāmo asāmikaṃ attuddesaṃ, so saṅghaṃ kuṭivatthudesanaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno kuṭivatthuṃ deseyya. Esā ñatti. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kattukāmo asāmikaṃ attuddesaṃ, so saṅghaṃ kuṭivatthudesanaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa bhikkhuno kuṭivatthuṃ deseti, yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno kuṭivatthussa desanā, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Desitaṃ saṅghena itthannāmassa bhikkhuno kuṭivatthu, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti –

“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me. This bhikkhu so-and-so, desiring to build a hut for himself by solicitation, one that is without an owner, asks the Saṅgha to designate a site for the hut. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha designate a site for the hut for bhikkhu so-and-so. This is the motion. Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me. This bhikkhu so-and-so, desiring to build a hut for himself by solicitation, one that is without an owner, asks the Saṅgha to designate a site for the hut. The Saṅgha designates a site for the hut for bhikkhu so-and-so. Let the venerable ones who approve of the designation of a site for the hut for bhikkhu so-and-so remain silent. Let anyone who does not approve speak. The site for the hut has been designated by the Saṅgha for bhikkhu so-and-so. The Saṅgha approves; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

Evaṃ [M 0.0240] padabhājane vuttena ñattidutiyena kammena. Āḷavikā nāma āḷaviraṭṭhe jātā dārakā, te pabbajitakālepi “āḷavikā”tveva paññāyiṃsu. Te sandhāya vuttaṃ āḷavike bhikkhū”ti. Lepe ghaṭiteti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.353) antolepe vā antolepena saddhiṃ bhittiñca chadanañca ekābaddhaṃ katvā ghaṭite, bahilepe vā bahilepena saddhiṃ ghaṭite. Dve ca dukkaṭāni sārambhaaparikkamanavasena. Ubhayavipannāti ubhayehi desanāpamāṇehi vipannā virahitā ubhayavipannā, adesitavatthukā pamāṇātikkantāti attho. Tasminti dvārabandhe vā vātapāne vā. Lepo na ghaṭiyatīti pubbe dinnalepo dvārabandhena vā vātapānena vā saddhiṃ na ghaṭiyati, ekābaddhaṃ hutvā na tiṭṭhatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tanti dvārabandhaṃ vā vātapānaṃ vā parāmasati. Paṭhamamevāti lepakiccassa niṭṭhitattā dvārabandhavātapānānaṃ ṭhapanato pubbeyeva, lepassa niṭṭhitakkhaṇeyevāti adhippāyo. “Bhikkhu kuṭiṃ karoti desitavatthukaṃ pamāṇikaṃ sārambhaṃ saparikkamanaṃ, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bhikkhu kuṭiṃ karoti desitavatthukaṃ pamāṇikaṃ anārambhaṃ aparikkamanaṃ, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pārā. 355) padabhājaniyaṃ vuttattā “kevalaṃ sārambhāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vippakatanti [V 0.0223] aniṭṭhitaṃ. Aññassa dadato cāti aññassa puggalassa vā saṅghassa vā dadato ca. Guhā nāma iṭṭhakaguhā vā silāguhā vā dāruguhā vā bhūmiguhā vā. Tiṇakuṭi nāma sattabhūmikopi pāsādo tiṇacchadano “tiṇakuṭikā”ti vuccati. Aññassāti ācariyassa vā upajjhāyassa vā saṅghassa vā. Vāsāgāraṃ ṭhapetvāti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.364) attano vasanatthāya vāsāgāraṃ ṭhapetvā. Uposathāgārādīsūti ettha ādisaddena jantāgharabhojanasālāaggisālānaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Heṭṭhimapamāṇasambhavoti catuhatthavitthiṇṇatā. Adesāpetvā karototi vatthuṃ adesāpetvā pamāṇātikkantaṃ, pamāṇayuttaṃ vā karoto. Ettha ca vatthuno adesāpanaṃ akiriyā. Kuṭikaraṇaṃ kiriyā.

By the act consisting of a motion and one announcement, as stated in the word-analysis. The 'Āḷavikas' were boys born in the country of Āḷavi; even when they went forth they were known as 'Āḷavikas.' It is with reference to them that 'the Āḷavika bhikkhus' is said. 'When the plaster is applied' means when it is applied on the inner plaster, or when the wall and the roof are made into one unit together with the inner plaster; or when it is applied on the outer plaster, or applied together with the outer plaster. And there are two offenses of wrong-doing on account of the undertaking and the site-preparation. 'Deficient in both' means deficient or lacking in both designation and measurement; the meaning is that the site was not designated and the size was exceeded. 'In that' means in the door frame or in the window. 'The plaster does not join' means the plaster previously applied does not join with the door frame or window; it is said that it does not become a single solid piece. 'That' means he touches the door frame or the window. 'At the very first' means before the installation of the door frame and window, since the work of plastering is finished; the intention is at the very moment the plastering is finished. Because it is stated in the word-analysis, 'A bhikkhu builds a hut on a designated site and of the proper size, with an undertaking and with site-preparation: this is an offense of wrong-doing. A bhikkhu builds a hut on a designated site and of the proper size, without an undertaking and without site-preparation: this is an offense of wrong-doing,' the phrase 'only for the undertaking,' etc., is said. 'Incomplete' means unfinished. 'And in giving to another' means in giving to another person or to the Saṅgha. A 'cave' means a brick cave, a stone cave, a wood cave, or an earth cave. A 'grass hut'—even a seven-storied mansion, if it has a grass roof, is called a 'grass hut.' 'To another' means to a teacher, a preceptor, or the Saṅgha. 'Having set aside a dwelling' means having set aside a dwelling for one's own residence. 'In an Uposatha hall, etc.'—here by the word 'etc.' a steam bath, a dining hall, and a fire hall are included. 'The possibility of the lower measurement' means a width of four cubits. 'He builds without having had it designated' means he builds it exceeding the measurement without having the site designated, or he builds it of the correct measurement. And here, not having the site designated is non-action, while the building of the hut is action.

Kuṭikārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning the hut-builder is concluded.

7. Vihārakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Building a Dwelling

Mahantaṃ [M 0.0241] lāti gaṇhātīti mahallako, taṃ mahallakaṃ. Yo ca yaṃ gaṇhāti, so tassa atthīti āha “mahantabhāvo etassa atthīti mahallako”ti. So ca mahantabhāvo kena, kuto cāti āha “sasāmikabhāvenā”tiādi. Na kevalaṃ sasāmikabhāvenevāti āha “yasmā vā”tiādi. Yadi evaṃ atha kasmā “mahallako nāma vihāro sasāmiko vuccatī”ti (pārā. 367) ettakameva padabhājane vuttanti āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Viharanti etthāti vihāro, āvāso. Mātikāyaṃ bhikkhū vā anabhineyyāti ettha vā-saddo “ayaṃ vā so mahānāgo”tiādīsu viya avadhāraṇattho.

Because it takes up (`lāti gaṇhāti`) what is large, it is a large one (`mahallaka`); that is, a large dwelling. And whatever one takes, that belongs to him, thus it is said: 'The state of being large belongs to it, thus it is a large one.' And that state of being large—by what, and from where? It is said: 'By the state of having an owner,' and so on. Not only by the state of having an owner, thus it is said: 'Or because,' and so on. If so, then why is only this much said in the word-analysis: 'A dwelling called "large" is said to have an owner'? It is said: 'But because,' and so on. 'They dwell in it,' thus it is a dwelling (`vihāra`), an abode. In the Mātikā, in the phrase 'monks or those who are not to be led away,' the word 'or' (`vā`) has the sense of emphasis, as in such phrases as 'this indeed is that great nāga.'

Kosambiyanti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.365) evaṃnāmake nagare. Tassa kira nagarassa ārāmapokkharaṇiādīsu tesu tesu ṭhānesu kosambarukkhāva ussannā ahesuṃ, tasmā taṃ “kosambī”ti saṅkhaṃ gacchati. “Kusumbassa nāma isino assamato avidūre māpitattā”ti eke. Channattheraṃ ārabbhāti yo abhinikkhamanakāle saddhiṃ nikkhanto, yassa ca satthārā parinibbānakāle brahmadaṇḍo (cūḷava. 445) āṇatto, taṃ channattheraṃ ārabbha. Cetiyarukkhanti cittīkataṭṭhena cetiyaṃ, pūjārahānaṃ devaṭṭhānānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ, “cetiya”nti sammataṃ rukkhaṃ cetiyarukkhaṃ. Vatthuno adesanāya āpajjanato “akiriyamattato samuṭṭhānabhāvo”ti vuttaṃ. Matta-saddena kiriyato samuṭṭhānataṃ paṭikkhipati. Keci pana “vatthuadesanāya, kuṭikaraṇena ca samuṭṭhānato kiriyākiriyato samuṭṭhātī”ti vadanti. Pamāṇaniyamābhāvova viseso.

At Kosambī means in the city so named. It is said that in the parks, ponds, and various other places of that city, kosamba trees were abundant; therefore it came to be known as 'Kosambī.' Some say it is 'because it was built not far from the hermitage of the seer named Kusumba.' Concerning the Elder Channa: this refers to the Elder Channa who went forth with the Bodhisatta at the time of the great renunciation, and on whom the Teacher imposed the higher penalty at the time of his final nibbāna. A shrine-tree: because it is an object of reverence, it is a shrine (`cetiya`); this is a designation for abodes of deities worthy of veneration. A tree considered a 'shrine' is a shrine-tree. Because one falls into an offense by not indicating the site, it is said that 'the arising is from non-action only.' The word 'only' (`matta`) excludes an arising from action. But some say: 'Because it arises from not indicating the site and from building the hut, it arises from both action and non-action.' The difference is just the absence of a rule about the size.

Vihārakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on Building a Dwelling is concluded.

8. Duṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Training Rule on Malicious Ill Will

Dūsīyatīti [V 0.0224] duṭṭho, dūseti paraṃ vināsetīti doso. Tenāha “dūsito cevā”tiādi. Idāni “dūsito ceva dūsako cā”ti iminā [M 0.0242] saṅkhepena vuttamevatthaṃ vitthāretvā dassetuṃ “uppanne hi dose”tiādimāha. Pakatibhāvaṃ jahāpitoti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.385-386) sommabhāvaṃ jahāpitoti attho, vikāramāpāditoti vuttaṃ hoti. Ākāranānāttenāti dūsitākārassa ceva dūsakākārassa cāti imesaṃ dvinnaṃ ākārānaṃ nānābhāvena. Nappatitoti pītisukhādīhi na abhigato anupagato, na upagatoti attho. Yo ca pītisukhādīhi anupagato, so tehi vajjito nāma hotīti āha “pītisukhādīhi vivajjito”ti. Yo ca tehi vajjito, na so tehi abhisaṭo nāma hotīti āha “na abhisaṭo”ti, pītisukhādīhi na patthaṭoti attho. Nāssa mūlanti amūlakaṃ. Taṃ pana amūlakattaṃ yasmā codakavasena adhippetaṃ, na cuditakavasena, tasmā tadatthaṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ codakenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yanti pārājikaṃ. Etanti cuditakassa āpannānāpannattaṃ. Idhāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade.

'He is corrupted,' thus he is malicious (`duṭṭha`); 'it corrupts, it destroys another,' thus it is ill will (`dosa`). Hence it is said: 'both corrupted,' etc. Now, to explain in detail the meaning stated concisely by 'both corrupted and a corrupter,' he says: 'when ill will has arisen,' etc. 'Made to abandon his natural state' means made to abandon his gentle state; that is to say, he is brought to a state of distortion. 'By the difference in mode' means by the different nature of the two modes: the mode of being corrupted and the mode of corrupting. 'Not attained' means not reached, not approached by rapture, happiness, and so on; the meaning is, not approached. Whoever is not approached by rapture, happiness, and so on, is indeed devoid of them; hence it is said: 'devoid of rapture, happiness, and so on.' And whoever is devoid of them is not pervaded by them; hence it is said: 'not pervaded,' meaning not suffused by rapture, happiness, and so on. 'It has no root' means groundless. But since that groundlessness is intended from the point of view of the accuser, not from the point of view of the accused, to show that meaning it is said: 'what by the accuser,' etc. Therein, 'what' means a pārājika offense. 'This' means whether the accused has fallen into the offense or not. 'Here' means in this training rule.

Idāni attanā vuttameva diṭṭhādiṃ vivarituṃ “ettha cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tathevāti “pasādasotena vā dibbasotena vā”ti imamatthaṃ atidisati. Parisaṅkitaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.385-386) pana tividhaṃ diṭṭhaparisaṅkitaṃ, sutaparisaṅkitaṃ, mutaparisaṅkitanti. Tattha bhikkhuñca mātugāmañca tathārūpe ṭhāne disvā “addhā imehi kata”nti vā “karissantī”ti vā parisaṅkitaṃ, idaṃ diṭṭhaparisaṅkitaṃ nāma. Andhakāre vā paṭicchannokāse vā bhikkhussa ca mātugāmassa ca vacanaṃ sutvā dutiyassa atthibhāvaṃ ajānato pubbe vuttanayena parisaṅkitaṃ, idaṃ sutaparisaṅkitaṃ nāma. Dhuttehi itthīhi saddhiṃ paccantavihāre maṇḍape vā sālādīsu vā pupphagandhamaṃsasurādīni anubhavitvā gataṭṭhānaṃ disvā “kena nu kho idaṃ kata”nti vīmaṃsantena tatra kenaci bhikkhunā gandhādīhi pūjā katā hoti, bhesajjatthāya ariṭṭhaṃ vā pītaṃ, so tassa gandhaṃ ghāyitvā “ayaṃ so bhavissatī”ti parisaṅkitaṃ, idaṃ mutaparisaṅkitaṃ nāma. Evaṃ tividhassa parisaṅkitassa abhāvo aparisaṅkitaṃ. Tenāha “diṭṭhasutamutavasena cetasā aparisaṅkita”nti. Tañca panetaṃ diṭṭhādikaṃ na kevalaṃ attano vāti āha “attano vā parassa vā”ti. Yasmā “tvaṃ paṇḍako”tiādivacanenāpi codayato āpattiyeva, tasmā “bhikkhuno anurūpesu ekūnavīsatiyā aññatarenā”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ atha kasmā padabhājane [M 0.0243] “pārājikena dhammenāti catunnaṃ aññatarenā”ti (pārā. 386) vuttanti āha “padabhājane [V 0.0225] panā”tiādi. Upasagganipātānaṃ vācakasaddasanniṭṭhāne tadatthajotanabhāvena pavattanato “dhaṃseyyā”ti vuttaṃ. Dhaṃsanañcettha abhibhavanaṃ. Tenāha “abhibhaveyyā”ti. “Tvaṃ methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevī”tiādinā nayena pavattāti “tvaṃ methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevi, adinnaṃ ādiyi, manussaṃ ghātayittha, abhūtaṃ ārocayitthā”ti evaṃ pavattā. Ettha ca “assamaṇosī’ti avandanakāraṇassa avuttattā antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpanno na vanditabbo”ti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ avandiyesu antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannassa avuttattā, “pacchā upasampannena pure upasampanno vandiyo”ti (pari. 468) vuttattā ca. Idaṃ pana attanā vattabbaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ.

Now, to explain what was said by oneself regarding what is seen, etc., the phrase 'and here,' etc., is stated. Similarly, it extends the meaning to 'with the physical ear-element or the divine ear-element.' But suspicion (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.385–386) is threefold: suspicion based on what is seen, suspicion based on what is heard, and suspicion based on what is inferred. Here, having seen a monk and a woman in such a place and suspecting, 'Surely, it has been done by them,' or 'They will do it'—this is called suspicion based on what is seen. Having heard the voices of a monk and a woman in the dark or in a concealed place, without knowing of the presence of a second person, and suspecting in the way stated above—this is called suspicion based on what is heard. Having seen a place in a remote dwelling, in a pavilion, or in a hall, etc., where dissolute women have gone after enjoying flowers, perfumes, meat, liquor, etc., and while investigating, 'By whom could this have been done?', one smells a scent from some monk who has made an offering with perfumes, etc., or has drunk a fermented medicinal drink, and suspects, 'This must be him'—this is called suspicion based on what is inferred. The absence of these three kinds of suspicion is 'unsuspected.' Hence it is said: 'unsuspected by mind by way of what is seen, heard, or inferred.' And this seeing, etc., is not only one's own; thus it is said: 'of oneself or of another.' Since one incurs an offense even by accusing with words such as 'You are a eunuch!', it is therefore said: 'by one of the nineteen things unbecoming of a monk.' If so, then why is it said in the word-analysis: 'by a Pārājika offense means by one of the four' (Pārā. 386)? It is said: 'But in the word-analysis,' etc. Because prefixes and particles function to illuminate the meaning when they are near a verb, it is said 'one might denounce' (`dhaṃseyyā`). And denunciation here is overpowering. Hence it says: 'one might overpower.' It proceeds in the manner of: 'You have engaged in sexual intercourse,' etc., meaning it proceeds thus: 'You have engaged in sexual intercourse; you have taken what was not given; you have killed a human being; you have claimed what is not a fact.' Here, some say: 'Since, in the case of the statement "You are not a recluse," the reason for not venerating is not stated, one who has committed a terminal offense is not to be venerated.' But this should not be accepted, because one who has committed a terminal offense is not mentioned among those who are not to be venerated, and because it is said: 'One ordained later should venerate one ordained earlier' (Parivāra 468). This, however, is said to show what one should say oneself.

Samīpeti dvādasahatthapamāṇe padese. Sikkhāpaccakkhānameva hi hatthamuddāya sīsaṃ na eti, idaṃ pana anuddhaṃsanaṃ, abhūtarocanañca etiyeva. Tenāha “hatthamuddāya eva vā”ti. Brahmacariyāti brahmaṃ seṭṭhaṃ pasatthaṃ cariyanti brahmacariyaṃ, brahmūnaṃ vā seṭṭhānaṃ buddhapaccekabuddhaariyasāvakānaṃ, brahmānañca cariyanti brahmacariyaṃ, tamhā brahmacariyā. Tenāha “seṭṭhacariyā”ti. Sādhu vatassa ekantena bhaddakaṃ bhaveyya. “Tajjanīyakammādisattavidhampi kammaṃ karissāmā”ti āpattiyā codentassa adhippāyo kammādhippāyo. “Āpattito vuṭṭhāpessāmā”ti adhippāyo vuṭṭhānādhippāyo. Anuvijjanādhippāyoti vīmaṃsanādhippāyo, upaparikkhādhippāyo. Anuvijjakenāti saṅghamajjhe otiṇṇaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchinituṃ nisinnena vinayadharena. Kiṃ te diṭṭhanti tayā kiṃ diṭṭhaṃ, paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, dutiyaṃ tatiyaṃ catutthaṃ pārājikaṃ āpajjanto diṭṭhoti vuttaṃ hoti. Ādisaddena “kinti te diṭṭhaṃ, kadā te diṭṭhaṃ, kattha te diṭṭha”nti imaṃ nayaṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

'Nearby' means in a place within the measure of twelve cubits. For it is only the giving up of the training that does not culminate through a hand gesture, but this denunciation and false accusation do culminate. Hence it is said, 'or just by a hand gesture.' The holy life (`brahmacariya`): it is a holy, supreme, and praised practice, thus it is the holy life; or it is the practice of the holy ones, the supreme ones—the Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and noble disciples—and the practice pertaining to what is best, thus it is the holy life. Hence it is said: 'the supreme practice.' 'Well now, may it be entirely good for him.' The intention of one who accuses him of an offense, thinking, 'We will carry out a formal act, one of the seven such as the act of censure,' is the intention for a formal act. The intention, 'We will have him rehabilitated from the offense,' is the intention for rehabilitation. The intention for investigation is the intention for inquiry, the intention for scrutiny. 'By an investigator' means by a Vinaya expert who is seated in the midst of the Sangha to decide on a legal issue that has come up. 'What did you see?' means it is said: 'What did you see? Did you see him committing the first pārājika offense? Did you see him committing the second, third, or fourth pārājika offense?' By the word 'etc.' it includes this line of questioning: 'How did you see it? When did you see it? Where did you see it?'

Samanatthāya pavattamānehi samathehi adhikātabbanti adhikaraṇaṃ. Yathā hi samanavasena samathānaṃ vivādādīsu adhikatabhāvo, evaṃ vivādādīnaṃ tehi adhikattabbatāti. Tenāha “samathehi adhikaraṇīyabhāvenā”tiādi. Iminā hi adhikaraṇasaddassa kammasādhanatā vuttā. Adhikaraṇanti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kiccādhikaraṇanti catubbidhaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ. Vivādādīni adhikaraṇāni samenti vūpasamentīti [M 0.0244] samathā, sammukhāvinayādayo. Atha vā adhikarīyanti etthāti adhikaraṇaṃ. Ke adhikarīyanti? Samathā. Kathaṃ adhikarīyanti? Samanavasena. Adhikaraṇaṃ samenti vūpasamentītipi samathāti evampettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ ṭhapetvā sesādhikaraṇehi codanāya abhāvato “idaṃ pana pārājikasaṅkhātaṃ [V 0.0226] āpattādhikaraṇameva adhippeta”nti vuttaṃ. Āpattiyeva adhikaraṇaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuddhaṃsitakkhaṇeyeva saṅghādiseso, so ce taṅkhaṇeyeva jānātīti adhippāyo.

An issue is what is to be dealt with by settlements that proceed for the sake of pacification. For just as settlements have a dealing-with role in regard to disputes and so on by way of pacification, so too disputes and so on are to be dealt with by them. Hence it is said: 'by settlements, because they are to be dealt with,' and so on. By this, the derivation of the word `adhikaraṇa` in the passive sense is stated. An issue: there are four kinds of issues: an issue of dispute, an issue of accusation, an issue of an offense, and an issue of a duty. Settlements are so called because they settle, they pacify, issues of dispute and so on; they are resolution face-to-face and so on. Alternatively, an issue is that wherein settlements are applied. What are applied? Settlements. How are they applied? By way of pacification. The meaning here should be understood thus: settlements are so called because they settle, they pacify, the issue. Since there is no accusation in the other issues apart from the issue of an offense, it is said: 'But here, only the issue of an offense, designated as a pārājika, is intended.' An offense itself is an issue of an offense. A saṅghādisesa offense occurs at the very moment of denunciation; if he knows it at that very moment—this is the intention.

Mettiyabhūmajaketi mettiyañca bhūmajakañca. Chabbaggiyānaṃ aggapurisā ete. Suddhaṃ vāti pārājikamanāpannaṃ vā. “Sace so taṅkhaṇeyeva jānātī”ti iminā āvajjanasamayamāha. Taṅkhaṇeyeva jānanaṃ nāma dukkaraṃ, samayena āvajjitvā ñāte pana ñātameva hoti. Pacchā ce jānāti, sīsaṃ na eti. Sikkhāpaccakkhānaabhūtārocanaduṭṭhullavācāattakāmaduṭṭhadosabhūtārocanasikkhāpadānīti sabbāneva hi imāni ekaparicchedāni. Yasmā pana parammukhā sattahipi āpattikkhandhehi vadato dukkaṭameva, tasmā “parammukhā codentassa pana sīsaṃ na etī”ti vuttaṃ. Vuttanayāpattiyoti “vācāya vācāyā”tiādinā vuttanayā saṅghādisesadukkaṭāpattiyo. Tathevāti vācāya vācāyeva. Vadantassāti sattahipi āpattikkhandhehi upasampannaṃ sammukhā vadantassa. Vuttanayenevāti vācāya vācāyeva. Okāsaṃ kāretvā upasampannaṃ sammukhā vadantassa vācāya vācāya pācittiyanti āha “okāsaṃ kāretvā vadantassa pācittiyamevā”ti. Evasaddena dukkaṭaṃ nivattīyati. Asammukhā sattahipi āpattikkhandhehi vadantassa dukkaṭaṃ. Sattavidhampi kammanti tajjanīyaṃ, niyasaṃ, pabbājanīyaṃ, paṭisāraṇīyaṃ, tividhañca ukkhepanīyanti sattavidhampi kammaṃ.

Mettiya and Bhūmajaka: Mettiya and Bhūmajaka. These were the chief persons among the group-of-six monks. 'Or pure' means or not having committed a pārājika offense. By 'If he knows at that very moment,' he states the time of adverting. Knowing at that very moment is indeed difficult, but when it is known after adverting in due course, it is indeed known. If he knows afterwards, it does not reach culmination. The training rules on renouncing the training, on a false charge, on coarse speech, on self-desire, and on a false charge out of malice—all these indeed belong to a single section. But since for one speaking in the absence of the other concerning any of the seven classes of offenses there is only an offense of wrong-doing, it is therefore said: 'But for one accusing in the absence of the other, it does not reach culmination.' 'The offenses in the stated manner' means the saṅghādisesa and dukkaṭa offenses in the manner stated beginning with 'for every word.' 'Just so' means for every word. 'For one speaking' means for one speaking face-to-face to an ordained person about any of the seven classes of offenses. 'In the stated manner' means for every word. He says, 'For one who, having asked for leave, speaks face-to-face to an ordained person, there is a pācittiya for every word,' as in the phrase 'for one who speaks having asked for leave, there is only a pācittiya.' By the word 'only,' an offense of wrong-doing is precluded. For one speaking not face-to-face about any of the seven classes of offenses, there is an offense of wrong-doing. The seven kinds of formal act are: the act of censure, the act of subordination, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, and the three kinds of act of suspension—these are the seven kinds of formal act.

Uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapentassa ca okāsakammaṃ natthīti ettha uposathato pure vā pacchā vā ṭhapitopi aṭṭhapito hoti. Khette ṭhapito pana ṭhapito hoti, tasmā “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ajjuposatho pannaraso, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho uposathaṃ kareyyā”ti ettha yāva re-kāraṃ bhaṇati, tāva ṭhapetabbo, idaṃ khettaṃ. Yya-kāre pana vutte ṭhapentena pacchā ṭhapito nāma hoti[M 0.0245]. “Suṇātu me”ti anāraddhe ṭhapentena pure ṭhapito hoti. Pavāraṇāṭṭhapanaṃ pana sabbasaṅgāhikaṃ, puggalikañcāti duvidhaṃ. Tattha sabbasaṅgāhike “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti su-kārato yāva re-kāro, tāva apariyositāva hoti pavāraṇā, etthantare ekapadepi ṭhapentena ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā. Yya-kāre pana patte pariyositāva hoti, tasmā tato paṭṭhāya ṭhapentena aṭṭhapitā hoti. Puggalikaṭṭhapane pana “saṅghaṃ, bhante, pavāremi…pe… tatiyampi bhante saṅghaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā…pe… passanto paṭī”ti (mahāva. 210) saṃ-kārato yāva ayaṃ sabbapacchimo ṭi-kāro, tāva apariyositāva hoti pavāraṇā, etthantare ekapadepi ṭhapentena ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā. “Karissāmī”ti vutte pana pariyositā hoti, tasmā “karissāmī”ti etasmiṃ pade sampatte ṭhapitāpi [V 0.0227] aṭṭhapitā hoti. Eseva nayo dvevācikaekavācikasamānavassikāsu. Etāsupi hi ṭi-kārāvasānaṃyeva ṭhapanakkhettanti. Tenāha “ṭhapanakkhettaṃ pana jānitabba”nti. Osaṭe vatthusminti codakena attanā vattabbe saṅghamajjhe udāhaṭe. Idañca idañca karotīti pāṇātipātaṃ, adinnādānañca karoti, jātarūparajatañca paṭiggaṇhāti. Asuko ca asuko ca assamaṇo, anupāsakoti akkosādhippāyena parammukhā vadantassa dukkaṭaṃ, sammukhā vadantassa pana pācittiyameva. Tenāha “sace pana odissa niyametvā”tiādi. Saṅkhyupagamananti vohārūpagamanaṃ.

For one suspending the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā, there is no act of asking for leave. Here, one who has suspended it either before or after the Uposatha has not suspended it. But one who has suspended it within the proper interval has suspended it. Therefore, in the phrase, 'Venerable sirs, let the Sangha hear me. Today is the Uposatha of the fifteenth. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, let the Sangha perform the Uposatha,' as long as one is reciting up to the syllable 're,' it can be suspended; this is the proper interval. But when the syllable 'yya' has been said, one suspending it has suspended it afterwards. One suspending it before 'Let the Sangha hear me' has been started has suspended it beforehand. The suspension of the Pavāraṇā, however, is twofold: general for the Sangha and individual. In the general suspension, in the phrase, 'Venerable sirs, let the Sangha hear me… let the Sangha invite for the third time,' from the syllable 'su' up to the syllable 're,' the Pavāraṇā is not yet concluded. In this interval, one suspending it even with a single word has suspended the Pavāraṇā. But when the syllable 'yya' has been reached, it is concluded; therefore, from then on, one suspending it has not suspended it. In the case of individual suspension, in the phrase, 'Venerable sirs, I invite the Sangha… For the third time, venerable sirs, I invite the Sangha, by what has been seen… seeing it, I will make amends,' from the syllable 'saṃ' up to this very last syllable 'ṭi,' the Pavāraṇā is not yet concluded. In this interval, one suspending it even with a single word has suspended the Pavāraṇā. But when 'I will do so' is said, it is concluded; therefore, when this phrase has been reached, even if suspended, it is not suspended. This is the same method for the invitations spoken twice, spoken once, and by those of the same seniority. For in these too, the proper interval for suspension ends only with the syllable 'ṭi.' Hence it is said: 'But the proper interval for suspension should be known.' 'When the matter has been brought up' means when what should be said by the accuser himself has been declared in the midst of the Sangha. Saying, 'He does this and this,' means: he commits the destruction of life and taking what is not given, and he accepts gold and silver. For one who says in the absence of the other with intent to revile, 'So-and-so is not a recluse, not a lay follower,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; but for one who says it face-to-face, there is only a pācittiya. Hence it is said: 'But if, having specified and determined...,' etc. 'Coming to be reckoned' means coming to be a matter of convention.

Duṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning malice is concluded.

9. Aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Another Part

Aññabhāgassāti aññakoṭṭhāsassa, yaṃ codetukāmo, tassa jātiādito aññassa tiracchānajātiādikoṭṭhāsassāti vuttaṃ hoti. Idanti napuṃsakaniddesena chagalakādiṃ niddisati, ayaṃ chagalakādikoti attho, adhikaraṇasaddāpekkhāya vā napuṃsakaniddeso, idaṃ chagalakādisaṅkhātaṃ adhikaraṇanti vuttaṃ hoti. Aññabhāgo vāti tiracchānajātiādibhedo añño koṭṭhāso vā. Assāti chagalakādikassa[M 0.0246]. Aññabhāgiyaṃ chagalakādi. Ettha ca “aññabhāgasambandhi aññabhāgiya”nti paṭhamaviggahassa attho, “aññabhāgavantaṃ aññabhāgiya”nti dutiyaviggahassa. Ṭhapetvā pana tiracchānajātiādikaṃ paramatthato visuṃ chagalakādike asatipi “paṭimāya sarīra”ntiādīsu viya abhedepi bhedakappanāya pavattalokavohāravasena “aññabhāgassa idaṃ, aññabhāgo vā assa atthī”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Adhikarīyati etthāti adhikaraṇaṃ. Tenāha “ādhāro veditabbo”ti. Ādharīyati asminti ādhāro, patiṭṭhānaṃ. Tenāha “vatthu adhiṭṭhānanti vuttaṃ hotī”ti.

'Of another part' means of a different portion. It is said to be of a portion, such as the portion of animal birth and so on, different from the birth and so on of him whom one wishes to accuse. 'This' (idaṃ), indicated by the neuter gender, refers to things like a goat, etc. The meaning is 'this is a goat, etc.' Alternatively, with reference to the word 'matter' (adhikaraṇa), the neuter gender is used, meaning 'this, designated as a goat, etc., is the matter.' 'Or another part' refers to a different portion, such as a division into animal birth, etc. 'Of it' (assa) refers to the goat, etc. 'Belonging to another part' refers to the goat, etc. Here, the meaning of the first analysis is 'connected to another part is that which belongs to another part,' while the meaning of the second analysis is 'possessing another part is that which belongs to another part.' However, even though, in ultimate truth, a goat or the like is not separate from animal birth, etc., just as in phrases like 'the body of a statue,' where there is no ultimate distinction, a distinction is made based on worldly convention. Thus, it is said, 'this belongs to another part,' or 'it has another part.' 'Matter' (adhikaraṇa) is that upon which something is based. Hence, it is said, 'it should be understood as a basis.' 'Basis' (ādhāra) is that upon which something is supported—a foundation. Therefore, it is said, 'the ground or support is meant.'

Idāni “aññabhāgassa ida”ntiādinā saṅkhepena vuttamevatthaṃ kevalaṃ nayadassanatthaṃ aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ āgatameva gahetvā vibhajanto “yo hi so”tiādimāha. Tena nanu anāgate evaṃ codentānaṃ pāpabhikkhūnaṃ lesokāsapidahanatthaṃ idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, na pana mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ. Tesañhi ādikammikattā anāpatti, tasmā sāmaññena attho vibhajitabbo. Na pana “yo hi so aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ dabbo mallaputto”tiādinā visesenāti edisī codanā anavakāsāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Hīti kāraṇatthe nipāto, yasmāti vuttaṃ hoti. Aṭṭhuppattiyanti [V 0.0228] atthassa uppatti atthuppatti, atthuppattiyeva aṭṭhuppatti, tassaṃ aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ, sikkhāpadassa nidāneti vuttaṃ hoti. Chagalakoti setachagalako. Soti chagalako. Imassa pana “hotī”ti iminā sambandho. Aññassa…pe… chagalakabhāvassa cāti “tiracchānajātiyā ceva chagalakabhāvassa cā”ti saṅkhātassa aññassa bhāgassa koṭṭhāsassa, pakkhassāti attho.

Now, in order to simply show the method, he analyzes the meaning already stated briefly in 'this is of another part,' etc., by taking up what has come in the origin story itself, saying, 'For he who...' and so on. By this, it should be understood that an objection of this sort is baseless: 'Surely, this training rule was laid down to prevent any opportunity for wicked monks who might make such accusations in the future, not for the Mettiyā and Bhūmajaka monks. For them, as they were the first offenders, there is no offense. Therefore, the meaning should be analyzed generally, and not specifically with 'for he who is Dabba the Mallian son in the origin story.'' The particle 'hi' is in the sense of a reason; it means 'because.' 'Origin story' means the arising of the matter—the arising of the matter itself is the origin story. In that origin story, it is said to be the basis of the training rule. 'Goat' (chagalako) means a white goat. 'He' (so) refers to the goat. The connection of this word is with 'is' (hoti). 'Of another... and of the state of a goat' refers to another portion, namely, 'both of animal birth and of the state of a goat,' which is designated as a part or a side; that is the meaning.

Kutoyamañño, yato “aññassa bhāgassā”ti vuttanti āha “yvāyaṃ…pe… tato”ti. Tattha manussajāti ceva bhikkhubhāvo cāti yo ayaṃ bhāgo koṭṭhāso pakkhoti sambandho, “manussajāti ceva bhikkhubhāvo cā”ti saṅkhāto yo ayaṃ bhāgo koṭṭhāso pakkhoti attho. Tatoti “manussajāti ceva bhikkhubhāvo cā”ti bhāgato. So vā aññabhāgoti yathāvuttatiracchānajātichagalakabhāvasaṅkhāto so aññabhāgo vā. Assāti chagalakassa. Atthīti upalabbhati. Tasmāti yasmā aññabhāgassa chagalako hoti, yasmā ca so vā aññabhāgo assa [M 0.0247] atthi, tasmā. Aññabhāgiyasaṅkhyaṃ labhatīti ettha “so yvāya”nti idha so-saddameva ānetvā so aññabhāgiyasaṅkhaṃ labhatīti yojetabbaṃ, “so”ti vā pāṭhaseso daṭṭhabbo. Ca-saddo samuccayattho. So pana adhikaraṇasaddato paraṃ daṭṭhabbo, “adhikaraṇa”nti ca veditabboti. Tesanti mettiyabhūmajakānaṃ. Imaṃ mayaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ nāma karomāti chagalakaṃ ajikāya vippaṭipajjantaṃ disvā “mayaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ chagalakaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ nāma karomā”ti vadantānaṃ. Nāmakaraṇasaññāyāti nāmakaraṇasaṅkhātāya saññāya. Etthāpi “yo so”tiādikaṃ ānetvā tassā nāmakaraṇasaññāya yo so aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ “dabbo mallaputto nāmā”ti chagalako vutto, so yasmā ādhāro vatthu adhiṭṭhānanti yojetabbaṃ.

'Whence is this other, that 'of another part' is said?' He says, 'that which is... from that.' There, the connection is 'human birth and the state of being a monk'—this portion, part, or side; the meaning is 'human birth and the state of being a monk'—this portion, part, or side. 'From that' (tato) means from that portion, 'human birth and the state of being a monk.' Or that other portion is that other portion, designated as the state of being a goat, of the animal realm, as was said. 'Of it' (assa) means of the goat. 'Is' (atthi) means is found. Therefore, since the goat belongs to the other portion, and since that other portion exists for it, therefore. In 'it receives the designation of belonging to another part,' here, having brought the word 'he' (so) from 'he, that which is,' it should be connected as 'he receives the designation of belonging to another part,' or 'he' (so) should be seen as a textual omission. The word 'ca' is for conjunction. But it should be seen after the word 'adhikaraṇa,' and 'and the matter' should be understood. 'Of them' (tesaṃ) means of the Mettiyā and Bhūmajaka monks. 'Let us name this one Dabba Mallaputta' means of those saying, having seen a goat behaving improperly towards a she-goat, 'We, friends, will name this goat Dabba Mallaputta.' 'By the perception of naming' means by the perception designated as naming. Here too, having brought 'he who' etc., it should be connected: because that goat, which in the origin story is called 'Dabba Mallaputta,' is the basis, the object, the foundation of that perception of naming.

Idāni kathametaṃ viññāyati “adhikaraṇa”nti cettha ādhāro veditabbo, na vivādādhikaraṇādīsu aññataranti anuyogaṃ sandhāyāha “tañhi sandhāyā”tiādi. Tattha tanti tassā nāmakaraṇasaññāya adhiṭṭhānabhūtaṃ chagalakaṃ paccāmasati. Vivādādhikaraṇādīsu aññataraṃ sandhāya na vuttanti sambandho. Tattha kāraṇaṃ pucchati “kasmā”ti. Kāraṇamāha “asambhavato”ti. Idāni tameva asambhavaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā dassetuṃ “na hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Na hi upādiyiṃsūti sambandho. Upādiyiṃsūti gaṇhiṃsu. Kiṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānampi leso atthi, yenevaṃ vuttanti āha “na ca catunnaṃ adhikaraṇāna”ntiādi. Idāni tameva samatthetuṃ “jātilesādayo hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha jātiyeva leso jātileso. Ādisaddena nāmalesādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Hoti cettha –

Now, referring to the query, "How is this understood as 'adhikaraṇa' (basis)? Here, 'basis' should be understood, not any of the disputes, etc.," he says, "referring to that," etc. There, "that" refers to the goat, which is the basis for that naming-perception. The connection is that it was not stated referring to any of the disputes, etc. There, he asks the reason, "Why?" He gives the reason, "Because of impossibility." Now, to make that very impossibility clear and show it, "not indeed," etc., is said. The connection is "indeed, they did not grasp." "Upādiyiṃsu" means "they grasped." "Is there even a trace of the four disputes, that it was said thus?" He says, "and not of the four disputes," etc. Now, to support that very thing, "for the traces of birth, etc.," is said. There, the mere trace of birth is the trace of birth. By "etc.," the grasping of the trace of name, etc., is meant. It exists here –

“Lesā [V 0.0229] jātināmagotta-liṅgāpattivasāpi ca;

Pattacīvarupajjhāyā-cariyāvāsavasā dasā”ti.

“Traces, according to birth, name, clan, gender, offense, bowl, robe, preceptor, teacher, and residence: these are the ten.”

Āpattileso nāma lahukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjanto diṭṭho hoti. Tañce pārājikena codeti “assamaṇosi, asakyaputtiyosī”ti, āpatti vācāya vācāya saṅghādisesassāti (pārā. 396) evaṃ āpattilesampi puggalasmiṃyeva āropetvā vuttattā “puggalānaṃyeva lesā vuttā”ti vuttaṃ[M 0.0248]. Tañca “dabbo mallaputto”ti nāmanti mettiyabhūmajakehi chagalakassa kataṃ taṃ “dabbo mallaputto”ti nāmañca. Evaṃ asambhavaṃ dassetvā idāni imināva pasaṅgena desalesasaddānaṃ atthaṃ saṃvaṇṇetuṃ “ettha cā”tiādimāha. Etthāti etesu dvīsu desalesesu. Deso nāma jātiādibhedo vohāro. Tenāha “jātiādīsū”tiādi. Aññampi vatthunti yasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ, taṃ muñcitvā aññampi vatthuṃ. Kathaṃ silissatīti āha “vohāramattenevā”tiādi, vohāramatteneva, na tu atthatoti adhippāyo. “Īsakaṃ allīyatī”ti iminā “leso”ti lisa allībhāveti imassa rūpanti dasseti. Kiñcāpi desalesānaṃ vuttanayena byañjanato nānākaraṇaṃ atthi, atthato pana natthīti āha “jātiādīnaṃyeva aññatarakoṭṭhāsassetaṃ adhivacana”nti.

The trace of an offense refers to someone seen committing a minor offense. If one accuses them with a pārājika offense, saying, "You are not an ascetic, not a follower of the Sakyan," then for each statement, there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa). (Pārā. 396) Thus, because even the trace of an offense is attributed to an individual, it is said, "Only the traces of individuals are mentioned." And that name, "Dabba the Mallian," is what was given to the goat by Mettiyā and Bhūmajaka. Having shown this impossibility, now, by this very occasion, to explain the meaning of the terms desa and lesa, he says, "Here too," and so on. "Here" means in these two, desa and lesa. Desa refers to usage with distinctions such as birth, etc. Hence it is said, "In birth, etc.," and so on. "Another object" means another object, leaving aside the object in which it is established. "How does it adhere?" He explains: "Merely by convention," and so on—the intention is merely by convention, not in ultimate meaning. By "it slightly clings," it shows that the term lesa is a form derived from the root lisa, meaning "to cling." Although there is a difference in wording between desa and lesa as explained, in meaning there is none. Hence it is said, "This is merely a designation for one portion of birth, etc."

Yadi pana nāmakaraṇasaññāya ādhārabhūtaṃ chagalakaṃ sandhāya “aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassā”ti vuttaṃ, atha kasmā padabhājane taṃ avibhajitvā “aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassāti āpattaññabhāgiyaṃ vā hoti adhikaraṇaññabhāgiyaṃ vā”tiādi (pārā. 393) vuttanti āha “padabhājane panā”tiādi. Tanti ādhārasaṅkhātaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ. Āvibhūtaṃ pākaṭaṃ. Atthuddhāravasenāti tena vattabbaatthānaṃ uddharaṇavasena. Nanu ca “atthamattaṃ pati saddā abhinivisantī”ti na ekena saddena anekatthā abhidhīyantīti? Saccametaṃ saddavisese apekkhite, tesaṃ tesaṃ pana atthānaṃ adhikaraṇasaddavacanīyatāsāmaññaṃ upādāya vuccamāno ayaṃ vicāro adhikaraṇasaddassa atthuddhāroti vutto. Tenevāha “adhikaraṇanti vacanasāmaññato atthuddhāravasena pavattāni cattāri adhikaraṇānī”ti. Aññabhāgiyatāti aññapakkhiyatā. Tabbhāgiyatāti tappakkhiyatā. Apākaṭā padabhājanato aññatra dassitaṭṭhānābhāvato. Avasāne āpattaññabhāgiyena codanañcāti “bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho hoti, saṅghādisese saṅghādisesadiṭṭhi hoti, tañce pārājikena codetī”tiādicodanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “adhikaraṇaññabhāgiya”nti. Ekamekañhi adhikaraṇaṃ itaresaṃ tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ aññabhāgiyaṃ aññapakkhiyaṃ [V 0.0230] aññakoṭṭhāsiyaṃ hoti vatthuvisabhāgattā. Ādisaddena [M 0.0249] “kathaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇassa aññabhāgiya”ntiādiko padavibhāgo saṅgahito.

If, however, 'of a legal issue belonging to another part' was said with reference to the young goat that is the basis for the designation by name, then why in the word-analysis was that not analyzed, but instead it was said: '“Of a legal issue belonging to another part” means it is one belonging to another part by way of an offense, or it is one belonging to another part by way of a legal issue,' etc.? He says: 'But in the word-analysis…' and so on. That refers to the legal issue designated as the 'basis.' Manifest means clear. 'By way of extracting the meaning' means by way of extracting the meanings that should be stated. But is it not so that 'words incline only toward the meaning,' so that one word does not signify many meanings? This is true when specific words are considered, but this discussion, which proceeds by taking up the commonality of being expressible by the word 'legal issue' for those various meanings, is called the extraction of the meaning of the word 'legal issue.' Therefore he said: 'The four legal issues proceed by way of extracting the meaning from the commonality of the word “legal issue.”' 'Belonging to another part' means belonging to another side. 'Belonging to that part' means belonging to that side. They are not manifest because no place is shown for them apart from the word-analysis. At the end, the phrase 'and an accusation by means of an offense belonging to another part' refers to an accusation such as: 'A bhikkhu is seen committing a saṅghādisesa offense; he has the perception of a saṅghādisesa in that saṅghādisesa offense; and if one accuses him of a pārājika offense,' etc. It is in reference to this that it is said, 'a legal issue belonging to another part.' For each single legal issue is one belonging to another part, to another side, to another division in relation to the other three, because of the dissimilarity of the subject matter. By the word 'etc.,' the word-division beginning 'How is a legal issue one belonging to another part of a legal issue?' is included.

Kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāyāti ettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, tassāpi asambhavadassanappasaṅgena heṭṭhā vuttattā “sesā vinicchayakathā aṭṭhame vuttasadisāyevā”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha sesā vinicchayakathāti “pārājikenāti bhikkhuno anurūpesu ekūnavisatiyā aññatarenā”tiādikā (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. duṭṭhadosasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vinicchayakathā. Vuttasadisāyevāti ettha imasmiṃ sikkhāpade yā vattabbā, tena sikkhāpadena sādhāraṇabhūtā sā vuttasadisāyevāti adhippetā, na asādhāraṇabhūtā apubbavaṇṇanāya adhippetattā. Tenevāha “ayaṃ panā”tiādi. Purimasmiṃ sikkhāpadepi tathāsaññino anāpattikattā “idha cā”ti vuttaṃ. Tathāsaññinopīti “pārājikaṃyeva ayaṃ āpanno”ti evaṃsaññinopi. Itisaddo ādiattho vā pakārattho vā. Tena kenaci bhikkhunā añño koci khattiyajātiko pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho hoti, atha so aññaṃ attano veriṃ khattiyajātikaṃ bhikkhuṃ passitvā taṃ khattiyajātilesaṃ gahetvā evaṃ codeti “khattiyo mayā diṭṭho pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpajjanto, tvaṃ khattiyo pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannosi, atha vā tvaṃ kho khattiyo, na añño, pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannosi, assamaṇosi, asakyaputtiyosi, natthi tayā saddhiṃ uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā saṅghakammaṃ vā”ti, āpatti vācāya vācāya saṅghādisesassa. Ettha ca tesaṃ khattiyānaṃ aññamaññaṃ asadisassa tassa tassa dīghādino vā diṭṭhādino vā vasena aññabhāgiyatā, khattiyajātipaññattiyā ādhāravasena adhikaraṇatā ca veditabbā. Esa nayo nāmalesādīsupi.

Regarding the phrase 'by taking up a mere trace of some part': since it has been stated above that what should be said here would also entail seeing an impossibility, it is said: 'The remaining discussion of the decision is just like what was said in the eighth.' Here, the remaining discussion of the decision is the discussion of the decision beginning: '“By a pārājika” means by any one of the nineteen offenses analogous to a pārājika for a bhikkhu' (cf. Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. on the Duṭṭhadosa Sikkhāpada). 'Just like what was said' is intended to mean that what should be said in this training rule, being common to that training rule, is just like what was said; it is not intended to be something uncommon by way of a new explanation. Therefore he says: 'But this…' and so on. Since in the previous training rule too one with such a perception is without offense, it is said: 'and here…' 'Even of one with such a perception' means even of one with the perception, 'This one has indeed committed a pārājika.' The word iti has the sense of 'etc.' or indicates the manner. Thus, some bhikkhu has seen some other person of the warrior caste committing a pārājika offense. Then, seeing another bhikkhu of the warrior caste who is his enemy, he takes up that trace of the warrior caste and accuses him thus: 'I saw a warrior committing a pārājika offense. You are a warrior; you have committed a pārājika offense.' Or: 'You indeed are the warrior, not another, who has committed a pārājika offense. You are not a recluse, not a son of the Sakyan. There is no Uposatha or Pavāraṇā or formal act of the Saṅgha with you.' For every single statement, there is a saṅghādisesa offense. And here, the state of belonging to another part should be understood by way of the dissimilarity of those warriors to one another in regard to being tall, etc., or being seen, etc., and the state of being the legal issue should be understood by way of the designation of the warrior caste being the basis. This is the method also in cases of a trace of a name, etc.

Āpattilese pana kenaci bhikkhunā koci bhikkhu lahukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjanto diṭṭho hoti, so cetaṃ bhikkhuṃ pārājikena codeti, āpatti vācāya vācāya saṅghādisesassa. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ aññabhāgiyaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hotīti? Yañhi so lahukaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, taṃ pārājikassa aññabhāgiyaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ, tassa pana aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa leso nāma. Yo so sabbakhattiyānaṃ sādhāraṇo khattiyabhāvo viya sabbāpattīnaṃ sādhāraṇo āpattibhāvo. Eteneva upāyena [M 0.0250] “kenaci bhikkhunā koci bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho hotī”tiādikaṃ visesaṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

But in the case of a trace of an offense: some bhikkhu has seen some bhikkhu committing a light offense, and he accuses that bhikkhu of a pārājika; for every single statement, there is a saṅghādisesa offense. If so, how is it a legal issue belonging to another part? The light offense that he committed is a legal issue belonging to another part relative to the pārājika. The trace of that legal issue belonging to another part is this: the nature of an offense, which is common to all offenses, just as the nature of a warrior is common to all warriors. By this method, he includes the specific case beginning: 'some bhikkhu has seen some bhikkhu committing a saṅghādisesa offense,' etc.

Aññabhāgiyasikkhaṃ [V 0.0231] yo, neva sikkhati yuttito;

Gacche vinayaviññūhi, aññabhāgiyataṃva so. (vajira. ṭī. pārājika 408);

Whoever does not train properly in the training concerning what belongs to another faction, he himself comes to belong to another faction in the view of those wise in the Vinaya.

Aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on what belongs to another faction is finished.

10. Saṅghabhedasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Training Rule on Schism in the Sangha

Sahitassāti kāyacittehi ekībhūtassa. Tenāha “cittena ca sarīrena ca aviyuttassāti attho”ti. Assāti “samaggassā”ti padassa. Samānasaṃvāsakoti samāno ekūposathādibhedo saṃvāso assāti samānasaṃvāsako, laddhinānāsaṃvāsakena vā kammanānāsaṃvāsakena vā virahito. Kāyasāmaggidānatoti kāyena, kāyassa vā sāmaggiyā sahitabhāvassa dānato, tesu tesu saṅghakammesu hatthapāsūpagamanatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Kathaṃ nāmāyaṃ bhijjeyyāti ayaṃ saṅgho kena nu kho upāyena vaggo bhaveyya. Vāyāmeyyāti ussāhaṃ kareyya, pakkhaṃ pariyeseyya, gaṇaṃ bandheyyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Attano phalaṃ karotīti karaṇaṃ, yaṃ kiñci kāraṇaṃ, adhikaṃ karaṇanti adhikaraṇaṃ, visesakāraṇaṃ, visesakāraṇañca saṅghabhedassāti vuttaṃ “bhedanassā”tiādi. Bhedakaravatthuvasena aṭṭhārasavidhanti –

“United” means being unified in body and mind. Therefore it is said: “The meaning is: not separated in mind and body.” This refers to the word “harmonious” (samaggassa). “Of the same communion” (samānasaṃvāsako) means one for whom there is a common communion, such as a single Uposatha observance, etc., one who is devoid of a separate communion based on views or a separate communion based on formal acts. “By means of bodily harmony” means by the body, or by giving the state of harmony of the body; that is to say, by coming within arm's reach in the various formal acts of the Sangha. “How indeed could this be broken?” means: “By what means could this Sangha become divided?” “One should strive” means one should make an effort, seek a faction, and form a group, so it is said. A “making” (karaṇaṃ) is what produces its own result; it is any cause. A “special making” (adhikaṃ karaṇaṃ) is a “legal issue” (adhikaraṇaṃ), a specific cause. And a specific cause of schism in the Sangha is what is meant by “of division,” etc. By way of the grounds for causing schism, they are of eighteen kinds:

“Idhupāli bhikkhū adhammaṃ ‘dhammo’ti dīpenti, dhammaṃ ‘adhammo’ti dīpenti. Avinayaṃ ‘vinayo’ti dīpenti, vinayaṃ ‘avinayo’ti dīpenti. Abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena ‘bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenā’ti dīpenti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena ‘abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenā’ti dīpenti. Anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena ‘āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenā’ti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena ‘anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenā’ti dīpenti. Apaññattaṃ tathāgatena ‘paññattaṃ tathāgatenā’ti dīpenti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena [M 0.0251] ‘apaññattaṃ tathāgatenā’ti dīpenti. Anāpattiṃ ‘āpattī’ti dīpenti, āpattiṃ ‘anāpattī’ti dīpenti. Lahukaṃ āpattiṃ ‘garukā āpattī’ti dīpenti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ ‘lahukā āpattī’ti dīpenti. Sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ ‘anavasesā āpattī’ti dīpenti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ ‘sāvasesā āpattī’ti dīpenti. Duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ ‘aduṭṭhullā āpattī’ti dīpenti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ ‘duṭṭhullā āpattī’ti dīpentī”ti (cūḷava. 352) –

“Here, Upāli, monks declare what is not the Dhamma to be ‘the Dhamma,’ and what is the Dhamma to be ‘not the Dhamma.’ They declare what is not the Vinaya to be ‘the Vinaya,’ and what is the Vinaya to be ‘not the Vinaya.’ They declare what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata to be ‘spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata,’ and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata to be ‘not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata.’ They declare what was not practiced by the Tathāgata to be ‘practiced by the Tathāgata,’ and what was practiced by the Tathāgata to be ‘not practiced by the Tathāgata.’ They declare what was not prescribed by the Tathāgata to be ‘prescribed by the Tathāgata,’ and what was prescribed by the Tathāgata to be ‘not prescribed by the Tathāgata.’ They declare a non-offense to be ‘an offense,’ and an offense to be ‘a non-offense.’ They declare a light offense to be ‘a grave offense,’ and a grave offense to be ‘a light offense.’ They declare an offense with a remainder to be ‘an offense without a remainder,’ and an offense without a remainder to be ‘an offense with a remainder.’ They declare a gross offense to be ‘not a gross offense,’ and a non-gross offense to be ‘a gross offense’” (Cv VII 5.1) –

Evaṃ [V 0.0232] kammakkhandhake vuttānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ bhedakaraṇānaṃ vasena aṭṭhārasavidhaṃ. Kāraṇañhi tadāyattavuttitāya phalaṃ ettha vasatīti “vatthū”ti vuccati. Honti cettha –

Thus, by way of the eighteen grounds for causing schism mentioned in the Chapter on Formal Acts, they are of eighteen kinds. For a cause (kāraṇa) is called a “ground” (vatthu) because the result has its occurrence dependent on it and dwells therein. And here there are:

“Dhammavinayabhāsitā-ciṇṇapaññattikā dukā;

Āpattilahuduṭṭhulla-sāvasesadukāni ca.

“The pairs concerning Dhamma and Vinaya, what was spoken, practiced, and prescribed;

And the pairs concerning offense, light offense, gross offense, and offense with a remainder.

“Etānaṭṭhārasa ‘bheda-karavatthū’ti vuccare;

Vipallāsagahitāni, vādamūlūpanissayā”ti.

“These eighteen are called ‘grounds for causing schism’;

They are grasped with distortion, a supporting condition for the root of disputes.”

Paggayhāti paggahitaṃ abbhussitaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā. Tiṭṭheyyāti yathāsamādinnaṃ, yathāpaggahitameva ca katvā accheyya. Yasmā pana evaṃ paggaṇhatā, tiṭṭhatā ca taṃ dīpitañceva avinissaṭṭhañca hoti, tasmā “dīpeyya ceva nappaṭinissajjeyya cā”ti vuttaṃ. Kīva dūre sutvā gantvā avadantānaṃ dukkaṭanti āha “sabbantimena paricchedenā”tiādi. Pi-saddo cettha aṭṭhānappayutto, tassa “aḍḍhayojanamatta”nti iminā sambandho veditabbo. Tattha “aḍḍhayojanamatta”nti iminā ekavihāre vattabbameva natthīti dīpeti. “Gantvā”ti iminā dūtaṃ vā paṇṇaṃ vā pesetvā vadatopi āpattimokkho natthi, sayameva pana gantvā “garuko kho, āvuso, saṅghabhedo, mā saṅghabhedāya parakkamī”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.411) nivāretabboti dīpeti.

“Having taken it up” means having taken it up, raised it aloft, and made it manifest. “Should stand by it” means one should remain, having acted just as one undertook it and just as one took it up. But since, by taking it up and standing by it in this way, that view is both explained and not relinquished, it is therefore said, “one should both explain it and not relinquish it.” As for the dukkaṭa offense for not going to speak after having heard from a certain distance, he says: “by the uttermost boundary,” etc. Here the particle “pi” is used in the wrong place; its connection should be understood with “about half a yojana.” Therein, “about half a yojana” shows that within a single monastery there is no requirement to speak at all. “By going” shows that there is no exemption from the offense even for one who speaks by sending a messenger or a letter, but one should go oneself and restrain them, saying: “Friend, schism in the Sangha is a grave matter; do not strive for schism in the Sangha” (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.411). This is what is shown.

Samāgacchatūti ekībhavatu. Ekībhāvo ca samānaladdhivasena hotīti āha “ekaladdhiko hotū”ti. Ekā laddhi gahaṇaṃ assāti ekaladdhiko, ekadiṭṭhikoti attho. Aññamaññasampattiyāti aññamaññassa samānadiṭṭhicittatāsaṅkhātāya sampattiyā. “Aññamaññassa guṇalābhādikāya sampattiyā”ti [M 0.0252] keci. Asamaggo hi visuṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisati, bahisīmāyaṃ vā anupariveṇiyaṃ vāti na ekuddeso. Tenāha “ekato pavattapātimokkhuddesoti attho”ti. Appaṭinissajjato dukkaṭanti visuṃ visuṃ vadantānaṃ gaṇanāya dukkaṭaṃ. Samanubhāsanakammaṃ kātabbanti yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanakammaṃ kātabbaṃ, “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmo bhikkhu samaggassa saṅghassa bhedāya parakkamatī”tiādinā (pārā. 413) padabhājane vuttāhi ñatticatutthāhi tīhi samanubhāsanakammavācāhi kammaṃ kātabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. “Bhedāya parakkameyyā”ti visuṃ vuttattā bhedanasaṃvattanikassa adhikaraṇassa samādāya paggaṇhanato pubbepi pakkhapariyesanādivasena saṅghabhedāya parakkamantassa samanubhāsanakammaṃ kātabbanti [V 0.0233] veditabbaṃ. Paṭinissajjantassa anāpattibhāvato “sotthibhāvo tassa bhikkhuno”ti vuttaṃ.

“May he come together” means may he become united. And since unity comes about by way of a common view, he says, “May he be of one view.” “One for whom there is a single view or grasping” is “one of a single view” (ekaladdhiko); the meaning is “one of a single opinion” (ekadiṭṭhiko). “By mutual attainment” means by the attainment consisting in the state of having a common view and mind with one another. Some say: “By the attainment of one another's virtues, gains, etc.” For one who is not in harmony recites the Pātimokkha separately, either outside the boundary or in a separate residence; thus there is no single recitation. Therefore it is said: “The meaning is the recitation of the Pātimokkha proceeding as one.” The dukkaṭa for not relinquishing: there is a dukkaṭa for each one counted among those who speak separately. The formal act of admonition should be performed: the formal act of admonition should be performed up to the third time. That is to say, the act should be performed with the three formal announcements of admonition, which are a motion-as-fourth act, stated in the word-analysis with “Venerable sirs, let the Sangha listen to me. This monk so-and-so is striving for a schism in the harmonious Sangha…” (Pārā. 413), etc. Since it is stated separately, “He might strive for schism,” it should be understood that the formal act of admonition should be performed even before he has taken up and stood by a legal issue conducive to schism, for one who strives for schism in the Sangha by seeking a faction, etc. Since for one who relinquishes it there is no offense, it is said, “There is well-being for that monk.”

Kiñcāpi bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ na bhindati, apica kho bhedāya parakkamatīti “sādhāraṇapaññattī”ti vuttaṃ. Saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjantassa ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā ca paṭippassambhantīti āha “samanubhāsanakamme”tiādi. Tañca dukkaṭaṃ te ca thullaccayā paṭippassambhantīti yañca ñattipariyosāne dukkaṭaṃ āpanno, ye ca dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccaye, tā tissopi āpattiyo liṅgaparivattena asādhāraṇāpattiyo viya paṭippassambhanti. Sace panassa ñattipariyosāne lajjidhammo okkamati, saṃvaro uppajjati, taṃ paṭinissajjati, ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ desetvā muccati. Atha taṃ na paṭinissajjati, bhedāya parakkamati ceva bhedanasaṃvattanikaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samādāya paggayha tiṭṭhati ca, ñattidukkaṭaṃ paṭippassambhati, paṭhamakammavācāya thullaccaye patiṭṭhāti. Esa nayo itarakammavācāyampi. Asamanubhāsiyamānassa appaṭinissajjantassāpi saṅghādisesena anāpatti. Paṭinissajjantassāpi ñattito pubbe vā ñattikkhaṇe vā ñattipariyosāne vā paṭhamāya vā anussāvanāya dutiyāya vā tatiyāya vā yāva yya-kāraṃ na sampāpuṇāti, tāva paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādisesena anāpatti. Tenāha “asamanubhāsiyamānassa cā”tiādi.

Although a bhikkhunī does not split the Sangha, yet she does strive for schism; therefore this is called a 'shared prescription.' For one who is incurring a Saṅghādisesa, there is a dukkaṭa at the motion and thullaccayas at the two formal announcements, and these are allayed; thus it is said: 'In the formal act of admonition,' etc. That dukkaṭa and those thullaccayas are allayed means that the dukkaṭa one has incurred at the conclusion of the motion and the thullaccayas from the two formal announcements—these three offenses are allayed, just as non-shared offenses are allayed by a change of gender. But if, at the conclusion of the motion, a sense of shame overcomes him, restraint arises, and he relinquishes that view, he is freed after confessing the dukkaṭa for the motion. Then, if he does not relinquish it, but strives for schism and persists in taking up and holding to the legal issue conducive to schism, the dukkaṭa for the motion is allayed and he becomes established in a thullaccaya at the first formal announcement. This is the method for the other formal announcements too. For one who is not being admonished, even if he does not relinquish it, there is no Saṅghādisesa offense. And for one who relinquishes it—whether before the motion, at the moment of the motion, at the conclusion of the motion, or during the first, second, or third proclamation, as long as the formal act is not completed—there is no Saṅghādisesa offense. Therefore it is said: 'And for one who is not being admonished,' etc.

Ettha pana (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.416) “devadatto samaggassa saṅghassa bhedāya parakkami, tasmiṃ vatthusmi”nti (pari. 17) parivāre āgatattā devadatto ādikammiko, so ca kho [M 0.0253] saṅghabhedāya parakkamanasseva, na appaṭinissajjanassa. Na hi tassa taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ. Kathamidaṃ jānitabbanti ce? Suttato. Tathā hi “ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmi”nti parivāre āgatattā ariṭṭhassa kammaṃ katanti paññāyati, na tathā devadattassa. Athāpissa katena bhavitabbanti koci attano rucimattena vadeyya, tathāpi appaṭinissajjane ādikammikassa anāpatti nāma natthi. Na hi paññattaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ vītikkamantassa aññatra odissa anuññātato anāpatti nāma dissati. Yampi ariṭṭhasikkhāpadassa padabhājane anāpattiyaṃ “ādikammikassā”ti potthakesu likhitaṃ, taṃ pamādalikhitaṃ, pamādalikhitabhāvo ca tassa “paṭhamaṃ ariṭṭho bhikkhu codetabbo, codetvā sāretabbo, sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetabbo”ti (cūḷava. 65) evaṃ kammakkhandhake āpattiropanato veditabbo.

Here, however (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.416), since it comes in the Parivāra (Pari. 17), 'Devadatta strove for a schism in the harmonious Sangha; in that case,' Devadatta is the originator (ādikammika), but he was the originator only of striving for schism, not of not relinquishing it. For that formal act was not performed on him. If it is asked, 'How is this to be known?' From the Sutta. For since it comes in the Parivāra, 'The monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-trapper, did not relinquish his evil view after being admonished up to the third time; in that case,' it is understood that the formal act was performed on Ariṭṭha, but not so for Devadatta. Now, if someone were to say out of mere preference, 'It must have been done for him,' still, in the case of not relinquishing, there is no such thing as no-offense for the originator. For one who transgresses a prescribed training rule, no no-offense is seen, except where specifically permitted. And as for what is written in the books in the no-offense section of the word-analysis of the Ariṭṭha training rule, 'for the originator,' that is a scribal error. That it is a scribal error should be understood from the imposition of the offense in the Chapter on Formal Acts, where it says: 'First, the monk Ariṭṭha should be charged; having been charged, he should be reminded; having been reminded, the offense should be imposed on him' (Cv I.34.2).

Idha [V 0.0234] bhedāya parakkamane ādikammikassa devadattassa yasmā taṃ kammaṃ na kataṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.416), tasmāssa āpattiyeva na jātā. Sikkhāpadaṃ pana taṃ ārabbha paññattanti katvā “ādikammiko”ti vutto. Iti āpattiyā abhāvatoyevassa anāpatti vuttā. Sā panesā kiñcāpi “asamanubhāsiyamānassā”ti imināva siddhā. Yasmā pana asamanubhāsiyamāno nāma yassa kevalaṃ samanubhāsanaṃ na karonti, so vuccati, na ādikammiko. Ayañca devadatto ādikammikoyeva. Tasmā “ādikammikassā”ti (pārā. 416) vuttaṃ. Eteneva upāyena ṭhapetvā ariṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ sabbasamanubhāsanāsu vinicchayo veditabbo. Kāyavācācittato samuṭṭhānato samanubhāsanasamuṭṭhānaṃ. “Paṭinissajjāmī”ti kāyavikāraṃ vā vacībhedaṃ vā akarontasseva pana āpajjanato akiriyaṃ. “Nappaṭinissajjāmī”ti saññāya abhāvena muccanato saññāvimokkhaṃ. “Nappaṭinissajjāmī”ti jānanacitteneva sacittakaṃ.

Here, in the case of striving for a schism, since that formal act was not performed on Devadatta, the originator (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.416), no offense arose for him. However, because the training rule was laid down concerning him, he is called 'the originator.' Thus, it is because of the absence of an offense that 'no offense' is stated for him. Yet this is already established by the phrase 'for one who is not being formally admonished.' For 'one who is not being formally admonished' is the name for one on whom they simply do not perform the formal admonition; this does not refer to the originator. But this Devadatta was indeed the originator. Therefore it is said, 'for the originator' (Pārā. 416). By this same method, with the exception of the training rule concerning Ariṭṭha, the decision in all cases of formal admonition should be understood. It arises from the formal admonition, which itself arises from body, speech, and mind. It is inaction, since one incurs the offense precisely by not making a bodily gesture or a verbal utterance such as, 'I relinquish it.' It is release by perception, since one is absolved through the absence of the perception, 'I will not relinquish it.' It is intentional, since it is done with a mind that knows, 'I will not relinquish it.'

Saṅghabhedasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on schism in the Sangha is finished.

11. Bhedānuvattakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Following a Schismatic

Tassevāti [M 0.0254] bhedāya parakkamantasseva. Khoti nipātamattaṃ. Panāti visese nipāto. Yaṃ vacanaṃ samaggepi vagge avayavabhūte karoti bhindati, taṃ kalahakārakavacanaṃ idha “vagga”nti vuccatīti āha “vaggaṃ asāmaggipakkhiyavacanaṃ vadantī”ti. Asāmaggipakkhe bhavā asāmaggipakkhiyā, kalahakārakā, tesaṃ vacanaṃ asāmaggipakkhiyavacanaṃ, asāmaggipakkhe vā bhavaṃ vacanaṃ asāmaggipakkhiyavacanaṃ. “Na hi saṅgho saṅghassa kammaṃ karotī”ti idaṃ niggahavasena kattabbaṃ kammaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, ubbāhikādikammaṃ pana bahūnampi kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Dhammavādīti bhūtavādī. Vinayavādīti vūpasamavādī. Jānāti noti etthāpi “chandañca ruciñcā”ti idaṃ ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Tenāha “amhākaṃ chandādīni jānātī”ti. Bhāsatīti ettha “no”ti idaṃ vibhattivipariṇāmena yujjati. Tenāha “evaṃ karomāti amhehi saddhiṃ bhāsatī”ti. “Eta”nti iminā tassa kammaṃ paccāmaṭṭhanti āha “yaṃ so karotī”tiādi. Soti saṅghabhedāya parakkamanto. Sametāyasmantānanti ettha “citta”nti ajjhāharitabbanti āha “āyasmantānaṃ citta”nti. Vuttasadisāyevāti ettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadaṭṭhakathāya vaṇṇanāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vuttameva.

'Of that same one' means: of the one striving for a schism. 'Kho' is a mere particle. 'Pana' is a particle indicating a special case. That speech which creates division and breaks up a united group, or a constituent part of it, is quarrel-making speech. This is here called 'factional,' thus it is said: 'they speak factional speech, speech on the side of disunity.' Those on the side of disunity are 'on the side of disunity,' that is, quarrel-makers; their speech is 'speech on the side of disunity.' Or, speech that is on the side of disunity is 'speech on the side of disunity.' The statement 'The Sangha does not perform a formal act for the Sangha' is said with reference to a formal act that should be done by way of censure; but a formal act such as a suspension may be done by many. 'A speaker on the Dhamma' means a speaker of what is factual. 'A speaker on the Vinaya' means a speaker of what leads to tranquility. In 'he knows or not,' here too the words 'and desire and inclination' should be brought in and connected. Thus it is said: 'he knows our desire, etc.' In 'he speaks,' here the word 'no' (us) is connected by a change of case ending. Thus it is said: 'he speaks with us, saying, “Let us do it this way.”' By 'this,' they refer back to his action, thus it is said: 'what he does,' etc. 'He' is the one striving for a schism. In 'the venerable ones being united,' here the word 'mind' should be supplied, thus it is said: 'the mind of the venerable ones.' In 'just as was said,' what should be said here has already been stated below in the explanation in the commentary on the training rule concerning sharing in what belongs to another (see Kankhāvitaranī-aṭṭhakathā, explanation of the Aññabhāgiya training rule).

Bhedānuvattakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on following a schismatic is finished.

12. Dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

12. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Being Difficult to Admonish

Dukkhena [V 0.0235] vattabbo anusāsituṃ asakkuṇeyyo sabhāvo assāti dubbacajātiko, vilomabhāvī. Tenāha “dubbacasabhāvo”tiādi. Vattuṃ asakkuṇeyyoti kismiñci vuccamāne asahanato ovadituṃ asakkuṇeyyo. Uddisīyatīti uddeso, pātimokkho, tasmiṃ pariyāpannā antogadhā uddesapariyāpannā, tesu uddesapariyāpannesu. Tenāha “uddese”tiādi. Atha sabbāneva sikkhāpadāni kathaṃ pātimokkhuddesapariyāpannānīti āha “yassa siyā āpatti, so ‘āvikareyyā’ti evaṃ saṅgahitattā”ti. “Yassa siyā āpattī”ti iminā [M 0.0255] sabbāpi āpattiyo nidānuddese saṅgahitā eva honti. Sikkhāpadesūti adhisīlasikkhāya adhigamūpāyabhūtesu vinayapaññattīsūti attho. So pana pākaṭoyevāti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ na vutto. Pañcahi sahadhammikehīti bhikkhubhikkhunisāmaṇerasāmaṇerisikkhamānāhi. Sikkhitabbattāti labbhamānavasena sikkhitabbattā. Tathā hi tehi yathāsakaṃ sikkhā sikkhīyati, na sabbā. Buddhapaññattenāti buddhena ṭhapitena, vihitenāti attho. Atha vā sahadhammikena sakāraṇena vuccamānoti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Vacanāyāti nissakke sampadānavacananti āha “tato mama vacanato”ti.

One whose nature is to be difficult to speak to, impossible to instruct, is of a nature difficult to admonish (`dubbacajātiko`), of a contrary disposition (`vilomabhāvī`). Thus he says: 'of a difficult nature,' etc. 'Impossible to speak to' means that because of his intolerance when something is said, he is impossible to advise. 'What is recited' is the recitation (`uddeso`), the Pātimokkha. Included in it, contained within it, are those included in the recitation (`uddesapariyāpannā`); among those included in the recitation. Thus he says: 'in the recitation,' etc. Now, how are all the training rules included in the Pātimokkha recitation? He says: because they are included thus: 'Whoever should have an offense, he should disclose it.' By this 'Whoever should have an offense,' all offenses are indeed included in the introductory recitation. 'In the training rules' means: in the Vinaya regulations which are the means for the attainment of the training in the higher virtue. But since this is obvious, it is not stated in the commentary. 'With five co-religionists' means: with bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male novices, female novices, and female probationers. 'Because it is to be trained in' means: because it is to be trained in according to what is attainable. For they each train in their respective training, not in all of them. 'Established by the Buddha' means: laid down by the Buddha, prescribed. Alternatively, the meaning here should be seen thus: 'being spoken to with reason by a co-religionist.' 'For the speaking' (`vacanāya`): this is a dative of purpose. Thus he says: 'on account of my speaking'.

Dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on being difficult to admonish is finished.

13. Kuladūsakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

13. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Corrupting Families

Nagarassāpi gāmavisesattā idha gāmaggahaṇeneva nagarampi gahitanti āha “nagarampi gāme antogadhamevā”ti, vā-saddena vā anuttavikappatthena gahaṇanti evaṃ vuttaṃ. Ettha ca apākāraparikkhepo sāpaṇo nigamo, sapākārāpaṇaṃ nagaraṃ, taṃtaṃviparīto gāmoti imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ viseso daṭṭhabbo. Kulāni dūsetīti khattiyabrāhmaṇavessasuddavasena cattāri kulāni vikāraṃ āpādeti. Dūsento ca na asucikaddamādīhi dūseti, atha kho attano duppaṭipattiyā tesaṃ pasādaṃ vināseti. Tenāha “pupphadānādīhī”tiādi. Tattha haritvā vā harāpetvā vā pakkositvā vā pakkosāpetvā vā sayaṃ vā upagatānaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.436-437) yassa kassaci attano santakassa pupphassa kulasaṅgahatthāya dānaṃ pupphadānaṃ, taṃ ādi yesaṃ te pupphadānādayo, tehi pupphadānādīhi. Ādisaddena (pārā. 437) phaladānacuṇṇamattikādantakaṭṭhaveḷuvejjikājaṅghapesanikānaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Saddhaṃ vināsentoti tathā akarontesu [V 0.0236] aññesu pesalesu bhikkhūsu appasādaṃ adassanaṃ gamento. Pupphadānādīhi ca tehi katasaṅgahehi aññe pesale tathā akaronte te manussā issanti na allīyantīti so tesaṃ pasādaṃ vināseti nāmāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pāpakā samācārāti buddhappaṭikuṭṭhattā lāmakā samācārā[M 0.0256]. Te pana yasmā kulasaṅgahatthaṃ mālāvaccharopanādayo idha adhippetā, tasmā “mālāvaccharopanādayo”ti vuttaṃ. Ārāmādīnamatthāya pana kappiyavohārādīhi ropāpanādikaṃ vaṭṭati. Tattha mālāvacchanti taruṇapuppharukkhaṃ. Taruṇakā hi puppharukkhāpi pupphagacchāpi “mālāvacchā”tveva vuccanti, tassa ropanaṃ mālāvaccharopanaṃ, taṃ ādi yesaṃ te mālāvaccharopanādayo. Ādisaddena cettha ropāpanasiñcanasiñcāpanaocinanaocināpanaganthanaganthāpanānaṃ gahaṇaṃ.

Since a city is also a type of village, here a city is included by the term “village,” as it is said: “A city too is included within a village.” Or, it is taken by the word “vā” in the sense of an alternative. Thus it is stated. Here, the distinction among these three should be seen: a market town (nigama) is a settlement without surrounding walls and with shops; a city (nagara) is one with surrounding walls and shops; and a village (gāma) is the opposite of these. “He corrupts families” means he causes the four families—those of khattiyas, brāhmaṇas, vessas, and suddas—to become corrupted. And in corrupting, he does not corrupt with impure mud and the like, but rather destroys their faith through his own misconduct. Therefore, it is said: “by giving flowers, etc.” In this context, “giving flowers” (pupphadāna) is the giving of one’s own flowers to anyone—whether having taken them, caused them to be taken, summoned, or caused to be summoned, or even to those who have come on their own (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.436–437)—for the purpose of gaining favor with families. Those things of which this is the beginning are “giving flowers, etc.” (pupphadānādayo), and by these “giving flowers, etc.” By the word “etc.” (Pārā. 437) is meant the giving of fruits, powders, clay, tooth-sticks, bamboo, medical treatments, and messenger services. “Destroys their faith” means that by acting in such a way, he causes people to lose confidence in and aversion towards other virtuous monks who do not act thus. And it should be understood that by the favor done by them through flower-giving and the like, while other virtuous monks do not act thus, those people become jealous and do not associate with them, and thus he destroys their faith. “Evil conduct” means despicable conduct because it is rejected by the Buddha. But since here “planting young flowering trees, etc.” are intended for the purpose of gaining favor with families, therefore it is said: “planting young flowering trees, etc.” However, for the sake of monasteries and the like, practices such as planting and causing to be planted are allowable, using permissible expressions and the like. Here, “mālāvaccha” refers to a young flowering tree. Indeed, young flowering trees and flowering plants are called “mālāvacchā.” Planting them is “mālāvaccharopana.” Those things of which this is the beginning are “mālāvaccharopanādayo.” And by the word “etc.” here is meant planting, causing to be planted, watering, causing to be watered, gathering, causing to be gathered, binding, and causing to be bound.

Mātikāyaṃ dissantīti ye paccakkhato passanti, tehi dissanti. Suyyantīti ye parato suṇanti, tehi sotadvārena sutvā upadhārīyanti. Duṭṭhānīti dūsitāni. Alaṃ te idha vāsenāti tava idha vāsena alaṃ, mā idha tava vāso hotūti attho. Vāraṇattho hi idha alaṃ-saddo. Pabbājanīyakammakatoti codetvā sāretvā āpattiṃ āropetvā “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, ime assajipunabbasukā”tiādinā (pārā. 434) padabhājane vuttāya ñatticatutthakammavācāya katapabbājanīyakammo. Yasmiñca vihāre vasatīti gāmato bahivihāramāha. Neva tasmiṃ gāme…pe… carituṃ labhatīti sacepi gāmo vā nigamo vā dvādasayojanaparamo hoti, tiyojanaparamo ca vihāro hoti, neva tasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā piṇḍāya carituṃ labhati, na vihāre vasituṃ. Tasmiṃ vihāre vasantena sāmantagāmepi piṇḍāya na caritabbaṃ, sāmantavihārepi vasantena tasmiṃ gāme piṇḍāya na caritabbaṃ. Sāmantavihāre vasantena pana sāmantagāme carituṃ vaṭṭati. Āpajjitabbā āpattiyoti kulasaṅgahatthaṃ attano santakadāne dukkaṭaṃ, issaravatāya saṅghasantakadāne thullaccayaṃ, pasayha dāne pārājikanti imā āpattiyo. Mātikāyaṃ “pakkamatā yasmā”ti pabbājanīyakammakatassa vattavasena vuttaṃ. Ādimhi pana pabbājanīyakammavasena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Assajipunabbasuketi assajiñceva punabbasukañca.

“They are seen in the list” means they are seen by those who see them directly. “They are heard” means those who hear from others hear them through the ear-door and take them to heart. “Corrupted” means defiled. “Enough for you to stay here” means “enough with your staying here; may your stay here not happen.” Here, the word “alaṃ” has the sense of prohibition. “One who has been subjected to the act of banishment” means one for whom the act of banishment has been carried out with a motion and three announcements, as stated in the section on word-division (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.434), after having been accused, reminded of the offense, and charged with an offense, beginning with “Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me, these Assaji and Punabbasu…” And “whatever dwelling he resides in” refers to a dwelling outside the village. “He is not allowed to walk for alms in that village…”: Even if the village or town is at most twelve yojanas away, and the dwelling is at most three yojanas away, he is not allowed to walk for alms in that village or town, nor to stay in the dwelling. One staying in that dwelling should not walk for alms even in neighboring villages. One staying in a neighboring dwelling should not walk for alms in that village. However, one staying in a neighboring dwelling is permitted to walk for alms in a neighboring village. “Offenses to be committed” means these offenses: a dukkaṭa offense for giving what belongs to oneself for the purpose of gaining favor with families; a thullaccaya offense for giving what belongs to the Saṅgha with authority; and a pārājika offense entailing expulsion for giving forcibly. In the list, “Let him depart from there” is stated in terms of the proper conduct for one subjected to the act of banishment. But at the beginning, it should be understood in terms of the act of banishment itself. “Assaji and Punabbasu” means Assaji and Punabbasu.

Kuladūsakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Corrupting Families is concluded.

Saṅghādisesanigamanavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Conclusion of the Saṅghādisesa Offenses

Paṭhamāpattikāti [M 0.0257][V 0.0237] avayavena viggaho samudāyo samāsatthoti āha “paṭhamaṃ āpatti etesanti paṭhamāpattikā”ti. Vītikkamanakkhaṇeyevāti vatthuvītikkamanakkhaṇeyeva. Eva-kārena samanubhāsanakammakkhaṇaṃ paṭikkhipati. Ahassa yattako paricchedo yāvatīhaṃ. Tenāha “yattakāni ahānī”ti. Ahānīti ca divasānīti attho.

Regarding `Paṭhamāpattikā`: the analysis is by its components, and the aggregate is the meaning of the compound. Thus it is said: 'They have the first offense, therefore they are `paṭhamāpattikā`.' 'At the very moment of transgression' means at the very moment of transgressing the basis. The particle 'eva' excludes the moment of the formal act of admonishment. `Yāvatīhaṃ` means 'whatever the extent of a day is.' Therefore, it is said: 'as many days.' And `ahāni` means 'days'.

Vatthuvasena vāti asucimocanādivītikkamamattavasena vā. Idanti idaṃ vītikkamaṃ. Nāmamattavasena vā ayaṃ itthannāmā āpattīti “ayaṃ saṅghādiseso nāma āpattī”ti evaṃ vinā vatthuṃ nāmavasena vā. Mattasaddena cettha vatthuṃ paṭikkhipati. Potthakesu pana katthaci “nāmagottavasena vā”ti likhanti, taṃ na sundaraṃ “ayaṃ itthannāmā āpattī”ti vuttattā. Idāni naṃ kassaci na ārocessāmīti sambandho.
