Dhuraṃ nikkhipitvāti ārocane ussāhaṃ ṭhapetvā. Na kevalaṃ vatthunāmavaseneva āpattisaññī hutvā chādentasseva, atha kho yopi evaṃ ajānanto kevalaṃ “āpattiṃ chādemī”ti āpattisaññāya chādeti, tassapi channā hotīti veditabbaṃ. Sace panettha anāpattisaññī vā hoti, aññāpattikkhandhasaññī vā vematiko vā hutvā “na dāni naṃ kassaci ārocessāmī”ti evaṃ chādetukāmova dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpeti, acchannāva hotīti ānetvā yojetabbaṃ. Anāpatti pana āpattisaññāyapi anāpattisaññāyapi chādentena acchāditāva hoti. Lahukaṃ vā “garukā”ti garukaṃ vā “lahukā”ti chādeti, alajjipakkhe tiṭṭhati, āpatti pana acchannā hoti. Garukaṃ “lahukā”ti maññamāno deseti, neva desitā hoti nacchannā.

“According to the basis” means merely by the act of transgressing the basis, such as the emission of semen, etc. “This” refers to this transgression. Or “by mere name,” meaning “this is an offense named so-and-so,” as in “this is an offense called a saṅghādisesa,” thus by name without the basis. Here, the word “matta” (mere) excludes the basis. In some texts, however, it is written as “nāmagottavasena vā” (by name and lineage), but that is not proper because it is said, “this is an offense named so-and-so.” “Now, I will not disclose it to anyone”—this is the connection. “Having abandoned the burden” means having set aside the effort for disclosure. It should be understood that not only for one who, perceiving an offense based on the basis or name alone, conceals it, but also for one who, not knowing thus, simply thinks, “I will conceal the offense,” and conceals it with the perception of an offense—for him too, it is concealed. But if here one has no perception of an offense, or perceives it as belonging to another class of offenses, or is doubtful, and, desiring to conceal it, thinks, “I will not disclose it to anyone now,” and having abandoned the burden, lets the dawn arise—it remains unconcealed. This should be applied accordingly. However, an act that is not an offense remains unconcealed, even if one conceals it with the perception of an offense or without such perception. If one conceals a minor offense as grave or a grave offense as minor, he stands on the side of the shameless, but the offense remains unconcealed. If one, thinking a grave offense is minor, confesses it, it is neither confessed nor concealed.

Pakato sabhāvabhūto attā assāti pakatatto, na kammehi vikatattoti attho. Tenāha “anukkhitto samānasaṃvāsako”ti. Vuttanayenevāti “na dāni naṃ kassaci ārocessāmī”tiādinā vuttaneva nayena. Atha “mayhaṃ saṅghena kammaṃ kata”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) apakatattasaññī hutvā chādeti, acchannāva hoti. Apakatattena pana pakatattasaññinā vā pakatattena apakatattasaññinā vā chāditāpi acchannāva hoti. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

“Pakatatto” means one whose self is in its natural state, not altered by a formal act; this is the meaning. Therefore, it is said: “unexpelled, living in communion.” “By the stated method” means by the method stated beginning with “Now, I will not disclose it to anyone.” Then, if one conceals it, perceiving oneself as not being in a normal state, thinking, “The Saṅgha has performed an act against me” (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 102), it remains unconcealed. However, if an offense is concealed by one who is not in a normal state but perceives himself as being in a normal state, or by one who is in a normal state but perceives himself as not being in a normal state, it remains unconcealed. And this has been stated—

“Āpajjati [M 0.0258] garukaṃ sāvasesaṃ;

Chādeti anādariyaṃ paṭicca;

Na [V 0.0238] bhikkhunī no ca phuseyya vajjaṃ;

Pañhāmesā kusalehi cintitā”ti. (pari. 481);

“He incurs a grave offense with a remainder; he conceals it out of disrespect; he is not a bhikkhunī, nor does he touch upon the fault; this is a question considered by the skilled.” (Pari. 481)

Ayañhi pañho ukkhittakena kathito.

Indeed, this question was stated by one who was expelled.

Dasasu antarāyesu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Sace pana yo bhīrukajātikatāya andhakāre amanussacaṇḍamigabhayena antarāyikasaññī hutvā chādeti, acchannāva hoti. Yassapi pabbatavihāre vasantassa kandaraṃ vā nadiṃ vā atikkamitvā ārocetabbaṃ hoti, antarāmagge ca caṇḍavāḷaamanussādibhayaṃ atthi, magge ajagarā nipajjanti, nadī pūrā hoti, etasmiṃ satiyeva antarāye antarāyikasaññī hutvā chādeti, acchannāva hoti. Antarāyikassa pana antarāyikasaññāya vā anantarāyikasaññāya vā chādayato acchannāva.

What is to be said concerning the ten obstacles has already been stated below. But if someone, being of a fearful nature, perceives an obstacle out of fear of non-human beings or fierce animals in the dark and conceals it, it remains unconcealed. And for one dwelling in a mountain monastery who must cross a ravine or a river to disclose it, and on the way there is fear of fierce beasts, non-human beings, and so on, or pythons lie on the path, or the river is in flood—if, while such an obstacle exists, he perceives it as an obstacle and conceals the offense, it remains unconcealed. Furthermore, for one who has an obstacle, if he conceals it, whether perceiving it as an obstacle or not perceiving it as an obstacle, it remains unconcealed.

Bhikkhunoti sabhāgassa bhikkhuno. Sacassa mukhe appamattako gaṇḍo vā hoti, hanukavāto vā vijjhati, danto vā rujjati, bhikkhā vā mandā laddhā hoti, tāvatakena pana neva vattuṃ na sakkoti, na gantuṃ. Apica kho “na sakkomī”ti saññī hoti, ayaṃ pahu hutvā appahusaññī nāma. Iminā chāditāpi acchāditā. Appahunā pana vattuṃ vā gantuṃ vā asamatthena pahusaññinā vā appahusaññinā vā chāditāpi acchāditāva.

“To a bhikkhu” means to a bhikkhu of the same communion. If he has a small boil on his face, or if he has lockjaw, or if a tooth aches, or if he has received little almsfood, he is not, on that account alone, unable to speak or to go. And yet, he perceives, “I am unable.” This is called one who, being capable, perceives himself as incapable. An offense concealed by such a one remains unconcealed. But an offense concealed by one who is incapable, unable to speak or to go—whether he perceives himself as capable or as incapable—also remains unconcealed.

Idaṃ uttānamevāti idaṃ aṅgadvayaṃ uttānatthameva. Sace pana “chādessāmī”ti dhuranikkhepaṃ katvā purebhatte vā pacchābhatte vā paṭhamayāmādīsu vā lajjidhammaṃ okkamati, antoaruṇeyeva āroceti, ayaṃ chādetukāmo na chādeti nāma.

“This is self-evident” means these two factors are for the sake of clarity. However, if, having laid aside the burden with the thought, “I will conceal it,” whether before the meal, after the meal, or during the first watch of the night and so on, a sense of shame overcomes him, and he discloses it before the dawn has risen, this is called one who desires to conceal but does not conceal.

Yassa pana abhikkhuke ṭhāne vasantassa āpattiṃ āpajjitvā sabhāgassa bhikkhuno āgamanaṃ āgamentassa vā, sabhāgassa santikaṃ vā gacchantassa aḍḍhamāsopi māsopi atikkamati, ayaṃ nacchādetukāmo chādeti nāma. Ayampi acchannāva hoti.

But as for one who, dwelling in a place without bhikkhus, commits an offense, and while he is awaiting the arrival of a bhikkhu of the same communion or is going to the presence of a bhikkhu of the same communion, half a month or a month passes by, this is called ‘one who conceals without wishing to conceal.’ This offense of his also remains unconcealed.

Yo [M 0.0259] pana āpannamattova aggiṃ akkantapuriso viya sahasā apakkamitvā sabhāgaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā āvi karoti, ayaṃ nacchādetukāmova na chādeti nāma. Sabhāgamattameva pamāṇanti averisabhāgamattameva pamāṇaṃ. Averisabhāgassa hi santike ārocetabbaṃ. Yo pana visabhāgo hoti sutvā pakāsetukāmo, evarūpassa upajjhāyassapi santike na ārocetabbā. Tattha purebhattaṃ [V 0.0239] āpattiṃ āpanno hotu, pacchābhattaṃ vā divā vā rattiṃ vā, yāva aruṇaṃ na uggacchati, tāva ārocetabbaṃ. Uddhaste aruṇe paṭicchannā hoti, paṭicchādanapaccayā ca dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati. Saṅkhepatoti samāsato. Vitthārato pana samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttoti adhippāyo.

But one who, as soon as he has committed an offense, like a man who has stepped on a fire, quickly departs and goes to a place with bhikkhus of the same communion to disclose it—this is called one who, not wishing to conceal, does not conceal. The standard is simply a bhikkhu of the same communion; the standard is indeed only a non-hostile bhikkhu of the same communion. For it should be declared in the presence of a non-hostile bhikkhu of the same communion. But if there is one of a different communion who, on hearing it, wishes to publicize it, the offense should not be declared even in the presence of one's preceptor if he is of such a kind. In this regard, whether one has committed the offense before the meal or after the meal, by day or by night, it should be declared as long as the dawn has not risen. When the dawn has risen, it becomes concealed, and on account of the concealment, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. “In brief” means concisely. The intention is that this is stated in detail in the Samantapāsādikā.

Akāmā parivatthabbanti appaṭikammakatāya āpattiyā saggamokkhāvaraṇabhāvato anicchantenāpi parivasitabbanti attho. Tenāha “na kāmenā”tiādi. Parivāsaṃ samādāyāti parivāsavattaṃ saṅghamajjhe samādiyitvā. Yadipi catubbidho parivāso appaṭicchannaparivāso, paṭicchannaparivāso, suddhantaparivāso, samodhānaparivāsoti, tathāpi appaṭicchannaparivāso idha na adhippetoti āha “tattha paṭicchanna…pe… tividho parivāso”ti. Tatthāti tasmiṃ vākye. Paṭicchannāya āpattiyā sati dātabbo parivāso paṭicchannavisayatāya paṭicchannaparivāso. Suddhantato paṭṭhāya dātabbo parivāso suddhantaparivāso. Samodahitvā dātabbo parivāso samodhānaparivāso.

“They undergo probation unwillingly” means that one must undergo probation even if one does not wish to, because an offense for which amends have not been made is an obstruction to heaven and liberation; this is the meaning. Therefore he said: “not by desire,” and so on. “Having undertaken probation” means having undertaken the probationary duties in the midst of the Saṅgha. Although probation is of four kinds—unconcealed probation, concealed probation, probation-until-purity, and combined probation—nevertheless, since unconcealed probation is not intended here, he said: “there, concealed… probation is threefold.” “There” means in that statement. Probation to be given when there is a concealed offense is ‘concealed probation’ because its domain is what is concealed. Probation to be given starting from the end of a pure period is ‘probation-until-purity.’ Probation to be given after aggregating is ‘combined probation.’

Idāni te tividheyeva parivāse sarūpato dassetuṃ “tatthā”tiādimāha. Hīti yasmā. Ekāhaṃ paṭicchannā ekāhappaṭicchannā. Vuttanayenāti “āpatti ca hotī”tiādinā vuttena nayena. Ekāhappaṭicchannanti ettha itisaddo “iti vā, iti evarūpā visūkadassanā paṭivirato”tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.13, 197) viya ādiattho. Tena “sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavisaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yācāmī”ti imaṃ pāḷisesaṃ (cūḷava. 102) saṅgaṇhāti. Evaṃ parivāsaṃ yācāpetvāti evaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ yācāpetvā. Khandhake āgatanayenāti samuccayakkhandhake (cūḷava. 97 ādayo) āgatanayena. Tatoti pakkhato [M 0.0260] paṭṭhāya. Atirekapakkhappaṭicchannanti pakkhassa atireko atirekapakkho, taṃ paṭicchannanti attho. Tatoti tiṃsatimadivasato paṭṭhāya. Māsappaṭicchannanti sattānaṃ āyuṃ minanto viya siyati antaṃ karotīti māso, tiṃsarattindivo, taṃ paṭicchannanti attho. Saṃvacchare puṇṇeti taṃ taṃ sattaṃ, dhammappavattiñca saṅgamma vadanto viya sarati pavattatīti saṃvaccharo, dvādasa māsā, tasmiṃ paripuṇṇe.

Now, to show the nature of those three kinds of probation, he says, 'there,' etc. `Hi` means 'because.' 'Concealed for one day' is `ekāhappaṭicchannā`. `By the stated method` means by the method stated with 'and it is an offense,' etc. Here in `ekāhappaṭicchannanti`, the word `iti` has the sense of 'etc.,' as in 'or thus, he abstains from such shows,' etc. (Dī. Ni. 1.13, 197). Thereby it includes the rest of the text: 'So I, venerable sir, request the Sangha for one day of probation for one intentional offense of emission of semen, concealed for one day' (Cūḷava. 102). `Having had him request probation thus` means having had him request it up to the third time. `By the method that has come down in the Khandhaka` means by the method that has come down in the Samuccayakkhandhaka (Cūḷava. 97ff.). `From that` means starting from the fortnight. `Concealed for more than a fortnight` means an excess of a fortnight is `atirekapakkho`; the meaning is concealing that. `From that` means starting from the thirtieth day. `Concealed for a month` means concealing for a month, which is thirty days and nights. `When a year is complete`: a year is twelve months; when that is complete.

Vatthukittanavasena vāti nāmena saha vatthukittanavasena vāti attho. Teneva hi upari “nāmamattavasena vā”ti mattaggahaṇaṃ katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nāmamattavasenāti vatthukittanaṃ vinā kevalaṃ nāmasseva vasena. Tasmāti yasmā duvidhe nāme “āpattī”ti sabbasādhāraṇaṃ nāmaṃ, tasmā[V 0.0240]. Sukkavissaṭṭhīti sukkavissaṭṭhi nāmāyaṃ. Itisaddo hettha vacanīyatthaṃ nidasseti. Nidassanamattañcetaṃ “sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti kāyasaṃsaggādīnampi vatthuādibhāvena icchitabbattā. Vatthu ceva gottañcāti vītikkamattā vatthu ceva anaññasādhāraṇattā gottañca. Gaṃ tāyatīti gottaṃ, sajātito aññattha kāyasaṃsaggādīsu gantuṃ adatvā buddhiṃ, vacanañca rakkhatīti attho. Saṅghādisesoti saṅghādiseso nāmāyaṃ. Ettha pana itisaddo vacanavacanīyasamudāyaṃ nidasseti. Tenāha “nāmañceva āpatti cā”ti, sajātisādhāraṇanāmattā nāmañceva tena tena vītikkamenāpajjitabbattā āpatti cāti attho. Idampi nidassanamattameva “āpattiyo”ti imassāpi nāmādibhāvena icchitabbattā. Itisaddo vā ādiattho. Evañca katvā “kāyasaṃsaggantiādivacanenāpī”tiādikampi samatthitaṃ hoti.

`Or by way of mentioning the ground` means by way of mentioning the ground together with the name. It should be understood that for this very reason the word 'merely' was used above in the phrase 'or merely by way of the name.' `Merely by way of the name` means solely by way of the name, without mentioning the ground. `Therefore` means: because of the two kinds of names, 'offense' is the general name, therefore... `Emission of semen`: this is the name 'emission of semen.' Here the word `iti` indicates the thing to be expressed. And this is just an example, for 'emission of semen' is intended to include bodily contact and so on as grounds. `Both ground and clan`: it is the 'ground' because it is a transgression, and it is the 'clan' because it is not common to others. `Gotta` (clan) protects one's going; the meaning is that it guards one's mind and speech, not allowing them to go elsewhere to bodily contact and so on, outside of its own kind. `Saṅghādisesa`: this is the name 'Saṅghādisesa.' But here the word `iti` indicates the combination of the expression and the thing expressed. Therefore he said, `both the name and the offense.` The meaning is: it is the 'name' because it is a name common to its class, and it is the 'offense' because it is to be incurred by this or that transgression. This too is just an example, for 'offenses' is also intended to be by way of name, etc. Or the word `iti` has the sense of 'etc.' And having taken it thus, statements such as 'by the word "bodily contact," etc.' are also accounted for.

Tayidaṃ kammavācāya kena vacanena gahitanti anuyogaṃ sandhāya “tatthā”tiādimāha. “Āpattī”ti sabbasādhāraṇanāmattā, vītikkamena āpajjitabbattā ca nāmañceva āpatti ca hotīti āha “āpattiyoti vacanenāpī”ti. Tasmāti yasmā idaṃ parivāsādivinayakammaṃ vatthuvasena, gottavasena, nāmavasena, āpattivasena ca kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva, tasmā. Etesūti vatthuādīsu, sukkavissaṭṭhiādīsu vā. Vattaṃ samādātabbanti yathāvuttesu dvīsu padesu ekenapi samādātabbaṃ. Dvīhi pana susamādinnaṃyeva. Teneva vakkhati “samādānepi eseva nayo”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā).

With reference to the question, 'By what word in the formal act is this taken?' he says, 'there,' etc. `Offense`: because it is a name common to all and because it is to be incurred by transgression, it is both a name and an offense; thus he says, 'also by the word "offense".' `Therefore` means: because this Vinaya procedure of probation, etc., may indeed be performed by way of the ground, the clan, the name, or the offense, therefore... `Among these` means among the ground, etc., or among cases of emission of semen, etc. `The observance should be undertaken`: it should be undertaken by at least one of the two ways mentioned. But when undertaken by both, it is very well undertaken. For this very reason, it will be said: 'In the undertaking, too, this is the method' (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Nidānavannanā).

Ārocetvāti [M 0.0261] –

`Having announced`:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ ekāhappaṭicchannaṃ, sohaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ yāciṃ, tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā ekāhappaṭicchannāya ekāhaparivāsaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ parivasāmi, vedayāmahaṃ, bhante, ‘vedayatī’ti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) –

'Venerable sir, I committed one offense, an intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. I requested the Sangha for one day's probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. The Sangha granted me one day's probation for that one offense of intentional emission of semen, concealed for one day. I am now undergoing probation. I make it known, venerable sir. May the Sangha remember me as one who is making it known.' (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102)

Evamādinā taṃ taṃ yojanānurūpaṃ ārocetvā. Imañca panatthaṃ gahetvā yāya kāyaci bhāsāya ārocetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102). “Puna āgatāgatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocentenā”ti idaṃ āgantukaṃ bhikkhuṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ettha ca ekassa ārocentena avasāne [V 0.0241] “vedayatīti maṃ āyasmā dhāretu”, dvinnaṃ “āyasmantā dhārentu”, tiṇṇaṃ “āyasmanto dhārentū”ti vattabbaṃ. Vattabhedañca ratticchedañca akatvāti “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sāditabbaṃ pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccupaṭṭhāna”ntiādinā (cūḷava. 75) pārivāsikakkhandhake yāni catunavuti vattāni vuttāni, tesaṃ bhedañca, yo ca “tayo kho, upāli, pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā sahavāso vippavāso anārocanā”ti (cūḷava. 83) ratticchedo vutto, tañca akatvā.

...having announced in this way, etc., in accordance with the particular application. And having grasped this meaning, it is indeed permissible to announce it in any language whatsoever (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102). The statement 'by one who announces to the bhikkhus who come again and again' is said with reference to an incoming bhikkhu. Here, when announcing to one bhikkhu, at the end one should say: 'May the venerable one remember me as one who is making it known.' To two: 'May you, venerable sirs, remember me as one who is making it known.' To three or more: 'May you, venerable sirs, remember me as one who is making it known.' `And without breaking the observances or interrupting the nights` means: without breaking the ninety-four observances that are stated in the Pārivāsikakkhandhaka with the words, 'Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu on probation should not consent to a salutation or being attended upon by bhikkhus in good standing,' etc. (Cūḷavagga 75), and without committing an interruption of the nights, of which it is said: 'Upāli, there are these three interruptions of the nights for a bhikkhu on probation: dwelling together, dwelling apart, and not announcing' (Cūḷavagga 83).

Ayaṃ hettha vinicchayo – sace (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76) āgantukā muhuttaṃ vissamitvā vā avissamitvā eva vā vihāramajjhena gacchanti, tesampi ārocetabbaṃ. Sace tassa ajānantasseva gacchanti, ayañca gatakāle jānāti, gantvā ārocetabbaṃ. Sampāpuṇituṃ asakkontassa ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ. Yepi antovihāraṃ appavisitvā upacārasīmaṃ okkamitvā gacchanti, ayañca nesaṃ chattasaddaṃ vā ukkāsitasaddaṃ vā khipitasaddaṃ vā sutvāva āgantukabhāvaṃ jānāti, gantvā ārocetabbaṃ. Gatakāle jānantenāpi anubandhitvā ārocetabbameva. Sampāpuṇituṃ asakkontassa ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ. Yopi rattiṃyeva āgantvā rattiṃyeva gacchati, sopissa ratticchedaṃ karoti. Aññātattā [M 0.0262] pana vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ natthi. Sace ajānitvāva abbhānaṃ karoti, akatameva hotīti kurundiyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76) vuttaṃ. Tasmā adhikā rattiyo gahetvā kātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ apaṇṇakappaṭipadā.

Here is the decision in this matter: If (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 76) visiting bhikkhus, whether they have rested for a moment or not, pass through the middle of the monastery, they should be informed. If they pass through without one knowing, and one becomes aware of it after they have departed, one should go and inform them. If one is unable to reach them, there is only a forfeiture of the night, and no dukkaṭa offense for breaking the observance. Even those who do not enter the inner monastery but step into the boundary area and leave—if one hears the sound of their umbrella, their cough, or their spitting and thereby knows they are visiting bhikkhus—one should go and inform them. Even if one becomes aware after they have departed, one should follow and inform them. If one is unable to reach them, there is only a forfeiture of the night, and no dukkaṭa offense for breaking the observance. If someone arrives at night and departs at night, they cause a forfeiture of the night for him. But because of not knowing, there is no dukkaṭa offense for breaking the observance. If one performs the reinstatement without knowing, it is as if it was not done—as stated in the Kurundī (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 76). Therefore, one should act by taking the extra nights. This is the faultless procedure.

Nadiādīsu nāvāya gacchantampi paratīre ṭhitampi ākāse gacchantampi pabbatatalaaraññādīsu dūre ṭhitampi bhikkhuṃ disvā sace “bhikkhū”ti vavatthānaṃ atthi, nāvādīhi vā gantvā, mahāsaddaṃ katvā vā vegena anubandhitvā vā ārocetabbaṃ, anārocentassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhedadukkaṭañca. Sace vāyamantopi sampāpuṇituṃ vā sāvetuṃ vā na sakkoti, ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ.

If one sees a bhikkhu traveling by boat on rivers, etc., standing on the opposite shore, traveling through the sky, or staying far away in mountainous regions, forests, etc., and if there is an ascertainment 'a bhikkhu,' then one should inform him, whether by going by boat, etc., making a loud noise, or quickly following after him. For one who does not inform him, there is a forfeiture of the night and an offense of violating the observance. But if, even while striving, one is not able to reach him or make him hear, there is only a forfeiture of the night, not an offense of violating the observance.

Aññaṃ kañci vihāraṃ gatenapi bhikkhūnaṃ ārocetabbameva (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76). Sace sabbe ekaṭṭhāne ṭhite passati, ekaṭṭhāne ṭhiteneva ārocetabbaṃ. Atha rukkhamūlādīsu visuṃ visuṃ ṭhitā honti, tattha tattha gantvā ārocetabbaṃ. Sañcicca anārocentassa ratticchedo ca hoti, vattabhede ca dukkaṭaṃ. Atha vicinanto ekacce na passati, ratticchedova hoti[V 0.0242], na ca vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ. Sañcicca anārocentassa pana ratticchedo ceva hoti, vattabhede ca dukkaṭaṃ.

Even having gone to another monastery, it must be announced to the monks (Cūḷavagga, Aṭṭha. 76). If he sees all staying in one place, he should announce it while staying in that one place. But if they are staying separately at the roots of trees and so on, he must go to each place and announce it. For one who intentionally does not announce it, there is a forfeiture of the night and also a `dukkaṭa` offense for breaking the observance. However, if while searching he does not see some, there is only a forfeiture of the night, but no `dukkaṭa` offense for breaking the observance. But for one who intentionally does not announce it, there is both a forfeiture of the night and a `dukkaṭa` offense for breaking the observance.

Tatthevāti māḷakasīmāyameva. Māḷakato pana bhikkhūsu nikkhantesu ekassapi santike nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97). Māḷakato nikkhamitvā satiṃ paṭilabhantena saha gacchantassa santike nikkhipitabbaṃ. Tenāha “ekapuggalassa vā santike”ti. Sace sopi pakkanto, aññassa yassa māḷake nārocitaṃ, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pakatattaṭṭhāneti saṅghakammānaṃ arahaṭṭhāne. Dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvāti (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.97) bhikkhūnaṃ sajjhāyanasaddasavanūpacāravijahanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Mahāmaggato okkammāti maggappaṭipannabhikkhūnaṃ upacāravijahanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Gumbena vā vatiyā vā paṭicchannaṭṭhāneti dassanūpacāravijahanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetabbanti vuttanayeneva vattaṃ samādiyitvā parivāso ārocetabbo. “Ārocetabba”nti pana sāmaññena vuttaṃ. Ārocentena ca sace navakataro hoti, “āvuso”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace vuḍḍhataro, “bhante”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace añño koci bhikkhu kenacideva karaṇīyena taṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati. Sace [M 0.0263] esa naṃ passati, saddaṃ vā tassa suṇāti, ārocetabbaṃ. Anārocentassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhedo ca. Tenāha “yampi aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ passati, tassāpi ārocetabbamevā”ti. Atha dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ okkamitvā ajānantasseva gacchati, ratticchedo hotiyeva, vattabhedo pana natthi. Uṭṭhiteti uggate. Yaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ bhikkhunti vihārato nikkhamantaṃ vā āgantukaṃ vā sabbapaṭhamaṃ yaṃ aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ passati. Tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbanti anārocentassa dukkaṭaṃ siyā, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na tu ratticchedaṃ sandhāya. Itarathā hi “vihārasīmāpariyāpannānaṃ sabbesaṃ ārocetvā”ti vadeyya. Yāva rattiyo pūrentīti yattakā rattiyo āpatti paṭicchannā hoti, tattakā rattiyo yāva pūrenti, tāva parivatthabbaṃ. Samantapāsādikāyaṃ pana “evaṃ yattakāni divasāni āpatti paṭicchannā hoti, tattakāni, tato adhikatarāni vā kukkuccavinodanatthāya parivasitvā”ti vuttaṃ. Vitthāroti papañco.

There, indeed: within the boundary of the Māḷaka. However, when the monks have left the Māḷaka, it is permissible to place it in the presence of even one monk (Cūḷavagga, Aṭṭha. 97). Having left the Māḷaka and regained mindfulness, it should be placed in the presence of one who is going along with him. Therefore, it is said, 'in the presence of one individual.' If that one has also departed, it should be announced to another to whom it was not announced in the Māḷaka, and then placed. 'In a proper place' means in a place suitable for acts of the Saṅgha. 'Having gone beyond two stone-throws' (Sāratthadīpanī, Cūḷavagga 3.97) is said for the purpose of leaving the range of the sound of the monks' recitation. 'Turning aside from the great road' is said for the purpose of leaving the range of monks walking on the path. 'In a place concealed by a bush or a fence' is said for the purpose of leaving the range of sight. 'Having undertaken the observance, it should be announced' means that having undertaken the observance in the prescribed manner, the probation should be announced. But 'it should be announced' is said generally. When announcing, if the other is more junior, one should say, 'āvuso.' If he is more senior, one should say, 'bhante.' If some other monk comes to that place for some reason, and if one sees him or hears his sound, it should be announced. For one who does not announce it, there is a forfeiture of the night and a breaking of the observance. Therefore, it is said, 'whomever other monk one sees, it must be announced to him as well.' But if one enters the twelve-cubit vicinity and the other passes by without knowing, there is indeed a forfeiture of the night, but there is no breaking of the observance. 'Risen' means arisen. 'Whichever monk first' refers to whichever other monk one sees first, whether he is leaving the monastery or is a newcomer. The statement 'it should be placed after announcing to him' is said in reference to the `dukkaṭa` offense that would be incurred by one who does not announce, not in reference to the forfeiture of the night. Otherwise, it would have been said, 'having announced to all who are included within the monastery boundary.' 'Until the nights are completed' means that for as many nights as the offense was concealed, one must live on probation for that many nights until they are completed. However, in the Samantapāsādikā, it is said: 'Thus, for as many days as the offense was concealed, or for even more for the sake of dispelling remorse, one should live on probation.' 'Elaboration' means proliferation.

Itaresu pana dvīsūti suddhantaparivāso, samodhānaparivāsoti dvinnaṃ majjhe. Khandhaketi samuccayakkhandhake (cūḷava. 156 ādayo). Cūḷasuddhanto mahāsuddhantoti ettha yo upasampadato (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 242) paṭṭhāya anulomakkamena vā ārocitadivasato paṭṭhāya paṭilomakkamena vā “asukañca asukañca divasaṃ vā pakkhaṃ vā māsaṃ vā saṃvaccharaṃ vā tava suddhabhāvaṃ jānāsī”ti pucchiyamāno “āma, bhante, jānāmi[V 0.0243], ettakaṃ nāma kālaṃ ahaṃ suddho”ti vadati, tassa dinno suddhantaparivāso “cūḷasuddhanto”ti vuccati.

But among the other two—that is, `suddhantaparivāsa` and `samodhānaparivāsa`—it is between these two. 'In the Khandhaka' refers to the Samuccayakkhandhaka (beginning with Cūḷavagga 156). Regarding 'cūḷasuddhanta' and 'mahāsuddhanta': herein, one who, starting from his higher ordination (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 102; Vinayasaṅgaha Aṭṭha. 242) in forward order, or starting from the day of announcement in reverse order, when asked, 'Do you know your state of purity on such and such a day, fortnight, month, or year?' replies, 'Yes, venerable sir, I know; I have been pure for such and such a time'—the `suddhantaparivāsa` given to him is called 'cūḷasuddhanta.'

Taṃ gahetvā parivasantena yattakaṃ kālaṃ attano suddhabhāvaṃ jānāti, tattakaṃ apanetvā avasesaṃ māsaṃ vā dvemāsaṃ vā parivasitabbaṃ. Sace “māsamattaṃ asuddhomhī”ti sallakkhetvā parivāsaṃ aggahesi, parivasanto ca puna aññaṃ māsaṃ sarati, tampi māsaṃ parivasitabbameva, puna parivāsadānakiccaṃ natthi. Atha “dvemāsaṃ asuddhomhī”ti sallakkhetvā aggahesi, parivasanto ca “māsamattamevāhaṃ asuddhomhī”ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ karoti, māsameva parivasitabbaṃ, puna parivāsadānakiccaṃ natthi. Ayañhi suddhantaparivāso uddhampi ārohati, heṭṭhāpi orohati, idamassa lakkhaṇaṃ.

Having undertaken that, one living on probation should deduct the period for which he knows his own purity, and live on probation for the remaining month or two months. If, having considered, 'I am impure for about a month,' he undertook probation, and while on probation he remembers another month, that month too must be lived on probation; there is no need for a further granting of probation. But if, having considered, 'I am impure for two months,' he undertook it, and while on probation he concludes, 'I was impure for only about a month,' he should live on probation for only a month; there is no need for a further granting of probation. For this probation until purity both ascends upwards and descends downwards—this is its characteristic.

Yo [M 0.0264] pana yathāvuttena anulomappaṭilomavasena pucchiyamānopi rattipariyantaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) na jānāti nassarati, rattipariyante vematiko vā hoti, tassa dinno suddhantaparivāso “mahāsuddhanto”ti vuccati. Taṃ gahetvā gahitadivasato yāva upasampadadivaso, tāva rattiyo gaṇetvā parivasitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ uddhaṃ nārohati, heṭṭhā pana orohati. Tasmā sace parivasanto rattiparicchede sanniṭṭhānaṃ karoti “māso vā saṃvaccharo vā mayhaṃ āpannassā”ti, māsaṃ vā saṃvaccharaṃ vā parivasitabbaṃ. Ettha ca kiñcāpi “ettakaṃ kālaṃ ahaṃ suddho”ti vadantassa cūḷasuddhanto dīyati, tathāpi niyameneva jānanābhāvā “duvidhopi cesa…pe… dātabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Tassa dānavidhi khandhake āgatoti tassa duvidhassāpi suddhantassa dānavidhi “tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā…pe… evamassa vacanīyo”tiādinā samuccayakkhandhake (cūḷava. 156) āgato. Tasmā tattha vuttanayeneva veditabboti adhippāyo. Esa nayo vinicchayakathā pana vitthārato samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttāti etthāpi.

But one who, even when questioned in the aforesaid forward and backward manner, does not know or does not remember the extent of the nights (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 102), or is uncertain about the extent of the nights—the `suddhantaparivāsa` given to him is called 'mahāsuddhanta.' Having undertaken that, he must count the nights from the day it was undertaken back to the day of his higher ordination and live on probation for that long. This does not ascend upwards, but it does descend downwards. Therefore, if while living on probation he determines the number of nights, thinking, 'It has been a month or a year since my offense,' he should live on probation for a month or a year. And here, although the `cūḷasuddhanta` is given to one who says, 'I was pure for this long,' nevertheless, because of the definite lack of knowledge, it is said, 'this, being of two kinds... should be given.' The procedure for giving it is found in the Khandhaka: thus, the procedure for giving both kinds of `suddhanta` is found in the Samuccayakkhandhaka (Cūḷavagga 156), beginning with: 'Then, monks, that monk should approach the Saṅgha... and this should be said to him...' Therefore, the meaning is that it should be understood according to the method stated there. This is the method; but the detailed discussion for determining this is stated in the Samantapāsādikā, and so too here.

Odhunitvā avadhuya pahāya samodhāno odhānasamodhāno. Cirappaṭicchannānaṃ agghena samodhāno agghasamodhāno. Missakānaṃ samodhāno missakasamodhāno. Idāni taṃ tividhampi samodhānaparivāsaṃ saṅkhepato dassetuṃ “tatthā”tiādimāha. Antarāpattiṃ āpajjitvā paṭicchādentassāti yo parivāsaṃ gahetvā anikkhittavatto hutvā parivasanto apariniṭṭhiteyeva parivāse antarā vemajjhe saṅghādisesāpattiṃ āpajjitvā paṭicchādeti, tassa. Parivutthadivaseti lakkhaṇavacanametaṃ, tena “mānattaciṇṇadivase cā”tipi vuttameva hoti. Makkhetvāti ñatticatutthena [V 0.0244] kammena mūlāya paṭikassanavasena makkhetvā. Samodahitvāti mūlāpattiṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā, pakkhipitvāti attho. Dātabbaparivāsoti “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”tiādinā ñatticatutthena kammena dātabbaparivāso. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yo paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivāsaṃ gahetvā parivasanto (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 243) vā mānattāraho vā mānattaṃ caranto vā abbhānāraho vā anikkhittavatto aññaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā purimāpattiyā samā vā ūnatarā vā rattiyo [M 0.0265] paṭicchādeti, tassa mūlāya paṭikassanena te parivutthadivase ca mānattaciṇṇadivase ca sabbe odhunitvā adivase katvā pacchā āpannāpattiṃ mūlāpattiyaṃ samodhāya parivāso dātabboti.

Having swept away, having shaken off, having abandoned, the combination is the covering-combination. The combination by value for things long concealed is the value-combination. The combination of mixed things is the mixed-combination. Now, to briefly present that threefold probation with combination, he says, beginning with ‘In that case,’ and so on. For one who, having committed an intermediate offense, conceals it—that is, for one who, having undertaken probation, and while remaining without having relinquished the duties, and while undergoing probation, before the probation is completed, commits and conceals a Saṅghādisesa offense in the interim—for him. ‘On the day the probation is completed’—this is a term indicating a characteristic. Hence, it is also said, ‘And on the day the penance is completed.’ ‘Having annulled’—having annulled by means of a four-fold formal act of motion, in the manner of sending back to the root. ‘Having combined’—having placed it at the place of the root offense, meaning having inserted it. ‘Probation to be given’—the probation to be given by a four-fold formal act of motion, beginning with, ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me.’ This is what is meant: Whoever, having taken probation for a concealed offense, while undergoing probation (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102; Vinaya Saṅghādisesa Aṭṭhakathā 243), or being eligible for penance, or undergoing penance, or being eligible for rehabilitation, while remaining without having relinquished the duties, commits another offense and conceals it for the same or fewer nights as the original offense—for him, by sending him back to the root, all those days spent on probation and the days of penance must be swept away, treated as non-days, and afterward, the newly committed offense must be combined with the root offense, and probation must be given.

Sace pana antarāpatti mūlāpattito atirekappaṭicchannā hoti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102), taṃ mūlāpattiṃ katvā tattha itaraṃ samodhāya parivāso dātabbo. Sace pana antarāpatti appaṭicchannā hoti, mūlāya paṭikassanaṃ akatvā pubbe gahitaparivāseneva parivasitabbaṃ.

But if the intermediate offense is concealed for a longer period than the root offense (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102), that root offense should be made the basis, and the other combined with it, and probation should be given. However, if the intermediate offense is unconcealed, without sending back to the root, one should undergo probation with the probation previously undertaken.

Yā ekā vā…pe… sabbacirappaṭicchannāyoti yā ekā vā āpatti sabbacirappaṭicchannā, yā dve vā tisso vā sambahulā vā āpattiyo sabbacirappaṭicchannāyoti attho. Tāsanti sabbacirappaṭicchannānaṃ āpattīnaṃ. Dānavidhi panassa khandhake vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

‘One that is... and so on... completely concealed for a long time’ means one offense that is completely concealed for a long time, or two or three or numerous offenses that are completely concealed for a long time—this is the meaning. ‘Those’ refers to the offenses that are completely concealed for a long time. Its procedure for giving, however, should be understood in the way stated in the Khandhaka.

Yassa pana sataṃ āpattiyo dasāhapaṭicchannā, aparampi sataṃ āpattiyo dasāhapaṭicchannā, aparampi sataṃ āpattiyo dasāhapaṭicchannāti evaṃ dasakkhattuṃ katvā āpattisahassaṃ divasasatapaṭicchannaṃ hoti, tena kiṃ kātabbanti? Sabbaṃ samodahitvā dasa divase parivasitabbaṃ. Evaṃ ekeneva dasāhena divasasatampi parivasitameva hoti. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

But if one has a hundred offenses concealed for ten days, and another hundred offenses concealed for ten days, and yet another hundred offenses concealed for ten days—thus doing this ten times, so that a thousand offenses are concealed for a hundred days—what should be done then? All should be combined, and one should undergo probation for ten days. Thus, even a hundred days of probation is undertaken with just one ten-day period. And this has also been said:

“Dasasataṃ rattisataṃ, āpattiyo chādayitvāna;

Dasa rattiyo vasitvāna, mucceyya pārivāsiko”ti. (pari. 477);

“Having concealed a thousand offenses for a hundred nights; having dwelt for ten nights, one on probation should be released.” (Pari. 477)

Ayaṃ agghasamodhāno nāma.

This is called the value-combination.

Idāni [V 0.0245] missakasamodhānaṃ niddisituṃ “missakasamodhāno nāmā”tiādimāha. Tatrāyaṃ nayo –

Now, to explain the mixed combination, he says, beginning with ‘The mixed combination is called.’ Herein, this is the method:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ, ekaṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ, ekaṃ duṭṭhullavācaṃ, ekaṃ attakāmaṃ, ekaṃ sañcarittaṃ, ekaṃ kuṭikārakaṃ, ekaṃ vihārakārakaṃ, ekaṃ duṭṭhadosaṃ, ekaṃ aññabhāgiyaṃ, ekaṃ saṅghabhedaṃ, ekaṃ bhedānuvattakaṃ, ekaṃ dubbacaṃ, ekaṃ kuladūsakaṃ, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānaparivāsaṃ yācāmī”ti –

“Venerable sirs, I have committed several Saṅghādisesa offenses: one emission of semen, one bodily contact, one lewd speech, one procuring for oneself, one acting as a go-between, one building a hut, one building a dwelling, one false accusation, one siding with an opponent, one causing schism in the Saṅgha, one following a schismatic, one being difficult to speak to, one corrupting families. Venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for combined probation for these offenses.”

Tikkhattuṃ [M 0.0266] yācāpetvā tadanurūpāya kammavācāya parivāso dātabbo. Ettha ca “saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ nānāvatthukāyo”tipi “saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji”ntipi evaṃ pubbe vuttanayena vatthuvasenapi gottavasenapi nāmavasenapi āpattivasenapi yojetvā kammavācaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭhatiyevāti. Ayaṃ missakasamodhāno. Sabbaparivāsakammavācāvasāne pana nikkhittānikkhittavattādikathā purimanayeneva veditabbā. Tividhepi samodhānaparivāse atthamattasseva vuttattā, vinicchayādīnaṃ vā anāmaṭṭhattā “ayaṃ tividhepi samodhānaparivāse saṅkhepakathā”ti vuttaṃ. Mahāvisayattā samodhānavicāraṇāya sā niravasesā kuto laddhabbāti āha “vitthāro”tiādi.

Having caused him to request three times, probation should be granted with a corresponding formal act. And here, whether one says, ‘I have committed Saṅghādisesa offenses with various grounds,’ or ‘I have committed Saṅghādisesa offenses,’ it is indeed fitting to formulate the formal act by combining it in the previously stated manner, whether by way of the ground, or by way of the lineage, or by way of the name, or by way of the offense. This is the mixed combination. At the conclusion of all formal acts for probation, however, the discussion concerning the relinquished and un-relinquished duties, etc., should be understood in the former manner. Since only the meaning itself is stated in the threefold combined probation, and because the adjudication, etc., are not touched upon, it is said, ‘This is the summary account for the threefold combined probation.’ Due to the extensive subject matter, from where is a complete investigation of the combination to be obtained? Hence, he says, ‘The detailed account,’ and so on.

Chārattanti rā saddo tīyati chijjati etthāti ratti, sattānaṃ saddassa vūpasamanakāloti attho, cha rattiyo samāhaṭā, channaṃ rattīnaṃ vā samāhāro charattaṃ, charattameva chārattaṃ, avayavabyatirekena samudāyassābhāvato cha rattiyoti attho vutto.

‘Chāratta’—the word ‘rā’ means to diminish or cease, hence ‘ratti’ (night) is where sound diminishes or ceases; meaning, it is the time when the sounds of beings subside. Six nights are gathered together, or the collection of six nights is ‘charatta’; ‘charatta’ itself is ‘chāratta’. Because there is no aggregate apart from its parts, the meaning ‘six nights’ is stated.

Parivāsaṃ adatvā mānattameva dātabbanti yasmā āpatti appaṭicchannā, yasmā ca āpannabhāveneva mānattāraho hoti, tasmā parivāsaṃ adatvā kevalaṃ mānattameva dātabbaṃ. Yaṃ paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivutthaparivāsassa dīyati, idaṃ paṭicchannamānattaṃ nāmāti āha “yassa paṭicchannā hotī”tiādi. Idanti paṭicchannamānattaṃ. Idhāti imasmiṃ vākye. Kathaṃ pana tesaṃ dvinnaṃ mānattānaṃ dānavidhi ca vinicchayakathā ca veditabbāti āha “ubhinnampi panā”tiādi.

‘Penance alone should be given without assigning probation’—because the offense is unconcealed, and because one is deserving of penance by the mere fact of having committed the offense, therefore, without assigning probation, penance alone should be given. That which is given for a concealed offense to one who has completed probation is called concealed penance, as he says, beginning with ‘For one whose offense is concealed,’ and so on. This, namely, is concealed penance. ‘Here’ means in this sentence. But how should the procedure for assigning these two types of penance, and the discussion of their determination, be understood? He says, beginning with ‘For both, however,’ and so on.

Ayanti vakkhamānaṃ sandhāyāha. Parivāse vuttappakāraṃ padesanti parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato[V 0.0246], aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā mahāmaggato okkamma gumbena vā vatiyā vā paṭicchannaṭṭhānaṃ. Samādiyitvāti antoaruṇeyeva samādiyitvā. Ārocetvāti –

‘This’ refers to what is about to be said. ‘The place of the kind stated in connection with probation’ means, for an enclosed monastery, from its boundary; for an unenclosed one, from a place suitable for a boundary, having gone beyond two stone-throws and stepped away from the main road to a place concealed by bushes or a thicket. ‘Having undertaken’ means having undertaken within the dawn itself. ‘Having informed’ means:

“Ahaṃ, bhante, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ sañcetanikaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ appaṭicchannaṃ, sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ yāciṃ[M 0.0267], tassa me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā sañcetanikāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā appaṭicchannāya chārattaṃ mānattaṃ adāsi, sohaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vedayāmahaṃ, bhante, vedayatī’ti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”tiādinā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) –

“Venerable sirs, I committed one offense—intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. I, venerable sirs, requested the Saṅgha for six-nights’ penance for that one offense—intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. The Saṅgha granted me six-nights’ penance for that one offense—intentional emission of semen, unconcealed. I am undergoing penance. I declare, venerable sirs; may the Saṅgha remember me as one who declares.” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 97)

Āpattidivasānurūpaṃ ārocetvā. Imañca pana atthaṃ gahetvā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) yāya kāyaci bhāsāya ārocetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Ārocitakālato paṭṭhāya ca ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ ṭhapetvā sesehi sati karaṇīye gantumpi vaṭṭati. Aruṇe uṭṭhite tassa bhikkhussa santike vattaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace sopi kenaci kammena pure aruṇeyeva gacchati, aññaṃ vihārato nikkhantaṃ vā āgantukaṃ vā yaṃ paṭhamaṃ passati, tassa santike ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ayañca yasmā gaṇassa ārocetvā, bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāva vasi, tenassa ūne gaṇe caraṇadoso vā vippavāso vā na hoti. Sace pana kañci na passati, vihāraṃ gantvā yaṃ paṭhamaṃ passati, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ. Tenāha “tato tesu gatesu vā agatesu vā purimanayena paṭipajjitabba”nti.

Having informed according to the number of days of the offense. And having grasped this meaning (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 97), it is indeed fitting to inform in whatever language. And from the time of informing onwards, except for one bhikkhu, it is permissible for the rest to go if there is something to be done. When dawn has arisen, the duty should be entrusted to that bhikkhu. If he too goes for some business before dawn, then one should inform and entrust the duty to the first bhikkhu seen, whether one who has left the monastery or a visitor. And because he informed the Saṅgha, and remained only after considering the presence of the bhikkhus, there is no fault for him of undergoing the practice with an incomplete Saṅgha, nor of separation. But if he does not see anyone, he should go to the monastery and inform the first one he sees, then entrust the duty. Therefore, he says: ‘Then, whether they have gone or not, one should proceed according to the former method.’

Yattha siyāti yassaṃ samānasaṃvāsakasīmāyaṃ vīsatigaṇo bhikkhusaṅgho atthi. Avhātabboti abbhānakammavasena pakkositabbo. Abbhānakammaṃ pana kathanti āha “abbhānakammaṃ panā”tiādi. Pāḷivasenāti “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”tiādinā (cūḷava. 101) pāḷivasena. Vinicchayavasenāti “abbhantehi ca paṭhamaṃ abbhānāraho kātabbo. Ayañhi nikkhittavattattā pakatattaṭṭhāne ṭhito, pakatattassa ca abbhānaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, tasmā vattaṃ samādapetabbo. Vatte samādinne abbhānāraho hoti. Tenāpi vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetvā abbhānaṃ yācitabbaṃ. Anikkhittavattassa pana vattasamānakiccaṃ natthi. So hi chārattātikkameneva abbhānāraho hotī”tiādinā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) vinicchayavasena. Taṃ panetaṃ sabbaṃ parivāsādikammaṃ pāḷivasena (cūḷava. 75) ca aṭṭhakathāvasena (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 75, 97) ca [V 0.0247] suviññeyyattā ativitthārabhayena na vitthārayimha, atthikehi pana tatova gahetabbaṃ. Imassa [M 0.0268] pana kammassa vīsativaggakaraṇīyattā tato ūnatarena kataṃ kuppati. Tenāha “ekenāpi ce…pe… anabbhito”ti. Ayanti ayaṃ yathāvuttā. Sāmīcīti vattaṃ.

Where there may be: where a monastic community of twenty bhikkhus exists within a common residential boundary. Should be summoned: he should be summoned by way of the act of rehabilitation. But how is the act of rehabilitation performed? He says, “But the act of rehabilitation...” and so on. By means of the Pāḷi text: by means of the Pāḷi text, beginning with “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me...” (Cv.V.20.4). By means of the decision: by means of the decision, beginning with “And first, one fit for rehabilitation should be made so. For since he is one who has laid down the observance, he stands in the position of a regular bhikkhu; but it is not fitting to perform rehabilitation for a regular bhikkhu, therefore he should be made to undertake the observance. When he has undertaken the observance, he becomes fit for rehabilitation. Having undertaken the observance and informed the Saṅgha, he should request rehabilitation. But for one who has not laid down the observance, there is no duty similar to undertaking the observance. For he becomes fit for rehabilitation simply by the passing of six nights...” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 97) and so on. This entire procedure, the probation and so forth, is easily understood from the Pāḷi text (Cūḷavagga 75) and the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 75, 97), so we have not elaborated on it for fear of excessive detail; but those who are interested should take it from there. Because this formal act requires a group of twenty, it is invalid if performed with fewer than that. Therefore, he says, “Even by one... not rehabilitated.” This: this, as stated above. Proper conduct: the observance.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the Explanation of the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the Elucidation of Subtle Meanings,

Saṅghādisesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the Explanation of the Saṅghādisesa Rules is concluded.

Aniyatakaṇḍaṃ

The Section on the Indefinite

1. Paṭhamaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Indefinite Training Rule

“Mātugāmenā”ti [M 0.0269][V 0.0248] vatvā puna “ekāyā”ti vuttattā “mātugāmasaṅkhātāya ekāya itthiyā”ti vuttaṃ. Rahoti appakāsaṃ. Appakāsatā ca yo anāpattiṃ karoti, tassa apaccakkhabhāvatoti āha “cakkhussa raho”ti. Nanu “raho nāma cakkhussa raho, sotassa raho. Cakkhussa raho nāma na sakkā hoti akkhiṃ vā nikhaṇiyamāne, bhamukaṃ vā ukkhipiyamāne, sīsaṃ vā ukkhipiyamāne passituṃ. Sotassa raho nāma na sakkā hoti pakatikathā sotu”nti padabhājanapāḷiyaṃ sotassa rahoti āgataṃ, atha kasmā taṃ avatvā “cakkhussa raho”ti ettakameva vuttanti āha “kiñcāpī”tiādi. Iminā pāḷiyaṃ “sotassa raho”ti idaṃ atthuddhāravasena vuttanti dasseti. Atha kathametaṃ viññāyati “cakkhusseva raho idha adhippeto”ti? “Paṭicchanne āsane”ti vacanato “sakkā hoti methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitu”nti (pārā. 445) ca vuttattā. Tenevāha “sacepī”tiādi. “Pihitakavāṭassā”ti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.444-445) iminā paṭicchannabhāvato cakkhussa rahosabbhāvaṃ dasseti. Apihitakavāṭassa (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.444-445) pana dvāre nisinno anāpattiṃ karoti, na kevalaṃ apihitakavāṭassa gabbhassa dvāre nisinnova anāpattiṃ karoti, antodvādasahatthe okāse nisinnopīti veditabbo. Tenāha “yattha pana sakkā daṭṭhu”ntiādi. Yasmā nisīditvā niddāyanto kapimiddhapareto kañci kālaṃ cakkhūni ummīleti, kañci kālaṃ nimīleti, na ca mahāniddaṃ okkamati, tasmā “niddāyantopi anāpattiṃ karotī”ti vuttaṃ. Nipajjitvā niddāyanto pana tādiso na hotīti āha “nipajjitvā niddāyantopi na karotī”ti, anāpattiṃ na karotīti attho. Methunassa mātugāmo dutiyo na hoti. Itthiyo hi aññamaññissā vajjaṃ paṭicchādenti. Teneva vesāliyaṃ (pārā. 76-77) mahāvane dvāraṃ vivaritvā nipanne bhikkhumhi sambahulā itthiyo yāvadatthaṃ [V 0.0249] katvā pakkamiṃsu. Tenāha “itthīnaṃ pana satampi na karotī”ti. Taṃ kammanti ajjhācārakammaṃ. Yasmā nisīditvāva nipajjati, tasmā [M 0.0270] nipajjanampi antokatvā “nisajjaṃ kappeyyā”ti vuttanti dassetuṃ “ettha cā”tiādimāha. Tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ aññatarena kāretabboti nisajjaṃ paṭijānamānassa tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ aññatarasamāyogo hotiyevāti vuttaṃ. Pārājikena, pana saṅghādisesena ca pācittiyena ca tenākārena nisajjaṃ paṭijānamānova kāretabbo. Na appaṭijānamānoti nisajjaṃ appaṭijānamāno tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ aññatarena na kāretabboti. Alajjīpi hi paṭijānamānova āpattiyā kāretabbo. Yāva na paṭijānāti, tāva “neva suddho”ti vā “na asuddho”ti vā vattabbo, vattānusandhinā pana kāretabboti. Vuttañhetaṃ –

Having said “with a woman,” and then again “with one alone,” it is stated “with a single woman, who is counted as a woman.” Secluded means not public. And this non-public nature is due to being out of sight of one whose presence would make it a non-offense; thus it is said, “secluded from the eye.” Now, is it not said in the Pāḷi word-analysis: “Secluded means secluded from the eye, secluded from the ear. Secluded from the eye means one cannot see even if one were to open one's eye, raise one's eyebrow, or lift one's head. Secluded from the ear means one cannot hear ordinary speech”? So why, without mentioning the latter, was only “secluded from the eye” stated? He says, “Although...” and so on. By this he shows that in the Pāḷi, “secluded from the ear” is stated by way of extracting the meaning. Then how is it understood that only “secluded from the eye” is intended here? Because of the text “on a concealed seat” and because it is said, “it is possible to engage in the sexual act.” Therefore he says, “Even if...” and so on. By “of one with a closed door,” he shows the existence of seclusion from the eye due to concealment. But one sitting at the door of a room with an unclosed door makes it a non-offense. It should be understood that not only one sitting at the door of a room with an unclosed door makes it a non-offense, but also one sitting in a space within twelve cubits. Therefore he says, “But where one can be seen...” and so on. Because one who is dozing while sitting, overcome by “monkey-sleep,” for some time opens his eyes and for some time closes them, and does not fall into a deep sleep, therefore it is said, “even one who is dozing makes it a non-offense.” But one who is dozing while lying down is not like that, so he says, “one dozing while lying down does not make it a non-offense,” meaning, he is not a valid witness. A woman is not a valid second person for the sexual act. For women conceal one another's faults. For that reason, in Vesālī, in the Great Wood, when a bhikkhu was lying down having opened the door, many women did as they pleased and departed. Therefore he says, “But even with a hundred women, it is not made a non-offense.” “That act” means the act of transgression. Because one lies down only after sitting, to show that lying down is also included when it says “he should arrange a sitting,” he says “And here...” and so on. “He should be dealt with by one of three things” means that for one who confesses to the sitting, there is necessarily a connection with one of the three things. He who confesses to the sitting in that manner should be dealt with by a Pārājika, a Saṅghādisesa, or a Pācittiya. “Not one who does not confess” means that one who does not confess to the sitting should not be dealt with by one of the three things. For even a shameless person should be dealt with for an offense only if he confesses. As long as he does not confess, he should be addressed as “neither pure” nor “not impure,” but he should be dealt with in accordance with the facts of the case. For it is said—

“Paṭiññā lajjīsu katā, alajjīsu evaṃ na vijjati;

Bahumpi alajjī bhāseyya, vattānusandhitena kāraye”ti. (pari. 359);

“Confession is for the scrupulous; it is not found among the shameless. Though a shameless one may say much, one should deal with him in accordance with the facts of the case.”

Na kevalaṃ tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ aññatarena codanāyameva evaṃ paṭiññāya kāretabbo, atha kho nisajjādinā ākārena saddhiṃ codanāyapīti dassetuṃ “yena vā sā saddheyyavacasā upāsikā vadeyya, tena so bhikkhu kāretabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Tenevāha “nisajjādīsu ākāresū”tiādi. Ettha ca “paṭijānamāno”ti avuttepi adhikārattā “paṭijānamānova tena so bhikkhu kāretabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Tathārūpāya (sārattha. ṭī. 2.444-445) upāsikāya vacane aññathattābhāvato diṭṭhaṃ nāma tathāpi hoti, aññathāpi hotīti dassane aññathattasambhavaṃ dasseti. Anekaṃsikatāya na niyatoti aniyato. Tenāha “tiṇṇaṃ āpattīna”ntiādi.

To show that he should be dealt with on confession not only when charged with one of the three offenses, but also when charged in connection with the manner of sitting and so on, it is said: “Or by whatever a trustworthy laywoman might say, by that the bhikkhu should be dealt with.” Therefore he says, “In the manners of sitting, etc....” and so on. And here, although “confessing” is not stated, because it is the topic under discussion, it is said, “that bhikkhu should be dealt with only when he confesses.” Regarding the statement of such a laywoman, although there is no falsity in her words, in showing that what was seen could be one way or another, he points out the possibility of a different state of affairs. Because it is not definite, it is “undetermined” (aniyata). Therefore he says, “Of the three offenses...” and so on.

Rahonisajjassādena mātugāmassa santikaṃ gantukāmo akkhiṃ añjeti, dukkaṭaṃ. Nivāsanaṃ nivāseti, kāyabandhanaṃ bandhati, cīvaraṃ pārupati, sabbattha payoge payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Gacchati, padavāre padavāre dukkaṭaṃ. Gantvāna nisīdati, dukkaṭameva. Tenāha “methunadhammasannissitakilesasaṅkhātenā”tiādi. Ettha ca rahonisajjassādassa asatipi methunarāgabhāve tappaṭibaddhakilesattā vuttaṃ “methunadhammasannissitakilesasaṅkhātenā”ti. Teneva sannissitaggahaṇaṃ kataṃ. Rahassādenāti “itthannāmāya saddhiṃ raho nisīditvā hasitalapitādikaṃ kareyya”nti uppannaassādahetu[M 0.0271]. Nisajjāya pācittiyaṃ asati upacāragate nipajjitvā aniddāyante anandhe viññupuriseti adhippāyo. Sace sā itthī kenaci karaṇīyena uṭṭhāyuṭṭhāya punappunaṃ [V 0.0250] nisīdati, nisajjāya nisajjāya pācittiyaṃ. Yaṃ sandhāya gato, sā na diṭṭhā, aññā āgantvā nisīdati, assāde uppanne pācittiyaṃ. Sace sambahulā āgacchanti, mātugāmagaṇanāya pācittiyaṃ. Sace uṭṭhāyuṭṭhāya punappunaṃ nisīdanti, nisajjāgaṇanāyapi pācittiyāni. Aniyametvā “diṭṭhadiṭṭhāya saddhiṃ rahassādaṃ kappissāmī”ti gantvā nisinnassāpi āgatāgatānaṃ vasena, punappunaṃ nisajjāya vasena ca vuttanayeneva āpattiyo veditabbā. Vuttappakāre puriseti anandhe viññupurise. Upacāragate satīti dvādasahatthabbhantaragate sati. Sace suddhacittena gantvā nisinnassa santikaṃ āgantvā nisinnāya itthiyā rahassādo uppajjati, evampi anāpatti.

Desiring to go near a woman for the pleasure of sitting in seclusion, if he anoints his eye, it is a dukkaṭa offense. If he puts on his lower robe, fastens his belt, or drapes his outer robe, for each action there is a dukkaṭa offense. As he goes, there is a dukkaṭa offense for every step. Having gone, when he sits down, it is also a dukkaṭa offense. Hence it is said, “by what is designated as a defilement connected with the sexual act,” and so on. And here, even if there is no sexual lust in the pleasure of sitting in seclusion, because it is a defilement connected with that, it is said “by what is designated as a defilement connected with the sexual act.” For this reason the word “connected with” was used. “For the pleasure of seclusion” means because of the pleasure that has arisen from thinking, “I will sit in seclusion with such-and-such a woman and laugh, chat, etc.” The intention is that for sitting it is a pācittiya offense when a discerning man—who is not lying down, not sleeping, and not blind—is not present in the vicinity. If that woman, for some reason, gets up and sits down again and again, there is a pācittiya offense for each and every sitting. If the one for whom he went is not seen, and another woman comes and sits down, it is a pācittiya offense if pleasure arises. If many women come, there is a pācittiya offense for each woman counted. If they get up and sit down again and again, there are also pācittiya offenses for each sitting counted. If he goes without specifying anyone, thinking, “I will arrange for the pleasure of seclusion with whomever I see,” and sits down, offenses should be understood according to the aforementioned method for each one who comes and for each time they sit down again. “The man of the type mentioned” means a discerning man who is not blind. “When he has entered the vicinity” means when he has come within twelve cubits. If he goes with a pure mind and sits down, and pleasure in seclusion arises when a woman comes and sits near him, even so it is a non-offense.

Paṭhamaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the First Indeterminate Rule is concluded.

2. Dutiyaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Indeterminate Rule

Naheva kho pana paṭicchannanti ettha pana yampi bahi parikkhittaṃ anto vivaṭaṃ pariveṇaṅgaṇādi, tampi antogadhanti veditabbaṃ. “Evarūpañhi ṭhānaṃ appaṭicchanneyeva gahita”nti mahāpaccariyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.453) vuttaṃ. Saṅghādisesena vāti kāyasaṃsaggaduṭṭhullobhāsanasaṅkhātena saṅghādisesena vā. Teneva hi padabhājane “sā ce evaṃ vadeyya ‘ayyo, mayā diṭṭho nisinno mātugāmena saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjanto’”tiādi (pārā. 455) vuttaṃ. Idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ duṭṭhullavācāvasena āgataṃ. Duṭṭhullavācañca sutvā taṃ mātugāmopi na paṭicchādeti. Tathā hi duṭṭhullavācāsikkhāpade (pārā. 283 ādayo) yā pana tā itthiyo hirimanā, tā nikkhamitvā bhikkhū ujjhāpesuṃ, tasmā idha itthīpi anāpattiṃ karotīti āha “itthīpī”ti. Atha vā idha appaṭicchannattā itthīpi anāpattiṃ karoti, paṭhame pana paṭicchannattā itthisatampi anāpattiṃ na karotīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Anandho abadhiroti ettha kāyasaṃsaggavasena anandho vutto, duṭṭhullavācāvasena abadhiro.

"It is not, however, a secluded place": Here, even what is enclosed on the outside but open on the inside, such as the courtyard of a monastic dwelling, should be understood as included within this. For it is said in the Mahāpaccarī: “Such a place is taken as unsecluded.” "Or by a Saṅghādisesa": by a Saṅghādisesa offense reckoned as physical contact or lewd speech. For this reason, in the word-analysis it is said: “If she were to say, ‘Venerable sir, I saw him sitting and engaging in physical contact with a woman…’” and so on. This training rule has come down in connection with lewd speech. And having heard lewd speech, that woman does not conceal it. For in the training rule on lewd speech, those women who were conscientious went out and complained about the bhikkhus. Therefore, here it is said, “even the woman,” meaning she too commits no offense. Or else, the meaning should be seen here thus: here, because it is an unsecluded place, even the woman commits no offense; but in the first case, because it is a secluded place, the presence of even a hundred women does not constitute a non-offense. Here, in the phrase "not blind, not deaf," ‘not blind’ is said in connection with physical contact, and ‘not deaf’ in connection with lewd speech.

Samuṭṭhānādīsu [M 0.0272] idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ tisamuṭṭhānaṃ – kāyacittato vācācittato kāyavācācittato samuṭṭhāti, kiriyaṃ, saññāvimokkhaṃ, sacittakaṃ, lokavajjaṃ, kāyakammaṃ, vacīkammaṃ, akusalacittaṃ, sukhamajjhattavedanāhi dvivedanaṃ. Tenāha “samuṭṭhānādīni panettha adinnādānasadisānevā”ti. Ettha ca kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjanto duṭṭhullampi bhaṇati, duṭṭhullaṃ bhaṇanto [V 0.0251] nisīdati cāti “kāyavācācittato ca samuṭṭhātī”ti vuttaṃ, duṭṭhullameva vā sandhāya vuttanti gahetabbaṃ.

Regarding the origins, etc., this training rule has three origins: it arises from body and mind, from speech and mind, or from body, speech, and mind. It is an action, a release through perception, intentional, a fault in the world, a bodily action, a verbal action, with unwholesome consciousness, and it is twofold in feeling, connected with pleasure and neutrality. Therefore it is said: “Herein, the origins, etc., are just like those for taking what is not given.” Here, one who engages in physical contact also utters lewd speech, and one who utters lewd speech also sits down; thus it is said to arise “from body, speech, and mind.” Or it should be understood that this is said referring only to lewd speech.

Dutiyaaniyatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Indeterminate Rule is finished.

“Aniyatuddeso cāyaṃ diṭṭhādisamūlakacodanāya vatthuṃ paṭijānamānova āpattiyā kāretabbo, na itaroti āpattiropanāropanalakkhaṇadassanatthaṃ vutto”ti vadanti.

“And this is the recitation of the Indeterminate. One who acknowledges the grounds of an accusation based on what was seen, etc., should be made to deal with the offense, not otherwise. This is stated to show the characteristic of imposing and not imposing an offense,” they say.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the commentary on the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the Elucidation of the Obscure Meaning,

Aniyatavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Indeterminate Rules is finished.

Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Forfeiture

1. Cīvaravaggo

1. The Robe Chapter

1. Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Kathina Training Rule

Niṭṭhitacīvarasminti [M 0.0273] (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.462-463) [V 0.0252] niṭṭhitañca taṃ cīvarañcāti niṭṭhitacīvaraṃ, niṭṭhite ānisaṃsamūlake cīvare, paccāsācīvare cāti attho. Yasmā pana taṃ cīvaraṃ karaṇenapi niṭṭhitaṃ hoti nāsanādīhipi, tasmā “sūcikammapariyosānena vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yaṃ kiñci sūciyā kattabbaṃ pāsakapaṭṭagaṇṭhikapaṭṭapariyosānakammaṃ, taṃ sūcikammapariyosānaṃ nāma, tena. Naṭṭhanti corādīhi haṭaṃ. Etampi hi karaṇapalibodhassa niṭṭhitattā “niṭṭhita”nti vuccati. Vinaṭṭhanti upacikādīhi khāditaṃ. Daḍḍhanti agginā daḍḍhaṃ. Cīvarāsā vā upacchinnāti “asukasmiṃ nāma kule cīvaraṃ labhissāmī”ti yā cīvarāsā uppannā hoti, sā upacchinnā. Etesampi karaṇapalibodhasseva niṭṭhitattā niṭṭhitabhāvo veditabbo. Tenāha “imesu vā”tiādi. Etena cīvarapalibodhābhāvo vutto. Tenāha “cīvarassa karaṇapalibodhe upacchinneti attho”ti. Kathametaṃ viññāyatīti āha “atthatakathinassa hī”tiādi. Pañcānisaṃse aññattha gantuṃ adatvā saṅgaṇhanaṭṭhena kathinaṃ, thiranti attho, atthataṃ kathinaṃ yena so atthatakathino, tassa atthatakathinassa. Hīti kāraṇatthe nipāto. Tāva kathinānisaṃsaṃ labhatīti ettha yo atthatakathino bhikkhūti ajjhāharitabbaṃ, tāva so atthatakathino bhikkhūti veditabbo, anāmantacārādikaṃ kathinānisaṃsaṃ labhatīti attho. “Atthatakathinassa bhikkhuno”ti idaṃ vā “atthatakathino bhikkhū”ti vibhattivipariṇāmaṃ katvā yojetabbaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – cīvarapalibodho āvāsapalibodhoti dve palibodhā. Tesu ekapalibodhepi sati yasmā anāmantacārādikaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ labhati, nāsati. Kasmā? “Niṭṭhitacīvarasmi”nti etassa cīvarassa karaṇapalibodhe upacchinneti ayamattho [V 0.0253] viññāyatīti. Saṅghassāti saṅghena. Kattari cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Ubbhateti aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānamaññatarena, antarubbhārena vā uddhaṭe.

"When the robe is finished": The finished robe is that which is finished and is a robe; the meaning is: when the robe that is the basis for the benefits is finished, or the expected robe. Since that robe is finished by its making and also by its destruction, etc., it is therefore said, "or by the completion of needlework," and so on. Here, whatever has to be done with a needle—the work ending with the loop, the hem, and the knot—is called the completion of needlework; by that. "Lost" means carried off by thieves, etc. This too is called “finished” because the obstacle of making it is finished. "Destroyed" means eaten by termites, etc. "Burned" means burned by fire. "Or the hope for a robe is cut off": the hope that has arisen, “I will get a robe from such-and-such a family,” is cut off. The state of being finished should be understood for these too because the obstacle of making is finished. Hence it is said, "or in these cases," etc. By this, the absence of the robe-obstacle is stated. Hence it is said, “The meaning is that the obstacle of making the robe is cut off.” How is this to be understood? He says, "For one who has spread the kathina," etc. Kathina means ‘firm’; it is in the sense of consolidating the five benefits without giving them up to go elsewhere. He by whom the kathina is spread is one who has spread the kathina; for him. "Hi" is a particle in the sense of a reason. Here, in the phrase "he obtains the kathina benefits for that long," the words “the bhikkhu who has spread the kathina” should be supplied. It should be understood that for that long that bhikkhu who has spread the kathina obtains the kathina benefits, such as traveling without informing. Or the phrase 'for the bhikkhu who has spread the kathina' should be construed by changing its case ending to the nominative. This is the meaning: there are two obstacles, the robe-obstacle and the residence-obstacle. Among these, even when one obstacle is present, since he obtains the benefits such as traveling without informing, they are not lost. Why? Because from the phrase "when the robe is finished," this meaning is understood: “when the obstacle of making the robe is cut off.” "By the Saṅgha": by the Saṅgha. This is the genitive in the sense of the agent. "When it is withdrawn": when it is withdrawn by one of the eight grounds or by an interim withdrawal.

Tatrāti [M 0.0274] tasmiṃ kathine. Ubbhāro uddharaṇaṃ. Purimavassaṃvuṭṭhe tiṃsamatte pāveyyake bhikkhū uddissa “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kathinaṃ attharitu”nti kathinakkhandhake (mahāva. 306) bhagavatā kathinassa anuññātattā “ayañhi kathinatthāro nāma…pe… anuññāto”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha purimavassaṃvuṭṭhānanti vassacchedaṃ akatvā purimavassaṃvuṭṭhānanti attho. Etena vuṭṭhavassavasena tāva purimikāya vassaṃ upagatāyeva kathinatthāraṃ labhanti, na pacchimikāya upagatāti dasseti. Vuṭṭhavassavasena tāva evaṃ hotu, gaṇanavasena taṃ kittakā labhantīti āha “so”tiādi. Soti kathinatthāro. Sabbantimena paricchedenāti gaṇanavasena pacchimakoṭiyā. Pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatīti pacchimakoṭiyā cattāro kathinadussassa dāyakā, eko paṭiggāhakoti pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭati. Keci pana “pañcavaggakaraṇīyattā ‘pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī’ti vutta”nti vadanti, taṃ tesaṃ matimattaṃ “tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ catuvaggo bhikkhusaṅgho ṭhapetvā tīṇi kammāni upasampadaṃ pavāraṇaṃ abbhāna”nti campeyyakkhandhake (mahāva. 388) vuttattā. Tasmāti yasmā vuṭṭhavassavasena purimavassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ anaññāto, yasmā ca sabbantimena paricchedena pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭati, tasmā. Yatthāti yasmiṃ vihāre. Ānisaṃseti anāmantacārādike kathinānisaṃse. Atha pana cattāro bhikkhū vassaṃ upagatā, eko paripuṇṇavasso sāmaṇero sace pacchimikāya upasampajjati, gaṇapūrako ceva hoti, ānisaṃsañca labhati. Tayo bhikkhū, dve sāmaṇerā, dve bhikkhū, tayo sāmaṇerā, eko bhikkhu, cattāro sāmaṇerāti etthāpi eseva nayo.

"Therein": in that kathina. "Withdrawal" is the lifting. Because the Blessed One permitted the kathina in the Kathina Chapter, referring to the thirty-odd bhikkhus from Pāvā who had completed the earlier rains-residence, with the words, “I allow, bhikkhus, the spreading of the kathina by bhikkhus who have completed the rains-residence,” it is said: “For this spreading of the kathina … is permitted.” Therein, "those who have completed the earlier rains-residence" means those who have completed the earlier rains-residence without a break in the residence. By this he shows that, with respect to the completed rains-residence, only those who have entered upon the rains-residence during the earlier period obtain the spreading of the kathina, not those who have entered upon it during the later period. Let it be so with respect to the completed rains-residence, but with respect to number, how many obtain it? He says, "That," etc. "That": the spreading of the kathina. "By the very last limit": by the final limit in terms of number. "It is allowable for five persons": at the final limit, four are donors of the kathina cloth and one is the recipient; thus it is allowable for five persons. But some say: “It is said, ‘it is allowable for five persons,’ because it is to be done by a group of five.” This is merely their opinion, because it is said in the Campeyyaka Chapter: “Therein, bhikkhus, this Saṅgha of four bhikkhus, apart from three formal acts—higher ordination, the invitation, and rehabilitation….” "Therefore": because, with respect to the completed rains-residence, it is permitted to those who have completed the earlier rains-residence, and because by the very last limit it is allowable for five persons, therefore. "Where": in whatever monastery. "The benefits": the kathina benefits such as traveling without informing. Further, if four bhikkhus have entered upon the rains-residence, and one novice whose rains-residence is complete receives the higher ordination during the later period, he both completes the quorum and obtains the benefits. The same method applies in the cases of three bhikkhus and two novices, two bhikkhus and three novices, and one bhikkhu and four novices.

Khandhake vuttāya ñattidutiyakammavācāyāti –

By the formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement stated in the Khandhaka:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dadeyya kathinaṃ attharituṃ, esā ñatti. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno deti kathinaṃ attharituṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati imassa kathinadussassa itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dānaṃ kathinaṃ attharituṃ, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Dinnaṃ idaṃ saṅghena kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa [M 0.0275] bhikkhuno kathinaṃ attharituṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (mahāva. 307) –

“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me. This kathina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give this kathina cloth to the bhikkhu named so-and-so to spread the kathina. This is the motion. Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me. This kathina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha gives this kathina cloth to the bhikkhu named so-and-so to spread the kathina. Let the venerable ones who approve of the giving of this kathina cloth to the bhikkhu named so-and-so to spread the kathina remain silent. Let anyone who disapproves speak up. This kathina cloth has been given by the Saṅgha to the bhikkhu named so-and-so to spread the kathina. The Saṅgha approves; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

Evaṃ [V 0.0254] kathinakkhandhake vuttāya ñattidutiyakammavācāya. Kathinatthārārahassāti kathinaṃ attharituṃ bhabbassa. So ca kho pubbakaraṇajānanādīhi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgatoti veditabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ vinayavinicchaye “aṭṭhadhammakovido bhikkhu, kathinatthāramarahatī”ti. Parivārepi (pari. 409) vuttaṃ –

Thus by the formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement stated in the Kathina Chapter. "For one worthy of spreading the kathina": for one who is fit to spread the kathina. And he should be understood as one endowed with the eight factors, such as knowledge of the preliminary duties. For this is said in the Vinayavinicchaya: “A bhikkhu skilled in the eight things is worthy of spreading the kathina.” It is also stated in the Parivāra:

“Aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ. Katamehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ? Pubbakaraṇaṃ jānāti, paccuddhāraṃ jānāti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, atthāraṃ jānāti, mātikaṃ jānāti, palibodhaṃ jānāti, uddhāraṃ jānāti, ānisaṃsaṃ jānāti, imehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharitu”nti.

“A person endowed with eight factors is qualified to spread the kathina. With which eight factors is a person qualified to spread the kathina? He knows the preliminary work, he knows the withdrawal, he knows the determination, he knows the spreading, he knows the matrix, he knows the obstacles, he knows the removal, and he knows the benefits. A person endowed with these eight factors is qualified to spread the kathina.”

Ettha ca pubbakaraṇaṃ nāma dhovanavicāraṇacchedanabandhanasibbanarajanakappakaraṇaṃ. Paccuddhāro nāma purāṇasaṅghāṭiādīnaṃ paccuddharaṇaṃ. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ nāma kathinacīvarādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Atthāro nāma kathinatthāro. Mātikā nāma aṭṭha mātikā. Palibodho nāma āvāsapalibodho cīvarapalibodhoti dve palibodhā. Uddhāro nāma pakkamanantikādayo. Ānisaṃso nāma pañcānisaṃsā.

Here, preliminary work means washing, examining, cutting, binding, sewing, dyeing, and making it suitable. Withdrawal means the withdrawal of the old outer robe and so on. Determination means the determination of the kathina robe. Spreading means the spreading of the kathina. The matrix means the eight matrices. Obstacle means the two obstacles: the obstacle of the residence and the obstacle of the robe. Removal means the conditions for removal, such as that ending with departure. Benefit means the five benefits.

Yaṃ pana samantapāsādikāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) vuttaṃ “kathinaṃ pana kena attharitabbaṃ? Yassa saṅgho kathinacīvaraṃ deti, saṅghena pana kassa dātabbaṃ? Yo jiṇṇacīvaro hoti, sace bahū jiṇṇacīvarā honti, vuḍḍhassa dātabbaṃ. Vuḍḍhesupi yo mahāpariso tadaheva cīvaraṃ katvā attharituṃ sakkoti, tassa dātabbaṃ. Sace vuḍḍho na sakkoti, navakataro sakkoti, tassa dātabbaṃ. Apica saṅghena mahātherassa saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, tasmā ‘tumhe, bhante, gaṇhatha, mayaṃ katvā dassāmā’ti vattabba”nti, tampi kathinatthārārahaṃyeva gahetvāva dātabbaṃ. Dentena pana tīsu cīvaresu yaṃ yaṃ jiṇṇaṃ [M 0.0276] hoti, taṃ tadatthāya dātabbaṃ. Pakatiyā dupaṭṭacīvarassa dupaṭṭatthāyeva dātabbaṃ. Sacepissa ekapaṭṭacīvaraṃ ghanaṃ hoti, kathinasāṭako ca pelavo, sāruppatthāya dupaṭṭappahonakameva dātabbaṃ. “Ahaṃ alabhanto ekapaṭṭaṃ pārupāmī”ti vadantassāpi dupaṭṭaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Yo pana lobhapakatiko hoti, tassa na dātabbaṃ. Tenāpi kathinaṃ attharitvā pacchā sibbetvā “dve cīvarāni karissāmī”ti na gahetabbaṃ.

Moreover, as is said in the Samantapāsādikā: “But by whom should the kathina be spread? By the one to whom the Saṅgha gives the kathina robe. But to whom should the Saṅgha give it? To a bhikkhu whose robe is worn out. If there are many whose robes are worn out, it should be given to the most senior. Even among the seniors, it should be given to one who has a large following and is able to make and spread the robe on that same day. If the senior is unable, but a more junior one is able, it should be given to him. Furthermore, it is proper for the Saṅgha to support the great elder, so it should be said, ‘Venerable sir, please accept it; we will make it and give it to you.’” This, too, should be given only after having ascertained that he is a suitable person to spread the kathina. When giving, whichever of the three robes is worn out, it should be given for that purpose. Normally, for one who has a double-layered robe, it should be given for the purpose of a double-layered robe. But if his single-layered robe is thick and the kathina cloth is thin, a cloth sufficient for a suitable double-layered robe should be given. Even to one who says, ‘If I do not get one, I will wear a single-layered robe,’ it is proper to give a double-layered one. However, it should not be given to one who is greedy by nature. And that bhikkhu, having spread the kathina, should not accept it thinking, ‘I will sew it later and make two robes.’”

Tenāti kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā. Tadahevāti tasmiṃyeva divase. Pañca vā atirekāni vā [V 0.0255] khaṇḍāni chinditvāti yathā pañcakhaṇḍikādīnaṃ saṅghāṭiādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññatarappahonakāni mahāmaṇḍalaaḍḍhamaṇḍalādivasena pañca khaṇḍāni vā atirekāni vā sattādikhaṇḍāni honti, evaṃ chinditvā. Tasmiñca kathinacīvare kariyamāne “ahaṃ thero”ti vā “bahussuto”ti vā ekenāpi akātuṃ na labbhati. Anādariyena akarontassa dukkaṭaṃ. Tasmā sabbeheva sannipatitvā dhovanachedanasibbanarajanāni niṭṭhāpetabbāni. Tenāha “sesabhikkhūhipi tassa sahāyehi bhavitabba”nti. Katacīvaramevāti niṭṭhitaparikammameva kathinadussaṃ. Sabbantimena paricchedena antaravāsakopi chinditvāva kātabbo aññathā atthāravipattito. Yathāha –

By ‘by him’ is meant by the bhikkhu who spreads the kathina. By ‘on that very day’ is meant on that same day. ‘Having cut into five or more pieces’ means having cut it in such a way that it becomes five pieces, or more than five pieces such as seven, etc., by way of the large panel, half-panel, etc., sufficient for any of the three robes, such as the five-piece outer robe.
