And while that kathina robe is being made, it is not allowable for even a single one to refrain from working on it, saying, ‘I am an elder’ or ‘I am very learned.’ For one who does not work on it out of disrespect, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Therefore, all should assemble and complete the washing, cutting, sewing, and dyeing. Hence it is said: ‘The remaining bhikkhus, too, should be his helpers.’ By ‘only a made robe’ is meant a kathina cloth on which the work has been completed. As the very final delimitation, even an inner robe must be made only after cutting it; otherwise, the spreading fails. As it is said:

“Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ? Na ullikhitamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ…pe… na aññatra pañcakena vā atirekapañcakena vā tadaheva sañchinnenā”ti (mahāva. 308).

“And how, bhikkhus, is the kathina not spread? The kathina is not spread merely by marking it out… (etc.) … nor is it spread with anything other than a robe cut on that very day into five or more than five panels.” (Mahāva. 308).

Tenevāha “acchinnāsibbitaṃ pana na vaṭṭatī”ti. Tena bhikkhunāti atthārakena bhikkhunā. Attharitabbanti attharaṇaṃ kātabbaṃ. Tañca kho tathāvacībhedakaraṇamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yathāha –

Therefore he said: “But an uncut and unsewn one is not allowable.” By ‘by that bhikkhu’ is meant by the bhikkhu who is the spreader. By ‘it should be spread’ is meant the spreading should be done. And this should be understood as simply the making of a specific verbal utterance. As it is said:

“Sace saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇikā saṅghāṭi paccuddharitabbā, navā saṅghāṭi adhiṭṭhātabbā, ‘imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī’ti vācā bhinditabbā”ti (pari. 413) –

“If one wishes to spread the kathina with an outer robe, the old outer robe should be withdrawn, the new outer robe should be determined, and the utterance should be made: ‘With this outer robe I spread the kathina.’” (Pari. 413)

Vitthāro. “Bhante, āvuso”ti ca “anumodatha, anumodāhī”ti ca vacanabhedaṃ sandhāya “therānañcā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

In detail: The words ‘of the elders, etc.’ are stated with reference to the difference in speech, that is, ‘Venerable sir’ (bhante) and ‘friend’ (āvuso), and ‘You (all) approve’ (anumodatha) and ‘You approve’ (anumodāhi).

Evaṃ [M 0.0277] atthārakena paṭipajjitabbavidhiṃ dassetvā idāni anumodakehi paṭipajjitabbavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “tehipī”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Anumodāmā”ti attanāva attani gāravavasena vuttaṃ. Kiñcāpi evaṃ vuttaṃ, tathāpi ekakena “anumodāmā”ti vattuṃ na vaṭṭati, “anumodāmi”cceva vattabbanti vadanti, vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ. Idāni kathinānisaṃse dassetuṃ bhūmiṃ vicārayanto “purimavassaṃvuṭṭhesupī”tiādimāha. Tattha tesaṃyevāti atthārakaanumodakānaṃyeva. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre “dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ atthārakassa [V 0.0256] ca anumodakassa cā”ti (pari. 403). Teti atthārakaanumodakā. Tato paṭṭhāyāti atthārānumodanato paṭṭhāya. Yāva kathinassubbhārāti na kevalaṃ cīvaramāseyeva, atha kho aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānaṃ aññatarena vā antarubbhārena vā yāva kathinassubbhārā pañcānisaṃse labhanti, uddhaṭe pana na labhantīti attho.

Having thus shown the procedure to be followed by the spreader, to show the procedure to be followed by the approvers, the text now begins with ‘by them too,’ etc. ‘We approve’ (anumodāma) is said by oneself out of self-respect. Although it is said thus, some say that it is not proper for a single person to say ‘we approve’; one should say ‘I approve’ (anumodāmi). This should be accepted after investigation. Now, examining the basis for showing the benefits of the kathina, he says, ‘even for those who have completed the earlier rains-residence,’ etc. Here, ‘for them only’ means for the spreader and the approvers only. For it is said in the Parivāra: ‘The kathina is spread for two persons: for the spreader and for the approver’ (Pari. 403). ‘They’ are the spreader and the approvers. ‘From then on’ means from the time of the spreading and approving. ‘Until the removal of the kathina’ means that they obtain the five benefits not only during the robe-month but until the removal of the kathina by one of the eight matrices or by an interim removal. The meaning is that once it is removed, they do not obtain them.

Idāni te pañcānisaṃse sarūpato dassetuṃ “anāmantacāro”tiādimāha. Tattha anāmantacāro nāma pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ aññatarena nimantitassa santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā kulesu cārittāpajjanaṃ. Asamādānacāro nāma nāmenādhiṭṭhitassa cīvarassa asamādānacaraṇaṃ, nāmenādhiṭṭhitānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānamaññataraṃ cīvaraṃ yattha katthaci nikkhipitvā aññattha aruṇuṭṭhāpananti attho, cīvaravippavāsoti vuttaṃ hoti. Yāvadatthacīvaranti yāvatā cīvarena attho hoti, tāvatakaṃ anadhiṭṭhitaṃ avikappitaṃ cīvaradhāraṇaṃ, dasāhamatikkamitvā cīvarassa ṭhapananti attho. Gaṇassa bhojanaṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ. Gaṇoti cettha cattāro vā tatuttari vā bhikkhū. Tesaṃ viññattito vā nimantanato vā laddhassa odanādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ aññatarabhojanassa saha gahaṇanti attho. Yo ca tattha cīvaruppādoti tattha kathinatthatasīmāya matakacīvaraṃ vā hotu, saṅghaṃ uddissa dinnaṃ vā saṅghikena tatruppādena ābhataṃ vā yena kenaci ākārena yaṃ saṅghikaṃ cīvaraṃ uppajjati, taṃ tesaṃ bhavissatīti attho. Tenāha “tasmiṃ āvāse saṅghassa uppannacīvarañcā”ti.

Now, to show these five benefits in their own form, he begins with ‘going about without asking leave,’ etc. Here, ‘going about without asking leave’ (anāmantacāra) means, when one has been invited to one of the five kinds of meals, to go on alms round among families without asking permission from a resident bhikkhu. ‘Going about without having undertaken the robe’ (asamādānacāra) means not carrying a determined robe; the meaning is to leave one of the three determined robes somewhere and to be elsewhere when dawn breaks; this is called ‘being away from one’s robe’ (cīvaravippavāsa). ‘A robe for as long as one needs’ (yāvadatthacīvara) means wearing an undetermined and unshared robe for as long as one needs it; the meaning is keeping a robe beyond the ten-day limit. ‘A group meal’ (gaṇabhojana) is a meal for a group. Here, a ‘group’ means four or more bhikkhus. The meaning is the partaking together of any of the five kinds of food, such as boiled rice, that has been received through an invitation or a request made to them. ‘Whatever robe-gain there is’ (yo ca tattha cīvaruppādo) means that whatever communal robe arises within the boundary where the kathina was spread—be it the robe of a deceased bhikkhu, or one given for the Sangha, or one brought from a communal gain there, or one that has arisen in any way—that will belong to them. Hence it is said: ‘and the robe that has arisen for the Sangha in that residence.’

“Yaṃ pana tattha saṅghassa uppannaṃ pattādi vā aññaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ vā, taṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Yaṃ pana tatruppādena taṇḍulādinā vatthaṃ cetāpitaṃ, atthatakathinānameva tāni vatthāni pāpuṇanti. Vatthehi pana taṇḍulādīsu cetāpitesu [M 0.0278] sabbesaṃ tāni pāpuṇantī”ti gaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ, tampi cetāpitakālato paṭṭhāya cīvaruppādo na hotīti suvuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Anatthatakathinā pana imesu pañcasu ānisaṃsesu cīvaramāse asamādānacāraṃ ṭhapetvā sesānisaṃse labhanti. Yadi asamādānacāropi labbheyya, pāveyyakā bhikkhū vassaṃvuṭṭhā okapuṇṇehi cīvarehi na bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkameyyuṃ. Yasmā taṃ na labbhati, tasmā cīvaramāsepi cīvaraṃ samādāya eva bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamiṃsu.

“But whatever bowls or other requisites have arisen there for the Sangha, that belongs to all. But whatever cloth has been acquired with rice and other things obtained there, those cloths belong only to those for whom the kathina has been spread. When, however, rice and other things are acquired with cloths, those belong to all.” This is stated in the Gaṇṭhipada, and it should be understood as well-said that from the time of acquisition, it is not a ‘robe-gain.’ Those for whom the kathina has not been spread obtain the other benefits among these five during the robe-month, with the exception of ‘going about without having undertaken the robe.’ If ‘going about without having undertaken the robe’ were also allowed, the bhikkhus from Pāvā, having completed the rains-residence, would not have approached the Blessed One with their water-logged robes. Since that is not allowed, they approached the Blessed One only after undertaking their robes, even during the robe-month.

Evaṃ kathinatthāraṃ dassetvā idāni ubbhāraṃ dassento “taṃ panetaṃ kathina”ntiādimāha. Tattha mātikāti mātaro, janettiyoti attho. Kathinubbhārañhi etā aṭṭha janenti. Tāsu pakkamanaṃ anto etissāti pakkamanantikā. Evaṃ sesāpi veditabbā. Tattha yo bhikkhu atthatakathino [V 0.0257] kathinacīvaraṃ ādāya tasmiṃ āvāse nirapekkho “na paccessa”nti pakkamati, tassevaṃ pakkamato kathinuddhāro atikkantamattāya sīmāya hotīti pakkamanantiko kathinuddhāroti veditabbo.

Having thus shown the spreading of the kathina, now, to show its removal, he begins with ‘But this kathina,’ etc. Here, ‘matrix’ (mātikā) means mothers, that is, progenitors. For these eight generate the removal of the kathina. Among them, ‘departure-ending’ (pakkamanantikā) is that which has departure as its end. The others should be understood in the same way. Here, when a bhikkhu for whom the kathina has been spread takes the kathina robe and departs from that residence without any expectation of returning, thinking, ‘I will not come back,’ for him the removal of the kathina occurs the moment he crosses the boundary. This should be understood as the ‘departure-ending’ removal of the kathina.

Yo pana ānisaṃsacīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati, tassa bahisīmāgatassa evaṃ hoti “idhevimaṃ karissāmi, na puna taṃ vihāraṃ gacchissāmī”ti tasmiṃ āvāse nirapekkho hutvā taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti, tassa bhikkhuno niṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro.

But if a bhikkhu, having taken a privilege-robe, departs, and after going outside the boundary thinks, 'I will make it right here and will not return to that monastery,' and, being unconcerned about that dwelling, has that robe made, for that bhikkhu the removal of the Kathina is one that ends upon completion.

Yadi pana ānisaṃsamūlacīvaraṃ ādāya bahisīmāgato “nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ karissāmi, na ca taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchissāmī”ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ karoti, tadā sanniṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro.

If, however, having taken the basic privilege-robe and gone outside the boundary, he makes the resolution, 'I will neither make this robe nor return to that dwelling,' then the removal of the Kathina is one that ends upon resolution.

Tadeva ānisaṃsacīvaraṃ laddhā taṃ ādāya bahisīmaṃ gantvā “idhevimaṃ cīvaraṃ karissāmi, na gacchissāmī”ti karontassa sace taṃ cīvaraṃ nassati vinassati ḍayhati, nāsanantiko kathinuddhāro hoti.

Having obtained that same privilege-robe, taken it, and gone outside the boundary, if, while he is making it with the thought, 'I will make this robe right here and will not go back,' that robe is lost, destroyed, or burned, the removal of the Kathina is one that ends upon its loss.

Sace pana ānisaṃsacīvaraṃ laddhā tasmiṃ vihāre sāpekkhova bahisīmāgato “vihāre bhikkhūhi antarubbhāraṃ kata”nti suṇāti, tassa savanantiko kathinuddhāro hoti.

But if a bhikkhu, having obtained a privilege-robe, goes outside the boundary while still having concern for that monastery, and he hears, 'An interim removal of the Kathina has been done by the bhikkhus in the monastery,' for him the removal of the Kathina is one that ends upon hearing.

Āsāya avacchedo etissāti āsāvacchedikā. Yo pana yena kenaci “tuyhaṃ cīvaraṃ dassāmī”ti vutto tasmiṃ cīvare āsāya vihāre apekkhaṃ pahāya bahisīmāgato puna tena “na sakkomi dātu”nti [M 0.0279] vutte āsaṃ chindati, tassa āsāvacchediko kathinuddhāro hoti.

'Cutting off hope' (āsāvacchedikā) is so called because it is the cutting off of hope. If a bhikkhu has been told by someone, 'I will give you a robe,' and because of his hope for that robe he abandons his concern for the monastery and goes outside the boundary, and then when that person says, 'I am not able to give it,' he cuts off his hope, for him the removal of the Kathina is one that is a cutting off of hope.

Yo pana vassaṃvuṭṭhavihārato aññaṃ vihāraṃ sāpekkhova gantvā āgacchanto antarāmaggeyeva kathinuddhāraṃ vītināmeti, tassa sīmātikkamanantiko kathinuddhāro.

If a bhikkhu, having gone with concern from the monastery where he spent the rains to another monastery, is returning, and the removal of the Kathina is concluded while he is still on the way, for him the removal of the Kathina is one that ends upon his crossing the boundary.

Saha ubbhārenāti sahubbhārā. Ānisaṃsacīvaraṃ ādāya sāpekkhova bahi gantvā kathinuddhāraṃ sambhuṇantassa kathinuddhāro sahubbhāroti veditabbo.

'With the removal' (sahubbhāra) is so called because it is together with the removal. When a bhikkhu, having taken a privilege-robe, goes outside while still having concern, and learns of the removal of the Kathina, his removal of the Kathina should be understood as being 'with the removal'.

“Etasmiṃ pana pakkamanantike kathinuddhāre paṭhamaṃ cīvarapalibodho chijjatī”tiādinā cīvarapalibodhupacchedādikassa vinicchayassa vitthārato samantapāsādikāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 311) vuttattā [V 0.0258]8 “tattha vitthāravinicchayo”tiādimāha. Atthārubbhārānaṃyeva vā vitthāravinicchayassa tatthāgatattā evaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sesapalibodhābhāvanti avasesassa palibodhassa abhāvaṃ, āvāsapalibodhābhāvanti attho.

Because the detailed decision concerning the cutting off of the robe-obstruction and so on has been stated in detail in the Samantapāsādikā (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 311) with the words beginning, 'But in this lifting of the Kathina that ends upon departure, first the robe-obstruction is cut off,' he therefore states the text beginning, 'Therein is the detailed decision.' Or it should be understood that this is said because the detailed decision found there pertains only to the eight kinds of lifting. 'Absence of the remaining obstructions' means the absence of the remaining obstruction; the meaning is the absence of the dwelling-obstruction.

Assāti kālassa. Dasāhaparamanti accantasaṃyoge upayogavacananti āha “taṃ dasāhaparamaṃ kāla”nti. Atirekanti adhikaṃ, so ca adhikabhāvo adhiṭṭhitavikappitacīvaratoti āha “adhiṭṭhitavikappitesū”tiādi. Khomanti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.636-638) khomasuttehi vāyitaṃ khomapaṭṭacīvaraṃ. Tathā sesāni. Kambalaṃ nāma manussalomavāḷalome ṭhapetvā sesalomehi vāyitvā katavatthaṃ. Sāṇaṃ nāma sāṇavākehi katavatthaṃ. Bhaṅgaṃ nāma khomasuttādīhi pañcahi missetvā katavatthaṃ. “Pāṭekkaṃ vākamayamevā”tipi vadanti. Tadanulomānaṃ vāti dukūlaṃ pattuṇṇaṃ somārapaṭṭaṃ cīnapaṭṭaṃ iddhijaṃ devadinnanti tesaṃ khomādīnaṃyeva anulomānaṃ channaṃ cīvarānaṃ vā, tattha dukūlaṃ sāṇassa anulomaṃ vākamayattā. Pattuṇṇadese pāṇakehi sañjātavatthaṃ pattuṇṇaṃ. Somāradese jātaṃ vatthaṃ somārapaṭṭaṃ. Tathā cīnapaṭṭaṃ. Imāni tīṇipi koseyyassa anulomāni pāṇakehi katasuttamayattā. Iddhijaṃ ehibhikkhūnaṃ puññiddhiyā nibbattacīvaraṃ. Taṃ pana khomādīnamaññataraṃ hotīti tesaṃyeva anulomaṃ. Devehi dinnaṃ cīvaraṃ devadinnaṃ, taṃ kapparukkhe nibbattaṃ jāliniyā devakaññāya anuruddhattherassa [M 0.0280] dinnavatthasadisaṃ, tampi khomādīnaṃyeva anulomaṃ hoti tesu aññatarabhāvato.

'Its' means of time. 'For a maximum of ten days': this is a statement of usage in the sense of continuous connection; thus he says, 'that period of a maximum of ten days.' 'Extra' means additional, and that state of being additional is in relation to robes that have been determined or shared; thus he says the text beginning, 'in regard to those determined or shared.' 'Linen' (khoma) (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.636–638) is a linen-cloth robe woven with linen threads. Likewise for the rest. A 'blanket' (kambala) is a cloth made by weaving with other kinds of hair, excluding human hair and horsehair. 'Hemp cloth' (sāṇa) is cloth made from hemp bark. 'Mixed cloth' (bhaṅga) is cloth made by mixing the five, beginning with linen thread. Some also say: 'Or each made of bark-fiber.' 'Or of those conforming to them' refers to the six kinds of robes conforming to those linen cloths, etc., namely, dukūla cloth, pattuṇṇa cloth, Somāra cloth, Cīna cloth, cloth produced by psychic power, and cloth given by devas. Therein, dukūla cloth conforms to hemp cloth because it is made of bark-fiber. Pattuṇṇa cloth is cloth produced from insects in the Pattuṇṇa country. Somāra cloth is cloth that comes from the Somāra country. Likewise for Cīna cloth. These three conform to silk because they are made of thread produced by insects. 'Produced by psychic power' is a robe that arises through the psychic power of merit for the 'Come, bhikkhu' monks. But since that is one of the linen cloths, etc., it conforms to them. 'Given by devas' is a robe given by devas; it is produced on a wish-fulfilling tree and is like the cloth given to the Elder Anuruddha by the deva-maiden Jālinī. That too conforms to the linen cloths, etc., because it is one of them.

Dīghato vaḍḍhakihatthappamāṇaṃ, vitthārato tato upaḍḍhappamāṇaṃ vikappanupagaṃ pacchimaṃ. Aṭṭhaṅgulaṃ sugataṅgulenāti ettha sugataṅgulaṃ nāma idāni majjhimassa purimassa tīṇi aṅgulāni, tena sugataṅgulena aṭṭhaṅgulaṃ vaḍḍhakihatthappamāṇanti attho. Caturaṅgulavitthatanti etthāpi yathāvuttānusāreneva attho veditabbo. Yesaṃ pana adhiṭṭhānavikappanānaṃ abhāvato adhiṭṭhitavikappitesu apariyāpannattā idaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ nāma hoti.

The minimum size suitable for sharing is the measure of a carpenter's cubit in length, and half that measure in width. 'Eight fingerbreadths by the Sugata's fingerbreadth': here, the Sugata's fingerbreadth is three fingerbreadths of a man of medium build of the present time. By that Sugata's fingerbreadth, eight fingerbreadths is the measure of a carpenter's cubit—this is the meaning. 'Four fingerbreadths in width': here too the meaning should be understood in accordance with what has been said. However, for those robes for which there is an absence of determination and sharing, because they are not included among those that have been determined or shared, this is called an 'extra robe'.

Taṃ adhiṭṭhānavikappanaṃ kenākārena jānitabbanti anuyogaṃ sandhāya taṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ pana vutta”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yaṃ pana vuttanti atirekacīvaraṃ dassetuṃ “adhiṭṭhitavikappitesu apariyāpannattā”ti amhehi yaṃ vuttanti attho. Ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātunti nāmaṃ vatvā adhiṭṭhātuṃ. Na vikappetunti saṅghāṭiādināmena vikappetuṃ na anujānāmīti attho. “Imaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappemī”ti pana vikappetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Sāmaññavacanaṃ pana ticīvarassa kaṇḍupaṭicchādivassikasāṭikānaṃ viya kālavasena visesābhāvā cassa vikappetabbatāti dassanatthaṃ[V 0.0259], na pana sabbathā vikappanapaṭisedhanatthanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tathā hi purāṇacīvaraṃ paccuddharitvā navassa adhiṭṭhānavacanato, “anāpatti adhiṭṭheti vikappetī”tiādivacanato (pārā. 469) ca ticīvarassapi vikappanāya okāso dinno. Esa nayo sabbattha. Ticīvarādīni hi adhiṭṭhahantena “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”tiādinā taṃ taṃ nāmaṃ vatvā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Vikappentena pana “imaṃ saṅghāṭi”ntiādinā tassa tassa cīvarassa nāmaṃ aggahetvā “imaṃ cīvaraṃ tuyhaṃ vikappemī”ti vikappetabbaṃ. Ticīvaraṃ vā hotu, aññaṃ vā, yadi taṃ taṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā vikappeti, avikappitaṃ hoti, atirekacīvaraṭṭhāneyeva tiṭṭhati. Tato paraṃ vikappetunti catumāsato paraṃ “imaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappemī”ti vikappetuṃ. Idañca paribhuñjituṃ anuññātaṃ. Keci pana (sārattha. ṭī. 2.469) “tato paraṃ vikappetvā yāva āgāmisaṃvacchare vassānaṃ catumāsaṃ, tāva ṭhapetuṃ anuññāta”nti vadanti. Tato paranti ābādhato paraṃ. “Imāsañca pana vassikasāṭikakaṇḍupaṭicchādīnaṃ tato paraṃ vikappetvā paribhogassa anuññātattā tathāvikappitaṃ [M 0.0281] aññanāmena adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjitabba”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Adhiṭṭhātabbavikappetabbatā jānitabbāti adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ vikappetabbanti evaṃ adhiṭṭhānavikappanā jānitabbāti attho.

With reference to the question, 'In what way should that determination and sharing be known?' the text beginning 'But what was said...' was started in order to show that. Herein, 'But what was said' means what was said by us: 'because they are not included among those that have been determined or shared,' in order to show what an extra robe is. 'To determine the three robes' means to determine them after stating their names. 'One should not share it' means: I do not allow one to share it by a name such as 'outer robe.' But it is indeed proper to share it by saying, 'I share this robe.' The general statement is to show that the three robes may be shared, since, like a rainy-season cloth or a cloth for covering sores, there is no distinction based on time, not to prohibit sharing altogether. For indeed, from the statement about determining a new robe after relinquishing an old one, and from statements such as, 'There is no offense if one determines it or shares it' (Pārā. 469), an opportunity is given for sharing the three robes as well. This is the method everywhere. For when determining the three robes, etc., one should determine them by stating each name, such as, 'I determine this outer robe.' But when sharing, one should share by saying, 'I share this robe with you,' without taking the name of that particular robe, such as 'this outer robe.' Whether it is one of the three robes or another, if one shares it taking its specific name, it is not properly shared; it remains in the category of an extra robe. 'To share it after that' means to share it after four months by saying, 'I share this robe.' And this is permitted to be used. Some, however, say (Sāratthadīpanī Ṭīkā 2.469): 'It is permitted to share it after that and to keep it until the four months of the rains in the coming year.' 'After that' means after the illness. 'And since for these rainy-season cloths and cloths for covering sores, use is permitted after they have been shared, they should be determined under another name and then used'—this is said in the glosses. 'The state of being determinable and shareable should be known' means: 'it should be determined, it should be shared'—in this way determination and sharing should be known.

Pañcaparimāṇaṃ assāti pañcakaṃ, muṭṭhissa muṭṭhihatthassa sambandhaṃ pañcakaṃ muṭṭhipañcakaṃ. Esa na yo muṭṭhittikanti etthāpi. Pārupanenapi sakkā nābhiṃ paṭicchādetunti āha “dvihatthopi vaṭṭatī”ti. Na kevalaṃ aḍḍhateyyova vaṭṭati, atha kho dvihatthopi vaṭṭatīti pi-saddassa attho daṭṭhabbo. Atirekañcāti sugatacīvarappamāṇampi tato adhikampi. Paccuddharāmīti ṭhapemi, pariccajāmīti vā attho. “Imaṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.469) evampi vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Kāyavikāraṃ karontenāti hatthādinā cīvaraṃ parāmasantena, cālentena vā. Idañhi adhiṭṭhānaṃ yena kenaci sarīrāvayavena aphusantassa na vaṭṭati. Duvidhanti sammukhāparammukhabhedena duvidhaṃ. Vācā bhinditabbāti vacanaṃ nicchāretabbaṃ. Antogabbhādīsūti antogabbhauparipāsādesu. Sāmantavihāreti yattha tadaheva gantvā nivattetuṃ sakkā, evarūpe samīpavihāre. Idañca desanāsīsamattaṃ, tasmā dūre ṭhitampi adhiṭṭhātabbanti vadanti. “Ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ sallakkhetvā”ti iminā cīvarasaṃlakkhaṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Na hi ṭhapitaṭṭhānamattasallakkhaṇena kiñci payojanaṃ atthi.

'Fivefold' (pañcaka) is so called because it has a fivefold measure; the 'fivefold-fist' (muṭṭhipañcaka) is the fivefold connected with the 'fist-cubit' of a confused person. This same method applies also in the case of the 'three-fist' measure. 'It is possible to cover the navel even with a wrap-around cloth'; thus he says, 'even two cubits is proper.' The meaning of the particle 'pi' (even) should be seen as: not only is two and a half proper, but even two cubits is proper. 'And extra' means both the measure of the Sugata's robe and more than that. 'I relinquish' means 'I set aside' or 'I abandon.' It is also proper to say thus: 'I determine this robe as an outer robe' (Sāratthadīpanī Ṭīkā 2.469). 'By one making a bodily gesture' means by one touching or moving the robe with the hand, etc. For this determination is not valid for one who does not touch it with some bodily limb. 'Twofold' means twofold by the distinction of 'in person' and 'by proxy.' 'The words should be broken' means the statement should be uttered. 'In an inner chamber, etc.' means in an inner chamber, on an upper terrace, etc. 'In a nearby monastery' means in a neighboring monastery of such a kind that one can go and return on that very day. This is just a heading of the teaching; therefore, they say it can be determined even when one is far away. By this, 'having marked the place where it was put,' the marking of the robe is stated. For there is no purpose in merely marking the place where it was put.

Adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitavatthehīti paccattharaṇamukhapuñchanacoḷaparikkhāracoḷavasena adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitavatthehi. Adhiṭṭhānato pubbe saṅghāṭiādivohārassa abhāvato “imaṃ paccuddharāmī”ti paccattharaṇādīnaṃ [V 0.0260] visuṃ paccuddharaṇavidhiṃ dasseti. Paccattharaṇādināmena pana adhiṭṭhātabbattā “imaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ paccuddharāmī”tiādinā vuttepi nevatthi doso. Puna adhiṭṭhātabbānīti saṅghāṭiādināmena adhiṭṭhātabbāni. Parikkhāracoḷakassa pana parikkhāracoḷavasena adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitavatthehipi saṅghāṭiādimhi kate paccuddharitvā puna adhiṭṭhātabbanti natthi. Pubbe katādhiṭṭhānameva adhiṭṭhānaṃ. Adhiṭṭhitena pana tena saddhiṃ mahantatarameva dutiyaṃ paṭṭaṃ vā khaṇḍaṃ vā saṃsibbantena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, same vā khuddake vā adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthi. Sukhaparibhogatthanti vippavāsadosābhāvato yattha katthaci ṭhapetvā dhammassavanādinā kiccena aññattha aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetvā āgantvā nissajjanaṃ vināva [M 0.0282] paribhuñjituṃ sakkuṇeyyatāya sukhaparibhogatthaṃ. Parikkhāracoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātunti parikkhāracoḷaṃ katvā adhiṭṭhātuṃ.

By robes determined and set aside: by robes determined and set aside as a ground-covering cloth, a face-wiping cloth, or an accessory cloth. Since before the determination there is no designation such as 'outer robe,' the phrase 'I withdraw this' shows the separate procedure for withdrawing the ground-covering cloth and so on. However, since they are to be determined by names such as 'ground-covering cloth,' there is no fault even if one says, 'I withdraw this ground-covering cloth,' and so on. 'To be determined again' means they are to be determined by the names 'outer robe,' etc. But in the case of an accessory cloth, even with robes determined and set aside as an accessory cloth, when an outer robe, etc., is made from them, there is no need to withdraw the determination and determine them again. The previous determination remains the determination. However, when sewing a larger second strip or piece together with that determined cloth, it must be determined anew; but if it is of the same size or smaller, there is no need for determination. For the sake of comfortable use: this is for the sake of comfortable use because, as there is no fault in being separated from it, one can set it aside anywhere, go elsewhere for some business such as listening to the Dhamma, and, upon returning after dawn has broken, use it without having to relinquish it. 'To determine an accessory cloth' means to make it an accessory cloth and then determine it.

Anatirittapamāṇāti “dīghaso cha vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṃ aḍḍhateyyā”ti (pāci. 543) vuttappamāṇato anadhikapamāṇā. Paccuddharitvā vikappetabbāti vassikasāṭikabhāvato apanetvā vikappetabbā, hemantassa paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya antodasāhe vassikasāṭikāvassikasāṭikabhāvato apanetvā “imaṃ cīvaraṃ tuyhaṃ vikappemī”tiādinā nayena vikappetabbāti vuttaṃ hoti. Aññathā hi “vassikasāṭikā vassānamāsātikkamenāpi, kaṇḍupaṭicchādi ābādhavūpasamenāpi adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatī”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vakkhamānattā vassānamāsato paraṃ asati adhiṭṭhāne kiṃ paccuddhareyyāti “paccuddharitvā”ti vacanameva nopapajjeyya.

‘Not exceeding the measure’ means of a size not exceeding the measure stated as: ‘six spans long by the Sugata’s span, and two and a half spans wide.’ ‘It should be allocated after being withdrawn’ means it should be allocated after removing it from its state as a rains-retreat cloth. This means it is said that starting from the first day of the winter season, within ten days, the rains-retreat cloth should be allocated after removing it from its state as a rains-retreat cloth, by the method of saying, ‘I allocate this robe to you,’ and so on. Otherwise, since it will be said later that ‘the rains-retreat cloth loses its determination also by the passing of the rains-retreat months, and the itch-covering cloth also by the subsiding of the illness,’ if there were no determination after the rains-retreat months, what would one withdraw? Thus, the very word ‘after being withdrawn’ would not be appropriate.

Keci pana (sārattha. ṭī. 2.469) “yathā kathinamāsabbhantare uppannacīvaraṃ kathinamāsātikkame nissaggiyaṃ hoti, evamayaṃ vassikasāṭikāpi vassānamāsātikkame nissaggiyā hoti. Tasmā kattikapuṇṇamadivase paccuddharitvā tato paraṃ hemantassa paṭhamadivase vikappetabbāti evamattho gahetabbo, paccuddharitvā tato paraṃ vikappetabbāti padayojanā veditabbā”ti ca vadanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Kathinamāse uppannañhi cīvaraṃ atirekacīvaraṭṭhāne ṭhitattā avasānadivase anadhiṭṭhitaṃ kathinamāsātikkame nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ pana vassikasāṭikā adhiṭṭhahitvā ṭhapitattā na tena sadisāti vassānātikkame kathaṃ nissaggiyaṃ hoti anadhiṭṭhitaavikappitameva hi taṃ kālātikkame nissaggiyaṃ hoti, tasmā hemantepi vassikasāṭikā dasāhaparihāraṃ labhati. Evaṃ kaṇḍupaṭicchādipi adhiṭṭhānavijahanato paraṃ dasāhaparihāraṃ labhati. Dasāhaṃ pana anatikkāmetvā vikappetabbā. Nahānatthāya anuññātattā vaṇṇabhedamattarattāpi cesā vaṭṭatīti vuttaṃ. “Dve pana na vaṭṭantī”ti dvinnaṃ adhiṭṭhānābhāvato vuttaṃ[V 0.0261]. “Sace vassāne aparā vassikasāṭikā uppannā hoti, purimavassikasāṭikaṃ paccuddharitvā, vikappetvā ca adhiṭṭhātabbā”ti vadanti.

However, some say: ‘Just as a robe that has arisen during the Kathina month becomes subject to forfeiture when the Kathina month is over, so this rains-retreat cloth becomes subject to forfeiture when the rains-retreat months are over. Therefore, it should be withdrawn on the full-moon day of Kattika and then allocated on the first day of the winter season—this is the meaning to be taken. The construction of the words should be understood as “having been withdrawn, it should then be allocated.”’ But this is not correct. For a robe that has arisen during the Kathina month, because it stands in the position of an extra robe, if it is not determined on the last day, it becomes subject to forfeiture when the Kathina month is over. But this rains-retreat cloth, because it has been determined and set aside, is not similar to that. How could it become subject to forfeiture when the rains-retreat is over? For it is only what is undetermined and unallocated that becomes subject to forfeiture when the time is exceeded. Therefore, even in the winter season, the rains-retreat cloth obtains a ten-day allowance. Similarly, the itch-covering cloth also obtains a ten-day allowance after the abandonment of its determination. But it should be allocated without exceeding ten days. Because it is allowed for the purpose of bathing, it is said to be allowable even if it is dyed only to the extent of a change in color. ‘But two are not allowable’ is said because there is no determination of two. Some say: ‘If another rains-retreat cloth arises during the rains-retreat, the earlier rains-retreat cloth should be withdrawn and allocated, and then the new one should be determined.’

Pamāṇayuttanti “dīghaso sugatavidatthiyā dve vidatthiyo, vitthārato diyaḍḍhaṃ dasā vidatthī”ti (pāci. 531 ādayo) iminā pamāṇena yuttaṃ. Pamāṇikāti “sugatavidatthiyā [M 0.0283] dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo, tiriyaṃ dve vidatthiyo”ti evaṃ vuttappamāṇayuttā. Paccuddharitvā vikappetabbāti ettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Yasmā bhikkhūnaṃ ticīvare paripuṇṇe, atthe ca sati parissāvanādīhi “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhāracoḷaka”nti (mahāva. 357) bahūnaṃ pattatthavikaparissāvanādīnaṃ saṅgahavasena parikkhāracoḷādhiṭṭhānamanuññātaṃ, tasmā “parikkhāracoḷe gaṇanā natthī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Bhagavatā hi yaṃ yaṃ bhikkhū labhanti, taṃ taṃ iminā vidhānena adhiṭṭhahitvā puna “yena yena parissāvanādinā attho hoti, taṃ taṃ katvā gaṇhantū”ti anukampāya anuññātaṃ. Tenevāha “thavikāpī”tiādi. Ādisaddena “etāni cīvarāni parikkhāracoḷāni adhiṭṭhāmī”ti asammukhādhiṭṭhānaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. “Senāsanaparikkhāratthāya dinnapaccattharaṇe cā”ti iminā attano santakaṃ paṭikkhipati. Keci pana (sārattha. ṭī. 2.469) “anivāsetvā, apārupitvā ca kevalaṃ pañcapīṭhesuyeva attharitvā paribhuñjiyamānaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ attano santakampi anadhiṭṭhitaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, taṃ ayuttaṃ senāsanaparikkhāratthāya dinna”nti paccattharaṇassa visesitattā. Bhisibibbohanapāvārakojavānampi senāsanaparikkhāratoyeva adhiṭṭhānakiccaṃ natthīti veditabbaṃ.

‘Conforming to the measure’ means conforming to this measure: ‘two spans long by the Sugata’s span, one and a half spans wide, with a border of a span.’ ‘Of the standard measure’ means conforming to the stated measure: ‘four spans long by the Sugata’s span, and two spans across.’ Regarding ‘it should be withdrawn and allocated,’ what needs to be said on this has been said above. Because the determination of an accessory cloth was allowed for collecting many things such as a bowl-bag and a water-strainer when the bhikkhus’ three robes are complete and there is a need for such things, the Buddha said: ‘I allow, bhikkhus, an accessory cloth.’ Therefore it is said: ‘There is no count for accessory cloths,’ etc. Indeed, out of compassion, the Blessed One allowed that whatever the bhikkhus obtain, they may determine it by this method and then, having made whatever is needed, such as a water-strainer, they may take it. That is why he said ‘even a bag,’ etc. By the word ‘etc.,’ determination in absence is included, as in ‘I determine these cloths as accessory cloths.’ By the phrase ‘and in the case of a ground-covering cloth given for the purpose of furnishing a lodging,’ it excludes one’s own property. Some, however, say: ‘A ground-covering cloth that is one’s own property, which is used merely by spreading it on a seat without wearing it as a lower garment or draping it over oneself, is allowable even if undetermined.’ This is not correct, because the ground-covering cloth is specified as ‘given for the purpose of furnishing a lodging.’ It should be understood that for a mattress, pillow, coverlet, and rug, too, there is no need for determination, precisely because they are furnishings for a lodging.

Adhiṭṭhitañca panetaṃ cīvaraṃ paribhuñjato kathaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatīti āha “sabbañca paneta”ntiādi. Tattha acchinditvā gahaṇenāti corādīhi acchinditvā gahaṇena. Hīnāyāvattanenāti gihibhāvāya āvattanena, vibbhamenāti attho, “sīlavantova hutvā gihī bhavissāmī”ti setavatthanivāsanenāti vuttaṃ hoti. “Antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannassa setavatthanivāso vā kāsāyacajanaṃ vā hīnāyāvattana”nti keci. “‘Hīnāyāvattanenā’ti iminā bhikkhuniyā eva adhiṭṭhānavijahanaṃ gahitaṃ hoti. Sā hi yadā vibbhamati, tadā assamaṇī hoti. Bhikkhu pana vibbhamantopi yāva sikkhaṃ na paccakkhāti, tāva bhikkhuyevāti adhiṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatī”ti apare. Sikkhāpaccakkhānenāti liṅge ṭhitasseva sikkhāya paccakkhānena. Yo hi bhikkhuliṅge ṭhitova sikkhaṃ paccakkhāti, tassa kāyalaggampi cīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahatīti. Kālaṅkiriyāyāti maraṇena. Liṅgaparivattanenāti purisaliṅgassa[V 0.0262], itthiliṅgassa vā parivattanena, purisassa itthiliṅgapātubhāvena, itthiyā vā purisaliṅgapātubhāvenāti vuttaṃ hoti.

And as for this determined robe, how is the determination abandoned by one who is using it? He says: 'But all this…' etc. Herein, 'by its being snatched away' means by its being taken by thieves and others. 'By reverting to the low state' means by returning to the lay life, that is, by disrobing; this means by wearing white clothes with the thought, 'Having been virtuous, I will become a layman.' Some say: 'For one who has committed a terminal offense, wearing white clothes or discarding the ochre robe is reverting to the low state.' Others say: 'By the phrase “by reverting to the low state,” the abandonment of determination is taken to apply only to a bhikkhunī. For when she disrobes, she becomes a non-samaṇī. But a bhikkhu, even when disrobing, remains a bhikkhu as long as he does not renounce the training; thus the determination is not abandoned.' 'By renunciation of the training' means by renouncing the training while still retaining the outward sign of a bhikkhu. For one who renounces the training while still retaining the outward sign of a bhikkhu, the determination is abandoned even for the robe on his body. 'By making an end of one's time' means by death. 'By a change of sex' means by the transformation of the male sex or the female sex; that is, by the appearance of the female sex in a male, or by the appearance of the male sex in a female.

Kaniṭṭhaṅgulinakhapiṭṭhippamāṇenāti [M 0.0284] heṭṭhimaparicchedaṃ dasseti. Oratoti abbhantarato. Yo pana dubbalaṭṭhāne paṭhamaṃ aggaḷaṃ datvā pacchā dubbalaṭṭhānaṃ chinditvā apaneti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ na bhijjati. Maṇḍalaparivattanepi eseva nayo. Dupaṭṭassa pana ekasmiṃ paṭale chidde vā jāte, galite vā adhiṭṭhānaṃ na bhijjati. Khuddakaṃ cīvaraṃ mahantaṃ karoti, mahantaṃ vā khuddakaṃ karoti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ na bhijjati. Ubho koṭiyo majjhe karonto sace pana paṭhamaṃ chinditvā pacchā ghaṭeti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ bhijjati. Atha ghaṭetvā chindati, na bhijjati. Rajakehi dhovāpetvā setaṃ karontassāpi adhiṭṭhānaṃ adhiṭṭhānameva. Vassānamāsātikkamenāpīti ettha pi-saddo sampiṇḍanattho. Tena na kevalaṃ pubbe vuttena dānādinā aṭṭhavidheneva kāraṇena vassikasāṭikā adhiṭṭhānaṃ vijahati, atha kho vassānamāsātikkamenapīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Esa nayo ābādhavūpasamenāpīti etthāpi. Vikappanasikkhāpadeti (pāci. 372 ādayo) pācittiye surāpānavaggassa navamasikkhāpade.

'By the measure of the back of the little finger's nail' shows the lower limit. 'From the edge' means from the inside. But if one first applies a patch to a weak spot and later cuts away the weak spot, the determination is not broken. This is the same method in the case of replacing a patch. In the case of a double-layered robe, if a hole appears in one layer or it wears out, the determination is not broken. If one makes a small robe large, or a large robe small, the determination is not broken. If, when bringing both ends to the middle, one first cuts and then joins, the determination is broken. But if one joins first and then cuts, it is not broken. Even for one who has it washed by a washerman and made white, the determination remains the determination. Regarding 'also by the passing of the rains-retreat months': here the word 'also' has a cumulative sense. By this, the meaning should be seen thus: it is not only for the eight reasons previously stated, beginning with giving, that the determination of a rains-retreat cloth is abandoned, but also by the passing of the rains-retreat months. This same method applies also in the case of 'also by the subsiding of the illness.' 'In the training rule on allocation' refers to the ninth training rule in the Surāpāna Vagga of the Pācittiya.

Taṃ atikkāmayatoti ettha tanti cīvaraṃ, kālaṃ vā parāmasatīti āha “taṃ yathāvuttajātippamāṇa”ntiādi. Assāti bhikkhussa. Tassa yo aruṇoti tassa cīvaruppādadivasassa yo atikkanto aruṇo. Cīvaruppādadivasena saddhinti cīvaruppādadivasassa aruṇena saddhiṃ. Divasasaddena cettha taṃdivasanissito aruṇo vutto. Idāni yassa ca nissajjitabbaṃ, yathā ca nissajjitabbaṃ, taṃ dassetuṃ “taṃ gahetvā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ nayoti tasmiṃ nissajjane ayaṃ vidhi. Aññathāpīti bhāsantarenāpi, yāya kāyaci bhāsāyapīti attho. Paṭibalenāti vattuṃ samatthena. Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsīti upari saṃvaramāpajjeyyāsi, saṃvutakāyavacīdvāro bhaveyyāsīti attho. Imāni ca “passasī”tiādīni yathākkamaṃ paṭiggāhakadesakehi vattabbavacanāni. Tathā hi “passasī”ti paṭiggāhakena vattabbavacanaṃ, “āma passāmī”ti tadanudesakena vattabbavacanaṃ. “Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī”ti tadanuppaṭiggāhakena vattabbavacanaṃ, “sādhu suṭṭhu saṃvarissāmī”ti tadanudesakena vattabbavacanaṃ. Iminā ca attano āyatiṃ saṃvare patiṭṭhitabhāvaṃ dasseti. Dvīsu, pana sambahulāsu vāti dvīsu vā sambahulāsu vā āpattīsu purimanayeneva vacanabhedo kātabbo. Ñattiyaṃ āpattiṃ sarati vivaratīti ettha “dve [M 0.0285] āpattiyo”ti vā “sambahulā āpattiyo”ti vā [V 0.0263] vacanabhedo kātabbo. Dvīsu, bahūsu vā vacanabhedo kātabboti “saṅgho imāni cīvarānī”ti vatthuvasena vacanabhedo kātabbo.

Here, in 'Taṃ atikkāmayato,' 'taṃ' (it) refers to the robe, or it alludes to the time. Thus it is said: 'Taṃ yathāvuttajātippamāṇa,' and so on. 'Assa' means 'of the bhikkhu.' 'Tassa yo aruṇo' means the dawn that has passed on the day the robe arose for him. 'Cīvaruppādadivasena saddhiṃ' means together with the dawn of the day the robe arose. Here, by the word 'day' is meant the dawn connected with that day. Now, to show to whom it should be relinquished and how it should be relinquished, it is said: 'Taṃ gahetvā,' and so on. 'Tatrāyaṃ nayo' means: this is the method in that relinquishment. 'Aññathāpi' means even in another language; that is, in any language whatsoever. 'Paṭibalena' means by one who is competent to speak. 'Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsi' means: 'You should undertake restraint in the future'; that is, you should become one whose doors of body and speech are restrained. And these words—'passasi,' and so on—are the statements to be spoken in sequence by the receiver and the confessor. For 'Passasi' is the statement to be spoken by the receiver. 'Āma passāmi' is the statement to be spoken in response by the confessor. 'Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsi' is the statement to be spoken by the receiver. 'Sādhu suṭṭhu saṃvarissāmī' is the statement to be spoken in response by the confessor. And by this, one shows that one is established in future restraint. In the case of two or many offenses, however, the variation in wording should be made according to the previous method. In the formal announcement, when one recalls and discloses the offense, the variation in wording should be made as 'dve āpattiyo' or 'sambahulā āpattiyo.' The phrase 'a variation in wording should be made for two or many' means that a variation in wording should be made based on the object, as in 'the Saṅgha... these robes (imāni cīvarāni).'

Evaṃ saṅghassa nissajjanavidhiṃ dassetvā gaṇassa nissajjanavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “gaṇassa pana nissajjantenā”tiādimāha. Tattha sesaṃ purimasadisamevāti nissajjanāpattippaṭiggahaṇanissaṭṭhacīvaradānesu “āyasmantāna”ntiādinā vuttavacanabhedaṃ vinā avasesaṃ saṅghassa nissajjanādīsu vuttasadisamevāti attho.

Having thus shown the method for relinquishing to the Saṅgha, to show the method for relinquishing to a group, he says: 'Gaṇassa pana nissajjantena,' and so on. Herein, 'the rest is just like the previous case' means that apart from the variation in wording mentioned, such as 'āyasmantānaṃ,' in the relinquishment, the acceptance of the offense, and the giving of the relinquished robe, the remainder is just like what was said for relinquishing to the Saṅgha, and so on. This is the meaning.

Idāni puggalassa nissajjanavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “puggalassa panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dvīsu, tīsu vāti dvīsu, tīsu vā āpattīsu ceva dātabbacīvaresu ca. Yathā ca gaṇassa nissajjane, evaṃ dvinnaṃ nissajjanepi pāḷi veditabbā. Yadi hi viseso bhaveyya, yatheva “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kātuṃ, evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbo – byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena te bhikkhū ñāpetabbā”tiādinā (mahāva. 168) nayena tiṇṇaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ vatvā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dvinnaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kātuṃ, evañca pana, bhikkhave, kattabbo – therena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅga”ntiādinā nayena visuṃyeva dvinnaṃ pārisuddhiuposatho vutto, evaṃ idhāpi visuṃ pāḷiṃ vadeyya. Yasmā pana natthi, tasmā avatvāva gatoti gaṇassa vuttā pāḷiyevettha pāḷi. Āpattippaṭiggahaṇe pana ayaṃ viseso – yathā gaṇassa nissajjitvā āpattiyā desiyamānāya āpattippaṭiggāhako bhikkhu ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, evaṃ aṭṭhapetvā dvīsu aññatarena yathā ekapuggalo paṭiggaṇhāti, evaṃ āpatti paṭiggahetabbā. Dvinnañhi ñattiṭṭhapanaṃ nāma natthi. Yadi siyā, dvinnaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ visuṃ na vadeyya. Nissaṭṭhacīvaradānepi yathā “imaṃ cīvaraṃ āyasmato dammī”ti eko vadati, evaṃ “mayaṃ imaṃ cīvaraṃ āyasmato demā”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Ito garukatarānipi hi ñattidutiyakammāni apaloketvā kātabbānīti vuttāni atthi, tesaṃ etaṃ anulomaṃ. Tenevāha “dvinnaṃ panā”tiādi. Nissaṭṭhacīvaraṃ pana dātabbameva, adātuṃ na labbhati. Vinayakammamattameva hetaṃ. Na taṃ tena saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā puggalassa vā dinnameva hoti. Tenāha “nissaṭṭhavatthu”ntiādi.

Now, to show the method for relinquishing to an individual, it is said: 'Puggalassa pana,' and so on. Herein, 'in the case of two or three' refers to both offenses and robes to be given involving two or three bhikkhus. And just as in the case of relinquishing to a group, so the Pāḷi should be understood for relinquishing to two. For if there were a difference, just as after stating the purity Uposatha for three with the words, 'I allow, bhikkhus, three to perform the purity Uposatha…' (Mahāvagga 168), the purity Uposatha for two was stated separately with the words, 'I allow, bhikkhus, two to perform the purity Uposatha…,' so too here he would have stated a separate Pāḷi text. But since there is none, it is understood without being stated that the Pāḷi stated for a group is the Pāḷi here. However, in the acceptance of the offense, there is this difference: whereas when relinquishing to a group and the offense is being confessed, the bhikkhu receiving the offense puts forward a motion, here, without putting forward a motion, one of the two should accept the offense in the way a single individual accepts it. For there is no such thing as putting forward a motion for two. If there were, he would not have stated the purity Uposatha for two separately. Also in the giving of the relinquished robe, just as one says, 'I give this robe to the venerable one,' so it is proper to say, 'We give this robe to the venerable one.' For there are even more serious formal acts with a motion as the second step that are said to be done after announcing them; this is in conformity with that. Therefore he says: 'Dvinnaṃ pana,' and so on. The relinquished robe, however, must be given back; it is not allowable not to give it. This is merely a formal act of the Vinaya. By this it is not actually given to the Saṅgha, or a group, or an individual. Therefore it is said: 'Nissaṭṭhavatthu,' and so on.

Anissajjitvā [M 0.0286] paribhuñjantassa dukkaṭanti sakiṃ nivatthaṃ vā sakiṃ pārutaṃ vā kāyato amocetvā divasampi carati, ekameva dukkaṭaṃ. Mocetvā nivāseti vā pārupati vā, payoge payoge dukkaṭaṃ. Dunnivatthaṃ vā duppārutaṃ vā saṇṭhāpentassa anāpatti. Aññassa taṃ paribhuñjatopi [V 0.0264] anāpatti. “Aññena kataṃ paṭilabhitvā paribhuñjatī”tiādivacanañcettha (pārā. 570) sādhakaṃ. Dasāhaṃ anatikkantepi atikkantasaññino, vematikassa ca dukkaṭanti etthāpi “paribhuñjantassā”ti ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Atikkante anatikkantasaññinopīti dasāhaṃ atikkante cīvare “anatikkantaṃ ida”nti evaṃ saññino, dasāhe vā atikkante “anatikkanto dasāho”ti evaṃ saññino.

'For one who uses it without having relinquished it, there is a dukkaṭa offense': If one goes about for a whole day wearing it once as a lower robe or once as an upper robe without removing it from the body, there is only one dukkaṭa offense. If one removes it and then wears it as a lower robe or drapes it as an upper robe, there is a dukkaṭa offense for each effort. There is no offense for one who adjusts a poorly worn lower robe or a poorly draped upper robe. There is also no offense for another who uses it. The statement, 'Having received what was made by another, one uses it…' (Pārā. 570), is the proof here. 'Even when the ten days have not been exceeded, for one who perceives them as exceeded and for one who is in doubt, there is a dukkaṭa offense': here too the words 'for one who uses it' should be supplied and connected. 'Also for one who perceives it as not exceeded when it is exceeded' means: when the ten days for the robe have been exceeded, one perceives, 'This has not been exceeded'; or when the ten-day period has been exceeded, one perceives, 'The ten-day period has not been exceeded'.

Idāni “anadhiṭṭhite adhiṭṭhitasaññino nissaggiya”ntiādiāpattivāraṃ saṅgahetvā dassento “tathā”tiādimāha. Tathāti yathā dasāhaṃ atikkante saññābhedena tikapācittiyaṃ, tathā anadhiṭṭhitādīsu sattasu vikappesu adhiṭṭhitādisaññābhedatoti attho. Tattha avissajjite vissajjitasaññinoti kassaci adinne apariccatte “dinnaṃ pariccattaṃ mayā”ti evaṃ saññino. Anaṭṭhe naṭṭhasaññinoti attano cīvarena saddhiṃ bahūni aññesaṃ cīvarāni ekato ṭhapitāni, tāni ce corā haranti, tatresa attano cīvare anaṭṭhe naṭṭhasaññī hoti, tassa naṭṭhasaññino. Esa nayo avinaṭṭhādīsupi. Avilutteti ettha pana gabbhaṃ bhinditvā pasayhāvahāravasena avilutteti veditabbaṃ.

Now, summarizing and showing the section on offenses beginning, 'Anadhiṭṭhite adhiṭṭhitasaññino nissaggiyaṃ,' he says: 'Tathā,' and so on. 'Tathā' means: just as when the ten days have been exceeded there is a threefold pācittiya based on the distinctions of perception, so too in the seven alternatives beginning with 'undetermined,' based on the distinctions of perception regarding 'determined,' and so on. This is the meaning. Herein, 'perceiving as relinquished what has not been relinquished' means: perceiving of what has not been given to anyone, not been surrendered, 'It has been given by me, it has been surrendered by me.' 'Perceiving as lost what is not lost' means: one's own robe has been placed together with many robes belonging to others, and thieves carry them off; in this case, regarding one's own robe which is not lost, one perceives it as lost—this is 'one who perceives it as lost.' This is the method also for 'not destroyed,' and so on. Here, however, 'not plundered' should be understood in the sense of not carried off by force after breaking into an inner room.

Vissajjiteti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.469) aññassa dinne. Kathaṃ pana dinnaṃ hoti, kathaṃ gahitaṃ? “Imaṃ tuyhaṃ demi, dadāmi, dajjāmi, oṇojemi, pariccajāmi, vissajjāmi, nissajjāmī”ti vā vadati, “itthannāmassa demi…pe… nissajjāmī”ti vā vadati, sammukhāpi parammukhāpi dinnaṃyeva hoti. “Tuyhaṃ gaṇhāhī”ti vutte “mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti vadati, sudinnaṃ, suggahitañca. “Tava santakaṃ karohi, tava santakaṃ hotu, tava santakaṃ karissasī”ti vutte “mama santakaṃ karomi, mama santakaṃ hotu, mama santakaṃ karissāmī”ti vadati, duddinnaṃ, duggahitañca. Neva dātā dātuṃ jānāti, na itaro gahetuṃ. Sace pana “tava santakaṃ karohī”ti vutte “sādhu, bhante, mayhaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti gaṇhāti, suggahitaṃ, sace pana eko “gaṇhāhī”ti vadati, itaro “na gaṇhāmī”ti vadati, puna so “dinnaṃ mayā [M 0.0287] tuyhaṃ, gaṇhāhī”ti vadati, itaropi “na mayhaṃ iminā attho”ti vadati. Tato purimopi “mayā dinna”nti dasāhaṃ atikkāmeti, pacchimopi “mayā paṭikkhitta”nti, kassāpattīti? Na kassaci. Yassa pana ruccati, tena adhiṭṭhahitvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo pana adhiṭṭhāne vematiko, tena kiṃ kātabbaṃ? Vematikabhāvaṃ ārocetvā “sace anadhiṭṭhitaṃ bhavissati, evaṃ me kappiyaṃ hotī”ti vatvā vuttanayeneva nissajjitabbaṃ. Na hi evaṃ jānāpetvā vinayakammaṃ karontassa musāvādo hoti.

'Relinquished' means given to another. But how is it given, and how is it received? When one says, 'I give this to you, I offer, I present, I bestow, I surrender, I release, I relinquish,' or says, 'I give to so-and-so...I relinquish,' it is properly given whether face-to-face or in one's absence. If, when told, 'Take this for yourself,' one says, 'I take it for myself,' it is well-given and well-received. If, when told, 'Make it your own, let it be your own, you will make it your own,' one replies, 'I make it my own, let it be my own, I will make it my own,' it is poorly given and poorly received. Neither the giver knows how to give, nor the other how to receive. But if, when told, 'Make it your own,' one takes it, saying, 'Good, venerable sir, I take it for myself,' it is well-received. However, if one says, 'Take it,' and the other says, 'I will not take it,' and the first one says again, 'I have given it to you, take it,' but the other still says, 'I have no use for this,' then if the first one lets the ten days pass thinking, 'It has been given by me,' and the latter does so thinking, 'It has been rejected by me,' to whom is there an offense? To no one. But whoever wants it should determine it and use it. But what is to be done by one who is in doubt about the determination? Having announced one's state of doubt, one should say, 'If it happens to be undetermined, may it thus be allowable for me,' and then relinquish it in the way that has been stated. For there is no false speech for one who performs a Vinaya act after having made it known thus.

Yathā [V 0.0265] ca idaṃ, evaṃ ito parānipīti yathā idaṃ atirekacīvaradhāraṇasikkhāpadaṃ ācāravipatti, evaṃ ito parānipi sikkhāpadāni ācāravipattiyevāti attho. Tenāha “ubhatopātimokkhesū”tiādi. Ājīvavipattipaccayā pana ṭhapetvā dubbhāsitaṃ cha āpattikkhandhā paññattāti –

'And as this one, so too those that follow' means: just as this training rule on keeping an extra robe is a corruption of conduct, so too the training rules that follow this are also corruptions of conduct. This is the meaning. Therefore it is said: 'In both Pātimokkhas,' and so on. However, on account of a corruption of livelihood, excepting wrong speech, six classes of offenses are laid down—

“Ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapati, āpatti pārājikassa. Ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā sañcarittaṃ samāpajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa. Ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā ‘yo te vihāre vasati, so bhikkhu arahā’ti bhaṇati, paṭivijānantassa āpatti thullaccayassa. Ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā bhikkhu paṇītabhojanāni agilāno attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pācittiyassa. Ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā bhikkhunī paṇītabhojanāni agilānā attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa. Ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā bhikkhu sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilāno attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (pari. 287) –

“For the sake of livelihood, for the purpose of livelihood, a person of evil wishes, overcome by desire, claims a non-existent, unreal superhuman state; this is an offense of defeat. For the sake of livelihood, for the purpose of livelihood, one engages in matchmaking; this is an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Sangha. For the sake of livelihood, for the purpose of livelihood, knowing it to be untrue, one says, ‘The bhikkhu who lives in your monastery is an arahant’; this is a grave offense. For the sake of livelihood, for the purpose of livelihood, a bhikkhu who is not ill, having requested choice foods for his own sake, eats them; this is an offense entailing expiation. For the sake of livelihood, for the purpose of livelihood, a bhikkhunī who is not ill, having requested choice foods for her own sake, eats them; this is an offense to be acknowledged. For the sake of livelihood, for the purpose of livelihood, a bhikkhu who is not ill, having requested soup or rice for his own sake, eats it; this is an offense of wrong-doing.”

Evaṃ pārājikādivasena ṭhapetvā dubbhāsitaṃ ājīvavipattipaccayā cha āpattikkhandhā paññattā. Diṭṭhivipattipaccayā pācittiyadukkaṭavasena dve āpattikkhandhā paññattāti samanubhāsanāya pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissajjane ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ, kammavācāpariyosāne pācittiyanti evaṃ diṭṭhivipattipaccayā [M 0.0288] pācittiyadukkaṭavasena dve āpattikkhandhā paññattā. Etthāti vipattikathāsu.

Thus, setting aside wrong speech, six classes of offenses are laid down on account of a failure in livelihood, by way of defeat and so on. On account of a failure in view, two classes of offenses are laid down, namely, expiation and wrong-doing. For not renouncing a wrong view after being formally admonished, there is an offense of wrong-doing at the motion, and an offense of expiation at the conclusion of the formal act. Thus, on account of a failure in view, two classes of offenses are laid down, namely, expiation and wrong-doing. Here ends the discussion on failures.

Gaṇanupagatāti divasagaṇanaṃ upagatabhāvo. Aññehi “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa demā”ti parahatthe dinnampi “na tāva taṃ gaṇanupagaṃ, yāva na hatthaṃ gacchatī”ti (mahāva. 259) cammakkhandhake vuttattā yāva āharitvā vā na dinnaṃ, “tumhākaṃ, bhante, cīvaraṃ uppanna”nti pahiṇitvā vā anārocitaṃ, tāva divasagaṇanaṃ na upeti, anadhiṭṭhitaṃ vaṭṭati. Yadā pana ānetvā dinnaṃ hoti, “uppanna”nti vā sutaṃ, tato paṭṭhāya gaṇanupagaṃ hoti, antodasāhe adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Kathinasaññitaṃ samuṭṭhānamassāti kathinasamuṭṭhānaṃ, tatiyachaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānavasena dvisamuṭṭhānanti attho. Kāyavācāhi kattabbaadhiṭṭhānavikappanānaṃ akaraṇena kāyavācato, citte pana sati kāyavācācittato ca samuṭṭhātīti vuttaṃ hoti. Anadhiṭṭhānāvikappanavasena āpajjanato [V 0.0266] akiriyaṃ. Ajānantopi āpajjatīti nosaññāvimokkhaṃ. Kāyadvāre ca vacīdvāre ca kattabbākaraṇato kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ.

‘Included in the count’ means the state of having entered the counting of days. Although it is said by others, “We give this robe to so-and-so,” and it is given into another’s hand, because it is said in the Chapter on Hides, “It is not yet included in the count so long as it does not reach his hand,” so long as it has not been brought and given, or a message has not been sent and announced, “Venerable sir, a robe has arisen for you,” the counting of days does not begin; it is permissible for it to be undetermined. But when it has been brought and given, or when it is heard that it has “arisen,” from then on it is included in the count and must be determined within ten days. ‘Its origin is designated by the kathina’ means it has a kathina-origin; that is, it has two origins by way of the third and sixth origins. It is said that it originates from body and speech through the non-performance of the determination or disposal that should be done by body and speech; but when the mind is present, it originates from body, speech, and mind. It is non-action because one falls into it by way of not determining or disposing. It is not an exemption through non-perception because one falls into it even without knowing. It is bodily action and verbal action because of the non-performance of what should be done through the door of the body and the door of speech.

Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Kathina training rule is finished.

2. Udositasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Udosita Training Rule

Bhikkhunāti bhikkhussāti attho, sāmiatthe cetaṃ karaṇavacanaṃ. Tenāha “purimasikkhāpade viyā”tiādi. Atha kasmā karaṇavaseneva karaṇavacanassa atthaṃ aggahetvā sāmivasena attho veditabboti āha “karaṇavasena hī”tiādi. Hīti kāraṇatthe nipāto. Chinnapalibodhoti chinnacīvarāvāsapalibodho. Ekāva ratti ekarattaṃ, samāsantagatassa atthaṃ. Tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ samāhāroti ticīvaraṃ. Tena ticīvarena, tīhi cīvarehīti attho. Ekena vippavutthopi (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.475-476) hi ticīvarena vippavuttho nāma hoti paṭisiddhapariyāpannena vippavutthattā, avayavepi vā samudāyavohārato. Tenāha “ticīvarādhiṭṭhānanayenā”tiādi.

‘By a bhikkhu’ means ‘of a bhikkhu’; this instrumental word is in the sense of ownership. Therefore he said, ‘as in the previous training rule,’ etc. Then why should the meaning be understood in the sense of ownership, without taking the meaning of the instrumental word in the instrumental sense? He said, ‘For in the instrumental sense…’ etc. ‘Hi’ is a particle in the sense of reason. ‘One who has cut off impediments’ means one who has cut off the impediments concerning the robe and the dwelling. ‘One single night’ is ekarattaṃ; this is the meaning of the final member of the compound. ‘A collection of three robes’ is ticīvaraṃ, the triple robe. ‘With that triple robe’ means with the three robes. For even if one is separated from one, one is said to be separated from the triple robe, because one is separated from what is included in the prohibition, or because the term for the whole is used for a part. Therefore he said, ‘by the method of determining the triple robe,’ etc.

Idāni [M 0.0289] vippavāsalakkhaṇavavatthāpanatthaṃ “gāmo ekūpacāro”tiādimāha. Tattha nivesananti udositādīnaṃ vasena akatāya patissayavikatiyā adhivacanaṃ. Udositoti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.482-487) yānādīnaṃ bhaṇḍānaṃ sālā. Yo “udavasito”tipi vuccati. Aṭṭoti paṭirājādipaṭibāhanatthaṃ iṭṭhakāhi kato bahalabhittiko catupañcabhūmiko patissayaviseso. “Aṭṭoti bahalabhittikagehaṃ, yassa gopānasiyo aggahetvā iṭṭhakāhi eva chadanaṃ hotī”ti apare. “Aṭṭākārena karīyatī”tipi vadanti. Māḷoti ekakūṭasaṅgahito caturassapāsādo, ekakūṭasaṅgahito vā anekakoṇavanto patissayaviseso. “Māḷoti vaṭṭākārena katasenāsana”nti apare. Pāsādoti dīghapāsādo, aḍḍhayogādibhedo aṭṭamāḷahammiyavajjito sabbo vā pāsādo. Hammiyanti muṇḍacchadanapāsādo. “Candiyaṅgaṇayutta”nti apare. Nāvāti thalaṭṭhaudakaṭṭhavasena dvidhā nāvā. Satthoti jaṅghasattho, sakaṭasattho vā. Dhaññakaraṇanti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.491-494) khalaṃ vuccati. Ārāmoti pupphārāmo, phalārāmo vā. Vihāroti saparikkhitto vā aparikkhitto vā sakalo āvāso. “Gehampī”ti keci. Nivesanādīni cettha gāmato bahi niviṭṭhāni gahitāni. Antogāme ṭhitānaṃ pana gāmaggahaṇeneva gahitattā gāmaparihāroyevāti. “Nivesanādayo hammiyapariyosānā [V 0.0267] gāmaparikkhepato bahi niviṭṭhā”ti apare. Hatthapāsātikkameti ettha hatthapāso nāma aḍḍhateyyaratanappamāṇo padeso, tassa atikkamo hatthapāsātikkamo, tasmiṃ hatthapāsātikkame. Hatthapāsabbhantare pana vatthuṃ vaṭṭati. Taṃ pamāṇaṃ atikkamitvā sacepi iddhimā bhikkhu ākāse aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpeti, nissaggiyameva hoti.

Now, for the purpose of establishing the characteristic of separation, he said, ‘A village has a single precinct,’ etc. Therein, ‘dwelling’ (nivesana) is a term for a shelter that is not a modified residence, such as a plastered hall (udosita) and so on. A plastered hall (udosita) is a hall for goods such as vehicles; it is also called udavasita. A fort (aṭṭa) is a special kind of residence with thick walls made of bricks to ward off rival kings and so on, with four or five stories. Others say: ‘A fort is a house with thick walls, the roof of which is made of bricks without using rafters.’ Some also say: ‘It is made in the shape of a fort.’ A pavilion (māḷa) is a square palace with a single pinnacle, or a special kind of residence with many corners and a single pinnacle. Others say: ‘A pavilion is a dwelling made in a circular shape.’ A palace (pāsāda) is a long palace, of various kinds such as the half-yoke style, or any palace apart from a fort, pavilion, or upper chamber. An upper chamber (hammiya) is a palace with a flat roof. Others say: ‘It has a moon-terrace.’ A boat (nāvā) is twofold: on land and on water. A caravan (sattha) is a caravan on foot or a caravan of carts. A place for grain (dhaññakaraṇa) is called a threshing floor (khala). A park (ārāma) is a flower park or a fruit park. A monastery (vihāra) is an entire residence, whether enclosed or not. Some say ‘a house too.’ Here, dwellings and so on situated outside a village are taken. But those situated inside a village are included by the taking of ‘village,’ thus they are within the village’s confines. Others say: ‘Dwellings and so on, up to upper chambers, are situated outside the village enclosure.’ ‘On transgressing the hand’s reach’: here, a ‘hand’s reach’ (hatthapāsa) is a space measuring two and a half cubits. Transgressing it is ‘transgressing the hand’s reach.’ Within a hand’s reach, it is permissible to stay. But if a bhikkhu with psychic power makes the dawn arise while he is in the sky beyond that measure, it becomes subject to forfeiture.

Ayaṃ panettha vinicchayo – sace (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.477-478) gāmo ekassa rañño vā bhojakassa vā vasena ekakulassa hoti, pākārādinā parikkhittattā ekūpacāro ca, evarūpe gāme cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā tasmiṃ gāmabbhantare yathārucitaṭṭhāne vasitabbaṃ, sace aparikkhitto, yasmiṃ ghare cīvaraṃ nikkhittaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ ghare vasitabbaṃ, tassa gharassa samantato hatthapāsā vā na vijahitabbaṃ.

Here is the legal decision on this: If a village belongs to a single family under a single king or chieftain, and it has a single precinct because it is enclosed by a wall and so on, in such a village, having deposited the robe, one may dwell in any preferred place within that village. If it is unenclosed, one should dwell in the house where the robe has been deposited, and one should not leave the hand’s reach all around that house.

Sace [M 0.0290] gāmo vesālikusinārādayo viya nānārājūnaṃ vā bhojakānaṃ vā hoti, vuttappakārena parikkhitto ca, evarūpe gāme yasmiṃ ghare cīvaraṃ nikkhittaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ ghare vā vatthabbaṃ, tassa gharassa hatthapāsā vā na vijahitabbaṃ. Yassā vīthiyā gharaṃ hoti, tassā vīthiyā tassa gharassa sammukhāṭṭhāne sabhāyaṃ vā gharadvāre vā vatthabbaṃ, tesaṃ sabhādvārānaṃ hatthapāsā vā na vijahitabbaṃ.

If a village, like Vesālī, Kusinārā, and so on, belongs to various kings or chieftains, and is enclosed in the way described, in such a village one should dwell in the house where the robe has been deposited, and one should not leave the hand’s reach of that house. On whatever street the house is, one should dwell in the assembly hall or at the house door in a place facing that house on that street, and one should not leave the hand’s reach of those assembly halls or house doors.

Sace so gāmo aparikkhitto, yasmiṃ ghare cīvaraṃ nikkhittaṃ, tattha vā tassa hatthapāse vā vatthabbaṃ. Nivesane pana sace ekakulassa nivesanaṃ hoti, parikkhittañca, antonivesane cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā antonivesane vatthabbaṃ. Aparikkhittaṃ ce hoti, yasmiṃ gabbhe cīvaraṃ nikkhittaṃ, tasmiṃ vatthabbaṃ, tassa gabbhassa hatthapāsā vā na vijahitabbaṃ.

If that village is unenclosed, one should dwell in the house where the robe has been deposited or within its hand’s reach. But in the case of a dwelling, if the dwelling belongs to a single family and is enclosed, having deposited the robe inside the dwelling, one should dwell inside the dwelling. If it is unenclosed, one should dwell in the inner chamber where the robe has been deposited, and one should not leave the hand’s reach of that inner chamber.

Sace nānākulassa nivesanaṃ hoti, parikkhittañca, yasmiṃ gabbhe cīvaraṃ nikkhittaṃ, tasmiṃ gabbhe vatthabbaṃ, sabbesaṃ sādhāraṇadvāramūle vā tesaṃ gabbhadvāramūlānaṃ hatthapāsā vā na vijahitabbaṃ. Aparikkhittaṃ ce, yasmiṃ gabbhe cīvaraṃ nikkhittaṃ, tasmiṃ gabbhe vatthabbaṃ, tassa gabbhassa hatthapāsā vā na vijahitabbaṃ. Esa nayo udositādīsupi.

If the dwelling belongs to various families and is enclosed, one should dwell in the inner chamber where the robe has been deposited, or at the common doorway for all, and one should not leave the hand’s reach of the doorways of those inner chambers. If it is unenclosed, one should dwell in the inner chamber where the robe has been deposited, and one should not leave the hand’s reach of that inner chamber. This is the method also in the case of plastered halls and so on.

Sattho pana jaṅghasattho vā hotu, sakaṭasattho vā. Sace ekakulassa sattho hoti, satthe cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā purato vā pacchato vā sattabbhantarā na vijahitabbā, passato abbhantaraṃ na vijahitabbaṃ. Sace (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.489) sattho gacchanto gāmaṃ vā nadiṃ vā pariyādiyitvā [V 0.0268] tiṭṭhati, antopaviṭṭhena saddhiṃ ekābaddho hutvā orañca pārañca pharitvā ṭhito hoti, satthaparihārova labbhati. Atha gāme vā nadiyā vā pariyāpanno hoti antopaviṭṭho, gāmaparihāro ceva nadiparihāro ca labbhati. Sace vihārasīmaṃ atikkamitvā tiṭṭhati, antosīmāya ca cīvaraṃ hoti, vihāraṃ gantvā vasitabbaṃ. Sace bahisīmāya cīvaraṃ hoti, satthasamīpeyeva vasitabbaṃ. Sace gacchanto sakaṭe vā bhagge, goṇe vā naṭṭhe antarā chijjati, yasmiṃ koṭṭhāse cīvaraṃ nikkhittaṃ, tattha vasitabbaṃ.

Now, as for a caravan, whether it be a foot caravan or a cart caravan: if the caravan belongs to a single family, having placed the robe in the caravan, one should not go beyond seven abbhantaras in front or behind, nor beyond the range of sight. If the caravan, while travelling, encompasses a village or a river and stops, being unified and pervading both the near and far banks, the precinct of the caravan is obtained. But if it is encompassed by a village or a river and one has entered within it, the precinct of the village and the precinct of the river are obtained. If it stops after having crossed the monastery boundary, and the robe is within the boundary, one should go to the monastery and reside there. If the robe is outside the boundary, one should reside right near the caravan. If, while travelling, the caravan is broken up in the middle because a cart has broken or oxen have been lost, one should reside in whichever section the robe was placed.

Khettepi (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.490) sace ekakulassa khettaṃ hoti, parikkhittañca, antokhette cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā antokhette vatthabbaṃ. Sace aparikkhittaṃ, hatthapāsā [M 0.0291] cīvaraṃ na vijahitabbaṃ. Sace nānākulassa khettaṃ hoti, parikkhittañca, antokhette cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā khettadvāramūle vā vatthabbaṃ, tassa hatthapāsā vā na vijahitabbaṃ. Sace aparikkhittaṃ, cīvaraṃ hatthapāsā na vijahitabbaṃ. Esa nayo dhaññakaraṇārāmesu dvīsupi. Vihāre pana nivesane vuttasadisova vinicchayo.

In the case of a field, too: if the field belongs to a single family and is enclosed, having placed the robe within the field, one should reside within the field. If it is unenclosed, the robe should not be left beyond arm's reach. If the field belongs to various families and is enclosed, having placed the robe within the field, one should reside at the entrance to the field or not leave it beyond arm's reach. If it is unenclosed, the robe should not be left beyond arm's reach. This is the same method for both threshing floors and parks. But in a monastery or a dwelling, the ruling is just as has been stated.

Rukkhamūle pana yaṃ majjhanhike kāle samantā chāyā pharati, tasmiṃ ṭhāne aviraḷe padese tassa chāyāya phuṭṭhokāsassa antoyeva nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace viraḷasākhassa rukkhassa ātapena phuṭṭhokāse ṭhapeti, aruṇuggamane ca so bhikkhu tassa hatthapāse na hoti, aññasmiṃ ṭhāne tassa chāyāyapi hoti, nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Sace nānākulassa rukkho hoti, cīvarassa hatthapāsā na vijahitabbaṃ.

But at the foot of a tree, the robe should be placed right within the space touched by the shade in a dense spot in the area where the shade spreads all around at midday. If one places it in a spot touched by the sun under a tree with sparse branches, and at the rising of the dawn that bhikkhu is not within its arm's reach and its shade is also in another place, it becomes subject to forfeiture. If the tree belongs to various families, the robe should not be left beyond arm's reach.

Ajjhokāse pana viñjhāṭaviādīsu araññesupi samuddamajjhe macchabandhānaṃ agamanapathadīpakesupi cīvaraṃ ṭhapetvā tato samantā sattabbhantare padese yattha katthaci vasitabbaṃ, ito aññattha vasanto vippavuttho nāma hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

But in an open space—in wildernesses such as the Vindhya forest, or even in the middle of the ocean on islands that serve as markers on the routes of fishermen—having placed the robe, one should reside anywhere within a space of seven abbhantaras all around from there. It should be understood that one who resides elsewhere than this is called 'separated'.

Imassa pana vitthārassa idha avuttattā, samantapāsādikāyañca vuttattā “ayamettha saṅkhepo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Etthāti “ticīvarena vippavaseyyā”ti etasmiṃ pade. Saṅkhepoti saṅkhepavaṇṇanā. Ettha pana pāḷiyaṃ (pārā. 477) “gāmo ekūpacāro nānūpacāro”tiādinā avisesena mātikaṃ nikkhipitvāpi gāmanivesanaudositakhettadhaññakaraṇaārāmavihārānaṃ ekūpacāranānūpacāratā “gāmo ekūpacāro nāma ekakulassa gāmo hoti parikkhitto ca aparikkhitto cā”tiādinā (pārā. 478) parikkhittāparikkhittavasena [V 0.0269] vibhattā. Aṭṭamāḷapāsādahammiyanāvāsattharukkhamūlaajjhokāsānaṃ pana evaṃ avatvā “ekakulassa aṭṭo hoti, nānākulassa aṭṭo hotī”tiādinā (pārā. 484) nayena ekakulanānākulavasena ca ante “ajjhokāso ekūpacāro nāma agāmake araññe samantā sattabbhantarā ekūpacāro, tato paraṃ nānūpacāroti (pārā. 494) ca evaṃ ekūpacāranānūpacāratā vibhattā. Tasmā gāmādīsu parikkhittaṃ ekūpacāraṃ, aparikkhittaṃ [M 0.0292] nānūpacāranti ca, aṭṭādisu yaṃ ekakulassa, taṃ ekūpacāraṃ, yaṃ nānākulassa, taṃ nānūpacāranti ca gahetabbaṃ. Ajjhokāse vuttanayena gahetabbaṃ. Upacāroti hi “gāmo ekūpacāro nānūpacāro”tiādīsu dvāraṃ, “ajjhokāso ekūpacāro”ti ettha samantā sattabbhantarasaṅkhātaṃ pamāṇanti apare.

But since the detailed explanation of this is not stated here, and since it is stated in the Samantapāsādikā, the words 'This here is a summary,' etc., are said. 'Here' means in this phrase: 'he might be separated from his three robes.' 'Summary' means a summary explanation. Here, in the Pāli text, although the matrix is laid down without distinction with 'a village is of single precinct or of multiple precincts,' etc., the state of having a single precinct or multiple precincts for a village, dwelling, storehouse, field, threshing floor, park, and monastery is distinguished by way of being enclosed or unenclosed, with 'A village of single precinct means a village belonging to a single family, and it is enclosed or unenclosed,' etc. But for a watchtower, storied dwelling, mansion, peaked-roof house, boat, couch, the foot of a tree, and an open space, without stating it thus, the state of having a single precinct or multiple precincts is distinguished by way of belonging to a single family or various families, with the method 'A watchtower belongs to a single family; a watchtower belongs to various families,' etc., and at the end: 'An open space is of single precinct means that in a villageless wilderness, the single precinct is seven abbhantaras all around; beyond that it is of multiple precincts.' Therefore, for villages and so on, what is enclosed should be taken as of single precinct, and what is unenclosed as of multiple precincts. For watchtowers and so on, what belongs to a single family should be taken as of single precinct, and what belongs to various families as of multiple precincts. In the case of an open space, it should be taken according to the method stated. For according to some, 'precinct' in 'a village is of single precinct or of multiple precincts,' etc., means an entrance, while here in 'an open space is of single precinct,' it means the measure described as seven abbhantaras all around.

Aññatra bhikkhusammutiyāti bhikkhuno saṅghena dinnā sammuti bhikkhusammuti, taṃ vināti attho. Tenāha “yaṃ saṅgho”tiādi. Avippavāsasammutiṃ detīti avippavāsā sammuti, avippavāsāya vā sammuti avippavāsasammuti, taṃ ñattidutiyena kammena detīti attho.

'Except by the bhikkhus' consensus': the consensus given by the Saṅgha to a bhikkhu is the 'bhikkhus' consensus'; the meaning is 'without that.' Therefore it is said: 'what the Saṅgha,' etc. 'He gives the consensus for non-separation': the consensus for non-separation, or the consensus concerning non-separation, is the 'consensus for non-separation.' The meaning is that one gives it by means of an act consisting of a motion and one announcement.

Santaruttarenāti “antara”nti antaravāsako vuccati, “uttara”nti uttarāsaṅgo, saha antarena uttaraṃ santaruttaraṃ, tena santaruttarena, saha antaravāsakena uttarāsaṅgenāti attho. Antoaruṇe paccuddhaṭeti nivattitvā sampāpuṇitumasakkontena tattheva ṭhatvā anto aruṇe paccuddhaṭe. Paccāgantabbanti yathā rogo na kuppati, tathā puna cīvarassa ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ āgantabbaṃ. Yato paṭṭhāya hi satthaṃ vā pariyesati, “gacchāmī”ti ābhogaṃ vā karoti, tato paṭṭhāya vaṭṭati. “Na dāni gamissāmī”ti evaṃ pana dhuranikkhepaṃ karontena paccuddharitabbaṃ “atirekacīvaraṭṭhāne ṭhassatī”ti. Tenāha “tattheva vā ṭhitena paccuddharitabba”nti. Soti yassa sammuti dinnā, so rogo. Laddhakappiyameva puna sammutidānakiccaṃ natthīti adhippāyo.

'With the inner and outer robes': 'inner' is said for the inner robe; 'outer' is said for the upper robe. 'With the inner and outer' is santaruttaraṃ; the meaning is 'with the inner robe and the upper robe.' 'To be rescinded before dawn': by one who is unable to arrive after turning back, it is to be rescinded before dawn while staying right there. 'One must return': one must return to the place where the robe was put down in such a way that the illness does not become aggravated. For it is allowable from the time one starts searching for a caravan or makes the resolution, 'I will go.' But one who lays down the yoke, thinking, 'Now I will not go,' should rescind the determination with the thought, 'It will stand in the category of an extra robe.' Therefore it is said: 'or it should be rescinded by one staying right there.' 'That': that illness for which the consensus was given. The intention is that since what is allowable has been obtained, there is no further need to give consensus.

Adhiṭṭhitacīvaratāti ticīvarādhiṭṭhānanayena adhiṭṭhitacīvaratā. Vippavāso nāma yadi baddhasīmāyaṃ cīvaraṃ hoti, tato bahi aruṇuṭṭhāpanaṃ. Atha abaddhasīmāyaṃ, yathāvuttagāmādīnaṃ bahi hatthapāsātikkame aruṇuṭṭhāpanaṃ. Baddhasīmāyaṃ pana yattha katthaci cīvaraṃ ṭhapetvā antosīmāyameva yattha katthaci vasituṃ vaṭṭati. Idha apaccuddharaṇaṃ akiriyāti sambandho.

'The state of having a determined robe': the state of having a determined robe by the method of determining the three robes. 'Separation' means: if the robe is within a bounded boundary, it is the rising of the dawn while one is outside it. If it is in an unbounded boundary, it is the rising of the dawn when one has gone beyond arm's reach outside the aforesaid village, etc. But in a bounded boundary, having placed the robe anywhere, it is allowable to reside anywhere right within that boundary. Here, the connection is that not rescinding is a non-action.

Udositasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the storehouse is concluded.

3. Akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Out-of-Season Robes

Purimasikkhāpade [M 0.0293][V 0.0270] viya etthāpi bhikkhunāti sāmiatthe karaṇavacananti āha “niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ bhikkhunā”tiādi. “Akālacīvaraṃ nāma anatthate kathine ekādasamāse uppannaṃ, atthate kathine sattamāse uppannaṃ, kālepi ādissa dinnaṃ, etaṃ akālacīvaraṃ nāmā”ti (pārā. 500) padabhājaniyaṃ vuttattā “yvāyaṃ anatthate kathine”tiādimāha. Yvāyaṃ cīvarakālo vuttoti sambandho. Vassānassāti vassānasaṅkhātassa utuno. Pacchimo māso nāma cīvaramāso. Tasmiñhi anatthatepi kathine uppannaṃ cīvaraṃ anadhiṭṭhitaṃ, avikappitaṃ ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati. Pañca māsāti pacchimakattikamāso, hemantikā cattāro cāti pañca māsā. Aññadāti anatthate kathine ekādasamāse, atthate kathine sattamāse. Kālepīti “anatthate kathine cīvaramāso, atthate kathine pañca māsā”ti yathāvuttacīvarakālepi. “Ādinā nayenā”ti iminā “dadāmi dajjāmī”tiādīnaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.469) saṅgaho. Kiñcāpi cetāni sabbāni “akālacīvara”nti vuttāni, tathāpi piṭṭhisamayeyeva uppannāni “akālacīvara”nti idhādhippetāni.

Just as in the previous training rule, here too, regarding the word ‘bhikkhunā,’ he says it is an instrumental in the sense of agent, as in the phrase ‘by a bhikkhu when the robe is finished,’ and so on. Because it is said in the word-analysis: ‘An out-of-season robe, it is said, is one that has arisen during the eleven months when the kathina has not been spread, or one that has arisen during the seven months when the kathina has been spread, or one given with a specific designation even during the season—this is called an out-of-season robe’ (Pārā. 500), he says, ‘that which, when the kathina has not been spread,’ and so on. The connection is: ‘that robe season which has been mentioned.’ ‘Of the rains’ means of the season known as the rains. The last month is called the robe-month.
