For in that month, even when the kathina has not been spread, it is permissible to keep a robe that has arisen if it has not been determined (anadhiṭṭhita) or shared (avikappita). ‘Five months’ means the last month of Kattika and the four winter months, thus five months. ‘At another time’ means during the eleven months when the kathina has not been spread, or during the seven months when it has been spread. ‘Even in season’ means even during the aforementioned robe season, that is: ‘the robe-month when the kathina has not been spread, or the five months when it has been spread.’ By ‘by the method beginning with,’ the inclusion of ‘I give, I would give,’ etc. (Pārā-aṭṭha. 2.469) is indicated. Although all these are called ‘out-of-season robes,’ here only those that have arisen during the ‘back-season’ (piṭṭhisamaya) are intended as ‘out-of-season robes.’

“Kāle saṅghassa idaṃ akālacīvara”nti dinnaṃ pana akālacīvarasāmaññato atthuddhāravasena vuttaṃ. Yathā piṭṭhisamaye uppannaṃ cīvaraṃ vuṭṭhavassehi, sesehi ca sammukhībhūtehi bhājetuṃ labbhatīti akālacīvaraṃ nāma jātaṃ, tathevidampīti tadidaṃ akālacīvarasāmaññaṃ. Yadi evaṃ “puggalassa vā idaṃ tuyhaṃ ‘dammī’tiādinā nayena dinna”nti kasmā vuttaṃ, na hi puggalassa ādissa dinnaṃ kenaci bhājanīyaṃ hotīti? Nāyaṃ virodho, ādissa dānasāmaññato labbhamānamatthaṃ dassetuṃ tathā vuttanti. Attano vā dhanenāti attano kappāsasuttādinā dhanena. Imassa “uppajjeyyā”ti iminā sambandho veditabbo. “Sīmāya detī”tiādi puggalādhiṭṭhānanayena vuttaṃ. Ettha pana sīmāya dānaṃ ekā mātikā, katikāya dānaṃ dutiyā…pe… puggalassa dānaṃ aṭṭhamā.

However, something given as ‘this out-of-season robe for the Sangha during the season’ is mentioned by way of extracting the meaning from the general sense of ‘out-of-season robe.’ Just as a robe that has arisen in the ‘back-season’ can be divided by those who have completed the rains-residence and by the others who are present, and thus becomes what is called an ‘out-of-season robe,’ so too is this case. This, then, is the general sense of ‘out-of-season robe.’ If so, why is it said, ‘Or given to an individual by the method beginning with, “I give this to you”’? For what is given with a specific designation to an individual is not to be divided by anyone. There is no contradiction. It is said so to show the meaning that can be obtained from the general sense of a designated gift. ‘Or with one’s own wealth’ means with one’s own wealth such as cotton, thread, and so on. Its connection should be understood with ‘it might arise.’ ‘One gives within a boundary,’ etc., is said by way of individual designation. Here, however, a gift within a boundary is the first heading; a gift by agreement is the second... and so on... a gift to an individual is the eighth.

“Parikkhepārahaṭṭhānenā”ti iminā aparikkhittassa vihārassa dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānādito paṭhamaleḍḍupātassa anto upacārasīmāti dasseti. Idāni [M 0.0294] dutiyaleḍḍupātassapi anto upacārasīmāyevāti dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānampi sīmāpariyantagatameva veditabbaṃ. Āvāse vaḍḍhante vaḍḍhatīti sace upacārato abahibhūto hutvā āvāso vaḍḍhatīti adhippāyo. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “bhikkhūsupi vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhatī”ti vuttaṃ. “Sace [V 0.0271] vihāre sannipatitabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ ekābaddhā hutvā yojanasatampi pūretvā nisīdanti, yojanasatampi upacārasīmāva hoti, sabbesaṃ lābho pāpuṇātī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Bhikkhunīnaṃ ārāmapavesanasenāsanāpucchanānīti āgantukagamikānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ ārāmapavesanāpucchanaṃ, senāsanāpucchanañcāti attho. Tathā hi āgantukāya bhikkhuniyā ārāmapavesanaṃ āpucchitabbaṃ, gamikāya saṅghikaṃ dasavidhaṃ senāsanaṃ. Ettha ca kiñcāpi “bhikkhunīna”nti vuttaṃ, gamikassa pana bhikkhussāpi imissāyeva sīmāya vasena senāsanāpucchanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

By ‘by the place worthy of enclosure,’ he shows that for an unenclosed monastery, the area within the first clod-throw from the permanent meeting place is the vicinity boundary (upacārasīmā). Now, to show that the area within the second clod-throw is also the vicinity boundary, he begins with ‘Moreover,’ and so on. The permanent meeting place, too, should be understood as being included within the limits of the boundary. ‘When the residence expands, it expands’—the intention is that the residence expands if it does so without going beyond the vicinity boundary. In the Mahāpaccarī, however, it is said: ‘It expands even as the monks increase.’ In the Samantapāsādikā it is said: ‘If, having gathered in the monastery, the monks sit down connected together, filling up even a hundred yojanas, then even a hundred yojanas becomes the vicinity boundary, and the gain accrues to all’ (Mv-a. 379). ‘The nuns’ entering the monastery and asking about lodgings’ means the asking by visiting and departing nuns about entering the monastery and about lodgings. For a visiting nun must ask permission to enter the monastery, and a departing nun must ask about the ten kinds of Sangha lodgings. And here, although ‘nuns’ is said, it should be understood that a departing monk, too, must ask about lodgings with reference to this same boundary.

Parivāsamānattārocananti pārivāsikamānattacārīnaṃ parivāsārocanaṃ, mānattārocanañca. Vassacchedanissayasenāsanaggāhādividhānanti vassacchedavidhānaṃ, nissayaggāhavidhānaṃ, senāsanaggāhavidhānanti attho. Ādisaddena nissayapaṭippassaddhi, lābhaggāho āgantukavattaṃ pūretvā ārāmapavesananti evamādikaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Imissāva sīmāya vasenāti upacārasīmāyevāti yathāsambhavaṃ anto, bahi ca imassa sabbassa labbhanato vuttaṃ.

‘Announcing probation and penance’ means the announcing of probation for those on probation and the announcing of penance for those undergoing penance. ‘The procedure for cutting short the rains-residence, taking dependence, taking lodgings, etc.’ means the procedure for cutting short the rains-residence, the procedure for taking dependence, and the procedure for taking lodgings. By the word ‘etc.’ (ādi), he includes the revocation of dependence, the acceptance of a gain, fulfilling the duties for an incoming monk, entering the monastery, and so on. ‘With reference to this same boundary’ is said because all this can be obtained with reference to the vicinity boundary, as may be the case, whether inside or outside it.

Lābhatthāya ṭhapitā sīmā lābhasīmā (mahāva. 379), sā ca kho neva sammāsambuddhena anuññātā, na dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi ṭhapitā, apica kho lābhadāyakehi. Tenāha “yaṃ rājarājamahāmattādayo”tiādi. Samantāti vihārassa samantā. Yanti suṅkasassādi. “Sīmaṃ ṭhapentī”ti pāṭhaseso. Ekassa rañño āṇāpavattiṭṭhānanti coḷabhogo keraḷabhogoti evaṃ ekekassa rañño āṇāpavattiṭṭhānaṃ. Dvidhā āpo gato etthāti dīpo, oghena anajjhotthato bhūmibhāgo, sova sīmā dīpasīmā. Tenāha samuddantenā”tiādi. Cakkavāḷasīmā cakkavāḷapabbateneva paricchinnāti āha “ekacakkavāḷapabbataparikkhepabbhantaraṃ cakkavāḷasīmā”ti.

A boundary established for the sake of gain is a gain-boundary (Mv. 379). It was not authorized by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One nor established by the elder compilers of the Dhamma, but rather by the donors of the gain. Hence he says, ‘Which kings, royal ministers, etc....’ ‘All around’ means all around the monastery. ‘They go’ for customs duties, crops, and so on. ‘...they establish a boundary’ is the rest of the text. ‘The place where the command of one king prevails’ means a territory like that of the Coḷas or the Keraḷas; thus, the place where the authority of each single king extends. An island (dīpa) is where water has gone on two sides; it is a piece of land not overwhelmed by a flood. That itself is the boundary, an island-boundary. Hence he says, ‘by the edge of the ocean,’ and so on. A world-sphere-boundary is defined by the world-sphere mountain range. Thus he says: ‘A world-sphere-boundary is what is inside the circumference of a single world-sphere mountain range.’

Sesāti [M 0.0295] khaṇḍasīmādayo. Khaṇḍasīmāya demāti dinnanti khaṇḍasīmāya kenaci kammena sannipatitaṃ saṅghaṃ disvā “khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ saṅghassa demā”ti dinnaṃ. Khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhite rukkhe vā pabbate vā ṭhitopi heṭṭhā vā pathavivemajjhagatopi khaṇḍasīmāyeva ṭhitoti veditabbo. Samānasaṃvāsasīmāya dinnanti “samānasaṃvāsasīmāya dammī”ti dinnaṃ. Esa nayo sesesupi. Khaṇḍasīmā sīmantarikaṭṭhānaṃ na pāpuṇāti tattha samānasaṃvāsasīmāya abhāvatoti adhippāyo. Samānasaṃvāsaavippavāsasīmāsu dinnassa idaṃ nānāttaṃ – “avippavāsasīmāya dammī”ti dinnaṃ gāmaṭṭhānaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Kasmā? “Ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”ti (mahāva. 144) vuttattā[V 0.0272]. “Samānasaṃvāsasīmāya dammī”ti dinnaṃ pana gāme ṭhitānampi pāpuṇātīti. Abbhantarasīmāudakukkhepasīmāsu dinnanti tattha uposathādiatthāya sannipatite disvā “imissā abbhantarasīmāya demā”tiādinā dinnaṃ. Janapadaraṭṭharajjadīpacakkavāḷasīmāsupi gāmasīmādīsu vuttasadisova vinicchayoti āha “janapadasīmādīsū”tiādi. Ekopi gantvā sabbesaṃ saṅgaṇhituṃ labhatīti ekopi gantvā idha vassaggena bhājetvā gahetvā āgantuṃ labhatīti attho. Ekoti sabhāgo eko bhikkhu, ayampi bhāgameva gahetuṃ labhati. Tenāha “sabhāgānaṃ bhāgaṃ gaṇhātī”ti.

‘The rest’ means the partial boundary, and so on. ‘Given as “We give to the partial boundary”’ means given on seeing the Sangha assembled for some formal act within the partial boundary and saying, ‘We give to the Sangha in the partial boundary.’ A tree or a mountain standing in a partial boundary, or one standing below or having gone into the middle of the earth, should be understood as standing in the partial boundary itself. ‘Given to the boundary of common communion’ means given with the words, ‘I give to the boundary of common communion.’ This is the method in the remaining cases too. A partial boundary does not reach an intermediate place between boundaries; the intention is that this is because there is no boundary of common communion there. Regarding a gift given in a boundary of common communion and a boundary of non-separation, this is the difference: a gift given with the words, ‘I give to the boundary of non-separation,’ does not reach the village site. Why? Because it is said: ‘Excluding a village and a village’s vicinity’ (Mv. 144). But a gift given with the words, ‘I give to the boundary of common communion,’ reaches even those staying in the village. ‘Given in an inner boundary or a water-throwing boundary’ means given on seeing them assembled there for the purpose of the Uposatha, etc., and saying, ‘We give within this inner boundary,’ and so on. In the cases of a country-boundary, a regional boundary, a kingdom-boundary, an island-boundary, and a world-sphere-boundary, too, the decision is similar to that stated for a village-boundary, etc. Thus he says, ‘In a country-boundary, etc....’ ‘Even one person going can collect for all’ means that even one person is permitted to go, divide it there by seniority, take it, and come back. ‘One’ means one monk who has a share. He, too, is permitted to take only a share. Hence he says: ‘He takes the share of those who have a share.’

Evaṃ tāva yo sīmaṃ parāmasitvā deti, tassa dāne vinicchayaṃ vatvā idāni yo “asukasīmāyā”ti vattuṃ na jānāti, kevalaṃ “sīmā”ti vacanamattameva jānanto vihāraṃ āgantvā “sīmāya dammī”ti vā “sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghassa dammī”ti vā bhaṇati, tattha vinicchayaṃ dassetuṃ “yo pana vihāraṃ pavisitvā”tiādimāha. Kataranti katarasīmaṃ. Ahametaṃ bhedaṃ na jānāmīti ahaṃ “asukā sīmā”ti etaṃ vibhāgaṃ na jānāmi. Upacārasīmaṭṭhehi bhājetabbaṃ lābhassa upacārasīmāya paricchinnattāti adhippāyo. Sāti samānalābhakatikā.

Thus, having first stated the decision concerning a gift from one who gives by referring to a boundary, now, to show the decision in a case where someone does not know how to say 'to such-and-such a boundary,' but, knowing only the mere word 'boundary,' comes to the monastery and says, 'I give to the boundary,' or 'I give to the Sangha established in the boundary,' he says, 'But whoever, having entered the monastery…' and so on. 'Which one?' means which boundary. 'I do not know this difference' means 'I do not know this distinction as “such-and-such a boundary.”' It should be divided by those established in the vicinity boundary; the intention is that the gain is defined by the vicinity boundary. 'That' means an agreement for an equal gain.

Yattha mayhaṃ dhuvakārā karīyantīti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) ettha yasmiṃ vihāre tassa cīvaradāyakassa santakaṃ saṅghassa pākavattaṃ vā vattati. Yasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū attano bhāraṃ katvā sadā gehe bhojeti, yattha vā anena āvāso vā kārito, salākabhattādīni vā nibaddhāni, ime dhuvakārā [M 0.0296] nāma. Yena pana sakalopi vihāro patiṭṭhāpito, tattha vattabbameva natthi. Tenāha “yattha tassa pākavattaṃ vā vattatī”tiādi. Tattha pākavattanti dānavattaṃ. Vattatīti pavattati. Yatoti yasmā vihārā. Yatthāti yasmiṃ vihāre. Sabbatthāti sabbesu vihāresu. Mātikaṃ āropetvāti ekasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū bahutarā, ekasmiṃ thokatarā, ekañca vatthaṃ, dhuvakāraṭṭhānañca bahukaṃ, kattha demāti pucchitvā, yadi pana mañco vā pīṭhaṃ vā ekameva hoti, taṃ pucchitvā yassa vā vihārassa, ekavihārepi vā yassa senāsanassa so vicāreti, tattha dātabbaṃ. Sacepi “asukabhikkhu gaṇhatū”ti vadati, vaṭṭati. Atha “mayhaṃ dhuvakāre dethā”ti vatvā avicāretvāva gacchati, saṅghassapi vicāretuṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ pana vicāretabbaṃ – “saṅghattherassa vasanaṭṭhāne dethā”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace tattha senāsanaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti, yattha nappahoti, tattha dātabbaṃ. Sace eko bhikkhu “mayhaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne senāsanaparibhogabhaṇḍaṃ natthī”ti vadati, tattha dātabbaṃ.

“Where my regular support is provided” (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): Here, this refers to a monastery where a customary offering belonging to the robe-donor is maintained for the Sangha. Or a monastery where a donor, having taken it upon himself as a responsibility, always provides meals for the bhikkhus in his house; or where a residence has been built by him, or where regular provisions like ticket-food are established—these are called “regular support.” But when the entire monastery has been established by him, there is nothing more to be said. Therefore, it is said, “where his customary offering is maintained,” and so on. Here, “customary offering” means the duty of giving. “Is maintained” means it is in practice. “From where” means from whichever monastery. “In which” means in whatever monastery. “Everywhere” means in all monasteries. “Having established a guideline”: If in one monastery the bhikkhus are more numerous and in another fewer, and there is only one robe-cloth but many places of regular support, one should ask, “Where should we give it?” But if there is only one bed or bench, having asked, it should be given to whichever monastery, or even within a single monastery to whichever lodging, he decides upon. Even if he says, “Let such-and-such a bhikkhu take it,” it is permissible. But if he says, “Give it to my places of regular support,” and leaves without deciding, the Sangha may also decide. It should be decided thus: “It should be given to the dwelling place of the Sangha's elder.” If the lodging there is fully supplied, it should be given where there is a need. If one bhikkhu says, “In my dwelling place, there are no lodging requisites for use,” it should be given there.

Saṅghassa [V 0.0273] dammīti dinnanti “imāni cīvarāni saṅghassa dammī”ti evaṃ dinnaṃ. Tato bahiddhāpīti upacārasīmāto bahiddhāpi. Tehi saddhinti upacārasīmāgatehi saddhiṃ. Ekābaddhānañca pāpuṇāti parisāvasena vaḍḍhitā sīmā hotīti katvāti adhippāyo. Tasmāti yasmā upacārasīmāgatānaṃ pāpuṇāti, yasmā ca tato bahiddhāpi upacārasīmokkantehi ekābaddhānaṃ pāpuṇāti, tasmā. Tesanti upacārasīmāgatānaṃ, tato bahiddhā tehi saddhiṃ ekābaddhānañca. Gāhate satīti antevāsikādike gaṇhante sati. Asampattānampīti upacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitehi ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā kālaṃ ghosetvā lābhabhājanaṭṭhānaṃ asampattānampi upacārasīmāya paviṭṭhānaṃ, tehi vā saddhiṃ ekābaddhānaṃ hutvā attano vihāradvāre vā antovihāreyeva vā ṭhitānañcāti attho. Bhāgo dātabboti saṅghanavakassa dinnepīti adhippāyo. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷhe āgatānaṃ paṭhamabhāgo na pāpuṇāti. Dutiyabhāgato vassaggena dātabbaṃ.

Given to the Sangha: that is, given with the words, “I give these robes to the Sangha.” Then also outside: that is, even outside the vicinity boundary. With them: that is, with those who have come within the vicinity boundary. And it is due to those in a continuous group: the meaning is that the boundary is considered extended by the presence of the assembly. Therefore: because it is due to those who have come within the vicinity boundary, and because it is also due to those in a continuous group with them even when they have passed outside that vicinity boundary, therefore. To them: that is, to those who have come within the vicinity boundary, and to those in a continuous group with them outside it. When it is taken: that is, when a resident disciple or the like takes it. Even to those who have not arrived: This means even to those who, having struck the bell and announced the time, are standing within the vicinity boundary but have not yet reached the place for distributing gains; or to those who have entered the vicinity boundary; or to those who, being in a continuous group with them, are standing at their own monastery gate or even within the monastery itself. A share should be given: the meaning is that it is given even to the most junior bhikkhu of the Sangha. But in the second round of distribution, the first portion is not due to those who arrive after the elders have taken their seats. From the second portion onwards, it should be given according to seniority by rains-residence.

Sace pana “bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitānaṃ dethā”ti vadanti, na dātabbaṃ. Yadi pana vihāro mahā hoti, therāsanato paṭṭhāya vatthesu dīyamānesu [M 0.0297] alasajātikā mahātherā pacchā āgacchanti, “bhante, vīsativassānaṃ dīyati, tumhākaṃ ṭhitikā atikkantā”ti na vattabbā. Ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā tesaṃ datvā pacchā ṭhitikāya dātabbaṃ.

But if they say, “Give to those standing outside the vicinity boundary,” it should not be given. If, however, the monastery is large, and while the robe-cloths are being distributed starting from the elders' seats, some indolent elder bhikkhus arrive late, one should not say: “Venerable sirs, it is being given to those of twenty years' seniority; your turn has passed.” Setting aside the regular sequence, one should give to them, and afterwards continue giving according to the sequence.

“Asukavihāre kira bahucīvaraṃ uppanna”nti sutvā yojanantarikavihāratopi bhikkhū āgacchanti, sampattasampattānaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya dātabbaṃ, ayamettha saṅkhepo. Vitthāro pana samantapāsādikāya cīvarakkhandhakavaṇṇanāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vuttanayena veditabbo.

Having heard, “It is said that much robe-cloth has arisen in such-and-such a monastery,” bhikkhus come even from monasteries a yojana away. It should be given to each one as they arrive, starting from the place where they are standing. This is the summary here. The detailed explanation, however, should be understood according to the method stated in the Commentary on the Robe Chapter in the Samantapāsādikā (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379).

Evaṃ vihāraṃ pavisitvā “imāni cīvarāni saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnesu vinicchayaṃ vatvā idāni bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā “saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnesu vinicchayaṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ekābaddhaparisāya pāpuṇātīti sace yojanaṃ pharitvā parisā ṭhitā hoti, ekābaddhā ce, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇātīti attho. Ekābaddhatā cettha dvādasahatthabbhantarato paricchinditabbā. Tenāha “ye panā”tiādi.

Having thus stated the ruling for when robes are given after one has entered a monastery and said, “I give these robes to the Sangha,” now, to show the ruling for when they are given after seeing a bhikkhu outside the vicinity boundary and saying, “I give them to the Sangha,” the passage beginning “But whatever...” was stated. “It is due to a continuous assembly” means that if an assembly is standing spread out over a yojana, it is due to all of them if the assembly is continuous. Here, continuity should be determined as being within twelve cubits. Therefore, it is said, “But those who...” and so on.

Ubhatosaṅghassa dinnanti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) “ubhatosaṅghassa dammī”ti dinnaṃ. “Dvedhāsaṅghassa dammi, dvinnaṃ saṅghānaṃ dammi, bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunisaṅghassa ca dammī”ti vuttepi ubhatosaṅghassa dinnameva hoti. Upaḍḍhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, upaḍḍhaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ dātabbanti dve bhāge same [V 0.0274] katvā eko bhāgo bhikkhūnaṃ, eko bhāgo bhikkhunīnaṃ dātabbo. Gahetuṃ labhati ubhatosaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattāti adhippāyo. Cetiyassāti thūpādino. Tañhi dhātāyatanādibhāvena citattā, lokassa cittīkāraṭṭhānatāya ca “cetiya”nti vuccati. Na koci visesoti āha “idha pana cetiyassā”tiādi.

Given to the dual Sangha (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): that is, given with the words, “I give this to the dual Sangha.” Even if it is said, “I give to the twofold Sangha,” “I give to the two Sanghas,” or “I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus and the Sangha of bhikkhunīs,” it is still considered given to the dual Sangha. Half should be given to the bhikkhus and half to the bhikkhunīs: having made two equal portions, one portion should be given to the bhikkhus and one portion to the bhikkhunīs. The meaning is that one is entitled to take it because it has been accepted by the acceptance of the dual Sangha. To the cetiya: that is, to a stupa and so on. For it is called a “cetiya” because it is built up as a repository for relics and so on, and because it is an object of reverence for the world. He says there is no difference, hence the words, “But here, to the cetiya...” and so on.

“Ubhatosaṅghassa ca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana dvāvīsatikoṭṭhāse katvā dasa bhikkhūnaṃ, dasa bhikkhunīnaṃ, eko puggalassa, eko cetiyassa dātabbo. Tattha puggalo saṅghatopi attano vassaggena puna gahetuṃ labhati, cetiyassa ekoyeva. Ayaṃ pana vāro yathāvutteneva nayena ñāyatīti katvā idha na vutto. Samantapāsādikāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) pana vuttoyeva.

But when it is said, “To the dual Sangha, to you, and to the cetiya,” then it should be divided into twenty-two portions: ten for the bhikkhus, ten for the bhikkhunīs, one for the individual, and one for the cetiya. In that case, the individual is entitled to take again from the Sangha's portion according to his seniority by rains-residence, but the cetiya receives only one portion. However, since this case is understood by the method already stated, it is not mentioned here. But in the Samantapāsādikā (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379), it is indeed mentioned.

Na [M 0.0298] majjhe bhinditvā dātabbaṃ “bhikkhunīna”nti puggalikavasena vuttattā. Puggalo visuṃ na labhatīti pubbe viya visuṃ puggalikakoṭṭhāsaṃ na labhati. Pāpuṇanaṭṭhānato ekameva labhatīti attano vassaggena pattabbaṭṭhānato ekameva koṭṭhāsaṃ labhati. Kasmā? Bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyassa ekapuggalapaṭivīso labbhati, puggalassa visuṃ na labbhati. Tasmā ekaṃ cetiyassa datvā avasesaṃ bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā bhājetabbaṃ. Tenāha “cetiyassa cāti vutte panā”tiādi.

It should not be divided in the middle and given, because "to the bhikkhunīs" is stated on an individual basis. An individual does not receive a separate share: that is, unlike before, he does not receive a separate individual portion. He receives only one portion from the place of attainment: that is, he receives only one portion from the place where it is to be obtained according to his seniority by rains-residence. Why? Because he is included by the term "Sangha of bhikkhus." Even when it is said, "To the Sangha of bhikkhus, to the bhikkhunīs, to you, and to the cetiya," the cetiya receives the share of a single person, but the individual does not receive a separate share. Therefore, after giving one portion to the cetiya, the remainder should be divided after counting both the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs. Hence it is said, "But when it is said, '...and to the cetiya...'" and so on.

Tehi saddhiṃ puggalacetiyaparāmasanaṃ anantaranayasadisamevāti tehi bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ puggalassa ca cetiyassa ca gahaṇaṃ anantaranayasadisamevāti attho. “Bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca, bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca cetiyassa ca, bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyassa ekapaṭivīso labbhati, puggalassa visuṃ natthi, bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvāva bhājetabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Puggalassa visuṃ na labbhatīti puggalassa visuṃ paṭivīso na labbhati, vassaggena ekova labbhatīti attho. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana cetiyassa visuṃ paṭivīso labbhatīti āha “cetiyassa pana labbhatī”ti. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyasseva visuṃ labbhati, na puggalassa. Cetiyassa pana labbhatiyevāti “bhikkhūnañca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana cetiyassa visuṃ paṭivīso labbhatīti [V 0.0275] attho. “Bhikkhūnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyasseva visuṃ labbhati, na puggalassa. Bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ ādiṃ katvāpi evameva yojetabbaṃ.

The inclusion of an individual and a cetiya along with them is just like the immediately preceding method: the meaning is that the inclusion of an individual and a cetiya along with those bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs is just like the immediately preceding method. This means it is said that even when it is stated, "To the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs and to you," "To the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs and to the cetiya," or "To the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, to you, and to the cetiya," a single share is obtained for the cetiya, but there is no separate share for the individual; it should be divided after counting the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. An individual does not receive a separate share: the meaning is that a separate portion is not allotted to the individual; only one share is obtained according to seniority by rains-residence. But when it is said, "To the Sangha of bhikkhus and to the cetiya," he says that a separate portion is obtained for the cetiya: "But for the cetiya, it is obtained." Even when it is said, "To the Sangha of bhikkhus, to you, and to the cetiya," a separate share is obtained only for the cetiya, not for the individual. "But for the cetiya, it is indeed obtained": the meaning is that when it is said, "To the bhikkhus and to the cetiya," a separate portion is obtained for the cetiya. Even when it is said, "To the bhikkhus, to you, and to the cetiya," a separate share is obtained only for the cetiya, not for the individual. The same method should be applied starting with the Sangha of bhikkhunīs.

Etthāha – yaṃ panetarahi (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) paṇḍitamanussā sadhātukaṃ paṭimaṃ vā cetiyaṃ vā ṭhapetvā buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa dānaṃ denti, paṭimāya vā cetiyassa vā purato ādhārake pattaṃ ṭhapetvā dakkhiṇodakaṃ datvā “buddhānaṃ demā”ti, tattha yaṃ paṭhamaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ denti, vihāraṃ vā āharitvā “idaṃ cetiyassa demā”ti piṇḍapātañca mālāgandhādīni ca denti, tattha kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Vuccate – mālāgandhādīni tāva cetiye āropetabbāni, vatthehi paṭākā, telena [M 0.0299] padīpā kātabbā, piṇḍapātamadhuphāṇitādīni pana yo nibaddhacetiyajaggako hoti pabbajito vā gahaṭṭho vā, tassa dātabbāni. Nibaddhajaggake asati āhaṭabhattaṃ ṭhapetvā vattaṃ katvā paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Upakaṭṭhe kāle bhuñjitvā pacchāpi vattaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

Here it is said: Now, when wise people establish an image with a relic or a shrine and give a gift to the Sangha of both kinds headed by the Buddha, or when, having placed a bowl on a stand in front of the image or shrine and poured the dedicatory water, they say, 'We give to the Buddhas'; and when they first give hard and soft food, or bring it to the monastery and say, 'We give this to the shrine,' and give almsfood, garlands, perfumes, and so on—how should one act in such a case? It is said: Garlands, perfumes, and so on should first be offered at the shrine. Banners should be made from cloths and lamps lit with oil. But almsfood, honey, molasses, and the like should be given to whoever is the regular caretaker of the shrine, whether one who has gone forth or a householder. If there is no regular caretaker, it is allowable to set aside the food that has been brought, perform the duties, and then consume it. It is also allowable to eat when the time is near and perform the duties afterwards.

Mālāgandhādīsu ca yaṃ kiñci “idaṃ haritvā cetiyapūjaṃ karothā”ti vutte dūrampi haritvā pūjetabbaṃ. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa harā”ti vuttepi haritabbaṃ. Sace pana “ahaṃ piṇḍāya carāmi, āsanasālāyaṃ bhikkhū atthi, te harissantī”ti vutte “bhante, tuyhaṃyeva dammī”ti vadati, bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Atha pana “bhikkhusaṅghassa dassāmī”ti harantassa gacchato antarāva kālo upakaṭṭho hoti, attano pāpetvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati.

And in the case of garlands, perfumes, and so on, if anything is given with the words, 'Take this and make an offering at the shrine,' it should be taken even a long distance and offered. Even when it is said, 'Take it for the Sangha of bhikkhus,' it should be taken. If, however, when the bhikkhu says, 'I am going on almsround; there are bhikkhus in the meeting hall, they will take it,' the donor replies, 'Venerable sir, I give it to you alone,' it is allowable to eat it. But if, while one is carrying it with the intention, 'I will give this to the Sangha of bhikkhus,' the time for the meal grows near along the way, it is allowable to take it for oneself and eat it.

Vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa dammīti vadatīti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) “vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa imāni cīvarāni dammī”ti vadati. Tesaṃ bahisīmaṭṭhānampi pāpuṇātīti atthate kathine bahisīmaṭṭhānampi yāva kathinassa ubbhārā pāpuṇāti, tasmā disāpakkantassāpi sati paṭiggāhake dātabbaṃ. Anatthate pana kathine antohemante, evañca pana vatvā dinnaṃ pacchimavassaṃvuṭṭhānampi pāpuṇāti. Yattha katthacīti yesu kesuci vihāresu. Evaṃ vadatīti “vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa dammī”ti vadati. Tatra sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā. Sace pana “vassaṃ vasantānaṃ dammī”ti vadati, antovasseyeva vassaṃ vasantāva labhanti, chinnavassā na labhanti. Cīvaramāse pana “vassaṃ vasantānaṃ dammī”ti vutte pacchimikāya vassūpagatānaṃyeva pāpuṇāti, purimikāya vassūpagatānañca chinnavassānañca na pāpuṇāti.

'I give to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379) means one says, 'I give these robes to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence.' 'It reaches even those staying outside the boundary' means: when the kathina has been spread, it reaches even those staying outside the boundary until the withdrawal of the kathina. Therefore, it should be given even to one who has departed for another region, if there is a recipient. But when the kathina has not been spread, within the winter season, what is given with this statement also reaches those who completed the later rains-residence. 'In whatever place' means in whatever monasteries. When one speaks thus, saying, 'I give to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence,' it reaches all who are present because it arose in their absence. But if one says, 'I give to those dwelling the rains,' only those dwelling the rains within that rains-residence receive it; those who have broken the rains-residence do not. However, during the robe-month, if it is said, 'I give to those dwelling the rains,' it reaches only those who undertook the later rains-residence; it does not reach those who undertook the earlier rains-residence nor those who have broken the rains-residence.

Cīvaramāsato paṭṭhāya yāva hemantassa pacchimo divaso, tāva “vassāvāsikaṃ demā”ti vutte [V 0.0276] kathinaṃ atthataṃ vā hotu, anatthataṃ vā, atītavassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya vutte pana mātikā āropetabbā “atītavassāvāsassa pañca māsā atikkantā, anāgato catumāsaccayena bhavissati, kataravassāvāsassa desī”ti. Sace “atītavassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ dammī”ti vadati, taṃantovassaṃvuṭṭhānameva pāpuṇāti, disā pakkantānampi sabhāgā gaṇhituṃ labhanti.

From the robe-month up to the last day of the winter season, when it is said, 'We give a rains-residence offering,' whether the kathina has been spread or not, it reaches only those who have completed the past rains-residence. But if this is said starting from the first day of the summer season, a matrix-heading should be established: 'Five months have passed since the past rains-residence; the future one will be after the lapse of four months. For which rains-residence do you designate it?' If one says, 'I give to those who have completed the past rains-residence,' it reaches only those who completed that rains-residence. Even those who have departed for other regions are able to receive their share.

Sace [M 0.0300] “anāgate vassāvāsikaṃ dammī”ti vadati, taṃ ṭhapetvā vassūpanāyikadivase gahetabbaṃ. Atha “agutto vihāro, corabhayaṃ atthi, na sakkā ṭhapetuṃ, gaṇhitvā vā āhiṇḍitu”nti vutte “sampattānaṃ dammī”ti vadati, bhājetvā gahetabbaṃ. Sace vadati “ito me, bhante, tatiye vasse vassāvāsikaṃ na dinnaṃ, taṃ dammī”ti, tasmiṃ antovasse vuṭṭhabhikkhūnaṃ pāpuṇāti. Sace te disā pakkantā, añño vissāsiko gaṇhāti, dātabbaṃ. Atha ekoyeva avasiṭṭho, sesā kālaṅkatā, sabbaṃ ekasseva pāpuṇāti. Sace ekopi natthi, saṅghikaṃ hoti, sammukhībhūtehi bhājitabbaṃ.

If one says, 'I will give a rains-residence offering in the future,' it should be set aside and received on the day of undertaking the rains-residence. But if, when it is said, 'The monastery is unguarded, there is danger from thieves, it cannot be set aside, nor can one take it and travel around,' the donor says, 'I give to those who are present,' it should be divided and taken. If one says, 'Venerable sir, my rains-residence offering for the third year past was not given; I give it now,' it reaches the bhikkhus who resided during that rains-residence. If they have departed for another region, another trustworthy bhikkhu may receive it; it should be given. If only one remains, the rest having passed away, everything goes to that one alone. If not even one is there, it becomes the property of the Sangha and should be divided by those present.

Yehi nimantitehi yāgu pītāti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) nimantitehi yehi bhikkhūhi yāgu pītā, yehi pana bhikkhācāravattena gharadvārena gacchantehi vā gharaṃ paviṭṭhehi vā yāgu laddhā, yesaṃ vā āsanasālato pattaṃ āharitvā manussehi nītā, yesaṃ vā therehi pesitā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Sace pana nimantitabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ aññepi bahū āgantvā antogehañca bahigehañca pūretvā nisinnā, dāyako ca evaṃ vadati “nimantitā vā hontu, animantitā vā, yesaṃ mayā yāgu dinnā, sabbesaṃ imāni vatthāni hontū”ti, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Yehi pana therānaṃ hatthato yāgu laddhā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Atha so “yehi mayhaṃ yāgu pītā, sabbesaṃ hotū”ti vadati, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Bhattakhajjakādīhīti ettha ādisaddenapi cīvarasenāsanabhesajjānaṃ gahaṇaṃ.

'By those invited who drank the gruel' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): This refers to the gruel drunk by the invited bhikkhus. A subsequent gift does not reach those bhikkhus who obtained gruel while on their almsround, passing by a house door or having entered a house; nor those for whom people brought it after fetching their bowls from the meeting hall; nor those to whom it was sent by the elders. But if, along with the invited bhikkhus, many others come and sit down, filling the house both inside and out, and the donor says, 'Whether invited or uninvited, let these cloths be for all to whom I have given gruel,' it reaches all of them. But it does not reach those who received gruel from the hands of the elders. If, however, the donor says, 'Let it be for all who drank my gruel,' it reaches all of them. 'By rice, hard food, etc.': here, by the word 'etc.,' robes, lodgings, and medicines are also included.

Puggalassāti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) sammukhāsammukhabhūtassa puggalassa. Tenāha “idaṃ cīvara”ntiādi. Sace pana “idaṃ tumhākañceva tumhākaṃ antevāsikānañca dammī”ti evaṃ vadati, therassa ca antevāsikānañca pāpuṇāti. Uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgato, gahetvā gacchanto ca atthi, tassāpi pāpuṇāti. Tumhehi saddhiṃ nibaddhacārikabhikkhūnaṃ dammī”ti vutte uddesantevāsikānaṃ vattaṃ katvā uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Etthāti aṭṭhasu mātikāsu. Yadi pana ayamettha saṅkhepakathā, vitthāro pana kathaṃ ñātabboti āha [V 0.0277] “samantapāsādikāyaṃ vutto”ti. Samantapāsādikāyaṃ cīvarakkhandhakavaṇṇanāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vuttoti attho.

'To an individual' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379) means to an individual whether present or not present. Therefore it is said, 'This robe,' etc. But if one says, 'I give this to you and to your pupils,' it reaches the elder and the pupils. It also reaches one who has come to receive a recitation passage and one who is leaving after having received it. When it is said, 'I give to the bhikkhus who regularly travel with you,' it reaches all the pupils of recitation who wander about performing their duties and undertaking recitation, inquiry, and so on. 'Here' means in these eight matrix-headings. But if this is the summary statement here, how is the detailed account to be known? It is said: 'It is stated in the Samantapāsādikā.' The meaning is that it is stated in the commentary to the Robes Section in the Samantapāsādikā.

“Ñātakehi [M 0.0301] vā me cīvaratthāya pesitaṃ, mittehi vā pesitaṃ, te ābhate cīvare dassantī”ti evaṃ ñātito vā mittato vā paccāsā hotīti veditabbaṃ. Kappiyabhaṇḍenāti kappāsasuttādinā attano dhanena. Saṇhanti sukhumaṃ. Aññaṃ paccāsācīvaraṃ labhitvā eva kālabbhantare kāretabbanti aññaṃ mūlacīvarasadisaṃ paccāsācīvaraṃ labhitvāyeva māsabbhantare kāretabbaṃ. Tañca kho satiyāyeva paccāsāya, asatiyā pana paccāsāya mūlacīvaraṃ dasāhaṃ ce sampattaṃ, tadaheva adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Tenāha “sace na labhatī”tiādi. Paccāsācīvarampi parikkhāracoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbanti paṭhamataraṃ uppannaṃ thūlapaccāsācīvarampi sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pi-saddena na kevalaṃ mūlacīvaramevāti dasseti.

It should be understood that there is an expectation from relatives or friends, thus: 'It has been sent by my relatives for the sake of a robe, or sent by my friends; they will give me the robe when it is brought.' 'With allowable goods' means with one's own funds, such as cotton thread. 'Fine' means delicate. 'Having obtained another hoped-for robe, one should have it made within the time period' means: only after obtaining another hoped-for robe similar to the original robe should one have it made within a month. And that is only when there is an expectation. But when there is no expectation, if the original robe has been held for ten days, it should be determined on that very day. Therefore it is said, 'If one does not obtain it,' and so on. 'Even a hoped-for robe should be determined as a requisite-cloth' is said with reference to a coarse hoped-for robe that arose first. The particle 'pi' (even) shows that it is not only the original robe.

Akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning untimely robes is finished.

4. Purāṇacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Training Rule on an Old Robe

“Amhākameva ñātī”ti ñāyatīti ñāti, sāva ñātikā, na ñātikā aññātikā, tāya aññātikāya. Tenāha “na ñātikāyā”ti. Mātito vā pitito vāti mātipakkhato vā pitipakkhato vā. Yāva sattamaṃ yuganti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.503-505) yāva sattamassa purisassa, sattamāya vā itthiyā āyuppamāṇaṃ, yāva pitāmahayugaṃ pitāmahiyugaṃ mātāmahayugaṃ mātāmahiyuganti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha vā yāva sattamaṃ yuganti yāva sattamadvandanti attho. Yugasaddo cettha ekasesanayena daṭṭhabbo “yugo ca yugo ca yugā”ti. Evañhi tattha tattha dvandaṃ gahitaṃ hoti. Kenaci ākārena asambaddhāyāti bhātubhaginibhāgineyyaputtapaputtādīsu yena kenaci ākārena asambaddhāya. Pitā, pitupitā, tassa pitā, tassāpi pitāti evaṃ yāva sattamā yugā, pitā, pitumātā, tassā pitā ca mātā ca bhātā ca bhaginī ca, puttā ca, dhītaro cāti evampi uddhañca adho ca yāva sattamā yugā, pitā, pitubhātā, pitubhaginī, pituputtā, pitudhītaro, tesampi puttadhītuparamparāti evampi yāva sattamā yugā, mātā, mātumātā, tassā mātā, tassāpi mātāti evaṃ yāva sattamā yugā, mātā, mātupitā, tassa pitā ca mātā ca bhātā ca bhaginī ca puttā ca dhītaro cāti evampi uddhañca adho [M 0.0302] ca yāva sattamā yugā, mātā, mātubhātā, mātubhaginī, mātuputtā, mātudhītaro[V 0.0278], tesampi puttadhītuparamparāti evampi yāva sattamā yugā, tāva neva mātusambandhena, na pitusambandhena yā sambaddhā, sā “aññātikā nāmā”ti vuttaṃ hoti.

“Our own kinsfolk”: one who is known thus is a kinsman (ñāti); she is a kinswoman (ñātikā). One who is not a kinswoman is a non-kinswoman (aññātikā); by that non-kinswoman. Therefore it is said: “from a non-kinswoman.” “From the mother’s side or the father’s side” means from the mother’s lineage or the father’s lineage. “Up to the seventh generation” (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.503-505) means up to the seventh man, or the life-span of the seventh woman; it is said to mean up to the generation of the paternal grandfather, the paternal grandmother, the maternal grandfather, and the maternal grandmother. Alternatively, “up to the seventh generation” means up to the seventh couple. Here the word “generation” (yuga) should be understood by the principle of ellipsis (ekasesa) as “a couple and a couple are couples (yugā).” For in this way, a couple is taken in each case. “Unrelated in any way” means unrelated in any way among brothers, sisters, nephews, sons, grandsons, and so on. Father, paternal grandfather, his father, and his father—thus up to the seventh generation. Father, paternal grandmother, her father and mother, brothers and sisters, sons and daughters—thus both upwards and downwards up to the seventh generation. Father, paternal uncle, paternal aunt, their sons, their daughters, and the succession of their sons and daughters—thus up to the seventh generation. Mother, maternal grandmother, her mother, and her mother—thus up to the seventh generation. Mother, maternal grandfather, his father and mother, brothers and sisters, sons and daughters—thus both upwards and downwards up to the seventh generation. Mother, maternal uncle, maternal aunt, their sons, their daughters, and the succession of their sons and daughters—thus up to the seventh generation. She who is connected neither by the mother’s connection nor by the father’s connection within these limits is said to be what is called a “non-kinswoman”.

Sākiyāniyo viyāti pañcasatamattā sākiyāniyo viya. Nidassanamattañcetaṃ, tasmā bhikkhubhāve ṭhatvā parivattaliṅgā bhikkhuniyopi idha suddhabhikkhusaṅghe “upasampannā” icceva veditabbā. Ubhatosaṅghe vāti bhikkhunisaṅghe ñatticatutthena, bhikkhusaṅghe ñatticatutthenāti evaṃ ubhatosaṅghe vā. Purāṇacīvaranti ettha cīvaranti nivāsanapārupanupagameva adhippetanti āha “rajitvā”tiādi. Kappaṃ katvāti kappabinduṃ datvā. “Iminā adinnakappaṃ pācittiyavatthu na hotīti dassetī”ti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.505) vadanti. Paribhogasīsenāti kāyena phusitvā paribhogasīsena. Aṃseti jattumhi. Matthaketi sīsamatthake. Sace pana paccattharaṇassa heṭṭhā katvā nipajjati, hatthehi vā ukkhipitvā ākāse vitānaṃ katvā sīsena asamphusanto gacchati, ayaṃ paribhogo nāma na hoti.

'Like the Sakyan women' means like the five hundred or so Sakyan women. And this is just an illustration. Therefore, even bhikkhunīs whose sex has changed while they were established in the state of a bhikkhu should be known as 'ordained' right here in the pure Bhikkhu Sangha. 'Or in both Sanghas' means in the Bhikkhunī Sangha by a motion and three announcements, and in the Bhikkhu Sangha by a motion and three announcements; thus in both Sanghas. In the phrase 'an old robe,' 'robe' is intended to mean only the lower garment and the upper garment; thus he says 'having dyed,' etc. 'Having made it allowable' means having applied the determination mark. They say: 'He shows that by this, an item for which the determination mark has not been applied does not become an object for a pācittiya offense' (Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā 2.505). 'By way of use' means by way of use by touching it with the body. 'On the shoulder' means on the collarbone. 'On the head' means on the crown of the head. But if one lies down after placing it under the ground-covering, or if one lifts it with the hands and, making it a canopy in the air, walks along without touching it with one's head, this is not called 'use'.

Kāyavikāraṃ vā karotīti yathā sā “dhovāpetukāmo aya”nti jānāti, evaṃ kāyavikāraṃ karoti. “Antodvādasahatthe okāse ṭhatvā upari vā khipatī”ti iminā upacāraṃ muñcitvā orato khipantassa anāpattīti dasseti. Aññassa vā hatthe pesetīti antodvādasahatthe okāse ṭhatvā sikkhamānasāmaṇerasāmaṇeriupāsakaitthiyādīsu yassa kassaci aññassa hatthe vā peseti. Soti upāsako ca sāmaṇero ca. Upasampajjitvā dhovatīti ettha upāsako liṅge parivatte bhikkhunīsu pabbajitvā upasampajjitvā dhovati, sāmaṇero liṅge parivatte bhikkhunīsu upasampajjitvā dhovatīti yathāyogaṃ attho gahetabbo. Sace pana bhikkhuniyā hatthe dinnaṃ hoti, sace liṅge parivatte dhovati, vaṭṭati.

'Or he makes a bodily gesture' means he makes a bodily gesture in such a way that she knows, 'This one wants to have it washed.' By the phrase 'standing in a space within twelve cubits and throwing it up,' he shows that there is no offense for one who, having left the vicinity, throws it to the near side. 'Or he sends it into another's hand' means, standing in a space within twelve cubits, he sends it into the hand of any other person, such as a female probationer, a male novice, a female novice, a male lay follower, a woman, and so on. 'He' refers to the male lay follower and the male novice. 'Having been ordained, he washes it': here, the meaning should be taken as appropriate: a male lay follower, his sex having changed, having gone forth and been ordained among the bhikkhunīs, washes it; a male novice, his sex having changed, having been ordained among the bhikkhunīs, washes it. But if it was given into the hand of a bhikkhunī, and if she washes it after her sex has changed, it is allowable.

Ettha ca ekassa tikkhattuṃ nissajjanābhāvato tīṇipi kārentassa ekena nissaggiyaṃ, dvīhi dve dukkaṭāni. Dve kārentassa ekena nissaggiyaṃ, dutiyena dukkaṭaṃ. Tenāha “dhovanādīni tīṇī”tiādi. “Ekena vatthunā”ti [M 0.0303] paṭhamaṃ katvā niṭṭhāpitaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace pana “imaṃ cīvaraṃ rajitvā dhovitvā ānehī”ti vutte sā bhikkhunī paṭhamaṃ dhovitvā pacchā rajati, nissaggiyena dukkaṭameva, evaṃ sabbesu viparītavacanesu nayo netabbo. Sace pana “dhovitvā ānehī”ti vuttā dhovati ceva rajati ca, dhovāpanapaccayā eva āpatti, rajane anāpatti. Evaṃ sabbattha. Tenāha “sace pana‘dhovā’ti vuttā”tiādi. Bhikkhūnaṃ vasena ekato upasampannāya dhovāpentassa yathāvatthukamevāti āha “bhikkhunisaṅghavasenā”tiādi.

And here, because there is no threefold relinquishment for a single item, for one who has all three things done, there is one offense entailing forfeiture for one of them, and two offenses of wrong conduct for the other two. For one who has two things done, there is one offense entailing forfeiture for one, and an offense of wrong conduct for the second. Therefore He said: 'The three things beginning with washing,' and so on. 'With one object' is said in reference to what was first undertaken and completed. But if, when told, 'Dye this robe, wash it, and bring it,' that bhikkhunī first washes it and then dyes it, there is only an offense of wrong conduct for the forfeiture offense. This method should be applied in all cases of reversed instructions. But if, when told, 'Wash it and bring it,' she both washes and dyes it, the offense is incurred only on account of having it washed; there is no offense for the dyeing. This applies everywhere. Therefore He said: 'But if, when told, “Wash it…,”' and so on. To show that for one who has a robe washed by a woman ordained on one side by the Bhikkhus, the offense is just according to the case, he said: 'by the Bhikkhunī Sangha,' and so on.

Aññassa [V 0.0279] vā santakanti aññassa santakaṃ purāṇacīvaraṃ dhovāpentassāti attho. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇanti aññassa vā attano vā santakaṃ nisīdanañceva paccattharaṇañca. Nivāsanapārupanupagasseva ca idha “purāṇacīvara”nti adhippetattā attano santakampi nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ dhovāpentassa dukkaṭameva hoti, na nissaggiyaṃ. Avuttā vā dhovatīti uddesāya vā ovādāya vā āgatā kiliṭṭhacīvaraṃ disvā ṭhapitaṭṭhānato vā gahetvā, “detha ayya, dhovissāmī”ti āharāpetvā vā dhovati ceva rajati ca ākoṭeti ca, ayaṃ avuttā dhovati nāma. Yāpi “imaṃ cīvaraṃ dhovā”ti daharaṃ vā sāmaṇeraṃ vā āṇāpentassa bhikkhuno vacanaṃ sutvā “āharathayya, ahaṃ dhovissāmī”ti dhovati, tāvakālikaṃ vā gahetvā dhovitvā rajitvā deti, ayampi avuttā dhovati nāma.

'Or belonging to another' means having an old robe belonging to another washed. 'A sitting cloth or a ground-covering' means a sitting cloth and a ground-covering belonging to another or to oneself. And since 'old robe' is here intended to mean only the lower garment and the upper garment, for having even one's own sitting cloth or ground-covering washed, there is only an offense of wrong conduct, not one entailing forfeiture. 'Or she washes it unasked' means: having come for a recitation or an exhortation, she sees a soiled robe and, either taking it from where it was placed or having it brought by saying, 'Give it, venerable sir, I will wash it,' she washes, dyes, and beats it—this is called 'washing unasked.' Also, a bhikkhunī who, on hearing a bhikkhu's words ordering a junior bhikkhu or a male novice, 'Wash this robe,' washes it, saying, 'Bring it, venerable sir, I will wash it,' or who takes it for a time, washes and dyes it, and gives it back—this too is called 'washing unasked'.

Aññaṃ vā parikkhāranti upāhanatthavikapattatthavikaaṃsabaddhakakāyabandhanamañcapīṭhataṭṭikādiṃ yaṃ kiñci. “Upacāre ṭhatvā”ti vacanato pesitvā dhovanepi anāpatti. Upacāreti antodvādasahatthe okāse.

'Or another requisite' means any whatsoever, such as sandals, a bag for sandals, a bag for the bowl, a shoulder strap, a waistband, a bed, a chair, a mat, and so on. Because of the phrase 'standing in the vicinity,' there is no offense even in having it washed if one sends it. 'Vicinity' means a space within twelve cubits.

Purāṇacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Training Rule on an Old Robe is finished.

5. Cīvarappaṭiggahaṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Receiving a Robe

Channanti khomādīnaṃ channaṃ cīvarānaṃ majjhe. Upacāraṃ muñcitvāti dvādasahatthūpacāraṃ muñcitvā. Pi-saddena dhammakathaṃ kathentassa catasso parisā cīvarāni ca nānāvirāgavatthāni ca āharitvā pādamūle ṭhapenti, upacāre vā ṭhatvā upari khipanti, “sace sādiyati, paṭiggahitamevā”ti ettha vattabbameva [M 0.0304] natthīti dasseti. Khipatūti divā vā rattibhāge vā khipatu. Paṭiggahitameva hotīti kiñcāpi “idaṃ bhikkhuniyā, idaṃ aññesa”nti ñātuṃ na sakkā, tathāpi acittakabhāvena gahitameva hoti. Yassa kassaci pana anupasampannassāti sikkhamānasāmaṇerasāmaṇeriupāsakaupāsikādīsu yassa kassaci anupasampannassa. Ṭhapitanti bhikkhuniyā ṭhapitaṃ. Paṃsukūlaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvāti “assāmikaṃ ida”nti saññaṃ uppādetvā. Assāmikañhi “paṃsukūla”nti vuccati. Iminā “amhākamatthāya ṭhapita”ntiādikāya saññāya gahetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Aññatra pārivattakāti parivattetabbaṃ parivattaṃ, parivattameva pārivattakaṃ, parivattetvā diyyamānaṃ, taṃ vināti attho. Tenāha “yaṃ antamaso harīṭakakkhaṇḍampī”tiādi. [V 0.0280] Ābhogaṃ katvāti cittena samannāharitvā. Sace bhikkhunī vassāvāsikampi deti, tampi yathāvuttavidhānaṃ akatvā gahetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti veditabbaṃ.

'Of the six' means: among the six kinds of robes beginning with linen. 'Having left the vicinity' means: having left the twelve-cubit vicinity. By the word 'also' (`pi`), it shows that there is nothing more to be said in the following case: when one is giving a Dhamma talk, the four assemblies bring robes and various colored cloths and place them at his feet, or standing in the vicinity, they throw them up, and if he consents, it is considered received. 'Let him throw' means: he may throw either by day or in the nighttime. 'It is considered received' means: although it is not possible to know, “This is for a bhikkhunī, this is for others,” nevertheless, it is considered taken because it is unassigned. 'But for any unordained person' means: for any unordained person among probationers, male novices, female novices, male lay followers, female lay followers, etc. 'Placed' means: placed by a bhikkhunī. 'Having determined it as a refuse-rag' means: having generated the perception, “This is ownerless.” For what is ownerless is called a “refuse-rag.” By this it is shown that it is not proper to take it with a perception such as, “This was placed for our sake.” 'Except by exchange' means: what is to be exchanged is an exchange; an exchange itself is what is exchangeable, given after exchanging. The meaning is: apart from that. Therefore he said: “even so much as a piece of myrobalan fruit,” etc. 'Having made an intention' means: having adverted to it with the mind. It should be understood that if a bhikkhunī gives even a rains-residence robe, it is not proper to accept it without having followed the stated procedure.

Paṭilābhenāti gahaṇena. Tikapācittiyanti tīṇi parimāṇāni assāti tikaṃ,tikañca taṃ pācittiyañcāti tikapācittiyaṃ, aññātikāya ñātikasaññivematikaaññātikasaññīnaṃ vasena tīṇi pācittiyānīti attho. Ekatoupasampannāyāti bhikkhunīnaṃ santike upasampannāya. Tāya hi hatthato aññatra pārivattakā cīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇhantassa dukkaṭaṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ santike upasampannāya pana pācittiyameva. “Pattatthavikādimhi ca anadhiṭṭhātabbaparikkhāre”ti iminā bhisicchavimpi saṅgaṇhāti. Sā hi mahantāpi senāsanasaṅgahitattā cīvarasaṅkhaṃ na gacchatīti neva adhiṭṭhānupagā, na vikappanupagā ca. Vuttañhi samantapāsādikāyaṃ “sacepi mañcappamāṇā bhisicchavi hoti, vaṭṭatiyevā”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.514). “Hatthato cīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti vacanato pana aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā pesitaggahaṇepi anāpatti. Paṭiggahaṇato, parivattanākaraṇato ca kiriyākiriyaṃ.

'By acquisition' means: by taking. 'A pācittiya involving three cases' means: there are three cases for it, thus ‘three cases’; it is both ‘three cases’ and a ‘pācittiya,’ thus ‘a pācittiya involving three cases.’ The meaning is that there are three pācittiya offenses depending on whether one perceives an unrelated bhikkhunī as a relative, is uncertain, or perceives her as unrelated. 'Ordained on one side' means: ordained in the presence of bhikkhus. For one who accepts a robe from her hand, except by exchange, it is an offense of wrong-doing; but for one ordained in the presence of bhikkhunīs, it is a pācittiya offense. By the phrase 'and in the case of requisites that are not to be determined, such as a bowl-case,' it also includes a sitting-mat. For although it may be large, since it is included under lodgings, it does not count as a robe; thus it is subject neither to determination nor to assignment for shared use. For it is said in the Samantapāsādikā: “Even if a sitting-mat is the size of a couch, it is still allowable.” However, based on the phrase 'he accepts a robe from her hand,' there is no offense even in accepting what is sent by an unrelated bhikkhunī. The distinction between an act and a non-act is based on the acceptance and on the non-performance of an exchange.

Cīvarappaṭiggahaṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Receiving a Robe is finished.

6. Aññātakaviññattisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Requesting from a Non-relative

Gehassa [M 0.0305] pati jeṭṭhoti gahapati, taṃ gahapatiṃ, idha pana apabbajito yo koci manusso adhippeto. Tenāha “bhikkhūsu apabbajitamanussa”nti. Eseva nayo gahapatāninti etthāpi. “Viññāpeyyā”ti idaṃ suddhakattuatthe ca hetukattuatthe ca vattatīti āha “yāceyya vā yācāpeyya vā”ti. Yācāpanañcettha attano atthāyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evañca pana katvā “anāṇattika”nti idaṃ samatthitaṃ hoti. Aññatra samayāti sameti ettha, etena vā saṃgacchati satto, sabhāvadhammo vā sahajātādīhi, uppādādīhi vāti samayo, kālo, dhammappavattimattatāya atthato abhūtopi hi kālo dhammappavattiyā adhikaraṇaṃ, karaṇaṃ viya ca kappanāmattasiddhena rūpena voharīyati, taṃ samayaṃ ṭhapetvāti attho. Tenāha “yo acchinnacīvaro vā hotī”tiādi. Tattha rājādīsu yehi kehici acchinnaṃ cīvaraṃ etassāti acchinnacīvaro. Yathāha “acchinnacīvaro nāma bhikkhussa cīvaraṃ acchinnaṃ hoti, rājūhi vā corehi vā dhuttehi vā yehi kehici vā acchinnaṃ hotī”ti. Aggiādīsu yena kenaci naṭṭhaṃ cīvarametassāti naṭṭhacīvaro. Yathāha “naṭṭhacīvaro nāma bhikkhussa cīvaraṃ agginā vā daḍḍhaṃ hoti, udakena vā vūḷhaṃ hoti, undūrehi vā upacikāhi vā khāyitaṃ hoti[V 0.0281], paribhogajiṇṇaṃ vā hotī”ti (pārā. 519). Samayāti aññatrasaddāpekkhāya upayogatthe nissakkavacananti āha “taṃ samaya”nti. Aññasminti aññasmiṃ samaye.

A householder is the master and chief of a house. But here 'householder' refers to any unordained person. Hence he said: “an unordained person.” The same method applies also to the word 'householders'. 'Should request': this is used in the sense of both requesting and causing to request, thus he said: 'he should ask or cause to ask.' And it should be understood that here causing to ask is only for one's own benefit. And by this, the term 'anāṇattika' (offense without a command) is supported. 'Except on an occasion': an occasion (`samaya`) is when one meets with something, or a being comes together with it, or a natural state with its conascent conditions, etc., or with its arising, etc. Time (`kālo`), though in an ultimate sense unreal as it is merely the process of phenomena, is treated as a basis for the process of phenomena and is spoken of by means of a form established by mere convention as if it were an instrument. The meaning is: setting aside that occasion. Hence he said: 'if his robe has been stolen,' etc. Herein, 'one whose robe has been stolen' is one whose robe has been taken away by kings, thieves, rogues, or by anyone at all. As it is said: “One whose robe has been stolen means a bhikkhu's robe has been taken away by kings or by thieves or by rogues or by anyone at all.” 'One whose robe has been lost' is one whose robe has been destroyed by fire or some other agent, carried off by water, eaten by rats or by termites, or has become worn out through use. As it is said: “One whose robe has been lost means a bhikkhu's robe has been burnt by fire, or carried off by water, or eaten by rats or by termites, or has become worn out through use.” 'An occasion': with reference to the word ‘except,’ this is a locative of purpose. Thus he said: 'that occasion.' 'At another' means: at another occasion.

Tikapācittiyanti aññātake aññātakasaññivematikaññātakasaññīnaṃ vasena tīṇi pācittiyāni. Samayeti yathāvutte acchinnacīvarakāle ca naṭṭhacīvarakāle ca. Ñātakappavārite vā viññāpentassāti ñātake, pavārite ca “tumhākaṃ santhataṃ dethā”ti yācantassa. Ettha (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.521) ca saṅghavasena pavārite pamāṇameva yācituṃ vaṭṭati, puggalikavasena pavārite pana yaṃ yaṃ pavārenti, taṃ tameva viññāpetabbaṃ. Yo hi catūhi paccayehi pavāretvā sayameva sallakkhetvā kālānukālaṃ cīvarādīni divase divase yāgubhattādīni deti, evaṃ yena yena attho, taṃ taṃ deti, tassa viññāpanakiccaṃ natthi. Yo pana pavāretvā bālatāya [M 0.0306] vā satisammosena vā na deti, so viññāpetabbo. Yo “mayhaṃ gehaṃ pavāremī”ti vadati, tassa gehaṃ gantvā yathāsukhaṃ nisīditabbaṃ nipajjitabbaṃ, na kiñci gahetabbaṃ. Yo pana “yaṃ mayhaṃ gehe atthi, taṃ pavāremī”ti vadati, yaṃ tattha kappiyaṃ, taṃ viññāpetabbaṃ. Gehe pana nisīdituṃ vā nipajjituṃ vā na labbhati. Tassevatthāyāti “aññassā”ti laddhavohārassa tasseva buddharakkhitassa vā dhammarakkhitassa vā atthāya. Attano dhanena gaṇhantassāti attano kappiyabhaṇḍena kappiyavohāreneva gaṇhantassa cetāpentassa, parivattāpentassāti attho.

A pācittiya of three cases means: there are three pācittiya offenses with respect to a non-relative, depending on whether one perceives him as a non-relative, is uncertain, or perceives him as a relative. On an occasion means: at the aforesaid time when a robe has been snatched and the time when a robe has been lost. Or for one who requests from a relative or from one who has invited means: for one who asks a relative, or one who has invited, saying, “Give us your felt cloth.” Here, when an invitation has been made to the Saṅgha, it is proper to ask only for a limited amount. But when an invitation has been made to an individual, one should request only what they have offered in the invitation. If someone, having made an invitation with the four requisites, on his own accord takes note and from time to time gives robes and so on, and day by day gives rice gruel, meals, etc.—thus giving whatever is needed—for him there is no need to make a request. But if someone, having made an invitation, does not give out of foolishness or forgetfulness, he should be reminded by a request. If someone says, “I offer an invitation to my house,” one may go to his house and sit down and lie down as one likes, but nothing should be taken. But if someone says, “I offer whatever is in my house,” one may request whatever is allowable there. But one is not allowed to sit down or lie down in the house. For his sake means: for the sake of that very person who is designated as “another,” that is, for Buddharakkhita or Dhammarakkhita. For one who acquires it with his own funds means: for one who has it bought or exchanged with his own allowable goods through an allowable transaction.

Aññātakaviññattisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Requesting from a Non-relative is finished.

7. Tatuttarisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Further Training Rule

Taṃ-saddo cettha pakatatthavacano. Ceti nipātamattaṃ. Ceti vā yadīti attho, tassa “pavāreyyā”ti iminā sambandho veditabbo. Pavāreyya ceti yadi pavāreyyāti attho. “Abhīti upasaggo”ti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.523-524) iminā tassa atthavisesābhāvaṃ dasseti. Tenāha “haritunti attho”ti. Pavārasaddassa icchāyaṃ vattamānattā “icchāpeyyā”ti vuttaṃ. Icchaṃ uppādeyyāti paccaye icchaṃ uppādeyya. Upanimantanāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tenāha “yāvattaka”ntiādi. Nekkhammanti pabbajjaṃ. Daṭṭhūti daṭṭhuṃ. Chandānurakkhaṇatthañhettha anunāsikalopo. Khematoti nibbhayato. Kāyena vā vācāya vā abhiharitvā nimanteyyāti sambandho. Yathā ca kāyena abhihareyya, vācāya ca, taṃ vidhiṃ dassetuṃ “upanetvā”tiādi [V 0.0282] vuttaṃ saantaranti antaravāsakasahitaṃ. Uttaranti uttarāsaṅgaṃ. Paramanti avasānaṃ. Assa cīvarassāti assa samudāyabhūtassa haritabbassa cīvarassa. Tagguṇasaṃviññāṇo hi ayaṃ bāhiratthasamāso yathā “lambakaṇṇo”ti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tenāha “nivāsanenā”tiādi. Ukkaṭṭhaparicchedena hi sabbe taṃparamaṃyeva gahetuṃ labhanti.

Here, the word 'taṃ' has its usual meaning. 'Ce' is merely a particle. 'Ce' means 'or' or 'if'; its connection should be understood with 'pavāreyyā.' 'Pavāreyya ce' means 'if one should invite.' By the statement, 'The word “abhi” is a prefix' (Sāratthaṭīkā 2.523–524), it shows that it has no special meaning. Hence he says, 'it means “to take.”' Since the word 'pavāra' is used in the sense of desire, it is said, 'icchāpeyyā,' meaning 'one should arouse a desire.' He should arouse a desire for a requisite. This is a synonym for 'invitation.' Therefore he says, 'as much as,' and so on. 'Renunciation' means the going forth. 'Daṭṭhu' means 'to see' (daṭṭhuṃ). Here, the elision of the nasal is for the sake of preserving the meter. 'Khemato' means 'from a state of security.' The connection is: 'having brought it by body or speech, one should invite.' And to show the method of how one should bring it by body and by speech, it is said, 'having brought it near,' and so on. 'With the inner' means together with the inner robe. 'Upper' means the upper robe. 'At most' means the limit. 'Of this robe' means of this robe that is part of the collection to be taken. For this, it should be understood, is an external compound where the quality is understood, as in 'long-eared.' Hence he says, 'with the lower robe,' and so on. For by the highest limit, all are permitted to take only that much at most.

Yasmā [M 0.0307] acchinnasabbacīvarena ticīvaramattakeneva bhikkhunā evaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ, aññena pana aññathāpi, tasmā taṃ vibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “tatrāyaṃ vinicchayo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Adhiṭṭhitacīvarassāti ticīvarādhiṭṭhānanayena vā parikkhāracoḷavasena vā yena kenaci adhiṭṭhitacīvarassa, idañca yebhuyyena adhiṭṭhahitvā cīvaraṃ paribhuñjato vuttaṃ, na pana anadhiṭṭhitacīvarassa cīvare acchinne ayaṃ vidhi na sambhavatīti. Yassa vā ticīvarato adhikampi cīvaraṃ aññattha atthi, tattha natthi, tenāpi tadā tattha abhāvato dve sādituṃ vaṭṭati. Pakatiyāva santaruttarena caratīti (sārattha. ṭī. 2.523-524) atthatakathinattā vā sāsaṅkasikkhāpadavasena vā avippavāsasammutivasena vā tatiyassa alābhena vā carati. “Dve naṭṭhānī”ti adhikārattā vuttaṃ “dve sāditabbānī”ti. Ekaṃ sādiyanteneva samo bhavissatīti tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ dvīsu naṭṭhena ekaṃ sādiyantena samo bhavissati ubhinnampi santaruttaraparamatāya avaṭṭhānato. Yassa ekaṃyeva hoti aññena kenaci kāraṇena vinaṭṭhasesacīvarattā.

Since a bhikkhu not all of whose robes have been snatched should act thus with just the three robes, while another should act otherwise, therefore, to show that distinction, it is said: 'Herein, this is the decision,' and so on. 'Of one with a determined robe' means of one who has a robe determined in any way, whether by the method of determining the three robes or as an accessory cloth. And this is said with reference to one who generally uses a robe after having determined it; it is not that this procedure is impossible for one with an undetermined robe when his robe has been snatched. Or, for one who has more than the three robes elsewhere, but has none here, it is allowable for him to procure two at that time because he has none here. 'He lives by nature with just an inner and an upper robe' (Sāratthaṭīkā 2.523–524) means he lives thus either because the kathina has been spread, or because of the training rule involving what is dubious, or because of the consent for not being separated from his robes, or because of not obtaining a third. Because it is the topic under discussion, 'two were lost' is said to mean 'two may be procured.' 'He will become equal by procuring just one' means: when two of the three robes are lost, by procuring one he will become equal, because both are established as having at most an inner and an upper robe. This is for one who has only one robe because the remaining robes were lost for some other reason.

Pañcasu naṭṭhesūti ticīvaraṃ udakasāṭikā saṃkaccikāti imesu pañcasu cīvaresu naṭṭhesu. “Ekasmiṃ vā naṭṭhe”ti vacanavipariṇāmaṃ katvā yojetabbaṃ. Tato uttarīti santaruttaraparamato uttari.

'When five are lost' means when these five robes are lost: the three robes, the bathing cloth, and the shoulder-cloth. 'Or when one is lost' should be connected by changing the grammatical case. 'Further than that' means further than the maximum of an inner and an upper robe.

Sesakaṃ āharissāmīti dve cīvarāni katvā “sesakaṃ puna āharissāmī”ti attho. Sesakaṃ tuyhaṃyeva hotūti vuttassāti dānasamaye evaṃ vuttassa. Sace pana “sesakaṃ āharissāmī”ti vatvā gahetvā gamanasamayepi “sesakaṃ tuyhaṃyeva hotū”ti vadanti, laddhakappiyameva. Na acchinnanaṭṭhakāraṇā dinnanti bāhusaccādiguṇavasena dinnaṃ. Vuttanayenāti “ñātakappavārite vā viññāpentassa, samaye ca aññassa vā ñātakappavārite tassevatthāya viññāpentassa”ti vuttanayena.

'I will bring the remainder' means, having made two robes, 'I will bring the remainder again.' 'Let the remainder be yours alone' refers to one who was told this at the time of the gift. But if, having said, 'I will bring the remainder,' and having taken it, they also say at the time of departure, 'Let the remainder be yours alone,' it is allowable as received. 'Not given for the reason of being snatched or lost' means given on account of qualities such as great learning. 'By the method stated' means by the method stated thus: 'for one who requests from a relative or from one who has invited; or for one who, at the proper time, requests for his own sake from another who has been invited by a relative.'

Tatuttarisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Further Training Rule is concluded.

8. Paṭhamaupakkhaṭasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the First Set-Aside Training Rule

Bhikkhuṃ [V 0.0283][M 0.0308] paneva uddissāti ettha panāti nipātamattaṃ, tathā eva-saddopi. Tenāha “itthannāmassā”tiādi. Apadisitvāti kathetvā, ārabbhāti vā attho. Aññātakassa gahapatissāti aññātakagahapatināti attho. Karaṇatthe hi idaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana idaṃ suviññeyyanti na vicāritaṃ. Cīvaraṃ cetāpenti parivattenti etenāti cīvaracetāpannaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. 2.528-529), cīvaramūlaṃ, na-kāro panettha āgamo, “cīvaracetāpana”ntipi paṭhanti. Taṃ pana yasmā hiraññādīsu aññataraṃ hoti, tasmā “hiraññādika”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha hiraññanti kahāpaṇo vuccati. Ādisaddena suvaṇṇādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Upakkhaṭanti upaṭṭhāpitaṃ. Taṃ upakkharaṇaṃ tesaṃ tathā sajjitanti āha “upakkhaṭaṃ hotīti sajjitaṃ hotī”ti. Saṃharitvā ṭhapitanti rāsiṃ katvā ṭhapitaṃ. Parivattanañca akatassa kārāpanaṃ, katassa kiṇananti āha “kāretvā vā kiṇitvā vāti attho”ti. Acchādessāmīti pārupessāmīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tenāha “vohāravacanameta”nti. Vohāravacananti ca upacāravacananti attho.

In 'having designated a bhikkhu,' here 'pana' is merely a particle, and so too the word 'eva.' Hence it says, 'for so-and-so,' and so on. 'Apadisitvā' means having stated, or it means 'having referred to.' 'Of an unrelated householder' means 'by an unrelated householder.' For this genitive has the sense of the instrumental. However, in the commentary this was not discussed as it is easy to understand. 'Cīvaracetāpannaṃ' is that by which they procure or exchange a robe; it is the price of a robe (Sāratthaṭīkā 2.528–529). Here the letter 'n' is an augment; some also read it as 'cīvaracetāpana.' But since that is one or another of such things as gold, it is called 'gold, etc.' Therein, 'hirañña' refers to a kahāpaṇa. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), gold and so on are included. 'Set aside' means prepared. That provision is arranged for them thus; hence it says, ''is set aside' means 'is arranged'.' 'Collected and set down' means made into a pile and set down. And 'exchange' means having an unmade one made or buying a made one; hence it says, 'the meaning is “having had it made or having bought it”.' 'I will clothe' means 'I will dress (him).' Hence it says, 'This is a conventional expression.' And 'conventional expression' means a figurative expression.

“Tatra ce so bhikkhū”tiādīsu ko padasambandhoti āha “yatra so gahapati vā”tiādi. Pubbe appavāritoti “dassāmi, kīdisena te, bhante, cīvarena attho, kīdisaṃ te cīvaraṃ cetāpemī”ti pubbe avutto. Upasaṅkamitvāti gantvā. Padabhājane pacuravohāravasena “gharaṃ gantvā”ti (pārā. 529) vuttaṃ. Ettha ca pacuravohāravasenāti yebhuyyavohāravasena. Yebhuyyena hi gharasāmikaṃ daṭṭhukāmā tassa gharaṃ gacchantīti tatheva bahulavohāro. Vikappanti visiṭṭho kappo vikappo, vi-saddo cettha visiṭṭhattho. Tenāha “visiṭṭhakappa”nti. Iminā vacanatthamāha. “Adhikavidhāna”nti iminā pana adhippāyatthaṃ. Yathā pana tamāpajjatīti yenākārena taṃ vikappaṃ āpajjati. Taṃ dassetunti taṃ ākāraṃ dassetuṃ.

Regarding 'There, if that bhikkhu,' and so on, what is the connection of the words? He says, 'where that householder,' and so on. 'Not previously invited' means not previously told: 'I will give. What kind of robe do you need, venerable sir? What kind of robe shall I have procured for you?' 'Having approached' means having gone. In the analysis of the terms, 'having gone to the house' (Pārā. 529) is said on account of common usage. And here, 'on account of common usage' means on account of predominant usage. For generally, those wishing to see the master of the house go to his house; thus that is the frequent usage. 'Vikappa' is a specific suggestion; here the word 'vi' has the sense of 'specific.' Hence he says, 'a specific suggestion.' By this he states the literal meaning. But by 'an additional stipulation,' he states the intended meaning. 'In whatever way one undertakes it' means in whatever manner one makes that suggestion. 'To show that' means to show that manner.

“Sādhū”ti ayaṃ saddo sampaṭicchanasampahaṃsanasundarāyācanādīsu dissati. Tathā hesa “sādhu, bhanteti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṃ [M 0.0309] abhinanditvā anumoditvā”tiādīsu (ma. ni. 3.86) sampaṭicchane dissati, “sādhu sādhu sāriputtā”tiādīsu (dī. ni. 3.349; ma. ni. 1.340) sampahaṃsane.

The word 'sādhu' is seen in the senses of acceptance, praise, what is good, request, and so on. Thus it is seen in the sense of acceptance in such passages as: '"Good, venerable sir," that bhikkhu, having delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One's statement...' (MN 3.86); and in the sense of praise in such passages as: 'Good, good, Sāriputta!' (DN 3.349; MN 1.340).

“Sādhu [V 0.0284] dhammaruci rājā, sādhu paññāṇavā naro;

Sādhu mittānamaddubbho, pāpassākaraṇaṃ sukha”ntiādīsu. (jā. 2.18.101) –

in the sense of 'good' in such passages as: 'Good is a king who delights in the Dhamma, / good is a person endowed with wisdom; / good is non-treachery toward friends, / the non-doing of evil is happiness' (Ja 2.18.101);

Sundare, “sādhu me, bhante bhagavā, saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetū”tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 3.64-68) āyācane, idhāpi āyācaneyeva daṭṭhabboti (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.189; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1 mūlapariyāyasuttavaṇṇanā; su. ni. aṭṭha. 1.115 aggikabhāradvājasuttavaṇṇanā; bu. vaṃ. aṭṭha. 1.49) āha “sādhūti āyācane nipāto”ti. Tattha āyācaneti abhimukhaṃ yācane, abhipatthanāyanti attho. Parivitakke nipātoti sambandho. Ālapatīti āmanteti. Āyatādīsūti ettha ādisaddena vitthataappitasaṇhānaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Yasmā pana na imassa āpajjanamatteneva āpatti sīsaṃ eti, tasmā “tassa vacanenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Payogeti suttapariyesanādipayoge.

and in the sense of 'request' in such passages as: 'Good, venerable sir, let the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma in brief' (SN 3.64–68). Here too it should be seen as a request (DN-a 1.189; MN-a 1, Mūlapariyāyasuttavaṇṇanā; Snp-a 1.115, Aggikabhāradvājasuttavaṇṇanā; Bv-a 1.49); hence he says, ''Sādhu' is a particle used in a request.' Therein, 'in a request' means in asking directly; the meaning is 'in earnest longing.' The connection is: 'a particle in deliberation.' 'He addresses' means he calls out to. In 'long, etc.,' by the word 'etc.' are included broad, finely woven, and smooth. Since an offense does not come to a head merely by undertaking this, therefore it is said, 'by his word,' and so on. 'In the effort' means in the effort of searching for thread, and so on.

Mahagghaṃ cetāpetukāmaṃ appagghanti vīsatiagghanakaṃ cīvaraṃ cetāpetukāmaṃ “alaṃ mayhaṃ tena, dasaagghanakaṃ vā aṭṭhagghanakaṃ vā dehī”ti vadantassāti attho. Evarūpanti evaṃ samabhāgaṃ, iminā samakanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tañca kho agghavaseneva, na pamāṇavasena. Agghavaḍḍhanakañhi idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ.

The meaning is of one who, when someone wishes to have an expensive robe procured for him—that is, a robe worth twenty—says: 'Enough of that for me; give me one worth ten or eight.' 'Of such a kind' means of such an equal share; it means 'equal to this.' And that is by way of value, not by way of measure. For this training rule concerns an increase in value.

Paṭhamaupakkhaṭasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Prepared Training Rule is concluded.

9. Dutiyaupakkhaṭasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Second Prepared Training Rule

Kasmā iminā nayena attho veditabboti āha “idañhī”tiādi. Hīti kāraṇatthe nipāto. Na koci visesoti āha “kevala”ntiādi.

Why should the meaning be understood in this way? To this it is said: 'This is because,' etc. The particle hi is in the sense of a reason. There is no difference; thus it is said: 'Only,' etc.

Dutiyaupakkhaṭasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Prepared Training Rule is concluded.

10. Rājasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning a King

Rājato [M 0.0310] bhogganti rājato laddhabhoggaṃ. Rājabhoggoti rājāmatto. Rājato bhogoti raññā [V 0.0285] dinnaṃ issariyaṃ. Iminātiādīti “iminā cīvaracetāpannena cīvaraṃ cetāpetvā itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarena acchādehī”ti idaṃ. Āgamanasuddhinti mūlasuddhiṃ. Yadi hi iminā kappiyanīhārena apesetvā “idaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dehī”ti peseyya, sopi dūto taṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeyya “idaṃ kho, bhante, āyasmantaṃ uddissa cīvaracetāpannaṃ ābhataṃ, paṭiggaṇhātu āyasmā cīvaracetāpanna”nti (pārā. 538), tadā paṭikkhipitvāpi kappiyakārakaṃ puṭṭhena taṃ niddisituṃ na vaṭṭati. Tenāha “sace hī”tiādi. Akappiyavatthuṃ ārabbhāti hiraññādiṃ ārabbha. Īdisena dūtavacanenāti “paṭiggaṇhātu āyasmā cīvaracetāpanna”nti evarūpena dūtavacanena. Tasmāti yasmā sampaṭicchituṃ akappiyaṃ hoti, tasmā. Suvaṇṇanti jātarūpaṃ. Rajatanti rūpiyaṃ. Kahāpaṇenāti suvaṇṇamayo vā rūpiyamayo vā pākatiko vā kahāpaṇo. Māsakoti lohamāsako vā hotu, dārumāsako vā hotu, jatumāsako vā hotu, yo yo yattha yattha janapade yadā yadā vohāraṃ gacchati, antamaso aṭṭhimayopi cammamayopi rukkhaphalabījamayopi samuṭṭhāpitarūpopi asamuṭṭhāpitarūpopi sabbo idha māsakoti veditabbo. Ettha ca yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ rūpiyasikkhāpade vakkhāma.

Enjoying from the king means enjoying what is obtained from the king. A royal enjoyer means a king's minister. Enjoyment from the king means sovereignty given by the king. By this, etc., means this: 'With this robe-fund, having had a robe made, clothe the bhikkhu so-and-so with the robe.' Purity of arrival means purity of the source. For if, having sent it away by this allowable method, one were to send it saying, 'Give this to the bhikkhu so-and-so,' and that messenger, having approached that bhikkhu, were to say: 'Venerable sir, this robe-fund has been brought designated for the venerable one; let the venerable one accept the robe-fund,' then, even after having refused it, it is not allowable for him, when asked by the one who makes things allowable, to point it out. For that reason it is said: 'For if,' etc. Concerning an unallowable item means concerning gold, etc. By such words of the messenger means by words of the messenger of this kind: 'Let the venerable one accept the robe-fund.' Therefore means: because it is unallowable to accept, therefore... Gold means gold bullion. Silver means silver coin. With a kahāpaṇa means a kahāpaṇa that is made of gold, or made of silver, or a standard one. A māsaka: whether it is a copper māsaka, a wooden māsaka, or a lac māsaka; whatever is current in whatever country at whatever time—even one made of bone, of leather, or of the seed of a fruit tree; whether artificial or natural—all this should be understood here as a māsaka. And whatever should be said on this, we will say in the training rule on silver.

Muttāti hatthikumbhajādikā aṭṭhavidhā muttā. Tathā hi hatthikumbhaṃ varāhadāṭhaṃ, bhujaṅgasīsaṃ, valāhakaṃ, veḷu, macchasiro, saṅkho, sippīti aṭṭha muttāyoniyo. Tattha yā macchasaṅkhasippijātā, sā sāmuddikā, bhujaṅgajāpi kāci sāmuddikā hoti. Itarā asāmuddikā. Yasmā pana bahulaṃ sāmuddikāva muttā loke dissanti, tatthāpi sippijāva, itarā kadāci. Tasmā sammohavinodaniyaṃ “muttāti sāmuddikamuttā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 172) vuttaṃ. Maṇīti ṭhapetvā veḷuriyādike antamaso jātiphalikaṃ upādāya sabbopi nīlapītādivaṇṇabhedo maṇīti veditabbo, pacitvā kato pana kācamaṇiyeveko pattādibhaṇḍamūlatthaṃ sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Veḷuriyo nāma vaṃsavaṇṇamaṇi. Saṅkhoti dhamanasaṅkho dhotaviddho ratanamisso, pānīyasaṅkho [M 0.0311] pana ratanāmissakato, so ca añjanādibhesajjatthāya, bhaṇḍamūlatthāya ca sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Silāti dhotaviddhā ratanasaṃyuttā muggavaṇṇā silā. Ratanena pana amissā satthakanisānādiatthāya paṭiggaṇhituṃ vaṭṭati. Ettha ca “ratanasaṃyuttāti suvaṇṇena saddhiṃ yojetvā pacitvā katā”ti vadanti. Pavāḷanti dhotampi adhotampi sabbaṃ pavāḷaṃ. Lohitaṅkoti rattamaṇi. Masāragallanti kabaramaṇi. Yaṃ “marakata”ntipi vuccati.

Pearls means the eight kinds of pearls, such as those from an elephant's frontal globe. For these are the eight sources of pearls: from an elephant's frontal globe, a boar's tusk, a serpent's head, a cloud, bamboo, a fish's head, a conch, and an oyster. Among these, those born from a fish, a conch, and an oyster are marine; some born from a serpent are also marine. The others are non-marine.
