Sati karaṇīye āmasatoti sati karaṇīye purisaṃ āmasato anāpatti. Itthī pana sati karaṇīyepi āmasituṃ na vaṭṭati.

Here, for a monk who touches a nun with the intention of play, there is an offense of wrong conduct. Similarly, for a nun touching a monk, it is said: 'Here, a nun also for a monk, and a monk for an unordained woman...'. In all cases concerning what is connected to the body, and so on—'with the body on what is connected to the body, with what is connected to the body on the body, with what is connected to the body on what is connected to the body, with a thrown object on the body, with a thrown object on what is connected to the body, with a thrown object on a thrown object' (Pāc. 332)—it applies in all cases. 'When there is a reason, in touching' means that when there is a reason, for one who touches a man, there is no offense. A woman, however, is not permitted to touch even when there is a reason.

Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Poking with a Finger is concluded.

3. Hasadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Training Rule on Playing in Jest

Uparigopphaketi gopphakānaṃ uparibhāgappamāṇe. Hasādhippāyoti kīḷādhippāyo. Yena yena aṅgenāti hatthapādādīsu yena yena aṅgena. Tathā nāvāya kīḷatoti phiyārittādīhi nāvaṃ pājentassa vā tīre ussārentassa vā dukkaṭanti attho.

'Above the ankles' means the area measured above the ankles. 'With the intention of laughter' means with the intention of play. 'With whichever limb' means with whichever limb, such as the hands and feet. Similarly, 'playing with a boat' means there is an offense of wrong conduct for one who propels a boat with an oar or the like, or pulls it up on the shore.

Hasadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Playing in Jest is concluded.

4. Anādariyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Disrespect

Duvidhañhettha anādariyaṃ puggalānādariyañca dhammānādariyañcāti āha “puggalassa vā”tiādi. Tattha yo bhikkhu upasampannena paññattena vuccamāno “ayaṃ ukkhittako vā vambhito vā garahito vā, imassa vacanaṃ akataṃ bhavissatī”ti (pāci. 342) anādariyaṃ karoti, ayaṃ puggale anādariyaṃ karoti nāma. Yo pana paññattena vuccamāno “kathāyaṃ nasseyya vā vinasseyya [M 0.0404] vā antaradhāyeyya vā”ti, taṃ vā nasikkhitukāmo anādariyaṃ karoti, ayaṃ dhamme anādariyaṃ karoti nāma. Tenāha “tasmā”tiādi.

Here, disrespect is twofold: disrespect toward a person and disrespect toward the Dhamma. Thus it is said: 'toward a person, or...' and so forth. In this regard, when a bhikkhu, being addressed by one who is fully ordained according to what has been laid down, thinks, 'This one is suspended, or reviled, or censured—his word shall be as naught,' and shows disrespect, this is called disrespect toward a person. But when one, being addressed according to what has been laid down, thinks, 'May this teaching be lost, or perish, or disappear,' or being unwilling to train in it, shows disrespect, this is called disrespect toward the Dhamma. Therefore, it is said: 'Therefore...' and so forth.

Idaṃ [V 0.0370] na sallekhāya saṃvattatīti sammā kilese likhatīti sallekho, appicchatā, tadatthaṃ nayidaṃ saṃvattati. Ādisaddena “idaṃ na dhutatthāya saṃvattati, na pāsādikatāya, na apacayāya, na vīriyārambhāya saṃvattatī”ti (pāci. 343) idaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Apaññattenāti sutte vā abhidhamme vā āgatena. Paveṇiāgatanti saṅgītikālato paṭṭhāya mahākassapādiācariyaparamparāya āgataṃ. Sace pana yasmā ucchuraso sattāhakāliko, tassa kasaṭo yāvajīviko, dvinnaṃyeva samavāyo ucchuyaṭṭhi, tasmā vikāle ucchuyaṭṭhiṃ khādituṃ vaṭṭati guḷaharītakaṃ viyāti evamādikaṃ gārayhācariyuggahaṃ gahetvā “evaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyānaṃ uggaho paripucchā”ti bhaṇati, āpattiyeva.

'This does not lead to effacement.' 'Effacement' (sallekha) means rightly scraping away defilements; it is having few wishes. This does not serve that purpose. By the word 'etc.,' it includes: 'This does not lead to the ascetic practices, nor to serenity, nor to reverence, nor to arousing energy' (Pāc. 343). 'Not laid down' means that which is found in the Suttas or the Abhidhamma. 'Transmitted through tradition' means received from the lineage of teachers such as Mahākassapa, starting from the time of the Council. But if one, having taken up the blameworthy view of a teacher, argues, 'Since sugarcane juice is allowable for seven days, and its dregs are allowable for life, and a sugarcane stalk is just a combination of the two, therefore it is permissible to chew a sugarcane stalk at the wrong time, like jaggery with myrobalan,' and says, 'This is the learning and inquiry of our teachers,' it is an offense indeed.

Anādariyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Disrespect is concluded.

5. Bhiṃsāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Intimidation

Rūpādīnīti bhayānakāni rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbāni. Bhayānakakathanti corakantāravāḷakantārapisācakantārappaṭisaṃyuttakathaṃ.

'Forms, etc.' means frightening forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangible objects. 'Frightening talk' means talk connected with a wilderness of thieves, a wilderness of wild beasts, or a wilderness of demons.

Bhiṃsāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Intimidation is concluded.

6. Jotisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Training Rule on Fire

Agilānoti yassa vinā agginā phāsu hoti, so idha agilāno nāma. Jotinti aggiṃ.

'Not sick' means one who is comfortable without fire is here called 'not sick.' 'Light' means fire.

Bhaggesūti evaṃnāmake janapade. Bhaggānāma jānapadino rājakumārā, tesaṃ nivāso ekopi janapado ruḷhisaddena “bhaggā”ti vuccati. Tena vuttaṃ “bhaggesūti evaṃnāmake janapade”ti. Tathā patilātaṃ ukkhipantassāti ḍayhamānaṃ alātaṃ patitaṃ ukkhipantassa tathā dukkaṭanti attho. Tañcāti [M 0.0405] dukkaṭaṃ parāmasati. Avijjhātanti anibbutālātaṃ. Padīpajotikajantāghareti padīpujjalanapattapacanasedakammādīsu jotikaraṇe aggisālāyañca samādahantassa anāpattīti attho. Tathārūpappaccayeti ṭhapetvā padīpādīni aññasmimpi tathārūpapaccaye. Āpadāsūti duṭṭhavāḷamigaamanussehi upaddavesu.

'In the Bhagga country' means in a country of that name. The princes of that country were called the Bhaggas, and their residence, even a single territory, is known by the common term 'Bhagga.' Hence it is said, 'in the Bhagga country,' meaning in a country of that name. Similarly, 'for one who picks up a fallen firebrand' means there is likewise an offense of wrong conduct for one who picks up a fallen, burning firebrand. 'And that' refers to that offense of wrong conduct. 'Not extinguished' means an unextinguished firebrand. 'In a lamp, a light, or a steam-bath house' means there is no offense for one who kindles a fire in a fire-hall for such purposes as lighting a lamp, cooking a bowl, or for a sweating treatment. 'When there is such a reason' means also in other such circumstances, apart from lamps and so on. 'In times of calamity' means during troubles from vicious wild animals or non-humans.

Jotisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Fire is concluded.

7. Nahānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Bathing

“Diyaḍḍho [V 0.0371] māso seso gimhāna”nti “vassānassa paṭhamo māso”iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayoti gimhānaṃ seso diyaḍḍho māso uṇhasamayo, vassānassa paṭhamo māso pariḷāhasamayoti evaṃ ete aḍḍhateyyamāsā kamena uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayo nāma hotīti attho teneva padabhājaniyaṃ “uṇhasamayo nāma diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhāna”nti, “pariḷāhasamayo nāma vassānassa paṭhamo māso”ti vuttaṃ. Yadā vinā nahānena na phāsu hoti, ayaṃ gilānasamayo. Padabhājaniyaṃ (pāci. 364) pana gilāne nicchite gilānakālo nicchitova hotīti “yassa vinā nahānena na phāsu hoti, ‘gilānasamayo’ti nahāyitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Pariveṇasammajjanamattampīti antamaso pariveṇasammajjanamattampi.

'One and a half months remain of the hot season,' and 'the first month of the rainy season'—these two and a half months are the hot time and the scorching time. The remaining one and a half months of the hot season is the hot time, and the first month of the rainy season is the scorching time. Thus, these two and a half months are, in sequence, called the hot time and the scorching time. This is the meaning. For that reason, in the word-analysis it is said: 'The hot time is the remaining one and a half months of the hot season,' and 'the scorching time is the first month of the rainy season.' When one is not comfortable without bathing, this is the time of sickness. In the word-analysis (Pācittiya 364), however, since the time of sickness is determined when the sick person is determined, it is said: 'One for whom it is not comfortable without bathing should bathe, this being the time of sickness.' 'Even just the measure of sweeping the monastic compound' means at the very least, even just sweeping the monastic compound.

Vālukaṃ ukkiritvāti sukkhāya nadiyā vālikaṃ uttiritvā. Āvāṭesupīti pi-saddena nadiyaṃ vattabbameva natthīti dasseti. Āpadāsūti bhamarādīhi anubandhesu.

'Having dug up sand' means having dug up sand from a dry river. 'Even in pits': the particle 'pi' shows that there is nothing at all to be said about doing so in a river. 'In times of calamity' means when being pursued by bees and so on.

Nahānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Bathing is concluded.

8. Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule on Discoloring

Lābhasaddoyaṃ kammasādhano “ko bhavatā lābho laddho”tiādīsu viya, so cettha atītakālikoti āha “alabbhīti labho”ti[M 0.0406], laddhanti attho. “Labho eva lābho”ti iminā sakatthe ṇapaccayoti dasseti. Kiṃ alabbhīti kiṃ laddhaṃ. Navanti abhinavaṃ. Ettāvatā ca navañca taṃ cīvarañcāti navacīvaraṃ, navacīvaraṃ lābho etenāti navacīvaralābhoti evamettha samāso daṭṭhabboti. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ “navaṃ cīvaralābhenā”ti vuttanti āha “iti navacīvaralābhenā”tiādi. Ettha ca “vikappanupagaṃ pacchima”nti na vuttattā cīvaranti yaṃ nivāsetuṃ vā pārupituṃ vā sakkā hoti, tadeva veditabbanti āha “nivāsanapārupanupagaṃ cīvara”nti. “Dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ ādātabba”nti etaṃ kappabinduṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na nīlādīhi sakalacīvaraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ, tañca pana kappaṃ ādiyantena cīvaraṃ rajitvā catūsu vā koṇesu, tīsu vā dvīsu vā ekasmiṃ vā koṇe morassa akkhimaṇḍalamattaṃ vā maṅgulapiṭṭhimattaṃ vā ādātabbanti āha “tassā”tiādi. Kaṃsanīlenāti cammakāranīlena. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “ayomalaṃ lohamalaṃ, etaṃ kaṃsanīlaṃ nāmā”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 368) vuttaṃ[V 0.0372]. Pattanīlenāti yena kenaci nīlavaṇṇena paṇṇarasena. Kappabinduṃ ādiyitvāti vaṭṭaṃ ekaṃ kappabinduṃ ādiyitvā.

The word `lābha` is formed in the sense of the object, as in, “What gain has been obtained by you?” and so forth. Here, it is in the past tense, hence it is said, “‘That which was obtained’ is `labha`,” meaning “obtained.” By “`Labho` is indeed `lābho`,” it shows that the suffix `ṇa` is used in its own sense. “What was obtained?” means “what was gained.” “New” means fresh. By this much, “that which is a new robe” is `navacīvara`, and “a new robe is the gain by this” is `navacīvaralābha`; this is how the compound should be understood here. If so, how is it said, “by the gain of a new robe”? It is said, “Thus, ‘by the gain of a new robe,’” and so forth. And here, since “the last, suitable for determination” is not said, `cīvara` is to be understood as that which can be worn as a lower garment or an upper garment; hence, it is said, “a robe suitable for wearing as a lower or upper garment.” “A disfiguring mark should be applied” is said with reference to the `kappabindu` mark, not that the entire robe should be disfigured with blue and so forth. And when applying that `kappa` mark, having dyed the robe, a mark the size of a peacock’s eye-circle or the size of a bedbug’s back should be applied on one, two, three, or four of the corners; hence, it is said, “of that,” and so forth. “With bronze-blue” means with leather-worker’s blue. But in the Mahāpaccarī it is said, “Iron rust, metal rust, this is called bronze-blue.” “With leaf-blue” means with the juice of any kind of blue-colored leaf. “Having applied a `kappabindu` mark” means having applied one round `kappabindu` mark.

Pāḷikappakaṇṇikakappādayo pana sabbaṭṭhakathāsu paṭisiddhā. Aggaḷādīni kappakatacīvare pana pacchā āropetvā kappakaraṇakiccaṃ natthīti āha “pacchā āropitesū”tiādi. Aggaḷaanuvātaparibhaṇḍesūti uddharitvā alliyāpanakakhaṇḍapiṭṭhianuvātakucchianuvātesu. Kiriyākiriyanti nivāsanapārupanato, kappassa anādānato kiriyākiriyaṃ.

However, applying a line of marks, marks in the corners, and so forth, are prohibited in all the commentaries. But regarding fasteners and so forth on a robe that has already been made allowable, since there is no duty of making it allowable by attaching them afterwards, it is said, “when attached afterwards,” and so forth. “Regarding fasteners, border-strips, and hems” means regarding pieces that are lifted up and attached, back border-strips, and side border-strips. “Action and non-action”: from the wearing of the lower and upper garments it is an action; from the non-application of the `kappa` mark, it is a non-action.

Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on disfigurement is concluded.

9. Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Determination

Sammukhena vikappanā sammukhavikappanā. Parammukhena vikappanā parammukhavikappanā. Sannihitāsannihitabhāvanti āsannadūrabhāvaṃ. Āsannadūrabhāvo ca adhiṭṭhāne vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

Determination in one’s presence is face-to-face determination. Determination in one’s absence is determination through a proxy. “The state of being present or not present” means the state of nearness or farness. And this state of nearness or farness should be understood in the very same way as stated in the section on resolution (`adhiṭṭhāna`).

Mittoti daḷhamitto. Sandiṭṭhoti diṭṭhamatto nātidaḷhamitto. Akatapaccuddhāranti “mayhaṃ santakaṃ paribhuñja vā vissajjehi vā”tiādinā akatapaccuddhāraṃ. Yena vinayakammaṃ katanti yena saddhiṃ vinayakammaṃ kataṃ.

“A friend” means a firm friend. “An acquaintance” means one who is merely seen, not a very firm friend. “One from whom a withdrawal has not been made” means one from whom a withdrawal has not been made by such words as, “You may use or dispose of what is mine.” “With whom a disciplinary act was done” means with whom a disciplinary act was performed.

Paribhogena [M 0.0407] kāyakammaṃ, apaccuddhārāpanena vacīkammanti āha “samuṭṭhānādīni paṭhamakathinasadisānevā”ti. Kiriyākiriyanti ettha paribhuñjanaṃ kiriyaṃ. Apaccuddhārāpanaṃ akiriyaṃ.

By using, it is a bodily act; by not having the determination withdrawn, it is a verbal act. Thus it is said, “The origins and so forth are just like those of the first Kathina training rule.” As for action and non-action, here using is the action; not having the determination withdrawn is the non-action.

Vikappanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on determination is concluded.

10. Apanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Concealment

Adhiṭṭhānupaganti adhiṭṭhānayoggaṃ ayopattañceva mattikāpattañca. Sūkarantakaṃ nāma kuñcikākoso viya anto susiraṃ katvā koṭṭitaṃ.

“Suitable for determination” means suitable for resolution (`adhiṭṭhāna`), namely, an iron bowl and a clay bowl. “Boar’s-gut-like” (`sūkarantaka`) is the name for something made hollow inside like a key-case and then hammered into shape.

Aññaṃ [V 0.0373] parikkhāranti pāḷiyā anāgatapattatthavikādiṃ. Dhammakathaṃ katvāti “samaṇena nāma anihitaparikkhārena bhavituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti evaṃ “dhammakathaṃ kathetvā dassāmī”ti nikkhipato anāpatti.

“Another requisite” means a requisite not mentioned in the Pāḷi text, such as a bowl-bag and so forth. “Having given a Dhamma talk” means there is no offense for one who puts it aside thinking, “I will give it after delivering a Dhamma talk,” such as, “It is not proper for a recluse to be one whose requisites are not put away.”

Apanidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on concealment is concluded.

Surāpānavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Sixth Chapter: On Drinking Intoxicants.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Chapter on Living Beings

1. Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Intention

Pācittiyanti [V 0.0374] antamaso mañcapīṭhaṃ sodhento maṅgulabījakepi pāṇasaññī nikkāruṇikatāya taṃ bhindanto apaneti (pāci. aṭṭha. 382), pācittiyaṃ. Tenāha “taṃ khuddakampī”tiādi. Upakkamamahantatāya akusalaṃ mahantaṃ hotīti bahukkhattuṃ pavattajavanehi laddhāsevanāya sanniṭṭhāpakacetanāya vasena payogassa mahantattā akusalaṃ mahantaṃ hoti, mahāsāvajjaṃ hotīti adhippāyo.

“A `pācittiya` offense” means that if, at the very least, while cleaning a bed or a chair, one is aware of a living being, even a bedbug’s egg, and, out of mercilessness, crushes and removes it, it is a `pācittiya` offense. Therefore it is said, “even that small thing,” and so forth. “Because of the greatness of the undertaking, the unwholesome becomes great” means that due to the greatness of the effort—by way of the concluding volition that has gained practice through impulsions occurring many times—the unwholesome becomes great, it becomes highly blameworthy; this is the intention.

Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on intention is concluded.

2. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Water Containing Living Beings

Ettha [M 0.0408] ca paṭaṅgapāṇakānaṃ patanaṃ ñatvāpi suddhacittatāya padīpujjalane viya sappāṇakabhāvaṃ ñatvāpi udakasaññāya paribhuñjitabbato paṇṇattivajjatā veditabbā.

And here, it should be understood that this is a formulated offense because, even knowing of the presence of living beings, the water is to be used with the perception of water; this is like the lighting of a lamp where, even knowing that winged insects will fall into it, one has a pure mind.

Sappāṇakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on water containing living beings is concluded.

3. Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Reviving a Legal Issue

Tassa tassa bhikkhunoti yena yena vūpasamitaṃ, tassa tassa bhikkhuno. “Akataṃ kamma”ntiādīni vadantoti “akataṃ kammaṃ, dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ, puna kātabbaṃ kammaṃ, anihataṃ dunnihataṃ puna nihanitabba”nti (pāci. 394) vadanto. Yathāṭhitabhāvena patiṭṭhātuṃ na dadeyyāti tesaṃ pavatti ākāradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenāha “yaṃ pana dhammena adhikaraṇaṃ nihataṃ, taṃ sunihatamevā”ti.

“Of this and that bhikkhu” means of each and every bhikkhu by whom it was settled. “Saying, ‘The act is undone,’ and so forth” means one who says, “The act is undone, the act is badly done, the act should be done again; it is not settled, it is badly settled, it should be settled again.” “He would not allow it to stand as it is” is said in order to show the manner of their proceeding. Therefore, it is said, “But whatever legal issue is settled according to the Dhamma, that is well-settled indeed.”

Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on reviving a legal issue is concluded.

4. Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Grave Offense

Cattāri [V 0.0375] pārājikāni atthuddhāravasena padabhājaniyaṃ dassitānīti āha “duṭṭhullanti saṅghādisesaṃ adhippeta”nti. Yena kenaci upāyenāti “sāmaṃ vā jānāti, aññe vā tassa ārocenti, so vā ārocetī”ti (pāci. 399) vuttesu yena kenaci upāyena. Pācittiyaṃ dhuraṃ nikkhittamatteyevāti adhippāyo. Sace pacchāpi āroceti, dhuranikkhepane āpattito na muccati. Tenāha “sacepī”tiādi. Samaṇasatampi āpajjatiyevāti samaṇasatampi sutvā yadi chādeti, pācittiyaṃ āpajjatiyevāti attho. Yenassa ārocitanti yena dutiyena assa tatiyassa ārocitaṃ. Tassevāti tassa dutiyasseva. Ārocetīti paṭicchādanatthameva “mā kassaci ārocesī”ti vadati. Koṭichinnā hotīti (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.399) yasmā paṭicchādanapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjitvāva dutiyena [M 0.0409] tatiyassa ārocitaṃ, tasmā tappaccayā puna tena āpajjitabbāpattiyā abhāvato āpattiyā koṭi chinnā nāma hoti.

Since the four `pārājika` offenses are shown in the word-analysis by way of a summary of their meaning, it is said, “‘Grave offense’ means a `saṅghādisesa` offense is intended.” “By any means whatsoever” refers to any of the means mentioned in the text: “whether he knows it himself, or others inform him of it, or he himself informs others.” The intention is that a `pācittiya` offense is incurred at the very moment of laying down the burden. If he informs later, he is not freed from the offense incurred by laying down the burden. Therefore, it is said, “even if,” and so forth. “He incurs it even from a hundred recluses” means that if he conceals it after hearing from even a hundred recluses, he still incurs a `pācittiya` offense. “By whom it was reported to him” means by which second person it was reported to this third person. “To him alone” means to that second person alone. “He reports” means he speaks for the very purpose of concealment, saying, “Do not report this to anyone.” “The end is cut off” means that because it was reported by the second person to the third only after having incurred the offense on account of concealment, therefore, since there is no further offense to be incurred by him on that account, the end of the offense is said to be cut off.

Ādipadeti duṭṭhullāpattisaññī, vematiko, aduṭṭhullāpattisaññīti imesu tīsu “duṭṭhullāpattisaññī paṭicchādetī”ti (pāci. 400) imasmiṃ paṭhamapade. Itaresu dvīsūti “vematiko paṭicchādeti, aduṭṭhullāpattisaññī paṭicchādetī”ti imesu padesu. Aduṭṭhullāyāti avasesapañcāpattikkhandhe. Anupasampannassa duṭṭhulle vā aduṭṭhulle vā ajjhācāreti anupasampannassa purimapañcasikkhāpadavītikkamasaṅkhāte duṭṭhulle vā itarasmiṃ aduṭṭhulle vā ajjhācāre. Yaṃ pana samantapāsādikāyaṃ “anupasampannassa sukkavisaṭṭhi ca kāyasaṃsaggo cāti ayaṃ duṭṭhullaajjhācāro nāmā”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 400) vuttaṃ, taṃ duṭṭhullārocanasikkhāpadaṭṭhakathāya (pāci. aṭṭha. 78 ādayo) na sameti, na cāpi evaṃ vattuṃ yujjati “ārocane anupasampannassa duṭṭhullaṃ aññathā adhippetaṃ, paṭicchādane aññathā”ti (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 400) visesakāraṇassānupalabbhanato, tasmā taṃ upaparikkhitabbaṃ.

In the first clause, it is 'he conceals thinking it is a grave offense' (Pāc. 400), among these three: perceiving a grave offense, being doubtful, or perceiving a non-grave offense. In the other two cases, it is 'he conceals while being doubtful' and 'he conceals thinking it is not a grave offense.' 'Not grave' refers to the remaining five groups of offenses. 'Transgression towards one not yet ordained, whether grave or not grave' means a transgression towards one not yet ordained, whether a grave offense reckoned as transgression of the first five training rules, or the other non-grave one. However, what is stated in the Samantapāsādikā—'The grave transgression towards one not yet ordained includes emission of semen and physical contact' (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 400)—does not accord with the commentary on the rule about disclosing grave offenses (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 78 ff.). Nor is it proper to say, 'In disclosure, a grave offense towards one not yet ordained is meant one way, while in concealment, it is meant another way' (Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā, Pācittiya 400), since no special reason is found for such a distinction; therefore, that should be investigated.

Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Training Rule on Grave Offenses is concluded.

5. Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning One Under Twenty Years Old.

Gabbhavīsopi [V 0.0376] hi “paripuṇṇavīso” tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchatīti āha “paṭisandhiggahaṇato paṭṭhāyā”tiādi. Tattha paṭisandhiggahaṇato paṭṭhāyāti yaṃ mātukucchismiṃ paṭhamaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ paṭhamaṃ viññāṇaṃ pātubhūtaṃ, taṃ ādiṃ katvā. Soti yo puggalo ūnavīsativasso upasampādito, so puggalo. Aññaṃ upasampādetīti upajjhāyo vā kammavācācariyo vā hutvā aññaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādeti. Tanti ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ. Sīmaṃ vā sammannatīti navaṃ sīmaṃ bandhati.

Even one who is twenty years old from conception is reckoned as "fully twenty years old," hence it is said, "starting from the moment of rebirth-linking" and so on. Herein, "starting from the moment of rebirth-linking" means taking as the beginning the first mind that arises in the mother’s womb, the first consciousness that appears. "He" refers to the person who has been ordained when under twenty years of age. "Ordains another" means acting as the preceptor or the teacher of the formal act, he ordains another person. "Him" refers to the person under twenty years of age. "Or establishes a boundary" means he establishes a new boundary.

Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning one under twenty years old is concluded.

6. Theyyasatthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning a Caravan of Thieves.

Rājānaṃ vā vañcetvāti rājānaṃ thenetvā rañño santakaṃ kiñci gahetvā, “idāni tassa na dassāmā”ti maggappaṭipannā akatakammā ceva katakammā [M 0.0410] ca corāti vuttaṃ hoti. Esa nayo suṅkaṃ pariharitukāmāti etthāpi.

'Deceiving the king' means having stolen from the king, taking something belonging to the king, and then thinking, 'Now we will not give it to him'—those setting out on the road, whether they have committed the act or not, are called thieves. The same principle applies here to those who wish to evade customs duties.

Kālavisaṅketenāti kālassa visaṅketena, divasavisaṅketenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Maggavisaṅketena, pana aṭavivisaṅketena vā gacchato āpattiyeva.

'By an arrangement of time' means by an arrangement of the day. But if one goes by an arrangement of the road or by an arrangement of the forest, there is an offense.

Theyyasatthasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a caravan of thieves is concluded.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Training Rule on Arrangements.

Mātugāmenāti itthiyā. Ekatoupasampannā, pana sikkhamānā, sāmaṇerī cāti imā tissopi idha saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Imāsaṃ pana tissannaṃ samayo rakkhati. Ayametāsaṃ, mātugāmassa ca visesoti veditabbaṃ.

"With a woman" means with a female. This includes one who is fully ordained, a female probationer, and a female novice—these three are included here. However, for these three, time is a safeguard. It should be understood that this is the distinction between them and a woman.

Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on arrangements is concluded.

8. Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Ariṭṭha.

Taṃtaṃsampattiyā [V 0.0377] (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.417) vibandhanavasena sattasantānassa antare vemajjhe eti āgacchatīti antarāyo, diṭṭhadhammikādianattho, anatikkamanatthena tasmiṃ antarāye niyuttā, antarāyaṃ vā phalaṃ arahanti, antarāyassa vā karaṇasīlāti antarāyikā. Tenāha “saggamokkhānaṃ antarāyaṃ karontīti antarāyikā”ti (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.234). Te kammakilesavipākaupavādapaññattivītikkamavasena pañcavidhāti ettha ca pañcānantariyakammaṃ kammantarāyikaṃ nāma, tathā bhikkhunidūsakakammaṃ. Taṃ pana mokkhasseva antarāyaṃ karoti, na saggassa. Niyatamicchādiṭṭhidhammā kilesantarāyikā nāma. Paṇḍakatiracchānagataubhatobyañjanakānaṃ paṭisandhidhammā vipākantarāyikā nāma. Ariyūpavādā upavādantarāyikā nāma. Te pana yāva ariye na khamāpenti, tāvadeva, na tato paraṃ. Sañcicca āpannā āpattiyo paññattivītikkamantarāyikā nāma. Tāpi yāva bhikkhubhāvaṃ vā paṭijānāti, na vuṭṭhāti vā na deseti vā, tāvadeva, na tato paraṃ.

"Antarāya" (obstacle) is that which comes in between (eti āgacchati) in the continuity of beings, by way of obstructing various attainments (taṃtaṃsampattiyā vibandhanavasena), meaning harm in this life and so on. "Antarāyikā" are those who are engaged in that obstacle in the sense of its being insurmountable, or who deserve the fruit of the obstacle, or who are by nature creators of obstacles. Therefore, it is said, "Those who create obstacles to heaven and liberation are called antarāyikā" (Ma. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1.234). They are fivefold due to transgression by way of actions, defilements, results, reproach, and rules. Here, the five deeds of immediate retribution (pañcānantariyakamma) are called the obstacle of action (kammantarāyika), as is the act of violating a bhikkhunī (bhikkhunidūsakakamma). However, that obstructs only liberation, not heaven. Fixed wrong view is called the obstacle of defilement (kilesantarāyikā). The rebirth-conditions of eunuchs (paṇḍaka), animals, and hermaphrodites (ubhatobyañjanaka) are called obstacles of result (vipākantarāyikā). Reproaching noble ones is called the obstacle of reproach (upavādantarāyikā). But that lasts only until they apologize to the noble ones; not beyond that. Intentionally committed offenses (sañcicca āpannā āpattiyo) are called the obstacle of rule-transgression (paññattivītikkamantarāyikā). These too last only as long as one acknowledges one's bhikkhu-state and does not emerge from them or confess them; not beyond that.

Tatrāyaṃ [M 0.0411] (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.234; pāci. aṭṭha. 417) ariṭṭho bhikkhu bahussuto dhammakathiko sesantarāyike jānāti, vinaye pana akovidattā paṇṇattivītikkamantarāyike na jānāti, tasmā rahogato evaṃ cintesi “ime āgārikā pañca kāmaguṇe paribhuñjantā sotāpannāpi sakadāgāminopi anāgāminopi honti, bhikkhūpi manāpikāni cakkhuviññeyyāni rūpāni passanti…pe… kāyaviññeyye phoṭṭhabbe phusanti, mudukāni attharaṇapāvuraṇādīni paribhuñjanti, etaṃ sabbaṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā? Itthirūpā…pe… itthiphoṭṭhabbā eva na vaṭṭanti, etepi vaṭṭantī”ti evaṃ rasena rasaṃ saṃsanditvā sacchandarāgaparibhogañca nicchandarāgaparibhogañca ekaṃ katvā thūlavākehi saddhiṃ atisukhumasuttaṃ ghaṭento viya, sāsapena saddhiṃ sineruṃ upasaṃharanto viya ca pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppādetvā “kiṃ bhagavatā mahāsamuddaṃ bandhantena viya mahatā ussāhena paṭhamapārājikaṃ paññattaṃ, natthi ettha doso”ti sabbaññutaññāṇena saddhiṃ paṭivirujjhanto bhabbapuggalānaṃ āsaṃ chindanto jinassa āṇācakke pahāramadāsi. Tenāha “tesū”tiādi.

Here, the monk Ariṭṭha, learned in the Dhamma and a preacher, knew about the other obstacles but was unskilled in the Vinaya and did not know about obstacles due to transgressing the rules. Therefore, secluded, he thought thus: "These householders enjoy the five strands of sensual pleasure and yet are stream-enterers, once-returners, or non-returners. Even monks see pleasing forms cognizable by the eye... feel tactile objects cognizable by the body, use soft bedding and coverings—all this is permissible. Why? Forms of women... tactile contact with women—only these are not permissible? These too should be permissible." Thus, blending one taste with another, he equated enjoyment with desire and enjoyment without desire, like one trying to weave a very fine thread with coarse fibers or bringing Mount Sineru together with a mustard seed. Generating this evil viewpoint, he said, "Why did the Blessed One, with great effort like binding the great ocean, lay down the first pārājika rule? There is no fault in this." Thereby, opposing the knowledge of omniscience, cutting off the hope of capable individuals, he struck a blow against the wheel of the Buddha's command. Therefore, it is said: "Among them..." etc.

Tattha tesūti yathāvuttesu antarāyesu. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmāti ettha aṭṭhikaṅkalaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.417) nāma uraṭṭhi vā piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ vā sīsaṭṭhi vā. Tañhi nimmaṃsattā “kaṅkala”nti vuccati. Vigatamaṃsāya hi aṭṭhisaṅkhalikāya ekaṭṭhimhi vā kaṅkalasaddo niruḷho[V 0.0378], taṃsadisā kāmā appassādaṭṭhenāti attho. Ādisaddena “maṃsapesūpamā kāmā, tiṇukkūpamā kāmā, aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā, supinakūpamā kāmā, yācitakūpamā kāmā, rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā, asisūnūpamā kāmā, sattisūlūpamā kāmā, sappasirūpamā kāmā”ti (ma. ni. 1.234, 236; 2.43-48; pāci. 417; cūḷava. 65) etesaṃ gahaṇaṃ.

Among these, "tesu" refers to the obstacles as previously mentioned. "Desires are like a skeleton"—here, "aṭṭhikaṅkala" (as explained in the Sāratthadīpanī, Pācittiya 3.417) means a rib bone, the spine, or the skull. Because it is devoid of flesh, it is called "kaṅkala." Indeed, the word "kaṅkala" is established for a chain of bones stripped of flesh, or even for a single bone; desires are similar in that they offer little satisfaction—this is the meaning. The word "ādi" includes the following: "Desires are like a lump of flesh, desires are like a grass torch, desires are like a pit of embers, desires are like a dream, desires are like borrowed goods, desires are like tree fruits, desires are like a butcher's knife and block, desires are like a spear and stake, desires are like a snake's head" (Majjhima Nikāya 1.234, 236; 2.43-48; Pācittiya 417; Cūḷavagga 65).

Tattha maṃsapesūpamā kāmā (pāci. aṭṭha. 417) bahusādhāraṇaṭṭhena. Tiṇukkūpamā kāmā anudahanaṭṭhena. Aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā mahābhitāpanaṭṭhena. Supinakūpamā kāmā ittarapaccupaṭṭhānaṭṭhena. Yācitakūpamā kāmā tāvakālikaṭṭhena. Rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā sabbaṅgapaccaṅgapalibhañjanaṭṭhena. Asisūnūpamā adhikuṭṭanaṭṭhena. Sattisūlūpamā vinivijjhanaṭṭhena. Sappasirūpamā sāsaṅkasappaṭibhayaṭṭhena.

Here, 'desires are like a lump of meat' (Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā 417) signifies their shared accessibility. 'Desires are like a grass torch' signifies their consuming nature. 'Desires are like a pit of embers' signifies their great burning. 'Desires are like a dream' signifies their brief appearance. 'Desires are like borrowed goods' signifies their transient nature. 'Desires are like tree fruits' signifies the breaking of every major and minor part. 'Desires are like a sword and chopping block' signify their excessive cutting. 'Desires are like spears and stakes' signify their piercing through. 'Desires are like a snake's head' signify their apprehensive danger and fearfulness.

Tathevāti [M 0.0412] “mā āyasmā”tiādīhi. Itaresanti so saṅghamajjhaṃ ākaḍḍhitvā yehi “mā āyasmā”tiādinā vutto, tattha tehi aññesaṃ sutānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. Ñatticatutthena kammenāti “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, itthannāmassa bhikkhuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppanna”ntiādinā (pāci. 420) padabhājaniyaṃ vuttena ñatticatutthena kammena.

Similarly, with phrases like 'Venerable sir, do not...'—here, 'of the others' refers to those other monks who heard when Ariṭṭha was dragged into the midst of the Sangha and addressed by them with phrases like 'Venerable sir, do not...'. 'By a four-part formal act' refers to the four-part formal act as stated in the word analysis beginning with 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me; such-and-such an evil viewpoint has arisen in the bhikkhu named so-and-so...' (Pācittiya 420).

Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Ariṭṭha is concluded.

9. Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Training Rule on Association with One Who Has Been Suspended.

Akatānudhammenāti ukkhipitvā anosāritena. Tenāha “anudhammo vuccatī”tiādi. Ettha anudhammoti osāraṇā vuccatīti sambandho. Ukkhepanīyakammassānurūpo, pacchā kattabbo vā dhammoti anudhammo. Anulomavattaṃ disvāti “na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo”tiādikaṃ (cūḷava. 70) aṭṭhārasavidhaṃ vattaṃ disvā, etesu aṭṭhārasasu anulomavattesu vattantaṃ disvāti adhippāyo. Āmisasambhogaṃ vā dhammasambhogaṃ vāti ettha yaṃ kiñci āmisassa dānaṃ, paṭiggahaṇañca āmisasambhogo. Dhammassa uddisanaṃ, uddisāpanañca dhammasambhogo. Saṃvaseyyāti “uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā saṅghakammaṃ vā”ti (pāci. 425) evaṃ padabhājaniyaṃ vuttaṃ tividhaṃ saṃvāsaṃ kareyya. Yasmā panettha uposathapavāraṇāpi saṅghehiyeva kātabbattā saṅghakammāniyeva honti, tasmā “uposathādikaṃ saṅghakammaṃ kareyyā”ti vuttaṃ. Payoge payogeti dāne dāne, gahaṇe gahaṇe cāti attho.

'Akatānudhammena' means by one who has been suspended and not reinstated. Thus it is said, 'anudhammo is called,' and so forth. Here, 'anudhammo' refers to reinstatement—this is the connection. It is a procedure befitting the act of suspension, or a rule to be followed afterward—this is 'anudhammo.' 'Seeing the proper conduct' means seeing the eighteenfold conduct, such as 'one should not give ordination, one should not give dependence,' and so forth (Cūḷavagga 70). The meaning is that one sees him behaving in accordance with these eighteen proper practices. Here, 'sharing material gains or Dhamma gains' refers to any giving of material goods and the receiving of them—this is 'sharing material gains.' Teaching the Dhamma and having it taught—this is 'sharing Dhamma gains.' 'Should live together' means performing the threefold communal practices, such as 'the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, or Saṅgha acts' (Pācittiya 425), as stated in the word-by-word analysis. Since here the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā must also be performed by the Saṅgha, they are indeed Saṅgha acts; therefore, it is said, 'one should perform Saṅgha acts like the Uposatha, and so forth.' 'At every opportunity' means at every act of giving, at every act of receiving—this is the meaning.

Paṇṇattiṃ [V 0.0379] ajānantena arahatāpi kiriyābyākatacittena āpajjitabbattā “ticitta”nti vuttaṃ.

Because even an arahant, not knowing the designation, with a functional, indeterminate mind, can incur an offense, it is called 'three-mind'.

Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on association with one who has been suspended is concluded.

10. Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Training Rule on the Thorn.

Pireti (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.428) nipātapadaṃ sambodhane vattamānaṃ parasaddena samānatthaṃ vadantīti āha “para amāmakā”ti, amhākaṃ anajjhattikabhūtāti attho. Pireti [M 0.0413] vā “parato”ti iminā samānatthaṃ nipātapadaṃ, tasmā cara pireti parato gaccha, mā idha tiṭṭhāti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

'Pireti' (Sāratthadīpanī, Pācittiya 3.428) is an indeclinable particle used in the vocative sense, expressing the same meaning as the word 'para,' hence it is said, 'para amāmakā' (others, not ours), meaning those who are not internal to us. Alternatively, 'pireti' is an indeclinable particle with the same meaning as 'parato' (elsewhere); therefore, 'cara pireti' means 'go elsewhere, do not stay here'—this meaning should be understood in this context.

Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on the Thorn is concluded.

Sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The Seventh Chapter: On Living Beings.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Chapter on Companions in the Dhamma.

1. Sahadhammikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Companions in the Dhamma.

Sahadhammikaṃ vuccamānoti sahadhammikena vuccamāno. Karaṇatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. “Pañcahi sahadhammikehi sikkhitabbattā, tesaṃ vā santakattā ‘sahadhammika’nti laddhanāmena buddhapaññattena sikkhāpadena vuccamānoti attho”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā; pārā. aṭṭha. 2.425-426) dubbacasikkhāpade vuttattā “sahadhammikaṃ vuccamānoti imassattho dubbacasikkhāpade vutto”ti vuttaṃ. Anādariyabhayāti anādarakaraṇe bhayā, tattha pācittiyabhayāti attho. Lesena evaṃ vadantassāti ujukaṃ “na sikkhissāmī”ti avatvā “yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhu”ntiādinā lesena vadantassa.

'Sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno' means being addressed by a companion in the Dhamma. This is an instrumental usage. The meaning is that one is addressed by the training rule established by the Buddha, which has acquired the name 'sahadhammika' because one must train with five companions in the Dhamma, or because it belongs to them, as stated in the Dubbacasikkhāpada (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Dubbacasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā; Pārājika Aṭṭhakathā 2.425-426); hence it is said, 'The meaning of "sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno" is stated in the Dubbacasikkhāpada.' 'Anādariyabhayā' means because of the fear in showing disrespect; the meaning here is the fear of a pācittiya offense. 'Of one who speaks thus evasively' means of one who, without saying directly, 'I will not train,' speaks evasively with phrases like 'Until I have asked another monk...'

Sahadhammikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on companions in the Dhamma is concluded.

2. Vilekhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Disparaging.

Khuddakehi [V 0.0380] ca anukhuddakehi cāti saṅghādisesādīhi khuddakehi ceva thullaccayādīhi anukhuddakehi ca. Ṭhapetvā hi cattāri pārājikāni avasesāni sabbāni sikkhāpadāni pariyāyena khuddakāni ceva honti anukhuddakāni ca. Vuttañhetaṃ pañcasatikakkhandhake (cūḷava. 441) –

'With minor and lesser minor' refers to minor rules such as the Saṅghādisesa offenses and lesser minor rules such as the Thullaccaya offenses. Indeed, apart from the four Pārājika offenses, all the remaining training rules are, in a sense, both minor and lesser minor. This is stated in the Chapter on the Five Hundred (Cūḷavagga 441):

“Katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānīti? Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – ‘cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – ‘cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti. Ekacce [M 0.0414] therā evamāhaṃsu – ‘cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā dve aniyate ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā dve aniyate ṭhapetvā tiṃsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – ‘cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā dve aniyate ṭhapetvā tiṃsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā dvenavutipācittiye ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu ‘cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā dve aniyate ṭhapetvā tiṃsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā dvenavutipācittiye ṭhapetvā cattāro pāṭidesanīye ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’”ti.

'But, venerable sirs, what are the minor and lesser training rules?' Some elders said: 'Except for the four Pārājikas, the remaining training rules are minor and lesser.' Some elders said: 'Except for the four Pārājikas and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the remaining training rules are minor and lesser.' Some elders said: 'Except for the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, and the two Aniyatas, the remaining training rules are minor and lesser.' Some elders said: 'Except for the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the two Aniyatas, and the thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiyas, the remaining training rules are minor and lesser.' Some elders said: 'Except for the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the two Aniyatas, the thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiyas, and the ninety-two Pācittiyas, the remaining training rules are minor and lesser.' Some elders said: 'Except for the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the two Aniyatas, the thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiyas, the ninety-two Pācittiyas, and the four Pāṭidesanīyas, the remaining training rules are minor and lesser.'

Yaṃ pana nāgasenattherena milindaraññā puṭṭhena vuttaṃ “dukkaṭaṃ, mahārāja, khuddakaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ, dubbhāsitaṃ anukhuddaka”nti (mi. pa. 4.2.1), tattha antimakoṭṭhāsameva gahetvā vuttaṃ. Taṃ vādapathopacchedanatthanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

However, what the Elder Nāgasena said when questioned by King Milinda—'O great king, a Dukkaṭa is a minor training rule, and wrong speech is a lesser minor one' (Milindapañha 4.2.1)—was said taking only the last category. This should be understood as intended to cut off the path of debate.

Saṃvattanamariyādaparicchedavacananti saṃvattanassa mariyādā avadhi saṃvattanamariyādā, tāya niyamavasena yo paricchedo, tassa vacanaṃ saṃvattanamariyādaparicchedavacanaṃ. Idāni taṃ mariyādaṃ vivaritvā dassetuṃ “idaṃ vuttaṃ hotī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha uddisantīti ācariyā attano ruciyā uddisanti. Uddisāpentīti ācariyaṃ yācitvā antevāsikā uddisāpenti. Sajjhāyantīti [V 0.0381] dhārenti. Kukkuccavippaṭisāroti kukkuccasaṅkhāto vippaṭisāro. Vihesāvicikicchāmanovilekhāti vihesāvicikicchāsaṅkhātā manovilekhā. Garahaṇeti nindane.

'Saṃvattanamariyādaparicchedavacana' means the boundary of what it leads to (saṃvattana) is the limit (mariyādā); the expression (vacana) of the definition (pariccheda) determined by that limit is 'saṃvattanamariyādaparicchedavacana.' Now, to explain that limit further, it is said, 'This is what is meant,' and so forth. Here, 'uddisanti' means the teachers recite according to their own preference. 'Uddisāpenti' means the disciples, having requested the teacher, have it recited. 'Sajjhāyanti' means they memorize. 'Kukkuccavippaṭisāro' refers to remorse consisting of scruples. 'Vihesāvicikicchāmanovilekhā' means mental disturbance consisting of vexation and doubt. 'Garahaṇeti' means in reproach.

Anupasampannassa vivaṇṇaneti anupasampannassa santike nindato tassa tasmiṃ vimatiṃ uppādetuṃ vinayavivaṇṇane.

'Disparaging to one who is not fully ordained' means, in the context of disparaging the Vinaya, to criticize it in the presence of an unordained person in order to cause doubt about the Vinaya to arise in him.

Vilekhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Disparaging is concluded.

3. Mohanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Training Rule on Feigning Ignorance.

Tasmiṃ [M 0.0415] anācāreti tasmiṃ anācāre āciṇṇe. Mokkho natthīti tassā āpattiyā mokkho natthi. Tassa teti tassa tava. Alābhāti ye aññesaṃ pātimokkhe uddissamāne sādhukaṃ aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasikaraṇassa ānisaṃsasaññitā diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikā ca lābhā icchitabbā, te sabbe tuyhaṃ alābhā eva honti. Dulladdhanti puññavisesena laddhampi manussattaṃ dulladdhaṃ. Sādhukanti suṭṭhu. Aṭṭhiṃ katvāti atthikabhāvaṃ katvā, atthiko hutvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Ñattidutiyena kammenāti “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”tiādinā (pāci. 446) padabhājaniyaṃ vuttena mohāropanakena ñattidutiyena kammena.

He does not behave properly in that: when improper behavior is habitually practiced. There is no release: there is no release from that offense. For him, for you: for him, that is, for you. A loss: all those benefits, both in this life and for the future, which are to be desired from carefully and attentively listening to the recitation of the Pātimokkha for others—all those are indeed a loss for you. Hard to obtain: even human existence, obtained through special merit, is hard to obtain. Properly: well. Regarding it as important: having made it a matter of importance; that is to say, having become desirous. By a motion and one announcement: by the motion-and-one-announcement procedure that imputes delusion, as stated in the word analysis beginning with, “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me,” etc. (Pāci. 446).

Adhammakammeti ettha mohāropanakammaṃ adhippetaṃ.

Here, by unrighteous procedure is meant the procedure of imputing delusion.

Mohanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on delusion is concluded.

4. Pahārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Training Rule on Assault

Pahāraṃ dadeyyāti antamaso uppalapattaṃ upādāya kāyakāyappaṭibaddhanissaggiyānaṃ aññatarena pahāraṃ dadeyya. Evaṃ pana pahāre dinne hattho vā bhijjatu, pādo vā sīsaṃ vā, maratu vā, pācittiyameva. Tenāha “paharitukāmatāyā”tiādi.

He would strike: he would strike even with a lotus leaf, or with one of the things to be forfeited that are connected from body to body. But if, when such a blow is given, a hand, a foot, or the head is broken, or if he dies, it is only a Pācittiya offense. Therefore it is said, “with the intention to strike,” and so on.

Anupasampanneti gahaṭṭhe vā pabbajite vā itthiyā vā purise vā antamaso tiracchānagatepi. Sace pana rattacitto itthiṃ paharati, saṅghādiseso. Kenaci viheṭhiyamānassāti manussena [V 0.0382] vā tiracchānagatena vā viheṭhiyamānassa. Mokkhādhippāyassāti tato attano mokkhaṃ patthayamānassa. Sacepi antarāmagge (pāci. aṭṭha. 453) coraṃ vā paccatthikaṃ vā viheṭhetukāmaṃ disvā “upāsaka, ettheva tiṭṭha, mā āgamitthā”ti vatvā vacanaṃ anādiyitvā āgacchantaṃ “gaccha re”ti muggarena vā satthakena vā paharitvā yāti, so ce tena pahārena marati, anāpattiyeva. Vāḷamigesupi eseva nayo.

Unordained means a householder or a renunciant, whether a woman or a man, or even an animal. If, however, one strikes a woman out of lust, it is a Saṅghādisesa offense. Being harassed by anyone means being harassed by a human being or an animal. With the intention of freeing oneself means desiring one’s own release from that situation. Even if, while on the road, one sees a thief or an adversary intending to harass one and says, “Lay follower, stay right there, do not come any closer,” but disregarding the warning, they come forward, and one strikes them with a club or a weapon, saying, “Go away!”—if they die from that blow, there is no offense. The same principle applies to wild animals.

Pahārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on striking is concluded.

5. Talasattikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Training Rule on Raising the Hand

Talasattikanti [M 0.0416] talameva talasattikaṃ. “Pothanasamatthaṭṭhena sattika”nti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 456) eke. Uccāreyyāti ukkhipeyya. Napaharitukāmatāya dinnattā dukkaṭanti ettha paharitukāmatāya paharite purimasikkhāpadena pācittiyaṃ. Uccāretukāmatāya kevalaṃ uggiraṇamatte kate iminā pācittiyaṃ. Iminā pana virajjhitvā pahāro dinno, tasmā dukkaṭaṃ. Ettha pana “tiracchānagatādīnaṃ asucikaraṇādīni disvā kujjhitvāpi uggirantassa mokkhādhippāyoyevā”ti (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.471) vadanti.

Talasattika: the palm itself is the talasattika. Some say, “A sattika is that which is capable of striking.” Should raise means should lift up. Here, if one strikes with the intention to strike, it is a Pācittiya offense according to the previous training rule. If, with the intention of lifting the hand, one merely lifts it up, it is a Pācittiya offense according to this rule. But if, having transgressed this rule, a blow is given, it is therefore a dukkaṭa offense. Here, some say, “Even if one lifts up the hand out of anger upon seeing an animal or the like creating filth, the intention is only to escape the situation.”

Talasattikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on raising the hand is concluded.

6. Amūlakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Training Rule on Baseless Allegations

Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ uttānameva.

The sixth training rule is self-explanatory.

Amūlakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on baseless allegations is concluded.

7. Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Training Rule on Deliberately Causing Annoyance

Kukkuccaṃ uppādentassāti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 468) saṃsayaṃ janentassa. Paro kukkuccaṃ uppādetu vā, mā vā, taṃ appamāṇaṃ. Maññeti takkayāmi. Ādisaddena “vikāle maññe [V 0.0383] tayā bhuttaṃ, majjaṃ maññe tayā pītaṃ, mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho maññe tayā nisinna”ntiādīnaṃ (pāci. 466) gahaṇaṃ. Anupasampanneti sāmaṇere.

One arousing anxiety means one who generates doubt. Whether or not the other person feels anxiety is not the deciding factor. I think means I conjecture. By the word “etc.” is included such instances as, “I think you ate at an unseasonable time,” “I think you drank intoxicants,” “I think you sat in secret with a woman,” and so on. Unordained refers to a novice.

Sañciccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on deliberately causing annoyance is concluded.

8. Upassutisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule on Eavesdropping

Suyyatīti suti, saddo, sutiyā samīpaṃ upassutīti āha “sutisamīpa”nti, saddasamīpanti attho. Yattha pana ṭhitena sakkā hoti saddaṃ sotuṃ[M 0.0417], tattha tiṭṭhanto saddasamīpe tiṭṭhati nāmāti āha “yattha ṭhatvā”tiādi. Atha vā upecca suyyati etthāti upassuti, ṭhānaṃ, yaṃ ṭhānaṃ upagatena sakkā hoti kathentānaṃ saddaṃ sotuṃ, tatthāti evampettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Turitagamanepīti pacchato gacchantassa purato gacchantānaṃ saddasavanatthaṃ sīghagamanepi. Ohīyamānepīti purato gacchantassa pacchato gacchantānaṃ vacanasavanatthaṃ ohīyamānepi.

Hearing (`suti`) is sound, from the verb ‘it is heard’ (`suyyati`). Near (`upa`) hearing (`suti`) is eavesdropping (`upassuti`); hence it is said to be ‘near hearing,’ meaning near the sound. Where, standing, one can hear a sound, there one stands near the sound; hence it is said, “where standing,” etc. Alternatively, `upassuti` is a place where one approaches (`upecca`) and hears (`suyyati`). The meaning should be understood here thus: it is a place where one who has approached can hear the sound of those speaking. Even when moving quickly means even in swift movement, for the sake of hearing the sound of those going ahead while one is going behind. Even when falling behind means even when lagging behind, for the sake of hearing the speech of those going behind while one is going ahead.

Vūpasamissāmīti upasamaṃ gamissāmi, kalahaṃ na karissāmi. Attānaṃ parimocessāmīti mama akārakabhāvaṃ kathetvā attānaṃ parimocessāmi. Siyā kiriyanti kadāci sotukāmatāya gamanavasena samuṭṭhānato siyā kiriyaṃ. Siyā akiriyanti kadāci ṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ āgantvā mantayamānānaṃ ajānāpanavasena samuṭṭhānato siyā akiriyaṃ.

I shall calm down means I will attain peace; I will not quarrel. I shall free myself means by declaring my innocence, I shall free myself. There might be action means sometimes action arises from the desire to hear, by way of going. There might be inaction means sometimes inaction arises when, without informing them of one's presence, one listens to those who have come and are conversing in the place where one is standing.

Upassutisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on eavesdropping is concluded.

9. Kammappaṭibāhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Training Rule on Obstructing Procedures

Dhammikānanti dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena katattā dhammo etesu atthīti dhammikāni, tesaṃ dhammikānaṃ. Kammānanti catunnaṃ saṅghakammānaṃ. Tenāha “dhammenā”tiādi. Tattha dhammenāti bhūtena vatthunā. Vinayenāti codanāya ceva sāraṇāya ca. Satthusāsanenāti ñattisampadāya ceva anussavanāsampadāya ca. Samaggassa saṅghassāti sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvā chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā kattabbattā kāyena ceva cittena ca ekībhūtassa saṅghassa. Taṃ taṃ vatthunti avaṇṇabhaṇanādiṃ taṃ taṃ vatthu.

Legal: because they are done in accordance with the Dhamma, the Discipline, and the Teacher’s instruction, there is Dhamma in them, hence they are legal; of those legal procedures. Procedures means the four kinds of Sangha procedures. Therefore it is said, “by the Dhamma,” and so forth. Herein, “by the Dhamma” means by a true basis. “By the Discipline” means by accusation and by reminding. “By the Teacher’s instruction” means by the completeness of the motion and by the completeness of the proclamation. Of the united Sangha means of the Sangha united in body and mind, because a procedure is to be done after having purified the Sangha within the boundary and having brought the consent of those worthy of consent. That particular matter means that particular matter such as speaking dispraise, and so forth.

Osārenti [V 0.0384] saṅghamajjhaṃ etenāti osāraṇaṃ. Nissārenti saṅghamhā etenāti nissāraṇaṃ. Bhaṇḍukammanti muṇḍakaraṇaṃ, kesacchedanāpucchananti attho. Kammameva lakkhaṇaṃ kammalakkhaṇaṃ. Osāraṇādayo viya kammañca hutvā aññañca nāmaṃ na labhati, kammameva hutvā lakkhīyatīti kammalakkhaṇanti attho. “Osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇa”nti (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) cettha padasiliṭṭhatāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ pana nissāraṇā hoti, pacchā osāraṇāti āha [M 0.0418] “tattha kaṇṭakasāmaṇerassā”tiādi. Kaṇṭakasāmaṇerassa nāsanā viya nissāraṇāti yathā kaṇṭakasāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammanāsanā nissāraṇā, tathā buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā avaṇṇaṃ bhaṇato, akappiyaṃ “kappiya”nti dīpayato, micchādiṭṭhikassa antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgatassa aññassāpi sāmaṇerassa –

They lead him into the midst of the Sangha by this means, hence it is `osāraṇa` (reinstatement). They lead him out from the Sangha by this means, hence it is `nissāraṇa` (expulsion). `Bhaṇḍukamma` means shaving the head; the meaning is asking about cutting the hair. The procedure itself is the characteristic; this is `kammalakkhaṇa` (the mark of the procedure). Just as `osāraṇa` and the others, after being a procedure, do not acquire another name, but are recognized simply as a procedure—this is the meaning of `kammalakkhaṇa`. `Osāraṇa` and `nissāraṇa`: here, this is said for the sake of verbal elegance. However, first there is `nissāraṇa`, and afterwards `osāraṇa`—as stated in “concerning the thorny novice,” and so forth. Just as the expulsion of the thorny novice is `nissāraṇa`—that is, just as the thorny novice’s punishment and expulsion is `nissāraṇa`—similarly, for any other novice who speaks dispraise of the Buddha, Dhamma, or Sangha, or declares the improper to be proper, or is endowed with extremist views—

“Saṅghaṃ, bhante, pucchāmi ‘ayaṃ itthannāmo sāmaṇero buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā avaṇṇavādī micchādiṭṭhiko, yaṃ aññe sāmaṇerā labhanti dirattatirattaṃ bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ sahaseyyaṃ, tassa alābhāya nissāraṇā ruccati saṅghassā’ti. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ pucchāmi ‘ayaṃ itthannāmo sāmaṇero…pe… ruccati saṅghassā’ti, cara pire vinassā”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) –

“Venerable sir, I ask the Sangha: ‘This so-named novice speaks disparagingly of the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Sangha, and holds wrong views. Does the Sangha approve of his expulsion, so that he may not obtain that which other novices obtain, namely co-residence with the monks for two or three nights?’ A second time… and a third time, venerable sir, I ask the Sangha: ‘This so-named novice… does the Sangha approve of his expulsion?’ Go, wretch, perish!”

Kattabbanāsanā nissāraṇāti attho. Tādisaṃyeva sammāvattantaṃ disvā pavesanā osāraṇāti tādisaṃyeva aparena samayena “ahaṃ, bhante, bālatāya aññāṇatāya alakkhikatāya evaṃ akāsiṃ, svāhaṃ saṅghaṃ khamāpemī”ti khamāpentaṃ disvā yāvatatiyaṃ yācāpetvā –

The meaning is: expulsion is a banishment to be carried out. Seeing just such a one behaving rightly, his readmission is called reinstatement. At a later time, seeing one who asks for forgiveness, saying, ‘Venerable sir, through foolishness, ignorance, and thoughtlessness I acted thus; I ask the Sangha for forgiveness,’ and having had him ask up to a third time—

“Saṅghaṃ, bhante, pucchāmi ‘ayaṃ itthannāmo sāmaṇero buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā avaṇṇavādī micchādiṭṭhiko, yaṃ aññe sāmaṇerā labhanti bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ dirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ, tassa alābhāya nissārito, svāyaṃ idāni sorato nivātavutti lajjidhammaṃ okkanto hirottappe patiṭṭhito katadaṇḍakammo accayaṃ deseti, imassa sāmaṇerassa yathā pure kāyasambhogasāmaggidānaṃ ruccati saṅghassā’ti. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ pucchāmi…pe… ruccati saṅghassā”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) –

“Venerable sir, I ask the Sangha: ‘This so-named novice, who spoke disparagingly of the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Sangha, and held wrong views, was expelled so that he would not obtain that which other novices obtain, namely co-residence with the monks for two or three nights. Now he is compliant, humble, has undertaken the state of modesty, and is established in conscience and fear of wrongdoing. Having undergone the penalty, he confesses his transgression. Does the Sangha approve of granting this novice communion in bodily association and harmony as before?’ A second time… and a third time, venerable sir, I ask the Sangha… does the Sangha approve?”

Pavesanā osāraṇāti attho.

The meaning is: admission is reinstatement.

Kesacchedanāpucchananti [V 0.0385] sīmāpariyāpanne bhikkhū sannipātāpetvā pabbajjāpekkhaṃ tattha netvā “saṅghaṃ, bhante, imassa dārakassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmī”ti [M 0.0419] tikkhattuṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā sakiṃ vā vacanaṃ. Idha ca “imassa dārakassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmā”tipi “imassa samaṇakaraṇaṃ āpucchāmā”tipi “imassa pabbājanaṃ āpucchāmā”tipi “ayaṃ samaṇo hotukāmo”tipi “ayaṃ pabbajitukāmo”tipi vattuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

‘Asking about cutting the hair’ means, having had the monks who are within the boundary assemble, and having brought the candidate for the going-forth there, the statement made three times, twice, or once: ‘Venerable sirs, I ask the Sangha about the tonsure for this boy.’ And here it is also permissible to say, ‘We ask about the tonsure for this boy,’ or ‘We ask about making him a recluse,’ or ‘We ask about his going-forth,’ or ‘This one wishes to become a recluse,’ or ‘This one wishes to go forth.’

Mukharassāti mukhena kharassa. Yaṃ avandiyakammaṃ anuññātanti sambandho. Ūruṃ vivaritvā dassanādivatthūsūti –

‘Of one who is sharp-tongued’ means of one who is harsh with his mouth. The connection is with ‘what act of disrespect was permitted?’ In cases such as exposing the thigh and so on—

“Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo kaddamodakena osiñcanti ‘appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyu’nti, kāyaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti, ūruṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti, aṅgajātaṃ vivaritvā bhikkhunīnaṃ dassenti, bhikkhuniyo obhāsenti, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ sampayojenti ‘appeva nāma amhesu sārajjeyyu’”nti (cūḷava. 411) –

“Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sprinkled the nuns with muddy water, thinking, ‘Perhaps they might become infatuated with us.’ They exposed their bodies to the nuns, they exposed their thighs to the nuns, they exposed their genitals to the nuns, they made suggestive remarks to the nuns, and they made advances towards the nuns, thinking, ‘Perhaps they might become infatuated with us.’”

Imesu vatthūsu.

In these matters.

Acchinnacīvarakādīnanti acchinnacīvarajiṇṇacīvaranaṭṭhacīvaragilānabahussutasaṅghabhāranittharakādīnaṃ. Cīvarādīnīti cīvarabhesajjasenāsanādīni. Paribhuñjitabbānīti paribhuñjitabbāni mūlatacapattaaṅkurapupphaphalādīni. Apanetabbānipi vatthūnīti āvāsakaraṇādiatthaṃ haritabbānipi chāyūpagaphalūpagarukkhādīni. Tathārūpaṃ vā dhammikaṃ katikaṃ karontehīti cīvarapiṇḍapātatthāya dinnato āvāsajagganādikaṃ tādisaṃ vā aññampi dhammikaṃ katikaṃ karontehi.

‘Of those with uncut robes, and so forth’ means of those with uncut robes, worn-out robes, or lost robes, the sick, the very learned, those who discharge the Sangha’s burdens, and so forth. ‘Robes, and so forth’ means robes, medicines, lodgings, and so forth. ‘Things that may be used’ means roots, bark, leaves, shoots, flowers, fruits, and so forth, that may be used. ‘Things that may also be removed’ means shade-providing trees, fruit-bearing trees, and other such trees that may be taken for the purpose of constructing dwellings, and so forth. ‘By those making a similar lawful agreement’ means by those making a lawful agreement concerning the maintenance of dwellings and so on from what was given for the sake of robes and alms-food, or any other such lawful agreement.

Neva suttaṃ āgacchatīti na mātikā āgacchati. No suttavibhaṅgoti vinayopi na paguṇo. Byañjanacchāyāya atthaṃ paṭibāhatīti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 233) byañjanamattameva gahetvā atthaṃ paṭisedheti. Jātarūparajatakhettavatthuppaṭiggahaṇādīsu vinayadharehi bhikkhūhi āpattiyā kāriyamāne disvā “kiṃ ime āpattiyā kāretha, nanu ‘jātarūparajatappaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hotī’ti (dī. ni. 1.10, 194) evaṃ sutte paṭiviratimattameva vuttaṃ, natthi ettha āpattī”ti vadati. Aparo dhammakathiko suttassa āgatattā olambetvā nivāsentānaṃ āpattiyā [V 0.0386] āropiyamānāya “kiṃ imesaṃ āpattiṃ āropetha, nanu ‘parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā’ti (pāci. 576) evaṃ [M 0.0420] sikkhākaraṇamattameva vuttaṃ, natthi ettha āpattī”ti vadati. Ubbāhika vinicchayeti samathakkhandhake vuttaubbāhikavinicchaye “sīlavā hotī”tiādikāya hi dasaṅgasampattiyā samannāgate dve tayo bhikkhū uccinitvā vinicchayo ubbāhikavinicchayoti daṭṭhabbo.

‘The Sutta does not come to him’ means the matrix does not come to him. ‘And no Suttavibhaṅga’ means the Vinaya is also not mastered. ‘He obstructs the meaning by the shadow of the letter’ means that, grasping only the letter, he rejects the meaning. For instance, when monks who are experts in the Vinaya are being dealt with for an offense regarding the acceptance of gold and silver, fields and land, etc., seeing this, one says: ‘Why are you dealing with them for an offense? Is it not said in the Sutta, “He abstains from accepting gold and silver”? Thus, only mere abstention is mentioned in the Sutta; there is no offense here.’ Another Dhamma teacher, with regard to what is found in a Sutta, when an offense is being charged against those who wear their lower robe hanging down, says: ‘Why do you charge them with an offense? Is it not said, “The training rule, ‘I will wear the lower robe all around,’ is to be undertaken”? Thus, only the undertaking of a training rule is mentioned; there is no offense here.’ ‘In the Ubbāhika procedure’: in the Ubbāhika procedure mentioned in the Samathakkhandhaka, the Ubbāhika procedure should be understood as a decision made after selecting two or three monks endowed with the ten accomplishments, beginning with ‘He is virtuous.’

Pavāraṇappaccukkaḍḍhanāti pavāraṇāya ukkassanā, uddhaṃ kaḍḍhanāti attho. Tiṇavatthārakasamathe sabbasaṅgāhikañatti cāti “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ…pe… ṭhapetvā gihippaṭisaṃyutta”nti (cūḷava. 212-213) evaṃ tiṇavatthārakasamathe katā sabbapaṭhamā sabbasaṅgāhikañatti ca.

‘Withdrawal of the Pavāraṇā’ means the postponement of the Pavāraṇā; the meaning is ‘drawing it up.’ And ‘the all-inclusive motion in the settlement by covering with grass’ is the very first, all-inclusive motion made in the settlement by covering with grass, thus: ‘Venerable sirs, let the Sangha hear me. As we were living quarrelsomely… excluding what is connected with householders…’

Alābhāya parisakkanādikehīti catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ alābhatthāya payogakaraṇādikehi. Ādisaddena “anatthāya parisakkanaṃ, anāvāsāya parisakkanaṃ, akkosanaparibhāsanaṃ, bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedanaṃ, buddhassa avaṇṇabhaṇanaṃ, dhammassa avaṇṇabhaṇanaṃ, saṅghassa avaṇṇabhaṇana”nti (cūḷava. 265) avasesaṃ sattaṅgaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgatassāti aṭṭhahi ceva aṅgehi ekekenapi aṅgena ca samannāgatassa. Asambhogakaraṇatthanti tena dinnassa deyyadhammassa appaṭiggahaṇatthaṃ. Pattanikkujjanavasenāti kammavācāya pattanikkujjanavasena, na adhomukhaṭṭhapanavasena. Pattukkujjanavasenāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Tassevāti yo pattanikkujjanavasena katanissāraṇo, tasseva upāsakassa. Sammāvattantassāti yena samannāgatassa pattukkujjanaṃ, tena samannāgatassa. Sāti yathāvuttā nissāraṇā, osāraṇā ca.

‘By striving for non-gain, and so forth’ means by making an effort for the non-acquisition of the four requisites, and so forth. By the word ‘and so forth,’ the remaining seven factors are included: ‘striving for what is not beneficial, striving for non-residence, reviling and disparaging, dividing monks from monks, speaking in dispraise of the Buddha, speaking in dispraise of the Dhamma, speaking in dispraise of the Sangha.’ ‘Of one endowed with the eight factors’ means of one endowed with all eight factors, or with any single one of them. ‘For the purpose of non-communion’ means for the purpose of not accepting a gift given by him. ‘By way of overturning the bowl’ means by overturning the bowl through a formal act of the Sangha, not by merely placing it face down. ‘By way of turning the bowl upright’: here the same method applies. ‘Of that very one’ means of that very lay follower for whom the expulsion was carried out by way of overturning the bowl. ‘Of one who is behaving rightly’: of one endowed with that for which the bowl is turned upright. ‘That’ refers to the aforementioned expulsion and reinstatement.

Sūciyādiappamattakaṃ taṃtadatthikānaṃ vissajjeti detīti appamattakavissajjako. Sāṭiyaggāhāpakoti vassikasāṭiyaggāhāpako. Kammaṃ karonte ārāmike pesanatthāya dātabbā sammuti ārāmikapesakasammuti. Esa nayo sāmaṇerapesakasammutīti etthāpi.

An ‘apportioner of trifles’ is one who gives away or distributes a small thing, such as a needle, to those who have need of it. A ‘procurer of cloths’ is a procurer of the rains-bathing cloth. The ‘authorization for sending a monastery attendant’ is the authorization to be given for the purpose of sending a monastery attendant while he is doing work. This same method applies also in the case of the ‘authorization for sending a novice.’

Tajjanīyakammādīnaṃ sattannanti tajjanīyaṃ, niyasaṃ, pabbājanīyaṃ, paṭisāraṇīyaṃ, tividhañca ukkhepanīyanti tajjanīyādīnaṃ sattannaṃ. Aṭṭhayāvatatiyakāti bhikkhūnaṃ vasena cattāro, bhikkhunīnaṃ vasena cattāroti aṭṭha saṅghādisesā.

‘Of the seven beginning with the act of censure’ means the seven beginning with censure: the act of censure, the act of subordination, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, and the three kinds of acts of suspension. ‘The eight that are confessed on the third asking’ are the eight Saṅghādisesa offenses: four for monks and four for nuns.

Ñattikammādivasenāti [M 0.0421] ñattikammañattidutiyakammañatticatutthakammavasena. “Kariyamānaṃ daḷhataraṃ [V 0.0387] hoti, tasmā kātabba”nti ekacce vadanti. Evaṃ pana sati kammasaṅkaro hoti, tasmā na kātabbanti paṭikkhittameva. Sace pana akkharaparihīnaṃ vā padaparihīnaṃ vā duruttapadaṃ vā hoti, tassa sodhanatthaṃ punappunaṃ vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Idaṃ akuppakammassa daḷhīkammaṃ hoti, kuppakamme kammaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhati. Sakalakkhaṇenevāti ñattiñca catasso ca kammavācāyo sāvetvāva. Na sesakammavasenāti apalokanakammādinā avasesakammavasena na kātabbaṃ.

By way of an act preceded by a motion, etc., means by way of an act preceded by a motion, an act with a motion and one recitation, and an act with a motion and three recitations. Some say, 'What is being done becomes firmer; therefore, it should be done.' But if that were the case, there would be a confusion of acts; therefore, it should not be done—this has been rejected. However, if there is a deficiency in letters, a deficiency in words, or a poorly uttered word, it is permissible to repeat it again and again for the purpose of correction. This serves as a strengthening of an unshakeable act; in a shakeable act, it stands as a valid act. 'With all its characteristics' means having announced both the motion and the four recitations of the act. 'Not by way of the remaining acts' means it should not be done by way of the remaining acts, such as an act of seeking consent.

Kammappaṭibāhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on obstructing a formal act is concluded.

10. Chandaṃadatvāgamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Training Rule on Going Away without Giving Consent.

Ārocitaṃ vatthu avinicchitanti ārocitavatthu āpattikabhāvena na vinicchitaṃ. Ettha ca codakena ca cuditakena ca attano kathā kathitā, anuvijjako sammato, ettāvatā vatthumeva ārocitaṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkameyyāti “kathaṃ idaṃ kammaṃ kuppaṃ assa, vaggaṃ assa, na kareyyā”ti (pāci. 481) iminā adhippāyena chandaṃ adatvā nisinnāsanato uṭṭhāya gaccheyya. Tenāha “yo bhikkhū”tiādi. Kiriyākiriyanti ettha gamanaṃ kiriyaṃ, chandassa adānaṃ akiriyaṃ.

'A matter reported but not decided' means a reported matter that has not been decided as to whether it is an offense. Here, both the accuser and the accused have stated their cases, and an investigator has been appointed. Up to this point, it should be understood that the matter has only been reported. 'Without giving consent, one might rise from one's seat and depart' means that with the intention, 'How might this formal act be made invalid, be made partisan, not be carried out?' (Pāc. 481), one might, without giving consent, rise from the seat where one is sitting and leave. Therefore, it is said, 'Whatever monk...' and so on. 'Action and inaction': here, going away is the action; the not-giving of consent is the inaction.

Chandaṃadatvāgamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on going away without giving consent is concluded.

11. Dubbalasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. Explanation of the Training Rule on Weakening.

Yathāsanthutanti yathāmittaṃ. Tenāha “yo yo”ti ādi. Tattha mittasandiṭṭhasambhattavasenāti mittasandiṭṭhasambhattānaṃ vasena. Tattha mittā mittāva. Sandiṭṭhā tattha tattha saṅgamma diṭṭhamattā nātidaḷhamittā. Sambhattā suṭṭhu bhattā sinehavanto daḷhamittāti daṭṭhabbā.

'As one is familiar with' means as with a friend. Therefore, it is said, 'Whoever...' and so on. 'By way of friends, acquaintances, and intimates' means by way of friends, acquaintances, and intimates. Therein, friends are simply friends. Acquaintances are those merely seen upon meeting here and there, not very firm friends. Intimates should be understood as those who are well-devoted, affectionate, and firm friends.

Pañca garubhaṇḍānīti rāsivasena pañca garubhaṇḍāni, sarūpavasena panetāni bahūni honti. Tenāha “rāsivasena pañca garubhaṇḍāni vuttānī”ti. Ārāmo [M 0.0422] (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 227) nāma pupphārāmo vā phalārāmo vā. Ārāmavatthu nāma tesaṃyeva ārāmānaṃ atthāya paricchinditvā ṭhapitokāso, tesu vā ārāmesu vinaṭṭhesu tesaṃ porāṇakabhūmibhāgo[V 0.0388]. Vihāro nāma yaṃ kiñci pāsādādisenāsanaṃ. Vihāravatthu nāma tassa patiṭṭhānokāso. Mañco nāma masārako bundikābaddho, kuḷīrapādako, āhaccapādakoti imesaṃ pubbe vuttānaṃ catunnaṃ mañcānaṃ aññataro. Pīṭhaṃ nāma masārakādīnaṃyeva catunnaṃ pīṭhānaṃ aññataraṃ. Bhisi nāma uṇṇabhisiādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ bhisīnaṃ aññatarā. Bibbohanaṃ nāma rukkhatūlalatātūlapoṭakitūlānaṃ aññatarena puṇṇaṃ. Lohakumbhī nāma kāḷalohena vā tambalohena vā yena kenaci lohena katā kumbhī. Lohabhāṇakādīsupi eseva nayo. Ettha pana bhāṇakanti arañjaro vuccati. Vārakoti ghaṭo. Kaṭāhaṃ kaṭāhameva. Vāsiādīsu, valliādīsu ca duviññeyyaṃ nāma natthi. Evaṃ –

'The five heavy articles': in terms of categories, there are five heavy articles, but in terms of individual types, they are numerous. Therefore, it is said, 'Five heavy articles are mentioned by category.' A park (ārāma) is a flower park or a fruit park. A park site (ārāmavatthu) is the space demarcated and set aside for those very parks, or, when those parks are ruined, their former portion of land. A dwelling (vihāra) is any lodging such as a mansion. A dwelling site (vihāravatthu) is the space for its foundation. A bed (mañca) is any one of the four previously mentioned beds: a masāraka bed, a bundikābaddha bed, a kuḷīrapādaka bed, or an āhaccapādaka bed. A bench (pīṭha) is any one of the four benches, such as a masāraka bench. A cushion (bhisi) is any one of the five cushions, such as a woollen cushion. A pillow (bibbohana) is one filled with tree cotton, creeper cotton, or cloth cotton. A metal pot (lohakumbhī) is a pot made of any metal, whether iron or copper. The same principle applies to metal vessels and so on. Here, a vessel (bhāṇaka) is called a large water jar (arañjara). A jar (vāraka) is a water pot (ghaṭa). A pan (kaṭāha) is just a pan. Regarding axes and so on, and creepers and so on, there is nothing difficult to understand. Thus—

Dvisaṅgahāni dve honti, tatiyaṃ catusaṅgahaṃ;

Catutthaṃ navakoṭṭhāsaṃ, pañcamaṃ aṭṭhabhedanaṃ.

There are two twofold collections, the third is a fourfold collection; the fourth has nine parts, the fifth has eight divisions.

Iti pañcahi rāsīhi, pañcanimmalalocano;

Pañcavīsavidhaṃ nātho, garubhaṇḍaṃ pakāsayi. (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 227);

Thus, in five categories, the Lord, the one with the Five Eyes, declared twenty-five kinds of heavy articles.

Vissajjetuṃ vā vibhajituṃ vā na vaṭṭatīti mūlacchejjavasena vissajjetuṃ vā vibhajituṃ vā na vaṭṭanti. Parivattanavasena pana vissajjantassa, vibhajantassa ca anāpatti. Tenāha “thāvarenā”tiādi. Tattha thāvarena thāvaranti ārāmaārāmavatthuvihāravihāravatthunā ārāmaṃ ārāmavatthuṃ vihāraṃ vihāravatthuṃ. Itarenāti athāvarena, pacchimarāsittayenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Akappiyenāti suvaṇṇamayamañcādinā ceva akappiyabhisibibbohanehi ca. Mahagghakappiyenāti dantamayamañcādinā ceva pāvārādinā ca. Itaranti athāvaraṃ. Kappiyaparivattanena parivattetunti yathā akappiyaṃ na hoti, evaṃ parivattetuṃ.

'To give away or to divide is not permissible' means it is not permissible to give away or to divide in a way that constitutes permanent alienation. However, for one who gives away or divides by way of exchange, there is no offense. Therefore, it is said, 'by what is durable,' and so on. Here, 'by a durable thing, a durable thing' means a park for a park, a park site for a park site, a dwelling for a dwelling, and a dwelling site for a dwelling site. 'By the other' means by what is not durable; that is to say, the last three categories. 'By what is unsuitable' means by a golden bed and so on, and by unsuitable cushions and pillows. 'By what is highly valuable and suitable' means by an ivory bed and so on, and by cloaks and so on. 'The other' means what is not durable. 'To exchange with a suitable exchange' means to exchange in such a way that it does not become unsuitable.

Tatrāyaṃ parivattananayo (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 228) – saṅghassa nāḷikerārāmo dūre hoti, kappiyakārakāva bahutaraṃ khādanti, yampi na khādanti, tato [M 0.0423] sakaṭavetanaṃ datvā appameva āharanti. Aññesaṃ pana tassārāmassa avidūre gāmavāsīnaṃ manussānaṃ vihārassa samīpe ārāmo hoti, te saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā sakena ārāmena taṃ ārāmaṃ yācanti, saṅghena “ruccati saṅghassā”ti apaloketvā sampaṭicchitabbo. Sacepi bhikkhūnaṃ rukkhasahassaṃ hoti, manussānaṃ pañcasatāni, “tumhākaṃ ārāmo khuddako”ti na vattabbaṃ. Kiñcāpi ayaṃ khuddako, atha kho itarato bahutaraṃ āyaṃ deti. Sacepi samakameva deti[V 0.0389], evampi icchiticchitakkhaṇe paribhuñjituṃ sakkāti gahetabbameva. Sace pana manussānaṃ bahutarā rukkhā honti, “nanu tumhākaṃ bahutarā rukkhā”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace “atirekaṃ amhākaṃ puññaṃ hotu, saṅghassa demā”ti vadanti, jānāpetvā sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhūnaṃ rukkhā phaladhārino, manussānaṃ rukkhā na tāva phalaṃ gaṇhanti. Kiñcāpi na gaṇhanti, na cirena gaṇhissantīti sampaṭicchitabbameva. Manussānaṃ rukkhā phaladhārino, bhikkhūnaṃ rukkhā na tāva phalaṃ gaṇhanti, “nanu tumhākaṃ rukkhā phaladhārino”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace “gaṇhatha, bhante, amhākaṃ puññaṃ bhavissatī”ti denti, jānāpetvā sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ ārāmena ārāmo parivattetabbo, eteneva nayena ārāmavatthupi vihāropi vihāravatthupi ārāmena parivattetabbaṃ. Ārāmavatthunā ca mahantena vā khuddakena vā ārāmaṃ ārāmavatthuṃ vihāraṃ vihāravatthunti.

Here is the method of exchange (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 321; Vinaya Saṅgaha Aṭṭha. 228): The Sangha’s coconut grove is far away, and the lay attendants consume most of it. Even of what they do not consume, only a small amount is brought back after paying for cart hire. However, other people, village-dwellers, have a grove near the monastery. They approach the Sangha and ask for that grove in exchange for their own. The Sangha, having made an announcement with the words, 'Does it please the Sangha?', should accept it. Even if the monks have a thousand trees and the people have five hundred, it should not be said, 'Your grove is small.' Although it is small, it provides a much greater yield than the other. Even if it provides an equal yield, it should still be accepted, since it can be enjoyed at any desired moment. But if the people have more trees, it should be said, 'Do you not have more trees?' If they say, 'Let the excess be for our merit; we give it to the Sangha,' it is permissible to accept after having made this known. If the monks’ trees are fruit-bearing and the people’s trees do not yet bear fruit, it should still be accepted, for although they do not bear fruit now, they will do so before long. If the people’s trees are fruit-bearing and the monks’ trees do not yet bear fruit, it should be said, 'Are not your trees fruit-bearing?' If they say, 'Take it, venerable sirs, it will be for our merit,' it is permissible to accept after having made this known. In this way, a grove should be exchanged for a grove.
