Tattha yasmiṃ vihāre uppannanti “yasmiṃ vihāre mayhaṃ iminā patto gahito, cīvaraṃ gahita”ntiādinā (pari. aṭṭha. 341) nayena pattacīvarādīnaṃ atthāya vivādādhikaraṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Tasmiṃyeva vā sammatīti tasmiṃ vihāreyeva āvāsikehi sannipatitvā “alaṃ, āvuso”ti atthapaccatthike saññāpetvā pāḷimuttakavinicchayeneva vūpasamentehi sammati. Sace pana taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ nevāsikā vūpasametuṃ na sakkonti, athañño vinayadharo āgantvā “kiṃ, āvuso, imasmiṃ vihāre uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā ṭhitā”ti pucchati, tehi ca tasmiṃ kāraṇe kathite taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ khandhakato ca parivārato ca suttena vinicchinitvā vūpasameti. Evampi etasmiṃyeva sammatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Having thus shown the legal questions, now, to show that this legal question among them is settled by such and such means of settlement, 'tatra' (therein) and so forth is stated. The connection is: 'In whichever monastery it arose, it is settled in that very place.' The same applies to the rest. Here, 'in whichever monastery it arose' refers to a legal question of dispute arising for the sake of bowls, robes, and so forth, according to the method (Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā 341) of saying, 'In this monastery, my bowl was taken, my robe was taken,' and so forth. 'It is settled in that very place' means that it is settled by the resident monks who gather in that very monastery and, having persuaded the parties involved by saying, 'Enough, friends,' resolve it solely by a judgment outside of the Pāḷi. However, if the residents are unable to settle that legal question, then another Vinaya expert arrives and asks, 'Friends, has the Uposatha or Pavāraṇā been suspended in this monastery?' When they explain the reason, he resolves the legal question by judging it according to the Khandhakas, the Parivāra, and the Sutta. Even in this case, it should be understood that it is settled in that very place.

Aññattha vūpasametuṃ gacchantānaṃ antarāmagge vā sammatīti “na mayaṃ etassa vinicchaye tiṭṭhāma, nāyaṃ vinaye kusalo, amukasmiṃ nāma gāme vinayadharā therā vasanti, tattha gantvā vinicchinissāmā”ti gacchantānaṃ antarāmagge vā kāraṇaṃ sallakkhetvā aññamaññaṃ saññāpentehi, aññehi vā te bhikkhū nijjhāpentehi sammati. Na heva kho pana aññamaññasaññattiyā vā sabhāgabhikkhunijjhāpanena vā vūpasantaṃ hoti, apica kho paṭipathaṃ āgacchanto eko vinayadharo disvā “katthāvuso, gacchathā”ti pucchitvā “amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ iminā nāma karaṇenā”ti vutte “alaṃ, āvuso, kiṃ tattha gatenā”ti tattheva dhammena vinayena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameti. Evampi antarāmagge vūpasammati nāma.

Or it is settled on the way for those going to settle it elsewhere. It is settled on the way for those going, saying, 'We will not abide by this decision. This one is not skilled in the Vinaya. In such-and-such a village, elder Vinaya experts dwell; having gone there, we will decide'—either by them examining the case and persuading one another, or by other bhikkhus causing them to understand. However, it is not settled merely by mutual persuasion or by being made to understand by fellow bhikkhus. Rather, a Vinaya expert, coming along the road and seeing them, asks, 'Where are you going, friends?' When they reply, 'To such-and-such a village for such-and-such a reason,' he says, 'Enough, friends, what is the point of going there?' and right there, he settles that legal question in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya. This too is called settling on the way.

Yattha gantvā saṅghassa niyyātitaṃ, tattha saṅghena vāti sace pana “alaṃ, āvuso, kiṃ tattha gatenā”ti vuccamānāpi “mayaṃ tattheva gantvā vinicchayaṃ pāpessāmā”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 341) vinayadharassa vacanaṃ anādiyitvā yattha gantvā sabhāgabhikkhusaṅghassa adhikaraṇaṃ niyyātitaṃ, tattha saṅghena “alaṃ, āvuso, saṅghasannipātaṃ nāma garuka”nti tattheva nisīditvā vinicchitaṃ sammati. Na heva kho pana sabhāgabhikkhūnaṃ saññattiyā vūpasantaṃ hoti, apica kho saṅghaṃ sannipātetvā ārocitaṃ saṅghamajjhe vinayadharā vūpasamenti. Evampi tattha saṅghena vinicchitaṃ sammati nāma.

Or, where it has been referred to the Sangha after going there, it is settled by the Sangha there. But if, even when being told, 'Enough, friends, what is the use of going there?', they disregard the words of the Vinaya expert and say, 'We will go there and reach a decision' (Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā 341), then where the legal question has been referred to a Sangha of like-minded bhikkhus after going there, it is settled by the Sangha right there, having sat down and said, 'Enough, friends, a Sangha gathering is indeed a serious matter.' However, it is not settled merely by the communication to like-minded bhikkhus. Rather, after assembling the Sangha and announcing it, the Vinaya experts settle it in the midst of the Sangha. Even so, it is called settled by the Sangha there.

Ubbāhikāya [M 0.0447][V 0.0412] sammatapuggalehi vā vinicchitanti apaloketvā vā khandhake vuttāya vā ñattidutiyakammavācāya sammatehi puggalehi visuṃ vā nisīditvā, tassāyeva vā parisāya “aññena na kiñci kathetabba”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 231) sāvetvā vinicchitaṃ. Ayanti ayaṃ yathāvuttā catubbidhā sammukhatā.

Or it is decided by individuals authorized by the ubbāhikā (drawing lots); or by individuals authorized either by simple declaration or by a motion with one announcement as stated in the Khandhaka, who decide either by sitting separately, or within that same assembly after having announced, 'Nothing is to be said by anyone else' (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 231). This is the aforementioned fourfold face-to-face presence.

Kārakasaṅghassāti vūpasametuṃ sannipatitassa kārakasaṅghassa. Saṅghasāmaggivasena sammukhībhāvoti “yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosantī”ti (cūḷava. 228) evaṃ vuttasaṅghasāmaggivasena sammukhībhāvo, etena yathā tathā padhānakārakapuggalānaṃ sammukhatāmattaṃ saṅghasammukhatā nāma na hotīti dasseti. Bhūtatāti tacchatā. Saccapariyāyo hi idha dhammasaddo “dhammavādī”tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.9, 194) viya. Vineti etenāti vinayo, tassa tassa adhikaraṇassa vūpasamanāya bhagavatā vuttavidhi, tassa vinayassa sammukhatā vinayasammukhatā. Tenāha “yathā taṃ…pe… vinayasammukhatā”ti. Yenāti yena puggalena. Atthapaccatthikānanti (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.228) vivādavatthusaṅkhāte atthe paccatthikānaṃ. Saṅghasammukhatā parihāyati sammatapuggaleheva vūpasamanato.

Of the performing Saṅgha means: of the performing Saṅgha that has assembled to settle the matter. The presence by way of the Saṅgha's unity means: 'As many bhikkhus as are entitled to participate in the act have arrived, the consent of those worthy of giving consent has been obtained, and those present do not oppose' (Cūḷavagga 228). Thus, it is shown that the mere presence in just any way of the principal individuals performing the act does not constitute the presence of the Saṅgha. Actuality means truth. Here, the word 'Dhamma' is a synonym for truth, as in expressions like 'speaker of the Dhamma' (Dīgha Nikāya 1.9, 194). One disciplines with this, thus it is the Discipline—this refers to the procedure taught by the Blessed One for settling each dispute; the presence of that discipline is the presence of the Discipline. Hence it is said: 'As it is... the presence of the Discipline.' By whom means: by which person. Of the parties and counter-parties (Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 3.228) means: of those who are opposed in the matter designated as the basis of the dispute. The presence of the Saṅgha is lost because the matter is settled only by the appointed individuals.

Nanti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Pañcaṅgasamannāgatanti (cūḷava. 234) “na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, gahitāgahitaṃ jānātī”ti vuttehi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ. Gūḷhakavivaṭakasakaṇṇajappakesu tīsu salākaggāhesūti “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ saññattiyā tayo salākaggāhake gūḷhakaṃ, vivaṭakaṃ, sakaṇṇajappaka”nti (cūḷava. 235) samathakkhandhake vuttesu tīsu salākaggāhesu. Salākaṃ gāhetvāti dhammavādīnañca adhammavādīnañca salākāyo nimittasaññaṃ āropetvā cīvarabhoge katvā samathakkhandhake vuttanayena gāhāpetvā. Evañhi tattha vuttaṃ –

This refers to a legal case of dispute. Endowed with five factors (Cūḷavagga 234) means endowed with the five factors stated: 'He does not go to favoritism, does not go to ill will, does not go to delusion, does not go to fear, and knows what has been taken and what has not been taken.' Among the three kinds of taking of ballots—secret, open, and whispering—as stated in the Khandhaka on Settlements: 'I allow, bhikkhus, for the purpose of convincing those bhikkhus, three kinds of taking of ballots: secret, open, and whispering' (Cūḷavagga 235). Having had the ballot taken means having assigned distinguishing marks to the ballots of those who speak according to the Dhamma and those who speak contrary to the Dhamma, and having made them into voting tickets, then having them taken according to the method stated in the Khandhaka on Settlements. For thus it is said there—

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, gūḷhako salākaggāho hoti? Tena salākaggāhāpakena bhikkhunā salākāyo vaṇṇāvaṇṇāyo katvā ekameko bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo [M 0.0448] ‘ayaṃ evaṃvādissa salākā, ayaṃ evaṃvādissa salākā, yaṃ icchasi, taṃ gaṇhāhī’ti. Gahite vattabbo ‘mā ca kassaci dassehī’ti. Sace jānāti ‘adhammavādī bahutarā’ti, ‘duggaho’ti paccukkaḍḍhitabbaṃ. Sace jānāti ‘dhammavādī bahutarā’ti[V 0.0413], ‘suggaho’ti sāvetabbaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, gūḷhako salākaggāho hoti.

And how, bhikkhus, is the secret taking of the ballot conducted? The bhikkhu who is the ballot-distributor should prepare ballots of various colors. Then, approaching each bhikkhu one by one, he should say to him: 'This is the ballot for one who speaks thus, this is the ballot for one who speaks thus. Take whichever you wish.' When it has been taken, he should be told: 'Do not show it to anyone.' If he knows that those who speak contrary to the Dhamma are the majority, it should be withdrawn, with the words, 'It is badly taken.' If he knows that those who speak in accordance with the Dhamma are the majority, it should be announced, with the words, 'It is well taken.' Thus, bhikkhus, is the secret taking of the ballot conducted.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, vivaṭako salākaggāho hoti? Sace jānāti ‘dhammavādī bahutarā’ti, vissaṭṭheneva vivaṭena gāhetabbo. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, vivaṭako salākaggāho hoti.

And how, bhikkhus, is the open taking of the ballot conducted? If one knows, 'Those who speak in accordance with the Dhamma are more numerous,' then he should have it taken confidently and openly. Thus, bhikkhus, is the open taking of the ballot conducted.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, sakaṇṇajappako salākaggāho hoti? Tena salākaggāhāpakena bhikkhunā ekamekassa bhikkhuno upakaṇṇake ārocetabbaṃ ‘ayaṃ evaṃvādissa salākā, ayaṃ evavādissa salākā, yaṃ icchasi, taṃ gaṇhāhī’ti. Gahite vattabbo ‘mā ca kassaci ārocehī’ti. Sace jānāti ‘adhammavādī bahutarā’ti, ‘duggaho’ti paccukkaḍḍhitabbaṃ. Sace jānāti ‘dhammavādī bahutarā’ti, ‘suggaho’ti sāvetabbaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sakaṇṇajappako salākaggāho hotī”ti.

And how, bhikkhus, is the whispering taking of the ballot conducted? The bhikkhu who is the ballot-distributor should announce in the ear of each bhikkhu: 'This is the ballot for one who speaks thus, this is the ballot for one who speaks thus. Take whichever you wish.' When it has been taken, he should be told: 'Do not tell anyone.' If he knows that those who speak contrary to the Dhamma are the majority, it should be withdrawn, with the words, 'It is badly taken.' If he knows that those who speak in accordance with the Dhamma are the majority, it should be announced, with the words, 'It is well taken.' Thus, bhikkhus, is the whispering taking of the ballot conducted.

Ettha ca alajjussannāya (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 235) parisāya gūḷhako salākaggāho kātabbo, lajjussannāya vivaṭako, bālussannāya sakaṇṇajappakoti veditabbo. Dhammavādīnaṃ yebhuyyatāyāti dhammavādīnaṃ ekenapi adhikatāya, ko pana vādo dvīhi tīhi.

Here, for an assembly abounding in shamelessness (Cūḷavagga Commentary 235), a secret taking of the ballot should be done; for one abounding in conscientiousness, an open one; and for one abounding in foolishness, a whispering one. This should be understood. By the majority of Dhamma-speakers means: by even one more Dhamma-speaker; what need to mention two or three?

“Catūhi samathehi sammatī”ti idaṃ sabbasaṅgāhakavasena vuttaṃ, tattha pana dvīhi eva vūpasamanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ vinicchitanti sace āpatti natthi, ubho khamāpetvā, atha atthi, āpattiṃ dassetvā ropanavasena vinicchitaṃ. Paṭikammaṃ pana āpattādhikaraṇasamathe parato āgamissatīti. Na samaṇasāruppaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ, samaṇehi akattabbaṃ, tasmiṃ. Ajjhācāre vītikkame sati.

'It is settled by the four settlements'—this is said by way of complete inclusion. However, in that case, the settlement should be seen as being by only two. Thus it is decided: if there is no offense, it is decided by having both ask for forgiveness; but if there is an offense, it is decided by way of establishing it after having pointed out the offense. The remedy, however, will come later in the settlement of legal cases concerning offenses. Not proper for a recluse, unascetic, not to be done by recluses: this refers to that misconduct, when there is a transgression.

Pārājikasāmantena [M 0.0449] vāti dukkaṭena vā thullaccayena vā. Methunadhamme hi pārājikasāmantā nāma dukkaṭaṃ hoti, adinnādānādīsu thullaccayaṃ. Paṭicaratoti paṭicchādentassa. Acchinnamūlo bhavissatīti pārājikaṃ anāpanno bhavissati, sīlavā bhavissatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Sammā vattitvāti vattaṃ pūretvā. Osāraṇaṃ labhissatīti kammappaṭippassaddhiṃ labhissati.

By that bordering on a pārājika means: by a dukkaṭa or by a thullaccaya. In the case of sexual intercourse, what borders on a pārājika is a dukkaṭa; in cases of theft and so on, it is a thullaccaya. For one who conceals it means: for one who covers it up. He will be one whose root is not cut off means: he will not be subject to a pārājika offense; that is to say, he will be virtuous. Having behaved rightly means: having fulfilled his duties. He will obtain restoration means: he will obtain the revocation of the formal act.

Tassāti [V 0.0414] āpattādhikaraṇassa. Sammukhāvinayeneva vūpasamo natthi paṭiññāya, tathārūpāya khantiyā vā vinā avūpasamanato. Yā pana paṭiññāti sambandho.

Of that means: of the legal case concerning an offense. There is no settlement by the face-to-face procedure alone without acknowledgement, or without such forbearance, because there is no settlement without them. But as for acknowledgement, there is a connection.

Etthāti āpattidesanāyaṃ. Siyāti avassaṃ. Kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāyāti kakkhaḷabhāvāya ceva vāḷabhāvāya ca. Thullavajjanti pārājikañceva saṅghādisesañca. Gihippaṭisaṃyuttanti gihīnaṃ hīnena khuṃsanavambhanadhammikappaṭissavesu āpannaṃ āpattiṃ.

Here means: in the declaration of offenses. It may be means: assuredly. Due to harshness and severity means: due to the state of harshness and the state of severity. A serious offense means: both a pārājika and a saṅghādisesa offense. Connected with laypeople means: an offense incurred through base scolding, reviling, and in relation to lawful promises concerning laypeople.

Yathānurūpanti “dvīhi samathehi, tīhi, catūhi, ekenā”ti evaṃ vuttanayeneva yathānurūpaṃ. Etthāti imasmiṃ samathādhikāre. Vinicchayanayoti vinicchayanayamattaṃ. Tenāha “vitthāro panā”tiādi. Assāti vitthārassa. Samantapāsādikāyaṃ vuttoti samantapāsādikāya nāma vinayaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vutto. Tasmā tattha vuttanayeneva veditabboti adhippāyo.

According to what is suitable means: according to the method stated, such as 'with two settlements, with three, with four, with one.' Here means: in this section on settlement. Method of decision means: merely the method of decision. Therefore, it is said, 'But the detailed explanation...' Of that means: of the detailed explanation. Stated in the Samantapāsādikā means: stated in the Vinaya commentary called the Samantapāsādikā. Therefore, the intention is that it should be understood according to the method stated there.

Ettakanti etaṃparamaṃ, na ito bhiyyo.

This much means: this is the limit; there is nothing more than this.

Adhikaraṇasamathavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition on the settlement of legal cases is concluded.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus, in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the commentary on the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

In the Vinayatthamañjūsā, which elucidates subtle meanings,

Bhikkhupātimokkhavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Pātimokkha for Bhikkhus is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Bhikkhunīpātimokkhavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Pātimokkha for Bhikkhunīs

Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

The Pārājika Chapter

Nātho [M 0.0451][V 0.0415] bhikkhunīnaṃ hitatthāya yaṃ pātimokkhaṃ pakāsayīti sambandho. Tattha pakāsayīti desayi, paññāpayīti attho.

The connection is that the Lord declared the Pātimokkha for the welfare of the bhikkhunīs. Here, declared means taught, made known—this is the meaning.

Sādhāraṇapārājikaṃ

The Shared Pārājika

1. Methunadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Sexual Intercourse

Abhilāpamattanti vacanamattaṃ, na atthoti adhippāyo. Liṅgabhedamattanti purisaliṅgaṃ itthiliṅganti visesamattaṃ. Visesoti nānāttaṃ. Chandena cevāti pemena ceva, sinehena cevāti attho[V 0.0416]. Ruciyā cāti icchāya ca. Padhaṃsitāyāti dūsitāya. Paripuṇṇā upasampadā yassā sā paripuṇṇūpasampadā, ubhatosaṅghena upasampannāti attho.

Mere expression means: mere speech; the intention is 'not the meaning.' Mere distinction of gender means: the mere distinction of male gender and female gender. Distinction means: diversity. And with consent means: with affection and with love—this is the meaning. And with inclination means: and with desire. Defiled means: corrupted. 'She for whom the ordination is complete is one with a complete ordination' means: ordained by both Saṅghas—this is the meaning.

Methunadhammasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on sexual intercourse is concluded.

Asādhāraṇapārājikaṃ

The Unshared Pārājika

5. Ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Above the Knees.

Ubbhakapparanti dutiyamahāsandhito uddhaṃ. Ito cito ca sañcaraṇanti hatthassa vā kāyassa vā tiriyaṃ ito cito ca sañcaraṇaṃ.

'Ubbhakapparanti' means above the second great joint. 'Ito cito ca sañcaraṇanti' means the sideways movement of the hand or body to and fro.

Ekatoavassuteti (pāci. aṭṭha. 662) bhikkhuniyā avassave, bhikkhuniyā kāyasaṃsaggarāgena avassutabhāve satīti attho. Bhikkhuniyā vaseneva ca ekatoavassutabhāvo gahetabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 662) –

'Ekatoavassuteti' (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 662) means when a bhikkhunī is defiled by lust; that is, when there is a state of being defiled by lust for physical contact on the part of the bhikkhunī. And the state of being defiled by lust on one side should be understood as being on the part of the bhikkhunī. This is stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 662):

“Ekatoavassuteti [M 0.0452] ettha kiñcāpi ‘ekato’ti avisesena vuttaṃ, tathāpi bhikkhuniyā eva avassute sati ayaṃ āpattibhedo vuttoti veditabbo”ti.

Although 'ekato' is stated here without specification, it should be understood that this classification of offense is stated for when the bhikkhunī alone is defiled.

Purisassa kāyanti purisassa yaṃ kañci kāyaṃ. Ubhatoavassutepīti bhikkhuniyā ceva purisassa ca kāyasaṃsaggarāgena avassutabhāve satipi. Kāyenāti yathāparicchinnena attano kāyena. Kāyappaṭibaddhanti purisassa kāyappaṭibaddhaṃ. Avasesakāyena vāti yathāparicchinnakāyato avasesena kāyena, ubbhakkhakaadhojāṇumaṇḍalaadhokapparasaṅkhātena kāyenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tassa kāyanti avassutassa tassa purisassa yaṃ kañci kāyaṃ. Yathā cettha sayaṃ āmasantiyā thullaccayaṃ, evaṃ tassa āmasanaṃ sādiyantiyāpīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Purisassa kāyasaṃsaggarāgo natthīti purisassa methunarāgo, gehasitapemaṃ, suddhacittaṃ vā. Avaseseti pārājikakhettato avasese. Kāyappaṭibaddhena kāyappaṭibaddhādibhedeti “kāyappaṭibaddhena kāyappaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassā”tiādike [V 0.0417] (pāci. 659, 662) sabbavāre. “Asañciccā”tiādīsu virajjhitvā vā āmasantiyā, aññavihitāya vā, “ayaṃ puriso”ti vā “itthī”ti vā ajānantiyā vā, tena phuṭṭhāyapi taṃ phassaṃ assādayantiyā vā āmasanepi sati anāpatti.

'Purisassa kāyanti' means any part of a man's body. 'Ubhatoavassutepīti' means even when there is defilement due to lust for bodily contact in both the bhikkhunī and the man. 'Kāyenāti' refers to one's own body as specifically defined. 'Kāyappaṭibaddhanti' means what is connected to a man's body. 'Avasesakāyena vāti' means with the remaining part of the body other than the specifically defined part; that is to say, with the body reckoned as that above the collarbone, below the knee-circle, and below the elbow. 'Tassa kāyanti' refers to any part of the body of that defiled man. Just as a thullaccaya offense is incurred here if she herself touches him, so too it should be understood that one is incurred when she consents to his touching. 'Purisassa kāyasaṃsaggarāgo natthīti' means the man has no lust for sexual contact, no householder's affection, or has a pure mind. 'Avaseseti' refers to what remains apart from the area of a pārājika offense. 'Kāyappaṭibaddhena kāyappaṭibaddhādibhedeti' refers to all the cases in such passages as, 'If she touches what is connected to the body with what is connected to the body, there is an offense of wrong conduct' (pāci. 659, 662). In cases such as 'unintentionally' and so on, or if she touches after becoming dispassionate, or if she is distracted, or if she does not know whether 'this is a man' or 'a woman,' or even if, having been touched by him, she enjoys that contact while touching, there is no offense.

Ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on Above the Knees is concluded.

6. Vajjappaṭicchādikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Concealing an Offense.

Pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannanti bhikkhūhi sādhāraṇānaṃ catunnaṃ, asādhāraṇānaṃ catunnañcāti aṭṭhannamaññataraṃ ajjhāpannaṃ. Idañca pārājikaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 666) pacchā paññattaṃ, saṅgītikārakācariyehi pana purimena saddhiṃ yugaḷaṃ katvā imasmiṃ okāse ṭhapitanti veditabbaṃ. “Aṭṭhannaṃ pārājikānaṃ aññatara”nti (pāci. 666) vacanato pana vajjappaṭicchādikaṃ yā paṭicchādeti, sāpi vajjappaṭicchādikā evāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kiñcāpi vajjappaṭicchādanaṃ pemavasena hoti, tathāpi [M 0.0453] sikkhāpadavītikkamacittaṃ domanassameva hotīti katvā dukkhavedanaṃ hotīti “tatra hi pācittiyaṃ…pe… sesaṃ tādisamevā”ti vuttaṃ.

'Pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannanti' means having committed any one of the eight pārājika offenses—the four common to bhikkhus and the four that are not. It should be understood that this pārājika rule (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 666) was laid down later, but the teachers of the council paired it with the preceding one and placed it in this section. From the statement 'any one of the eight pārājika offenses' (Pāci. 666), it should be understood that she who conceals the offense of concealing a fault is also a 'vajjappaṭicchādikā' (one who conceals a fault). Although the concealment of an offense may arise out of affection, the mind that transgresses the training rule is still one of distress, and thus painful feeling arises. Therefore, it is said: 'Here, a pācittiya offense... the rest is similar.'

Vajjappaṭicchādikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on concealing an offense is concluded.

7. Ukkhittānuvattikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Following a Suspended Bhikkhunī.

Satthusāsanenāti ñattisampadāya ceva anussāvanasampadāya ca. Idha pana codanāsāraṇāpubbakameva ñattianussāvanaṃ satthusāsananti āha “idhāpī”tiādi. Karaṇanti ñattiṭṭhapanañceva anussāvanāvacanañca. Anādaranti puggale ceva dhamme ca ādaravirahitaṃ. Tenāha “yenā”tiādi. Tattha pariyāpannagaṇe vāti tasmiṃ saṅghe pariyāpanne sambahulapuggalasaṅkhāte gaṇe vā. “Sammāvattanāya avattamānanti attho”ti iminā adhippāyattho vutto. Ekakammādiketi ekakammaekuddesasamasikkhātāya. Saha ayanabhāvenāti saha vattanabhāvena. Samāno saṃvāso etesanti samānasaṃvāsakā.

'Satthusāsanenāti' means through the accomplishment of the motion and the accomplishment of the proclamation. Here, however, the motion and proclamation, preceded by rebuke and reminding, themselves constitute the teaching of the Master; hence it is said 'idhāpī' and so on. 'Karaṇanti' means both the presentation of the motion and the utterance of the proclamation. 'Anādaranti' means the absence of respect towards both the individual and the Dhamma. Therefore, it is said 'yenā' and so on. There, 'pariyāpannagaṇe vāti' means in that Saṅgha, or in the group consisting of many individuals who are included. The intended meaning is explained by 'Sammāvattanāya avattamānanti attho' (not proceeding in accordance with proper conduct). 'Ekakammādiketi' refers to having one act, one recitation, and the same training. 'Saha ayanabhāvenāti' means together with the state of conducting oneself. 'Samāno saṃvāso etesanti' means those who have the same communion, that is, 'samānasaṃvāsakā'.

Idāni yena saṃvāsena te “samānasaṃvāsakā”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 669) vuttā, so saṃvāso [V 0.0418] tassa ukkhittakassa tehi saddhiṃ natthi, yehi ca saddhiṃ tassa so saṃvāso natthi, na tena te bhikkhū attano sahāyā katā honti, tasmā so akatasahāyo nāmāti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “yassa panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Evaṃ padavaṇṇanaṃ katvā idāni atthamattaṃ dassetuṃ “samānasaṃvāsakabhāvaṃ anupagatanti attho”ti vuttaṃ. Kiṃ taṃ anuvattananti kassaci āsaṅkā siyāti taṃ sarūpato dassento “yaṃdiṭṭhiko so hotī”tiādimāha. Tattha soti yo ukkhittako, so.

Now, concerning the communion by which they are called 'samānasaṃvāsakā' (those who share the same communion) (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 669), that communion no longer exists for that suspended one with those bhikkhunīs. And those with whom that communion does not exist for her, those bhikkhunīs are not made her companions by her. Therefore, she is called 'akatasahāyo' (one who has not made companions). To demonstrate this meaning, 'yassa panā' and so on is stated. Having thus explained the wording, now to demonstrate just the meaning, 'It means she has not attained the state of being a samānasaṃvāsaka' is stated. 'What is that conformity (anuvattana)?'—lest someone should have doubt, showing it in its essential nature, he said 'yaṃdiṭṭhiko so hotī' and so on. There, 'so' refers to the suspended one.

Ukkhittānuvattikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on following a suspended bhikkhunī is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhavatthukāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Eight Bases.

Lokassādamittasanthavavasenāti (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.675) lokassādasaṅkhātassa mittasanthavassa vasena. Kiṃ tanti āha “kāyasaṃsaggarāgenā”ti. Kāyasaṃsaggarāgeneva [M 0.0454] tintā idha avassutā nāma, na methunarāgenāti. Kathametaṃ viññāyatīti āha “ayameva hī”tiādi. Kiṃ panettha kāraṇanti āha “samantapāsādikāyaṃ panassa vicāraṇā katā”ti. Tatthāyaṃ vicāraṇā – ettha ca asaddhammoti kāyasaṃsaggova veditabbo, na methunadhammo. Na hi methunassa sāmantā thullaccayaṃ hoti. “Viññū paṭibalo kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjitu”nti (pāci. 676) vacanampi cettha sādhakanti. Yaṃ yena kataṃ, taṃ tasseva hotīti. Purisapuggalassāti sāmivacananti dassetuṃ “yaṃ purisapuggalenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha hatthoti attano hattho. Na kevalañcettha hatthaggahaṇanti “hattho nāma kapparaṃ upādāya yāva agganakhā”ti (pāci. 676) vuttassa hatthasseva gahaṇaṃ, atha kho tassa ca aññassapi apārājikakhettassa gahaṇaṃ ekajjhaṃ katvā “hatthaggahaṇa”nti vuttaṃ. Tathā saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇanti na kevalaṃ saṅghāṭikaṇṇasseva gahaṇaṃ, atha kho tassa ca aññassapi yassa kassaci cīvarappadesassa gahaṇaṃ vuttanti dassetuṃ “ettha ca yassa kassacī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Itthannāmaṃ ṭhānanti evaṃnāmakaṃ ṭhānaṃ. “Paṭipāṭiyā vā uppaṭipāṭiyā vā pūretvā”ti idaṃ nidassanamattaṃ. Tasmā paṭipāṭiyā vā uppaṭipāṭiyā vā ekantarikāya vā yena tena nayena pūretvāti attho.

“By way of the pleasure of worldly companionship” (Sārattha. Ṭī. Pācittiya 3.675): by way of the companionship reckoned as worldly pleasure. “What is meant by ‘stained’?” He says: “by lust for physical contact.” Here, “stained” means being defiled solely by lust for physical contact, not by lust for sexual intercourse. “How is this understood?” He says: “For this very reason,” and so on. “What is the reason here?” He says: “Its analysis has been made in the Samantapāsādikā.” There, this is the analysis: here, “improper conduct” should be understood as physical contact, not sexual intercourse. For a grave offense does not occur in the vicinity of sexual intercourse. The statement “a wise person is capable of engaging in physical contact” (Pācittiya 676) also serves as proof here. “Whatever is done by someone, that belongs to that person.” To show that “of a person” (purisapuggalassa) is a possessive case, it is said “that which by a person” (yaṃ purisapuggalena), and so on. Here, “hand” means one’s own hand. And here, “taking of a hand” does not mean merely taking the hand as stated (Pācittiya 676)—“hand” means from the elbow up to the tip of the nails—but rather, it is said “taking of a hand” by combining the taking of that and any other area that is not subject to a pārājika offense. Similarly, “taking the edge of the outer robe” does not mean merely taking the edge of the outer robe, but rather, to show that it means taking that and any other part of the robe whatsoever, it is said “here, any part,” and so on. “A place called such and such” means a place with such a name. The phrase “filling it in order or out of order” is merely an illustration. Therefore, the meaning is filling it in order, or out of order, or with an interval, or in any other way.

Tā āpattiyoti tā āpannā āpattiyo. Yathā cekekasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ evaṃ visuṃ visuṃ sattasu vatthūsu satakkhattumpi vītikkantesu tā āpattiyo desetvā muccati. Gaṇanūpikāti desitagaṇanaṃ [V 0.0419] upagacchati. Dhuranikkhepaṃ katvāti “aññaṃ vatthuṃ āpajjissāmī”ti ussāhaṃ ṭhapetvā.

“Those offenses” means those offenses that have been incurred. Just as in each single matter, so in the seven matters separately, even when transgressed a hundred times, one is freed by confessing those offenses. “Entering into the count” means one undertakes the counting of what has been confessed. “Having laid down the burden” means having set aside the resolve: “I will commit another offense.”

Aṭṭhavatthukāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Eight Bases is concluded.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus, in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the Explanation of the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the Elucidation of Hidden Meanings,

Bhikkhunipātimokkhe pārājikavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the Explanation of the Pārājika Section in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha is concluded.

Saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ

The Saṅghādisesa Section

1. Ussayavādikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Training Rule on Contentious Talk

Mānussayavasena [M 0.0455][V 0.0420] kodhūssayavasenāti bāhullanayena vuttaṃ. Teneva vakkhati “ticittaṃ tivedana”nti. Aḍḍakaraṇatthāyāti ettha aḍḍoti vohārikavinicchayo vuccati. Yaṃ pabbajitā “adhikaraṇa”ntipi vadanti, tassa karaṇatthāya vohārikavinicchayatthāyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Vītikkamakkhaṇeyevāti vatthujjhācārakkhaṇeyeva, na tatiyāya samanubhāsanāyāti adhippāyo. Bhikkhuniṃ saṅghato nissāretīti āpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ bhikkhunisaṅghamhā nissāreti. Hetumhi cāyaṃ kattuvohāro “nissāraṇahetubhūtadhammo ‘nissāraṇīyo’ti vutto”ti katvā.

“By way of contention due to conceit, by way of contention due to anger”—this is stated in a general sense. Therefore, he will say: “three minds, three feelings.” For the purpose of adjudication: here, “adjudication” refers to a conventional judgment. What renunciants also call an “issue” (adhikaraṇa), its purpose is for adjudication, meaning for the sake of conventional judgment. “At the very moment of transgression” means at the very moment of the transgression concerning the object, not at the third admonition—this is the intended meaning. “The Saṅgha expels a bhikkhunī” means it expels an offending bhikkhunī from the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. Here, this agent usage is in the sense of cause, as it is said: “The phenomenon that is the cause of expulsion is called ‘that which leads to expulsion’.”

Yattha ṭhitāyāti upassayabhikkhācāramaggādīsu yasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhitāya. Tato paṭṭhāya gacchantiyāti tato paṭṭhāya vohārikānaṃ santikaṃ gacchantiyā. Dutiyeti dutiyārocane. Tenāti upāsakena. Evaṃ vuttāyāti “mama ca tava ca kathaṃ tvaṃyeva ārocehī”ti vuttāya. Aññena kathāpetīti kappiyakārakena kathāpeti. Yathā vā tathā vā hi ārociyamāneti kappiyakārako vā bhikkhuniyā kathaṃ paṭhamaṃ ārocetu, itaro vā attano kathaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 679). Kappiyakārako vā ubhinnampi kathaṃ, itaro vā ubhinnampi kathaṃ ārocetūti evaṃ yathā tathā ārociyamāne. Ubhinnampi pana kathaṃ sutvāti yathā tathā vā ārocitaṃ pana ubhinnampi kathaṃ sutvā.

“Where she stands” means the place where she is standing, such as the lodging, the alms-round, or the path. “From there, she goes” means from that place, she goes to the vicinity of the lay authorities. “Second” refers to the second announcement. “By him” means by the lay follower. “Thus spoken” means when she was told, “Between me and you, you alone should announce the matter.” “She has it announced by another” means she has it announced by a suitable person. “However it is announced” means whether the suitable person first announces the bhikkhunī’s message, or the other first announces his own message (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 679); or the suitable person may announce the message of both, or the other may announce the message of both—thus, however it is announced. “But having heard the message of both” means however it is announced, upon hearing the message of both.

Ākaḍḍhiyamānā gacchatīti vuccamānā vohārikānaṃ santikaṃ gacchati, imassa “tassā anāpattī”ti iminā sambandho. Evaṃ sesesupi. Rakkhaṃ yācatīti dhammikaṃ rakkhaṃ yācati. Idāni yathā yācitā rakkhā dhammikā hoti, taṃ dassetuṃ “upassaye aññehi kataṃ anācāraṃ anodissa ācikkhantī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha atītaṃ ārabbha atthi odissa ācikkhanā (pāci. aṭṭha. 679), atthi [V 0.0421] anodissa ācikkhanā, anāgataṃ ārabbhāpi atthi odissa ācikkhanā, atthi anodissa ācikkhanā.

“Being dragged along, she goes” means, being summoned, she goes to the vicinity of the lay authorities. The connection to this is, “There is no offense for her.” The same applies to the rest. “She requests protection” means she requests rightful protection. Now, to show how the protection requested is rightful, it is said: “In the dwelling, she reports misconduct done by others without specifying it.” Here, concerning the past, there is reporting by specifying and reporting without specifying; concerning the future also, there is reporting by specifying and reporting without specifying.

Kathaṃ [M 0.0456] atītaṃ ārabbha odissa ācikkhanā hoti? Bhikkhunupassaye gāmadārakā, dhuttādayo vā ye keci anācāraṃ vā ācaranti, rukkhaṃ vā chindanti, phalāphalaṃ vā haranti, parikkhāre vā acchindanti. Bhikkhunī vohārike upasaṅkamitvā “amhākaṃ upassaye idaṃ nāma kata”nti vadati. “Kenā”ti vutte “asukena ca asukena cā”ti ācikkhati. Evaṃ atītaṃ ārabbha odissa ācikkhanā hoti, sā na vaṭṭati. Tañce sutvā te vohārikā tesaṃ daṇḍaṃ karonti, sabbaṃ bhikkhuniyā gīvā hoti. “Daṇḍaṃ gaṇhissantī”ti adhippāyepi sati gīvāyeva hoti. Sace pana tassa “daṇḍaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vadati, pañcamāsakamatte gahite pārājikaṃ hoti.

How is a specific report concerning the past made? In the bhikkhunīs’ residence, village boys, rogues, or whoever else misbehaves—they cut down trees, steal fruits, or take away requisites. A bhikkhunī approaches the lay authorities and says, “Such and such was done in our residence.” When asked, “By whom?” she replies, “By so-and-so and so-and-so.” In this way, a specific report concerning the past is made, and that is not allowable. If, upon hearing this, those lay authorities punish them, the entire blame falls on the bhikkhunī. Even if she merely intends, “They will be punished,” the blame still falls on her. But if she says to them, “Punish them,” and they impose a fine of five māsakas, it becomes a pārājika offense.

Tehi “kenā”ti vutte pana “asukenā’ti vattuṃ amhākaṃ na vaṭṭati, tumheyeva jānissatha. Kevalañhi mayaṃ rakkhaṃ yācāma, taṃ no detha, avahaṭabhaṇḍampi āharāpethā”ti vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ anodissa ācikkhanā hoti, sā vaṭṭati. Evaṃ vutte sacepi te vohārikā te kārake gavesitvā tesaṃ daṇḍaṃ karonti, sabbaṃ sāpateyyampi gahitaṃ, bhikkhuniyā neva gīvā, na āpatti.

However, when asked by them, “By whom?”, it should be said: “It is not proper for us to say, ‘By so-and-so.’ You yourselves will know. We merely ask for protection—give us that and have the stolen goods brought back.” This is how to report without specifying, and that is allowable. If, after speaking thus, those lay authorities investigate those who did it and punish them, and even if all the stolen property is seized, the bhikkhunī incurs neither blame nor offense.

Parikkhāraṃ harante disvā tesaṃ anatthakāmatāya “coro coro”ti vattumpi na vaṭṭati. Evaṃ vuttepi hi yaṃ tesaṃ daṇḍaṃ karonti, sabbaṃ bhikkhuniyā gīvā hoti. Attano vacanakaraṃ pana “iminā me parikkhāro gahito, taṃ āharāpehi, mā cassa daṇḍaṃ karothā”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Dāsadāsivāpiādīnaṃ atthāya aḍḍaṃ karonti, ayaṃ akappiyaaḍḍo nāma, na vaṭṭati.

Seeing them carrying away the requisites, even out of a desire for their harm, it is not proper to say, “Thief! Thief!” For even if this is said, whatever punishment they inflict, it all falls on the bhikkhunī’s neck. However, it is proper to say to one who obeys one’s words, “This requisite was taken by him; have it brought back, and do not punish him.” They also bring a charge for the sake of male and female slaves and others; this is called an improper charge, and it is not allowable.

Kathaṃ anāgataṃ ārabbha odissa ācikkhanā hoti? Vuttanayeneva parehi anācārādīsu katesu bhikkhunī vohārike evaṃ vadati “amhākaṃ upassaye idañcidañca karonti, rakkhaṃ no detha āyatiṃ akaraṇatthāyā”ti. “Kena evaṃ kata”nti vutte “asukena ca asukena cā”ti ācikkhati. Evaṃ anāgataṃ ārabbha odissa ācikkhanā hoti, sāpi na vaṭṭati. Tesañhi daṇḍe kate purimanayeneva sabbaṃ bhikkhuniyā gīvā. Sesaṃ purimasadisameva.

How is a specific report concerning the future made? In the same way as before, when others have committed misconduct and so forth, a bhikkhunī tells the lay authorities, saying, “In our residence, such and such things are being done. Please give us protection so that they do not happen again in the future.” When asked, “By whom was this done?” she replies, “By so-and-so and so-and-so.” Thus, a specific report concerning the future is made, and that too is not allowable. For if punishment is inflicted on them, everything falls on the bhikkhunī’s neck as before. The rest is similar to the previous case.

Sace [M 0.0457] pana vohārikā bhikkhunupassaye evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ karontānaṃ “imaṃ nāma daṇḍaṃ karomā”ti [V 0.0422] bheriṃ carāpetvā āṇāya atiṭṭhamāne pariyesitvā daṇḍaṃ karonti, bhikkhuniyā neva gīvā, na āpatti.

If, however, the lay authorities, having become aware of such misconduct in the bhikkhunīs’ residence, announce, “We will impose this penalty,” and having a drum beaten to proclaim it, seek out and impose the penalty on those who do not abide by the order, the bhikkhunī incurs neither blame nor offense.

Yo cāyaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ vutto, bhikkhūnampi eseva nayo. Bhikkhunopi hi odissa ācikkhanā na vaṭṭati, yaṃ tathā ācikkhite tesaṃ daṇḍaṃ karonti, taṃ sabbaṃ gīvā hoti. Vuttanayeneva daṇḍaṃ gaṇhāpentassa pārājikaṃ. Yo pana “daṇḍaṃ karissantī”ti jānantopi anodissa katheti, te ca pariyesitvā daṇḍaṃ karontiyeva, na doso. Vihārasīmāya rukkhādīni chindantānaṃ vāsipharasuādīni gahetvā pāsāṇe koṭṭenti, na vaṭṭati. Sace dhārā bhijjati, kārāpetvā dātabbā. Upadhāvitvā tesaṃ parikkhāre gaṇhanti, tampi na kātabbaṃ. Lahuparivattañhi cittaṃ, theyyacetanāya uppannāya mūlacchejjampi gaccheyya.

And the rule that has been stated for bhikkhunīs applies also to bhikkhus. For a bhikkhu too, a specific report is not allowable; if punishment is inflicted on them based on such a report, all the blame falls on him. If one prompts punishment in the manner described above, it is a pārājika offense. However, if someone speaks without specifying, even knowing that they will be punished, and they are indeed sought out and punished, there is no fault. It is not allowable to take the axes, adzes, and so forth of those cutting trees within the monastery boundary and strike them against a stone. If a blade breaks, it must be repaired and returned. Seizing their tools after running after them is also not to be done. For the mind is quick to change, and if a thought of theft arises, it could lead to the complete uprooting of virtue.

Ussayavādikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Contentious Talk is concluded.

2. Corivuṭṭhāpikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Training Rule on Ordaining a Female Thief

Mallagaṇabhaṭiputtagaṇādikantiādīsu (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.683) mallagaṇo nāma nārāyanabhattiko tattha tattha pānīyaṭṭhapanapokkharaṇikhaṇanādipuññakammakārako gaṇo. Bhaṭiputtagaṇo nāma kumārabhattikagaṇo. Dhammagaṇoti sāsanabhattiko anekappakārapuññakammakārako gaṇo. Gandhikaseṇīti anekappakārasugandhivikatikārako gaṇo. Dussikaseṇīti dussavāṇijasamūho, pesakāragaṇoti attho.

In terms such as 'Mallagaṇabhaṭiputtagaṇādīsu' (Sārattha. Ṭī. Pācittiya 3.683), 'Mallagaṇo' means a group devoted to Nārāyaṇa, performing meritorious deeds such as providing drinking water, digging ponds, and so forth, in various places. 'Bhaṭiputtagaṇo' means a group devoted to Kumārabhattika. 'Dhammagaṇo' refers to a group devoted to the Dispensation, performing various kinds of meritorious deeds. 'Gandhikaseṇī' means a guild of perfumers. 'Dussikaseṇī' refers to a group of cloth merchants, meaning a guild of weavers.

Vuṭṭhāpentiyāti upasampādentiyā. Kenaci karaṇīyena pakkantāsu bhikkhunīsu agantvā khaṇḍasīmaṃ yathānisinnaṭṭhāneyeva attano nissitakaparisāya saddhiṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā vācācittato samuṭṭhāti (pāci. aṭṭha. 683), aññaṃ sīmaṃ vā nadiṃ vā gantvā vuṭṭhāpentiyā kāyavācācittato samuṭṭhātīti āha “corivuṭṭhāpanasamuṭṭhāna”nti. Anāpucchā vuṭṭhāpanavasena kiriyākiriyaṃ. Paññattiṃ ajānantā ariyāpi vuṭṭhāpentīti vā kammavācāpariyosāne āpattikkhaṇe vipākābyākatasamaṅgitāvasena vā ticittaṃ.

To ordain means to confer the full ordination. When the bhikkhunīs have departed for some necessary business, without going to the defective boundary, if she ordains them while remaining in her original seated position, together with her dependent group, the offense arises from speech and mind (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 683). If she goes to another boundary or a river and ordains them, it arises from body, speech, and mind—hence it is called 'the arising of the ordination of a thief.' The offense is of the nature of action and non-action in the case of ordaining without asking permission. Or, even noble ones, not knowing the regulation, may ordain; or, at the moment of offense at the conclusion of the Kammavācā, due to association with resultant and indeterminate consciousness, it is a threefold consciousness.

Corivuṭṭhāpikāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Training Rule on Ordaining a Thief is concluded.

3. Ekagāmantaragamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The explanation of the Training Rule on Going Alone Between Villages

Añño [V 0.0423][M 0.0458] gāmo gāmantaraṃ. Nadipāranti nadiyā pārimatīraṃ. “Gāmantaraṃ gaccheyyā”ti (pāci. 687, 691) vuttattā aññasmiṃ gāmeyeva āpatti, na sakagāmeti āha “sakagāmato tāvā”tiādi. Parikkhepe vā upacāre vā atikkanteti parikkhittassa gāmassa parikkhepe vā aparikkhittassa gāmassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhāne vā atikkante. Dutiyena atikkantamatteti dutiyena pādena itarassa gāmassa parikkhepe vā upacāre vā atikkantamatte. Yesu pana potthakesu “ekena pādena itarassa gāmassa parikkhepe vā atikkante, upacāre vā okkante thullaccayaṃ, dutiyena atikkantamatte, okkantamatte vā saṅghādiseso”ti pāṭho dissati, tattha “okkante, okkantamatte vā”ti etāni dve padāni pāḷiyā virujjhanti. “Aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ atikkāmentiyā”ti (pāci. 692) hi pāḷi. Tathā samantapāsādikāyapi virujjhanti. Tattha hi –

Gāmantaraṃ means another village. 'Beyond the river' means the far bank of the river. Because it is said, 'She would go to another village' (Pāc. 687, 691), the offense occurs in another village, not in her own village. Hence, it is stated, 'From her own village, as long as...' 'Crossed the boundary or the vicinity' means having gone beyond the boundary of an enclosed village or the area treated as the boundary of an unenclosed village. 'Just having crossed with the second step' means just having crossed the boundary or vicinity of the other village with the second foot. However, in some texts, the passage is found: 'If one crosses into the boundary or vicinity of another village with one foot, a grave offense is incurred. If one just crosses or just enters with the second step, it is a saṅghādisesa offense.' Here, the phrases 'entered' or 'just having entered' conflict with the Pāli. For the Pāli states, 'When crossing beyond the vicinity of an unenclosed village' (Pāc. 692). Similarly, they are also contradicted in the Samantapāsādikā. There it says—

“Parikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃ ekena pādena atikkamati, thullaccayaṃ. Dutiyena atikkantamatte saṅghādiseso. Apicettha sakagāmato…pe… ekena pādena itarassa gāmassa parikkhepe vā upacārevā atikkantamatte thullaccayaṃ, dutiyena atikkantamatte saṅghādiseso”ti –

‘If one transgresses the area treated as the boundary with one foot, it is a grave offense. Just having transgressed with the second foot, it is a saṅghādisesa offense. Furthermore, in this case, when crossing from one’s own village… with one foot just having transgressed the boundary or the vicinity of another village, it is a grave offense; just having transgressed with the second foot, it is a saṅghādisesa offense.’

Vuttaṃ. “Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmentiyā”tiādivacanato (pāci. 692) padasā gamanameva idhādhippetanti āha “padasā pavisantiyā āpattī”ti. Iminā sacepi hatthipiṭṭhiādīhi vā iddhiyā vā pavisati, vaṭṭatiyevāti dasseti. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana samantapāsādikāya (pāci. aṭṭha. 692) vuttoti adhippāyo.

It is said. From the statement beginning ‘passing beyond the first foot’ (Pāc. 692), it is intended here that merely going on foot is meant; thus it is stated, ‘there is an offense for one entering on foot.’ By this, it is shown that even if one enters by means of an elephant’s back or by supernormal power, it is permissible. This is the summary here; however, the detailed explanation is as stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 692)—this is the intention.

Nadipāragamane vuttalakkhaṇāya nadiyāti “nadī nāma timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādetvā yattha katthaci uttarantiyā antaravāsako temiyatī”ti (pāci. 692) nadipāragamanavibhaṅge vuttalakkhaṇāya nadiyā. Nadipāragamanavibhaṅgo hi idha nadipāragamanasaddena vutto. Puna orimatīrameva paccuttarantiyā vāti paratīraṃ gantukāmatāya otiṇṇattā vuttaṃ. Itarissā pana ayaṃ pakkantaṭṭhāne ṭhitā hoti, tasmā paratīraṃ gacchantiyā anāpatti. Sace sajjhāyaṃ [M 0.0459] vā padhānaṃ vā aññaṃ vā kiñci kammaṃ kurumānā “pure aruṇeyeva dutiyikāya santikaṃ gamissāmī”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 692) ābhogaṃ karoti, ajānantiyā eva tassā aruṇo uggacchati[V 0.0424], anāpattīti āha “pure aruṇeyevā”tiādi. Atha pana “yāva aruṇuggamanā idheva bhavissāmī”ti vā anābhogena vā vihārassa ekadese acchati, dutiyikāya hatthapāsaṃ na otarati, aruṇuggamane saṅghādiseso. Hatthapāsoyeva hi idha pamāṇaṃ. Hatthapāsātikkame ekagabbhopi na rakkhati. Tenāha “ekagabbhe…pe… āpattī”ti.

Regarding the characteristics of a river as mentioned in connection with crossing a river, a river is defined as ‘a place where, after covering the three (lower) parts (of the body), the inner robe gets wet wherever one crosses’ (Pāc. 692). This refers to the characteristics of a river as explained in the analysis of river-crossing. Here, the analysis of river-crossing is referred to by the term ‘river-crossing.’ Furthermore, ‘for one crossing back to this shore’ is stated because she had entered the water with the intention of reaching the opposite shore. However, if the other nun remains in the place from which she departed, then for the one going to the other shore, there is no offense. If, while engaged in recitation, meditation, or any other task, she thinks, ‘I will go to the other nun before dawn’ (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 692), and without her knowledge, dawn breaks, there is no offense—thus it is said, ‘before dawn,’ and so on. But if she thinks, ‘I will stay here until sunrise,’ or remains in a part of the dwelling without any intention, and does not come within the other nun’s arm’s reach, then at sunrise, it is a saṅghādisesa offense. Here, the measure is simply the arm’s reach. Beyond the arm’s reach, even a single room does not protect her. Therefore, it is said, ‘in a single room… there is an offense.’

Dassanūpacāraṃ vā savanūpacāraṃ vāti ettha dassanūpacāro nāma yattha ṭhitaṃ dutiyikā passati. Savanūpacāro nāma yattha ṭhitā maggamūḷhasaddena viya, dhammassavanārocanasaddena viya ca “ayye”ti saddāyantiyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Tasmāti yasmā ohīyanaṃ nāma dassanūpacārasavanūpacārānamaññatarassa vijahanaṃ, tasmā. Antogāme pana ohīyanaṃ vaṭṭatīti āha “indakhīlātikkamato paṭṭhāyā”ti ādi. Tattha indakhīlātikkamatoti ummārātikkamato. Bahigāmeti gāmassa bahipadese. Maggamūḷhā uccāsaddaṃ karontīti āha “maggamūḷhasaddena viyā”ti. Maggamūḷhaṃ avhāyantassa saddena viyātipi vadanti. Saddāyantiyāti saddaṃ karontiyā. “Saddassavanātikkame āpattiyevā”ti iminā dassanūpacāro evarūpe savanūpacāre vijahite na rakkhati, jahitamatteva āpatti saṅghādisesassāti dasseti.

The range of sight or the range of hearing—here, the range of sight is a place where the companion nun sees one standing. The range of hearing is a place where one standing hears a sound, like the sound of one lost on the road, or like the sound announcing a Dhamma talk, and the sound of one calling out, ‘Noble lady!’ Therefore, since ‘being left behind’ means abandoning either the range of sight or the range of hearing, it is so. Moreover, being left behind is permissible within the village, as stated: ‘beginning from crossing the boundary pillar,’ and so on. Here, ‘crossing the boundary pillar’ means crossing the threshold. ‘Outside the village’ refers to the area outside the village. Those who are lost on the road make a loud sound; hence it is said: ‘like the sound of one lost on the road.’ Some also say it is like the sound of someone calling out to one who is lost on the road. ‘Calling out’ means making a sound. By the phrase ‘By transgressing the hearing of a sound, an offense is indeed incurred,’ it is shown that the range of sight does not protect when the range of hearing is abandoned in such a case; the offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred as soon as it is abandoned.

Maggaṃ gacchantīti ekamaggaṃ gacchanti. Sace purimāyo aññena maggena gacchanti, pakkantā nāma honti, anāpattiyeva. Dvinnaṃ gacchantīnaṃ ekā anubandhituṃ asakkontī “gacchatu aya”nti ohīyati, itarāpi “ohīyatu aya”nti gacchati, dvinnampi āpatti. Sace pana gacchantīsu purimāpi aññaṃ maggaṃ gaṇhāti, pacchimāpi aññaṃ, ekā ekissā pakkantaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati, dvinnampi anāpatti.

'Going on a path' means going on one path. If those in front go by another path, they are considered to have departed, and there is no offense. If two are going and one, unable to follow, says, 'Let this one go,' and falls behind, while the other also says, 'Let this one fall behind,' and goes on, both incur an offense. However, if while going, the one in front takes one path and the one behind takes another, and one stands at the point where the other departed, then both are without offense.

“Saṅghādisesā caturo”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 479) ayaṃ pañho aruṇuggamane gāmantarapariyāpannaṃ nadipāraṃ okkantabhikkhuniṃ sandhāya vutto. Sā hi sakagāmato paccūsasamaye nikkhamitvā aruṇuggamanakāle vuttappakāraṃ nadipāraṃ okkantamattāva [M 0.0460] rattivippavāsagāmantaranadipāragamanagaṇamhāohīyanalakkhaṇe ekappahāreneva caturo saṅghādisese āpajjati.

'The four Saṅghādisesas' (Pari. Aṭṭha. 479)—this question refers to a nun who, at dawn, has entered the far bank of a river, which is included within the scope of 'between villages.' For she, having left her own village in the early morning, at the time of sunrise, just as she crossed to the far bank of the river in the manner described, incurs all four Saṅghādisesas simultaneously, due to the characteristics of staying away overnight, going between villages, crossing a river, and being left behind by the group.

Pakkhasaṅkantāya vāti titthāyatanaṃ saṅkantāya. Anantarāyenāti hatthimocanādiantarāyaṃ vinā.

The phrase 'Or at the change of the fortnight' means having gone to a bathing place. 'Without an obstacle' means without obstacles such as the release of an elephant, etc.

Ekagāmantaragamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Training Rule on Going Alone Between Villages is concluded.

4. Ukkhittakaosāraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Training Rule on the Reinstatement of a Suspended Bhikkhu

Tasseva [V 0.0425] kārakasaṅghassāti yo ukkhepanīyakammakārako gaṇo, tasseva kārakasaṅghassa. Vatte vā vattantinti tecattālīsappabhede netthāravatte vattamānaṃ.

“Of that very acting Saṅgha” means of that very group that performed the act of suspension, of that very acting Saṅgha. “In the procedure or while it is in progress” means while it is in progress in the forty-three-fold procedure of rehabilitation.

Ukkhittakaosāraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Reinstatement of a Suspended Bhikkhu is concluded.

5. Bhojanappaṭiggahaṇapaṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the First Training Rule concerning the Acceptance of Food

Ekatoavassuteti puggalassa vā bhikkhuniyā vā avassute. Mahāpaccariyaṃ panettha “bhikkhuniyā avassutabhāveti daṭṭhabba”nti (pāci. aṭṭha. 701) vuttaṃ. Taṃ “anavassutoti jānantī paṭiggaṇhātī”ti (pāci. 703) imāya pāḷiyā na sameti. Yadi hi puggalassa avassutabhāvo nappamāṇaṃ, kiṃ “anavassutoti jānantī”ti iminā vacanena, “anāpatti ubhatoanavassutā honti, anavassutā paṭiggaṇhātī”ti ettakameva vattabbaṃ siyā. Ubhosu anavassutesūti puggalo ceva bhikkhunī cāti ubhosu anavassutesu gaṇhantiyā sabbathāpi anāpatti. “Anavassuto”ti vā ñatvā gaṇhantiyāti sayaṃ anavassutā samānā avassutepi “anavassuto aya”nti saññāya tassa hatthato paṭiggaṇhantiyā. Atha sayaṃ anavassutāpi aññaṃ avassutaṃ vā anavassutaṃ vā “avassuto”ti ñatvā paṭiggaṇhāti, dukkaṭameva. Vuttañhetaṃ anantarasikkhāpade “kissa tvaṃ, ayye, na paṭiggaṇhāsīti, avassutā, ayyeti, tvaṃ pana, ayye, avassutāti, nāhaṃ, ayye, avassutā”ti.

“Lustful on one side” means a person or a bhikkhunī is lustful. In the Mahāpaccariya, however, it is said, “It should be understood as ‘the bhikkhunī is lustful’” (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 701). This does not align with the Pāli text, “Knowing he is not lustful, she receives it” (Pāc. 703). For if the lustfulness of the person were not a determining factor, what is the point of this statement, “knowing he is not lustful”? It would suffice to say, “There is no offense if both are not lustful; she who is not lustful receives.” When both are not lustful—meaning both the person and the bhikkhunī—there is absolutely no offense for the one receiving. Or, “knowing he is not lustful,” she receives it, means: for her who, being herself not lustful, receives from his hand, perceiving even a lustful one as, “He is not lustful.” But if she, though not lustful herself, perceives another—whether lustful or not—as “lustful” and receives, it is a wrong-doing. This is stated in the immediately preceding training rule: “Why do you not accept it, venerable lady?” “He is lustful, sir.” “But are you, venerable lady, lustful?” “No, sir, I am not lustful.”

Bhojanappaṭiggahaṇapaṭhamasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the First Training Rule concerning the Acceptance of Food is concluded.

6. Bhojanappaṭiggahaṇadutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Second Training Rule concerning the Acceptance of Food

Dukkaṭādikā [M 0.0461] saṅghādisesapariyosānā āpattiyo iminā sikkhāpadena uyyojikāyeva, itarissā pana āpattibhedo paṭhamasikkhāpadenāti āha “sā evaṃ uyyojanenā”tiādi.

By this training rule, the offenses beginning with wrong-doing and ending with formal meeting are indeed for the instigator. But for the other bhikkhunī, the distinction of offenses is as in the first training rule. Thus he said, “She, by such instigation…” and so on.

Kulānuddayatāyāti kulānukampakatāya.

“Out of compassion for families” means out of sympathy for families.

Bhojanappaṭiggahaṇadutiyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Second Training Rule concerning the Acceptance of Food is concluded.

7-13. Sañcarittādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7-13. Explanation of the Training Rules on Acting as a Go-between, etc.

Sattamādīni [V 0.0426] uttānatthāneva.

The seventh and so on are straightforward in meaning.

Sañcarittādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rules on Acting as a Go-between, etc., is concluded.

14-17. Saṅghabhedakādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

14-17. Explanation of the Training Rules Regarding Causing a Schism in the Saṅgha, etc.

Bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ na bhindatīti kammaṃ, uddeso cāti dvīhi bhedo, so tāya saddhiṃ natthīti bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ na bhindati. Na kevalaṃ parivāsābhāvoyevāti āha “chādanapaccayāpī”tiādi. Ettha ca “chādanapaccayāpi na dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatī”ti pāṭho daṭṭhabbo, chādanapaccayāpi dukkaṭaṃ na āpajjatīti attho. Evañca katvā –

A bhikkhunī does not split the Saṅgha: the act (kamma) and the recitation (uddesa)—the division is twofold. This division does not exist for her; thus, a bhikkhunī does not split the Saṅgha. It is not only that there is an absence of probation (parivāsa); thus, it is said, “even due to concealment,” and so on. And here, the reading, “even due to concealment, she does not incur a wrong-doing,” should be noted; the meaning is that even due to concealment, she does not incur a wrong-doing. This being the case—

“Āpajjati garukaṃ sāvasesaṃ;

Chādeti anādariyaṃ paṭicca;

Na bhikkhunī no ca phuseyya vajjaṃ;

Pañhāmesā kusalehi cintitā”ti. (pari. 481) –

“He incurs a grave offense with a remainder; he conceals it out of disrespect; it is not a bhikkhunī, nor would she touch the fault; this question has been pondered by the skilled.”

Ettha bhikkhuninisedho upapanno hoti. Yesu pana potthakesu “chādanapaccayā pana dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatī”ti vinā na-kāraṃ pāṭho dissati, so pamādalekhoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā parivāso nāma natthi, tasmā. Attano sīmaṃ sodhetvā vihārasīmāya vāti vihāre baddhasīmameva [M 0.0462] sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sodhetuṃ asakkontīhīti vihārasīmaṃ sodhetuṃ asakkontīhi.

Here, the prohibition regarding bhikkhunīs is fitting. But in those books where the reading, “due to concealment, one incurs a wrong-doing,” appears without the negative particle ‘na’, that should be regarded as a scribal error. ‘Therefore’ means: because there is no such thing as probation, therefore… “Having purified one’s own boundary or the monastery boundary”—this is said referring specifically to the boundary established within the monastery. “By those unable to purify” means by those unable to purify the monastery boundary.

Mukhamattanidassananti pavesopāyamattanidassanaṃ. Etthāha – atha kasmā yathā bhikkhumānattakathāya “parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato, aparikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato dve leḍḍupāte atikkammā”ti (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nigamanavaṇṇanā) vuttaṃ, evamavatvā “gāmūpacārato ca bhikkhūnaṃ vihārūpacārato ca dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā”ti idha vuttanti? Tatra ceke vadanti “bhikkhūnaṃ vuttappakāraṃ padesaṃ atikkamitvā gāmepi taṃ kammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, bhikkhunīnaṃ pana gāme na vaṭṭati, tasmā evaṃ vutta”nti. Apare pana bhaṇanti “bhikkhūnampi gāme na vaṭṭati, bhikkhuvihāro nāma pubbeyeva gāmūpacāraṃ atikkamitvā tiṭṭhati[V 0.0427], tasmā gāmaṃ avatvā vihārūpacārameva heṭṭhā vuttaṃ. Bhikkhunīnaṃ pana vihāro gāmeyeva, na bahi, tasmā gāmūpacārañca vihārūpacārañca ubhayamevettha dassitaṃ. Tasmā ubhayatthāpi atthato nānātthaṃ natthī”ti. Vīmaṃsitvā yañcettha yujjati, taṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Showing just the entrance” means showing just the means of entry. Here it is said: But why, when in the discussion on the penance for a bhikkhu it is stated, “beyond two stone-throws from the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, or from a place suitable for an enclosure of an unenclosed monastery” (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Nigamanavaṇṇanā), is it not said in the same way here, but rather, “having gone beyond two stone-throws from the vicinity of the village and from the vicinity of the bhikkhus’ monastery”? Regarding this, some say: “For bhikkhus, it is permissible to perform that act in a village, having gone beyond the specified area, but for bhikkhunīs, it is not permissible in a village—hence it is stated thus.” Others, however, say: “For bhikkhus also it is not permissible in a village. A bhikkhu’s monastery is established already beyond the vicinity of a village; therefore, without mentioning the village, only the vicinity of the monastery is mentioned below. But a bhikkhunīs’ monastery is in the village itself, not outside; therefore, both the vicinity of the village and the vicinity of the monastery are shown here. Thus, in both cases, there is no difference in meaning.” Having investigated, whatever is logical here should be accepted.

Tato paṭṭhāyāti ārocitakālato paṭṭhāya.

“From that time onwards” means from the time of the announcement onwards.

Saṅghabhedakādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rules Regarding Causing a Schism in the Saṅgha, etc., is concluded.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the Explanation of the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the Elucidation of Subtle Meanings,

Bhikkhunipātimokkhe saṅghādisesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the Explanation of the Saṅghādisesa in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha is concluded.

Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Forfeiture

1. Pattavaggo

1. The Bowl Section

1. Pattasannicayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule concerning Accumulating Bowls

Paṭhamaṃ [M 0.0463][V 0.0428] uttānatthameva.

The first has an obvious meaning.

Pattasannicayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning the accumulation of bowls is concluded.

2. Akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Training Rule concerning Untimely Robes

Yaṃ attanā laddhaṃ, taṃ nissaggiyaṃ hotīti yaṃ cīvaraṃ bhājāpitāya attanā laddhaṃ, tameva nissaggiyaṃ hoti, taṃ vinayakammaṃ katvāpi attanā na labbhati. Tenāha “nissaṭṭha”ntiādi. Tattha nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvāpīti “ayyāya, dammī”ti evaṃ nissaṭṭhaṃ paṭilabhitvāpi. Yathādāneyeva upanetabbanti yathā dāyakehi dinnaṃ, tatheva upanetabbaṃ, akālacīvarapakkheyeva ṭhapetabbanti vuttaṃ hoti.

“What is obtained by oneself is subject to forfeiture” means that the robe which was obtained by oneself through allocation is precisely what is subject to forfeiture. Even after performing the disciplinary act, it is not obtained by oneself. Hence it is said, “relinquished,” and so on. Here, “even after receiving back what was relinquished” means receiving it back after having relinquished it, saying, “To the venerable lady, I give this.” “It should be brought forward just as it was given” means it should be brought forward just as it was given by the donors. It is said that it should be placed in the category of untimely robes.

Akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning untimely robes is concluded.

3. Cīvaraparivattanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Training Rule concerning the Exchange of Robes

Metanti me etaṃ. Sakasaññāya gahitattā pācittiyañceva dukkaṭañca vuttaṃ, itarathā bhaṇḍagghena kāretabbaṃ.

‘This is mine’ means ‘this is for me.’ Because it was taken with the perception that it was her own, both an offense of expiation and a wrong-doing are stated; otherwise, she should be made to pay its value.

Cīvaraparivattanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the exchange of robes is concluded.

4. Aññaviññāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Training Rule concerning Requesting Another Thing

Paṭilābhenāti [V 0.0429] paṭhamaviññattito ūnatarassāpi aññassa paṭilābhena.

By 'acquisition' is meant: by the acquisition of another thing, even if it is inferior to what was first requested.

Tasmiṃ appahonte puna taññevāti yaṃ paṭhamaṃ viññattaṃ, thokattā tasmiṃ appahonte puna taññeva viññāpentiyāti attho. Aññenapi atthe [M 0.0464] satī ti paṭhamaṃ viññattito aññenapi atthe sati. Tena saddhiṃ aññañcāti yaṃ paṭhamaṃ viññattaṃ, tena saddhiṃ aññañca. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Sace paṭhamaṃ sappi viññattaṃ, “yamakaṃ pacitabba”nti ca vejjena vuttattā telenāpi attho hoti. Tato “telenāpi me attho”ti evamādinā aññañca viññāpentiyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvāti “sace kahāpaṇassa sappi ābhataṃ hoti, iminā mūlena dviguṇaṃ telaṃ labbhati, telenāpi ca idaṃ kiccaṃ nippajjati, tasmā telaṃ āharā”ti evaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā.

When that is insufficient, she requests the same thing again—this means that when what was first requested is insufficient because it is too little, she requests that very same thing again. When there is another need—this means when there is another need besides what was first requested. Along with that, something else—this means along with what was first requested, something else. What is meant? If ghee was first requested, and because the physician said, 'A double portion should be cooked,' oil is also needed. Then, by saying, 'I also need oil,' and so on, she requests something else as well—this is what is meant. Having shown the advantage—this means, by showing the advantage thus: 'If a kahāpaṇa's worth of ghee is brought, with this price, double the amount of oil can be obtained, and this task can also be accomplished with oil; therefore, bring oil.'

Aññaviññāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning requesting another thing is concluded.

5. Aññacetāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Training Rule concerning Causing Another Thing to be Procured

Tato aññaṃ cetāpeyyāti paṭhamaṃ cetāpitato yaṃ kiñci aññaṃ cetāpeyya.

Then she may cause another to be procured—this means, whatever other thing she may cause to be procured after having first caused one to be procured.

Aññacetāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning causing another thing to be procured is concluded.

6. Paṭhamasaṅghikacetāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the First Training Rule concerning Causing Procurement with what Belongs to the Sangha

Aññassatthāya dinnenāti yaṃ cetāpeti, tato aññassatthāya dinnena. Aññuddisikenāti purimassevatthadīpanaṃ.

'By what was given for the sake of another' means: with what was given for a purpose other than that for which she causes something to be procured. 'With a different designation' is simply an explanation of the meaning of the former term.

Sesakaṃ upanentiyāti yadatthāya dinno, taṃ cetāpetvā avasesaṃ aññassatthāya upanentiyā. Sāmike apaloketvāti dāyake āpucchitvā. Evarūpāsū āpadāsu upanentīnanti evarūpesu upaddavesu aññassa yassa kassaci atthāya upanentīnaṃ.

She applies the remainder for another purpose—meaning, having caused that for which it was given to be procured, she applies the remainder for the sake of another. Having informed the owner—meaning, having asked the donor. In such emergencies, when applying it for another—meaning, in such calamities, when applying it for the sake of anyone whomsoever.

Paṭhamasaṅghikacetāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the first training rule concerning causing procurement with what belongs to the Sangha is concluded.

7. Dutiyasaṅghikacetāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Second Training Rule concerning Causing Procurement with what Belongs to the Sangha

Na [M 0.0465][V 0.0430] kevalaṃ teneva parikkhārenāti āha “sayaṃ yācitakenāpī”ti. Vuttañhetaṃ pāḷiyaṃ “bhikkhuniyo tena ca parikkhārena sayampi yācitvā bhesajjaṃ cetāpetvā paribhuñjiṃsū”ti (pāci. 763). Mātikāyaṃ pana gamyamānattā pi-saddo nappayutto. Gamyamānatthassa hi saddassa payogaṃ pati kāmacāroti yutti.

'Not only with that requisite'—thus it is said, 'even with what is requested by oneself.' For this is stated in the Pāḷi: 'The bhikkhunīs, with that requisite and having themselves requested, had medicine procured and used it' (Pāc. 763). However, in the Mātikā, the particle 'pi' is not used because it is understood. For regarding the use of a word whose meaning is understood, there is freedom of choice—this is the reasoning.

Dutiyasaṅghikacetāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the second training rule concerning causing procurement with what belongs to the Sangha is concluded.

8-9-10. Paṭhamagaṇikacetāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8-9-10. Explanation of the Training Rules concerning Causing Procurement for a Group, etc.

Aṭṭhamanavamadasamāni uttānatthāneva.

The eighth, ninth, and tenth have an obvious meaning.

Paṭhamagaṇikacetāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rules concerning causing procurement for a group, etc., is concluded.

Pattavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter: The Bowl Chapter.

2. Cīvaravaggo

2. The Robe Chapter

11. Garupāvuraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. Explanation of the Training Rule concerning a Heavy Cloak

Yasmā pavāritaṭṭhāne viññatti nāma na paṭisedhetabbā, tasmā bhagavā dhammanimantanavasena pavāritaṭṭhāne “vadethāyye, yenattho”ti (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.784) vuttāya catukkaṃsaparamaṃ viññāpetabbanti paricchedaṃ dassetīti veditabbaṃ. Teneva “cetāpetabbanti ṭhapetvā sahadhammike ca ñātakappavārite ca aññena kismiñcideva guṇe parituṭṭhena ‘vadethāyye, yenattho’ti vuttāya viññāpetabba”nti vuttaṃ. Rājānanti pasenadikosalarājānaṃ.

Because a request made in a situation of invitation should not be refused, it should be understood that the Blessed One, by way of a Dhamma invitation in an invited situation where it is said, 'Speak, venerable lady, what is your need?' (Sārattha. Ṭī. Pācittiya 3.784), shows the limit that one may request up to a maximum of four kaṃsas. For that reason it is said: 'Setting aside the general rule about procurement, one may make a request from fellow practitioners, from invited relatives, or from another person who, pleased by some quality, has said, 'Speak, venerable lady, what is your need?'' 'The king' means King Pasenadi of Kosala.

Garupāvuraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a heavy cloak is concluded.

12. Lahupāvuraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

12. Explanation of the Training Rule on a Light Cloak

Dutiyaṃ [M 0.0466][V 0.0431] uttānatthameva.

The second has an obvious meaning.

Lahupāvuraṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a light cloak is concluded.

Cīvaravaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter: The Robe Chapter.
