Thus in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the Explanation of the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the Elucidation of Subtle Meanings,

Bhikkhunipātimokkhe nissaggiyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the explanation of the Nissaggiya section in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha is concluded.

Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ

The Pācittiya Section

1. Lasuṇavaggo

1. The Chapter on Garlic

1. Lasuṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Garlic

“Lasuṇa”nti [M 0.0467][V 0.0432] kiñcāpi avisesena vuttaṃ, tathāpi magadhesu jātaṃ lasuṇameva idhādhippetaṃ, tampi bhaṇḍikalasuṇamevāti āha magadharaṭṭhe jāta”ntiādi.

Though 'garlic' is mentioned without distinction, nevertheless, only garlic grown in Magadha is intended here. And that too is only bhaṇḍika-garlic; therefore it is said, 'grown in the Magadha country,' etc.

Bhaṇḍikalasuṇanti poṭṭalikalasuṇameva, sampuṇṇamiñjānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tenāha “na ekadvitimiñjaka”nti. Ajjhohāre ajjhohāreti (pāci. aṭṭha. 795) ettha sace dve tayo bhaṇḍike ekatoyeva saṅkhāditvā ajjhoharati, ekaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Bhañjitvā ekekamiñjakaṃ khādantiyā pana payogagaṇanāya pācittiyāni.

Bhaṇḍika-garlic is simply poṭṭalika-garlic; this is a designation for those with full cloves. Therefore it is said, 'not with one or two cloves.' In the phrase 'swallowing, swallowing' (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 795), if one chews and swallows two or three bulbs together at once, one pācittiya offense is incurred. But for one who breaks them and eats each clove separately, there are pācittiya offenses counted according to the number of actions.

Palaṇḍukādīnaṃ vaṇṇena vā miñjāya vā nānāttaṃ veditabbaṃ – vaṇṇena tāva palaṇḍuko nāma paṇḍuvaṇṇo hoti, bhañjanako lohitavaṇṇo, haritako haritapaṇṇavaṇṇo. Miñjāya pana palaṇḍukassa ekā miñjā hoti, bhañjanakassa dve, haritakassa tisso. Cāpalasuṇo amiñjako. Aṅkuramattameva hi tassa hoti. Mahāpaccariyādīsu pana “palaṇḍukassa tīṇi miñjāni, bhañjanakassa dve, haritakassa eka”nti (pāci. aṭṭha. 797) vuttaṃ. Ete palaṇḍukādayo sabhāveneva vaṭṭanti. Sūpasampākādīsu pana māgadhakampi vaṭṭati. Tañhi paccamānesu muggasūpādīsu vā macchamaṃsavikatiyā vā tele vā badarasāḷavādīsu vā ambilasākādīsu vā uttaribhaṅgesu vā yattha katthaci antamaso yāgubhattepi pakkhittaṃ vaṭṭati. Badarasāḷavaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.793-797) nāma badaraphalāni sukkhāpetvā cuṇṇetvā kattabbā khādanīyavikati.

The differences among palaṇḍuka and others should be understood by color or by cloves. First, by color: the palaṇḍuka is pale in color, the bhañjanaka is reddish, and the haritaka is the color of green leaves. By cloves, the palaṇḍuka has one clove, the bhañjanaka has two, and the haritaka has three. The cāpalasuṇa has no cloves—it is merely a sprout. However, in the Mahāpaccariya and other texts, it is said: 'The palaṇḍuka has three cloves, the bhañjanaka has two, and the haritaka has one.' These palaṇḍuka and others are suitable by their own nature. But in soups and prepared dishes, the māgadhaka is also suitable. For when cooking mung bean soup, or in dishes of fish and meat, or in oil, or in preparations like badarasāḷava, or in sour greens, or in leftovers—wherever it is added, even in porridge or rice, it is suitable. Badarasāḷava refers to an edible preparation made by drying jujube fruits and grinding them into powder.

Lasuṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Garlic is concluded.

2. Sambādhalomasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Hair in Concealed Places

“Paṭicchannokāse”ti [M 0.0468][V 0.0433] etassa vibhāgadassanatthaṃ “upakacchakesu ca muttakaraṇe cāti attho”ti vuttaṃ.

To show the distinction of 'in a concealed place,' it is said that the meaning is 'in the armpits and at the genitals.'

Ābādhapaccayāti kaṇḍukacchuādiābādhapaccayā saṃharāpentiyā anāpatti. “Bhikkhussa ettha ca lasuṇe ca dukkaṭa”nti (vajira. ṭī. pācittiya 800) porāṇā.

Due to illness as a condition: There is no offense for one who has hair removed due to an illness caused by conditions like itching, scabies, and so on. The ancients say, 'For a monk, there is a dukkaṭa offense concerning both this matter and garlic' (Vajiraṭīkā, Pācittiya 800).

Sambādhalomasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Hair in Concealed Places is concluded.

3. Talaghātakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Blow with the Palm

Talaghātaketi matthake pahāradāne, tañca kho talaṃ “muttakaraṇe pahāraṃ detī”ti (pāci. 804) padabhājaniyaṃvuttattā “muttakaraṇassā”ti viññāyatīti āha “muttakaraṇassa talaghātane”ti. Purimanayeneva sāṇattikanti attano atthāya aññaṃ āṇāpentiyā sāṇattikaṃ.

Regarding 'a blow with the palm': this can mean giving a blow on the head. But since in the word analysis (Pāc. 804) it is said, 'she gives a blow on the genitals,' it is understood as 'of the genitals.' Therefore, it is said, 'in striking the genitals.' By the same method as before, an offense by command is incurred by one who, for her own sake, commands another.

Talaghātakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Blow with the Palm is concluded.

4. Jatumaṭṭhakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Lac-and-Wood Implement

Vatthuvasenetaṃ vuttanti “jatumaṭṭhake”ti etaṃ nidānavasena uppannassa vatthuno vaseneva vuttaṃ. Yaṃ kiñci pana daṇḍakaṃ pavesentiyā āpattiyeva. Tenāha “kāmarāgena panā”tiādi.

This is stated by way of the subject matter: the phrase 'regarding the lac-and-wood implement' is stated only with reference to the subject matter that arose from the origin story. However, for one who inserts any kind of rod, there is an offense. Therefore, it is said, 'but through sensual desire,' etc.

Jatumaṭṭhakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Lac-and-Wood Implement is concluded.

5. Udakasuddhikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Water Purification

Ādātabbanti pavesetabbaṃ. Aggapabbanti kesaggamattampi aggapabbaṃ. Tatiyaṃ pabbaṃ pavesetīti kesaggamattampi tatiyaṃ pabbaṃ paveseti. Vuttañhetaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 812) “gambhīrato dvinnaṃ pabbānaṃ upari kesaggamattampi pavesentiyā pācittiya”nti.

‘To be used’ means ‘to be inserted.’ ‘The tip-joint’ means even a hair-tip's measure is the tip-joint. ‘She inserts the third joint’ means she inserts even a hair-tip's measure of the third joint. This is stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 812): 'A pācittiya offense is incurred for inserting even a hair-tip's measure beyond the depth of two joints.'

Atigambhīraṃ [M 0.0469][V 0.0434] udakasuddhikaṃ ādiyanavatthusminti atianto pavesetvā udakadhovanakaraṇavatthusmiṃ. Udakasuddhipaccayena (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.812) pana satipi phassassādiyane yathāvuttaparicchede anāpatti.

Regarding 'in the case of using a water-purifier too deeply': this means in the case of inserting it too far inside for the purpose of washing with water. But even if there is enjoyment of contact due to the need for water purification (Sāratthadīpanī, Pācittiya 3.812), there is no offense within the stated limits.

Udakasuddhikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Water Purification is concluded.

6. Upatiṭṭhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Attendance

Takkādīsu vā aññatarenāti takkadadhimatthurasakhīrādīsu aññatarena. Yāya kāyaci bījaniyāti antamaso cīvarakaṇṇaṃ upādāya yāya kāyaci bījaniyā.

Regarding 'among buttermilk and so forth, or by any other means': this means by any of buttermilk, curds, whey, juice, milk, and so forth. Regarding 'by any fan whatsoever': this means by any fan whatsoever, up to and including the corner of one’s robe.

Imaṃ pivathāti imaṃ pānīyaṃ vā sūpādiṃ vā pivatha. Iminā bījathāti iminā tālavaṇṭena bījatha. Dāpentiyāti aññena ubhayampi dāpentiyā.

‘Drink this’: this means drink this beverage or soup and so forth. ‘Fan with this’: this means fan with this palm-leaf fan. ‘Causing to be given’: this means causing another person to give both.

Upatiṭṭhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Attendance is concluded.

7. Āmakadhaññasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Raw Grain

Tasmāti yasmā viññatti ceva bhojanañca pamāṇaṃ, tasmā. Na kevalañcettha paṭiggahaṇeyeva dukkaṭaṃ hoti, paṭiggaṇhitvā pana araññato āharaṇepi sukkhāpanepi vaddalidivase bhajjanatthāya uddhanasajjanepi kapallasajjanepi dabbisajjanepi dārūni ādāya aggikaraṇepi kapallamhi dhaññapakkhipanepi dabbiyā saṅghaṭṭanesupi koṭṭanatthaṃ udukkhalamusalādisajjanesupi koṭṭanapapphoṭanadhovanādīsupi yāva mukhe ṭhapetvā ajjhoharaṇatthaṃ dantehi saṅkhādati, tāva sabbappayogesu dukkaṭānīti āha “paṭiggahaṇato paṭṭhāya yāva dantehi saṃkhādanaṃ, tāva pubbappayogesu dukkaṭānī”ti.

‘Therefore’: because both the request and the eating are the measure, therefore. Not only is there a dukkaṭa offense in the act of receiving here, but also after receiving, when bringing it from the forest, when drying it, on a rainy day, for the purpose of roasting, when preparing the hearth, when preparing the pan, when preparing the ladle, when taking firewood to make a fire, when putting grain in the pan, when stirring with the ladle, when preparing the mortar and pestle for pounding, when pounding, winnowing, washing, and so on—up to placing it in the mouth and chewing it with the teeth for the purpose of swallowing—in all these preparatory actions, there are dukkaṭa offenses. Thus it is said: 'From the act of receiving up to chewing with the teeth, in all the preceding actions, there are dukkaṭa offenses.'

Āmakadhaññasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Raw Grain is concluded.

8. Paṭhamauccārachaḍḍanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the First Training Rule on Discarding Excrement

Tirokuṭṭeti [M 0.0470][V 0.0435] gharakuṭṭassa parabhāge. Tiropākāreti parikkhepapākārassa tirobhāge, te ca kho kuṭṭapākārā iṭṭhakasiladārūnaṃ vasena tippakārāti āha “yassa kassaci kuṭṭassa vā pākārassa vā parato”ti. Sabbānipetāni ekato chaḍḍentiyāti etāni cattāripi vatthūni ekato chaḍḍentiyā. Pāṭekkaṃ pana chaḍḍentiyā vatthugaṇanāya āpattiyo. Āṇattiyampi eseva nayo.

‘Beyond the wall’: this means on the outer side of the house wall. ‘Beyond the enclosure wall’: this means on the outer side of the surrounding wall. And those walls and enclosure walls are of three kinds, being made of brick, stone, or wood; hence it is said, ‘beyond anyone’s wall or enclosure wall.’ Regarding ‘when she discards all these together’: this means for one who discards these four things together. But for one who discards them one by one, offenses are reckoned according to the number of things. The same principle applies to a command.

Bhikkhussa dukkaṭanti bhikkhussa sabbattha dukkaṭaṃ.

‘For a monk, a dukkaṭa offense’: this means for a monk, there is a dukkaṭa offense in every case.

Paṭhamauccārachaḍḍanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the first training rule on discarding excrement is completed.

9. Dutiyauccārachaḍḍanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Second Training Rule on Discarding Excrement

Bhikkhuniyāpīti pi-saddena bhikkhuṃ samuccinoti. Anikkhittabījesu (pāci. aṭṭha. 830) pana khettesu koṇādīsu vā asañjātaropimesu khettamariyādādīsu vā chaḍḍetuṃ vaṭṭati. Manussānaṃ kacavarachaḍḍanaṭṭhānepi vaṭṭatiyeva. Chaḍḍitakhetteti manussesu sassaṃ uddharitvā gatesu chaḍḍitakhettaṃ nāma hoti, tattha vaṭṭati. Yattha pana “lāyitampi pubbaṇṇādi puna uṭṭhahissatī”ti rakkhanti, tattha yathāvatthukameva. Sāmike apaloketvāti ettha khettapālakā, ārāmādigopakā ca sāmikāva. Iminā ca saṅghasantake bhikkhussa chaḍḍetuṃ vaṭṭati saṅghapariyāpannattā, na bhikkhunīnaṃ. Bhikkhunīnaṃ pana attano santake bhikkhusantake vuttanayeneva vaṭṭatīti dasseti, evaṃ santepi sāruppavasena kātabbaṃ.

'Even for a bhikkhunī': by the word 'pi' (even), a bhikkhu is included. However, in fields where seeds have not been scattered (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 830), such as in corners and so forth, or in places where sprouts have not grown, or on field boundaries and so forth, it is permissible to discard. It is also permissible in places where people discard rubbish and refuse. 'In an abandoned field': when people have harvested the grain and left, it is called an abandoned field; there, it is permissible. But where they guard it, thinking, 'Even what has been reaped, like early grain, will sprout again,' there, it must be done according to the actual situation. 'Having informed the owner': here, field keepers, monastery keepers, and so forth are themselves the owners. By this, it is shown that it is permissible for a bhikkhu to discard on Sangha property, because he is included in the Sangha, but not for bhikkhunīs. For bhikkhunīs, however, it is permissible on their own property or on a bhikkhu’s property, in the manner explained. Even so, it should be done in a suitable manner.

Dutiyauccārachaḍḍanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the second training rule on discarding excrement is completed.

10. Naccagītasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Training Rule on Dancing and Singing

Naccanti naṭādayo vā naccantu, soṇḍā vā antamaso morasuvamakkaṭādayopi, sabbametaṃ naccameva. Tenāha “naccanti antamaso moranaccampī”ti[M 0.0471]. Gītanti naṭādīnaṃ vā gītaṃ hotu, ariyānaṃ parinibbānakāle ratanattayaguṇūpasaṃhitaṃ sādhukīḷitagītaṃ vā, antamaso “dantagītampi [V 0.0436] gāyissāmā”ti pubbabhāge okūjantā karonti, sabbametaṃ gītameva. Tenāha “gītanti antamaso dhammabhāṇakagītampī”ti. Tattha dhammabhāṇakagītaṃ nāma asaññatabhikkhūnaṃ taṃ taṃ vattaṃ bhinditvā atidīghaṃ katvā gītassarena dhammabhaṇanaṃ, tampi neva bhikkhuno, na bhikkhunīnaṃ vaṭṭati. Tathā hi vuttaṃ paramatthajotikāya khuddakaṭṭhakathāya (khu. pā. aṭṭha. 2.pacchimapañcasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ gītaṃ vaṭṭati, gītūpasaṃhito pana dhammo na vaṭṭatī”ti. Tasmā dhammaṃ bhaṇantena jātakavattādiṃ taṃ taṃ vattaṃ avināsetvā caturassena (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 249) vattena parimaṇḍalāni padabyañjanāni dassetabbāni. Vāditanti tantibaddhādivādanīyabhaṇḍavāditaṃ vā hotu, kuṭabherivāditaṃ vā antamaso udakabherivāditampi, sabbamevetaṃ vāditameva. Tenāha “vāditanti antamaso udakabherivādita”nti. Yaṃ pana niṭṭhubhantī vā sāsaṅke vā ṭhitā accharikaṃ vā phoṭeti, pāṇiṃ vā paharati, tattha anāpatti. Dassanena cettha savanampi saṅgahitaṃ virūpekasesanayena. Ālocanasabhāvatāya vā pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ savanakiriyāyapi dassanasaṅkhepasabbhāvato “dassanāya”icceva vuttanti āha “etesu yaṃ kiñci dassanāya gacchantiyā”ti. Yattha ṭhitāti evaṃ gantvā yasmiṃ padese ṭhitā.

'Dancing': let actors and so forth dance, or drunkards, or even down to peacocks, parrots, monkeys, and so forth—all this is dancing. Hence it is said: 'They dance, even the dance of a peacock.' 'Singing': let it be the singing of actors and so forth, or a well-sung song connected with the qualities of the Triple Gem at the time of the final passing of the noble ones, or even what some do, croaking in the first part, thinking, 'We will sing a tooth-song'—all this is singing. Hence it is said: 'They sing, even the singing of Dhamma reciters.' Here, the singing of Dhamma reciters refers to unrestrained bhikkhus breaking this or that recitation style, making it very long, and reciting the Dhamma with a singing tone; this is not proper for a bhikkhu or a bhikkhunī. For it is stated in the Paramatthajotikā, the commentary on the Khuddakapāṭha (Khu. Pā. Aṭṭha. 2, Pacchimapañcasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā): 'Singing connected with the Dhamma is permissible, but the Dhamma connected with singing is not permissible.' Therefore, when reciting the Dhamma, without destroying the respective styles for Jātaka recitation and so forth, one should present well-rounded words and syllables in a balanced style. 'Instrumental music': let it be the playing of instruments such as those with strings, or the beating of pot-drums, or even down to the playing of a water-drum—all this is instrumental music. Hence it is said: 'They play, even the playing of a water-drum.' However, when one spits, or stands in suspense, or snaps one's fingers, or claps one's hands, there is no offense. Here, hearing is also included with seeing by way of the method of the dissimilar remainder. Alternatively, because of the nature of initial cognition, the act of hearing is also included under the summary term 'seeing' for the five consciousnesses. Hence it is said, 'of one going to see any of these.' 'Where she stands' means: having gone thus, in which place she stands.

Nanu ca sayaṃnaccanādīsu pācittiyaṃ pāḷiyaṃ na vuttaṃ, atha kathaṃ gahetabbanti āha “sabbaaṭṭhakathāsu vutta”nti, iminā pāḷiyaṃ avuttepi aṭṭhakathāpamāṇena gahetabbanti dasseti. Samuṭṭhānādīni eḷakalomasadisānīti pana mātikāgatapācittiyasseva vasena vuttaṃ, sabbesaṃ vasena pana chasamuṭṭhānanti gahetabbaṃ. “Ārāme ṭhatvā”ti idaṃ nidassanamattaṃ sesairiyāpathehi yuttāya passantiyā anāpattiyā icchitabbattā. Itarathā hi nisinnāpi passituṃ na labheyya. “Passissāmī”ti vihārato vihāraṃ gacchantiyā āpattiyeva. Āsanasālāya nisinnā passati, anāpatti, “passissāmī”ti uṭṭhahitvā gacchantiyā āpatti. Vīthiyaṃ ṭhatvā gīvaṃ parivattetvā passantiyāpi āpattiyeva. Bhikkhussāpi eseva nayo, āpattibhedova nānaṃ.

But is it not so that in the Pāḷi, a pācittiya offense is not mentioned for dancing oneself and so forth? So how is it to be understood? He says, 'It is stated in all the commentaries.' By this, he shows that even if it is not stated in the Pāḷi, it should be accepted on the authority of the commentaries. However, that the origins and so forth are like a ram's fleece is stated only with reference to the pācittiya that has come in the matrix. But with reference to all of them, it should be understood that there are six origins. 'Standing in the monastery': this is merely an illustration, because it is intended that there is no offense for one who sees while engaged in the other postures. Otherwise, even if seated, she would not be able to see. For one who goes from monastery to monastery, thinking, 'I will see,' there is an offense. If she is seated in a hall and sees, there is no offense; for one who gets up and goes, thinking, 'I will see,' there is an offense. For one who stands in the street and turns her neck to see, there is also an offense. This is the same principle for a bhikkhu; only the type of offense is different.

Naccagītasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on dancing and singing is completed.

Lasuṇavaggo paṭhamo.

The Section on Garlic, the First.

2. Rattandhakāravaggo

2. The Chapter on the Darkness of Night

1. Rattandhakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on the Darkness of Night

Arahopekkhāyāti [M 0.0472][V 0.0437] narahoassādāpekkhāya. Aññavihitāyāti rahoassādato aññavihitāva hutvā ñātiṃ vā pucchantiyā, dāne vā pūjāya vā mantentiyā.

'Without expectation of privacy' means without expectation of the pleasure of privacy. 'Otherwise engaged' means being engaged otherwise than with the pleasure of privacy, such as when asking about relatives, or discussing gifts or offerings.

Rattandhakārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on the darkness of night is completed.

2-3. Paṭicchannokāsaajjhokāsasallapanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2-3. Explanation of the Training Rule on Conversation in Concealed and Open-Air Places

Dutiyatatiyāni uttānatthāneva.

The second and third are of obvious meaning.

Paṭicchannokāsaajjhokāsasallapanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on conversation in concealed and open-air places is completed.

4. Dutiyikauyyojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Training Rule on Dismissing a Companion

“Purimanayenevā”ti iminā “santiṭṭheyya vāti hatthapāse ṭhitamattāya pācittiyaṃ, sallapeyya vāti tattha ṭhatvā gehasikakathaṃ kathentiyāpi pācittiyameva, nikaṇṇikaṃ vā jappeyyāti kaṇṇamūle jappentiyāpi pācittiyamevā”ti imaṃ nayaṃ dasseti.

By 'in the previous manner,' he indicates this principle: 'Or if she should stand near: merely by standing within arm's reach, it is a pācittiya offense. Or if she should converse: even by standing there and speaking household talk, it is a pācittiya offense. Or if she should whisper in the ear: even by whispering at the base of the ear, it is a pācittiya offense.'

Dutiyikauyyojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on dismissing a companion is completed.

5. Anāpucchāpakkamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The explanation of the training rule on departing without asking permission.

Āsīdanti etthāti āsananti āha “pallaṅkassokāsabhūte”ti, ūrubaddhāsanassa okāseti attho. Anovassakanti nibbakokāsaṃ. Ajjhokāse upacāranti ajjhokāse nisīditvā dvādasahatthappamāṇaṃ padesaṃ. Gilānāyāti yā tādisena gelaññena āpucchituṃ na sakkoti[V 0.0438]. Āpadāsūti ghare aggi vā uṭṭhito hoti, coro vā, evarūpe upaddave anāpucchā pakkamati, anāpatti.

'They sit here, thus it is a seat': he says, 'in a place that is a space for a couch,' meaning the space for a seat with legs crossed. 'Not rained upon' means a place without a roof. 'In the precincts in the open air' means, having sat in the open air, a region measuring twelve cubits. 'For one who is sick' means one who is unable to ask permission due to such an illness. 'In emergencies' means when a fire has broken out in the house, or a thief is present; in such a calamity, if she departs without asking, there is no offense.

Anāpucchāpakkamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on departing without asking permission is completed.

6. Anāpucchāabhinisīdanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The explanation of the training rule on sitting down without asking permission.

Dhuvapaññatteti [M 0.0473] bhikkhunīnaṃ atthāya niccapaññatte.

'In the permanent regulation' means in the regulation perpetually established for the sake of the bhikkhunīs.

Anāpucchāabhinisīdanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on sitting down without asking permission is completed.

7. Anāpucchāsantharaṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The explanation of the training rule on spreading out a sitting cloth without asking permission.

Kulānīti kulassa gharāni.

'Families' means the houses of a family.

Anāpucchāsantharaṇasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on spreading out a sitting cloth without permission is completed.

8. Paraujjhāpanakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The explanation of the training rule on causing another to complain.

Aṭṭhamaṃ uttānatthameva.

The eighth is of obvious meaning.

Paraujjhāpanakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule on causing another to reproach is concluded.

9. Paraabhisapanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The commentary on the training rule concerning cursing another.

Manussadobhaggena vāti “kāṇā homi, kuṇī homi, itarā vā īdisā hotū”tiādinā manussavirūpabhāvena. Atthadhammaanusāsanipurekkhārānanti ettha atthapurekkhārāyāti aṭṭhakathaṃ kathentiyā. Dhammapurekkhārāyāti pāḷiṃ vācentiyā. Anusāsanipurekkhārāyāti “idānipi tvaṃ edisā, sādhu viramassu, no ce viramasi, addhā puna [V 0.0439] evarūpāni kammāni katvā niraye uppajjissasi, tiracchānayoniyā uppajjissasī”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 878) evaṃ anusāsaniyaṃ ṭhatvā vadantiyā.

“Or by human misfortune” means by human deformity, such as with the words, “May I be one-eyed, may I be crooked-limbed, or may another become like this,” and so on. Herein, regarding “with meaning, Dhamma, or instruction as the foremost consideration”: “with meaning as the foremost consideration” refers to one who is explaining the commentary. “With Dhamma as the foremost consideration” refers to one who is reciting the Pāli. “With instruction as the foremost consideration” refers to one who speaks while established in what should be instructed, saying, “Even now you are like this; it is good that you refrain. If you do not refrain, surely, having done such deeds again, you will be reborn in hell, you will be reborn in the animal realm” (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 878).

Paraabhisapanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning cursing another is concluded.

10. Rodanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The commentary on the training rule concerning weeping.

Dasamaṃ uttānatthameva.

The tenth is just clear in meaning.

Rodanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning weeping is concluded.

Rattandhakāravaggo dutiyo.

The second chapter: the Chapter on Night Darkness.

3. Naggavaggo

3. The Chapter on the Naked

1-2. Naggādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1-2. The commentary on the training rules beginning with the naked.

Idanti [M 0.0474] idaṃ udakasāṭikacīvaraṃ.

‘This’ means this bathing-cloth robe.

Dutiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

The second is just clear in meaning.

Naggādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rules beginning with the naked is concluded.

3. Cīvarasibbanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The commentary on the training rule concerning robe-sewing.

Visibbetvāti vijaṭetvā. Dhuraṃ nikkhittamatteti dhure nikkhittamatte, dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā sacepi pacchā sibbati, āpattiyevāti attho.

‘Having unsewn’ means having unstitched. ‘Just when the task is set down’ means when the task has just been set down; the meaning is that even if one sews afterwards, having set down the task, it is indeed an offense.

Cīvarasibbanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning robe-sewing is concluded.

4. Saṅghāṭicārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The commentary on the training rule concerning wandering with the outer robe (saṅghāṭi).

“Idaṃ [V 0.0440] me cīvaraṃ mahagghaṃ īdise corabhaye na sakkā dhāretunti evarūpāsu āpadāsū”ti ettha pāṭho. So pana kākapadasañjanitamohehi lekhakehi uparisikkhāpade likhito. Kiñcāpi tattha likhito, ettheva pana daṭṭhabbo.

The reading here is: ‘This robe of mine is valuable; it cannot be worn in such danger from thieves,’ and ‘in such calamities.’ But this was written by scribes, confused by crow’s-foot marks, in the preceding training rule. Although it is written there, it should be understood here.

Saṅghāṭicārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning wandering with the outer robe (saṅghāṭi) is concluded.

5. Cīvarasaṅkamanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The commentary on the training rule concerning exchanging robes.

Āpadāsu vā dhāretīti sace apārutaṃ vā anivatthaṃ vā corā haranti, evarūpāsū āpadāsu dhāreti, anāpatti.

‘Or she may keep it in emergencies’ means: if thieves take it when it is uncovered or not being worn, in such emergencies she may keep it; there is no offense.

Cīvarasaṅkamanīyasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning exchanging robes is concluded.

6. Gaṇacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The commentary on the training rule concerning a community robe.

Aññasmiṃ parikkhāreti yattha katthaci thālakādīnaṃ vā sappitelādīnaṃ vā aññatarasmiṃ. “Samagghakāle dassathā”ti evaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā nivārentiyāti [M 0.0475] “kittakaṃ agghanakaṃ dātukāmatthā”ti pucchitvā (pāci. aṭṭha. 909) “ettakaṃ nāmā”ti vutte “āgametha tāva, idāni vatthaṃ mahagghaṃ, katipāhena kappāse āhaṭe samagghaṃ bhavissati, tasmiṃ kāle dassathā”ti evaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā nivārentiyā.

‘She stores it elsewhere’ means in any place whatsoever among bowls and so on, or ghee, oil, and so on. ‘By showing the benefit and preventing it, saying, “You should give it when the price is fair”’ refers to one who, having asked, “What price are you willing to give?” (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 909) and having been told, “So much,” prevents it by showing the benefit in this way: “Wait a while. Right now, cloth is expensive. In a few days, when cotton has been brought, it will be of fair price. At that time, you should give it.”

Gaṇacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning a community robe is concluded.

7-10. Paṭibāhanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7–10. The commentary on the training rules beginning with obstruction.

Ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā paṭibāhantiyāti “ekissā ekaṃ sāṭakaṃ nappahoti, āgametha tāva, katipāhena uppajjissati, tato bhājessāmā”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 915) evaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā paṭibāhantiyā anāpatti.

For one who obstructs by showing the benefit, saying, ‘One cloth is not enough for one nun. Wait a while; in a few days more will arise, then we will distribute them’ (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 915)—for one who obstructs by showing the benefit in this way, there is no offense.

Aṭṭhamanavamāni [V 0.0441] uttānatthāneva.

The eighth and ninth are just clear in meaning.

Sesanti “dhammike vematikāyā”tiādikaṃ avasesaṃ. Tattha ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā paṭibāhantiyāti “bhikkhunisaṅgho jiṇṇacīvaro, kathinānisaṃsamūlako mahālābho”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 931) evarūpaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā paṭibāhantiyā anāpatti.

‘The rest’ means the remainder, beginning with ‘being in doubt about what is lawful.’ Therein, for one who obstructs by showing a benefit, such as, ‘The community of nuns has worn-out robes; the great gain is rooted in the benefit of the kathina’ (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 931)—for one who obstructs by showing such a benefit, there is no offense.

Paṭibāhanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rules beginning with obstruction is concluded.

Naggavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on the Naked.

4. Tuvaṭṭavaggo

4. The Chapter on Turning Over.

1-3. Ekamañcatuvaṭṭanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1–3. The Explanation of the Training Rules Beginning with Turning on a Single Couch.

Paṭhamaṃ uttānatthameva.

The first is clear in meaning.

Vavatthānaṃ dassetvāti (pāci. aṭṭha. 940) majjhe kāsāyaṃ vā kattarayaṭṭhiṃ vā antamaso kāyabandhanampi ṭhapetvā nipajjantīnaṃ anāpattīti attho.

‘Having shown a boundary’ means placing an ochre cloth or a small stick in the middle, or even just a waistband, then lying down—there is no offense.

Tatiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

The third is clear in meaning.

Ekamañcatuvaṭṭanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rules Beginning with Turning on a Single Couch is concluded.

4-9. Naupaṭṭhāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4–9. The Explanation of the Training Rules Beginning with Non-Attendance.

Pariyesitvā [M 0.0476] alabhantiyāti aññaṃ upaṭṭhāyikaṃ alabhantiyā. Gilānāyāti sayaṃ gilānāya. Āpadāsūti tathārūpe upaddave sati.

‘Having searched but not obtaining’ means not obtaining another attendant. ‘For the sick’ means being sick herself. ‘In emergencies’ means when such a misfortune occurs.

Pañcamachaṭṭhasattama [V 0.0442] aṭṭhamanavamāni uttānatthāneva.

The fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth are clear in meaning.

Naupaṭṭhāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rules Beginning with Non-Attendance is concluded.

10. Cārikanapakkamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Departing on a Journey.

Dhure nikkhittamatteti sace dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā pacchā pakkamati, āpattiyevāti attho. Antarāye satīti dasavidhesu antarāyesu aññatarasmiṃ sati. “Gacchissāmī”ti nikkhantā, nadī vā pūrā, vanadāho vā āgato, corā vā magge honti, megho vā uṭṭhahati, nivattituṃ vaṭṭati.

‘Just having set down the burden’ means if, having set down the burden, she afterwards departs, there is an offense. ‘When there is an obstacle’ means when any of the ten kinds of obstacles is present. Having set out thinking, ‘I will go,’ but the river is full, a forest fire has come, bandits are on the road, or a cloud has arisen—it is proper to turn back.

Cārikanapakkamanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Departing on a Journey is concluded.

Tuvaṭṭavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter on Turning Over.

5. Cittāgāravaggo

5. The Chapter on the Picture Hall.

1. Rājāgārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Royal Residences.

Kīḷanacittasālanti na raññova kīḷanacittasālaṃ, atha kho yesaṃ kesañci manussānaṃ kīḷanatthaṃ yattha katthaci katasālaṃ. Esa nayo “kīḷanaupavana”ntiādīsupi. Yathāha “rājāgāraṃ nāma yattha katthaci rañño kīḷituṃ ramituṃ kataṃ hotī”tiādiko (pāci. 979) vitthāro. Tattha kīḷanaupavananti kīḷanatthaṃ antonagare kataṃ ārāmaṃ. Kīḷanuyyānanti tatheva bahinagare kataṃ uyyānaṃ.

‘Pleasure picture-hall’ does not mean only a pleasure picture-hall of the king, but any hall built anywhere for the amusement of any people whatsoever. The same principle applies to terms like ‘pleasure grove,’ etc. As it is said: ‘A royal residence is a place made anywhere for the king to play and enjoy himself,’ and so on (Pāc. 979) in the detailed explanation. Here, ‘pleasure grove’ means a park built within the city for amusement. ‘Pleasure garden’ similarly means a garden built outside the city.

Rājāgārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Royal Residences is concluded.

2. Āsandiparibhuñjanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Using High Seats.

Atikkantappamāṇāti [M 0.0477][V 0.0443] aṭṭhaṅgulato atikkantappamāṇapādakā. Vuttoti padabhājaniyaṃ vutto. “Akappiyarūpākulo akappiyamañco pallaṅko”ti (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.254) sārasamāsācariyo.

‘Exceeding the measure’ means having feet exceeding the measure of eight fingerbreadths. ‘It is said’ refers to what is stated in the word analysis. ‘Unsuitable in appearance, an unsuitable bed or couch,’ as the teacher of the Sārasamāsa says (Sāratthaṭīkā, Mahāvagga 3.254).

Āsandiparibhuñjanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Using High Seats is concluded.

3. Suttakantanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Spinning Thread.

Ujjavujjaveti uggiritvā uggiritvā veṭhane. Kantitasuttaṃ kantantiyāti dasikasuttādiṃ saṅghāṭetvā kantantiyā, dukkantitaṃ vā paṭikantantiyā.

‘Ujjavujjaveti’ means repeatedly drawing up for winding. ‘Spinning spun thread’ means spinning by joining a ten-thread cord and the like, or by re-spinning badly spun thread.

Suttakantanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Spinning Thread is concluded.

4. Gihiveyyāvaccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Service to Householders.

Attano veyyāvaccakarassa cāti sacepi mātāpitaro āgacchanti, yaṃ kiñci bījaniṃ vā sammuñjanidaṇḍakaṃ vā kārāpetvā veyyāvaccakaraṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā yaṃ kiñci vā pacituṃ vaṭṭati.

‘And for one's own attendant’: even if her parents arrive, having had a fan or a broomstick made and placed in the attendant’s place, it is permissible to cook anything.

Gihiveyyāvaccasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule on Service to Householders is concluded.

5-6. Adhikaraṇādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5–6. The Explanation of the Training Rules Beginning with Legal Disputes.

Anantarāyikinīti dasavidhesu antarāyesu ekenāpi anantarāyikinī. Dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā pacchā vinicchinantī āpattiṃ āpajjitvāva vinicchināti.

‘Unhindered’ means not hindered by even one of the ten kinds of hindrances. Deciding afterward, having laid down the responsibility, she decides only after incurring an offense.

Chaṭṭhaṃ uttānatthameva.

The sixth is simply clear in meaning.

Adhikaraṇādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rules on legal disputes and so forth is concluded.

7. Āvasathacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Robe for a Lodging

Āpadāsūti [M 0.0478][V 0.0444] mahagghacīvaraṃ sarīrato mocetvā suppaṭisāmitampi corā haranti, evarūpāsu āpadāsu anissajjitvā nivāsentiyā anāpatti.

In times of danger: when thieves take even a valuable robe that has been removed from the body and stored away well. In such dangers, there is no offense for one who wears it without having relinquished it.

Āvasathacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a robe for a lodging is concluded.

8. Āvasathavihārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Dwelling Used as a Lodging

Kavāṭabaddhavihāranti dvārabaddhavihāraṃ. Gilānāyāti vacībhedaṃ kātuṃ asamatthāya. Āpadāsūti raṭṭhe bhijjante āvāse chaḍḍetvā gacchanti, evarūpāsu āpadāsu.

'A dwelling with a fastened door' means a dwelling with a closed door. 'For the sick one' means for one unable to articulate. 'In times of danger' means when the kingdom is disintegrating, they abandon their dwellings and leave; in such dangers.

Āvasathavihārasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a dwelling used as a lodging is concluded.

9. Tiracchānavijjāpariyāpuṇanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Learning Low Arts

Hatthiādīsupi (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.1015) sippasaddo paccekaṃ yojetabbo, tathā āthabbaṇādīsu mantasaddo. Tattha tharūti khaggamuṭṭhi. Āthabbaṇamanto nāma āthabbaṇavedavihito parūpaghātakaro manto. Khilanamanto nāma dārusārakhilaṃ mantetvā pathaviyaṃ pavesetvā māraṇamanto. Agadappayogo nāma visayojanaṃ.

In regard to elephants and so forth, the word 'skill' should be applied to each individually; similarly, in regard to the Atharva Veda and so forth, the word 'mantra'. Therein, 'tharu' means a sword hilt. The 'Atharvan mantra' is a mantra prescribed in the Atharva Veda that causes harm to others. The 'khilana mantra' is a mantra for killing, recited after enchanting a peg of hardwood and driving it into the ground. 'Agada application' means the application of poison.

Tiracchānavijjāpariyāpuṇanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on learning low arts is concluded.

10. Tiracchānavijjāvācanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Teaching Low Arts

Lekheti likhasippe. Dhāraṇāya vāti dhāraṇasatthe, yasmiṃ vuttanayena paṭipajjantā bahūnipi ganthāni dhārenti. Nāgamaṇḍalādiketi ettha nāgamaṇḍalaṃ nāma sappānaṃ pavesanivāraṇatthaṃ maṇḍalabaddhamanto.

'In writing' means in the skill of writing. 'Or for retention' means in the science of retention, by which, practicing in the prescribed manner, they retain many texts. 'In the nāgamaṇḍala, etc.'—here, 'nāgamaṇḍala' is a mantra arranged in a circle for the purpose of preventing snakes from entering.

Tiracchānavijjāvācanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on teaching low arts is concluded.

Cittāgāravaggo pañcamo.

The Cittāgāra Chapter is the fifth.

6. Ārāmavaggo

6. The Ārāma Chapter

1-2. Ārāmapavisanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1-2. The Explanation of the Training Rules on Entering a Monastery and so forth

Sīsānulokikāyāti [M 0.0479][V 0.0445] sīsaṃ anulokentiyā. Yattha vā bhikkhuniyo sannipatitāti yattha bhikkhuniyo paṭhamataraṃ sajjhāyanacetiyavandanādiatthaṃ sannipatitā. Āpadāsūti kenaci upaddutā hoti, evarūpāsu āpadāsu pavisituṃ vaṭṭati.

'For one looking around with her head' means for one looking around with her head. 'Or where nuns have gathered' means where nuns have first assembled for the purpose of recitation, veneration of shrines, and so forth. 'In times of danger' means when she is assailed by someone; in such dangers, it is permissible to enter.

Dutiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

The second is simply clear in meaning.

Ārāmapavisanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rules on entering a monastery and so forth is concluded.

3-4. Gaṇaparibhāsanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3-4. The Explanation of the Training Rules on Disparaging a Group and so forth

Sesanti “atthadhammaanusāsanipurekkhārāyā”tiādikaṃ avasesaṃ. Tattha anusāsanipurekkhārāyāti “idānipi tvaṃ bālā abyattā”tiādinā (pāci. aṭṭha. 1036) nayena anusāsanipakkhe ṭhatvā vadantiyā anāpatti.

'The remainder' means the remaining part beginning with 'for the sake of instruction in the goal and the Dhamma.' Therein, 'for the sake of instruction' means there is no offense for one who speaks while standing on the side of instruction, in the manner of saying, 'Even now you are foolish and unskilled,' and so on.

Catutthaṃ uttānatthameva.

The fourth is simply clear in meaning.

Gaṇaparibhāsanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rules on disparaging a group and so forth is concluded.

5. Kulamaccharinīsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

5. The Explanation of the Training Rule on a Nun Miserly Toward a Family

Kule maccharo kulamaccharoti purimasmiṃ pakkhe sakatthe inīpaccayo, taṃ kulaṃ assaddhaṃ appasannanti kulassa aguṇaṃ, ayasaṃ vā bhāsantiyāti attho. Bhikkhunīnaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsantiyāti “bhikkhuniyo dussīlā pāpadhammā”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 1043) bhikkhunīnaṃ aguṇaṃ, ayasaṃ vā bhāsantiyā.

'Miserliness regarding a family is miserly toward a family': in the first part, the suffix '-inī' is in the possessive sense. 'That family is faithless and without confidence' means speaking of the family's faults or disrepute. 'Speaking ill of the nuns' means speaking of the nuns' faults or disrepute by saying, 'The nuns are immoral and of bad character.'

Santaṃyeva [V 0.0446] ādīnavanti kulassa vā bhikkhunīnaṃ vā santaṃyeva aguṇaṃ.

'An actual fault' means an actual fault of either the family or the nuns.

Kulamaccharinīsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on a nun miserly toward a family is concluded.

6-8. Abhikkhukāvāsādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6-8. The Explanation of the Training Rules on a Residence Without Monks and so forth

Samantapāsādikāyaṃ [M 0.0480] vuttoti samantapāsādikāya ovādavaggassa paṭhamasikkhāpade (pāci. aṭṭha. 144) vutto.

'Stated in the Samantapāsādikā' means it is stated in the first training rule of the Ovāda Chapter of the Samantapāsādikā (Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā 144).

Sattamaṭṭhamāni uttānatthāneva.

The seventh and eighth are simply clear in meaning.

Abhikkhukāvāsādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on residing without monks, and so forth, is concluded.

9-10. Ovādūpasaṅkamanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9–10. Explanation of the Training Rule on Approaching for Exhortation, and so forth.

Uposathassa pucchanaṃ uposathapucchā, sāvakapaccayaṃ, rassattañca katvā “uposathapucchaka”nti vuttāti āha “uposathapucchana”nti. Ovādatthāyāti ovādayācanatthāya.

The asking about the Uposatha is 'uposathapucchā'. The term 'uposathapucchaka' is used, having been shortened and formed with a suffix in the agent sense; thus it says 'uposathapucchana'. 'For the purpose of exhortation' means for the purpose of requesting exhortation.

Dasamaṃ uttānatthameva.

The tenth is simply clear in meaning.

Ovādūpasaṅkamanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning approaching for instruction, and so forth, is concluded.

Ārāmavaggo chaṭṭho.

The sixth chapter, the Chapter on Parks.

7. Gabbhinīvaggo

7. The Chapter on Pregnant Women

1-2. Gabbhinīādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1–2. The explanation of the training rule concerning pregnant women, and so forth.

Paṭhamaṃ [V 0.0447] uttānatthameva.

The first is simply clear in meaning.

Thane bhavaṃ thaññaṃ, khīraṃ. Yaṃ pāyetīti yaṃ dārakaṃ pāyeti.

Thaññaṃ, that which is in the breast, is milk. ‘Yaṃ pāyeti’ means ‘the child whom she feeds’.

Gabbhinīādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning pregnant women, and so forth, is concluded.

3. Paṭhamasikkhamānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the First Training Rule for Female Probationers

Padabhājane vuttanayenāti “pāṇātipātā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmi…pe… vikālabhojanā veramaṇiṃ dve vassāni [M 0.0481] avītikkamma samādānaṃ samādiyāmī”ti (pāci. 1079) padabhājanasamīpe aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ vuttanayena. Imā pana cha sikkhāyo saṭṭhivassāyapi pabbajitāya dātabbāyeva, na etāsu asikkhitā upasampādetabbā.

‘In the manner stated in the word-by-word analysis’ means: in the manner stated in the origin story near the word-by-word analysis (Pāc. 1079): ‘I undertake the training rule to abstain from killing living beings for two years without transgression… I undertake the training rule to abstain from eating at the wrong time for two years without transgression.’ These six training rules, however, should be given even to a woman who has gone forth at sixty years of age; one who has not trained in these should not be given full ordination.

Paṭhamasikkhamānasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the first training rule for female probationers is concluded.

4-5. Dutiyasikkhamānādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4–5. The explanation of the training rule concerning a second female probationer, and so forth.

Padabhājane vuttā upasampadāsammuti na dinnā hotīti padabhājanasamīpe aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ vuttā upasampadāsammuti ñattidutiyāya kammavācāya na dinnā hoti.

‘The agreement for full ordination mentioned in the word-by-word analysis has not been given’ means: the agreement for full ordination mentioned in the origin story near the word-by-word analysis has not been given by a formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement.

Pañcamaṃ uttānatthameva.

The fifth is simply clear in meaning.

Dutiyasikkhamānādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a second female probationer, and so forth, is concluded.

6-10. Dutiyagihigatādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6–10. The explanation of the training rule concerning a second woman who has returned to lay life, and so forth.

Dasavassāya [V 0.0448] gihigatāya sikkhāsammutiṃ datvā paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ upasampādetuṃ vaṭṭati.

It is permissible to give the agreement for training to a woman who has returned to lay life at ten years of age, and then to give her full ordination when she is fully twelve years of age.

Sattamaaṭṭhamanavamadasamāni uttānatthāneva.

The seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth are simply clear in meaning.

Dutiyagihigatādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a second woman who has returned to lay life, and so forth, is concluded.

Gabbhinīvaggo sattamo.

The seventh chapter, the Chapter on Pregnant Women.

8. Kumāribhūtavaggo

8. The Chapter on Maidens

1-5. Paṭhamakumāribhūtādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1–5. The explanation of the training rule concerning the first maiden, and so forth.

Sabbapaṭhamā dve mahāsikkhamānāti gabbhinivagge vuttā dve sikkhamānā. “Sikkhamānā”icceva vattabbāti sammutikammādīsu evaṃ vattabbā. “Gihigatā”ti [M 0.0482] vā “kumāribhūtā”ti vā na vattabbāti sace vadanti, kammaṃ kuppatīti adhippāyo.

‘The very first two great female probationers’ means the two female probationers mentioned in the Chapter on Pregnant Women. ‘They should be called only “female probationers”’ means they should be referred to thus in the acts of agreement, and so forth. ‘They should not be called “one who has returned to lay life” or “a maiden”’ means: if they do say this, the formal act is invalid—this is the intention.

Catutthapañcamāni uttānatthāneva.

The fourth and fifth are simply clear in meaning.

Paṭhamakumāribhūtādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the first maiden, and so forth, is concluded.

6-8. Khīyanadhammādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6–8. The explanation of the training rule concerning things subject to decay, and so forth.

Vuṭṭhāpanasammutiyā yācitāyāti upasampadāsammutiyā yācitāya.

Vuṭṭhāpanasammutiyā yācitāyāti: that is, requested for the agreement for full ordination.

Sattamaṭṭhamāni uttānatthāneva.

The seventh and eighth are clear in meaning.

Khīyanadhammādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning things subject to decay, and so forth, is concluded.

9. Sokāvāsasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. The explanation of the training rule concerning residence during mourning.

Āgacchamānāti [V 0.0449] āgacchantī.

Āgacchamānāti: that is, āgacchantī, coming.

Sokāvāsasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning residence during mourning is concluded.

10. Ananuññātasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. The explanation of the training rule concerning the unpermitted.

Tesaṃ atthibhāvaṃ ajānantiyāti (pāci. aṭṭha. 1163) tesaṃ mātādīnaṃ atthibhāvaṃ ajānantiyā. Ananuññātasamuṭṭhānanti yaṃ vācato, kāyavācato, vācācittato, kāyavācācittato ca samuṭṭhāti, taṃ ananuññātasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Kathaṃ? Abbhānakammādīsu kenacideva karaṇīyena khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ nisinnā “pakkosatha sikkhamānaṃ, idheva naṃ upasampādessāmā”ti upasampādeti, evaṃ vācato samuṭṭhāti. “Upassayato uṭṭhāya upasampādessāmī”ti vatvā khaṇḍasīmaṃ gacchantiyā kāyavācato samuṭṭhāti. Dvīsu ṭhānesu paṇṇattiṃ jānitvā vītikkamaṃ karontiyā vācācittato, kāyavācācittato ca samuṭṭhāti. Ananujānāpetvā upasampādanato kiriyākiriyaṃ.

Tesaṃ atthibhāvaṃ ajānantiyāti (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 1163): that is, not knowing the existence of those, such as her mother, and so forth. Ananuññātasamuṭṭhānanti: that is, what arises from speech, from body and speech, from speech and mind, or from body, speech, and mind; that is an origin from not having permission. How? In cases like the act of rehabilitation, and so forth, when someone is seated within a broken boundary for some necessary reason and says, ‘Summon the probationer, we will ordain her right here,’ thus it originates from speech. Or when one says, ‘I will rise from the residence and ordain her,’ and while going to the broken boundary, it originates from body and speech. Or when one, knowing the regulation in two instances, commits a transgression, it originates from speech and mind, or from body, speech, and mind. From ordaining without having obtained permission, it is an offense of action and inaction.

Ananuññātasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning the unpermitted is concluded.

11. Pārivāsikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. The explanation of the training rule concerning a woman on a temporary stay.

Dāruṇanti [M 0.0483] pāpaṃ. Patimānentanti olokentaṃ.

Dāruṇanti: that is, pāpaṃ, evil. Patimānentanti: that is, olokentaṃ, looking.

Pārivāsikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a woman on a temporary stay is concluded.

12. Anuvassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

12. The explanation of the training rule on ordaining annually.

Ekantarikanti ekena vassena antarikaṃ katvā.

Ekantarikanti: that is, ekena vassena antarikaṃ katvā, having made an interval of one year.

Anuvassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on ordaining annually is concluded.

13. Ekavassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

13. The explanation of the one-year training rule.

Mātikāyaṃ [V 0.0450] ekaṃ vassaṃ dveti ekantarike ekekasmiṃ saṃvacchare dve. Ekantarikaṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyāti imasmiṃ vasse ekaṃ, puna ekantarikaṃ ekanti dve vuṭṭhāpentiyā anāpatti.

In the Mātikā, the phrase ‘two in one year’ means two in each alternate year. ‘Ordaining with an interval of one year’ means: for one who ordains one in this year, and again one with an interval of one year—thus ordaining two—there is no offense.

Ekavassasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the one-year training rule is concluded.

Kumāribhūtavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Kumāribhūta Chapter, the Eighth.

9. Chattupāhanavaggo

9. The Chapter on Umbrellas and Sandals.

1-2. Chattupāhanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1-2. The explanation of the training rule on umbrellas, sandals, and so forth.

Vuttalakkhaṇaṃ chattanti “chattaṃ nāma tīṇi chattāni – setacchattaṃ, kilañjacchattaṃ, paṇṇacchattaṃ maṇḍalabaddhaṃ, salākabaddha”nti (pāci. 1181) evaṃ padabhājane vuttalakkhaṇaṃ chattaṃ. Tādisaṃ ṭhānaṃ patvāti gacchakaddamādīsu taṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ patvā.

‘An umbrella of the stated characteristic’ means an umbrella of the characteristic stated in the word-analysis thus: ‘An umbrella is of three kinds: a white umbrella, a rush umbrella, and a leaf umbrella, bound in a circle or with ribs’ (Pāc. 1181). ‘Having reached such a place’ means having reached those respective places, such as in grass, mud, and so forth.

Chattassevāti kaddamādīni patvā upāhanā omuñcitvā chattasseva dhāraṇaṃ. Upāhanānaṃyeva vāti gacchādīni disvā chattaṃ apanāmetvā upāhanānaṃyeva dhāraṇaṃ.

‘Only the umbrella’ means, having reached mud and so forth, taking off the sandals and holding only the umbrella. ‘Or only the sandals’ means, having seen grass and so forth, setting aside the umbrella and holding only the sandals.

Dutiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

The second is clear in meaning.

Chattupāhanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on umbrellas, sandals, and so forth, is concluded.

3-5. Saṅghāṇiādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3-5. The explanation of the training rules on the saṅghāṇi and so forth.

Saṅghāṇinti [M 0.0484] kaṭiyaṃ anubhavitabbaṃ ābharaṇaṃ. Tenāha “yaṃ kiñci kaṭūpaga”nti.

‘Saṅghāṇi’ means an ornament to be worn on the hip. Therefore it is said, ‘whatever pertains to the hip.’

Catutthapañcamāni [V 0.0451] uttānatthāneva.

The fourth and fifth are clear in meaning.

Saṅghāṇiādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rules on the saṅghāṇi and so forth is concluded.

6. Vāsitakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. The explanation of the training rule on scented things.

Gandhavāsitakenāti gandhaparibhāvitena.

‘Gandhavāsitakena’ means by something imbued with fragrance.

Vāsitakasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on scented things is concluded.

7-10. Bhikkhuniummaddāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7-10. Explanation of the Training Rule on Having a Bhikkhunī Massage, etc.

Gilānāyāti (pāci. aṭṭha. 1208) antamaso maggagamanaparissamenāpi ābādhikāya. Āpadāsūti corabhayādinā sarīrakampanādīsu.

‘For a sick woman’ (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 1208) means for one who is afflicted even by the fatigue of walking the path. ‘In times of danger’ means in cases such as trembling of the body due to fear of thieves, etc.

Aṭṭhamanavamadasamesu kiñci vattabbaṃ natthi.

There is nothing to be said about the eighth, ninth, and tenth training rules.

Bhikkhuniummaddāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning having a nun massage, etc., is concluded.

11. Anāpucchāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

11. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Not Asking Permission.

Upacāraṃ sandhāyāti samantā dvādasahatthūpacāraṃ sandhāya.

‘Considering the vicinity’ means considering the vicinity of twelve cubits all around.

Anāpucchāsikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on not asking permission is concluded.

12. Pañhāpucchanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

12. The Explanation of the Training Rule on Questioning.

Anodissāti “amukasmiṃ nāma ṭhāne pucchāmī”ti evaṃ aniyametvā kevalaṃ “pucchitabbaṃ atthi, pucchāmi, ayyā”ti evaṃ vatvā.

‘Without specifying’ means not specifying thus: ‘I will ask in such and such a place,’ but simply saying thus: ‘There is something to ask, I will ask, venerable sirs.’

Pañhāpucchanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on asking questions is concluded.

13. Asaṃkaccikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

13. The Explanation of the Asaṃkaccika Training Rule.

Parikkhittassa [M 0.0485][V 0.0452] gāmassa parikkhepaṃ, aparikkhittassa upacāraṃ atikkamantiyā vā okkamantiyā vāti ettha parikkhittassa gāmassa parikkhepaṃ atikkamantiyā vā aparikkhittassa gāmassa upacāraṃ okkamantiyā vāti yathākkamaṃ sambandho veditabbo. Āpadāsūti mahagghaṃ saṃkaccikaṃ pārupitvā gacchantiyā upaddavo uppajjati, evarūpāsu āpadāsu.

‘Crossing the boundary of a village with a boundary, or entering the vicinity of a village without a boundary’—here, the connection should be understood in due order as: ‘crossing the boundary of a village with a boundary, or entering the vicinity of a village without a boundary.’ ‘In times of danger’ means in such dangers as when trouble arises for one going along wearing a valuable saṃkaccika.

Asaṃkaccikasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Asaṃkaccika training rule is concluded.

Chattupāhanavaggo navamo.

The Chapter on Umbrellas and Sandals, the Ninth.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus, in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the explanation of the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the elucidation of hidden meanings,

Bhikkhunipātimokkhe pācittiyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the explanation of the Pācittiya section in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha is concluded.

Asādhāraṇasamuṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Uncommon Arisings.

Acittakānīti (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.1214) “nacca”ntiādinā ajānitvā dassanādiṃ karontiyā āpattisambhavato vatthuajānanacittena acittakāni. Lokavajjānīti “nacca”ntiādinā jānitvā dassanādiṃ karontiyā akusaleneva āpajjanato lokavajjāni. Tenāha “ayaṃ panettha adhippāyo”tiādi sacittakānīti “corī”tiādinā vatthuṃ jānitvā karaṇeyeva āpattisambhavato sacittakāni. Upasampadādīnaṃ ekantākusalacitteneva akattabbattā paṇṇattivajjāni. “Idha sacittakācittakatā paṇṇattijānanājānanatāya aggaheṭṭhā vatthujānanājānanatāya gahetabba”nti vadanti.

‘Acittakāni’ (Sārattha. Ṭī. Pācittiya 3.1214): Because an offense arises for one performing actions like watching, etc., without knowing, as in the case of ‘dancing,’ etc., they are ‘acittakāni’ due to a mind ignorant of the object. ‘Lokavajjāni’: Because one incurs an offense through what is unwholesome when performing actions like watching, etc., knowing, as in the case of ‘dancing,’ etc., they are ‘lokavajjāni’. Therefore it is said, ‘This is the meaning here,’ etc. ‘Sacittakāni’: Because an offense arises only when one performs actions like ‘theft,’ etc., knowing the object, they are ‘sacittakāni’. For matters like ordination, etc., because they should absolutely not be done with an unwholesome mind, they are ‘paṇṇattivajjāni’. Some say, ‘Here, whether something is sacittaka or acittaka should be understood as based primarily on knowing or not knowing the object, and secondarily on knowing or not knowing the rule.’

Asādhāraṇasamuṭṭhānavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the uncommon arisings is concluded.

Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

The Section on Offenses Requiring Confession.

2. Telaviññāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Training Rule on Requesting Oil, etc.

Pāḷiyaṃ [M 0.0486][V 0.0453] anāgatesu pana aṭṭhasupīti pāḷimuttakesu sappiādīsu aṭṭhasupi.

But concerning the eight kinds of condiment not mentioned in the Pāli text, this means the eight kinds of condiment, such as ghee, etc., that are outside the Pāli text.

Telaviññāpanādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on requesting oil, etc., is concluded.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus, in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the explanation of the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

in the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the elucidation of subtle meanings,

Bhikkhunipātimokkhe pāṭidesanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the explanation of the Pāṭidesanīya section in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha is concluded.

1. Parimaṇḍalādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. The explanation of the training rule concerning roundness, etc.

Sekhiyāni cevāti pañcasattati sekhiyāni ceva. “Bhikkhupātimokkhavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbā”ti iminā yasmā tādisaṃyevettha atthavinicchayaṃ vidū vadanti, tasmā visuṃ tesaṃ atthavaṇṇanā na vuttā. Tattha yā vuttā, sā idhāpi vuttāyevāti dasseti.

The Sekhiya training rules are indeed seventy-five. Since the wise declare the determination of meaning here to be exactly as stated in the commentary on the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, a separate explanation of their meaning is not given. This shows that what was stated there is also stated here.

Parimaṇḍalādisikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning wearing the lower robe all around, etc., is concluded.

Iti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyā pātimokkhavaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the commentary on the Pātimokkha,

Vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ

In the Vinayatthamañjūsā, the elucidation of subtle meanings,

Bhikkhunipātimokkhavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha is concluded.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Conclusion

Yaṃ [V 0.0454] pātimokkhassa vaṇṇanaṃ ārabhinti sambandho. “Mahāvihāravāsīna”nti idaṃ purimapacchimapadehi saddhiṃ sambandhitabbaṃ, mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ porāṇaṭṭhakathāhi vāti ca. Pāḷiyatthañca kevalanti sakalaṃ pāḷiatthañca, ubhatovibhaṅgañcāti vuttaṃ hoti. Etthāti etissaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ. Yasmā [M 0.0487] na hi atthīti sambandho. Yanti yaṃ padaṃ. Sīhaḷaṭṭhakathānayanti sīhaḷamātikaṭṭhakathānayaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāsāranti sīhaḷamātikaṭṭhakathāyaṃ atthasāraṃ, atha vā vinayaṭṭhakathāsu atthasāraṃ. Tenetaṃ dasseti – sīhaḷamātikaṭṭhakathāyaṃ atthasāraṃ ādāya imaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇiṃ karonto vinayaṭṭhakathāsupi idha vinicchaye yogakkhamaṃ atthasāraṃ ādāyeva akāsinti.

The connection is with the words, “I shall begin the commentary on the Pātimokkha.” The phrase “of the residents of the Mahāvihāra” should be connected with the preceding and following words, meaning “from the ancient commentaries of the residents of the Mahāvihāra.” “And the entire meaning of the Pāli” means the entire meaning of the Pāli, that is, both Vibhaṅgas. “Here” means in this Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī. The connection is “because it does not exist.” “Which” refers to the word “yaṃ.” “The method of the Sinhala commentaries” means the method of the Sinhala Mātikā commentaries. “The essence of the commentaries” refers to the essential meaning in the Sinhala Mātikā commentary, or alternatively, the essential meaning in the Vinaya commentaries. Therefore, this shows that in composing this Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, the author took the essential meaning from the Sinhala Mātikā commentary, and also took the essential meaning from the Vinaya commentaries as suitable for the determination here.

Idāni sadevakassa lokassa accantasukhādhigamāya attano puññaṃ pariṇāmento “yathā ca niṭṭhaṃ sampattā”tiādigāthādvayamāha. Kalyāṇanissitāti kusalanissitā. Sabbasattānanti kāmāvacarādibhedānaṃ sabbesaṃ sattānaṃ.

Now, dedicating his own merit for the attainment of ultimate happiness by the world with its deities, he speaks the two verses beginning with “yathā ca niṭṭhaṃ sampattā.” “Dependent on the good” means dependent on the wholesome. “All beings” refers to all beings of various kinds, such as those in the sense-sphere and others.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the conclusion is concluded.

Nigamanakathā

Conclusion

Ettāvatā ca –

And thus far—

1.

1.

Laṅkissaro yo vijitārirājo;

Rājā parakkantabhujo yasassī;

Tidhāgataṃ sīhaḷamekarajjaṃ;

Akā nikāyañca tathā samaggaṃ.

He who is the lord of Laṅkā, the king who has conquered his foes, the glorious king with mighty arms, made the threefold Sīhaḷa into a single kingdom, and likewise made the Nikāya harmonious.

2.

2.

Pure pulatthimhi vare purānaṃ;

Majjhamhi nānāratanākarānaṃ;

Anantasampattibharābhirāme;

Varācaluttaṅgagharābhirāme.

In the excellent, ancient city of Pulatthi; in its midst, a mine of various jewels; delightful with its abundance of boundless prosperity; charming with its excellent, lofty, mountain-like palaces.

3.

3.

Abhejjapākārasugopurasmiṃ[V 0.0455];

Nirākulānekakulākulasmiṃ;

Munindadāṭhaṅkuravāsabhūte;

Yo locanānandavahe vasanto.

In the city with unbreachable ramparts and fine gateways, thronged with many families yet unperturbed, which has become the dwelling place of the Sage-King’s tooth relic, he who dwells there brings delight to the eyes.

4.

4.

Suphullitabbhoruhasādusīta [M 0.0488]

Pasannanīrehi jalāsayehi;

Supupphitānekakadambajambu-

Punnāganāgādihi vābhiramme.

With ponds of clear, sweet, cool water, adorned with fully blooming lotuses; and delightful with many flowering kadamba, jambu, punnāga, and nāga trees.

5.

5.

Sudhāvadātehi manoharehi;

Pākārapantīhi ca gopurehi;

Vikiṇṇamuttāphalasannibhehi;

Vilokanīyehi sudhātalehi.

With charming, pure white rows of ramparts and gateways; and with plastered surfaces lovely to behold, resembling scattered pearls.

6.

6.

Katvāna pāsādasahassaramme;

Tahiṃ tahiṃ pītikare vihāre;

Mahādayo jetavanādayopi;

Susaṃyamānaṃ yatinaṃ adāsi.

Having built a thousand delightful mansions and joy-bringing monasteries here and there, the great-hearted one, like the donor of Jetavana and other great parks, gave them to the well-restrained ascetics.

7.

7.

Yo sādubhūtaṃ catupaccayañca;

Guṇappasanno samaṇesu tesu;

Niccaṃ mahoghaṃ viya vattayanto;

Yojeti te ganthavipassanāsu.

He who, confident in the virtues of those ascetics, provided the excellent four requisites, ever maintaining the flow like a great flood, and engaged them in study and insight.

8.

8.

Kāritesu vihāresu, tena tesu yasassinā;

Rammo yo pacchimārāmo, pupphārāmādisobhito.

Among the monasteries built by that illustrious one, there is the delightful Western Park, adorned with flower gardens and the like.

9.

9.

Pariveṇamhi nāmena, tahiṃ coḷakulantike;

Pāsāde dassanīyamhi, vasanto karuṇāparo.

Residing in a lovely mansion in a pariveṇa there, near the dwelling of the Coḷa clan, he, being full of compassion...

10.

10.

Sisso [V 0.0456] sasīkarasvaccha-sīlācārassa dhīmato;

Sāriputtamahāthera-mahāsāmissa tādino.

A disciple of the wise and steadfast great master, the Great Elder Sāriputta, whose virtue and conduct were as pure as the rays of the moon.

11.

11.

Dhīrānekaguṇoghena, therena sucivuttinā;

Vinayaṭṭhitikāmena, sumedhenābhiyācito.

I was earnestly entreated by the wise Elder Sumedha, who possesses a flood of many virtues, is of pure conduct, and is desirous of the stability of the Vinaya.

12.

12.

So buddhanāgattherohaṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ paramaṃ hitaṃ;

Mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ, yatīnaṃ samayānugaṃ.

I, that Elder Buddhānāga, for the highest welfare of the monks, the ascetics dwelling in the Mahāvihāra, in accordance with their tradition,

13.

13.

Vinayatthādimañjūsaṃ[M 0.0489], līnatthassa pakāsaniṃ;

Mātikaṭṭhakathāyemaṃ, akāsiṃ sādhu vaṇṇanaṃ.

Have skillfully composed this commentary on the Mātikā commentary, a treasure chest of the meaning of the Vinaya, an elucidation of the hidden meaning.

14.

14.

Sāyaṃ subodhā budhavaṇṇanīyā;

Saṃvaṇṇanā sattasahassamattā;

Nirākarontī vinayamhi mohaṃ;

Tamaṃ carantī sasi kheva bhātu.

May this exposition, easy to understand and praiseworthy by the wise, consisting of seven thousand units of text, dispelling delusion concerning the Vinaya, shine like the moon moving through the sky, dispelling the darkness.

15.

15.

Ākaṅkhamānena paratthamiṭṭhaṃ;

Mahatthasāraṃ suvinicchayañca;

Saṃvaṇṇanaṃ sādhu pakubbatā yaṃ;

Citaṃ mayā puññamanappabhūtaṃ.

Whatever abundant merit has been accumulated by me in skillfully composing this exposition, which is desired for the welfare of others and contains the essence of great meaning and clear discernment,

16.

16.

Puññena tenācitadānasīla-

Mayādinānekavidhena ceva;

Sattā anīghā sukhino averā;

Pappontu sabbe sugatiṃ sivañca.

By that merit, and by the many kinds of merit accumulated through generosity, virtue, and so on, may all beings be without affliction, happy, and free from enmity; may they all attain a good destiny and the state of peace.

17.

17.

Saddhiṃ yathopaddavamantarena;

Gatā hi līnatthapadīpanīyaṃ;

Tathā [V 0.0457] janānaṃ api dhammayuttā;

Manorathā siddhimupentu niccaṃ.

Just as this ‘Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning’ has reached completion without obstruction, so too may the righteous aspirations of people always attain fulfillment.

18.

18.

Kāle pavassantu sadā payodā;

Dhammena pālentu mahiṃ mahindā;

Sattā pasannā ratanattayasmiṃ;

Dānādipuññābhiratā bhavantūti.

May the clouds always rain in season; may the great rulers protect the earth with righteousness; may beings be confident in the Triple Gem and be delighted in meritorious deeds such as giving.

Vinayatthamañjūsā līnatthappakāsanīnāmikākaṅkhāvitaraṇīabhinavaṭīkā niṭṭhitā.

The Vinayatthamañjūsā, a new sub-commentary on the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, also named Līnatthappakāsanī (The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning), is concluded.
